HP:0002907.definition: Microscopic hematuria detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine.
exact_synonyms: Small amount of blood in urine

HP:0002909.label: Generalized aminoaciduria
HP:0002909.definition: An increased concentration of all types of amino acid in the urine.
HP:0002909.comment: This abnormality is distinct from aminoacidurias in which the urinary concentration of a single amino acid, or a of single group of amino acids, is increased.

HP:0002910.label: Elevated circulating hepatic transaminase concentration
HP:0002910.definition: Elevations of the levels of SGOT and SGPT in the serum. SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) are transaminases primarily found in the liver and heart and are released into the bloodstream as the result of liver or heart damage. SGOT and SGPT are used clinically mainly as markers of liver damage.

HP:0002912.label: Methylmalonic acidemia
HP:0002912.definition: Increased concentration of methylmalonic acid in the blood.
HP:0002912.comment: Methylmalonic aciduria is a genetically heterogeneous disorder of methylmalonate and cobalamin (cbl; vitamin B12) metabolism.

HP:0002913.label: Myoglobinuria
HP:0002913.definition: Presence of myoglobin in the urine.
HP:0002913.comment: Myoglobinuria is usually associated with rhabdomyolysis or muscle destruction.

HP:0002914.label: Hyperchloriduria
HP:0002914.definition: An increased concentration of chloride in the urine.

HP:0002917.label: Hypomagnesemia
HP:0002917.definition: An abnormally decreased magnesium concentration in the blood.

HP:0002918.label: Hypermagnesemia
HP:0002918.definition: An abnormally increased magnesium concentration in the blood.

HP:0002919.label: Ketonuria
HP:0002919.definition: High levels of ketone bodies (acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, and acetone) in the urine. Ketone bodies are insignificant in the blood and urine of normal individuals in the postprandial or overnight-fasted state.
HP:0002919.comment: Acetone is the main component of the ketone bodies.

HP:0002920.label: Decreased circulating ACTH concentration
HP:0002920.definition: The concentration of corticotropin, also known as adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), is below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

HP:0002921.label: Abnormal cerebrospinal fluid morphology
HP:0002921.definition: An abnormality of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
HP:0002921.comment: The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is secreted by the choroid plexus, and flows uninterrupted throughout the central nervous system (the central cerebrospinal canal of the spinal cord and through the four interconnected cerebral ventricles in the brain).

HP:0002922.label: Increased CSF protein concentration
HP:0002922.definition: Increased concentration of protein in the cerebrospinal fluid.

HP:0002923.label: Rheumatoid factor positive
HP:0002923.definition: The presence in the serum of an autoantibody directed against the Fc portion of IgG.

HP:0002925.label: Elevated circulating thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration
HP:0002925.definition: Increased concentration of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood circulation.

HP:0002926.label: Abnormality of thyroid physiology
HP:0002926.definition: An abnormal functionality of the thyroid gland.

HP:0002927.label: Histidinuria
HP:0002927.definition: An increased concentration of histidine in the urine.
HP:0002927.comment: Normal urinary histidine total (free and combined form) excretion is around 190 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0002928.label: Decreased activity of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
exact_synonyms: Decreased activity of the PDH complex

HP:0002930.label: Impaired sensitivity to thyroid hormone
HP:0002930.definition: Reduced sensitivity of end organs to thyroid hormone characterized by elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed thyroid stimulating hormone.
HP:0002930.comment: Impaired sensitivity to thyroid hormone may be accompanied by goiter and no clear symptoms and signs of thyrotoxicosis. The etiologies of this feature include defects in the thyroid hormone receptor, reduced cellular access of the biologically active thyroid hormone, T3 related to defects of thyroid hormone cell membrane transport, and a defect reducing the intracellular metabolism generating T3 from T4.
exact_synonyms: Elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed TSH

HP:0002932.label: Aldehyde oxidase deficiency
HP:0002932.definition: A reduction in aldehyde oxidase level.
HP:0002932.comment: Aldehyde oxidase generates carboxylic acids from aldehydes.

HP:0002933.label: Ventral hernia
HP:0002933.definition: Ventral hernia refers to a condition in which abdominal contents protrude through a weakened portion of the abdominal wall.

HP:0002936.label: Distal sensory impairment
HP:0002936.definition: An abnormal reduction in sensation in the distal portions of the extremities.
exact_synonyms: Distal sensory impairment of the lower extremities
Distal sensory loss, upper and lower limbs
Distal sensory impairment in lower limbs

HP:0002937.label: Hemivertebrae
HP:0002937.definition: Absence of one half of the vertebral body.
HP:0002937.comment: Lateral hemivertebrae represent a developmental defect resulting from the failure of the contralateral chondral center to develop. Dorsal hemivertebrae result from a developmental defect in which the anterior chondral centers fail to develop, and ventral hemivertebrae result from failure of the posterior centers to ossify. The affected half of the vertebral body may by hypoplastic or absent, as is the pedicle, and (for thoracic vetebrae) the corresponding rib. The affected half of the vertebral body may also show a fusion or segmentation defect.

HP:0002938.label: Lumbar hyperlordosis
HP:0002938.definition: An abnormal accentuation of the inward curvature of the spine in the lumbar region.
exact_synonyms: Excessive inward curvature of lower spine

HP:0002942.label: Thoracic kyphosis
HP:0002942.definition: Over curvature of the thoracic region, leading to a round back or if sever to a hump.

HP:0002945.label: Intervertebral space narrowing
HP:0002945.definition: Decreased height of the intervertebral disk.
HP:0002945.comment: A decrease in the height of the intervertebral disks is usually observed as a narrowing of the space between the vertebrae on X-ray examination.

HP:0002947.label: Cervical kyphosis
HP:0002947.definition: Exaggerated convexity of the cervical vertebral column, causing the cervical spine to bow outwards and take on a rounded appearance.

HP:0002948.label: Vertebral fusion
HP:0002948.definition: A developmental defect leading to the union of two adjacent vertebrae.

HP:0002949.label: Fused cervical vertebrae
HP:0002949.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more cervical vertebral bodies with one another.

HP:0002951.label: Partial absence of cerebellar vermis
HP:0002951.definition: Congenital absence of a part of the vermis of cerebellum.

HP:0002953.label: Vertebral compression fracture
exact_synonyms: Compression fracture of a vertebral body

HP:0002955.label: Granulomatosis
HP:0002955.definition: A granulomatous inflammation leading to multiple granuloma formation, which is a specific type of inflammation. A granuloma is a focal compact collection of inflammatory cells, mononuclear cells predominating, usually as a result of the persistence of a non-degradable product and of active cell mediated hypersensitivity.
HP:0002955.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by tissue biopsy. A granuloma is a compact (organized) collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes (macrophages and/or epithelioid cells) which may or may not be accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis or the infiltration of other inflammatory leukocytes (Adams DO. The granulomatous inflammatory response. Am J Pathol 1976:84:163-192).

HP:0002958.label: Immune dysregulation
HP:0002958.definition: Altered immune function characterized by lymphoid proliferation, immune activation, and excessive autoreactivity often leading to autoimmune/inflammatory complications.

HP:0002959.label: Impaired Ig class switch recombination
HP:0002959.definition: An impairment of the class-switch recombination process that normally leads B lymphocytes to produce IgG, IgA, or IgE.
HP:0002959.comment: The generation of the antibody repertoire requires two successive steps. The first is antigen- and T-cell-independent; it takes place in the fetal liver and the bone marrow. Immature B lymphocytes rearrange their immunoglobulin-gene variable segments (V segments), diversity segments (D segments) and joining segments (J segments), producing a functionally integrated VDJ segment linked to the mu constant region (C-mu), which determines the primary antibody repertoire composed of IgM antibodies. The second step is antigen- and T-cell-dependent and takes place in secondary lymphoid organs. After encountering antigen, B cells proliferate and form germinal centers. In this unique anatomic formation, two genetic events lead to generation of the secondary antibody repertoire: class-switch recombination (CSR) and somatic hypermutation (SHM). CSR of immunoglobulins occurs by a recombination process between two different switch regions (S regions) located upstream of each C region. Replacement of C-mu by a constant region of another class of immunoglobulin (C-gamma, C-alpha or C-epsilon) ensues and leads to the production of IgG, IgA or IgE.

HP:0002960.label: Autoimmunity
HP:0002960.definition: The occurrence of an immune reaction against the organism's own cells or tissues.

HP:0002961.label: Dysgammaglobulinemia
HP:0002961.definition: Selective deficiency of one or more, but not all, classes of immunoglobulins.

HP:0002963.label: Abnormal delayed hypersensitivity skin test
HP:0002963.definition: Delay in cutaneous immune reaction to specific antigens mediated not by antibodies but by cells. The delayed hypersensitivity test is an immune function test measuring the presence of activated T cells that recognize a specific antigen and is performed by injecting a small amount of the antigen into the skin. The area of the injection is examined 48-72 hours thereafter.
HP:0002963.comment: This is an immune function test measuring the presence of activated T cells that recognize a certain substance.

HP:0002965.label: Cutaneous anergy
HP:0002965.definition: Inability to react to a delayed hypersensitivity skin test.
HP:0002965.comment: Anergy skin testing assesses the responses to skin-test antigens to which a cell-mediated, delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response is expected.
exact_synonyms: Lack of delayed skin hypersensitivity reaction
Absence of delayed hypersensitivity skin test

HP:0002967.label: Cubitus valgus
HP:0002967.definition: Abnormal positioning in which the elbows are turned out.

HP:0002970.label: Genu varum
HP:0002970.definition: A positional abnormality marked by outward bowing of the legs in which the knees stay wide apart when a person stands with the feet and ankles together.

HP:0002971.label: Absent microvilli on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes
HP:0002971.definition: Absence of the fingerlike protrusive, actin-dependent structures found on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes.

HP:0002972.label: Reduced delayed hypersensitivity
HP:0002972.definition: Decreased ability to react to a delayed hypersensitivity skin test.
exact_synonyms: Decreased reactivity to skin test antigens

HP:0002973.label: Abnormal forearm morphology
HP:0002973.definition: An abnormality of the lower arm.

HP:0002974.label: Radioulnar synostosis
HP:0002974.definition: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the radius and the ulna.

HP:0002977.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the central nervous system
HP:0002977.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of tissue in the central nervous system.

HP:0002979.label: Bowing of the legs
HP:0002979.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature affecting a long bone of the leg.

HP:0002981.label: Abnormality of the calf
HP:0002981.definition: An abnormality of the calf, i.e. of the posterior part of the lower leg.

HP:0002982.label: Tibial bowing
HP:0002982.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the tibia.
HP:0002982.comment: A developmental defect with posteromedial tibial angulation.

HP:0002983.label: Micromelia
HP:0002983.definition: The presence of abnormally small extremities.
exact_synonyms: Smaller or shorter than typical limbs

HP:0002986.label: Radial bowing
HP:0002986.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the radius.
exact_synonyms: Bowing of outer large bone of the forearm
Bowing of radius bone of the forearm

HP:0002987.label: Elbow flexion contracture
HP:0002987.definition: An elbow contracture that limits the ability of the elbow joint to be extended (straightened), meaning that the elbow is fixed in an flexed (bent) position.
exact_synonyms: Fixed flexion at the elbow joint

HP:0002991.label: Abnormal fibula morphology
HP:0002991.definition: An anomaly of the calf bone (fibula), one of the two bones of the calf.

HP:0002999.label: Patellar dislocation
HP:0002999.definition: The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar dislocation occurs if the patella fully dislocates out of the groove.

HP:0003002.label: Breast carcinoma
HP:0003002.definition: The presence of a carcinoma of the breast.

HP:0003005.label: Ganglioneuroma
HP:0003005.definition: A benign neoplasm that usually arises from the sympathetic trunk in the mediastinum, representing a tumor of the sympathetic nerve fibers arising from neural crest cells.
HP:0003005.comment: Ganglioneuromas and ganglioneuroblastomas are tumors of the sympathetic nervous system. They originate from neural crest sympathogonia, which are completely undifferentiated cells of the sympathetic nervous system.

HP:0003006.label: Neuroblastoma
HP:0003006.definition: Neuroblastoma is a solid tumor that originate in neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Most neuroblastomas originate in the abdomen, and most abdominal neuroblastomas originate in the adrenal gland. Neuroblastomas can also originate in the thorax, usually in the posterior mediastinum.

HP:0003010.label: Prolonged bleeding time
HP:0003010.definition: Prolongation of the time taken for a standardized skin cut of fixed depth and length to stop bleeding.
HP:0003010.comment: The bleeding time test measures the time taken for blood vessel constriction and platelet plug formation to occur. No clot is allowed to form, so that the arrest of bleeding depends exclusively on blood vessel constriction and platelet action. To perform the test, pressure is maintained throughout the test by inflating a sphygmomanometer cuff on the upper arm. The dorsal surface of the forearm is then cleaned, and the bleeding time device placed onto the skin and the trigger is depressed. At 30-second intervals, the flow of blood is blotted with filter paper. The time from puncture to cessation of bleeding is then recorded as the bleeding time. Normal values depend on the device used and other parameters, but are around 2 to 9 minutes.

HP:0003011.label: Abnormality of the musculature
HP:0003011.definition: Abnormality originating in one or more muscles, i.e., of the set of muscles of body.

HP:0003013.label: Bulging epiphyses
HP:0003013.definition: A morphological abnormality of epiphyses whereby they are abnormally outwardly curving (protuberant).

HP:0003015.label: Flared metaphysis
HP:0003015.definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones.
HP:0003015.comment: Figure 11 of PMID:12853662 shows metaphyseal flaring.
exact_synonyms: marked metaphyseal flaring of long bones
Flared wide portion of long bone

HP:0003016.label: Metaphyseal widening
HP:0003016.definition: Abnormal widening of the metaphyseal regions of long bones.
exact_synonyms: Broad wide portion of long bone

HP:0003019.label: Abnormality of the wrist
HP:0003019.definition: Abnormality of the wrist, the structure connecting the hand and the forearm.

HP:0003021.label: Metaphyseal cupping
HP:0003021.definition: Metaphyseal cupping refers to an inward bulging of the metaphyseal profile giving the metaphysis a cup-like appearance.

HP:0003023.label: Bowing of limbs due to multiple fractures
HP:0003023.definition: Curvature of the shafts of the long bones due to multiple fractures.
exact_synonyms: Bowed limbs due to multiple fractures

HP:0003025.label: Metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0003025.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphyses.
exact_synonyms: Irregular wide portion of a long bone

HP:0003026.label: Short long bone
HP:0003026.definition: One or more abnormally short long bone.
HP:0003026.comment: Long bones are also known as tubular bones.

HP:0003027.label: Mesomelia
HP:0003027.definition: Shortening of the middle parts of the limbs (forearm and lower leg) in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
HP:0003027.comment: Shortening of the limbs where the predominant shortness is in the middle bones.
exact_synonyms: Disproportionately short middle portion of limb

HP:0003028.label: Abnormality of the ankle
HP:0003028.definition: An anomaly of the joint that connects the foot with the leg.

HP:0003031.label: Ulnar bowing
HP:0003031.definition: Bending of the diaphysis (shaft) of the ulna.
HP:0003031.comment: Ulnar bowing is usually in the convex posterior direction.

HP:0003034.label: Diaphyseal sclerosis
HP:0003034.definition: An elevation in bone density in one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in shaft of long bone

HP:0003037.label: Enlarged joints
HP:0003037.definition: Increase in size of one or more joints.

HP:0003041.label: Humeroradial synostosis
HP:0003041.definition: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the radius and the humerus.
exact_synonyms: Fusion of upper and lower arm bones

HP:0003042.label: Elbow dislocation
HP:0003042.definition: Dislocation of the distal humerus out of the elbow joint, where the radius, ulna, and humerus meet.

HP:0003043.label: Abnormal shoulder morphology
HP:0003043.definition: An abnormality of the shoulder, which is defined as the structures surrounding the shoulder joint where the humerus attaches to the scapula.

HP:0003044.label: Shoulder flexion contracture
HP:0003044.definition: Chronic reduction in active and passive mobility of the shoulder joint due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.

HP:0003048.label: Radial head subluxation
HP:0003048.definition: Partial dislocation of the head of the radius.

HP:0003051.label: Enlarged metaphyses
HP:0003051.definition: Abnormal increase in size of one or more metaphyses.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged wide portion of a long bone

HP:0003066.label: Limited knee extension
HP:0003066.definition: Reduced ability to extend (straighten) the knee joint.

HP:0003067.label: Madelung deformity
HP:0003067.definition: An anomaly related to partial closure, or failure of development of the ulnar side of the distal radial growth plate, which results in an arrest of epiphyseal growth of the medial and volar portions of the distal radius. This leads to shortening of the radius and relative overgrowth of the ulna.

HP:0003072.label: Hypercalcemia
HP:0003072.definition: An abnormally increased calcium concentration in the blood.

HP:0003073.label: Hypoalbuminemia
HP:0003073.definition: The concentration of albumin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0003074.label: Hyperglycemia
HP:0003074.definition: An increased concentration of glucose in the blood.

HP:0003075.label: Hypoproteinemia
HP:0003075.definition: A decreased concentration of protein in the blood.

HP:0003076.label: Glycosuria
HP:0003076.definition: An increased concentration of glucose in the urine.
HP:0003076.comment: Glycosuria, the excretion of abnormal amounts of glucose in the urine, generally results in osmotic diuresis.

HP:0003077.label: Hyperlipidemia
HP:0003077.definition: An elevated lipid concentration in the blood.
HP:0003077.comment: Hyperlipidemia is an elevation of the blood levels of lipids including primarily cholesterol, phospholipids and triglycerides and cholesterol esters. The lipids are transported on lipoproteins some of which are commonly used for clinical measurements, including chylomicrons, very-low density lipoproteins (VLDL), intermediate-density lipoproteins (IDL), low-density lipoproteins, and high-density lipoproteins (HDL).

HP:0003079.label: Defective DNA repair after ultraviolet radiation damage

HP:0003080.label: Hydroxyprolinuria
HP:0003080.definition: An increased concentration of 4-hydroxy-L-proline in the urine.

HP:0003081.label: Increased urinary potassium
HP:0003081.definition: An increased concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.

HP:0003083.label: Dislocated radial head
HP:0003083.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint.

HP:0003084.label: Recurrent long bone fractures
HP:0003084.definition: An increased tendency to fractures of the long bones (Mainly, the femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius, and ulna).

HP:0003090.label: Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0003090.definition: Underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Underdevelopment of the innermost thighbone end part

HP:0003091.label: Trophic limb changes
HP:0003091.definition: Trophic changes occurring in a limb.

HP:0003093.label: Limited hip extension
HP:0003093.definition: Limitation of the extension of the hip, i.e., decreased ability to straighten the hip joint and thereby increase the angle between torso and thigh; moving the thigh or top of the pelvis backward.
HP:0003093.comment: Reduced ability to straighten out the femur.

HP:0003097.label: Short femur
HP:0003097.definition: An abnormal shortening of the femur.

HP:0003099.label: Fibular overgrowth
HP:0003099.definition: Relatively increased growth of the fibula compared to that of the tibia.

HP:0003100.label: Slender long bone
HP:0003100.definition: Reduced diameter of a long bone.

HP:0003102.label: Increased carrying angle
HP:0003102.definition: An abnormal increase in the carrying angle, which is the angle he long axis of the extended forearm as it lies lateral to the long axis of the arm.
HP:0003102.comment: Anatomically, the carrying angle in human adults is approximately 10 degrees in men and 13 degrees in women. Increasing the carrying angle may lead to elbow instability and pain during exercise or in throwing activities of sports, may reduce function of elbow flexion, predispose to risk of elbow dislocation, and increase evidence of elbow fracture when falling on the outstretched hand and fracture of the distal humeral epiphysis.

HP:0003103.label: Abnormal cortical bone morphology
HP:0003103.definition: An abnormality of compact bone (also known as cortical bone), which forms the dense surface of bones.

HP:0003105.label: Protuberances at ends of long bones
HP:0003105.definition: The presence of multiple protuberances (bulges, or knobs) at the ends of the long bones.
exact_synonyms: Protuberances at ends of long bones

HP:0003106.label: Subperiosteal bone resorption
HP:0003106.definition: Loss of bone mass occurring beneath the periosteum (the periosteum is the connective-tissue membrane that surrounds all bones except at the articular surfaces). This process may create a serrated and lace-like appearance in periosteal cortical bone.

HP:0003107.label: Abnormal circulating cholesterol concentration
HP:0003107.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of cholesterol in the blood circulation.

HP:0003108.label: Hyperglycinuria
HP:0003108.definition: An increased concentration of glycine in the urine.
HP:0003108.comment: Normal urinary glycine total (free and combined form) excretion is around 450 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0003109.label: Hyperphosphaturia
HP:0003109.definition: An increased excretion of phosphates in the urine.

HP:0003110.label: Abnormality of urine homeostasis
HP:0003110.definition: An abnormality of the composition of urine or the levels of its components.

HP:0003111.label: Abnormal blood ion concentration
HP:0003111.definition: Abnormality of the homeostasis (concentration) of a monoatomic ion.

HP:0003112.label: Abnormal circulating amino acid concentration
HP:0003112.definition: The presence of an abnormal decrease or increase of one or more amino acids in the blood circulation.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of serum amino acid levels
Abnormality of serum amino acid level

HP:0003113.label: Hypochloremia
HP:0003113.definition: An abnormally decreased chloride concentration in the blood.

HP:0003117.label: Abnormal circulating hormone concentration
HP:0003117.definition: Concentration of a hormone in the blood circulation outside of normal limits.

HP:0003118.label: Increased circulating cortisol level
HP:0003118.definition: Overproduction of the hormone of cortisol by the adrenal cortex, resulting in a characteristic combination of clinical symptoms termed Cushing syndrome, with truncal obesity, a round, full face, striae atrophicae and acne, muscle weakness, and other features.

HP:0003119.label: Abnormal circulating lipid concentration
HP:0003119.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a lipid in the blood circulation.
HP:0003119.comment: According to CHEBI:18059 'Lipids' is a loosely defined term for substances of biological origin that are soluble in nonpolar solvents. They consist of saponifiable lipids, such as glycerides (fats and oils) and phospholipids, as well as nonsaponifiable lipids, principally steroids.

HP:0003121.label: Limb joint contracture
HP:0003121.definition: A contracture (chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin) that prevent normal movement of one or more joints of the limbs.

HP:0003124.label: Hypercholesterolemia
HP:0003124.definition: An increased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0003125.label: Reduced factor VIII activity
HP:0003125.definition: Reduced activity of coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.

HP:0003126.label: Low-molecular-weight proteinuria
HP:0003126.definition: Excretion in urine of proteins of a size smaller than albumin (molecular weight 69 kD).

HP:0003127.label: Hypocalciuria
HP:0003127.definition: An abnormally decreased calcium concentration in the urine.

HP:0003128.label: Lactic acidosis
HP:0003128.definition: An abnormal buildup of lactic acid in the body, leading to acidification of the blood and other bodily fluids.
HP:0003128.comment: Note that the term acidemia is used to describe the state of low pH in the blood, whereas acidosis is used to describe the processes that lead to acidemia. In medical jargon, however, the two terms are used interchangeably.

HP:0003130.label: Abnormal peripheral myelination
HP:0003130.definition: An abnormality of the myelination of motor and sensory peripheral nerves. These are axons for motor nerves and dendrites for sensory nerves in the strict anatomic sense.
HP:0003130.comment: This finding may be observed upon biopsy of the sural nerve. Myelination, i.e., the presence of a segmented lipid-rich sheath (myelin), enables faster and more energetically efficient conduction of electrical impulses. The sheath is formed by the cell membranes of Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system (GO:0022011).

HP:0003131.label: Cystinuria
HP:0003131.definition: An increased concentration of cystine in the urine.
HP:0003131.comment: Cystine is a sulfur-containing amino acid.

HP:0003133.label: Abnormal spinocerebellar tract morphology
HP:0003133.definition: An abnormality of the spinocerebellar tracts, a set of axonal fibers originating in the spinal cord and terminating in the ipsilateral cerebellum. The spinocerebellar tract convey information to the cerebellum about limb and joint position (proprioception). They comprise the ventral spinocerebellar tract, the anterior spinocerebellar tract, and the posterior spinocerebellar tract.

HP:0003134.label: Abnormality of peripheral nerve conduction
HP:0003134.definition: An abnormality of the conduction of electrical impulses by peripheral (motor or sensory) nerves. This finding is elicited by a nerve conduction study (NCS).
HP:0003134.comment: A nerve conduction study (NCS) is commonly conducted together with electromyography in order to evaluate muscle disorders. For the NCS, dermal electrodes are placed at intervals over the nerve to be examined, and a low-intensity current is introduced to generate action potentials. The velocity of the action potential is related to the diameter of the nerve fiber and the presence of a myelin sheath. Diseases of the myelin sheath characteristically reduce the nerve conduction velocity (NCV). The amplitude of the response is also measured.
exact_synonyms: Sensory and motor nerve conduction abnormalities

HP:0003137.label: Prolinuria
HP:0003137.definition: Level of proline in the urine anove the upper limit of normal.
HP:0003137.comment: Normal urinary proline total (free and combined form) excretion is around 40 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0003138.label: Increased blood urea nitrogen
HP:0003138.definition: An increased amount of nitrogen in the form of urea in the blood.

HP:0003139.label: Panhypogammaglobulinemia
HP:0003139.definition: A reduction in the circulating levels of all the major classes of immunoglobulin. is characterized by profound decreases in all classes of immunoglobulin with an absence of circulating B lymphocytes.

HP:0003140.label: T-wave inversion in the right precordial leads

HP:0003141.label: Increased LDL cholesterol concentration
HP:0003141.definition: An elevated concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0003144.label: Increased serum serotonin
HP:0003144.definition: A increased concentration of serotonin in the blood.

HP:0003145.label: Decreased circulating adenosylcobalamin concentration
HP:0003145.definition: The concentration of adenosylcobalam in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. Adenosylcobalamin is one of the active forms of vitamin B12.

HP:0003146.label: Hypocholesterolemia
HP:0003146.definition: An decreased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0003148.label: Elevated serum acid phosphatase
HP:0003148.comment: Acid phosphatase can free attached phosphate groups from other molecules. It is a lysosomal enzyme.

HP:0003149.label: Hyperuricosuria
HP:0003149.definition: An abnormally high level of uric acid in the urine.
HP:0003149.comment: Xanthine oxidase oxidizes oxypurines such as xanthine and hypoxanthine to uric acid. Uric acid is the final oxidation product of purine catabolism.

HP:0003150.label: Glutaric aciduria
HP:0003150.definition: The concentration of glutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0003153.label: Cystathioninuria
HP:0003153.definition: An elevated urinary concentration of cystathionine.
HP:0003153.comment: Cystathionine can be directly interconverted to cysteine. Normal cystathione urinary values are under 150 micromole per gram creatinine.

HP:0003154.label: Increased circulating ACTH level
HP:0003154.definition: An abnormal increased in the concentration of corticotropin, also known as adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), in the blood.

HP:0003155.label: Elevated circulating alkaline phosphatase concentration
HP:0003155.definition: Abnormally increased serum levels of alkaline phosphatase activity.

HP:0003158.label: Hyposthenuria
HP:0003158.definition: An abnormally low urinary specific gravity, i.e., reduced concentration of solutes in the urine.
HP:0003158.comment: Hyposthenuria may occur with impaired renal concentrating power or upon abnormally low hormonal stimulation, as in diabetes insipidus.

HP:0003159.label: Hyperoxaluria
HP:0003159.definition: Increased excretion of oxalates in the urine.
exact_synonyms: Increased level of oxalate in urine

HP:0003160.label: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin
HP:0003160.definition: Glycosylated transferrin concentrations can be measured in serum as a marker of N-linked glycosylation fidelity. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II. These terms are retained for historical reasons but for new annotations the precise glycosylation defect should be recorded.
HP:0003160.comment: Human serum transferrin has two N-glycosylation sites, which are normally both fully occupied by disialylated biantennary glycans to generate tetrasialotransferrin.

HP:0003161.label: 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvic aciduria
HP:0003161.definition: Increased relative concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid in the urine.

HP:0003163.label: Elevated urinary delta-aminolevulinic acid
HP:0003163.definition: An increased concentration of 5-aminolevulinic acid (CHEBI:17549) in the urine.
HP:0003163.comment: Delta-aminolevulinic acid synthesis is a rate-controlling step in heme synthesis.

HP:0003164.label: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone deficiency
HP:0003164.definition: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) deficiency (IGD) is characterized by inappropriately low serum concentrations of the gonadotropins LH (luteinizing hormone) and FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) in the presence of low circulating concentrations of sex steroids (primarily testosterone or estradiol). GnRH is not typically assayed directly because it is released in pulses from the hypothalamus, and its concentration can fluctuate rapidly and in a complex pattern that makes single blood measurements less informative than the pituitary's response.

HP:0003165.label: Elevated circulating parathyroid hormone level
HP:0003165.definition: An abnormal increased concentration of parathyroid hormone.

HP:0003166.label: Increased urinary taurine
HP:0003166.definition: Increased concentration of taurine in the urine.

HP:0003167.label: Carnosinuria
HP:0003167.definition: An increased concentration of carnosine in the urine.
HP:0003167.comment: Carnosine is the N-(beta-alanyl) derivative of L-histidine.

HP:0003168.label: Dibasicaminoaciduria
HP:0003168.definition: An increased level of a dibasic amino acid in the urine. Dibasic amino acids are usually referred to simply as basic aminoacids because they contain basic side chains at neutral pH. These are arginine (Arg), lysine (Lys), and histidine (His).

HP:0003170.label: Abnormal acetabulum morphology
HP:0003170.definition: An abnormality of the acetabulum, i.e., the Acetabular part of hip bone, which together with the head of the femur forms the hip joint.

HP:0003172.label: Abnormal pubic bone morphology
HP:0003172.definition: An anomaly of the the pubic bone, i.e., of the ventral and anterior of the three principal components (pubis, ilium, ischium) of the hip bone.

HP:0003173.label: Hypoplastic pubic bone
HP:0003173.definition: Underdevelopment of the pubis, which together with the ilium and the ischium, is one of the three bones that make up the hip bone.

HP:0003174.label: Abnormal ischium morphology
HP:0003174.definition: An anomaly of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.
HP:0003174.comment: The ischium, together with the ilium and the pubis, forms the hip bone (os coxae).

HP:0003175.label: Hypoplastic ischia
HP:0003175.definition: Underdevelopment of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.

HP:0003177.label: Squared iliac bones
HP:0003177.definition: A shift from the normally round (convex) appearance of the iliac wing towards a square-like appearance.

HP:0003179.label: Protrusio acetabuli
HP:0003179.definition: Intrapelvic bulging of the medial acetabular wall.
HP:0003179.comment: Protrusion of the acetabulum, which is the socket that together with the head of the femur forms the hip joint. The protrusion is the result of increased depth of the socket and results in medial displacement of the femoral head.

HP:0003180.label: Flat acetabular roof
HP:0003180.definition: Flattening of the superior part of the acetabulum, which is a cup-shaped cavity at the base of the hipbone into which the ball-shaped head of the femur fits. The acetabular roof thereby appears horizontal rather than arched, as it normally does.

HP:0003183.label: Wide pubic symphysis
HP:0003183.definition: Abnormally increased width of the pubic symphysis is the midline cartilaginous joint uniting the superior rami of the left and right pubic bones.

HP:0003184.label: Decreased hip abduction
HP:0003184.definition: Reduced ability to move the femur outward to the side.

HP:0003185.label: Short greater sciatic notch
HP:0003185.definition: The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a reduction in the height of the notch.

HP:0003186.label: Inverted nipples
HP:0003186.definition: The presence of nipples that instead of pointing outward are retracted inwards.

HP:0003189.label: Long nose
HP:0003189.definition: Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased length from the nasal root to the nasal base.

HP:0003191.label: Cleft ala nasi
HP:0003191.definition: The presence of a notch in the margin of the ala nasi.
HP:0003191.comment: The alae nasi are the lateral portions of the nose or the wings of the nostrils, which partly encircle the nostrils (nares). They are usually about the width of the columella, but vary greatly depending on the shape of the nostril. Note that individuals may be described as having a cleft ala nasi, but have a severely Underdeveloped ala nasi. In an underdeveloped ala the continuity of the tissue encircling the nostril is undisturbed while in a cleft it is disrupted. The term coloboma has been replaced because a coloboma is a remnant of a physiologically occurring discontinuity of tissue; the alae nasi do not have such a discontinuity.

HP:0003193.label: Allergic rhinitis
HP:0003193.definition: It is characterized by one or more symptoms including sneezing, itching, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea.

HP:0003194.label: Short nasal bridge
HP:0003194.definition: Decreased superior-inferior length of the nasal bridge, which is the saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose.
exact_synonyms: Decreased length of bridge of nose

HP:0003196.label: Short nose
HP:0003196.definition: Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations below the mean, or alternatively, an apparently decreased length from the nasal root to the nasal tip.
HP:0003196.comment: Note: a small nose has both decreased height and a decreased width. These should be coded separately.

HP:0003198.label: Myopathy
HP:0003198.definition: A disorder of muscle unrelated to impairment of innervation or neuromuscular junction.
HP:0003198.comment: The diagnosis of myopathy is often confirmed on the basis of myopathic changes in muscle biopsy.

HP:0003200.label: Ragged-red muscle fibers
HP:0003200.definition: An abnormal appearance of muscle fibers observed on muscle biopsy. Ragged red fibers can be visualized with Gomori trichrome staining as irregular and intensely red subsarcolemmal zones, whereas the normal myofibrils are green. The margins of affect fibers appear red and ragged. The ragged-red is due to the accumulation of abnormal mitochondria below the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to the appearance of a red rim and speckled sarcoplasm.
HP:0003200.comment: This finding is demonstrated by muscle biopsy. Note that additionally, muscle fibers with mitochondrial proliferation stain darkly for succinic dehydrogenase (SDH).

HP:0003201.label: Rhabdomyolysis
HP:0003201.definition: Breakdown of muscle fibers that leads to the release of muscle fiber contents (myoglobin) into the bloodstream.

HP:0003202.label: Skeletal muscle atrophy
HP:0003202.definition: The presence of skeletal muscular atrophy (which is also known as amyotrophy).
exact_synonyms: Neurogenic muscle atrophy, especially in the lower limbs

HP:0003203.label: Decreased neutrophil oxidative burst
HP:0003203.definition: Abnormal decrease of neutrophil oxidative burst, commonly measured through oxidation of dihydrorhodamine (DHR) using flow cytometry or through nitroblue tetrazolium test (NBT) using optical microscopy, upon stimulation with phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA), E. coli or other ligands.
HP:0003203.comment: The NBT test measures the ability of neutrophils to convert nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT), to a deep blue color. This test can be abnormal in chronic granulomatous disease. An abnormal test result implies a reduction in the ability of neutrophils to kill bacteria. Polymorphonuclear neutrophils comprise more than 60% of the circulating white blood cells in humans. They have a central role in innate immunity and they regulate adaptive immunity. In healthy individuals, circulating neutrophils are freely flowing in a resting, dormant state. Upon infection, neutrophils are the first circulating cells to arrive at the infection and inflammatory site. Phagocytosis triggers the activation program of the neutrophils, leading to the intraphagosomal release of antibacterial peptides, proteases, myeloperoxidase, and superoxide anion (O2-), which is produced via the activation of the NADPH oxidase. Superoxide anion is the initiating spark leading to the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), i.e., hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), hydroxylradical and hypochlorous acid (HOCl), all contributing to the death and destruction of the bacteria within the phagosome. ROS production by the phagocytes was first referred as the respiratory burst or oxidative burst due to the rapid and cyanide-insensitive increase in oxygen uptake, increase in glucose consumption, andimmediate ROS release. The enzyme system dedicated to superoxide anion production, i.e., the phagocyte NADPH oxidase, a member of the NOX family of proteins also referred as NOX2, is composed of six proteins, two trans-membrane proteins (p22phox and gp91phox) that form theflavocytochrome b558, and four soluble proteins (p47phox,p67phox, and p40phox and the small G-proteins, Rac1/2).
exact_synonyms: Reduced reactive oxygen species production in neutrophils

HP:0003204.label: Intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0003204.definition: The intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent storage material.
HP:0003204.comment: Accumulation of intracellular autofluorescent material or aging pigment has been characterized as a normal aging event. Lipofuscin (from the Greek word for fat and the Latin word for dark), refers to intracellular autofluorescent material that accumulates in aging cells with a excitation wavelength between 320 and 480 nm and an emission wavelength between 460 and 630 nm. Lpofuscin consists of a mixture of oxidized proteins and lipids, carbohydrates and trace amount of metals. Ceroid iss a lipofuscin-like lipopigment that arises from pathological conditions such as disease, malnutrition, and cell stress. Subunit c of mitochondrial ATP synthase makes up approximately 40% of this lipopigment/ceroid accumulation.

HP:0003205.label: Curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0003205.definition: An intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material in a curved pattern.
exact_synonyms: Intracellular curvilinear profiles on ultrastructural analysis

HP:0003207.label: Arterial calcification
HP:0003207.definition: Pathological deposition of calcium salts in one or more arteries.
HP:0003207.comment: Most individuals aged over 60 years have progressively enlarging deposits of calcium mineral in their major arteries. This vascular calcification reduces aortic and arterial elastance, which impairs cardiovascular hemodynamics, resulting in substantial morbidity and mortality in the form of hypertension, aortic stenosis, cardiac hypertrophy, myocardial and lower-limb ischemia, congestive heart failure, and compromised structural integrity.The severity and extent of mineralization reflect atherosclerotic plaque burden and strongly and independently predict cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. (From PMID:18519861).

HP:0003208.label: Fingerprint intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0003208.definition: An intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material in a trabecular or fingerprint-like pattern.

HP:0003209.label: Decreased pyruvate carboxylase activity
HP:0003209.definition: A decreased rate of pyruvate carboxylase activity.
HP:0003209.comment: Pyruvate carboxylase (EC 6.4.1.1) is a nuclear-encoded mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate, a precursor for the citric acid cycle.

HP:0003210.label: Decreased methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity
HP:0003210.definition: An abnormality of Krebs cycle metabolism that is characterized by a decreased rate of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity.
HP:0003210.comment: The product of the enzyme, succinyl-CoA, is a key molecule of the TCA (Krebs) cycle. The substrate of the enzyme, methylmalonyl-CoA, is primarily derived from propionyl-CoA, a substance formed from the catabolism of isoleucine, valine, threonine, methionine, thymine, uracil, cholesterol, or odd-chain fatty acids.

HP:0003212.label: Increased circulating IgE concentration
HP:0003212.definition: An abnormally increased overall level of immunoglobulin E in blood.

HP:0003213.label: Deficient excision of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers in DNA

HP:0003214.label: Prolonged G2 phase of cell cycle

HP:0003215.label: Dicarboxylic aciduria
HP:0003215.definition: An increased concentration of dicarboxylic acid in the urine.
HP:0003215.comment: A dicarboxylic acid is an oxoacid containing two carboxy groups. Dicarboxylic aciduria occurs during increased mobilization or inhibited beta-oxidation of fatty acids, where a number of 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids are excreted in the urine.

HP:0003216.label: Generalized amyloid deposition
HP:0003216.comment: According to MeSH (D000682), Amyloid is fibrous protein complex that consists of proteins folded into a specific cross beta-pleated sheet structure. This fibrillar structure has been found as an alternative folding pattern for a variety of functional proteins. Deposits of amyloid in the form of amyloid plaques are associated with a variety of degenerative diseases. The amyloid structure has also been found in a number of functional proteins that are unrelated to disease.

HP:0003217.label: Hyperglutaminemia
HP:0003217.definition: An increased concentration of glutamine in the blood.
HP:0003217.comment: Normal glutamine blood levels are around 550-600 micromole per liter.

HP:0003218.label: Oroticaciduria
HP:0003218.definition: An increased concentration of orotic acid in the urine.
HP:0003218.comment: Orotic acid is an intermediate in the biosynthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides. Some enzymatic deficiencies can cause the excretion of a large amount of orotic acid in the urine and a defect in pyrimidine biosynthesis.

HP:0003219.label: Ethylmalonic aciduria
HP:0003219.definition: The concentration of ethylmalonic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0003219.comment: Ethylmalonic acid is a dicarboxylic acid obtained by substitution of one of the methylene hydrogens of malonic acid by an ethyl group.

HP:0003220.label: Abnormality of chromosome stability
HP:0003220.definition: A type of chromosomal aberration characterized by reduced resistance of chromosomes to change or deterioration.

HP:0003221.label: Chromosomal breakage induced by crosslinking agents
HP:0003221.definition: Increased amount of chromosomal breaks in cultured blood lymphocytes or other cells induced by treatment with DNA cross-linking agents such as diepoxybutane and mitomycin C.
HP:0003221.comment: Increased tendency to chromosomal breakage induced by crosslinking agents is typical for the various forms of Fanconi anemia.
exact_synonyms: Chromosomal breakage induced by mitomycin C

HP:0003223.label: Decreased circulating methylcobalamin concentration
HP:0003223.definition: The concentration of methylcobalamin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12.

HP:0003224.label: Increased cellular sensitivity to UV light

HP:0003225.label: Reduced coagulation factor V activity
HP:0003225.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor V.
HP:0003225.comment: Factor V is activated to factor Va by means of minute amounts of thrombin (and inactivated by larger amounts of thrombin). Activated factor V (fVa) is a cofactor in the formation of the prothrombinase complex.

HP:0003226.label: Rectilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0003226.definition: An intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material in a straight or rectilinear pattern.

HP:0003228.label: Hypernatremia
HP:0003228.definition: An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the blood.

HP:0003231.label: Hypertyrosinemia
HP:0003231.definition: An increased concentration of tyrosine in the blood.

HP:0003233.label: Decreased HDL cholesterol concentration
HP:0003233.definition: An decreased concentration of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0003234.label: Decreased circulating carnitine concentration
HP:0003234.definition: Concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
HP:0003234.comment: Carnitine is responsible for the transport of fatty acids from the cytosol into the mitochondria.

HP:0003235.label: Hypermethioninemia
HP:0003235.definition: An increased concentration of methionine in the blood.
HP:0003235.comment: Elevated blood methionine levels in the range of 500-2000 micromolar.

HP:0003236.label: Elevated circulating creatine kinase concentration
HP:0003236.definition: An elevation of the level of the enzyme creatine kinase (also known as creatine phosphokinase (CK; EC 2.7.3.2) in the blood. CK levels can be elevated in a number of clinical disorders such as myocardial infarction, rhabdomyolysis, and muscular dystrophy.
HP:0003236.comment: Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) activity is usually an indicator of muscle damage. Diseases with very high CK values include subtypes of muscular dystrophies, idiopathic inflammatory myopathies and metabolic myopathies. However, a normal or only slightly elevated CK value does not exclude the presence of a myopathy. The normal range in the blood circulation is 34-171 U/l in males and 34-145 U/l in females, but may vary according to the test used.

HP:0003237.label: Increased circulating IgG concentration
HP:0003237.definition: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin G in blood.

HP:0003238.label: Hyperpepsinogenemia I
HP:0003238.definition: The concentration of pepsinogen I in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0003239.label: Phosphoethanolaminuria
HP:0003239.definition: An increased level of phosphoethanolamine (synonym: O-phosphoethanolamine) in the urine.
exact_synonyms: Increased level of O-phosphoethanolamine in urine

HP:0003240.label: Increased phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
HP:0003240.definition: Abnormally elevated level of the enzyme phosphoribosyl pyrophosphatesynthetase, which catalyzes the synthesis of PP-ribose-P from ATP and ribose-5-phosphate.

HP:0003241.label: External genital hypoplasia
HP:0003241.definition: Underdevelopment of part or all of the external reproductive organs.
HP:0003241.comment: Partial or complete failure of the genitalia to develop, often as a consequence of hypogonadism.

HP:0003244.label: Penile hypospadias
HP:0003244.definition: Location of the urethral opening on the inferior aspect of the penis.

HP:0003246.label: Prominent scrotal raphe
HP:0003246.definition: Increased size of the ridge of tissue that extends along the midline of the scrotum.

HP:0003248.label: Gonadal tissue inappropriate for external genitalia or chromosomal sex

HP:0003254.label: Abnormality of DNA repair
HP:0003254.definition: An abnormality of the process of DNA repair, that is, of the process of restoring DNA after damage.

HP:0003256.label: Abnormality of the coagulation cascade
HP:0003256.definition: An abnormality of the coagulation cascade, which is comprised of the contact activation pathway (also known as the intrinsic pathway) and the tissue factor pathway (also known as the extrinsic pathway) as well as cofactors and regulators.

HP:0003259.label: Elevated circulating creatinine concentration
HP:0003259.definition: An increased amount of creatinine in the blood.

HP:0003260.label: Hydroxyprolinemia
HP:0003260.definition: An increased concentration of hydroxyproline in the blood.
HP:0003260.comment: Hydroxyproline is an imino acid normally present in human plasma and is derived primarily from endogenous collagen turnover and the breakdown of dietary collagen. Hyperhydroxyprolinemic patients show hydroxyproline blood levels between 150 and 500 micromole per liter. Normal levels are around 10-20 micromole per liter.

HP:0003261.label: Increased circulating IgA concentration
HP:0003261.definition: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin A in blood.

HP:0003262.label: Anti-smooth muscle antibody positivity
HP:0003262.definition: The presence in serum of antibodies against smooth muscle.
HP:0003262.comment: Anti smooth muscle antibody (SMA) may be present in a number of conditions including chronic active hepatitis, autoimmune hepatitis, cirrhosis, and infectious mononucleosis.

HP:0003264.label: Deficiency of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase
HP:0003264.comment: N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase catalyzes the initial step in the synthesis of the mannose 6-phosphate determinant required for efficient intracellular targeting of newly synthesized lysosomal hydrolases to the lysosome.

HP:0003265.label: Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia
HP:0003265.definition: A type of hyperbilirubinemia with neonatal onset.
exact_synonyms: High blood bilirubin levels in neonate

HP:0003267.label: Reduced orotidine 5-prime phosphate decarboxylase level
HP:0003267.definition: An abnormal decrease in orotidine 5'-phosphate decarboxylase level.
HP:0003267.comment: The enzyme orotidine-5-prime-phosphate decarboxylase (EC 4.1.1.23) catalyzes the reaction H(+) + orotidine 5'-phosphate = CO(2) + UMP (uridine monophosphate). The enzyme is thusinvolved in pyrimidine biosynthesis.

HP:0003268.label: Argininuria
HP:0003268.definition: A increased concentration of arginine in the urine.
HP:0003268.comment: Normal urinary arginine total (free and combined form) excretion is around 30 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0003270.label: Abdominal distention
HP:0003270.comment: Abdominal distention can be a secondary feature associated with a number of conditions such as bowel obstruction.

HP:0003271.label: Visceromegaly
HP:0003271.definition: Abnormal increased size of the viscera of the abdomen.
HP:0003271.comment: Visceromegaly is enlargement of the internal organs in the abdomen, including liver, spleen, stomach, kidneys, or pancreas.

HP:0003272.label: Abnormal hip bone morphology
HP:0003272.definition: An abnormality of the hip bone.
HP:0003272.comment: The hip region comprises the vasculature of hip, skin of hip, superficial fascia of hip, the hip bone, hip joint, and musculature of hip. The hip is part of the pelvic girdle.

HP:0003273.label: Hip contracture
HP:0003273.definition: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the hip joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

HP:0003275.label: Narrow pelvis bone
HP:0003275.definition: Reduced side to side width of the pelvis.

HP:0003276.label: Pelvic bone exostoses
HP:0003276.definition: A benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface of the pelvis. Exostoses are capped by cartilage, and arise from a bone that develops from cartilage.

HP:0003278.label: Square pelvis bone
HP:0003278.definition: An abnormally squared appearance of the bony pelvis, a normally rounded or basin-shaped structure.

HP:0003279.label: Coxa magna
HP:0003279.definition: Widening of the femoral head and neck.
HP:0003279.comment: Coxa magna can occur as a result of developmental dysplasia of the hip, Perthes disease, septic arthritis, Kniest dysplasia, among others.

HP:0003281.label: Increased circulating ferritin concentration
HP:0003281.definition: Increased concentration of ferritin in the blood circulation.
HP:0003281.comment: Ferritin is a ubiquitous intracellular protein that stores iron. Ferritin levels measured in serum usually have a direct correlation with the total amount of iron stored in the body, but ferritin levels may also be increased with anemia of chronic disease or in the course of an acute phase reaction.

HP:0003282.label: Decreased circulating alkaline phosphatase activity
HP:0003282.definition: Concentration or activity of alkaline phosphatase outside the upper or lower limtis of normal in the blood circulation.

HP:0003286.label: Cystathioninemia
HP:0003286.definition: An increased concentration of cystathionine in the blood.
HP:0003286.comment: Cystathionine can be directly interconverted to cysteine. Cystathionine is not normally detectable in plasma.

HP:0003292.label: Decreased serum leptin
HP:0003292.definition: A decreased concentration of leptin in the blood.
HP:0003292.comment: Leptin is an adipocyte-secreted hormone with a key role in energy homeostasis.

HP:0003295.label: obsolete Impaired FSH and LH secretion

HP:0003296.label: Hyperthreoninuria
HP:0003296.definition: An increased concentration of threonine in the urine.
HP:0003296.comment: Normal urinary threonine total (free and combined form) excretion is around 50 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0003297.label: Hyperlysinuria
HP:0003297.definition: An increased concentration of lysine in the urine.
HP:0003297.comment: Normal urinary lysine total (free and combined form) excretion is around 80 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0003298.label: Spina bifida occulta
HP:0003298.definition: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of a vertebral body with intact overlying skin.

HP:0003300.label: Ovoid vertebral bodies
HP:0003300.definition: When viewed in lateral radiographs, vertebral bodies have a roughly rectangular configuration. This term applies if the vertebral body appears rounded or oval.

HP:0003301.label: Irregular vertebral endplates
HP:0003301.definition: An irregular surface of the vertebral end plates, which are normally relatively smooth.

HP:0003302.label: Spondylolisthesis
HP:0003302.definition: Complete bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis resulting in the anterior slippage of the vertebra.
exact_synonyms: Displacement of one backbone compared to another

HP:0003304.label: Spondylolysis
HP:0003304.definition: Spondylolysis is an osseous defect of the pars interarticularis, thought to be a developmental or acquired stress fracture secondary to chronic low-grade trauma.
HP:0003304.comment: The pars interarticularis is one of the bony bridges that connect the upper with the lower facet joints of the vertebra. Lumbar spondylolysis is a common cause of lower back pain. The vast majority of cases of spondylolysis occur at the L5 or L4 levels, and is usually diagnosed radiographically. Over half of patients affected by spondylolysis have associated spondylolisthesis.

HP:0003305.label: Block vertebrae
HP:0003305.definition: Congenital synostosis between two or more adjacent vertebrae (partial or complete fusion of adjacent vertabral bodies).

HP:0003306.label: Spinal rigidity
HP:0003306.definition: Reduced ability to move the vertebral column with a resulting limitation of neck and trunk flexion.

HP:0003307.label: Hyperlordosis
HP:0003307.definition: Abnormally increased curvature (anterior concavity) of the lumbar or cervical spine.

HP:0003308.label: Cervical subluxation
HP:0003308.definition: A partial dislocation of one or more intervertebral joints in the cervical vertebral column.

HP:0003310.label: Abnormal odontoid process morphology
HP:0003310.definition: Abnormal structure of the odontoid process, which is a part of the C2 or axis vertebra and forms pivot of the structures forming the craniovertebral junction. The odontoid process is also known as the dens of the axis.
HP:0003310.comment: The dens of the axis is a protuberance of the C2 vertebral body around which the first vertebra rotates.

HP:0003311.label: Hypoplasia of the odontoid process
HP:0003311.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the dens of the axis.

HP:0003312.label: Abnormal form of the vertebral bodies

HP:0003316.label: Butterfly vertebrae
HP:0003316.definition: A butterfly vertebra (sagittal cleft vertebra or anterior rachischisis) is a sagittal defect in the vertebral body caused by failure of fusion of the two lateral chondrification centers during embryogenesis. The name is based on the appearance of the two hemivertebrae emerging as butterfly wings from the central cleft on x-ray.

HP:0003319.label: Abnormality of the cervical spine
HP:0003319.definition: Any abnormality of the cervical vertebral column.

HP:0003320.label: C1-C2 subluxation
HP:0003320.definition: A partial dislocation of the atlantoaxial joints.
HP:0003320.comment: A subluxation affecting the intervertebral joint between the first and second cervical vertebrae.

HP:0003324.label: Generalized muscle weakness
HP:0003324.definition: Generalized weakness or decreased strength of the muscles, affecting both distal and proximal musculature.

HP:0003325.label: Limb-girdle muscle weakness
HP:0003325.definition: Weakness of the limb-girdle muscles (also known as the pelvic and shoulder girdles), that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders and the pelvis.

HP:0003327.label: Axial muscle weakness
HP:0003327.definition: Reduced strength of the axial musculature (i.e., of the muscles of the head and neck, spine, and ribs).

HP:0003328.label: Abnormal hairshaft morphology
HP:0003328.definition: An abnormal structure of the hairshaft, i.e., of the nongrowing portion of a hair that protrudes from the skin.

HP:0003329.label: Hair shafts flattened at irregular intervals and twisted through 180 degrees about their axes

HP:0003330.label: Abnormal bone structure
HP:0003330.definition: Any anomaly in the composite material or the layered arrangement of the bony skeleton.

HP:0003333.label: Increased serum beta-hexosaminidase
HP:0003333.comment: This enzyme removes a beta-1,4-linked N-acetylhexosamine residue from the GM2 ganglioside.

HP:0003334.label: Elevated circulating catecholamine level
HP:0003334.definition: An abnormal increase in catecholamine concentration in the blood.
HP:0003334.comment: Elevated circulating catecholamine level is a common feature in patients with pheochromocytoma.

HP:0003336.label: Abnormal enchondral ossification
HP:0003336.definition: An abnormality of the process of endochondral ossification, which is a type of replacement ossification in which bone tissue replaces cartilage.
HP:0003336.comment: This term is intended to describe histological abnormalities of enchondral ossification observed upon bone biopsy.

HP:0003337.label: Reduced prothrombin consumption
HP:0003337.definition: The prothrombin consumption test measures the formation of intrinsic thromboplastin by determining the residual serum prothrombin after blood clotting is complete. If there is a defect in the process, less prothrombin will be converted to thrombin than normal (less prothrombin is consumed). This test may be abnormal with conditions including deficiency of factors VIII or IX, with circulating anticoagulants, thrombocytopenia.

HP:0003338.label: Focal necrosis of right ventricular muscle cells

HP:0003339.label: Pyrimidine-responsive megaloblastic anemia
HP:0003339.definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia that improves upon administration of pyrimidine supplements such as uridylic acid and cytidylic acid.
exact_synonyms: Anaemia corrected by uridylic acid and cytidylic acid
Anemia corrected by uridylic acid and cytidylic acid

HP:0003341.label: Lamina lucida cleavage
HP:0003341.definition: The formation of bullae (blisters) with cleavage in the lamina lucida layer of the skin.
HP:0003341.comment: Cleavage within the lamina lucida is observed in junctional epidermolysis bullosa.
exact_synonyms: Subepidermal blistering with cleavage in the lamina lucida

HP:0003343.label: Reduced glutathione synthetase level
HP:0003343.definition: Reduced level of the enzyme glutathione synthetase, which catalyzes the last step in the synthesis of glutathione and a deficiency results in low levels of glutathione. Acidosis is due to reduced feedback inhibition of gamma-glutamyl cysteine synthetase in the gamma-glutamyl cycle, which ultimately leads to overproduction and accumulation of 5-oxoproline.

HP:0003344.label: 3-Methylglutaric aciduria
HP:0003344.definition: An abnormally increased level of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid in the urine.

HP:0003345.label: Elevated urinary norepinephrine level
HP:0003345.definition: The concentration of noradrenaline in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0003347.label: Impaired lymphocyte transformation with phytohemagglutinin
HP:0003347.definition: Normal peripheral blood lymphocytes, when stimulated by phytohemagglutinin (PHA) are cytotoxic for homologous and heterologous cells but not for autologous cells in monolayer culture. The cytotoxic effect is thought to be indicative of the immunological competence of the lymphocytes.
HP:0003347.comment: The response of lymphocytes to PHA is measured by their ability to transform and to undergo mitosis.

HP:0003348.label: Hyperalaninemia
HP:0003348.definition: An increased concentration of alanine in the blood.
HP:0003348.comment: This class referring to the clinical feature Hyperalaninemia and not to the disease entry. Normal alanine blood levels are around 350-400 micromole per liter.

HP:0003349.label: Low cholesterol esterification rate
HP:0003349.definition: A reduction in the rate of cholesterol esterification.
HP:0003349.comment: Cholesterol esterification converts free cholesterol to cholesteryl esters between the carboxylate group of a fatty acid and the hydroxyl group of cholesterol. Esterification allows more cholesterol to be packaged into the interior of lipoproteins. Cholesterol esterification rates can be measured in skin fibroblasts using for instance a non-lipoprotein [3H]cholesterol source.

HP:0003351.label: Decreased circulating renin concentration
HP:0003351.definition: An decreased level of renin in the blood.

HP:0003352.label: Endopolyploidy on chromosome studies of bone marrow
HP:0003352.definition: An increase in the number of chromosome sets per cell in bone marrow cells.
HP:0003352.comment: Endopolyploidy is caused by replication without cell division.

HP:0003353.label: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency
HP:0003353.definition: An abnormality of amino acid metabolism characterized by a decreased level of propionyl-CoA carboxylase.
HP:0003353.comment: Propionyl-CoA is an important intermediate in the metabolism of several amino acids and is also produced by oxidation of odd-numbered fatty acids.

HP:0003354.label: Hyperthreoninemia
HP:0003354.definition: An increased concentration of threonine in the blood.

HP:0003355.label: Aminoaciduria
HP:0003355.definition: An increased concentration of an amino acid in the urine.
exact_synonyms: Increased levels of animo acids in urine

HP:0003357.label: Thymic hormone decreased
HP:0003357.definition: A reduction in the level of thymic horomone.

HP:0003358.label: Elevated intracellular cystine
HP:0003358.definition: An increased concentration of cystine within cells. This finding can be demonstrated on leukocytes, but is not specific to blood cells.
HP:0003358.comment: Cystine is a dimeric amino acid formed by the oxidation of two cysteine residues to form a disulfide bond.

HP:0003359.label: Decreased urinary sulfate
HP:0003359.definition: Decreased concentration of sulfate in the urine.

HP:0003361.label: Tryptophanuria
HP:0003361.definition: An increased concentration of tryptophan in the urine.
HP:0003361.comment: Normal urinary tryptophan total (free and combined form) excretion is around 40 mg per 24 hours.

HP:0003362.label: Increased VLDL cholesterol concentration
HP:0003362.definition: An increase in the amount of very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0003363.label: Abdominal situs inversus
HP:0003363.definition: A left-right reversal (or mirror reflection) of the anatomical location of the viscera of the abdomen.

HP:0003366.label: Abnormal femoral neck/head morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormal neck or head of thigh bone
Abnormality of the femoral neck or head region

HP:0003367.label: Abnormal femoral neck morphology
HP:0003367.definition: An abnormality of the femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

HP:0003368.label: Abnormal femoral head morphology
HP:0003368.definition: An abnormality of the femoral head.

HP:0003370.label: Flat capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0003370.definition: An abnormal flattening of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Flat end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0003371.label: Enlargement of the proximal femoral epiphysis
HP:0003371.definition: An abnormal enlargement of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0003375.label: Narrow greater sciatic notch
HP:0003375.definition: A narrowing of the sacrosciatic notch, i.e., the deep indentation in the posterior border of the hip bone at the point of union of the ilium and ischium.
HP:0003375.comment: The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a reduction in the lateral dimension of the notch.

HP:0003376.label: Steppage gait
HP:0003376.definition: An abnormal gait pattern that arises from weakness of the pretibial and peroneal muscles due to a lower motor neuron lesion. Affected patients have footdrop and are unable to dorsiflex and evert the foot. The leg is lifted high on walking so that the toes clear the ground, and there may be a slapping noise when the foot strikes the ground again.

HP:0003378.label: Axonal degeneration/regeneration
HP:0003378.definition: A pattern of simultaneous degeneration and regeneration of axons (see comment).
HP:0003378.comment: This finding is typically demonstrated by nerve biopsy. Following focal damage to an axon, the part of the axon that is distal to the lesion invariably degenerates, a process that is known as anterograde (or Wallerian) degeneration. During Wallerian degeneration, often a microenvironment is created that can allow successful regrowth of nerve fibers from the proximal nerve segment.

HP:0003380.label: Decreased number of peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
HP:0003380.definition: A loss of myelinated nerve fibers in the peripheral nervous system (in general, this finding can be observed on nerve biopsy).
HP:0003380.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by nerve biopsy.
exact_synonyms: Decreased number of large and small myelinated fibers
Decreased number of peripheral myelinated nerve fibres
Decreased number of large and small myelinated fibres

HP:0003383.label: Onion bulb formation
HP:0003383.definition: Repeated episodes of segmental demyelination and remyelination lead to the accumulation of supernumerary Schwann cells around axons, which is referred to as onion bulb formation. This finding affects peripheral nerves.
HP:0003383.comment: This feature is characteristic of chronic demyelinating neuropathies as well as certain hereditary neuropathies. Onion-bulb formation may be observed in electron microscopic examinations of peripheral nerve biopsy material. Often, this examination is performed on the sural nerve.

HP:0003384.label: Peripheral axonal atrophy
HP:0003384.definition: Atrophic changes of axons of the peripheral nervous system.
HP:0003384.comment: This finding is typically demonstrated by nerve biopsy.

HP:0003387.label: Decreased number of large peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
HP:0003387.definition: A reduced number of large myelinated nerve fibers.
HP:0003387.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by nerve biopsy.
exact_synonyms: Decreased number of large peripheral myelinated nerve fibres
Loss of larger myelinated nerve fibers
Loss of larger myelinated nerve fibres

HP:0003388.label: Easy fatigability
HP:0003388.comment: Fatigue describes the inability to continue performing a task after multiple repetitions.

HP:0003390.label: Sensory axonal neuropathy
HP:0003390.definition: An axonal neuropathy of peripheral sensory nerves.

HP:0003391.label: Gowers sign
HP:0003391.definition: A phenomenon whereby patients are not able to stand up without the use of the hands owing to weakness of the proximal muscles of the lower limbs.

HP:0003393.label: Thenar muscle atrophy
HP:0003393.definition: Wasting of thenar muscles, which are located on palm of the hand at the base of the thumb.

HP:0003394.label: Muscle spasm
HP:0003394.definition: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles.

HP:0003396.label: Syringomyelia
HP:0003396.definition: Dilated, glial-lined cavity in spinal cord. This cavity does not communicate with the central canal, and usually is between the dorsal columns unilaterally or bilaterally along the side of the cord.

HP:0003397.label: Generalized hypotonia due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
exact_synonyms: Generalised hypotonia due to defect at the neuromuscular junction

HP:0003398.label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction
HP:0003398.definition: Any abnormality of the neuromuscular junction, which is the synapse between the motor end plate of a motor neuron and the skeletal muscle fibers.

HP:0003400.label: Basal lamina onion bulb formation
HP:0003400.definition: A type of onion bulb formation prominently affecting the area of the basal lamina.
exact_synonyms: Basal lamina 'onion bulb' formations on nerve biopsy

HP:0003401.label: Paresthesia
HP:0003401.definition: Abnormal sensations such as tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin with no apparent physical cause.

HP:0003402.label: Decreased miniature endplate potentials
HP:0003402.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amplitude of the miniature endplate potentials, i.e. the postsynaptic response to transmitter released from an individual vesicle at the neuromuscular junction.
HP:0003402.comment: Miniature end plate potentials are the small (about 0.5mV) depolarisations of the postsynaptic terminal caused by the release of a single vesicle into the synaptic cleft.

HP:0003403.label: EMG: decremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation
HP:0003403.definition: A compound muscle action potential (CMAP) is a type of electromyography (EMG). CMAP refers to a group of almost simultaneous action potentials from several muscle fibers in the same area evoked by stimulation of the supplying motor nerve and are recorded as one multipeaked summated action potential. This abnormality refers to a greater than normal decrease in the amplitude during the course of the investigation.
HP:0003403.comment: The result of this test is abnormal if progressively fewer muscle fibers respond to nerve stimulation during a train of stimuli, thereby yielding a decrementing pattern in the CMAP.
exact_synonyms: EMG: decremental response of CMAP to repetitive nerve stimulation

HP:0003409.label: Distal sensory impairment of all modalities
HP:0003409.definition: Reduced ability to sense pain, temperature, touch, vibration stimuli in the distal regions of the extremities.
exact_synonyms: Distal sensory loss to all modalities

HP:0003411.label: Proximal femoral metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0003411.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the proximal metaphysis of the femur.

HP:0003413.label: Atlantoaxial abnormality
HP:0003413.definition: An anomaly of the atlantoaxial joint, i.e., of the joint between the first (atlas) and second (axis) cervical vertebrae.

HP:0003414.label: Atlantoaxial dislocation
HP:0003414.definition: Partial dislocation of the atlantoaxial joint.

HP:0003416.label: Spinal canal stenosis
HP:0003416.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal.
HP:0003416.comment: Stenosis of the spinal canal can result in neurological symptoms because of compression of the spinal cord or spinal nerve roots, depending on the location of the stenosis in the vertebral column.

HP:0003417.label: Coronal cleft vertebrae
HP:0003417.definition: Frontal schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.
HP:0003417.comment: Coronal cleft vertebrae result when there are two, instead of one, primary ossification centers in a vertebral body. An unossified cartilaginous brdige may be observed radiographically with the shape of a cleft. If the two ossification centers are ventral/dorsal, a coronal cleft is observed, and if the two ossification centers are left/right, than a sagittal cleft is observed.

HP:0003418.label: Back pain
HP:0003418.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back.

HP:0003419.label: Low back pain
HP:0003419.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the lower back.

HP:0003422.label: Vertebral segmentation defect
HP:0003422.definition: An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation during development.
HP:0003422.comment: The vertebral column derives from somites, transient paired segments of mesoderm that surround the neural tube in the early embryo. The formation of the vertebrar involves many processes including resegmentation of the rostral and caudal regions of adjacent somites that then fuse to form vertebral elements. Disruption of these processes can a cause of severe segmentation defects of the vetebrae. The frequency of segmentation defects of the vetebra has been estimated at 0.5 of 1000 births. The range of segmentation defects includes left-right uneven formation of somites that results in hemivertebrae or wedge vertebrae. Incomplete segmentation can result in fused segments such as block vertebrae. A failure of the process of resegmentation and migration of the sclerotomal compartment can result in a failure of midline fusion, such as butterfly vertebrae.

HP:0003429.label: CNS hypomyelination
HP:0003429.definition: Reduced amount of myelin in the central nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis.

HP:0003431.label: Decreased motor nerve conduction velocity
