HP:0003431.definition: A type of decreased nerve conduction velocity that affects the motor neuron.
HP:0003431.comment: Newborn infants have values that are approximately half that of adults, and adult values are normally reached by age 3 or 4. Motor nerve conduction is evaluated by recording the compound muscle action potential (CMAP) associated with a mechanical contraction of a given muscle in response to electrical stimulation of the motor nerve fibers supplying that muscle. The CMAP is the sum of all the action potentials occurring individually in the contracting muscle fibers.

HP:0003436.label: Prolonged miniature endplate currents
HP:0003436.definition: An abnormal prolongation of the miniature endplate potentials, i.e. the postsynaptic response to transmitter released from an individual vesicle at the neuromuscular junction.

HP:0003438.label: Absent Achilles reflex
HP:0003438.definition: Absence of the Achilles reflex (also known as the ankle jerk reflex), which can normally be elicited by tapping the tendon is tapped while the foot is dorsiflexed.

HP:0003443.label: Decreased size of nerve terminals
HP:0003443.definition: A reduction in the size of nerve terminals.
HP:0003443.comment: Nerve terminals are the output region of nerves located presynaptically and (in the case of chemical synapses) containing vesicles of chemical neurotransmitters. Presynaptic nerve terminals normally are larger in diameter than the axon and have the appearance of a bud. This feature can be demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0003444.label: EMG: chronic denervation signs
HP:0003444.definition: Evidence of chronic denervation on electromyography.
HP:0003444.comment: This is a bundled term that is kept for convenience. It is preferable to annotate the precise clinical abnormalities observed.

HP:0003445.label: EMG: neuropathic changes
HP:0003445.definition: The presence of characteristic findings of denervation on electromyography (fibrillations, positive sharp waves, and giant motor unit potentials).
HP:0003445.comment: This is a bundled term. It is preferable to annotate the precise clinical observations, but the term is kept now for convenience.

HP:0003447.label: Axonal loss
HP:0003447.definition: A reduction in the number of axons in the peripheral nervous system.
HP:0003447.comment: This finding can be observed upon nerve biopsy.

HP:0003448.label: Decreased sensory nerve conduction velocity
HP:0003448.definition: Reduced speed of conduction of the action potential along a sensory nerve.
HP:0003448.comment: The sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) in response to electrical stimulation is recorded from the nerve itself by means of dermal recording electrodes. The SNAP is the sum of all the action potentials generated in sensory nerve fibers by the applied electrical impulse.

HP:0003449.label: Cold-induced muscle cramps
HP:0003449.definition: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles brought on by exposure to cold temperatures.

HP:0003450.label: Axonal regeneration
HP:0003450.definition: The presence of axonal regeneration following a previous axonal lesion.
HP:0003450.comment: This finding is typically demonstrated by nerve biopsy. See the comment of term HP:0003378 for further information.

HP:0003451.label: Increased rate of premature chromosome condensation
HP:0003451.definition: An increased rate of premature chromosome condensation.

HP:0003452.label: Increased circulating iron concentration
HP:0003452.definition: The concentration of iron in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0003453.label: Antineutrophil antibody positivity
HP:0003453.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against neutrophils.
HP:0003453.comment: Circulating serum antibodies are measured by flow cytometry after incubation with normal neutrophils. Values greater than 2 standard deviations of a normal control population are interpreted as weakly positive and greater than 3 standard deviations as positive.

HP:0003454.label: Platelet antibody positive
HP:0003454.definition: The presence in the serum of autoantibodies directed against thrombocytes.

HP:0003455.label: Elevated circulating long chain fatty acid concentration
HP:0003455.definition: Increased concentration of long-chain fatty acids in the blood circulation.
HP:0003455.comment: This feature can be measured in plasma, as well as in cultured fibroblasts of amniocytes.

HP:0003456.label: Low urinary cyclic AMP response to PTH administration

HP:0003457.label: EMG abnormality
HP:0003457.definition: Abnormal results of investigations using electromyography (EMG).

HP:0003458.label: EMG: myopathic abnormalities
HP:0003458.definition: The presence of abnormal electromyographic patterns indicative of myopathy, such as small-short polyphasic motor unit potentials.

HP:0003459.label: Polyclonal elevation of IgM
HP:0003459.definition: A heterogeneous increase in IgM immunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.

HP:0003460.label: Decreased circulating total IgA
HP:0003460.definition: Undetectable serum immunoglobulin A level at a value < 5 mg/dL (0.05 g/L).

HP:0003461.label: Increased urinary O-linked sialopeptides
HP:0003461.definition: Excretion of peptides conjugated to sialic acid in the urine.

HP:0003463.label: Increased extraneuronal autofluorescent lipopigment
HP:0003463.definition: Lipofuscin, a generic term applied to autofluorescent lipopigment, is a mixture of protein and lipid that accumulates in most aging cells, particularly those involved in high lipid turnover (e.g., the adrenal medulla) or phagocytosis of other cell types (e g., the retinal pigment epithelium or RPE; macrophage). This term pertains if there is an increase in the extraneuronal accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.

HP:0003466.label: Paradoxical increased cortisol secretion on dexamethasone suppression test

HP:0003467.label: Atlantoaxial instability
HP:0003467.definition: Abnormally increased movement at the junction between the first cervical (atlas) and the second cervical (axis) vertebrae as a result of either a bony or ligamentous anomaly.
HP:0003467.comment: Neurological deficits ensue if the odontoid process, or posterior arch of the atlas, impinges on the spinal cord.

HP:0003468.label: Abnormal vertebral morphology
HP:0003468.definition: An abnormality of one or more of the vertebrae.
HP:0003468.comment: A vertebra is one of 33 bony segments that form the spinal column of humans. There are 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 4 coccygeal vertebrae (the coccygeal vertebrae are fused into one coccyx bone).

HP:0003469.label: Peripheral dysmyelination
HP:0003469.definition: Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths. Dysmyelination is distinguished from demyleination where there is destruction or damage of previously normal myelination.

HP:0003470.label: Paralysis
HP:0003470.definition: Paralysis of voluntary muscles means loss of contraction due to interruption of one or more motor pathways from the brain to the muscle fibers. Although the word paralysis is often used interchangeably to mean either complete or partial loss of muscle strength, it is preferable to use paralysis or plegia for complete or severe loss of muscle strength, and paresis for partial or slight loss. Motor paralysis results from deficits of the upper motor neurons (corticospinal, corticobulbar, or subcorticospinal). Motor paralysis is often accompanied by an impairment in the facility of movement.

HP:0003472.label: Hypocalcemic tetany
HP:0003472.definition: Hyperexcitability of the neuromuscular system related to abnormally low level of calcium in the blood, resulting in carpopedal or generalized spasms.

HP:0003473.label: Fatigable weakness
HP:0003473.definition: A type of weakness that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.
HP:0003473.comment: This type of weakness is pathognomonic for an abnormality of the neuromuscular junction such as myasthenia gravis. A characteristic form of muscular weakness that worsens after use of affected muscles. Myasthenia is caused by failure of neuromuscular transmission, which results from the binding of autoantibodies to proteins involved in signaling at the neuromuscular junction, including especially the nicotinic acetyl choline receptor (AChR) or, less frequently, a muscle-specific tyrosine kinase involved in AChR clustering.
exact_synonyms: Generalized muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
Proximal muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
Generalised muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction

HP:0003474.label: Somatic sensory dysfunction
HP:0003474.definition: An abnormality of the primary sensation that is mediated by peripheral nerves (pain, temperature, touch, vibration, joint position). The word hypoesthesia (or hypesthesia) refers to a reduction in cutaneous sensation to a specific type of testing.
HP:0003474.comment: This term does not include abnormalities of cortical sensation such as two-point discrimination, stereognosis, and graphesthesia.

HP:0003477.label: Peripheral axonal neuropathy
HP:0003477.definition: An abnormality characterized by disruption of the normal functioning of peripheral axons.
HP:0003477.comment: This abnormality can be assay by electromyography (EMG) or by nerve biopsy.

HP:0003481.label: Segmental peripheral demyelination/remyelination
HP:0003481.definition: A segmental pattern of demyelination and regeneration (remyelination) affecting peripheral nerves.

HP:0003482.label: EMG: axonal abnormality
HP:0003482.definition: Electromyographic (EMG) findings characteristic of axonal neuropathy, with normal or slightly decreased nerve conduction velocities, normal or slightly prolonged distal latencies, but significantly reduced motor potentials and sensory amplitudes. There may be spontaneous activity upon needle EMG studies, such as increased insertional activity, positive sharp waves, and fibrillation potentials.
HP:0003482.comment: This is a bundled term that is kept for convenience. It is preferable to record the precise clinical observations.

HP:0003484.label: Upper limb muscle weakness
HP:0003484.definition: Weakness of the muscles of the arms.

HP:0003487.label: Babinski sign
HP:0003487.definition: Upturning of the big toe (and sometimes fanning of the other toes) in response to stimulation of the sole of the foot. If the Babinski sign is present it can indicate damage to the corticospinal tract.
HP:0003487.comment: A positive Babinski sign can indicate damage to the corticospinal tract.

HP:0003489.label: Acute episodes of neuropathic symptoms
HP:0003489.comment: Neuropathic symptoms include numbness, dysesthesias, and a characteristic form of pain (neuralgia).

HP:0003490.label: obsolete Defective dehydrogenation of isovaleryl CoA and butyryl CoA

HP:0003491.label: Elevated urine pyrophosphate
HP:0003491.definition: An abnormally increased diphosphate(4-) concentration in the urine. Diphosphate(4-), as ester with two phosphate groups, is also known as pyrophosphate.

HP:0003492.label: High urinary gonadotropin level
HP:0003492.definition: An elevated concentration of a gonadotropin hormone (stimulating hormone or luteinizing hormone) in the urine, consistent with the diagnosis of primary hypogonadism.
HP:0003492.comment: 'has part' some ('increased amount' and ('inheres in' some ('Gonadotropin (adult human)' and ('part of' some urine))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0003493.label: Antinuclear antibody positivity
HP:0003493.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against nuclei or nuclear components.
HP:0003493.comment: Antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) are found in patients with a number of different autoimmune diseases, such as systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, polymyositis, scleroderma, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, juvenile diabetes mellitus, Addison disease, vitiligo, pernicious anemia, glomerulonephritis, and pulmonary fibrosis. ANAs can display various staining patterns such as homogeneous or diffuse; speckled; nucleolar; and peripheral or rim.

HP:0003494.label: obsolete Loss of heterozygosity, multiple chromosomes

HP:0003495.label: GM2-ganglioside accumulation
HP:0003495.comment: Gangliosides are the main glycolipids of neuronal cell plasma membranes which ensure normal cellular activities. GM2-gangliosidosis can be caused by mutations in three genes: HEXA, HEXB, and GM2A. In patients with HexA deficiency GM2 ganglioside accumulates inside lysosomes, which form characteristic inclusions within the cells, so called membranous cytoplasmic bodies, which are enlarged lysosomes filled with gangliosides. The highest concentration of GM2 ganglioside is found in neuronal cells, therefore, the HexA deficiency primarily affects the nervous system, causing mental and motor developmental delay in patients. Later, progressive destruction of neurons, proliferation of microglia and accumulation of complex lipids in macrophages are observed in the brain tissue.

HP:0003496.label: Increased circulating IgM level
HP:0003496.definition: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin M in blood.

HP:0003498.label: Disproportionate short stature
HP:0003498.definition: A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to differing extents.

HP:0003502.label: Mild short stature
HP:0003502.definition: A mild degree of short stature, more than -2 SD but not more than -3 SD from mean corrected for age and sex.

HP:0003508.label: Proportionate short stature
HP:0003508.definition: A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to a comparable extent.

HP:0003510.label: Severe short stature
HP:0003510.definition: A severe degree of short stature, more than -4 SD from the mean corrected for age and sex.
HP:0003510.comment: The term severe short stature is to be preferred over dwarfism, which has been used in the past to refer to individuals with an adult height under 4 feet 10 inches (147 cm).

HP:0003513.label: Reduced ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
HP:0003513.definition: A reduction of the ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance to below 0.01.
exact_synonyms: Reduced ration of renal Ca clearance to creatinine clearance
Reduced ration of renal Ca2+ to creatinine clearance
Reduced ration of kidney calcium clearance to creatinine clearance

HP:0003514.label: Deficiency or absence of cytochrome b(-245)
exact_synonyms: Deficiency or absence of cytochrome b

HP:0003521.label: Disproportionate short-trunk short stature
HP:0003521.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs.

HP:0003524.label: Decreased methionine synthase activity
HP:0003524.definition: A reduction in methionine synthase activity.
HP:0003524.comment: Cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase catalyzes the transfer of a methyl group from N5-methyltetrahydrofolate to homocysteine, producing tetrahydrofolate and methionine, i.e., (6S)-5-methyl-5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolate + L-homocysteine = (6S)-5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolate + L-methionine.

HP:0003526.label: Orotic acid crystalluria
HP:0003526.definition: Formation of crystals owing to an increased concentration of orotic acid in the urine.

HP:0003527.label: Hyperprostaglandinuria
HP:0003527.definition: An increased concentration of prostaglandin in the urine.

HP:0003528.label: Elevated circulating calcitonin concentration
HP:0003528.definition: Concentration of calcitonin, a 32-amino acid polypeptide hormone that is produced primarily by the parafollicular cells of the thyroid, in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0003528.comment: Calcitonin is a 32-amino acid polypeptide hormone that is produced primarily by the parafollicular cells of the thyroid. It acts to reduce blood calcium (Ca2+), opposing the effects of parathyroid hormone.

HP:0003529.label: Parathormone-independent increased renal tubular calcium reabsorption
HP:0003529.definition: An increase in the reabsorption of calcium by the renal tubulus that is not associated with increased parathormone levels.
HP:0003529.comment: This feature is seen with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia. This disease has three known genetic etiologies, in type 1 there is a loss of function mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor (encoded by CASR), in type 2 there is a gain of function mutation in GNA11, which is involved in calcium-sensing receptor signaling, and in type 3 there is a mutation in AP2S1, which encodes the adaptor-related protein complex 2, sigma 1 subunit, which alters calcium-sensing receptor endocytosis.
exact_synonyms: Parathormone-independent increased renal tubular Ca2+ reabsorption
Parathormone-independent increased renal tubular Ca reabsorption

HP:0003530.label: Elevated circulating glutaric acid concentration
HP:0003530.definition: An increased concentration of glutaric acid in the blood.

HP:0003532.label: Ornithinuria
HP:0003532.definition: Level of ornithine in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0003533.label: Reduced acetaldehyde dehydrogenase level
HP:0003533.definition: Decreased level of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH). ALDH and alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) are the primary enzymes involved in alcohol metabolism.
HP:0003533.comment: In the liver, alcohol dehydrogenase converts ethanol into acetaldehyde, which is then converted into acetic acid by acetaldehyde dehydrogenase.

HP:0003534.label: Reduced xanthine dehydrogenase level
HP:0003534.definition: An abnormal reduction in xanthine dehydrogenase level.
HP:0003534.comment: This enzyme is on the purine degradation pathway and catalzyes the reaction xanthine + NAD+ + H2O = urate + NADH + H+.

HP:0003535.label: 3-Methylglutaconic aciduria
HP:0003535.definition: An increased amount of 3-methylglutaconic acid in the urine.
HP:0003535.comment: 3-methylglutaconic aciduria describes five different disorders that impair mitochondrial function and resulting in buildup of 3-methylglutaconic acid and 3-methylglutaric acid and consequent increased excretion in the urine.

HP:0003536.label: Decreased fumarate hydratase activity
HP:0003536.definition: An abnormality of Krebs cycle metabolism that is characterized by a decreased rate of fumarate hydratase activity.
HP:0003536.comment: Fumarate hydratase belongs to the tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle. It catalyzes the conversion of fumarate to malate.

HP:0003537.label: Hypouricemia
HP:0003537.definition: An abnormally low level of uric acid in the blood.

HP:0003538.label: Increased iduronate sulfatase level
HP:0003538.definition: An increased level of iduronate-2-sulfatase activity in the blood.
HP:0003538.comment: Iduronate-2-sulfatase is required for the lysosomal degradation of heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate. Mutations in this X-chromosome gene are associated with Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II. Increased serum iduronate-2-sulfatase is observed in mucolipidosis II alpha/beta.

HP:0003540.label: Impaired platelet aggregation
HP:0003540.definition: An impairment in the rate and degree to which platelets aggregate after the addition of an agonist that stimulates platelet clumping. Platelet aggregation is measured using aggregometer to measure the optical density of platelet-rich plasma, whereby platelet aggregation causes the plasma to become more transparent.

HP:0003541.label: Urinary glycosaminoglycan excretion
HP:0003541.definition: Excretion of glycosaminoglycan in the urine. Glycosaminoglycans are long unbranched polysaccharides consisting of a repeating disaccharide unit.

HP:0003542.label: Increased circulating pyruvate concentration
HP:0003542.definition: The concentration of pyruvate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0003542.comment: An abnormal increase in the concentration of pyruvate in the blood. Pyruvate is involved in energy metabolism, forming part of glycolysis and the citric acid cycle.

HP:0003546.label: Exercise intolerance
HP:0003546.definition: A functional motor deficit where individuals whose responses to the challenges of exercise fail to achieve levels considered normal for their age and gender.

HP:0003547.label: Shoulder girdle muscle weakness
HP:0003547.definition: The shoulder, or pectoral, girdle is composed of the clavicles and the scapulae. Shoulder-girdle weakness refers to lack of strength of the muscles attaching to these bones, that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders.

HP:0003548.label: Subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormally shaped mitochondria
HP:0003548.definition: An abnormally increased number of mitochondria in the cytoplasma adjacent to the sarcolemma (muscle cell membrane), whereby the mitochondria also possess an abnormal morphology.
HP:0003548.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by electron microscopy. This finding is typical of mitochondrial myopathies.

HP:0003549.label: Abnormality of connective tissue
HP:0003549.definition: Any abnormality of the soft tissues, including both connective tissue (tendons, ligaments, fascia, fibrous tissues, and fat).

HP:0003550.label: Predominantly lower limb lymphedema
HP:0003550.definition: Localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system, affecting mainly the legs.

HP:0003552.label: Muscle stiffness
HP:0003552.definition: A condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm.

HP:0003554.label: Type 2 muscle fiber atrophy
HP:0003554.definition: Atrophy (wasting) affecting primary type 2 muscle fibers. This feature in general can only be observed on muscle biopsy.
HP:0003554.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0003555.label: Muscle fiber splitting
HP:0003555.definition: Fiber splitting or branching is a common finding in human and rat skeletal muscle pathology. Fiber splitting refers to longitudinal halving of the complete fiber, while branching originates from a regenerating end of a necrotic fiber as invaginations of the sarcolemma. In fiber branching, one end of the fiber remains intact as a single entity, while the other end has several branches.

HP:0003557.label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter
HP:0003557.definition: An abnormally high degree of muscle fiber size variation. This phenotypic feature can be observed upon muscle biopsy.
HP:0003557.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by muscle biopsy.
exact_synonyms: Increased variation in muscle fibre size
Increased variability in muscle fibre diameter
Increased variability in muscle fibre size
Increased variation in muscle fiber size
Increased variability in muscle fiber size

HP:0003558.label: Viral infection-induced rhabdomyolysis
HP:0003558.definition: Rhabdomyolysis induced by a viral infection.

HP:0003560.label: Muscular dystrophy
HP:0003560.definition: The term dystrophy means abnormal growth. However, muscular dystrophy is used to describe primary myopathies with a genetic basis and a progressive course characterized by progressive skeletal muscle weakness and wasting, defects in muscle proteins, and histological features of muscle fiber degeneration (necrosis) and regeneration. If possible, it is preferred to use other HPO terms to describe the precise phenotypic abnormalities.
HP:0003560.comment: Muscular dystrophy can be demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0003563.label: Decreased LDL cholesterol concentration
HP:0003563.definition: An decreased concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
HP:0003563.comment: Beta-lipoprotein cholesterol is a synonym for low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol.

HP:0003564.label: Folate-dependent fragile site at Xq28
HP:0003564.definition: The presence of a folate sensitive fragile site at chromosome Xq28.
HP:0003564.comment: Fragile sites can be defined as heritable specific loci on human chromosomes that exhibit non-random gaps, constrictions or breaks when chromosomes are exposed to specific cell culture conditions. Over 120 different fragile sites have been identified in the human genome. Some of these sites are sensitive to folate, that is, they can be induced by a culture medium deficient in folic acid and thymidine, and hence a medium with lowered levels of dTTP or dCTP, two immediate components of DNA, or by a medium enriched either in methotrexate, an inhibitor of folate metabolism, or in fluorodeoxyuridine, an inhibitor of thymidylate synthesis. The folate-dependent fragile phenotype occurs if more than a critical number of CCG/CGG repeats are present (e.g., > 230 repeats for FRAXA).

HP:0003565.label: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
HP:0003565.definition: An increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The ESR is a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen.

HP:0003566.label: Increased serum prostaglandin E2
HP:0003566.definition: An increased concentration of prostaglandin E2 in the blood.

HP:0003568.label: Decreased glucosephosphate isomerase level
HP:0003568.definition: A decreased level of glucose-6-phosphate isomerase.

HP:0003570.label: Molybdenum cofactor deficiency
HP:0003570.definition: Absence of molybdenum cofactor(2-), a cofactor for enzymes including sulfite oxidase, xanthine oxidoreductase, and aldehyde oxidase.

HP:0003571.label: Propionic acidemia
HP:0003571.definition: Increased concentration of proprionic acid in the blood circulation.

HP:0003572.label: Low plasma citrulline
HP:0003572.definition: A decreased concentration of citrulline in the blood.

HP:0003573.label: Increased total bilirubin
HP:0003573.definition: Increased concentration of total (conjugated and unconjugated) bilirubin in the blood.

HP:0003574.label: Positive regitine blocking test
HP:0003574.definition: A positive response to the regitine blocking test consisting of a substantial reduction in blood pressure following administration of regitine, indicative of the presence of increased levels of epinephrine and norepinephrine in the circulation, which is seen in pheochromocytoma-associated hypertension.
HP:0003574.comment: Regitine produces an alpha-adrenergic block of relatively short duration. In the regitine blocking test, regitine is injected rapidly and blood pressure is recorded immediately after injection, at 30-second intervals for the first 3 minutes, and at 60-second intervals for the next 7 minutes. A positive response to the reginitine blocking test is present when the blood pressure is reduced more than 35 mmHg systolic and 25 mmHg diastolic. A typical positive response is a reduction in pressure of 60 mmHg systolic and 25 mmHg diastolic. A positive response is suggestive of pheochromocytoma and should generally be confirmed by other diagnostic procedures such as measurement of urinary catecholamines or their metabolites.

HP:0003575.label: Increased intracellular sodium
HP:0003575.definition: An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the cytosol.

HP:0003577.label: Congenital onset
HP:0003577.definition: A phenotypic abnormality that is present at birth.
HP:0003577.comment: Congenital onset literally means present at birth. Congenital abnormalities are thus generally acquired during fetal development. Congenital abnormalities are often but not always hereditary in nature. Whether a disease manifestation is diagnosed to be intrauterine or congenital may depend on the time at which diagnostic procedures are performed. Thus, most congenital abnormalities are also intrauterine. This term should be used for phenotypic abnormalities or diseases initially observed at the time of birth. For abnormalities observed prior to (e.g., by fetal ultrasound), use the term Antenatal onset (HP:0030674).

HP:0003581.label: Adult onset
HP:0003581.definition: Onset of disease manifestations in adulthood, defined here as at the age of 16 years or later.

HP:0003584.label: Late onset
HP:0003584.definition: A type of adult onset with onset of symptoms after the age of 60 years.

HP:0003587.label: Insidious onset
HP:0003587.definition: Gradual, very slow onset of disease manifestations.

HP:0003593.label: Infantile onset
HP:0003593.definition: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease between 28 days to one year of life.
HP:0003593.comment: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease within the first 12 months of life.
exact_synonyms: Onset in first year of life

HP:0003596.label: Middle age onset
HP:0003596.definition: A type of adult onset with onset of symptoms at the age of 40 to 60 years.
HP:0003596.comment: Middle age is of course not amenable to precise definitions. We suggest using this term for onset of disease symptoms between the age of 40 and 60 years.

HP:0003606.label: Absent urinary urothione
HP:0003606.definition: Lack of urothione (the urinary metabolite of molybdenum cofactor) in the urine.
HP:0003606.comment: Urothione, a sulfur-containing pterin, is the normal metabolic degradation product of the molybdenum cofactor.

HP:0003607.label: 4-hydroxyphenylacetic aciduria
HP:0003607.definition: Increased concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid in the urine.
HP:0003607.comment: 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase participates in the tyrosine catabolic pathway by catalyzing the conversion of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate to homogentisate. A deficiency in this enzyme can result in 4-Hydroxyphenylacetic aciduria.

HP:0003609.label: Foam cells with lamellar inclusion bodies
HP:0003609.definition: The presence of foam cells that contain lamellar inclusion bodies.
HP:0003609.comment: Foam cells with lamellar inclusion bodies are thought to be a hallmark of cellular phospholipidosis, i.e., of the excess accumulation of phospholipids. This abnormality can be assayed by electron microscopy.

HP:0003610.label: Fibroblast metachromasia
HP:0003610.definition: Increased cytoplasmic staining of fibroblasts with toluidine blue.
HP:0003610.comment: Cultured fibroblasts from the genetic mucopolysaccharidoses store higher than normal amounts of glycosaminoglyeans. Histochemical stains such as toluidine blue and Alcian blue can be used to detect such intracellular glycosaminoglycans which, being negatively charged, are bound and precipitated by the cationic dyes. Cultured fibroblasts from homozygotes -and heterozygotes for the genetic mucopolysaccharidoses accumulate excessive quantities of glycosaminoglycans. The cytoplasmic staining with toluidine blue is referred to as metachromasia (pink) and orthochromasia (blue) and that with Alcian blue as alcianophilia.

HP:0003612.label: Positive ferric chloride test
HP:0003612.definition: If positive, the ferric chloride test indicates an increased concentration of phenols in the urine or blood.
HP:0003612.comment: The ferric chloride test indicates presence of high levels of phenylpyruvate in urine, because ferric ion forms a blue-green colored complex with phenylpyruvate. Some other compounds can also lead to a positive ferric chloride test. The ferric chloride test is no longer used in modern clinical practice, but this term is kept for historical reasons. The urine phenylpyruvate concentration is elevated in phenylketonuria.

HP:0003613.label: Antiphospholipid antibody positivity
HP:0003613.definition: The presence of circulating autoantibodies to phospholipids.
HP:0003613.comment: This group of autoantibodies comprises anticardiolipin, antiphosphatidylinositol, atiphosphatidylglycerol, and antiphosphatidylserine antibodies.

HP:0003614.label: Trimethylaminuria
HP:0003614.definition: Increased concentration of trimethylamine in the urine.
HP:0003614.comment: Increased concentration of trimethylamine, an organic amino compound with an odor characterized as that of rotting fish, in the urine. Trimethylaminuria is generally caused by impaired oxidation of trimethylamine into the odorless compound trimethylamine N-oxide.

HP:0003621.label: Juvenile onset
HP:0003621.definition: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease between the age of 5 and 15 years.
exact_synonyms: Signs and symptoms begin before 15 years of age

HP:0003623.label: Neonatal onset
HP:0003623.definition: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease within the first 28 days of life.
exact_synonyms: Onset in first weeks of life

HP:0003634.label: Amyoplasia
HP:0003634.definition: Congenital lack of development of the muscles, which are then replaced by a mixture of dense fat and fibrous tissue.

HP:0003635.label: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs
HP:0003635.definition: Loss (disappearance) of previously present subcutaneous fat tissue in arm or leg.
exact_synonyms: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from extremities
Loss of fat tissue below the skin in limbs

HP:0003637.label: Reduced circulating 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase activity
HP:0003637.definition: Activity or concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
HP:0003637.comment: Note: 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase corresponds to EC 1.13.11.27. 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase participates in the tyrosine catabolic pathway by catalyzing the conversion of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate to homogentisate. A deficiency in this enzyme can result in 4-Hydroxyphenylacetic aciduria.

HP:0003639.label: Elevated urinary epinephrine level
HP:0003639.definition: The concentration of epinephrine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0003640.label: CNS foam cells
HP:0003640.definition: The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, in the central nervous system.

HP:0003641.label: Hemoglobinuria
HP:0003641.definition: The presence of free hemoglobin in the urine.
HP:0003641.comment: If, following hemolysis, haptoglobins (hemoglobin-binding proteins) are saturated, then free hemoglobin appears in the urine.

HP:0003642.label: Type I transferrin isoform profile
HP:0003642.definition: Abnormal transferrin isoform profile consistent with a type I congenital disorder of glycosylation. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II.
HP:0003642.comment: There are several methods in use with which this feature can be diagnosed. Using HPLC analysis an increased asialo- and disialotransferrin and reduced tetrasialotransferrin are observed. Using immunoaffinity column analysis, the mono-oligosaccharide/di-oligosaccharide transferrin ratio, and/or the a-oligosaccharide/di-oligosaccharide transferrin ratio are abnormal.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin, type I pattern
Isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin consistent with CDG type I

HP:0003643.label: Sulfite oxidase deficiency
HP:0003643.comment: Sulfite oxidase is responsible for the oxidation of sulfite to sulfate and is the terminal enzyme in the oxidative degradation pathway of sulfur-containing amino acids.

HP:0003645.label: Prolonged partial thromboplastin time
HP:0003645.definition: Increased time to coagulation in the partial thromboplastin time (PTT) test, a measure of the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Phospholipid, and activator, and calcium are mixed into an anticoagulated plasma sample, and the time is measured until a thrombus forms.

HP:0003646.label: Bicarbonaturia
HP:0003646.definition: Abnormally increased concentration of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.

HP:0003647.label: Electron transfer flavoprotein-ubiquinone oxidoreductase defect
HP:0003647.definition: A deficiency of the electron transfer flavoprotein-ubiquinone oxidoreductase.

HP:0003648.label: Lacticaciduria
HP:0003648.definition: An increased concentration of lactic acid in the urine.

HP:0003649.label: Abnormal glycosidase enzyme activity
HP:0003649.definition: Abnormality of glycosidase enzyme activity. Glycoside hydrolases (GHs), including glycosidases and transglycosidases. These enzymes constitute 113 protein families that are responsible for the hydrolysis and/or transglycosylation of glycosidic bonds.
HP:0003649.comment: Glycosides are molecules with a sugar moiety bound to some other moiety.

HP:0003651.label: Foam cells
HP:0003651.definition: The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, where they ingest low-density lipoproteins and become laden with lipids, giving them a foamy appearance.
HP:0003651.comment: Foam cells may contain polymorphic cytoplasmic inclusions consisting of lamellar osmiophilic membranes on electron microscopy.

HP:0003652.label: Recurrent myoglobinuria
HP:0003652.definition: Recurring episodes of myoglobinuria, i.e., of the presence of myoglobin in the urine. This is usually a consequence of rhabdomyolysis, i.e., of the destruction of muscle tissue.

HP:0003653.label: Cellular metachromasia
HP:0003653.definition: Metachromasia (also known as metachromacy) is a characteristic color change which certain aniline dyes exhibit when bound to particular substances or when concentrated in solution. For example, the basic dye toluidine blue becomes distinctly pink when bound to cartilage matrix. In the sense used here, the metachromasia refers to a change in color not observed with normal tissues, anomalous staining with the cationic dyes toluidine blue O and Alcian blue resulting from excessive amounts of the polyanionic glycosaminoglycans.
HP:0003653.comment: This investigation is no longer in common use.

HP:0003654.label: Reduced dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase level
HP:0003654.definition: An abnormal reduction in dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (NADP+) level.
HP:0003654.comment: Pyrimidine 5-prime nucleotidase catalyzes the dephosphorylation of the pyrimidine 5-prime monophosphates to the corresponding nucleosides.

HP:0003655.label: Reduced level of N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase II
HP:0003655.definition: An abnormality of glycoprotein metabolism related to a decreased level of alpha-1,6-mannosylglycoprotein 2-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity.

HP:0003656.label: Decreased beta-glucocerebrosidase level
HP:0003656.definition: Reduced level of the enzyme beta-glucosidase, an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of glucosylceramide into ceramide and glucose.
HP:0003656.comment: An enzyme that hydrolyzes beta-glucosides in cerebrosides.

HP:0003657.label: Vascular granular osmiophilic material deposition
HP:0003657.definition: Accumulation of granular osmiophilic material in blood vessel walls. Osmiophilic material becomes black upon staining with osmium tetroxide. Deposition of granular osmiophilic material (GOM) is the vascular pathological hallmark of CADASIL, which is the most prevalent hereditary small vessel disease and is caused by missense mutations in the NOTCH3 gene. GOM have been shown to contain NOTCH3 ectodomain (NOTCH3ECD) and extracellular matrix proteins, and can be visualized ultrastructurally in the tunica media of small arteries and capillaries. These electron dense GOM deposits are located in the basement membrane of mural cells, i.e. vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. In both manifest and pre-manifest CADASIL patients, GOM deposits are present not only in brain vessels, but also in vessels of other organs, such as the skin.
HP:0003657.comment: In CADASIL (cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leucoencephalopathy), GOM deposits can be observed located in the neighborhood of the smooth muscle cells, often within an infolding of the cell membrane.

HP:0003658.label: Hypomethioninemia
HP:0003658.definition: A decreased concentration of methionine in the blood.
HP:0003658.comment: Normal methionine blood levels are around 30 micromole per liter.

HP:0003665.label: Amyotrophy of the musculature of the pelvis
HP:0003665.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles of the pelvis.

HP:0003674.label: Onset
HP:0003674.definition: The age group in which disease manifestations appear.
HP:0003674.comment: Adolescent is defined by WHO as a person between 10-19 years of age.

HP:0003676.label: Progressive
HP:0003676.definition: Applies to a disease manifestation that increases in scope or severity over the course of time, i.e., that worsens with age.

HP:0003677.label: Slowly progressive
HP:0003677.definition: Applies to a disease manifestation that only slowly increases in scope or severity over the course of time.
exact_synonyms: Signs and symptoms worsen slowly with time

HP:0003678.label: Rapidly progressive
HP:0003678.definition: Applies to a disease manifestation that quickly increases in scope or severity over the course of time.

HP:0003680.label: Nonprogressive
HP:0003680.definition: Applies to a disease manifestation that does not increase in scope or severity over the course of time, i.e., that does not worsen with age.

HP:0003682.label: Variable progression rate
HP:0003682.definition: Applies to a disease manifestation that quickly increases in scope or severity with a rate that varies. For instance, progression may be slow in one time period and rapid in another.

HP:0003687.label: Centrally nucleated skeletal muscle fibers
HP:0003687.definition: An abnormality in which the nuclei of sarcomeres take on an abnormally central localization (or in which this feature is found in an increased proportion of muscle cells).
HP:0003687.comment: Normally, the nuclei of muscle cells are located peripherally, immediately under the plasma membrane (sarcolemma).

HP:0003688.label: Cytochrome C oxidase-negative muscle fibers
HP:0003688.definition: An abnormally reduced activity of the enzyme cytochrome C oxidase in muscle tissue.
HP:0003688.comment: This abnormality can be assayed by muscle biopsy. Cytochrome C oxidase is an enzyme of the respiratory electron transport chain of mitochondria that is located in the mitochondrial membrane.
exact_synonyms: Decreased skeletal muscle cytochrome c oxidase activity
Decreased activity of cytochrome C oxidase in muscle tissue
Cytochrome c oxidase deficiency in skeletal muscle

HP:0003689.label: Multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions
HP:0003689.definition: The presence of multiple deletions of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).
HP:0003689.comment: This feature can be demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0003690.label: Limb muscle weakness
HP:0003690.definition: Reduced strength and weakness of the muscles of the arms and legs.

HP:0003691.label: Scapular winging
HP:0003691.definition: Abnormal protrusion of the scapula away from the surface of the back.
HP:0003691.comment: The serratus anterior muscle is responsible for controlling the scapula (shoulder blade), and weakness of this muscle (which may be caused by damage to the long thoracic nerve) can manifest as scular winging.

HP:0003693.label: Distal amyotrophy
HP:0003693.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting muscles in the distal portions of the extremities.
HP:0003693.comment: Most polyneuropathies affect distal lower extremity miuscles early on. Polyneuropathies are roughly symmeetric in distribution and tend to affect nerves in a length-dependent manner, with the longest nerves first (stocking-glove distribution).
exact_synonyms: Distal muscle atrophy, upper and lower limbs
Distal amyotrophy, especially of the hands and feet

HP:0003694.label: Late-onset proximal muscle weakness
HP:0003694.definition: Lack of strength of the proximal musculature occurring late in the clinical course.

HP:0003696.label: Absent epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0003696.definition: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of the outermost bone of the pinky finger
Absent end part of the outermost bone of the little finger
Absent end part of the outermost bone of the pinkie finger

HP:0003697.label: Scapuloperoneal amyotrophy
HP:0003697.definition: Muscular atrophy in the distribution of shoulder girdle and peroneal muscles.

HP:0003700.label: Generalized amyotrophy
HP:0003700.definition: Generalized (diffuse, unlocalized) amyotrophy (muscle atrophy) affecting multiple muscles.

HP:0003701.label: Proximal muscle weakness
HP:0003701.definition: A lack of strength of the proximal muscles.
HP:0003701.comment: Removed logical definition that used anonymous class. Outstanding term request in UBERON for proximal muscle organ.
exact_synonyms: Weakness in muscles of upper arms and upper legs

HP:0003707.label: Calf muscle pseudohypertrophy
HP:0003707.definition: Enlargement of the muscles of the calf due to their replacement by connective tissue or fat.
HP:0003707.comment: Pseudohypertrophy of the calf musculature is commonly seen in certain muscular dystrophies but also with spinal muscular atrophy and other denervating conditions.

HP:0003710.label: Exercise-induced muscle cramps
HP:0003710.definition: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles brought on by physical exertion.

HP:0003712.label: Skeletal muscle hypertrophy
HP:0003712.definition: Abnormal increase in muscle size and mass not due to training.
HP:0003712.comment: Increased muscle bulk based on clinical observation. Myofiber hyperplasia and hypertrophy may contribute but this is not easily tested clinically.

HP:0003713.label: Muscle fiber necrosis
HP:0003713.definition: Abnormal cell death involving muscle fibers usually associated with break in, or absence of, muscle surface fiber membrane and resulting in irreversible damage to muscle fibers.

HP:0003715.label: Myofibrillar myopathy
HP:0003715.definition: Myofibrillar structural changes characterized by abnormal intracellular accumulation of the intermediate filament desmin and other proteins.
HP:0003715.comment: This feature is demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0003719.label: Muscle mounding
HP:0003719.definition: Percussion-induced, local prolonged contractions (mounding) in muscle persisting for several seconds.
HP:0003719.comment: Transient swelling of muscle induced by percussion (e.g., tapping on muscle with a reflex hammer).

HP:0003720.label: Generalized muscle hypertrophy
HP:0003720.definition: Hypertrophy (increase in size) of muscle tissue in a generalized (not localized) distribution.
exact_synonyms: Generalized increase in muscle cell size
Generalised increase in muscle cell size

HP:0003722.label: Neck flexor weakness
HP:0003722.definition: Weakness of the muscles involved in neck flexion (sternocleidomastoid, longus capitus, longus colli, and scalenus anterior).

HP:0003724.label: Shoulder girdle muscle atrophy
HP:0003724.definition: Amyotrophy affecting the muscles of the shoulder girdle.

HP:0003725.label: Firm muscles
HP:0003725.definition: A state of increased firmness (i.e., a reduced tendency to yield to pressure) of skeletal muscle tissue. This finding is ascertained by palpation and is to be distinguished from increased muscle tone (abnormal elevation in the resting tension of a muscle, leading to stiffness and resistance to movement).
HP:0003725.comment: This finding has been described in Arthrogryposis, distal, type 5 and Glycogen storage disease II.

HP:0003730.label: EMG: myotonic runs
HP:0003730.definition: Spontaneous, repetitive electrical activity demonstrated by electromyography (EMG).
HP:0003730.comment: This is a characteristic abnormality seen in the myotonias and periodic paralyzes.

HP:0003731.label: Quadriceps muscle weakness
HP:0003731.definition: Weakness of the quadriceps muscle (that is, of the muscle fasciculus of quadriceps femoris).

HP:0003736.label: Autophagic vacuoles
HP:0003736.definition: The lysosomal-vacuolar pathway has a role in the controlled intracellular digestion of macromolecules such as protein complexes and organelles. This feature refers to the presence of an abnormally increased number of autophagic vacuoles in muscle tissue.

HP:0003737.label: Mitochondrial myopathy
HP:0003737.definition: A type of myopathy associated with mitochondrial disease and characterized by findings on biopsy such as ragged red muscle fibers.
HP:0003737.comment: This is a bundled term that should not be used for future annotations.

HP:0003738.label: Exercise-induced myalgia
HP:0003738.definition: The occurrence of an unusually high amount of muscle pain following exercise.

HP:0003740.label: Myotonia with warm-up phenomenon
HP:0003740.definition: Myotonia that occurs after a period of rest and decreases with continuing exercise.

HP:0003743.label: Genetic anticipation
HP:0003743.definition: A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that exhibits anticipation, the increase in severity and/or an earlier age of onset in subsequent generations.
HP:0003743.comment: This mode of inheritance is characteristic of trinucleotide and some other repeat disorders.

HP:0003744.label: Genetic anticipation with paternal anticipation bias
HP:0003744.definition: A type of genetic anticipation observed predominantly upon transmission from affected males.

HP:0003745.label: Sporadic
HP:0003745.definition: Cases of the disease in question occur without a previous family history, i.e., as isolated cases without being transmitted from a parent and without other siblings being affected.

HP:0003749.label: Pelvic girdle muscle weakness
HP:0003749.definition: Weakness of the muscles of the pelvic girdle (also known as the hip girdle), that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the pelvis.

HP:0003750.label: Increased muscle fatiguability
HP:0003750.definition: An abnormal, increased fatiguability of the musculature.

HP:0003752.label: Episodic flaccid weakness
HP:0003752.definition: Recurrent episodes of muscle flaccidity, a type of paralysis in which a muscle becomes soft and yields to passive stretching.

HP:0003755.label: Type 1 fibers relatively smaller than type 2 fibers
HP:0003755.definition: The presence of abnormal muscle fiber size such that type 1 fibers are smaller than type 2 fibers.
HP:0003755.comment: This feature can only be observed on muscle biopsy.
exact_synonyms: Type 1 fibres relatively smaller than type 2 fibres

HP:0003758.label: Reduced subcutaneous adipose tissue
HP:0003758.definition: A reduced amount of fat tissue in the lowest layer of the integument. This feature can be appreciated by a reduced skinfold thickness.
exact_synonyms: Reduced fat tissue below the skin

HP:0003759.label: Hypoplasia of lymphatic vessels
HP:0003759.comment: This feature can be demonstrated by lymphography.

HP:0003760.label: Percussion-induced rapid rolling muscle contractions
HP:0003760.definition: Mechanical percussion (i.e., striking a muscle with a reflex hammer) leads to spreading waves of muscle contractions that begin proximally and spread laterally across the muscle.

HP:0003761.label: Calcinosis
HP:0003761.definition: Formation of calcium deposits in any soft tissue.
exact_synonyms: Calcium buildup in soft tissues of body

HP:0003762.label: Uterus didelphys
HP:0003762.definition: A malformation of the uterus in which the uterus is present as a paired organ as a result of the failure of fusion of the mullerian ducts during embryogenesis.

HP:0003763.label: Bruxism
HP:0003763.definition: Bruxism is characterized by the grinding of the teeth including the clenching of the jaw and typically occur during sleep.
HP:0003763.comment: Rarely, bruxism can occur while the affected individual is awake, but this is less likely to result in the need for medical attention.

HP:0003764.label: Nevus
HP:0003764.definition: A nevus is a type of hamartoma that is a circumscribed stable malformation of the skin.
HP:0003764.comment: The word Nevus derives from the Latin word Knee-vus meaning birthmark or mole.

HP:0003765.label: Psoriasiform dermatitis
HP:0003765.definition: A skin abnormality characterized by redness and irritation, with thick, red skin that displays flaky, silver-white patches (scales).
HP:0003765.comment: The label Psoriaform dermatitis is used to emphasize that this term is meant to describe the morhpological abnormality of the skin and not all of the manifestations of the disease psoriasis (which can also include itching and nail pitsand other manifestations).

HP:0003771.label: Pulp calcification
HP:0003771.definition: Pulp calcifications may appear as punctate calcifications, irregular, roughly spherical mineralized masses in any part of the pulp. It may occur isolated or associated to calcifications elsewhere such as the carotid arteries and kidneys. The diagnosis pulp calcifications can be established using radiological studies.

HP:0003774.label: Stage 5 chronic kidney disease
HP:0003774.definition: A degree of kidney failure severe enough to require dialysis or kidney transplantation for survival characterized by a severe reduction in glomerular filtration rate (less than 15 ml/min/1.73 m2) and other manifestations including increased serum creatinine.
HP:0003774.comment: Equivalent with the National Kidney Foundation's definition of stage 5 chronic kidney disease.

HP:0003777.label: Pili torti
HP:0003777.definition: Pili (from Latin pilus, hair) torti (from Latin tortus, twisted) refers to short and brittle hairs that appear flattened and twisted when viewed through a microscope.

HP:0003778.label: Short mandibular rami
exact_synonyms: Short body and ramus of mandible

HP:0003782.label: Eunuchoid habitus
HP:0003782.definition: A body habitus that is tall, slim and underweight, with long legs and long arms (i.e., arm span exceeds height by 5 cm or more).

HP:0003785.label: Decreased CSF homovanillic acid concentration
HP:0003785.definition: Decreased concentration of homovanillic acid (HVA) in the cerebrospinal fluid. HVA is a metabolite of dopamine.

HP:0003787.label: Type 1 and type 2 muscle fiber minicore regions
HP:0003787.definition: Multiple small zones of sarcomeric disorganization and lack of oxidative activity (known as minicores) in type 1 and type 2 muscle fibers.
exact_synonyms: Type 1 and type 2 muscle fibre minicore regions

HP:0003789.label: Minicore myopathy
HP:0003789.definition: Multiple small zones of sarcomeric disorganization and lack of oxidative activity (known as minicores) in muscle fibers.

HP:0003795.label: Short middle phalanx of toe
HP:0003795.definition: Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of middle phalanx of toe.

HP:0003796.label: Irregular iliac crest
HP:0003796.definition: Irregularity of the iliac crest, which is the superior border of the wing of the ilium.

HP:0003797.label: Limb-girdle muscle atrophy
HP:0003797.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle.

HP:0003798.label: Nemaline bodies
HP:0003798.definition: Nemaline rods are abnormal bodies that can occur in skeletal muscle fibers. The rods can be observed on histological analysis of muscle biopsy tissue or upon electron microscopy, where they appear either as extensions of sarcomeric Z-lines, in random array without obvious attachment to Z-lines (often in areas devoid of sarcomeres) or in large clusters localized at the sarcolemma or intermyofibrillar spaces.
HP:0003798.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by muscle biopsy, which shows nemaline bodies (rods) on Gomori trichrome staining. Rod bodies characteristically stain red with MGT. The rods are delicate and accumulate subsarcolemmaly. They stain negative with ATPase, NADH and SDH as they lack myosin and mitochondria. Rods are characteristic of nemaline myopathy but also seen in central core disease and various other diseases which include neurogenic disorders (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, spinal muscular atrophy, undefined), inflammatory myopathies (dermatomyositis, polymyositis, periarteritis nodosa), metabolic myopathy (mitochondrial myopathy), muscular dystrophy (LGMD) and some undefined myopathies (Liouet al; Diagnostic role of nemaline rod in neuromuscular disease. Acta Neurol Sinica 1992;1: 218-23).

HP:0003800.label: Muscle abnormality related to mitochondrial dysfunction

HP:0003803.label: Type 1 muscle fiber predominance
HP:0003803.definition: An abnormal predominance of type I muscle fibers (in general, this feature can only be observed on muscle biopsy).
HP:0003803.comment: This finding is demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0003805.label: Rimmed vacuoles
HP:0003805.definition: Presence of abnormal vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles) in the sarcolemma. On histological staining with hematoxylin and eosin, rimmed vacuoles are popcorn-like clear vacuoles with a densely blue rim. The vacuoles are often associated with cytoplasmic and occasionally intranuclear eosinophilic inclusions.
HP:0003805.comment: Rimmed vacuoles are characteristic for inclusion-bosy myositis, but are also seen an a number of other diseases. This term implies that rimmed vacuoles are found histologically. In some cases, the majority of muscle fibers are involved, but in others, rimmed vacuoles can be found in only a minority of fibers.

HP:0003809.label: Reduced intrathoracic adipose tissue
HP:0003809.definition: An abnormally reduced amount of adipose tissue in the thoracic cavity.

HP:0003811.label: Neonatal death
HP:0003811.definition: Death within the first 28 days of life.

HP:0003812.label: Phenotypic variability
HP:0003812.comment: This term can be applied to disease entities but not to individuals. It may be made obsolete in future versions of the HPO.
exact_synonyms: Highly variable phenotype, even within families

HP:0003819.label: Death in childhood
HP:0003819.definition: Death in during childhood, defined here as between the ages of 2 and 10 years.
HP:0003819.comment: previous def was: 'has part' some (premature and ('inheres in' some death) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0003826.label: Stillbirth
HP:0003826.definition: Death of the fetus in utero after at least 22 weeks of gestation.
HP:0003826.comment: The age at which fetal demise is legally classified asa a miscarriage varies between countries with the US being 20 gestational weeks and the UK being 24 gestational weeks. The HPO chooses the average of these age ranges.

HP:0003828.label: Variable expressivity
HP:0003828.definition: A variable severity of phenotypic features.
HP:0003828.comment: This term can be applied to disease entities but not to individuals. It may be made obsolete in future versions of the HPO.

HP:0003829.label: Typified by incomplete penetrance
HP:0003829.definition: Description of conditions in which not all individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease. Penetrance is the proportion that develop disease given a lifespan of 80 years.
HP:0003829.comment: For example, Van der Woude syndrome due to IRF6 causes cleft lip and/or palate with penetrance estimated at 80%, and C9orf72 causes frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis with approximately 50% penetrance.

HP:0003831.label: Typified by age-related disease onset
HP:0003831.definition: Description of conditions in which age of onset is typically later in life and in which penetrance is dependent on the age of the subject.

HP:0003834.label: Shoulder dislocation
HP:0003834.definition: A displacement or misalignment of the humerus with respect to the other bones of the should joint. Note that a subluxation is a partial dislocation.

HP:0003835.label: Shoulder subluxation
HP:0003835.definition: A partial dislocation of the shoulder joint.

HP:0003837.label: Soft-tissue ossification around the shoulders
HP:0003837.definition: Formation of calcified tissue in the soft tissues surrounding the shoulder.
related_synonyms: Calcification of the soft-tissue around the shoulders

HP:0003839.label: Abnormal upper limb epiphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormal shape of end part of upper limb long bones
Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the upper limbs
Epihyseal plate abnormality of the upper limbs
Abnormality of upper limb epiphysis morphology

HP:0003840.label: Delayed upper limb epiphyseal ossification
HP:0003840.definition: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more long bones of the upper limbs.
related_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the end part of the upper limb bone

HP:0003841.label: Fragmented upper limb epiphysis
exact_synonyms: Fragmented epiphyses of the upper limbs
Fragmented end part of upper limb bones

HP:0003842.label: Irregular epiphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of upper limb bones

HP:0003843.label: Round epiphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Round end part of upper limb bones

HP:0003844.label: Small epiphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Small end part of upper limb bones

HP:0003846.label: Wide epiphyseal plates of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Broad epiphyseal plates of the upper limbs
Broad growth plates of upper limbs

HP:0003848.label: Cupped metaphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Cupped wide portion of the upper limb bone

HP:0003849.label: Flared upper limb metaphysis
HP:0003849.definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones of the arm.
exact_synonyms: Flared metaphyses of the upper limbs
Flared wide portion of the upper limb bone

HP:0003850.label: Upper-limb metaphyseal irregularity
exact_synonyms: Irregular wide portion of upper limb bones
Irregular metaphyses of the upper limbs

HP:0003851.label: Lytic defects in metaphyses of the upper limbs

HP:0003852.label: Normal density transverse bands in metaphyses of the upper limbs

HP:0003853.label: Sclerosis with transverse striations in metaphyses of the upper limbs

HP:0003854.label: Sclerosis of metaphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in wide portion of the upper limb bones

HP:0003855.label: Spurred metaphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Spurred wide portion of upper limb bone

HP:0003856.label: Upper limb metaphyseal widening
HP:0003856.definition: Increased width (breadth) of metaphyses of the arms.
exact_synonyms: Broad wide portion of upper limb bone
Wide/broad metaphyses of the upper limbs

HP:0003858.label: Cortical diaphyseal irregularity of the upper limbs

HP:0003859.label: Cortical diaphyseal thickening of the upper limbs

HP:0003860.label: Diaphyseal sclerosis of the upper limbs
HP:0003860.definition: An elevation in bone density in one or more diaphyses of the arms. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in central part of long bone of upper limbs

HP:0003861.label: Broad diaphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Wide shaft of long bone of the upper limbs
Broad shaft of long bone of the upper limbs
Wide diaphyses of the upper limbs

HP:0003862.label: Absent humerus
HP:0003862.definition: Missing humerus bone associated with congenital failure of development.
exact_synonyms: Absent long bone in upper arm

HP:0003863.label: Angulated humerus
exact_synonyms: Angulated long bone in upper arm

HP:0003864.label: Bifid humerus
exact_synonyms: Notched long bone in upper arm

HP:0003865.label: Bowed humerus
HP:0003865.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the humerus.
exact_synonyms: Bowed long bone in upper arm

HP:0003870.label: Crumpled humerus
exact_synonyms: Crumpled long bone in upper arm

HP:0003871.label: Deformed humerus
exact_synonyms: Deformed long bone in upper arm

HP:0003872.label: Humeral exostoses
HP:0003872.definition: Presence of more than one exostosis originating in one or both humerus bones. An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage, and arises from a bone that develops from cartilage.

HP:0003875.label: Humeral lytic defects
HP:0003875.definition: Destruction of an area of humerus bone due to a disease process, such as cancer.
HP:0003875.comment: Osteolytic defects can be observed by radiology studies such as an X-ray; however, the type of condition that is causing the lesion cannot be fully determined by the X-ray alone.

HP:0003879.label: Humeral pseudarthrosis
exact_synonyms: False joint (long bone in upper arm)

HP:0003881.label: Humeral sclerosis
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in long bone of upper arm

HP:0003882.label: Slender humerus
HP:0003882.definition: Reduction in diameter of the humerus.
exact_synonyms: Slender long bone of upper arm

HP:0003883.label: Tapered humerus
exact_synonyms: Tapered long bone of upper arm

HP:0003884.label: Triangular humerus
exact_synonyms: Triangular long bone of upper arm

HP:0003886.label: Wide humerus
exact_synonyms: Wide long bone of upper arm

HP:0003887.label: Abnormal humeral head morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormal head of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003888.label: Flattened humeral heads
exact_synonyms: Flattended head of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003891.label: Abnormal humeral epiphysis morphology
HP:0003891.definition: An anomaly of the humeral epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of the long bone of the upper arm

HP:0003892.label: Absent humeral epiphyseal ossification
HP:0003892.definition: Lack of formation of bone in the epiphysis of the humerus.
HP:0003892.comment: Normally, the proximal humeral epiphysis can be visualized at about 40 weeks of gestation.
exact_synonyms: Absent ossification of the humeral epiphyses
Absent maturation of end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003893.label: Advanced ossification of the humeral epiphysis
HP:0003893.definition: Ossification of the humeral epiphysis at an earlier age than normal.
exact_synonyms: Accelerated maturation of end part of long bone in upper arm
related_synonyms: Advanced maturation of the humeral epiphyses

HP:0003894.label: Delayed humeral epiphyseal ossification
HP:0003894.definition: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the humeral epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Delayed maturation/delayed ossification of the humeral epiphyses
related_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the end part of the long bone in upper arm

HP:0003895.label: Flattened humeral epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Flattened end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003896.label: Irregular humeral epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003897.label: Irregular ossification of the humeral epiphyses
related_synonyms: Irregular maturation of the end part of the long bone in upper arm

HP:0003898.label: Large humeral epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Large end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003899.label: Round humeral epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Round end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003900.label: Small humeral epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Small end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003901.label: Stippled calcification of the humeral epiphyses

HP:0003902.label: Epiphyseal stippling of the humerus
HP:0003902.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the humeral epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Stippled ossification of the humeral epiphyses

HP:0003903.label: Broad humeral epiphyses
HP:0003903.definition: Increased width of the humeral epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Wide end part of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003904.label: Wide epiphyses of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Broad epiphyses of the upper limbs
Wide end part of upper limb bones

HP:0003905.label: Abnormality of the humeral epiphyseal plate

HP:0003906.label: Broad humeral epiphyseal plate
HP:0003906.definition: Increased width of the humeral epiphyseal growth plate.

HP:0003907.label: Abnormal humeral metaphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the wide portion of the long bone in upper arm

HP:0003908.label: Corner fracture of metaphysis
HP:0003908.definition: Fracture or fragmentation at the lateral portion of the metaphysis of a long bone. The radiographic appearance is that of a small corner of metaphysis separated from the metaphyseal edge by thin linear radiolucency. This feature can be observed in child abuse but fragmented appearance of the metaphysis or facture-like lesions can also be detected in the setting of certain skeletal dysplasias.
HP:0003908.comment: A corner fracture is a subepiphyseal planer fracture through immature metaphyseal bone. The appearance of a corner, avulsion or bucket handle depends on the extent of bone failure and radiographic projection. Bone can fail in this pattern from both shearing and tensile stresses. The weakest area of bone for a given loading condition determines the injury threshold for that structure.

HP:0003909.label: Cortical subperiosteal resorption of humeral metaphyses

HP:0003910.label: Enlarged humeral metaphyses
exact_synonyms: Enlarged wide portion of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003911.label: Flared humeral metaphysis
HP:0003911.definition: Flaring (increase of width with a splayed appearance) of the humeral metaphysis.
exact_synonyms: Flared wide portion of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003913.label: Humeral metaphyseal irregularity
exact_synonyms: Irregular wide portion of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003914.label: Irregular ossification of humeral metaphyses
exact_synonyms: Irregular bone maturation of the wide portion of the long bone in upper arm

HP:0003915.label: Lytic defects of the humeral metaphysis

HP:0003916.label: Normal-density transverse humeral bands
HP:0003916.comment: Normal-density transverse bands of the humerus

HP:0003917.label: Pointed humeral metaphysis
exact_synonyms: Pointed wide portion of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003918.label: Sclerotic humeral metaphysis
exact_synonyms: Stiffening of wide portion of long bone of upper arm
Hardening of wide portion of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003919.label: Sclerotic humeral metaphysis with longitudinal striations

HP:0003920.label: Sloping humeral metaphysis
exact_synonyms: Sloping metaphysis of long bone of upper arm

exact_synonyms: Laterally sloping metaphysis of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003922.label: Spurred humeral metaphysis
exact_synonyms: Spurred metaphysis of long bone of upper arm

exact_synonyms: Square metaphysis of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003924.label: Stippled calcification of humeral metaphysis
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcification in metaphysis of long bone of upper arm

HP:0003926.label: Abnormal humeral diaphysis morphology
HP:0003926.definition: An anomaly of the humeral diaphysis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of shaft of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003927.label: Cortical irregularity of humeral diaphysis
HP:0003927.definition: An abnormal irregularity of the cortical surface of the diaphysis (shaft) of the humerus.

HP:0003929.label: Ground glass opacity of humeral diaphysis

HP:0003931.label: Periosteal new bone of humeral diaphysis

HP:0003933.label: Sclerosis of humeral diaphysis
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in shaft of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003935.definition: Increased width of the humeral diaphysis.
