Broad shaft of long bone in upper arm

HP:0003939.label: Humeroulnar synostosis
HP:0003939.definition: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the ulna and the humerus.

HP:0003943.label: Abnormality of the joint spaces of the elbow
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the joint spaces of the elbow

HP:0003944.label: Narrow joint spaces of the elbow
exact_synonyms: Narrow joint spaces of the elbow

HP:0003945.label: Irregular articular surfaces of the elbow joints

HP:0003946.label: Abnormal elbow epiphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the elbow
Abnormality of end part of the elbow bone

HP:0003947.label: Delayed elbow epiphyseal ossification
HP:0003947.definition: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more long bones that are part of the elbow.
exact_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the end part of the elbow bone

HP:0003948.label: Irregular epiphyses of the elbow
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of the elbow bone

HP:0003949.label: Abnormal elbow metaphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormal wide portion of elbow bone

HP:0003950.label: Flared elbow metaphyses
exact_synonyms: Flared wide portion of elbow bone

HP:0003951.label: Distal humeral metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0003951.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis at the distal end of the humerus (at the elbow).
exact_synonyms: Irregular wide portion of elbow bone

HP:0003952.label: Sclerotic foci of metaphyses of the elbow
exact_synonyms: Vertical linear mixed lucent and sclerotic pattern of metaphyses

HP:0003953.label: Absent forearm bone
HP:0003953.definition: Absence of one or more forearm bones associated with congenital failure of development.

HP:0003955.label: Bone-in-a-bone appearance of forearm
HP:0003955.definition: A descriptive term for a forearm bone that appears to have an additional bone within it on radiography.

HP:0003956.label: Bowed forearm bones
HP:0003956.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature affecting either the radius, the ulna, or both.

HP:0003957.label: Cortical thickening of the forearm bones

HP:0003961.label: Fractured forearm bone
HP:0003961.definition: Bone fracture in the radius, ulna, or wrist.

HP:0003963.label: Lytic defects of the forearm bones

HP:0003967.label: Sclerotic forearm bones
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of forearm bones

HP:0003971.label: Broad forearm bones
HP:0003971.definition: Abnormally wide bone of the skeleton of forearm.

HP:0003974.label: Absent radius
HP:0003974.definition: Missing radius bone associated with congenital failure of development.
exact_synonyms: Missing outer large bone of forearm

HP:0003982.label: Aplasia of the ulna
HP:0003982.definition: Missing ulna bone associated with congenital failure of development.

HP:0003991.label: Osteosclerosis of the ulna
HP:0003991.definition: Osteosclerosis (increased density related to increased bone mass) of the ulna.

HP:0003992.label: Slender ulna
HP:0003992.definition: Reduction in diameter of the ulna.

HP:0003994.label: Dislocated wrist
HP:0003994.definition: An injury of the wrist with displacement of any of the eight carpal bones.

HP:0004000.label: Cone-shaped distal radial epiphysis
HP:0004000.definition: The distal epiphysis (rounded portion of bone at the far end of the radius distal to the growth plate) has an abnormal cone-shaped appearance.
HP:0004000.comment: The phrase chevron-shaped (having the shape of a V or an inverted V) is synonymous.

HP:0004012.label: Premature fusion of the radial epiphyseal plates
HP:0004012.definition: A premature fusion of the epiphyseal plates of the radius. Epiphyseal plates are located at the distal and proximal ends of the long bones, in this case of the radius and premature fusion will have an effect on the growh of the radial bone, inhibiting or at least disturbing the normal growth and development of the bone.
HP:0004012.comment: The epiphyseal plate (or epiphysial plate, physis, or growth plate) is a hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at each end of a long bone. The plate is found in children and adolescents; in adults, who have stopped growing, the plate is replaced by an epiphyseal line. The growth plate has a very specific morphology in having a zonal arrangement. The growth plate includes a relatively inactive reserve zone at the epiphyseal end, moving distally into a proliferative and then hyper trophic zone and ending with a band of ossifying cartilage (the metaphysis).

HP:0004014.label: Broad radial epiphyseal plate
HP:0004014.definition: Abnormal increase in width of the epiphyseal growth plate of the radius.

HP:0004018.label: Flared radial metaphysis
HP:0004018.definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the radius.

HP:0004019.label: Radial metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0004019.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis of the radius.

HP:0004020.label: Irregular ossification of the radial metaphysis

HP:0004022.label: Sclerotic radial metaphysis with longitudinal striations

HP:0004026.label: Broad radial metaphysis
HP:0004026.definition: Increase in width (breadth) of the radial metaphysis.

HP:0004027.label: Abnormality of radial diaphysis
HP:0004027.definition: An anomaly of the radial diaphysis.

HP:0004031.label: Broad radial diaphysis
HP:0004031.definition: Increase in width of the diaphysis of radius.
HP:0004031.comment: Increased diameter of the shaft (diaphysis) of the radius.

HP:0004032.label: Abnormal olecranon morphology
HP:0004032.definition: Any structural abnormality of the olecranon, a bony eminence of the proximal ulna.

HP:0004035.label: Abnormal ulnar styloid process morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the styloid process of ulna

HP:0004037.label: Abnormal ulnar epiphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the epiphyseal plate of the ulna

HP:0004038.label: obsolete Bony spicule of ulnar epiphyseal plate

HP:0004039.label: Abnormal ulnar metaphysis morphology
HP:0004039.definition: Any structural abnormality of the portion of the ulna between the epiphysis and the diaphysis.

HP:0004042.label: Ulnar metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0004042.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis of the ulna.

HP:0004045.label: Sloping ulnar metaphysis
HP:0004045.definition: A sloped configuration of the metaphysis (shaft) of the ulna.

HP:0004047.label: Wide ulnar metaphysis
HP:0004047.definition: Increase in width (breadth) of the ulnar metaphysis.

HP:0004050.label: Absent hand
HP:0004050.definition: The total absence of the hand, with no bony elements distal to the radius or ulna.

HP:0004051.label: Advanced ossification of the hand bones
HP:0004051.definition: Ossification of hand bones at an earlier age than normal.
related_synonyms: Advanced maturation of the hand bones

HP:0004052.label: Delayed ossification of the hand bones
HP:0004052.definition: Ossification of hand bones is less advanced than would be expected according to age-adjusted norms.
exact_synonyms: Delay maturation/delayed ossification of the hand
related_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the hand bones

HP:0004053.label: Dysharmonic maturation of the hand bones
HP:0004053.definition: Pattern of hand-wrist development does not fit the normal sequence of ossification of the individual bones of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Dysharmonic ossification of the hand bones
Disharmonic maturation of the hand bones

HP:0004054.label: Sclerosis of hand bone
HP:0004054.definition: Osteosclerosis affecting one or more bones of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in hand bone
Increased bone density in hand bones

HP:0004057.label: Mitten deformity
HP:0004057.definition: Fusion of the hands and feet by a thin membrane of skin (scarring) seen in forms of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and leading to a "mitten" hand deformity.
HP:0004057.comment: Mitten deformity is also referred to as pseudosyndactyly, which should not be confused with true syndactyly (actual and complete fusion of fingers). Antenatally, pseudosyndactyly can be misinterpreted as syndactyly.

HP:0004060.label: Trident hand
HP:0004060.definition: A hand in which the fingers are of nearly equal length and deflected at the first interphalangeal joint, so as to give a forklike shape consisting of separation of the first and second as well as the third and fourth digits.
HP:0004060.comment: This abnormality is often seen in patients with achondroplasia.

HP:0004083.label: obsolete Laterally deviated terminal thumb phalanx

HP:0004090.label: obsolete Advanced maturation/advanced ossification of terminal thumb phalanx epiphysis

HP:0004097.label: Deviation of finger
HP:0004097.definition: Deviated fingers is a term that should be used if one or more fingers of the hand are deviated from their normal position, either to the radial or ulnar side. A deviation of a finger can be caused by an abnormal form of one or more of the phalanges of the affected finger, or by a deviation or displacement of one or more phalanges.
exact_synonyms: Finger pointing in a different direction than usual

HP:0004099.label: Macrodactyly
HP:0004099.definition: Significant increase in the length and girth of most or all of a digit compared to its contralateral digit (if unaffected) or compared to what would be expected for age/body build. The increased girth is accompanied by an increase in the dorso-ventral dimension AND the lateral dimension of the digit.
HP:0004099.comment: There are no recognized standards for the girth of digits and this finding can vary substantially in the population. This assessment relies on the judgment of the examiner to recognize when the difference between the expected and the observed is significant. The affected digits should be specified. The definition does not mandate the component of the increased size (bone, connective tissue, etc.), but should exclude edema. The requirement that the girth is most, or all, of the digit is intended to distinguish this from broad fingertips. This should be distinguished from Broad fingers or Broad fingertips as the girth is circumferential in macrodactyly, which is not the case for broad fingers or broad fingertips, which are increased only (or predominantly) in their lateral (A/P) width.

HP:0004100.label: Abnormal 2nd finger morphology
HP:0004100.definition: An anomaly of the second finger, also known as the index finger.

HP:0004110.label: obsolete Radially deviated index finger phalanges

HP:0004112.label: Midline nasal groove
HP:0004112.definition: An abnormal groove on the midline of the nose that may extend to the nasal tip.

HP:0004121.label: obsolete Radially displaced proximal index finger phalanx

HP:0004122.label: Midline defect of the nose
HP:0004122.definition: This term groups together three conditions that presumably represent different degrees of severity of a midline defect of the nose or nasal tip.

HP:0004132.label: Dimple on nasal tip
HP:0004132.definition: An abnormal indentation of the skin in the region of the nasal tip.

HP:0004139.label: obsolete Flared metaphysis of middle phalanx of index finger

HP:0004143.label: obsolete Radially deviated terminal index finger phalanx

HP:0004144.label: obsolete Duplication of terminal index finger phalanx

HP:0004150.label: Abnormal 3rd finger morphology
HP:0004150.definition: An anomaly of the third finger.

HP:0004196.label: obsolete Short phalanges of the ring finger

HP:0004197.label: Symphalangism of the 4th finger
HP:0004197.definition: Fusion of two or more bones of the 4th finger.

HP:0004207.label: Abnormal 5th finger morphology
HP:0004207.definition: An abnormality affecting one or both 5th fingers.

HP:0004209.label: Clinodactyly of the 5th finger
HP:0004209.definition: Clinodactyly refers to a bending or curvature of the fifth finger in the radial direction (i.e., towards the 4th finger).
HP:0004209.comment: Minor degrees of curvature of the small finger are so common as to be considered normal.
exact_synonyms: Permanent curving of the pinkie finger

HP:0004213.label: Abnormal 5th finger phalanx morphology
HP:0004213.definition: Abnormality of the phalanges of the 5th (little) finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the phalanges of the 5th finger
Abnormality of the pinkie finger bone
Abnormality of the little finger bone
Abnormality of the pinky finger bone

HP:0004216.label: Osteolytic defects of the phalanges of the 5th finger
HP:0004216.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the phalanges of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Lytic defects of the phalanges of the little finger

HP:0004218.label: Symphalangism of the 5th finger
HP:0004218.definition: Fusion of two or more bones of the 5th finger.

HP:0004219.label: Abnormality of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the middle bone of pinky finger
Abnormality of the middle bone of little finger
Abnormality of the middle bone of pinkie finger

HP:0004220.label: Short middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0004220.definition: Hypoplastic/small middle phalanx of the fifth finger.
HP:0004220.comment: Brachymesophalangia-V, a short and broad middle phalanx of the fifth digit, is the most common of all skeletal anomalies of the hand. When this feature appears alone, it is clinically known as brachydactyly type A3 (BDA3).

HP:0004222.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0004222.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the little finger of the hand, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of the phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of the outermost pinkie finger bone
Cone-shaped epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the little finger
Cone-shaped end part of the outermost pinky finger bone
Cone-shaped end part of the outermost little finger bone

HP:0004223.label: Ivory epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0004223.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the little finger, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the outermost pinkie finger bone
Ivory epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the little finger

HP:0004224.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0004224.definition: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the fifth finger. This epiphysis is located on the proximal end of the phalanx.

HP:0004226.definition: Curved appearance of the distal phalanx of the 5th (little) finger.
exact_synonyms: Curved terminal phalanx of the little finger

HP:0004227.label: Short distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0004227.definition: Hypoplastic/small distal phalanx of the fifth finger.

HP:0004230.label: Subluxation of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the little finger
HP:0004230.definition: A partial dislocation of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the little finger.
exact_synonyms: Partially dislocated innermost hinge joint of pinkie finger
Partially dislocated innermost hinge joint of pinky finger
Partially dislocated innermost hinge joint of little finger

HP:0004231.label: Carpal bone aplasia
HP:0004231.definition: Congenital absence of a carpal bone.
HP:0004231.comment: Radiographically difficult to distinguish between absent ossification of a carpal bone.

HP:0004232.label: Accessory carpal bones
HP:0004232.definition: The presence of more than the normal number of carpal bones.

HP:0004233.label: Advanced ossification of carpal bones
HP:0004233.definition: Ossification of carpal bones at an abnormally early age.

HP:0004234.label: Bone-in-a-bone appearance of carpal bones
HP:0004234.definition: The bone-in-bone sign is a radiographic finding produced by increased sclerosis (abnormally dense bone) occurring intermittently with zones of relatively normal bone density. This term should be used to describe such a finding in the carpal bones.

HP:0004236.label: Irregular carpal bones
HP:0004236.definition: Carpal bones with irregular or fragmented margins.

HP:0004241.label: Stippled calcification in carpal bones
HP:0004241.definition: Point-shaped (punctate) calcifications affecting the carpal bones.

HP:0004243.label: Abnormal scaphoid morphology
HP:0004243.definition: Any structural anomaly of the scaphoid. The scaphoid is the largest bone of the proximal row of carpal bones. It is located on the same side as the thumb.

HP:0004244.label: Accessory scaphoid
HP:0004244.definition: Variations in the development of carpal bones are uncommon, with the scaphoid bone typically forming from the fusion of the os centrale carpi and the radial chondrification center during embryogenesis. A bipartite scaphoid is a rare congenital disorder that occurs when these ossification centers fail to fuse.

HP:0004246.label: Delayed ossification of the scaphoid
HP:0004246.definition: Formation of bone tissue of scaphoid is less than expected for age.

HP:0004248.label: Abnormal lunate bone morphology
HP:0004248.definition: Any structural anomaly of the lunate bone, which is located in the proximal row of carpal bones.

HP:0004251.label: Lunate-triquetral fusion
HP:0004251.definition: Osseous fusion of the lunate and triquetrum.
HP:0004251.comment: Synostosis of the carpal bones is a rare congenital condition. Lunate and triquetrum are the bones more commonly involved.

HP:0004252.label: Abnormal trapezium morphology
HP:0004252.definition: An anomaly of the trapezium, which is the carpal bone located at the base of the thumb.

HP:0004254.label: Delayed ossification of the trapezium
HP:0004254.definition: Formation of bone tissue of trapezium is less than expected for age.

HP:0004256.label: Abnormal trapezoid bone morphology
HP:0004256.definition: A structural anomaly of the trapezoid bone, which is the smallest bone in the distal row of carpal bones.

HP:0004257.label: Delayed ossification of the trapezoid bone
HP:0004257.definition: Formation of bone tissue of trapezoid is less than expected for age.
exact_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the trapezoid bone

HP:0004259.label: Abnormal hamate bone morphology
HP:0004259.definition: A structural anomaly of the hamate bone, which is the ulnar-most bone located within the distal row of carpal bones, neighboured by the capitate bone radially.

HP:0004262.label: Abnormal capitate bone morphology
HP:0004262.definition: A structural anomaly of the capitate bone, which is the largest of the carpal bones in the human hand.

HP:0004267.label: Narrow small joints of the hand
exact_synonyms: Narrow small joints of the hand

HP:0004268.label: Osteoarthritis of the small joints of the hand

HP:0004269.label: Subluxation of the small joints of the hand
HP:0004269.definition: A partial dislocation of some or all of the small joints of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Partial dislocation of small joints of hand

HP:0004273.label: Cupped metaphyses of hand bones
exact_synonyms: Cupped wide portion of hand bones

HP:0004276.label: Exostoses of hand bones
HP:0004276.definition: Abnormal formation of new bone on the surface of a bone of the hand.

HP:0004278.label: Synostosis involving bones of the hand
HP:0004278.definition: An abnormal union between bones or parts of bones of the hand.

HP:0004279.label: Short palm
HP:0004279.comment: This term refers to a developmental finding resulting in short palms. This term is reserved for individuals with shortening of all four metacarpals 2-5. Individuals with fewer than four shortened metacarpals (in a eudactylous hand, the metacarpals of F2-5) should be coded as Metacarpal, short. See the entry for Hand, small for a discussion of this finding. "Short hand" should not be used as it is a bundle of two readily separable terms, Fingers, short (which, as noted above, can itself be a bundled term) and Palm, short.

HP:0004283.label: Narrow palm
HP:0004283.definition: For children from birth to 4 years of age, the palm width is more than 2 SD below the mean; for children from 4 to 16 years of age the palm width is below the 5th centile; or, the width of the palm appears disproportionately narrow for its length.
HP:0004283.comment: Palm width is measured across the palm at the level of the MCPJ (radial aspect of the F2 MCPJ to the ulnar aspect of the F5 MCPJ). Norms are specified in [Hall et al., 2007]. Caution is advised for the subjective assessment as the breadth may be in the normal range with disproportionately increased length, which appears narrow. This finding may be associated with elongated/slender limbs in general, but that finding does not bear on the coding of this feature. Proximal narrowing may indicate small thenar or hypothenar eminences. This term replaces "narrow hands" as that term may leave the impression that it includes the thumb, which it does not.

HP:0004286.label: Patchy sclerosis of hand bones
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in hand bones

HP:0004290.label: Sclerosis of hand bones with transverse striations

HP:0004294.label: Subluxation of metacarpal phalangeal joints
HP:0004294.definition: A partial dislocation affecting some or all of the metacarpophalangeal joints.

HP:0004295.label: Abnormal gastric mucosa morphology
HP:0004295.definition: An abnormality of the gastric mucous membrane.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the mucous membrane layer of stomach

HP:0004297.label: Abnormality of the biliary system
HP:0004297.definition: An abnormality of the biliary system.

HP:0004298.label: Abnormal abdominal wall morphology
HP:0004298.definition: The presence of any abnormality affecting the abdominal wall.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of external features of the abdomen

HP:0004299.label: Hernia of the abdominal wall
HP:0004299.definition: The presence of a hernia in the abdominal wall.
HP:0004299.comment: A hernia refers to a sac formed by the lining of the abdominal cavity (peritoneum). The sac can protrude through a hole or weak area in the abdominal fascia.

HP:0004303.label: Abnormal muscle fiber morphology
HP:0004303.definition: Any abnormality of the skeletal muscle cell. Muscle fibers are subdivided into two types. Type I fibers are fatigue-resistant and rich in oxidative enzymes (they stain light with the myosin ATPase reaction), and type II fibers are fast-contracting, fatigue-prone, and rich in glycolytic enzymes (these fibers stain darkly). Normal muscle tissue has a random distribution of type I and type II fibers.
HP:0004303.comment: Normal human muscle is composed of many individual muscle fibers bundled together by layers of connective tissue that are arranged in a nesting-doll like fashion. The inner most structure, the single muscle fiber, is covered by a thin layer of primarily reticular fibers called the endomysium. The endomysium is quite inconspicuous and muscle fibers appear to be in direct contact with each other. The finest capillaries, nerve twigs and lymphatic capillaries are found within the endomysium. Groups of muscle fibers are bound together by the thicker perimysium, forming structures called fascicles. Capillaries, nerve fibers and lymphatic vessels also track in the perimyseum. Bundles of fascicles are encased within the dense irregular connective tissue of the epimysium. These connective tissue layers provide mechanical protection for the muscle fibers and increase the tensile strength of the muscle. The layers are continuous with the tendon, which provides attachment to bone. Individual muscle fibers are syncytia, formed by embryonic fusion of many myoblasts or later, myosatellite cells. Each muscle fiber contains many nuclei, peripherally positioned immediately adjacent to the sarcolemmal membrane. In healthy muscle only 3-5 percent of fibers contain nuclei that are located internally, within the cell, but many disease processes lead to internal nuclei. Each nucleus provides a segment of the cell with needed translated protein products.

HP:0004305.label: Involuntary movements
HP:0004305.definition: Involuntary contractions of muscle leading to involuntary movements of extremities, neck, trunk, or face.

HP:0004307.label: Abnormal anatomic location of the heart
HP:0004307.definition: Developmental defect characterized by an anomalous anatomic location of the heart.

HP:0004309.label: Ventricular preexcitation
HP:0004309.definition: An abnormality in which the cardiac ventricles depolarize too early as a result of an abnormality of cardiac conduction pathways such as an accessory pathway.
HP:0004309.comment: Pre-excitation syndromes are generally caused by accelerated conduction along an accessory pathway, but in some cases there is accelerated conduction through the normal AV node.

HP:0004312.label: Abnormal reticulocyte morphology
HP:0004312.comment: Reticulocytes are immature erythrocytes that show a basophilic reticulum under vital staining.

HP:0004313.label: Decreased circulating immunoglobulin concentration
HP:0004313.definition: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin in blood.
HP:0004313.comment: In humans, immunoglobulins comprise the five antibody isotypes IgA, IgD, IgE, IgG and IgM.

HP:0004315.label: Decreased circulating IgG concentration
HP:0004315.definition: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in blood.

HP:0004319.label: Decreased circulating aldosterone concentration
HP:0004319.comment: Aldosterone is a hormone that is produce by the adrenal cortex and that acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts to favor retention of sodium excretion of potassium, and increased water retention, thereby tending to increase blood pressure. Aldosterone is sometimes called a mineralocorticoid because of its influence on sodium homeostasis.

HP:0004320.label: Vaginal fistula
HP:0004320.definition: The presence of a fistula of the vagina.

HP:0004321.label: Bladder fistula
HP:0004321.definition: The presence of a fistula connecting the urinary bladder to another organ or the skin. The fistula can involve the bowel, the vagina, or rarely, the skin.

HP:0004322.label: Short stature
HP:0004322.definition: A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. Although there is no universally accepted definition of short stature, many refer to "short stature" as height more than 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender (or below the 3rd percentile for age and gender dependent norms).

HP:0004323.label: Abnormality of body weight
HP:0004323.definition: An abnormal increase or decrease of weight or an abnormal distribution of mass in the body.

HP:0004326.label: Cachexia
HP:0004326.definition: Severe weight loss, wasting of muscle, loss of appetite, and general debility related to a chronic disease.

HP:0004327.label: Abnormal vitreous humor morphology
HP:0004327.definition: Any structural anomaly of the vitreous body.
HP:0004327.comment: The vitreous humor is the clear gel that fills the space between the lens and the retina.

HP:0004328.label: Abnormal anterior eye segment morphology
HP:0004328.definition: An abnormality of the anterior segment of the eyeball (which comprises the structures in front of the vitreous humor: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens).
HP:0004328.comment: The anterior segment comprises the structures in front of the vitreous humor: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the anterior segment of the eyeball
Abnormality of the anterior segment of the globe
Abnormality of the anterior segment of the eye

HP:0004329.label: Abnormal posterior eye segment morphology
HP:0004329.comment: The posterior segment comprises the anterior hyaloid membrane and all of the optical structures behind it: the vitreous humor, retina, choroid, and optic nerve.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the posterior segment of the eye
Abnormality of the posterior segment of the eyeball
Abnormal morphology of the posterior segment of the globe
Abnormality of the posterior segment of the globe

HP:0004330.label: Increased skull ossification
HP:0004330.definition: An increase in the magnitude or amount of ossification of the skull.

HP:0004331.label: Decreased skull ossification
HP:0004331.definition: A reduction in the magnitude or amount of ossification of the skull.

HP:0004332.label: Abnormal lymphocyte morphology
HP:0004332.comment: A lymphocyte refers to a cell of the B cell, T cell, or natural killer cell lineage.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of cells of the lymphoid lineage

HP:0004333.label: Bone-marrow foam cells
HP:0004333.definition: The presence of foam cells in the bone marrow, generally demonstrated by bone-marrow aspiration or biopsy. Foam cells have a vacuolated appearance due to the presence of complex lipid deposits, giving them a foamy or soap-suds appearance.
exact_synonyms: Large vacuolated foam cells ('NP cells') on bone marrow biopsy
Large vacuolated foam cells on bone marrow biopsy

HP:0004334.label: Dermal atrophy
HP:0004334.definition: Partial or complete wasting (atrophy) of the skin.

HP:0004336.label: Myelin outfoldings
HP:0004336.definition: The presence of excessive redundant myelin in the peripheral nerve sheath.
HP:0004336.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by nerve biopsy (e.g., sural nerve biopsy).
exact_synonyms: Excessive focal folding of myelin sheaths

HP:0004337.label: Abnormality of amino acid metabolism
HP:0004337.definition: Abnormality of an amino acid metabolic process.

HP:0004338.label: Abnormal circulating aromatic amino acid concentration
HP:0004338.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a aromatic amino acid in the blood circulation.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of aromatic amino acid family metabolism

HP:0004339.label: Abnormal circulating sulfur amino acid concentration
HP:0004339.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a sulfur amino acid in the blood circulation.
HP:0004339.comment: Cysteine and methionine contain a sulfur atom.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal circulating sulphur amino acid concentration

HP:0004341.label: Abnormality of vitamin B12 metabolism
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the vitamin B12 metabolism

HP:0004342.label: Abnormal galactosidase enyzme activity
HP:0004342.definition: Abnormality of galactoside metabolism. A galactoside is a glycoside (a sugar moiety bound to some other moiety) containing galactose.

HP:0004343.label: Abnormal glycosphingolipid metabolism
HP:0004343.comment: Glycosphingolipids are a subtype of glycolipids containing the amino alcohol sphingosine. A glycosphingolipid is a carbohydrate-containing derivative of a sphingoid or ceramide. It is understood that the carbohydrate residue is attached by a glycosidic linkage to O-1 of the sphingoid.

HP:0004345.label: Ganglioside accumulation
HP:0004345.definition: Defects in the lysosomal glycosidases or specific co-activators, result in accumulation of the substrates, such as glycosphingolipids, including gangliosides in GM1 gangliosidosis (Tay-Sachs disease) and GM2 gangliosidosis (Sandhoff disease).
HP:0004345.comment: A ganglioside is composed of a glycosphingolipid with one or more sialic acids linked on the sugar chain.

HP:0004347.label: Weakness of muscles of respiration
HP:0004347.definition: Reduced function of the muscles required to generate subatmospheric pressure in the thoracic cavity during breathing: the diaphragm, the external intercostal and the interchondral part of the internal intercostal muscles.

HP:0004348.label: Abnormality of bone mineral density
HP:0004348.definition: This term applies to all changes in bone mineral density which (depending on severity) can be seen on x-rays as a change in density and or structure of the bone. Changes may affect all bones of the organism, just certain bones or only parts of bones and include decreased mineralisation as may be seen in osteoporosis or increased mineralisation and or ossification as in osteopetrosis, exostoses or any kind of atopic calicfications of different origin and distribution. The overall amount of mineralization of the bone-organ can be measured as the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones, usually measured by densitometry of the lumbar spine or hip. The measurements are usually reported as g/cm3 or as a Z-score (the number of standard deviations above or below the mean for the patient's age and sex). Note that measurement with this method does not reflect local changes in other bones, and as such might not be correct with regard the hole bone-organ.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of bone mineralisation and ossification

HP:0004349.label: Reduced bone mineral density
HP:0004349.definition: A reduction of bone mineral density, that is, of the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones.
exact_synonyms: Low solidness and mass of the bones
Decreased bone mineral density Z score

HP:0004352.label: Abnormal circulating purine concentration
HP:0004352.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a purine in the blood circulation.
HP:0004352.comment: Purines are nitrogenous bases including the two nucleotide bases deoxyadenosine and deoxyguanosine.

HP:0004353.label: Abnormal circulating pyrimidine concentration
HP:0004353.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a pyrimidine in the blood circulation.

HP:0004354.label: Abnormal circulating carboxylic acid concentration
HP:0004354.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carboxylic acid in the blood circulation.
HP:0004354.comment: Carboxylic acid refers to an organic compound that contains a carboxyl group (-COOH).

HP:0004356.label: Abnormality of lysosomal metabolism
HP:0004356.comment: A major lysosomal function is the breakdown and recycling of macromolecules and organelles into basic precursors.

HP:0004357.label: Abnormal circulating leucine concentration
HP:0004357.definition: Any deviation from the normal circulation of leucine in the blood circulation.

HP:0004358.label: Abnormality of superoxide metabolism
HP:0004358.comment: NADPH oxidase catalyzes the production of superoxide, which in turn can react to form hydrogen peroxide, HOCl, and hydroxyl radical. Together, these oxygen-derived species participate in bacterial killing.

HP:0004359.label: Abnormal circulating fatty-acid concentration
HP:0004359.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of a fatty acid in the blood circulation.
HP:0004359.comment: A fatty acid is an aliphatic monocarboxylic acid derived from or contained in esterified form. Natural fatty acids commonly have a chain of 4 to 28 carbons (usually unbranched and even-numbered), which may be saturated or unsaturated. R-COOH. Fatty acids are usually derived from triglycerides or phospholipids.

HP:0004360.label: Abnormality of acid-base homeostasis
HP:0004360.definition: An abnormality of the balance or maintenance of the balance of acids and bases in bodily fluids, resulting in an abnormal pH.

HP:0004361.label: Abnormal circulating leptin concentration
HP:0004361.definition: An abnormal concentration of leptin in the blood.

HP:0004362.label: Abnormal enteric ganglion morphology
HP:0004362.definition: An abnormality of the enteric nervous system, which comprises two types of ganglia, the myenteric (Auerbach's) and submucosal (Meissner's) plexuses. The enteric nervous system functions to control gut movement, fluid exchange between the gut and its lumen, and local blood flow.

HP:0004363.label: Abnormal circulating calcium concentration
HP:0004363.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of calcium in the blood circulation.

HP:0004364.label: Abnormal circulating nitrogen compound concentration
HP:0004364.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a nitrogen compound in the blood circulation.
HP:0004364.comment: Ammonia (NH3), one of the most clinically important nitrogen compounds in human metabolism, is a substance containing nitrogen resulting from the catabolism of protein. It is converted to the less toxic substance urea prior to excretion in urine.

HP:0004365.label: Abnormal circulating tryptophan concentration
HP:0004365.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of tryptophan in the blood circulation.

HP:0004368.label: Increased circulating purine concentration
HP:0004368.definition: Abnormally elevated concentration of a purine compound. Purine compounds are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring.

HP:0004369.label: Decreased circulating purine concentration
HP:0004369.definition: Abnormally reduced concentration of a purine compound. Purine compounds are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring.

HP:0004371.label: Abnormality of glycosaminoglycan metabolism
HP:0004371.comment: A glycosaminoglycan is any polysaccharide containing a substantial proportion of aminomonosaccharide residues. Glycosaminoglycan (GAG) are long unbranched polysaccharides consisting of a repeating disaccharide unit. Among the most common GAGs are chondroitin sulfate, dermatan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, keratan sulfate, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan.

HP:0004372.label: Reduced consciousness
HP:0004372.definition: Abnormally diminished level of attention, responsiveness, or wakefulness.

HP:0004373.label: Focal dystonia
HP:0004373.definition: A type of dystonia that is localized to a specific part of the body.

HP:0004374.label: Hemiplegia/hemiparesis
HP:0004374.definition: Loss of strength in the arm, leg, and sometimes face on one side of the body. Hemiplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas hemiparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.
exact_synonyms: Paralysis or weakness of one side of body

HP:0004375.label: Neoplasm of the nervous system
HP:0004375.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the nervous system.

HP:0004376.label: Neuroblastic tumor
HP:0004376.definition: A family of tumors arising in the embryonal remnants of the sympathetic nervous system, which includes neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, and ganglioneuroma.
HP:0004376.comment: Along with neuroblastomas, ganglioneuromas and ganglioneuroblastomas are collectively known as neuroblastic tumors.

HP:0004377.label: Hematological neoplasm
HP:0004377.definition: Neoplasms located in the blood and blood-forming tissue (the bone marrow and lymphatic tissue).

HP:0004378.label: Abnormality of the anus
HP:0004378.comment: The anal canal is continuous proximally with the rectum and distally terminates with the anus.

HP:0004379.label: Abnormality of alkaline phosphatase level
HP:0004379.definition: An abnormality of alkaline phosphatase level.
HP:0004379.comment: Note that the alkaline phosphatase family has four isoenzymes in humans, each of which additionally can have different isoforms. The primary clinical importance of measuring alkaline phosphatase is to check the possibility of bone disease or liver disease.

HP:0004380.label: Aortic valve calcification
HP:0004380.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in the aortic valve.

HP:0004381.label: Supravalvular aortic stenosis
HP:0004381.definition: A pathological narrowing in the region above the aortic valve associated with restricted left ventricular outflow.

HP:0004382.label: Mitral valve calcification
HP:0004382.definition: Abnormal calcification of the mitral valve.

HP:0004383.label: Hypoplastic left ventricle
HP:0004383.definition: A severe congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of the left ventricle.
HP:0004383.comment: This feature most often occurs as part of the Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), which may comprise additional malfmorations atresia of the aortic or mitral orifice and hypoplasia of the ascending aorta. If present, the additional features should be coded with the corresponding HPO terms.

HP:0004384.label: Type I truncus arteriosus
HP:0004384.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with a short pulmonary trunk arises from the truncus arteriosus, giving rise to both pulmonary arteries.
HP:0004384.comment: According to the Van Praagh classification (PMID:2856609). The Van Praagh classification additionally specifies the presence (subtype A) or absence (subtype B) of a ventricular septal defect.

HP:0004386.label: Gastrointestinal inflammation
HP:0004386.definition: Inflammation of the alimentary part of the gastrointestinal system.

HP:0004387.label: Enterocolitis
HP:0004387.definition: An inflammation of the colon and small intestine. However, most conditions are either categorized as Enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine) or Colitis (inflammation of the large intestine).

HP:0004388.label: Microcolon
HP:0004388.definition: A colon of abnormally small caliber.

HP:0004389.label: Intestinal pseudo-obstruction
HP:0004389.definition: A functional rather than mechanical obstruction of the intestines, associated with manifestations that resemble those caused by an intestinal obstruction, including distension, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or diarrhea, in an individual in whom a mechanical blockage has been excluded.

HP:0004390.label: Hamartomatous polyposis
HP:0004390.definition: Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas. These can occur throughout the gastrointestinal tract. Hamartomatous polyps are composed of the normal cellular elements of the gastrointestinal tract, but have a markedly distorted architecture.
HP:0004390.comment: Patients with Cowden-Syndrom for example often have multiple hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps.

HP:0004392.label: Prune belly
HP:0004392.definition: A kind of congenital defect of the anterior abdominal wall in which the intestines are evident through the thin, lax, and protruding abdominal wall in affected infants.
HP:0004392.comment: Wrinkly folds of skin covering the abdomen as a result of partial or complete lack of abdominal muscles.

HP:0004395.label: Malnutrition
HP:0004395.definition: A deficiency in the intake of energy and nutrients.

HP:0004397.label: Ectopic anus
HP:0004397.definition: Abnormal displacement or malposition of the anus.

HP:0004398.label: Peptic ulcer
HP:0004398.definition: The term peptic ulcer refers to acid peptic injury of the digestive tract, resulting in mucosal break reaching the submucosa. Peptic ulcers are usually located in the stomach or proximal duodenum, but they can also be found in the esophagus or Meckel's diverticulum. Infection with Helicobacter pylori and the use of non steroidal antiinflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or aspirin are the main risk factors of both gastric and duodenal peptic ulcers.
HP:0004398.comment: Symptoms of peptic ulcer disease have limited predictive value because they are non-specific. Patients with duodenal ulcers typically feel hungry or have nocturnal abdominal pain. By contrast, patients with gastric ulcers have postprandial abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and weight loss. Patients with untreated peptic ulcer disease typically have relapsing symptoms because of spontaneous healing and relapse while the causal factor (eg, H pylori infection or NSAID use) persists.
exact_synonyms: Sore in the lining of gastrointestinal tract

HP:0004401.label: Meconium ileus
HP:0004401.definition: Obstruction of the intestine due to abnormally thick meconium.
HP:0004401.comment: Obstruction of the intestine is known as ileus.

HP:0004408.label: Abnormality of the sense of smell
HP:0004408.definition: An anomaly in the ability to perceive and distinguish scents (odors).
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the sense of smell

HP:0004409.label: Hyposmia
HP:0004409.definition: A decreased sensitivity to odorants (that is, a decreased ability to perceive odors).

HP:0004411.label: Deviated nasal septum
HP:0004411.definition: Positioning of the nasal septum to the right or left in contrast to the normal midline position of the nasal septum.

HP:0004414.label: Abnormality of the pulmonary artery
HP:0004414.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary artery.

HP:0004415.label: Pulmonary artery stenosis
HP:0004415.definition: An abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP:0004415.comment: Stenosis, or narrowing, of the branches of the pulmonary artery is a type of congenital heart disease that, if left untreated, may lead to significant complications. Ideally, interventions to treat stenosis occur before significant complications or long-term sequelae take place, often within the first 2 years of life.

HP:0004417.label: Intermittent claudication
HP:0004417.definition: Intermittent claudication is a symptom of peripheral arterial occlusive disease. After having walked over a distance which is individually characteristic, the patients experience pain or cramps in the calves, feet or thighs which typically subsides on standing still.
HP:0004417.comment: Vascular intermittent claudication caused by peripheral arterial disease most often related to severe atherosclerosis.

HP:0004418.label: Thrombophlebitis
HP:0004418.definition: Inflammation of a vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).

HP:0004419.label: Recurrent thrombophlebitis
HP:0004419.definition: Repeated episodes of inflammation of a vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).

HP:0004420.label: Arterial thrombosis
HP:0004420.definition: The formation of a blood clot inside an artery.

HP:0004421.label: Elevated systolic blood pressure
HP:0004421.definition: Abnormal increase in systolic blood pressure.
HP:0004421.comment: Normal systolic blood pressure is less than 120 mmHg in adults.

HP:0004422.label: Biparietal narrowing
HP:0004422.definition: A narrowing of the biparietal diameter (i.e., of the transverse distance between the protuberances of the two parietal bones of the skull).

HP:0004423.label: Cranium bifidum occultum
HP:0004423.definition: Cranium bifidum occultum, also known as Catlin mark, is a congenital midline skull defect presenting as an enlarged posterior fontanelle in the upper posterior angle of the parietal bone close to the intersection of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures. Cranium bifidum occultum occurs due to a defect in intramembranous ossification, a process through which skull bones (frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and occipital bones superior to the mendosal suture) ossify under a vascularized membrane toward the midline to cover the brain. Unlike cranium bifidum cysticum, cranium bifidum occultum does not have herniation of intracranial contents. As the skull grows, the midline cranium bifidum occultum defect is separated into bilateral enlarged parietal foramina (EPF) by a midline osseous bridge.
HP:0004423.comment: Cranium bifidum tends to resolve into distinct enlarged parietal foramina over the first few years of life through the midline ossification of a central bridge of bone bisecting the defect.

HP:0004426.label: Abnormal cheek morphology
HP:0004426.definition: An abnormality of the cheek- one of two bilateral soft tissue facial structures in the region of the face inferior to the eyes and between the nose and the ear. "Buccal" means relating to the cheek. The cheek is part of the midface

HP:0004428.label: Elfin facies
HP:0004428.definition: This is a description previously used to describe a facial form characterized by a short, upturned nose, wide mouth, widely spaced eyes, and full cheeks. Because of the imprecision in this definition it is preferable to describe these features precisely. This term is retained because it was often used in the past, but it should not be used for new annotations.

HP:0004429.label: Recurrent viral infections
HP:0004429.definition: Increased susceptibility to viral infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral infection.

HP:0004430.label: Severe combined immunodeficiency
HP:0004430.definition: A type of primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.

HP:0004431.label: Reduced circulating complement concentration
HP:0004431.definition: An immunodeficiency defined by the absent or suboptimal functioning of one of the complement system proteins.

HP:0004432.label: Agammaglobulinemia
HP:0004432.definition: A lasting absence of total IgG and total IgA and total IgM in the blood circulation, whereby at most trace quantities can be measured.

HP:0004433.label: Secretory IgA deficiency
HP:0004433.definition: Deficiency of secretory IgA (polymers of 2-4 IgA monomers are linked by two additional chains) and is the primary antibody response at the mucosal level, where it forms immune complexes with pathogens and allergens.

HP:0004434.label: Decreased circulating complement C8 concentration
HP:0004434.definition: Concentration of the complement component C8 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
HP:0004434.comment: The eighth component of complement (C8) plays an important role in the function of membrane attack complex (MAC) that is generated on target cells upon activation of the complement system. MAC is generated by sequential addition of C5b, C6, C7, C8, and C9 molecules, which results in the transmembrane pore and eventual cell lysis. Individuals with C8 deficiency tend to have recurrent neisserial infections.

HP:0004437.label: Cranial hyperostosis
HP:0004437.definition: Excessive growth of the bones of cranium, i.e., of the skull.

HP:0004438.label: Hyperostosis frontalis interna
HP:0004438.definition: Bony overgrowth of the internal (endosteal) surface of the frontal bone.
exact_synonyms: Overgrowth of the inner surface of the frontal bone
Excessive growth of inner surface of the frontal bone
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the frontal bone

HP:0004439.label: Craniofacial dysostosis
HP:0004439.definition: A characteristic appearance resulting from defective ossification of craniofacial bones.
HP:0004439.comment: Note: This term is used in the medical literature to describe an appearance of the face of patients with Crouzon syndrome (also called craniofacial dysostosis), which is characterized by acrocephaly, exophthalmos, hypertelorism, strabismus, parrot-beaked nose, and hypoplastic maxilla. This is thus probably mainly used as a bundled term and should be replaced by better descriptions in the future.

HP:0004440.label: Coronal craniosynostosis
HP:0004440.definition: Premature closure of the coronal suture of skull.

HP:0004442.label: Sagittal craniosynostosis
HP:0004442.definition: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the sagittal suture.
exact_synonyms: Early closure of midline skull joint

HP:0004443.label: Lambdoidal craniosynostosis
HP:0004443.definition: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the lambdoidal suture.

HP:0004444.label: Spherocytosis
HP:0004444.definition: The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped.
HP:0004444.comment: Erythrocytes are normally biconcave rather than spherical.

HP:0004445.label: Elliptocytosis
HP:0004445.definition: The presence of elliptical, cigar-shaped erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear.
HP:0004445.comment: Elliptocytes (ovalocytes) are abnormal erythrocytes ranging from slightly oval to elongated cigar-shaped forms.

HP:0004446.label: Stomatocytosis
HP:0004446.definition: The presence of erythrocytes with a mouth-shaped (stoma) area of central pallor on peripheral blood smear.

HP:0004447.label: Poikilocytosis
HP:0004447.definition: The presence of abnormally shaped erythrocytes.
HP:0004447.comment: General description for abnormally shaped erythrocytes.

HP:0004448.label: Fulminant hepatic failure
HP:0004448.definition: Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as fulminant if there is onset of encephalopathy within 4 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.

HP:0004450.label: Preauricular skin furrow
HP:0004450.definition: A groove of the skin immediately in front of the ear.
exact_synonyms: Skin sulcus in front of the ear
Skin groove in front of the ear

HP:0004451.label: Postauricular skin tag
HP:0004451.definition: A rudimentary tag of ear tissue often containing a core of cartilage and located just in back of the auricle (outer part of the ear).

HP:0004452.label: Abnormality of the middle ear ossicles
HP:0004452.definition: An abnormality of the middle-ear ossicles (three small bones called malleus, incus, and stapes) that are contained within the middle ear and serve to transmit sounds from the air to the fluid-filled labyrinth (cochlea).

HP:0004453.label: Overfolding of the superior helices
HP:0004453.definition: A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal.

HP:0004458.label: Dilatated internal auditory canal
HP:0004458.definition: The presence of a dilated inner part of external acoustic meatus.

HP:0004459.label: Exostosis of the external auditory canal
HP:0004459.definition: A benign bony growth projecting outward from a bone surface within the external auditory canal.

HP:0004461.label: Congenital earlobe sinuses
HP:0004461.definition: Pits in the earlobes at the location where ears are typically pierced for earrings.

HP:0004463.label: Absent brainstem auditory responses
HP:0004463.definition: Lack of measurable response to stimulation of auditory evoked potentials.

HP:0004464.label: Postauricular pit
HP:0004464.definition: Benign congenital lesion of the postauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.

HP:0004466.label: Delayed brainstem auditory evoked response conduction time
HP:0004466.definition: An abnormal increase (delay) in the conduction time of the brainstem auditory-evoked response.

HP:0004467.label: Preauricular pit
HP:0004467.definition: Small indentation anterior to the insertion of the ear.
HP:0004467.comment: Preauricular cysts and sinuses are ectodermal remnants from an aberrant development of the auditory tubercles, tend to be bilateral and are localized anterior to the tragus of the ear. The preauricular sinus is a benign congenital lesion of the preauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit. It is also known as preauricular pit, preauricular fistula, preauricular tract and preauricular cyst. It can be asymptomatic or present as an infected and discharging sinus. It presents as a small pit adjacent to the external ear usually located at the anterior margin of the ascending limb of the helix. The preauricular sinus is variably also termed a preauricular pit, preauricular fistula, preauricular tract and preauricular cyst.
exact_synonyms: Pit in front of the ear

HP:0004468.label: Anomalous tracheal cartilage
HP:0004468.definition: An abnormality of the C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage, normally 16 to 20 in number, that occupy the anterior two-thirds of the circumference of the trachea (the posterior portion of the ring is completed by fibrous and smooth muscle tissue).

HP:0004470.label: Atretic occipital cephalocele
HP:0004470.definition: A congenital defect in the occipital region of the skull, covered by skin of the scalp and containing meninges or remnants of glial or neural tissues.

HP:0004471.label: Aplasia cutis congenita over the scalp vertex
HP:0004471.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp vertex, often just lateral to the midline.

HP:0004472.label: Mandibular hyperostosis
HP:0004472.comment: This bundled term will be made obsolete in future versions of the HPO.

HP:0004474.label: Persistent open anterior fontanelle
HP:0004474.definition: The anterior fontanelle generally ossifies by around the 18th month of life. A persistent open anterior fontanelle is diagnosed if closure is delayed beyond this age.

HP:0004476.label: Aplasia cutis congenita over parietal area
HP:0004476.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp in the parietal area.
exact_synonyms: Absent cutis congenita over parietal area

HP:0004481.label: Progressive macrocephaly
HP:0004481.definition: The progressive development of an abnormally large skull.

HP:0004482.label: Relative macrocephaly
HP:0004482.definition: A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.

HP:0004484.label: Craniofacial asymmetry
HP:0004484.definition: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.

HP:0004485.label: Cessation of head growth
HP:0004485.definition: Stagnation of head growth seen as flattening of the head circumference curve.

HP:0004487.label: Acrobrachycephaly
HP:0004487.definition: An abnormality of head shape characterized by the presence of a short, wide head as well as a pointy or conical form of the top of the head owing to premature closure of the coronal and lambdoid sutures.

HP:0004488.label: Macrocephaly at birth
HP:0004488.definition: The presence of an abnormally large skull with onset at birth.
exact_synonyms: Head circumference large for gestational age

HP:0004490.label: Calvarial hyperostosis
HP:0004490.comment: The calvaria (skull cap) is made up of the frontal, occipital, right and left parietal, right and left temporal, sphenoid, and ethmoid bones, and thus comprises the upper dome-like part of the skull and does not include the lower jaw.

HP:0004491.label: Large posterior fontanelle
HP:0004491.definition: An enlargement of the posterior fontanelle relative to age-dependent norms.

HP:0004492.label: Widely patent fontanelles and sutures
HP:0004492.definition: An abnormally increased width of the cranial fontanelles and sutures.
HP:0004492.comment: This term indicates that both the fontanelles and the sutures are widely patent and thus represents a severe form of delay in closure of the fontanelles/sutures.

HP:0004493.label: Craniofacial hyperostosis
HP:0004493.definition: Excessive growth of the craniofacial bones.
exact_synonyms: Excessive bone growth of the skull and face

HP:0004499.label: Chronic rhinitis due to narrow nasal airway
exact_synonyms: Chronic nasal inflammation due to narrow nasal airway

HP:0004502.label: Bilateral choanal atresia
HP:0004502.definition: Bilateral absence (atresia) of the posterior nasal aperture (choana).
exact_synonyms: Bilateral blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
Bilateral obstruction of the rear opening of the nasal cavity

HP:0004510.label: Pancreatic islet-cell hyperplasia
HP:0004510.definition: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans, i.e., of the regions of the pancreas that contain its endocrine cells.
HP:0004510.comment: The islets of Langerhans contain the alpha cells (producing glucagon), beta cells (insulin and amylin), delta cells (somatostatin),PP cells (pancreatic polypeptide), and the epsilon cells (ghrelin).

HP:0004523.label: Long eyebrows
HP:0004523.definition: Increased length of the hairs of the eyebrows.

HP:0004524.label: Temporal hypotrichosis
HP:0004524.definition: Reduced or lacking hair growth in the temporal region (i.e., around the temples on the side of the skull).
exact_synonyms: Reduced hair growth in temporal region

HP:0004527.label: Large clumps of pigment irregularly distributed along hair shaft
exact_synonyms: Large clumps of pigment irregularly distributed along hair shaft

HP:0004528.label: Generalized hypotrichosis
HP:0004528.definition: Reduced or lacking hair growth in a generalized distribution.

HP:0004532.label: Sacral hypertrichosis
HP:0004532.definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the sacral region.

HP:0004535.label: Anterior cervical hypertrichosis
HP:0004535.definition: Anterior cervical hypertrichosis (ACH) or 'hairy throat' refers to the presence of a tuft of terminal hair on the anterior neck, just above the laryngeal prominence.

HP:0004540.label: Congenital, generalized hypertrichosis
HP:0004540.definition: A confluent, generalized overgrowth of silvery blonde to gray lanugo hair at birth.
HP:0004540.comment: Hypertrichosis refers to excessive, abnormal hairiness.

HP:0004552.label: Scarring alopecia of scalp
related_synonyms: Hair loss on scalp from scarring condition

HP:0004558.label: Cervical platyspondyly
HP:0004558.definition: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates affecting the cervical spine.

HP:0004563.label: Increased spinal bone density
HP:0004563.definition: Increased bone density affecting the bones of the spine (vertebral column).

HP:0004566.label: Pear-shaped vertebrae
HP:0004566.definition: Bulbous appearance of the anterior vertebral bodies, such that the vertebral bodies have the greatest vertical height anteriorly as well as bulbous anterior superior-inferior contours.

HP:0004568.label: Beaking of vertebral bodies
HP:0004568.definition: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the vertebral bodies.

HP:0004570.label: Increased vertebral height
HP:0004570.definition: Increased top to bottom height of vertebral bodies.

HP:0004573.label: Anterior wedging of T11
HP:0004573.definition: An abnormality of the shape of the thoracic vertebra T11 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).
exact_synonyms: Anterior wedging of the 11th thoracic vertebra

HP:0004576.label: Sclerotic vertebral endplates
HP:0004576.definition: Sclerosis (increased density) affecting vertebral end plates.

HP:0004580.label: Anterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
HP:0004580.definition: An excessive concavity of the anterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.
HP:0004580.comment: One cause of anterior scalloping is an aortic aneurysm, which because of its pulsatile pressure can cause a convex defect along the anterior surface of an adjacent vertebra body. The defect may have a sclerotic margin.

HP:0004586.label: Biconcave vertebral bodies
HP:0004586.definition: Exaggerated concavity of the anterior or posterior surface of the vertebral body, i.e., the upper and lower vertebral endplates are hollowed inward.
HP:0004586.comment: This finding has been called fish or codfish vertebra because of the characteristic biconcave form of fish vertebral bodies.

HP:0004590.label: Hypoplastic sacrum
HP:0004590.definition: A developmental defect characterized by undergrowth of the sacrum, which is a large, triangular bone at the base of the spine that forms by the fusing of the sacral vertebrae (S1-S5).

HP:0004592.label: Thoracic platyspondyly
HP:0004592.definition: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates affecting the thoracic spine.

HP:0004594.label: Hump-shaped mound of bone in central and posterior portions of vertebral endplate

HP:0004598.label: Supernumerary vertebral ossification centers
HP:0004598.definition: Three ossification sites are present in typical vertebral bodies (C3-L5): a single ossification center in the vertebral body, and one each in the two neural arches. This term applies if there are additional vertebral ossification centers present during the development and maturation of the spine.

HP:0004599.label: Absent or minimally ossified vertebral bodies

HP:0004601.label: Spina bifida occulta at L5
HP:0004601.definition: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of the vertebra L5 with intact overlying skin.

HP:0004602.label: Cervical C2/C3 vertebral fusion
HP:0004602.definition: Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C2 and C3, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development, leading to a short neck with a low hairline at the back of the head, and restricted mobility of the upper spine.

HP:0004605.label: Absent vertebral body mineralization
HP:0004605.definition: A lack of bone mineralization of the vertebral bodies.

HP:0004606.label: Unossified vertebral bodies
HP:0004606.definition: A lack of ossification of the vertebral bodies.

HP:0004607.label: Anterior beaking of lower thoracic vertebrae
HP:0004607.definition: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the lower thoracic vertebral bodies.

HP:0004608.label: Anteriorly placed odontoid process
HP:0004608.definition: Anterior mislocalization of the dens of the axis.

HP:0004610.label: Lumbar spinal canal stenosis
HP:0004610.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the lumbar spinal canal.
HP:0004610.comment: Symptoms of lumbar spinal canal stenosis include pseudoclaudication (pain, numbness,, or weakness induced by walking and relieved by rest; the prefix pseudo is used to differentiate this manifestation from claudication, which has similar symptoms but is caused by peripheral artery disease).

HP:0004614.label: Spina bifida occulta at S1
HP:0004614.definition: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of S1 with intact overlying skin.

HP:0004616.label: Cleft vertebral arch
HP:0004616.definition: A discontinuity of the vertebral arch, i.e., of the posterior part of a vertebra.

HP:0004617.label: Butterfly vertebral arch
HP:0004617.definition: Butterfly vertebrae have a cleft through the body of the vertebrae and a funnel shape at the ends.

HP:0004621.label: Enlarged vertebral pedicles
HP:0004621.definition: Increased size of the vertebral pedicle.
HP:0004621.comment: The vertebral pedicles are the two short, thick processes, which connect the body of the spinal vertebra to the arch.

HP:0004622.label: Progressive intervertebral space narrowing
HP:0004622.definition: A progressive form of decreased height of the intervertebral disk.

HP:0004625.label: Biconvex vertebral bodies
HP:0004625.definition: Presence of abnormal convexity of the upper and lower end plates of the vertebrae, i.e., an exaggerated bulging out of the upper and lower vertebral end plates.
HP:0004625.comment: Note that biconvex vertebral bodies can be a normal finding in newborns.

HP:0004630.label: Anterior beaking of thoracic vertebrae
HP:0004630.definition: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of thoracic vertebral bodies.

HP:0004631.label: Decreased cervical spine flexion due to contractures of posterior cervical muscles

HP:0004632.label: Cervical segmentation defect
HP:0004632.definition: An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation of cervical vertebrae during development.

HP:0004633.label: Lower thoracic kyphosis
HP:0004633.definition: Over curvature of the lower thoracic region, leading to a round back or if sever to a hump.

HP:0004635.label: Cervical C5/C6 vertebrae fusion
HP:0004635.definition: Fusion of the C5 and C6 cervical vertebrae.

HP:0004639.label: Elevated amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein
HP:0004639.definition: An elevation of alpha-feto protein measured in the amniotic fluid.
HP:0004639.comment: This feature can be found in pregnancies with fetuses affected by a range of abnormalities including for instance encephalocele.
exact_synonyms: Elevated amniotic fluid alpha foetal protein
Elevated amniotic fluid alpha fetal protein

HP:0004660.label: Hypoplasia of facial musculature
HP:0004660.definition: Underdevelopment of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

HP:0004661.label: Frontalis muscle weakness
HP:0004661.definition: Reduced strength of the frontalis muscle (which is located on the forehead).

HP:0004664.label: Facial midline hemangioma
HP:0004664.definition: Hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, occurring in the midline region of the face.

HP:0004673.label: Decreased facial expression
HP:0004673.definition: A reduced degree of voluntary and involuntary facial movements involved in responded to others or expressing emotions.

HP:0004681.label: Deep longitudinal plantar crease
HP:0004681.definition: Narrow, paramedian longitudinal depressions in the plantar skin of the forefoot.

HP:0004684.label: Talipes valgus
HP:0004684.definition: Outward turning of the heel, resulting in clubfoot with the person walking on the inner part of the foot.
HP:0004684.comment: The phrase talipes valgus is derived from the Latin words talus (ankle), pes (poot), and valgus (outward angulation of the distal segment of a bone).

HP:0004686.label: Short third metatarsal
HP:0004686.definition: Underdevelopment of the Third metatarsal bone leading to a short (hypoplastic) third metatarsal bone.

HP:0004690.label: Thickened Achilles tendon
HP:0004690.definition: An abnormal thickening of the Achilles tendon.

HP:0004691.label: 2-3 toe syndactyly
HP:0004691.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two and three.
exact_synonyms: Syndactyly of second and third toes

HP:0004692.label: 4-5 toe syndactyly
HP:0004692.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes four and five.

HP:0004695.label: Calcaneal epiphyseal stippling
HP:0004695.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the calcaneus.

HP:0004699.label: Osteoporotic metatarsal
HP:0004699.definition: Decrease in mass and density of the metatarsal bones.

HP:0004704.label: Short fifth metatarsal
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone

HP:0004712.label: Renal malrotation
HP:0004712.definition: An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal orientation of the kidney.
HP:0004712.comment: The final kidney position in the renal fossa results from the rotation of the kidney with an orientation of the renal pelvis to the medial and the renal calyces to the lateral. Malrotation of the kidney can lead to orientation of the renal pelvis anteriorly, posteriorly and laterally. In most cases, renal malrotation does not cause any symptoms, but, hydronephrosis or stone formation can be observed as complications of renal malformation.

HP:0004713.label: Reversible renal failure
HP:0004713.definition: Acute renal failure with resolution of manifestations.

HP:0004717.label: Axial malrotation of the kidney
HP:0004717.definition: An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal axial orientation of the kidney.

HP:0004719.label: Hyperechogenic kidneys
HP:0004719.definition: An increase in amplitude of waves returned in ultrasonography of the kidney, which is generally displayed as increased brightness of the signal.
HP:0004719.comment: Normal renal parenchyma is similar (isoechoic) or slightly darker (hypoechoic) compared with liver and includes the cortex and medulla. The thickness of the renal cortex is measured from the outer border of the medullary pyramids (yellow line) or from the arcuate arteries to the renal capsule. The medullary pyramids (white arrow) contain fluid in parallel tubules, which is anechoic (black) and appear as regularly spaced dark pools at the inner margin of the parenchyma (arrow). Because fat is echogenic, the central renal sinus appears bright.
exact_synonyms: Increased echogenicity of the renal parenchyma

HP:0004722.label: Thickened glomerular basement membrane
HP:0004722.definition: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM), reflecting an increase in thickness (subjective estimate) of the basal lamina of the glomerulus of the kidney.
HP:0004722.comment: This finding is demonstrated on renal biopsy.
exact_synonyms: Thickening of the glomerular basement membrane

HP:0004724.label: Calcium nephrolithiasis
HP:0004724.definition: The presence of calcium-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.
HP:0004724.comment: The overwhelming majority of renal calculi contain calcium.

HP:0004727.label: Impaired renal concentrating ability
HP:0004727.definition: A defect in the ability to concentrate the urine.
HP:0004727.comment: An impairment in renal concentrating ability can be easily recognized by the maximum concentrating ability (Umax) as determined by the urine osmolality reached after a fixed period of dehydration. Inability to maximally concentrate the urine is related to one or both of two basic tubular defects: 1) a failure of maximal free-water generation by the diluting segment in the ascending limb of Henle's loop; and 2) a failure of the distal tubular epithelium to achieve maximum permeability to water during water deprivation.

HP:0004729.label: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis
HP:0004729.definition: Acute inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

HP:0004732.label: Impaired renal uric acid clearance
HP:0004732.definition: A reduction in the ability of the kidneys to remove uric acid from the serum.

HP:0004734.label: Renal cortical microcysts
HP:0004734.definition: Cysts of microscopic size confined to the cortex of the kidney.

HP:0004736.label: Crossed fused renal ectopia
HP:0004736.definition: A developmental anomaly in which the kidneys are fused and localized on the same side of the midline. This anomaly is thought to result from disruption of the normal embryologic migration of the kidneys.

HP:0004737.label: Global glomerulosclerosis
HP:0004737.definition: Obliteration of the glomerular capillary lumen by increased collagenous matrix, with or without hyalinosis or foam cells. Sclerosis involves 100% of the glomerular tuft. Relative to other patent glomeruli in the sample, glomerular size is preserved, or increased/decreased by no more than 50%.
HP:0004737.comment: Glomerular changes can be focal (only in some glomeruli) or diffuse (in all or almost all the glomeruli), and segmental (only a part of the glomerulus) or global (the entire glomerulus).

HP:0004742.label: Abnormal renal collecting system morphology
HP:0004742.definition: An abnormality of the renal collecting system.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the renal collecting system

HP:0004743.label: Chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis
HP:0004743.definition: Chronic inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

HP:0004746.label: Glomerular subendothelial electron-dense deposits
HP:0004746.definition: Electron dense deposits at the glomerular basement membrane,
HP:0004746.comment: Subendothelial electron-dense deposits are a characteristic feature of dense-deposit disease.

HP:0004749.label: Atrial flutter
HP:0004749.definition: A type of atrial arrhythmia characterized by atrial rates of between 240 and 400 beats per minute and some degree of atrioventricular node conduction block. Typically, the ventricular rate is half the atrial rate. In the EKG; atrial flutter waves are observed as sawtooth-like atrial activity. Pathophysiologically, atrial flutter is a form of atrial reentry in which there is a premature electrical impulse creates a self-propagating circuit.
HP:0004749.comment: Atrial flutter can lead to palpitations, fatigue, dyspnea, and chest pain. Atrial flutter can be paroxysmal or persistent.

HP:0004751.label: Paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia
HP:0004751.definition: Episodes of ventricular tachycardia that have a sudden onset and ending.

HP:0004752.label: Congenital atrioventricular dissociation
HP:0004752.definition: A form of atrioventricular (AV) dissociation (i.e., the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers) with congenital onset.

HP:0004754.label: Permanent atrial fibrillation
HP:0004754.definition: Atrial fibrillation (AF) that cannot be successfully terminated by cardioversion, and longstanding (more than 1 year) AF, where cardioversion is not indicated or has not been attempted, is termed permanent.
HP:0004754.comment: The natural history of atrial fibrillation (AF) is characterized by a gradual worsening with time. AF itself produces changes in atrial function and structure. Note there is no precise definition of the duration of AF required to be regarded as chronic.

HP:0004755.label: Supraventricular tachycardia
HP:0004755.definition: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is an abnormally increased heart rate (over 100 beats per minute at rest) with origin above the level of the ventricles.
HP:0004755.comment: A narrow complex (QRS width less than 120 milliseconds) reflects rapid activation of the ventricles via the normal conduction pathway, i.e. His-Purkinje system, which in turn suggests that the tachycardia originated above the AV node and is thus supraventricular.

HP:0004756.label: Ventricular tachycardia
HP:0004756.definition: A tachycardia originating in the ventricles characterized by rapid heart rate (over 100 beats per minute) and broad QRS complexes (over 120 ms).
HP:0004756.comment: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia that presents as a wide QRS complex tachycardia, and is defined as three or more consecutive QRS complexes with a duration longer than 120 milliseconds (ms) and a rate of 100 beats per minute or more, whereby the complexes have a ventricular origin. VT can be subdivided as follows: (i) sustained VT persists for 30 seconds or more; (ii) non-sustained VT lasts less than 30 seconds; (iii) monomorphic VT displays a uniform QRS morphology; and (iv) polymorphic VT displays QRS morphologies that variy from beat to beat. VT is observed most commonly in individuals with structural heart disease or acute myocardial infarction (MI). VT may also be observed in in the setting of drug toxicity or electrolyte abnormalities or in individuals with Mendelian disease.

HP:0004757.label: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
HP:0004757.definition: Episodes of atrial fibrillation that typically last for several hours up to one day and terminate spontaneously.

HP:0004758.label: Effort-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
HP:0004758.definition: Polymorphic ventricular arrhythmias of varying morphologythat do not exist under resting conditions but appear only upon physical exercise or catecholamine administration.

HP:0004759.label: obsolete Nodular calcific aortic valve disease

HP:0004762.label: Hypoplasia of right ventricle
HP:0004762.definition: Underdevelopment or reduced size of the heart right ventricle, often due to a reduced number of cells.

HP:0004763.label: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
HP:0004763.definition: An episodic form of supraventricular tachycardia with abrupt onset and termination.
HP:0004763.comment: PSVT is a term used to denote intermittent supraventricular tachycardia other than atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter and multifocal atrial tachycardia (AT). The major causes are atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT), atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), and sinoatrial node reentrant tachycardia (SNRT).

HP:0004764.label: Myxomatous mitral valve degeneration
HP:0004764.definition: Myxomatous mitral valve is defined as the presence of excess leaflet tissue and leaflet thickening greater than 5 mm, resulting in a prolapse greater than 2 mm into the left atrium on parasternal long axis view.

HP:0004768.label: Sparse anterior scalp hair
HP:0004768.definition: Decreased number of head hairs per unit area on the anterior region of the scalp.
exact_synonyms: Sparse scalp hair at front of head
Thin scalp hair at front of head

HP:0004780.label: Elbow hypertrichosis
HP:0004780.definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the elbow region.

HP:0004783.label: Duodenal polyposis
HP:0004783.definition: Presence of multiple polyps in the duodenum.

HP:0004784.label: Juvenile gastrointestinal polyposis
