HP:0004784.definition: The presence of multiple juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine. The term juvenile polyps refer to a special histopathology and not the age of onset as the polyp might be diagnosed at all ages. The juvenile polyp has a spherical appearance and is microscopically characterized by overgrowth of an oedematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells and cystic glands. Juvenile polyps are a specific type of hamartomatous polyps.

HP:0004785.label: Malrotation of colon
HP:0004785.definition: An anatomical anomaly that results from an abnormal rotation of the gut as it returns to the abdominal cavity during embryogenesis.

HP:0004787.label: Fulminant hepatitis
HP:0004787.definition: Acute hepatitis complicated by acute liver failure with hepatic encephalopathy occurring less than 8 weeks after the onset of jaundice.
HP:0004787.comment: Note that different definitions of fulminant hepatitis are used in the medical literature.

HP:0004788.label: Intestinal lymphedema
HP:0004788.definition: Fluid retention and edema in the intestine caused by a compromised lymphatic system.

HP:0004791.label: Esophageal ulceration
HP:0004791.definition: Defect in the epithelium of the esophagus, essentially an open sore in the lining of the esophagus.

HP:0004792.label: Rectoperineal fistula
HP:0004792.definition: The presence of a fistula between the perineum and the rectum.

HP:0004794.label: Malrotation of small bowel
HP:0004794.definition: A deviation from the normal rotation of the midgut during embryologic development with mislocalization of the small bowel.
HP:0004794.comment: Malrotation results not only in the malposition of the bowel but also in the malfixation of the mesentery. The normally broad mesenteric attachment is shortened to a narrow pedicle that predisposes the patient to the complication of midgut volvulus.

HP:0004795.label: Hamartomatous stomach polyps
HP:0004795.definition: Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas located in the stomach.

HP:0004797.label: Multiple small bowel atresias
HP:0004797.definition: The presence of multiple areas of atresia affecting the small intestine.

HP:0004798.label: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
HP:0004798.definition: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract.
exact_synonyms: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
Recurrent infection of the GI tract

HP:0004802.label: Episodic hemolytic anemia
HP:0004802.definition: A form of hemolytic anemia that occurs in repeated episodes.

HP:0004804.label: Congenital hemolytic anemia
HP:0004804.definition: A form of hemolytic anemia with congenital onset.

HP:0004808.label: Acute myeloid leukemia
HP:0004808.definition: A form of leukemia characterized by overproduction of an early myeloid cell.

HP:0004809.label: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia
HP:0004809.definition: Low platelet count associated with maternal platelet-specific alloantibodies.
HP:0004809.comment: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia occurs following fetomaternal transfusions leading to generation of alloreactive antiplatelet antibodies.

HP:0004810.label: Congenital hypoplastic anemia
HP:0004810.definition: A type of hypoplastic anemia with congenital onset.
HP:0004810.comment: In this condition, hematopoiesis must have been inadequate in fetal life. Affected infant have marked pallor and reticulocytopenia or absence of red blood cell precursors in an otherwise normally cellular bone marrow. This term does not refer to a particular diagnosis or etiology (or which several are known) but to the phenotypic feature.

HP:0004812.label: B Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
HP:0004812.definition: A type of ALL characterized by elevated levels of B-cell lymphoblasts in the bone marrow and the blood.

HP:0004813.label: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia
HP:0004813.definition: Sudden onset of thrombocytopenia (reduced platelet count) within 5-10 days of the transfusion of blood products. The clinical presentation is post-transfusion purpura (PTP), wigth severe thrmbocytopenia, epistaxis, and hemorrhages.
HP:0004813.comment: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia is thought to be related to platelet-specific alloantibody from prior transfusion/pregnancy.

HP:0004814.label: Fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia
HP:0004814.definition: A kind of hemolytic anemia that is induced by the ingestion of fava beans.
HP:0004814.comment: Persons with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency are susceptible to fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia because of the oxidative stress induced by compounds in Fava beans (thought to be vicine and isouramil). The same underlying defect can make affected persons susceptible to hemolysis induced by a number of mediciations.
exact_synonyms: Hemolytic anaemia following ingestion of fava beans
Hemolytic anemia following ingestion of fava beans

HP:0004817.label: Drug-sensitive hemolytic anemia
HP:0004817.definition: A form of hemolytic anemia that is triggered by ingestion of certain drugs.

HP:0004819.label: Normocytic hypoplastic anemia
HP:0004819.definition: A type of hypoplastic anemia in which the erythrocytes have a normal cell volume (the mean corpuscular volume is within normal limits).

HP:0004820.label: Acute myelomonocytic leukemia
HP:0004820.definition: An acute leukemia characterized by the proliferation of both neutrophil and monocyte precursors.

HP:0004821.label: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei
HP:0004821.definition: An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil.
HP:0004821.comment: Neutrophils usually display 3-4 nuclear lobes. Hypersegmented neutrophile nuclei display 5 or more lobes. This feature can be seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency or with other etiologies.
exact_synonyms: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood

HP:0004823.label: Anisopoikilocytosis
HP:0004823.definition: A type of poikilocytosis characterized by the presence in the blood of erythrocytes of varying sizes and abnormal shapes.

HP:0004825.label: Increased hemoglobin oxygen affinity
HP:0004825.definition: An abnormal increase in the binding affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

HP:0004826.label: Folate-unresponsive megaloblastic anemia
HP:0004826.definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia that does not improve upon administration of folate. Since vitamin B12 acts by promoting recycling of folate, administration of vitamin B12 also does not improve this type of anemia.

HP:0004828.label: Refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts
HP:0004828.definition: A type of myelodysplastic syndrome characterized by less than 5% myeloblasts in the bone marrow, but with 15% or greater red cell precursors in the marrow being abnormal iron-stuffed cells called ringed sideroblasts.

HP:0004831.label: Recurrent thromboembolism
HP:0004831.definition: Repeated episodes of obstruction of blood flow due to an embolus, i.e., blood clot that has traveled from its point of origin within the blood stream.

HP:0004835.label: Microspherocytosis
HP:0004835.definition: The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped and reduced in size.

HP:0004836.label: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
HP:0004836.definition: A type of acute myeloid leukemia in which abnormal promyelocytes predominate.

HP:0004839.label: Pyropoikilocytosis
HP:0004839.definition: A form of severe hemolytic anemia characterized by erythrocyte morphology reminiscent of that seen in patients after a thermal burn.

HP:0004840.label: Hypochromic microcytic anemia
HP:0004840.definition: A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

HP:0004841.label: Reduced factor XII activity
HP:0004841.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XII. Factor XII (fXII) is part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway and binds to exposed collagen at site of vessel wall injury, activated by high-MW kininogen and kallikrein, thereby initiating the coagulation cascade.

HP:0004844.label: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia
HP:0004844.definition: A type of hemolytic anemia in which the Coombs test is positive.
HP:0004844.comment: The Coombs test measures a coating of immunoglobulin or complement on the red cell surface.

HP:0004845.label: Acute monocytic leukemia
HP:0004845.definition: The accumulation of transformed primitive hematopoietic blast cells, which lose their ability of normal differentiation and proliferation.

HP:0004846.label: Prolonged bleeding after surgery
HP:0004846.definition: Bleeding that persists longer than the normal time following a surgical procedure.

HP:0004848.label: Ph-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia
HP:0004848.definition: A subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia that results from a reciprocal translocation between the ABL-1 oncogene and a breakpoint cluster region (BCR), resulting in a fusion gene, BCR-ABL, that encodes an oncogenic protein with constitutively active tyrosine kinase activity.

HP:0004850.label: Recurrent deep vein thrombosis
HP:0004850.definition: Repeated episodes of the formation of a blot clot in a deep vein.

HP:0004851.label: Folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia
HP:0004851.definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of folate.

HP:0004852.label: Reduced leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
HP:0004852.definition: Decreased alkaline phosphatase measured within leukocytes.

HP:0004854.label: Intermittent thrombocytopenia
HP:0004854.definition: Reduced platelet count that occurs sporadically, i.e., it comes and goes.

HP:0004855.label: Reduced protein S activity
HP:0004855.definition: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein S. Protein S is a cofactor of protein C.
HP:0004855.comment: Protein S functions as a cofactor to Protein C in the inactivation of Factors Va and VIIIa in the coagulation pathway. Therefore, a defect in protein S is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

HP:0004856.label: Normochromic microcytic anemia
HP:0004856.definition: A type of anemia characterized by an normal concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

HP:0004857.label: Hyperchromic macrocytic anemia
HP:0004857.definition: A type of anemia characterized by abnormally large erythrocytes with abnormally high amounts of hemoglobin.

HP:0004859.label: Amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia
HP:0004859.definition: Thrombocytopenia related to lack of or severe reduction in the count of megakaryocytes.

HP:0004860.label: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia
HP:0004860.definition: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of thiamine.

HP:0004864.label: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count
HP:0004864.definition: Count of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow above the upper limit of normal. Ring sideroblasts are nucleated erythroblasts with a pathologic accumulation of iron granules in the mitochondrial matrix. They can be detected by Prussian blue staining as blue perinuclear aggregates in bone marrow aspirate erythroblasts.
HP:0004864.comment: Sideroblastic anemia includes a group of inherited and acquired anemias of ineffective erythropoiesis characterized by an accumulation of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow and decreased production of mature red blood cells. Additionally, refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts is a type of myelodysplastic syndrome that is characterized by anemia and the presence of at least 15 percent ring sideroblasts in the marrow.

HP:0004866.label: Impaired ADP-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0004866.definition: Abnormal platelet response to ADP as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ADP.

HP:0004870.label: Chronic hemolytic anemia
HP:0004870.definition: An chronic form of hemolytic anemia.

HP:0004871.label: Perineal fistula
HP:0004871.definition: The presence of a fistula between the bowel and the perineum.
HP:0004871.comment: The perineum is the diamond-shaped region of the body between the pubic arch and the anus.

HP:0004872.label: Incisional hernia
HP:0004872.definition: An abdominal hernia that occurs at a site of weakness in the abdominal wall resulting from an incompletely-healed surgical wound.

HP:0004876.label: Spontaneous neonatal pneumothorax
HP:0004876.definition: Pneumothorax occurring neonatally without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

HP:0004878.label: Intercostal muscle weakness
HP:0004878.definition: Lack of strength of the intercostal muscles, i.e., of the muscle groups running along the ribs that create and move the chest wall.

HP:0004880.label: Respiratory infections in early life
HP:0004880.definition: Increased susceptibility to respiratory infections in early life, as manifested by recurrent episodes of respiratory infections.

HP:0004887.label: Respiratory failure requiring assisted ventilation
HP:0004887.definition: A state of respiratory distress that requires a life saving intervention in the form of gaining airway access and instituting positive pressure ventilation.

HP:0004889.label: Intermittent episodes of respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

HP:0004890.label: Elevated pulmonary artery pressure
HP:0004890.definition: An abnormally elevated blood pressure in the circulation of the pulmonary artery.

HP:0004891.label: Recurrent infections due to aspiration
HP:0004891.definition: Increased susceptibility to infections due to aspiration, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infections due to aspiration.

HP:0004897.label: Stress/infection-induced lactic acidosis
HP:0004897.definition: A form of lactic acidemia that occurs in relation to stress or infection.

HP:0004898.label: Persistent lactic acidosis
HP:0004898.definition: A continuous form of lactic acidemia.

HP:0004900.label: Severe lactic acidosis
HP:0004900.definition: A severe form of lactic acidemia.

HP:0004901.label: Exercise-induced lactic acidemia
HP:0004901.definition: A form of lactic acidemia that occurs following exercise or exertion.

HP:0004902.label: Congenital lactic acidosis
HP:0004902.definition: A form of lactic acidemia with congenital onset.

HP:0004904.label: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young
HP:0004904.definition: The term Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) was initially used for patients diagnosed with fasting hyperglycemia that could be treated without insulin for more than two years, where the initial diagnosis was made at a young age (under 25 years). Thus, MODY combines characteristics of type 1 diabetes (young age at diagnosis) and type 2 diabetes (less insulin dependence than type 1 diabetes). The term MODY is now most often used to refer to a group of monogenic diseases with these characteristics. Here, the term is used to describe hyperglycemia diagnosed at a young age with no or minor insulin dependency, no evidence of insulin resistance, and lack of evidence of autoimmune destruction of the beta cells.
exact_synonyms: Maturity onset diabetes of the young

HP:0004905.label: Reduced circulating vitamin A concentration
HP:0004905.definition: Concentration of vitamin A below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

HP:0004911.label: Episodic metabolic acidosis
HP:0004911.definition: Repeated transient episodes of metabolic acidosis, that is, of the buildup of acid or depletion of base due to accumulation of metabolic acids.

HP:0004913.label: Intermittent lactic acidemia
HP:0004913.definition: An intermittent (discontinuous) form of lactic acidemia.

HP:0004914.label: Recurrent infantile hypoglycemia
HP:0004914.definition: Recurrent episodes of decreased concentration of glucose in the blood occurring during the infantile period.
exact_synonyms: Recurrent low blood sugar in infant

HP:0004918.label: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis
HP:0004918.definition: A form of metabolic acidosis with increased serum chloride levels.

HP:0004921.label: Abnormal magnesium concentration
HP:0004921.definition: An abnormality of magnesium ion homeostasis.

HP:0004923.label: Hyperphenylalaninemia
HP:0004923.definition: An increased concentration of L-phenylalanine in the blood.

HP:0004924.label: Abnormal oral glucose tolerance
HP:0004924.definition: An abnormal resistance to glucose, i.e., a reduction in the ability to maintain glucose levels in the blood stream within normal limits following oral administration of glucose.

HP:0004925.label: Chronic lactic acidosis
HP:0004925.definition: A chronic form of lactic acidemia.

HP:0004926.label: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction

HP:0004927.label: Pulmonary artery dilatation
HP:0004927.definition: An abnormal widening of the diameter of the pulmonary artery.

HP:0004930.label: Abnormality of the pulmonary vasculature
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the lung blood vessels

HP:0004931.label: Arteriosclerosis of small cerebral arteries
HP:0004931.definition: Arteriosclerosis (increased thickness, increased stiffness, loss of elasticity) of the small arteries of the brain.

HP:0004933.label: Ascending aortic dissection
HP:0004933.definition: A separation of the layers within the wall of the ascending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.
HP:0004933.comment: According to the Stanford classification, type A aortic dissection affects the ascending aorta and arch.

HP:0004935.label: Pulmonary artery atresia
HP:0004935.definition: A congenital anomaly with a narrowing or complete absence of the opening between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.
HP:0004935.comment: Pulmonary artery atresia means that unoxygenated blood in the right ventricle can not be effectively pumped into the lung for oxygenation.

HP:0004936.label: Venous thrombosis
HP:0004936.definition: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

HP:0004937.label: Pulmonary artery aneurysm
HP:0004937.definition: An aneurysm (severe localized balloon-like outward bulging) in the pulmonary artery.

HP:0004938.label: Tortuous cerebral arteries
HP:0004938.definition: Excessive bending, twisting, and winding of a cerebral artery.

HP:0004940.label: Generalized arterial calcification
HP:0004940.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts, affecting arteries distributed throughout the body.

HP:0004941.label: Extrahepatic portal hypertension
HP:0004941.definition: Increased pressure in the pre-hepatic portal vein.
HP:0004941.comment: Hypertension in the portal venous tree proper. previous def: 'has part' some ('increased pressure' and ('inheres in' some ('arterial blood' and ('part of' some 'Pre-hepatic portal vein (adult human)'))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0004942.label: Aortic aneurysm
HP:0004942.definition: Aortic dilatation refers to a dimension that is greater than the 95th percentile for the normal person age, sex and body size. In contrast, an aneurysm is defined as a localized dilation of the aorta that is more than 150 percent of predicted (ratio of observed to expected diameter 1.5 or more). Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.
HP:0004942.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe (pathological) form of dilatation of a segment of a blood vessel. In clinical practice, dilatation and aneurysm are occasionally used interchangeably. In this subhierarchy, we therefore use aneurysm as the primary label and list dilatation as a broad synonym.
exact_synonyms: Bulge in wall of large artery that carries blood away from heart

HP:0004943.label: Accelerated atherosclerosis
HP:0004943.definition: Atherosclerosis which occurs in a person with certain risk factors (e.g., SLE, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, family history of early heart disease) at an earlier age than would occur in another person without those risk factors.

HP:0004944.label: Dilatation of the cerebral artery
HP:0004944.definition: The presence of a localized dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.
HP:0004944.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0004945.label: Extracranial internal carotid artery dissection
HP:0004945.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the extracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.

HP:0004947.label: Arteriovenous fistula
HP:0004947.definition: An abnormal connection between an artery and vein.

HP:0004948.label: Vascular tortuosity
HP:0004948.definition: Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.

HP:0004950.label: Peripheral arterial stenosis
HP:0004950.definition: Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.
HP:0004950.comment: The ankle-brachial index (ABI; the ratio of systolic blood pressure in the ankle to that in the arm), is a measure of occlusion of peripheral arteries in the leg. Peripheral arterial stenosis may be observed with atherosclerosis and with increased intima media thickness as seen in diseases such as pseudoxanthoma elasticum. The most common cause of peripheral arterial stenosis in patients over 40 years of age is atherosclerosis. Cerebral and coronary arteries are by definition not included in peripheral artery disease.

HP:0004952.label: Pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas
HP:0004952.definition: A rare vascular anomaly with a direct communication between pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary bed.

HP:0004954.label: obsolete Dilatation of the descending aorta

HP:0004955.label: Generalized arterial tortuosity
HP:0004955.definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.

HP:0004959.label: Descending thoracic aorta aneurysm
HP:0004959.definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta.

HP:0004960.label: Absent pulmonary artery
HP:0004960.definition: A congenital defect with aplasia (absence) of one of the right or left pulmonary artery.
HP:0004960.comment: This is a rare feature that has been observed in recessive lethal osteogenesis imperfecta with mutation in CRTAP.

HP:0004961.label: Pulmonary artery sling
HP:0004961.definition: An anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery, such that it arises from the posterior aspect of the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and esophagus to reach the left hilum.

HP:0004962.label: Thoracic aorta calcification
HP:0004962.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the thoracic aorta.

HP:0004963.label: Calcification of the aorta
HP:0004963.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aorta.
HP:0004963.comment: Note that the phrase "aortic calcification" is mainly used to describe calcification of the aortic valve rather than of the aorta itself.

HP:0004964.label: Pulmonary arterial medial hypertrophy
HP:0004964.definition: Increase in mass of the tunica media of the arteries in the pulmonary circulation.
exact_synonyms: Hypertrophy of the pulmonary artery wall

HP:0004966.label: Medial calcification of large arteries
HP:0004966.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of large (conduit) arteries.

HP:0004968.label: Recurrent cerebral hemorrhage
HP:0004968.definition: Recurrent bleeding into the parenchyma of the brain.

HP:0004969.label: Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis
HP:0004969.definition: Stenosis of a peripheral branch of the pulmonary artery.

HP:0004970.label: Ascending tubular aorta aneurysm
HP:0004970.definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the tubular part of the ascending aorta.
HP:0004970.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.
exact_synonyms: Aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta
Bulging of wall of large artery located above heart

HP:0004972.label: Elevated mean arterial pressure
HP:0004972.definition: An abnormal increase in the average blood pressure in an individual during a single cardiac cycle.

HP:0004974.label: Coarctation of abdominal aorta
HP:0004974.definition: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the abdominal aorta.

HP:0004975.label: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of the femurs
exact_synonyms: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of distal femur

HP:0004977.label: Bilateral radial aplasia
HP:0004977.definition: Missing radius bone on both sides associated with congenital failure of development.

HP:0004979.label: Metaphyseal sclerosis
HP:0004979.definition: Abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in wide portion of long bone

HP:0004980.label: Metaphyseal rarefaction
HP:0004980.definition: Reduction in density of metaphyseal bony tissue.

HP:0004987.label: Mesomelic leg shortening
HP:0004987.definition: Shortening of the middle parts of the leg in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

HP:0004991.label: Rhizomelic arm shortening
HP:0004991.definition: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the arm (i.e. the humerus).
HP:0004991.comment: This term implies that the ulna and radius are not substantially shortened.

HP:0004993.label: Slender long bones with narrow diaphyses
HP:0004993.definition: Reduced diameter of a long bone with a more pronounced reduction of the diameter of the diaphysis of the long bones.
exact_synonyms: Slender long bones with narrow shaft

HP:0004997.label: Multicentric ossification of proximal humeral epiphyses

HP:0005003.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0005003.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Absent/underdeveloped end part of innermost thighbone
Absent/small end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0005004.label: Flattened proximal radial epiphyses
HP:0005004.definition: An abnormally flat form of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.

HP:0005005.label: Femoral bowing present at birth, straightening with time
HP:0005005.definition: Congenital onset bending or abnormal curvature of the femur that normalizes with age.
HP:0005005.comment: This feature can be diagnosed based on the medical history of congenital femoral bowing with spontaneous improvement.
exact_synonyms: Bowing of thighbone at birth, straightening with time

HP:0005009.label: Dumbbell-shaped humerus
HP:0005009.definition: The humerus is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.
exact_synonyms: Dumbbell-shaped long bone in upper arm

HP:0005010.label: Osteomyelitis leading to amputation due to slow healing fractures

HP:0005011.label: Mesomelic arm shortening
HP:0005011.definition: Shortening of the middle parts of the arm in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

HP:0005013.label: Dysplastic distal radial epiphyses
HP:0005013.definition: Abnormally developed (dysplastic) distal epiphysis of the radius.

HP:0005019.label: Diaphyseal undertubulation
HP:0005019.definition: Tubulation refers to the size and shape of tubular bones. In children and adolescents, the modeling process regulates normal bone growth. Final shaft (tube) diameter depends on appositional bone growth and the equilibrium between periosteal and endosteal bone resorption and formation. Undertubulation refers to a broad, widened form of the shafts (diaphyses) of long bones.
exact_synonyms: Thickening of shaft or central part of long bones

HP:0005025.label: Hypoplastic distal humeri
HP:0005025.definition: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the humerus.

HP:0005028.label: Widened proximal tibial metaphyses
exact_synonyms: Wide innermost wide portion of shankbone bone
Wide innermost wide portion of shinbone bone

HP:0005033.label: Distal ulnar hypoplasia
HP:0005033.definition: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the ulna.

HP:0005035.label: Shortening of all phalanges of the toes
HP:0005035.definition: Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of all phalanges of the foot.

HP:0005036.label: Unilateral ulnar hypoplasia
HP:0005036.definition: Underdevelopment of the ulna on only one side.

HP:0005037.label: Proximal radio-ulnar synostosis
HP:0005037.definition: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the proximal portions of the radius and the ulna.

HP:0005039.label: Multiple long-bone exostoses
HP:0005039.definition: Multiple exostoses originating in long bones.
exact_synonyms: Multiple exostoses of long tubular bones

HP:0005041.label: Irregular capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0005041.definition: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth capital femoral epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0005043.label: Proximal humeral metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0005043.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis at the proximal end of the humerus (at the shoulder).

HP:0005045.label: Diaphyseal cortical sclerosis
HP:0005045.definition: An elevation in bone density of the cortex of one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

HP:0005050.label: Anterolateral radial head dislocation
HP:0005050.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterolateral direction.

HP:0005054.label: Metaphyseal spurs
HP:0005054.definition: Bony outgrowths that extend laterally from the margin of the metaphysis.

HP:0005063.label: Fragmented, irregular epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Fragmented, irregular end part of bone

HP:0005066.label: Cone-shaped epiphyses fused within their metaphyses
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of long bone fused within their wide portion of wide bone

HP:0005067.label: Proximal fibular overgrowth
HP:0005067.definition: Overgrowth of the proximal part of the fibula.
exact_synonyms: Overgrowth of innermost part of calf bone

HP:0005070.label: Proximal radial head dislocation
HP:0005070.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an proximal direction.

HP:0005072.label: Wrist hypermobility
HP:0005072.definition: The ability of the wrist joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

HP:0005084.label: Anterior radial head dislocation
HP:0005084.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterior direction.

HP:0005085.label: Limited knee flexion/extension
HP:0005085.definition: A limited ability of the knee joint to perform extension and flexion.

HP:0005089.label: Abnormal metaphyseal trabeculation
HP:0005089.definition: An abnormality of the pattern of trabecula (small interconnecting rods of bone) in a metaphyseal region of bone.

HP:0005090.label: Lateral femoral bowing
HP:0005090.definition: A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.

HP:0005092.label: Streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
HP:0005092.definition: The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
exact_synonyms: Streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone

HP:0005093.label: Absent proximal radial epiphyses
HP:0005093.definition: Absence of the proximal radial epiphysis.

HP:0005096.label: Distal femoral bowing
HP:0005096.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the femur.

HP:0005100.label: Premature birth following premature rupture of fetal membranes
exact_synonyms: Premature birth following premature rupture of foetal membranes

HP:0005101.label: High-frequency hearing impairment
HP:0005101.definition: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).
HP:0005101.comment: High frequency hearing impairment often involves loss of ability to hear consonants such as s, f, t, and z, even though vowels can be heard normally.

HP:0005102.label: Cochlear degeneration
HP:0005102.definition: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the cochlea.

HP:0005103.label: Calcification of the auricular cartilage
HP:0005103.definition: Ossification affecting the external ear cartilage.

HP:0005104.label: Hypoplastic nasal septum
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of septum of nose

HP:0005105.label: Abnormal nasal morphology
HP:0005105.comment: This is a category for overall abnormal morphology that may be replaced later with more exact descriptions.

HP:0005106.label: Abnormality of the vertebral endplates
HP:0005106.definition: Any abnormality of the vertebral end plates, which are the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral disks.

HP:0005107.label: Abnormal sacrum morphology
HP:0005107.definition: An abnormality of the sacral bone.
HP:0005107.comment: The sacrum is the large, roughly triangular bone at the base of the verterbal column that is formed by fusion of the five sacral vertebrae S1 to S5.

HP:0005108.label: Abnormal intervertebral disk morphology
HP:0005108.definition: Any structural abnormality of the intervertebral disk.
HP:0005108.comment: Any abnormality of the fibrocartilaginous structures that are located between adjacent vertebral bodies.

HP:0005109.label: Abnormal Achilles tendon morphology
HP:0005109.definition: An abnormality of the Achilles tendon.

HP:0005110.label: Atrial fibrillation
HP:0005110.definition: An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.
HP:0005110.comment: The ventricular response to atrial fibrillation is irregularly irregular because of the large number of atrial impulses that transit the atrioventricular node, making the ventricle partially refractory to further impulses. Atrial fibrillation can cause a number of manifestations including excessive ventricular response with angina pectoris or hypotension in susceptible individuals, syncope, systemic embolization, fatigue, or anxiety. These features should be coded separately.
exact_synonyms: Quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat

HP:0005111.label: obsolete Dilatation of the ascending aorta

HP:0005112.label: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
HP:0005112.definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta.

HP:0005113.label: Aortic arch aneurysm
HP:0005113.definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch.

HP:0005114.label: obsolete Abnormalities of the peripheral arteries

HP:0005115.label: Supraventricular arrhythmia
HP:0005115.definition: A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.
HP:0005115.comment: Supraventricular arrhythmia includes atrial arrhythmias (atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation), atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, junctional ectopic tachycardia, atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (Wolf-Parkinson-White Syndrome), orthodromic or antidromic. Supraventricular arrhythmia is distinct from ventricular tachycardia, which originates in the ventricles.

HP:0005116.label: Arterial tortuosity
HP:0005116.definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.

HP:0005117.label: Elevated diastolic blood pressure
HP:0005117.definition: Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.
HP:0005117.comment: Normal diastolic blood pressure is less than 80 mmHg.

HP:0005120.label: Abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
HP:0005120.definition: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.

HP:0005121.label: Posterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
HP:0005121.definition: An excessive concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.
HP:0005121.comment: The posterior vertebral scalloping sign appears on a lateral radiograph of the spine as an exaggeration of the normal concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies. Neurofibromatosis may be associated with marked scalloping of the posterior borders of the vertebral bodies resulting from intraspinal tumors.

HP:0005132.label: Pericardial constriction
HP:0005132.definition: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.

HP:0005133.label: Right ventricular dilatation
HP:0005133.definition: Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle, which can be defined echocardiographically as a right ventricular to left ventricular ratio greater than 1:1.
HP:0005133.comment: Ventricular dilatation is to be distinguished from ventricular aneurysm, which refers to a diastolic as well as systolic outpouching of the ventricle containing endocardium, epicardium, and thin-wall non-contractile scarred myocardium, which mainly develop in the setting of a full-thickness infarct, replaced by fibrous tissue because of myocardial infarction.

HP:0005134.label: Absence of the pulmonary valve
HP:0005134.definition: Refers to the specific combination of defects with a severely dysplastic pulmonary valve and massively dilated branch pulmonary arteries.
HP:0005134.comment: The distinctive feature of APVS is the airway obstruction caused by tracheobronchial compression that results from massive dilatation of the main pulmonary artery (PA) and its first- and second-order branches. Consequential tracheomalacia and bronchomalacia determine the timing and severity of respiratory compromise, as well as the morbidity and mortality of these patients.

HP:0005135.label: Abnormal T-wave
HP:0005135.definition: An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.

HP:0005136.label: Mitral annular calcification
HP:0005136.definition: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.
HP:0005136.comment: MAC is a common degenerative process involving the fibrous annulus of the mitral valve, and is generally an incidental finding associated with aging. This term applies if MAC occurs at a substantially younger age than usual.

HP:0005143.label: Anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
HP:0005143.definition: The right pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

HP:0005144.label: Ventricular septal hypertrophy
HP:0005144.definition: The dividing wall between left and right sides of the heart, thickens and bulges into the left ventricle.

HP:0005145.label: Coronary artery stenosis
HP:0005145.definition: Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.

HP:0005146.label: Cardiac valve calcification
HP:0005146.definition: Abnormal calcification of a cardiac valve.

HP:0005148.label: Pulmonary valve defects
HP:0005148.definition: Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.

HP:0005150.label: Abnormal atrioventricular conduction
HP:0005150.definition: An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.

HP:0005151.label: Preductal coarctation of the aorta
HP:0005151.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized proximal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the preductal region of aortic arch.
HP:0005151.comment: Blood flow to the aorta distal to the coarctation may be dependent on a patent ductus arteriosus, and hence closure of the ductus arteriosus can lead to serious ischemia of the affected tissues.

HP:0005152.label: Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy
HP:0005152.definition: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized pathologically by hamartomatous lesions of cardiac Purkinje cells.
HP:0005152.comment: This HPO term intends to refer to the histological changes that characterize histiocytoid cardiomyopthy. The disease entity Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy is a rare arrhythmogenic disorder characterized by incessant ventricular tachycardia, cardiomegaly, and often sudden death by age 2 years.

HP:0005155.label: Ventricular escape rhythm
HP:0005155.definition: A ventricular escape rhythm occurs whenever higher-lever pacemakers in AV junction or sinus node fail to control ventricular activation. Escape rate is usually 20-40 bpm, often associated with broad QRS complexes (at least 120 ms).

HP:0005157.label: Concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
HP:0005157.definition: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

HP:0005160.label: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
HP:0005160.definition: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return refers to a congenital malformation in which all four pulmonary veins do not connect normally to the left atrium, but instead drain abnormally to the right atrium.
HP:0005160.comment: Pulmonary veins drain through abnormal connections to the right atrium.

HP:0005162.label: Abnormal left ventricular function
HP:0005162.definition: Inability of the left ventricle to perform its normal physiologic function. Failure is either due to an inability to contract the left ventricle or the inability to relax completely and fill with blood during diastole.

HP:0005164.label: Dysplastic pulmonary valve
HP:0005164.definition: A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

HP:0005165.label: Shortened PR interval
HP:0005165.definition: Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

HP:0005168.label: Elevated right atrial pressure
HP:0005168.definition: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.
HP:0005168.comment: Elevated mean right atrial pressure (RAP) can be measured by cardiac catheterization.

HP:0005170.label: Complete heart block with broad QRS complexes
HP:0005170.definition: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at a relatively low part of the conduction system (below the atrioventricular node), which produces a wide QRS complex.

HP:0005172.label: Left posterior fascicular block
HP:0005172.definition: Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

HP:0005174.label: Membranous subvalvular aortic stenosis
HP:0005174.definition: Subvalvular stenosis is caused by a diaphragm-like membrane. The stenosis is clinically manifested like any other form of aortic stenosis but is often associated with some aortic insufficiency.
HP:0005174.comment: An important feature in the differential diagnosis between valvular and subvalvular aortic stenosis is the fact that no ejection sound is present in the latter.

HP:0005176.label: Dysplastic aortic valve
HP:0005176.definition: A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

HP:0005177.label: Premature arteriosclerosis
HP:0005177.definition: Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.

HP:0005178.label: Complete heart block with narrow QRS complexes
HP:0005178.definition: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at the atrioventricular node, which produces a narrow QRS complex.

HP:0005180.label: Tricuspid regurgitation
HP:0005180.definition: Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.
HP:0005180.comment: This term should not be applied to Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve (see HP:0010316).

HP:0005181.label: Premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
HP:0005181.definition: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.

HP:0005182.label: Bicuspid pulmonary valve
HP:0005182.definition: The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.
HP:0005182.comment: The pulmonary valve normally has three cusps (flaps), that is, it is normally tricuspid.

HP:0005183.label: Pericardial lymphangiectasia
HP:0005183.definition: An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

HP:0005184.label: Prolonged QTc interval
HP:0005184.definition: A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

HP:0005185.label: Global systolic dysfunction
HP:0005185.definition: A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.

HP:0005186.label: Synovial lining hyperplasia
HP:0005186.definition: Synovial hyperplasia involves proliferation of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and leads to synovial thickening, which can be observed radiographically.
HP:0005186.comment: Synovial hyperplasia is a frequent clinical finding in patients with joint injury and other joint disorders.

HP:0005194.label: Flattened metatarsal heads
HP:0005194.definition: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.
HP:0005194.comment: The metatarsal heads articulate with the proximal phalanges of the toes.
exact_synonyms: Flattened head of long bone of foot

HP:0005197.label: Generalized morning stiffness
HP:0005197.definition: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.

HP:0005198.label: Stiff interphalangeal joints
HP:0005198.definition: Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

HP:0005199.label: Aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature

HP:0005202.label: Helicobacter pylori infection
HP:0005202.definition: A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.
HP:0005202.comment: The bacterial pathogen Helicobacter pylori has co-evolved with humans and colonizes approximately half of the human population, but only causes overt gastric disease in a subset of infected hosts.

HP:0005203.label: Spontaneous esophageal perforation
HP:0005203.definition: The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.
HP:0005203.comment: Esophageal perforation can lead to retained gastric contents, saliva, bile, and other substances entering the mediastinum, resulting in mediastinitis, which in turn may lead to sepsis.

HP:0005206.label: Pancreatic pseudocyst
HP:0005206.definition: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.

HP:0005208.label: Secretory diarrhea
HP:0005208.definition: Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

HP:0005209.label: Intrahepatic bile duct cysts
HP:0005209.definition: The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.

HP:0005212.label: Anal mucosal leukoplakia
HP:0005212.definition: Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.

HP:0005213.label: Pancreatic calcification
HP:0005213.definition: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.

HP:0005214.label: Intestinal obstruction
HP:0005214.definition: Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.

HP:0005215.label: Frequent Giardia lamblia infestation
HP:0005215.definition: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.

HP:0005216.label: Impaired mastication
HP:0005216.definition: An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.
HP:0005216.comment: Chewing and swallowing are interrelated. The act of chewing plays a fundamental role in the process of swallowing food. Mastication prepares food for swallowing by breaking it into small particles. Accordingly, loss of teeth has been associated with swallowing difficulties. Chewing difficulties may be caused by loss of teeth, partial dentures, or by tooth pain. Swallowing difficulties, in contrast, are often characterized by difficulties swallowing liquids, reflux, throat spasms, choking on dry food, or dysphagia.

HP:0005217.label: Abdominal organ duplication
HP:0005217.definition: A congenital malformation characterized by the development of an additional organ or organ-like structure, i.e., an extra copy of the organ normally located in the abdomen.

HP:0005218.label: Anoperineal fistula
HP:0005218.definition: The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.

HP:0005219.label: Absence of intrinsic factor
HP:0005219.definition: Absence of gastric intrinsic factor, which is normally produced by the parietal cells of the stomach, and is required for the absorption of vitamin B12.
HP:0005219.comment: This feature can be ascertained by immunoassay of gastric juices.
exact_synonyms: Intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice

HP:0005222.label: Bowel diverticulosis
HP:0005222.definition: The presence of multiple diverticula of the intestine.

HP:0005224.label: Rectal abscess
HP:0005224.definition: A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.

HP:0005225.label: Intestinal edema
HP:0005225.definition: Accumulation of cell free, noninflammatony fluid within the wall of the intestinal tract producing uniform thickening of the mucosal folds.
HP:0005225.comment: This finding can be observed upon abdominal radiography. The bowel lumen may be slightly dilated. Secondary to the fluid accumulation, there are anatomic and motor alterations in the intestine which are reflected in the roentgenogram.

HP:0005227.label: Adenomatous colonic polyposis
HP:0005227.definition: Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.

HP:0005232.label: Pancreatic dysplasia
HP:0005232.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the pancreas.
HP:0005232.comment: Dysplasia is defined in MPATH as a distortion or deficiency of the tissue or cellular architecture.

HP:0005233.label: Hypoplasia of the gallbladder
HP:0005233.definition: The presence of a hypoplastic gallbladder.

HP:0005235.label: Jejunal atresia
HP:0005235.definition: A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.

HP:0005236.label: Chronic calcifying pancreatitis
HP:0005236.definition: A form of chronic pancreatitis that is characterized by calcification.

HP:0005237.label: Degenerative liver disease
HP:0005237.definition: The presence of degenerative changes of the liver.

HP:0005241.label: Total intestinal aganglionosis
HP:0005241.definition: A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.

HP:0005242.label: Extrahepatic biliary duct atresia
HP:0005242.definition: Atresia in the extrahepatic bile duct.

HP:0005243.label: Partial abdominal muscle agenesis
HP:0005243.definition: Failure to form of portions of the abdominal musculature.

HP:0005244.label: Gastrointestinal infarctions
exact_synonyms: Death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply

HP:0005246.label: Giant hypertrophic gastritis
HP:0005246.definition: A type of gastritis characterized by excessive proliferation of the gastric mucosa and diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal folds.

HP:0005247.label: Hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature

HP:0005248.label: Intrahepatic biliary atresia
HP:0005248.definition: Atresia in the intrahepatic bile duct.

HP:0005255.label: Absence of pectoralis minor muscle
HP:0005255.definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor.

HP:0005256.label: Unilateral absence of pectoralis major muscle
HP:0005256.definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.
exact_synonyms: Unilateral aplasia of pectoralis major muscle

HP:0005259.label: Abnormal facility in opposing the shoulders
HP:0005259.definition: Increased range of shoulder movement related to aplasia or hypoplasia of the clavicles that results in the ability to approximate the shoulders in front of the chest.
HP:0005259.comment: This feature is characteristic of cleidocranial dysplasia. See Figure 2 of PMID:23289840

HP:0005262.label: Abnormal synovial membrane morphology
HP:0005262.definition: Any structural anomaly of the synovium, which is a membrane that lines the cavity of synovial joints and consists of a lining layer of macrophage-like synoviocytes and fibroblast-like synoviocytes, as well as a sublining of connective tissue. Synovial cells are thought to contribute to joint homeostasis by secreting various factors such as hyaluronic acid and lubricin important for joint lubrication and function, as well as disposing of the waste products.

HP:0005263.label: Gastritis
HP:0005263.definition: The presence of inflammation of the gastric mucous membrane.

HP:0005265.label: Abnormal jejunum morphology
HP:0005265.definition: An abnormality of the jejunum, i.e., of the middle section of the small intestine.

HP:0005266.label: Intestinal polyp
HP:0005266.definition: A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.

HP:0005267.label: Premature delivery because of cervical insufficiency or membrane fragility

HP:0005268.label: Miscarriage
HP:0005268.definition: A pregnancy that ends at a stage in which the fetus is incapable of surviving on its own, defined as the spontaneous loss of a fetus before the 22th week of pregnancy.
HP:0005268.comment: The age at which fetal demise is legally classified asa a miscarriage varies between countries with the US being 20 gestational weeks and the UK being 24 gestational weeks. The HPO chooses the average of these age ranges.

HP:0005272.label: Prominent nasolabial fold
HP:0005272.definition: Exaggerated bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion, or commissure).

HP:0005273.label: Absent nasal septal cartilage
HP:0005273.definition: Lack of the cartilage of the nasal septum.

HP:0005278.label: Hypoplastic nasal tip
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of tip of nose

HP:0005280.label: Depressed nasal bridge
HP:0005280.definition: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.
HP:0005280.comment: The adjective "depressed" here does not indicate an active process but a status. A depressed nasal bridge can occur irrespective of the width of the nasal bridge, and the width should be assessed independently. In infancy, the nasal bridge is relatively more posterior than in the older person. The term depressed nasal bridge should only be used when the bridge is more posterior than is typical for age and ethnic background.

HP:0005281.label: Hypoplastic nasal bridge
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of bridge of nose

HP:0005290.label: Internal carotid artery hypoplasia
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of internal carotid artery

HP:0005292.label: Intimal thickening in the coronary arteries

HP:0005294.label: Arterial dissection
HP:0005294.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of an artery.

HP:0005295.label: Pseudocoarctation of the aorta
HP:0005295.definition: Pseudocoarctation is a congenital anomaly of kinking, or buckling, of the aorta without a pressure gradient across the lesion. It is characterized by elongation and kinking of the aorta at the level of the ligamentum arteriosum.
HP:0005295.comment: Note that the ligamentum arteriosum, which develops from the ductus arteriosus, is attached to the superior surface of the pulmonary artery and the inferior surface of the aortic arch.

HP:0005297.label: Premature occlusive vascular stenosis
HP:0005297.definition: Peripheral arterial stenosis with onset before the age of 50 years.

HP:0005298.label: obsolete Atrioventricular canal defect with right ventricle aorta and pulmonary atresia

HP:0005301.label: Persistent left superior vena cava
HP:0005301.definition: A rare congenital vascular anomaly that results when the left superior cardinal vein caudal to the innominate vein fails to regress.

HP:0005302.label: Carotid artery tortuosity
HP:0005302.definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the carotid arteries.

HP:0005303.label: Aortic arch calcification
HP:0005303.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the arch of aorta.

HP:0005305.label: Cerebral venous thrombosis
HP:0005305.definition: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a cerebral vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

HP:0005306.label: Capillary hemangioma
HP:0005306.definition: The presence of a capillary hemangioma, which are hemangiomas with small endothelial spaces.

HP:0005310.label: Large vessel vasculitis
HP:0005310.definition: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) affecting large arteries such as the aorta and branches of the aorta.

HP:0005311.label: Agenesis of pulmonary vessels
HP:0005311.definition: A developmental defect characterized by the lack of formation of the pulmonary blood vessels.

HP:0005312.label: Pulmonary aterial intimal fibrosis
HP:0005312.definition: Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries in the pulmonary circulation.
HP:0005312.comment: Some causes of intimal fibrosis are hypertension, intimal fibroplasia, arterial atheroma, and CADASIL syndrome.

HP:0005313.label: Arterial fibromuscular dysplasia
HP:0005313.definition: An arterial lesion that is characterized by either intimal fibroplasia, with neointimal lesions of cells and matrix deposition, or medial fibroplasia, in which there is loss of smooth muscle cells and increased deposition of collagen and proteoglycans in the medial layer.
HP:0005313.comment: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is distinct from atherosclerotic lesions in that FMD lesions do not contain inflammatory cells or lipids. Instead, the pathology of FMD. FMD can result in arterial stenosis or occlusion, and less commonly, arterial dissection or aneurysm formation. FMD can affect almost any artery but most commonly affects the renal arteries, presenting as hypertension, and the carotid and vertebral arteries, leading to ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attacks, headaches, and pulsatile tinnitus.

HP:0005314.label: Anomalous branches of internal carotid artery

HP:0005317.label: Increased pulmonary vascular resistance
HP:0005317.definition: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) more than 3 wood units, as defined by the current definition of pulmonary hypertension. 95% of individuals have a PVR of less than 2.4 wood units.

HP:0005318.label: Cerebral vasculitis
HP:0005318.definition: Inflammation of the blood vessels within the brain.

HP:0005320.label: Lack of facial subcutaneous fat
exact_synonyms: Lack of facial fat below the skin

HP:0005321.label: Mandibulofacial dysostosis
HP:0005321.definition: A type of craniofacial dysostosis associated with abnormalities of the external ears, mirognathia, macrostomia, coloboma of the lower eyelid, and cleft palate. This is a bundled term that is left in the HPO now for convenience with legacy annotations but should not be used for new annotations.

HP:0005323.label: Hemifacial hypertrophy
HP:0005323.definition: Unilateral overgrowth of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.
exact_synonyms: Increase in size of half of face

HP:0005324.label: Disturbance of facial expression
HP:0005324.definition: An abnormality of the gestures or movements executed with the facial muscles with which emotions such as fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and disgust can be expressed.

HP:0005325.label: Extension of hair growth on temples to lateral eyebrow
HP:0005325.definition: A pattern of hair growth in which there is hair extending from the temples to the lateral eyebrows.
exact_synonyms: Unusual hairline with hair growth on temples extending to lateral eyebrow

HP:0005328.label: Progeroid facial appearance
HP:0005328.definition: A degree of wrinkling of the facial skin that is more than expected for the age of the individual, leading to a prematurely aged appearance.

HP:0005332.label: Recurrent mandibular subluxations
HP:0005332.definition: Recurrent partial dislocations of the mandible.

HP:0005338.label: Sparse lateral eyebrow
HP:0005338.definition: Decreased density/number and/or decreased diameter of lateral eyebrow hairs.
HP:0005338.comment: Abnormal sparseness of the eyebrows laterally.
exact_synonyms: Limited hair on end of eyebrow

HP:0005339.label: Abnormality of complement system
HP:0005339.definition: An abnormality of the complement system.
HP:0005339.comment: The complement system represents a family of over 25 serum proteins and cell surface receptors that act in a cascade manner leading to innate functions such as inflammation and enhancement of adaptive immunity. Three general pathways, i.e. classical, lectin and alternative, activate the complement system.

HP:0005341.label: Autonomic bladder dysfunction
HP:0005341.definition: Abnormal bladder function (increased urge or frequency of urination or urge incontinence) resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.

HP:0005344.label: Abnormal carotid artery morphology
HP:0005344.definition: Any structural abnormality of the carotid arteries, including the common carotid artery and its' arterial branches.

HP:0005345.label: Abnormal vena cava morphology
HP:0005345.definition: An abnormality of the structure of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

HP:0005347.label: Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve
HP:0005347.definition: Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve (TCS) is a rare congenital airway malformation in which distinct tracheal rings are replaced by a continuous cartilaginous segment. Vertically fused C- or O-shaped cartilaginous rings can extend from the subglottis to the carina or bronchus with little to no pars membranacea posteriorly. Comment:Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve has been associated with various craniosynostosis syndromes.

HP:0005348.label: Inspiratory stridor
HP:0005348.definition: Inspiratory stridor is a high pitched sound upon inspiration that is generally related to laryngeal abnormalities.

HP:0005352.label: Severe T-cell immunodeficiency
HP:0005352.definition: A primary immune deficiency that is characterized by defects or deficiencies of T-lymphocytes that causes specific susceptibility to intracellular micro-organisms.
HP:0005352.comment: Several diseases are classified as severe T cell immunodeficiencies: severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (SCID), reticular dysgenesis, thymic dysplasia (Nezelof syndrome), combined immunodeficiency disease (CID), and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS).

HP:0005353.label: Recurrent herpes
HP:0005353.definition: Increased susceptibility to herpesvirus, as manifested by recurrent episodes of herpesvirus.

HP:0005354.label: Absent cellular immunity
HP:0005354.definition: Complete inability of T cells to perform their functions in cell-mediated immunity.

HP:0005356.label: Decreased circulating complement factor I concentration
HP:0005356.definition: Concentration of the complement component factor I in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0005357.label: Defective B cell differentiation
HP:0005357.definition: Reduced functionality of the process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a B cell. A B cell is a lymphocyte of B lineage with the phenotype CD19-positive and capable of B cell mediated immunity.

HP:0005359.label: Aplasia of the thymus
HP:0005359.definition: Absence of the thymus. This feature may be appreciated by the lack of a thymic shadow upon radiographic examination.

HP:0005360.label: Susceptibility to chickenpox
HP:0005360.definition: Increased susceptibility to chicken pox, as manifested by recurrent episodes of chicken pox.

HP:0005363.label: Humoral immunodeficiency
HP:0005363.definition: A general term referring to a defect in immunity resulting from impaired antibody production.
HP:0005363.comment: If possible it is preferable to use a precise description of the observed manifestations leading to the inference of humoral immunodeficiency.

HP:0005366.label: Recurrent streptococcus pneumoniae infections
HP:0005366.definition: Increased susceptibility to streptococcus pneumoniae infections as manifested by a history of recurrent infections by streptococcus pneumoniae.

HP:0005368.label: Abnormality of humoral immunity
HP:0005368.definition: An abnormality of the humoral immune system, which comprises antibodies produced by B cells as well as the complement system.

HP:0005369.label: Decreased circulating complement factor H concentration
HP:0005369.definition: Concentration of the complement component factor H in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0005372.label: Abnormal B cell physiology
HP:0005372.definition: An abnormality of the physiological functioning of B cells.
HP:0005372.comment: This term refers to any abnormality of the B cells, which play a role in the humoral immune response. The main functions of B cells are to produce antibodies, to perform the role of antigen presenting cells, and to develop into memory cells.

HP:0005374.label: Cellular immunodeficiency
HP:0005374.definition: An immunodeficiency characterized by defective cell-mediated immunity or humoral immunity.

HP:0005376.label: Recurrent Haemophilus influenzae infections
HP:0005376.definition: Increased susceptibility to Haemophilus influenzae infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection by Haemophilus influenzae.

HP:0005381.label: Recurrent meningococcal disease
HP:0005381.definition: Recurrent infections by Neisseria meningitidis (one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis), which is also known as meningococcus.
exact_synonyms: Increased susceptibility to neisseria meningitidis infections

HP:0005384.label: Defective B cell activation
HP:0005384.definition: A reduced ability of a B cell to become activated, i.e., the change in morphology and behavior of

HP:0005386.label: Recurrent protozoan infections
HP:0005386.definition: Increased susceptibility to protozoan infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of protozoan infection.

HP:0005387.label: Combined immunodeficiency
HP:0005387.definition: A group of phenotypically heterogeneous genetic disorders characterized by profound deficiencies of T- and B-cell function, which predispose the patients to both infectious and noninfectious complications.

HP:0005389.label: Depletion of components of the alternative complement pathway
HP:0005389.definition: An abnormal reduction in the components of the alternative complement pathway, such as the C3 protein or its cleavage products.

HP:0005390.label: Recurrent opportunistic infections
HP:0005390.definition: Increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection by opportunistic agents, i.e., by microorganisms that do not usually cause disease in a healthy host, but are able to infect a host with a compromised immune system.

HP:0005396.label: Susceptibility to coronavirus 229e
HP:0005396.definition: Increased susceptibility to coronavirus 229e, as manifested by recurrent episodes of coronavirus 229e.

HP:0005400.label: Reduction of neutrophil motility
HP:0005400.definition: An abnormal reduction of the cell motility of neutrophils.

HP:0005401.label: Recurrent candida infections
HP:0005401.definition: An increased susceptibility to candida infections, as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of candida infections.

HP:0005403.label: Decreased total T cell count
HP:0005403.definition: The absolute number of T cells per volume is below the lower limit of normal.
exact_synonyms: Decreased numbers of circulating T cells

HP:0005404.label: Increased total B cell count
HP:0005404.definition: The absolute number of B cells in the blood, per microlitre is above the upper limit of normal of the reference range for the appropriate sex and age-group.

HP:0005406.label: Recurrent bacterial skin infections
HP:0005406.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections of the skin, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infectious dermatitis.
HP:0005406.comment: Infectious dermatitis may manifest as impetigo, multiple purulent blisters, erythema, lymphadenopathy near the site of infection.

HP:0005407.label: obsolete Decreased proportion of CD4-positive helper T cells

HP:0005409.label: obsolete Markedly reduced T cell function

HP:0005411.label: Chronic intestinal candidiasis
HP:0005411.definition: Persistent overgrowth of Candida albicans in the gastrointestinal tract.

HP:0005413.label: Elevated circulating alpha-globulin concentration
HP:0005413.definition: The concentration of alpha-globulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0005415.label: Decreased CD8+ T cell proportion
HP:0005415.definition: Abnormal decrease of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.
exact_synonyms: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive T cells
Decreased proportion of CD8+ T cells
Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells

HP:0005416.label: Decreased circulating complement factor B concentration
HP:0005416.definition: Concentration of the complement component factor B in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0005419.label: Decreased T cell activation
HP:0005419.definition: Decreased or impaired activation of T cells in response to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

HP:0005420.label: Recurrent gram-negative bacterial infections
HP:0005420.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection by gram-negative bacteria, as manifested by a medical history of repeated or frequent infections by these agents.
HP:0005420.comment: Gram-negative bacteria have a unique outer membrane, a thinner layer of peptidoglycan compared to gram-positive bacteria, and a periplasmic space between the cell wall and the membrane.

HP:0005421.label: Decreased circulating complement C3 concentration
HP:0005421.definition: Concentration of the complement component C3 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0005422.label: Absence of CD8-positive T cells
HP:0005422.definition: Lack of detectible CD8-positive T cells

HP:0005423.label: Dysfunctional alternative complement pathway
HP:0005423.definition: An abnormality of the functioning of any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.

HP:0005424.label: Absent specific antibody response
HP:0005424.definition: Absence of specific immunoglobulins directed against a specific antigen or microorganism.

HP:0005425.label: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections
HP:0005425.definition: An increased susceptibility to infections involving both the paranasal sinuses and the lungs, as manifested by a history of recurrent sinopulmonary infections.

HP:0005429.label: Recurrent systemic pyogenic infections
HP:0005429.definition: Increased susceptibility to systemic pyogenic infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of systemic pyogenic infections.

HP:0005430.label: Recurrent Neisserial infections
HP:0005430.definition: Recurrent infections by bacteria of the genus Neisseria, including N. meningitidis (one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis).

HP:0005432.label: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
HP:0005432.definition: At birth, newborns are endowed with maternal antibodies. IgG production normally begins at the age of two months. A delay in recovery from this physiological hypogammaglobulinemia between the 3rd and the 6th month of life, and of recovery period between 18 and 36 months defines transient newborn hypogammaglobulinemia.

HP:0005437.label: Recurrent infections in infancy and early childhood
HP:0005437.definition: Recurrent infections at an early age with improvement in later childhood.

HP:0005439.label: Maxillozygomatic hypoplasia
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex
related_synonyms: Decreased projection of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex

HP:0005441.label: Sclerotic cranial sutures
HP:0005441.definition: An increased density in the cranial sutures following obliteration.

HP:0005442.label: Widely patent coronal suture
HP:0005442.definition: The presence of a coronal suture (the cranial suture that separates the frontal and parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.

HP:0005445.label: Enlarged posterior fossa
HP:0005445.definition: Abnormal increased size of the posterior cranial fossa.

HP:0005446.label: Obtuse angle of mandible
HP:0005446.definition: Abnormally flat (obtuse) angle of the mandible. The angle of the mandibular, located at the junction between the body and the ramus of the mandible, is normally close to being a right angle. This terms describes an abnormal increase of this angle such that the mandible appears flatter than normal.
HP:0005446.comment: See PMID:17213440 Figure 1G for an example of an obtuse mandibular angle.

HP:0005450.label: Calvarial osteosclerosis
HP:0005450.definition: An increase in bone density affecting the calvaria (roof of the skull).

HP:0005453.label: Absent/hypoplastic paranasal sinuses
HP:0005453.definition: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the paranasal sinuses.

HP:0005456.label: Absent ethmoidal sinuses
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of ethmoid sinuses

HP:0005458.label: Premature closure of fontanelles
HP:0005458.definition: Normally, the posterior and lateral fontanelles are obliterated by about six months after birth, the anterior fontanelle closes by about the middle of the second year. This term refers to the situation in which the fontanelles close at an inappropriately early time point.

HP:0005462.label: Calcification of falx cerebri
HP:0005462.definition: The presence of calcium deposition in the falx cerebri.

HP:0005464.label: Craniofacial osteosclerosis
HP:0005464.definition: Abnormally increased density of craniofacial bone tissue.

HP:0005465.label: Facial hyperostosis
HP:0005465.definition: Excessive growth (overgrowth) of the facial bones, that is of the facial skeleton.
exact_synonyms: Increase in size of the facial bones

HP:0005466.label: Hypoplasia of the frontal bone
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of bone of forehead

HP:0005469.label: Flat occiput
HP:0005469.definition: Reduced convexity of the occiput (posterior part of skull).
HP:0005469.comment: Reduced convexity of the occiput gives an appearance of flattening. There are no objective measures for convexity of the occiput, and evaluation depends heavily on the experience of the observer. This finding may or may not be accompanied by Brachycephaly (which should be coded separately), and may be observed more frequently when an infant is placed to sleep on his/her back. Occipital plagiocephaly can result from fusion or sclerosis of the lambdoid suture. If unilateral, this is accompanied by unilateral occipital flattening and bulging of the ispilateral frontal bone.

HP:0005473.label: Fusion of middle ear ossicles
HP:0005473.definition: Bony fusion of malleus, incus, and stapes.

HP:0005474.label: Decreased calvarial ossification
HP:0005474.definition: Abnormal reduction in ossification of the calvaria (roof of the skull consisting of the frontal bone, parietal bones, temporal bones, and occipital bone).
HP:0005474.comment: A hypomineralised skull castes little or no acoustic shadow on prenatal ultrasound. This makes visualization of the intracranial anatomy clearer than normal. In conditions associated with profound hypomineralisation, the skull shape can be distorted by pressure from the ultrasound transducer later in pregnancy.

HP:0005476.label: Widely patent sagittal suture
HP:0005476.definition: The presence of a sagittal suture (the cranial suture that separates the left and right parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.

HP:0005477.label: Progressive sclerosis of skull base
HP:0005477.definition: Progressively increasing bone density of the skull base without significant changes in bony contour.

HP:0005479.label: Decreased circulating IgE concentration
HP:0005479.definition: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin E (IgE) in blood.

HP:0005482.label: Abnormality of the alternative complement pathway
HP:0005482.definition: A deviation in any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.
HP:0005482.comment: The alternative complement pathway is one of three complement pathways, which is an innate component of the immune system's natural defense against infections. The alternative complement pathway has three unique components, factor B, factor D, and properdin.

HP:0005484.label: Secondary microcephaly
HP:0005484.definition: Head circumference which falls below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender because of insufficient head growth after birth.

HP:0005486.label: Small fontanelle
HP:0005486.definition: A fontanelle that is small for age.

HP:0005487.label: Prominent metopic ridge
HP:0005487.definition: Vertical bony ridge positioned in the midline of the forehead.
HP:0005487.comment: The ridge may extend from the hairline to the glabella or may be partial. The frontal suture of the skull is a dense connective tissue structure that divides the two halves of the frontal bone of the skull in infants and children and usually undergoes closure by the age of six years. A persistent frontal suture is known as a metopic suture or sutura frontalis persistens. This can lead to a ridged appearance of the forehead.

HP:0005490.label: Postnatal macrocephaly
HP:0005490.definition: The postnatal development of an abnormally large skull (macrocephaly).

HP:0005495.label: Metopic suture patent to nasal root
HP:0005495.definition: The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone in infants and usually fuses by the age of six years. The suture runs from the bregma (the point on the skull at which the coronal suture is intersected perpendicularly by the sagittal suture) to the nasion or nasal root. This term applies if the suture is widely patent from bregma to nasal root.
HP:0005495.comment: This feature is a characteristic of Schinzel-Giedion midface retraction syndrome.
