HP:0005498.label: Midline skin dimples over anterior/posterior fontanelles

HP:0005506.label: Chronic myelogenous leukemia
HP:0005506.definition: A myeloproliferative disorder characterized by increased proliferation of the granulocytic cell line without the loss of their capacity to differentiate.

HP:0005507.label: Hemoglobin Barts
HP:0005507.definition: Normal adult hemoglobin is composed of two chains each of alpha and beta globin. Hb Barts (Hemoglobin Barts) is a tetramer with four gamma globin chains, and is essentially pathognomonic for one or another form of alpha thalassemia. Hb Barts has an extremely high affinity for oxygen, resulting in almost no oxygen delivery to the tissues.
HP:0005507.comment: Hb Bart is normally not present in adult blood. It makes up about 85-90 percent of hemoglobin in Hb Bart hydrops fetalis syndrome, and about 2-5 percent in HbH disease.

HP:0005508.label: Monoclonal immunoglobulin M proteinemia
HP:0005508.definition: Presence of a monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum.
HP:0005508.comment: This is a characteristic feature of Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (WM), which is defined as a B-cell lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, characterized by monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum and infiltration of bone marrow with lymphoplasmacytic cells.

HP:0005510.label: Transient erythroblastopenia
HP:0005510.definition: A transient reduction in the number of erythroblasts in the circulation.
HP:0005510.comment: An erythroblast, the immediate precursor of a normal erythrocyte which, still retains a cell nucleus.
exact_synonyms: Transient decrease in blood erythrocyte number

HP:0005511.label: Heinz body anemia
HP:0005511.definition: Anemia characterized by abnormal intracellular inclusions, composed of denatured hemoglobin, found on the membrane of red blood cells.

HP:0005512.label: obsolete Impaired neutrophil killing of staphylococci

HP:0005513.label: Increased megakaryocyte count
HP:0005513.definition: Increased megakaryocyte number, i.e., of platelet precursor cells, present in the bone marrow.

HP:0005517.label: T-cell lymphoma/leukemia
HP:0005517.definition: A type of T-cell lymphoma in which cancerous T-cells may present in the blood (leukemia), lymph nodes (lymphoma), skin or in multiple areas.
HP:0005517.comment: T-cell lymphoma/leukemia is linked to infection by the human T-cell lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-1).

HP:0005518.label: Increased mean corpuscular volume
HP:0005518.definition: Larger than normal size of erythrocytes.
HP:0005518.comment: Macrocytosis refers to a mean cell volume (MCV) greater than 100 fL. If macrocytosis is an isolated abnormality, the amount of hemoglobin in the cell increases proportionately, so the mean cell hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) remains within normal limits.

HP:0005520.label: Chronic disseminated intravascular coagulation
HP:0005520.definition: A chronic form of disseminated intravascular coagulation in which a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus is present and destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

HP:0005521.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
HP:0005521.definition: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is characterized by the widespread activation of coagulation, which results in the intravascular formation of fibrin and ultimately thrombotic occlusion of small and midsize vessels.
HP:0005521.comment: DIC is a complex syndrome in which there is pathological generation of thrombin and diffuse intravascular clot formation. DIC may occur as acute decompensated or chronic compensated form. In acute decompensated DIC, there is a sudden massive exposure of tissue factor over a brief time period; Intravascular coagulation can also compromise the blood supply to organs and, in conjunction with hemodynamic and metabolic derangements, may contribute to the failure of multiple organs. At the same time, the use and subsequent depletion of platelets and coagulation proteins resulting from the ongoing coagulation may induce severe bleeding. Chronic DIC, also known as compensated DIC, results from a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus. Under such conditions, destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

HP:0005522.label: Pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anemia
HP:0005522.definition: A type of sideroblastic anemia that is alleviated by pyridoxine (vitamin B-6) treatment.

HP:0005526.label: Lymphoid leukemia
HP:0005526.definition: A malignant lymphocytic neoplasm of B-cell or T-cell lineage involving primarily the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. This category includes precursor or acute lymphoblastic leukemias and chronic leukemias.

HP:0005527.label: Reduced kininogen activity
HP:0005527.definition: Amount or activity of kininogen is below the lower limit of normal. Kininogen functions as a cofactor in the contact phase of the intrinsic blood coagulation cascade.
HP:0005527.comment: Kininogen is cleaved into the following 6 chains: 1) Kininogen-1 heavy chain; 2) T-kinin; 3) Bradykinin; 4) Lysyl-bradykinin; 5) Kininogen-1 light chain; and 6) Low molecular weight growth-promoting factor.

HP:0005528.label: Bone marrow hypocellularity
HP:0005528.definition: A reduced number of hematopoietic cells present in the bone marrow relative to marrow fat.

HP:0005531.label: Biphenotypic acute leukemia
HP:0005531.definition: A type of actue leukemia with features characteristic of both the myeloid and lymphoid lineages. These leukemias are for this reason are designated mixed-lineage, hybrid or biphenotypic acute leukemias.

HP:0005534.label: Transient myeloproliferative syndrome
HP:0005534.definition: A unique clonal neoplastic disorder that is linked to trisomy 21, is restricted to neonatal period, and spontaneously regresses. It often has characteristics of megakaryocytic lineage and is associated with GATA1 mutations in myeloblasts.

HP:0005535.label: Exercise-induced hemolysis
HP:0005535.definition: A form of hemolytic anemia that can be triggered by exertion.

HP:0005537.label: Decreased mean platelet volume
HP:0005537.definition: Average platelet volume below the lower limit of the normal reference interval.
HP:0005537.comment: Mean platelet volume (MPV) is a measure of the average size of platelets, with a typical reference range of 7.5 to 11.5 femtoliters (fL).

HP:0005539.label: T cell chronic lymphocytic lymphoma/leukemia
HP:0005539.definition: A form of lymphoid leukemia or lymphoma in which too many T-cell lymphoblasts are found in the blood, bone marrow, and tissues. Leukemia or lymphoma classification depends on which feature is more prominent.

HP:0005540.label: Red blood cell keratocytosis
HP:0005540.definition: A form of poikilocytosis in which the abnormally shaped erythrocytes have notches that results in projections that look like horns.
HP:0005540.comment: Kerato- is derived from the Greek word for horn.
exact_synonyms: Distorted red blood cells resembling keratocytes

HP:0005541.label: Congenital agranulocytosis
HP:0005541.definition: Persistent absence of detectable circulating granulocytes in the blood with no detected secondary cause. Usually a value of less than 50 granulocytes per microliter is considered to be an absence.

HP:0005542.label: Prolonged whole-blood clotting time
HP:0005542.definition: An abnormal prolongation (delay) in the time required by whole blood to produce a visible clot.

HP:0005543.label: Reduced protein C activity
HP:0005543.definition: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein C. Protein C is activated to protein Ca by thrombin bound to thrombomodulin. Activated protein C degrades factors VIIIa and Va.
HP:0005543.comment: Protein C can function as an anticoagulant by irreversibly proteolytically inactivating Factor Va and Factor VIIIa. Therefore, a defect in protein C is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

HP:0005547.label: Myeloproliferative disorder
HP:0005547.definition: Proliferation (excess production) of hemopoietically active tissue or of tissue which has embryonic hemopoietic potential.
HP:0005547.comment: There are four main myeloproliferative disroders, 1) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML); 2) Polycythemia vera; 3) Essential thrombocytosis; and 4) Myelofibrosis.

HP:0005548.label: Megakaryocytopenia
HP:0005548.comment: Megakaryocytes are giant cells in the bone marrow. Mature blood platelets are released from the cytoplasm of megakaryocytes.

HP:0005549.label: obsolete Congenital neutropenia
HP:0005549.comment: This term was obsoleted - for annotation of congenital neutropenia, please use the class HP_0001875 Neutropenia and the Modifier Congenital Onset.

HP:0005550.label: Chronic lymphatic leukemia
HP:0005550.definition: A chronic lymphocytic/lymphatic/lymphoblastic leukemia (CLL) is a neoplastic disease characterized by proliferation and accumulation (blood, marrow and lymphoid organs) of morphologically mature but immunologically dysfunctional lymphocytes. A CLL is always a B-cell lymphocytic leukemia as there are no reports of cases of T-cell lymphocytic leukemias.

HP:0005556.label: Abnormality of the metopic suture
HP:0005556.definition: The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone of the skull in infants and children and generally undergoes fusion by the age of six. A persistent frontal suture is referred to as a "metopic suture".

HP:0005557.label: Abnormal zygomatic arch morphology
HP:0005557.definition: An abnormality of the zygomatic arch, also known as the cheek bone.
HP:0005557.comment: The zygomatic arch is formed by the zygomatic process of temporal bone and the temporal process of the zygomatic bone.

HP:0005558.label: Chronic leukemia
HP:0005558.definition: A slowly progressing leukemia characterized by a clonal (malignant) proliferation of maturing and mature myeloid cells or mature lymphocytes. When the clonal cellular population is composed of myeloid cells, the process is called chronic myelogenous leukemia. When the clonal cellular population is composed of lymphocytes, it is classified as chronic lymphocytic leukemia, hairy cell leukemia, or T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia.

HP:0005559.label: Abnormal kinin-kallikrein system component activity
HP:0005559.definition: The activity or concentration of a component of the kinin-kallikrein system is outside the limits of normal.
HP:0005559.comment: The kinin-kallikrein system (KKS) is a peptide cascade involved in several physiological processes such as inflammation, coagulation, pain, blood pressure control, and vascular permeability. In the KKS, kinins originate from kininogens through the action of tissue and plasma kallikreins. Some impacts of kinins are induced via activation of B1 and/or B2 receptors and downstream signaling such as nitric oxide.

HP:0005560.label: Imbalanced hemoglobin synthesis
HP:0005560.definition: Normal hemoglobin synthesis is characterized by production of equal amounts of alpha and beta globins. This term refers to a deviation from this pattern and is the main characteristic of the various forms of thalassemia.
HP:0005560.comment: While imbalanced hemoglobin synthesis can be inferred from other findings including those of hemoglobin electrophoresis, the determination of this feature requires investigation of hemoglobin synthesis in vitro, e.g., by incubation of washed peripheral blood erythrocytes and bone marrow cells with radioactively labeled leucine followed by column chromatography.

HP:0005561.label: Abnormal bone marrow cell morphology
HP:0005561.definition: An anomaly of the form or number of cells in the bone marrow.
exact_synonyms: Anomaly of the bone marrow cells
Abnormality of bone marrow cell morphology

HP:0005562.label: Multiple renal cysts
HP:0005562.definition: The presence of many cysts in the kidney.

HP:0005563.label: Decreased numbers of nephrons
HP:0005563.definition: A reduction in the count of nephrons per kidney.

HP:0005564.label: Absence of renal corticomedullary differentiation
HP:0005564.definition: A lack of differentiation between renal cortex and medulla on diagnostic imaging.

HP:0005565.label: Reduced renal corticomedullary differentiation
HP:0005565.definition: Reduced differentiation between renal cortex and medulla on diagnostic imaging.
exact_synonyms: Loss of definition of corticomedullary differentiation

HP:0005567.label: Renal magnesium wasting
HP:0005567.definition: High urine magnesium in the presence of hypomagnesemia.

HP:0005571.label: Increased renal tubular phosphate reabsorption
exact_synonyms: Increased percent tubular reabsorption of phosphorus

HP:0005574.label: Non-acidotic proximal tubulopathy
HP:0005574.definition: A type of proximal renal tubulopathy characterized by resorption defects leading to glycosuria, aminoaciduria, tubular proteinuria, renal hypophosphatemia, and urate tubular hyporeabsorption without bicarbonate loss.

HP:0005575.label: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome
HP:0005575.definition: A thrombotic microangiopathy with presence of non-immune, intravascular hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury. A vicious cycle of complement activation, endothelial cell damage, platelet activation, and thrombosis is the hallmark of the disease.

HP:0005576.label: Tubulointerstitial fibrosis
HP:0005576.definition: A progressive detrimental connective tissue deposition (fibrosis) on the kidney parenchyma involving the tubules and interstitial tissue of the kidney. Tubulointerstitial injury in the kidney is complex, involving a number of independent and overlapping cellular and molecular pathways, with renal interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IF/TA) as the final common pathway. However, IF and TA are separable, as shown by the profound TA in renal artery stenosis, which characteristically has little or no fibrosis (or inflammation). For new annotations it is preferable to annotate to the specific HPO terms for Renal interstitial fibrosis and/or Renal tubular atrophy.
HP:0005576.comment: This finding is usually shown by renal biopsy. Fibrosis involves an excess accumulation of extracellular matrix and usually results in loss of function when normal tissue is replaced with scar tissue. Tubulointerstitial renal fibrosis, characterized as a progressive detrimental connective tissue deposition on the kidney parenchyma, appears to be a harmful process leading inevitably to renal function deterioration, independently of the primary renal disease which causes the original kidney injury. Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) of tubular epithelial cells which are transformed to mesenchymal fibroblasts migrating to adjacent interstitial parenchyma constitutes the principal mechanism of renal fibrosis along with local and circulating cells. (PMID:20011086)

HP:0005579.label: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of chloride
HP:0005579.definition: Any impairment of reabsorption of chloride by the kidney.

HP:0005580.label: Duplication of renal pelvis
HP:0005580.definition: A duplication of the renal pelvis.

HP:0005583.label: Tubular basement membrane disintegration
HP:0005583.definition: DIsruption and breaking up of the basement membrane of the tubules of the kidney.
HP:0005583.comment: Throughout the rest of the nephron, tubule epithelial cells are attached to the tubular basement membrane that overlies the subjacent interstitial connective tissue. The disruption of cell-basement membrane adhesion results in loss of cell orientation, abnormal cell function, and can lead to tissue destruction.
exact_synonyms: Disintegration of the tubular basement membrane

HP:0005584.label: Renal cell carcinoma
HP:0005584.definition: A type of carcinoma of the kidney with origin in the epithelium of the proximal convoluted renal tubule.
HP:0005584.comment: Renal cell carcinoma (also known as hypernephroma) is the most common form of kidney cancer arising from the proximal renal tubule. The tissue of origin for renal cell carcinoma is the proximal renal tubular epithelium. Renal cell carcinoma can be classified as 1) clear cell carcinoma, 2) papillary carcinoma, 3) chromophobe renal carcinoma, and 4) collecting duct carcinoma.
exact_synonyms: Cancer starting in small tubes in kidneys

HP:0005588.label: Patchy palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0005588.definition: A focal type of palmoplantar keratoderma in which only certain areas of the palms and soles are affected.
HP:0005588.comment: Patchy palmoplantar keratoderma may develop at sites of recurrent friction.

HP:0005592.label: Giant melanosomes in melanocytes
HP:0005592.definition: The presence of large spherical melanosomes (1 to 6 micrometer in diameter) in the cytoplasm of melanocytes.
HP:0005592.comment: Giant melanosomes can be seen in cafe-au-lait spots and other melanocytic disorders. Giant melanosome and giant melanosome are synonymous. Macromelanosomes can be detected by electron microscopy of the skin.

HP:0005593.label: Macular hypopigmented whorls, streaks, and patches

HP:0005597.label: Congenital alopecia totalis
HP:0005597.definition: Loss of all scalp hair with congenital onset.

HP:0005598.label: Facial telangiectasia in butterfly midface distribution
HP:0005598.definition: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin in a butterfly midface distribution.

HP:0005600.label: Congenital giant melanocytic nevus
HP:0005600.definition: The giant congenital nevus is greater than 8 cm in size, pigmented and often hairy. A giant congenital nevus is smaller in infants and children, but it usually continues to grow with the child.
HP:0005600.comment: Between 4% and 6% of these lesions will develop into a malignant melanoma.

HP:0005605.label: Large cafe-au-lait macules with irregular margins
HP:0005605.definition: Large hypermelanotic macules with jagged borders.
HP:0005605.comment: This type of lesionk is observed in McCune Albright syndrome. The cafe-au-lait macules are larger than those seen in neurofibromatosis, and have more irregular borders. The borders of these macules have been compared to the coast of Maine, whereas the cafe-au-lait spots in neurofibromatosis type 1 have been compared to the coast of California.

HP:0005608.label: Bilobate gallbladder
HP:0005608.definition: The presence of a bilobed gallbladder, related to a duplication of the gallbladder primordium.
HP:0005608.comment: During the fifth or early sixth embryonic week, occasionally, the gallbladder primordium bifurcates and results in duplication of gallbladder. Duplication results from a split primordium whilst a true accessory gallbladder results from an extra primordium. There are no specific symptoms or signs associated with multiple gallbladders.

HP:0005613.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the femur
HP:0005613.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the femur.

HP:0005616.label: Accelerated skeletal maturation
HP:0005616.definition: An abnormally increased rate of skeletal maturation. Accelerated skeletal maturation can be diagnosed on the basis of an estimation of the bone age from radiographs of specific bones in the human body.

HP:0005619.label: Thoracolumbar kyphosis
HP:0005619.definition: Hyperconvexity of the thoracolumbar spine producing a rounded or humped appearance.

HP:0005620.label: Hypermobility of interphalangeal joints
HP:0005620.definition: The ability of the interphalangeal joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

HP:0005621.label: Trapezoidal vertebral body
HP:0005621.definition: An anomalous trapezoidal appearance of a vertebral body. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape that has two sides that are parallel and two sides that are not parallel. In this case, the two lateral sides of the vertebra are parallel, and the top and the bottom are slanted with respect to each other such that the vertebra is shorter in the front or back than on the other side.

HP:0005622.label: Broad long bones
HP:0005622.definition: Increased cross-section (diameter) of the long bones. Note that widening may primarily affect specific regions of long bones (e.g., diaphysis or metaphysis), but this should be coded separately.

HP:0005623.label: Absent ossification of calvaria
HP:0005623.definition: Acalvaria is an extremely rare congenital malformation characterized by an absence of flat bones of skull, dura mater, and associated muscles in the presence of normal cranial contents and facial bones.
HP:0005623.comment: Absent ossification of the calvaria (vault of the skull).

HP:0005626.label: Posterior fusion of lumbosacral vertebrae
HP:0005626.definition: Bony fusion of the posterior part of the L5 vertebral body with the sacrum.

HP:0005627.label: Type D brachydactyly
HP:0005627.definition: This type of brachydactyly is characterized by short and broad terminal phalanges of the thumbs and big toes.

HP:0005638.label: Decreased anterioposterior diameter of lumbar vertebral bodies

HP:0005639.label: Hyperextensible hand joints
HP:0005639.definition: The ability of the joints of the hand to move beyond their normal range of motion.

HP:0005645.label: Intervertebral disk calcification
HP:0005645.definition: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition of the intervertebral disk.

HP:0005648.label: Bilateral ulnar hypoplasia
HP:0005648.definition: Underdevelopment of the ulna on both sides.

HP:0005650.label: 2-5 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0005650.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second to the fifth fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

HP:0005652.label: Cortical sclerosis
HP:0005652.definition: Sclerosis (abnormal hardening) of cortical bone, characterized by increased radiodensity.

HP:0005655.label: Multiple digital exostoses
HP:0005655.definition: Multiple exostoses originating in the fingers and toes.
HP:0005655.comment: This feature is characteristic of metachondromatosis (MIM:156250).

HP:0005656.label: Positional foot deformity
HP:0005656.definition: A foot deformity resulting due to an abnormality affecting the muscle and soft tissue. In contrast if the bones of the foot are affected the term structural foot deformity applies.

HP:0005661.label: Salmonella osteomyelitis
HP:0005661.definition: Osteomyelitis caused by infection with the bacteria, salmonella.

HP:0005665.label: Massively thickened long bone cortices
HP:0005665.definition: Extreme thickening of the cortex of long bones.

HP:0005667.label: Os odontoideum
HP:0005667.definition: Separation of the odontoid process from the body of the axis.
HP:0005667.comment: With os odontoideum, the caudal fragment of the odontoid process may provide deficient stability for the atlantoaxial joint and lead to subsequent instability or dislocation and neurological deficits.

HP:0005671.label: Bilateral intracerebral calcifications
HP:0005671.definition: Deposition of calcium salts on both sides of the cerebrum.

HP:0005679.label: Dupuytren contracture
HP:0005679.definition: An abnormality of the hand resulting from contracture of the palmar fascia with a fixed flexion deformity of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints and the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints.
HP:0005679.comment: A Dupuytren contracture usually affects the fourth and fifth digits (the ring and small fingers). Affected persons are not able to extend the 4th and 5th fingers.

HP:0005680.label: Tongue-like lumbar vertebral deformities
HP:0005680.definition: A tongue-like protusion from the anterior aspect of lumbar vertebral bodies.

HP:0005684.label: Distal arthrogryposis
HP:0005684.definition: An inherited primary limb malformation disorder characterized by congenital contractures of two or more different body areas and without primary neurologic and/or muscle disease that affects limb function.

HP:0005686.label: Patchy osteosclerosis
HP:0005686.definition: Patchy (irregular) increase in bone density. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.
exact_synonyms: Patchy increase of bone mineral density

HP:0005687.label: Deformed humeral heads
exact_synonyms: Deformed head of long bone in upper arm

HP:0005688.label: Dysplastic distal thumb phalanges with a central hole

HP:0005694.label: Partial fusion of proximal row of carpal bones

HP:0005696.label: Postaxial polydactyly type A
HP:0005696.definition: Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand with a complete extra finger and extra metacarpal.

HP:0005700.label: Increased bone density with cystic changes

HP:0005707.label: Bilateral triphalangeal thumbs
HP:0005707.definition: A bilateral form of triphalangeal thumb.

HP:0005709.label: 2-3 toe cutaneous syndactyly
exact_synonyms: Complete cutaneous syndactyly of second and third toes
Cutaneous syndactyly of second and third toes

HP:0005715.label: Flattened knee epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Flattened end part of knee bone

HP:0005720.label: Shortening of all metacarpals
HP:0005720.definition: Abnormal reduction in length of all metacarpal bones.

HP:0005722.label: Hyperextensible thumb
HP:0005722.definition: The ability of the thumb joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

HP:0005725.label: Nonopposable triphalangeal thumb
HP:0005725.definition: A form of triphalangeal thumb that cannot be placed opposite the fingers of the same hand.

HP:0005731.label: Cortical irregularity
HP:0005731.definition: An abnormal irregularity of cortical bone.

HP:0005733.label: Spinal stenosis with reduced interpedicular distance
HP:0005733.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal related to a reduction in the interpedicular distance (i.e., the distance measured between the pedicles on frontal [coronal] imaging).
HP:0005733.comment: The pedicles are two short, thick processes that connect the body of the vertebrae to the arch.
exact_synonyms: Spinal stenosis due to short pedicles

HP:0005739.label: Posterior subluxation of radial head
HP:0005739.definition: Partial dislocation of the head of the radius in the posterior direction.

HP:0005743.label: Avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0005743.definition: Avascular necrosis of the proximal epiphysis of the femur occurring in growing children and caused by an interruption of the blood supply to the head of the femur close to the hip joint. The necrosis is characteristically associated with flattening of the femoral head, for which reason the term coxa plana has been used to refer to this feature in the medical literature.
HP:0005743.comment: In medical parlance, this is often referred to as Legg Calve Perthes disease. Here, the name 'Avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis' is preferred to emphasize that the term refers to a phenotypic feature rather than a disease entity. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head may result in pain in the hip, limp, stiffness and reduced range of motion, and some degree of atrophy of the affected leg. The phrase Legg Perthes syndrome or Legg Calve Perthes disease is also used to refer to a number of diseases, including the idiopathic form and a form that is related to mutation in the COL2A1 gene (MIM 150600). Legg-Calve-Perthes disease usually occurs in boys 4 to 10 years old, and is clinically characterized by limping, hip stiffness, limited range of motion, and can result in restriction of growth of the affected leg and wasting of the muscles of the upper thigh.

HP:0005744.label: obsolete Generalized osteoporosis with pathologic fractures

HP:0005746.label: Osteosclerosis of the base of the skull
HP:0005746.definition: An increase in bone density affecting the basicranium (base of the skull).
HP:0005746.comment: Bundled term. Consider obsoleting it and splitting of osteosclerosis of base of skull.

HP:0005750.label: Lower-limb joint contracture
HP:0005750.definition: A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint of the lower limb resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.
exact_synonyms: Contractures of the joints of the lower limbs

HP:0005756.label: Neonatal epiphyseal stippling
HP:0005756.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more epiphyses during the neonatal period.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in bone end parts in neonates

HP:0005758.label: Basilar impression
HP:0005758.definition: Abnormal elevation of the floor of the posterior fossa including occipital condyles and foramen magnum.

HP:0005759.label: Small flat posterior fossa
HP:0005759.definition: An abnormally small and flat configuration of the posterior cranial fossa.
exact_synonyms: Small and flat posterior skull bones
Small and flat posterior fossa of skull

HP:0005768.label: 2-4 toe cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0005768.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the toes 2, 3, and 4.
exact_synonyms: Webbed second, third and fourth toes
Soft tissue syndactyly of toes 2, 3, and 4

HP:0005769.label: Fifth finger distal phalanx clinodactyly
HP:0005769.definition: Bending or curvature of the distal phalanx of little finger in the radial direction (i.e., towards the 4th finger).

HP:0005772.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the tibia
HP:0005772.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the tibia.

HP:0005773.label: Short forearm
HP:0005773.definition: Underdevelopment of both forearm bones, the ulna and the radius, resulting in a shortened forearm.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of both radius and ulna

HP:0005780.label: Absent fourth finger distal interphalangeal crease
HP:0005780.definition: Absence of the distal interphalangeal flexion creases of the fourth finger.
exact_synonyms: No fourth finger distal interphalangeal crease

HP:0005787.label: Lumbar platyspondyly
HP:0005787.definition: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates affecting the lumbar spine.

HP:0005789.label: Generalized osteosclerosis
HP:0005789.definition: An abnormal increase of bone mineral density with generalized involvement of the skeleton.

HP:0005790.label: Short mandibular condyles
exact_synonyms: Bilateral hypoplasia of mandibular condylar neck
Bilateral hypoplasia of condylar process of mandible
Decreased height of condylar process of mandible
Decreased length of condylar process of mandible
Bilateral hypoplasia of mandibular condylar head

HP:0005791.label: Cortical thickening of long bone diaphyses
HP:0005791.definition: Abnormal thickening of the cortex of the diaphyseal region of long bones.

HP:0005792.label: Short humerus
exact_synonyms: Short long bone of upper arm

HP:0005793.label: Shortening of all distal phalanges of the toes
HP:0005793.definition: Abnormally short distal phalanx of toe of all toes.
exact_synonyms: Shortening of all outermost bone of the toes

HP:0005798.label: Posterior radial head dislocation
HP:0005798.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an posterior direction.

HP:0005815.label: Supernumerary ribs
HP:0005815.definition: The presence of more than 12 rib pairs.

HP:0005817.label: Postaxial polysyndactyly of foot
HP:0005817.definition: Combined syndactyly and polydactyly of the foot on the lateral side (i.e., on the side of the little toe).

HP:0005819.label: Short middle phalanx of finger
HP:0005819.definition: Short (hypoplastic) middle phalanx of finger, affecting one or more fingers.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the middle phalanges of the hand

HP:0005824.label: Clinodactyly of the 2nd toe
HP:0005824.definition: Bending or curvature of a second toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

HP:0005830.label: Flexion contracture of toe
HP:0005830.definition: One or more bent (flexed) toe joints that cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0005832.label: Dysharmonic delayed bone age
HP:0005832.definition: A type of dysharmonic skeletal maturation in which there is a delay in skeletal maturation whose degree differs markedly in different bones.

HP:0005833.label: obsolete Joint swelling onset late infancy

HP:0005837.label: obsolete Joint dislocations in young adult

HP:0005841.label: Calcific stippling of infantile cartilaginous skeleton

HP:0005844.label: Rounded middle phalanx of finger
HP:0005844.definition: An abnormally round shape of the middle phalanx of the finger.

HP:0005849.label: Diffuse cerebral calcification
HP:0005849.definition: Generalized deposition of calcium salts within the cerebrum.

HP:0005855.label: Multiple prenatal fractures
HP:0005855.definition: The presence of bone fractures in the prenatal period that are diagnosed at birth or before.
exact_synonyms: Numerous multiple fractures present at birth
Numerous multiple fractures that are present at birth

HP:0005856.label: Ulnar radial head dislocation
HP:0005856.definition: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an ulnar direction.

HP:0005863.label: Type E brachydactyly
HP:0005863.definition: In type E brachydactyly, shortening of the fingers is mainly in the metacarpals and metatarsals.

HP:0005864.label: Pseudoarthrosis
HP:0005864.definition: A pathologic entity characterized by a developmental defect in a long bone leading to bending and pathologic fracture, with inability to form a normal bony callus with subsequent fibrous nonunion, leading to the pseudarthrosis (or "false joint").

HP:0005866.label: Opposable triphalangeal thumb
HP:0005866.definition: A form of triphalangeal thumb that can be placed opposite the fingers of the same hand.

HP:0005867.label: 4-5 metacarpal synostosis
exact_synonyms: Synostosis of the fourth and fifth metacarpal bones
Ring finger and little finger metacarpal synostosis

HP:0005868.label: Metaphyseal enchondromatosis
HP:0005868.definition: An enchondroma is a benign growth of cartilage that develops within the medullary cavity of bone. Enchondromatosis refers to the presence of multiple enchondromas, and this term refers to the presence of multiple enchondromas within the medulla of metaphyseal bone. Radiographically an enchondroma presents a an oval, linear, or pyramidal osteolytic (radiolucent) lesion with well defined margins.

HP:0005871.label: Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
HP:0005871.definition: An abnormality of skeletal development characterized by a disturbance of the metaphysis and its histological structure with relatively normal epiphyses and vertebrae.
HP:0005871.comment: The term metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is usually used to describe a disease but is often also used to describe the corresponding phenotypic appearance. This use is retained in the HPO for convenience, but if possible a precise phenotypic description is preferred.

HP:0005872.label: Brachytelomesophalangy
HP:0005872.definition: Disproportionately short middle and distal phalanges compared to the hand/foot.
exact_synonyms: Short middle and distal phalanges of digits ii through v
Progressive brachydactyly of middle and distal phalanges

HP:0005873.label: Polysyndactyly of hallux
HP:0005873.definition: Combined syndactyly and polydactyly of the great toe.

HP:0005878.label: Enlarged sagittal diameter of the cervical canal

HP:0005879.label: Congenital finger flexion contractures
HP:0005879.definition: Multiple bent (flexed) finger joints that cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0005880.label: Metacarpophalangeal synostosis
HP:0005880.definition: Fusion of a metacarpal bone with the proximal phalanx of the finger distal to it across the corresponding metacarpophalangeal joint.
exact_synonyms: Fused long bone of hand with innermost finger bone

HP:0005885.label: Absent ossification of cervical vertebral bodies
HP:0005885.definition: A lack of bone mineralization of one or more body of cervical vertebra.

HP:0005886.label: Aphalangy of the hands
HP:0005886.definition: Absence of a digit or of one or more phalanges of a finger.

HP:0005890.label: Hyperostosis cranialis interna
HP:0005890.definition: Bony overgrowth of the internal (endosteal) surface of the calvaria and the base of skull.
exact_synonyms: Overgrowth of the inner surface of the skull bones
Excessive growth of inner surface of the skull bones
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the cranial bone
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the cranial bones

HP:0005891.label: Progressive forearm bowing
HP:0005891.definition: Progressive bending or abnormal curvature of the forearm skeleton.

HP:0005892.label: Proximal tibial and fibular fusion
HP:0005892.definition: A developmental defect characterized by the abnormal fusion of the proximal tibia and fibula.
exact_synonyms: Fusion of innermost shinbone and calf bone

HP:0005894.label: Double first metacarpals
HP:0005894.definition: Duplication of the metacarpal I bones.

HP:0005895.label: Radial deviation of thumb terminal phalanx

HP:0005900.label: Fifth metacarpal with ulnar notch
HP:0005900.definition: Presence of an angular or V -shaped indentation on the ulnar side of the fifth metacarpal bone (i.e., on the sides towards the fifth finger).
exact_synonyms: Fifth metacarpal notched on ulnar side

HP:0005905.label: Abnormal cervical curvature
HP:0005905.definition: The presence of an abnormal curvature of the cervical vertebral column.

HP:0005906.label: Delayed pneumatization of the mastoid process
HP:0005906.definition: An abnormally reduced degree of pneumatization (i.e., formation of air cells) in the mastoid process with respect to age-dependent norms.

HP:0005910.label: Rhomboid or triangular shaped 5th finger middle phalanx
HP:0005910.definition: Rhomboid or triangular shaped 5th (little) finger middle phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Rhomboid or triangular shaped fifth finger middle phalanx

HP:0005913.label: Abnormal metacarpal epiphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of long bone of hand

HP:0005914.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the metacarpal bones
HP:0005914.definition: Aplasia or Hypoplasia affecting the metacarpal bones.

HP:0005916.label: Abnormal metacarpal morphology
HP:0005916.definition: Any abnormal shape or structure of the metacarpal bones.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal shape of long bones of hand

HP:0005917.label: Supernumerary metacarpal bones
HP:0005917.definition: The presence of more than the normal number of metacarpal bones.

HP:0005918.label: Abnormal finger phalanx morphology
HP:0005918.definition: Abnormalities affecting the phalanx of finger.
HP:0005918.comment: This category is a supercategory for abnormalties affect phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the phalanges of the hand
Abnormal form of phalanges of the hand

HP:0005920.label: Abnormal epiphysis morphology of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0005920.definition: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand. Note that this includes the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal. In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5 (whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits).

HP:0005921.label: obsolete Abnormal ossification of hand bones

HP:0005922.label: Abnormal hand morphology
HP:0005922.definition: Any structural anomaly of the hand.
HP:0005922.comment: This is a category to be used for general descriptions of hand dysmorphology. In time, it should be replaced by more accurate descriptions.

HP:0005923.label: Abnormal hand metaphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormalities of the metaphyses of the hand
Abnormality of the wide portion of the hand bone

HP:0005924.label: Abnormal hand epiphysis morphology
HP:0005924.definition: Any abnormality of the epiphyses of the phalanges or metacarpal bones.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the hand bones
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the fingers
Abnormality of the end part of the hand bone
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the hand
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand

HP:0005925.label: Abnormal hand diaphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormalities of shaft of long bone of the hand
Abnormalities of the diaphyses of the hand

HP:0005926.label: Abnormal hand cortical bone morphology
HP:0005926.definition: An anomaly of the outer shell (cortex) of a hand bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the cortex of hand bones

HP:0005927.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the hand
HP:0005927.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the hand.

HP:0005928.label: Synostosis involving the fibula
exact_synonyms: Bone fusion involving the calf bones

HP:0005930.label: Abnormal epiphysis morphology
HP:0005930.definition: An anomaly of epiphysis, which is the expanded articular end of a long bone that developes from a secondary ossification center, and which during the period of growth is either entirely cartilaginous or is separated from the shaft by a cartilaginous disk.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal shape of end part of bone

HP:0005932.label: Abnormal renal corticomedullary differentiation
HP:0005932.definition: An abnormality of corticomedullary differentiation (CMD) on diagnostic imaging such as magnetic resonance imaging, computer tomography, or sonography. CMD is a difference in the visualization of cortex and medulla.
HP:0005932.comment: On T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, the signal intensity of the normal renal cortex is typically higher than medulla, resulting in easily visualized corticomedullary differentiation (CMD). Loss of CMD can be seen in disorders such as glomerulonephritis, acute tubular necrosis, end-stage chronic renal failure, obstructive hydronephrosis, and acute allograft rejection. Progressive corticomedullary differentiation (CMD) can be visualized as an echogenic cortex and a hypoechoic medulla. This CMD should be visible during the midtrimester sonographic evaluation.

HP:0005938.label: Abnormal respiratory motile cilium morphology
HP:0005938.definition: Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the motile cilium.

HP:0005942.label: Desquamative interstitial pneumonitis
HP:0005942.definition: Diffuse filling of the distal airspaces of the lungs, the alveoli, with macrophages. Desquamative interstitial pneumonitis (DIP) is characterized additionally by thickened alveolar septa and by a sparse inflammatory infiltrate that often includes plasma cells and occasional eosinophils. The alveoli are lined by plump cuboidal pneumocytes. Lymphoid aggregates may be present.
HP:0005942.comment: The name originated from the belief that the dominant histologic feature was desquamation of epithelial cells. However, this is now recognized to be intra-alveolar macrophage accumulation rather than desquamation of epithelial cells as originally thought by Liebow and Carrington. In adults the condition is almost invariable associated with cigarette smoke. However, rare cases occur in nonsmokers, some of whom have had exposure to environmental inhalation exposures including passive exposure to cigarette smoke. In children genetically caused surfactant dysfunction syndromes may have the histological pattern of DIP.
exact_synonyms: Filling of the alveoli with alveolar macrophages
related_synonyms: Filling of the alveoli with desquamated epithelial cells

HP:0005944.label: Bilateral lung agenesis
HP:0005944.definition: Bilateral lack of development of the lungs.

HP:0005945.label: Laryngeal obstruction
HP:0005945.definition: Blockage of the upper airway at the level of the larynx often accompanied by respiratory distress.

HP:0005946.label: Ventilator dependence with inability to wean

HP:0005947.label: Decreased sensitivity to hypoxemia
HP:0005947.definition: Reduced tendency to respond to a reduced concentration of oxygen in the blood by increasing respiration.
HP:0005947.comment: Note that hypoxia is defined as lack of oxygen in tissues. Hypoxia is usually preceded by hypoxemia (decreased concentration of oxygen in blood).

HP:0005948.label: Multiple pulmonary cysts
HP:0005948.definition: The presence of multiple lung cysts.
HP:0005948.comment: Emphysematous changes sometimes can be mistaken for multifocal lung cysts. In contrast to true cysts, the cystlike lucencies caused by the destruction of lung parenchyma in emphy-sema do not have walls. Nevertheless, emphysema can be accompanied by multiple cysts, such as bullae, or in association with LCH.

HP:0005949.label: Apneic episodes in infancy
HP:0005949.definition: Recurrent episodes of apnea occurring during infancy.

HP:0005950.label: Laryngeal web
HP:0005950.definition: A membrane-like structure that extends across the laryngeal lumen close to the level of the vocal cords.
HP:0005950.comment: Manifestations may appear at any age (hoarse or weak voice and frequent upper respiratory infections) but onset usually occurs during infancy (respiratory distress, stridor and an unusual cry).

HP:0005956.label: Anteroposteriorly shortened larynx
HP:0005956.definition: Abnormal shortening of the larynx in the anteroposterior (front to back) axis.

HP:0005961.label: Hypoargininemia
HP:0005961.definition: A decreased concentration of arginine in the blood.

HP:0005968.label: Temperature instability
HP:0005968.definition: Disordered thermoregulation characterized by an impaired ability to maintain a balance between heat production and heat loss, with resulting instability of body temperature.

HP:0005972.label: Respiratory acidosis
HP:0005972.definition: Acidosis because of respiratory retention of carbon dioxide.

HP:0005973.label: Fructose intolerance
HP:0005973.definition: Reduced intestinal absorption of fructose. Breath testing after ingestion of fructose has been widely adopted as a standard method of identifying fructose malabsorption and intolerance. A dose of 25 g of fructose dissolved in a 10% solution is generally accepted as the appropriate dose of fructose for clinical use of H2 and CH4 breath testing. High levels of hydrogen in exhaled breath subsequent hours indicate fructose intolerance. Presence of malabsorption and reproduction of symptoms during a breath test provides the best objective evidence and symptom correlation for fructose intolerance.

HP:0005978.label: Type II diabetes mellitus
HP:0005978.definition: A type of diabetes mellitus initially characterized by insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia and subsequently by glucose interolerance and hyperglycemia.
HP:0005978.comment: Persons with type II diabetes mellitus rarely develop ketoacidosis.

HP:0005979.label: Metabolic ketoacidosis
HP:0005979.definition: A metabolic acidosis due to accumulation of ketone bodies generally observed in the setting of poor nutritional intake.

HP:0005987.label: Multinodular goiter
HP:0005987.definition: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to multiple nodules in the thyroid gland.

HP:0005988.label: Congenital muscular torticollis
HP:0005988.definition: A congenital form of torticollis resulting from shortening of the sternocleidomastoid muscle and leading to a limited range of motion in both rotation and lateral bending.
HP:0005988.comment: Congenital muscular torticollis is thought to result from injury to the sternocleidomastoid muscle during birth trauma, resulting in fibrosis and unilateral shortening of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Congenital muscular torticollis is thus etiologically and phenotypically distinct from spasmodic torticollis.

HP:0005989.label: Redundant neck skin
HP:0005989.definition: Excess skin around the neck, often lying in horizontal folds.
HP:0005989.comment: With age and increased vertical growth of the neck, excess nuchal skin may disappear and the neck may become broad or webbed. If the skin folds are vertical or paravertical, the term Neck webbing should be used.

HP:0005990.label: Thyroid hypoplasia
HP:0005990.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the thyroid gland.

HP:0005991.label: Limited neck flexion
HP:0005991.definition: Reduced ability to lower the chin towards the chest by bending the neck.

HP:0005994.label: Nodular goiter
HP:0005994.definition: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to one or more nodules in the thyroid gland.

HP:0005995.label: Decreased adipose tissue around neck
HP:0005995.definition: Reduced amount of adipose tissue in the region of the neck.
exact_synonyms: Loss of adipose tissue around the neck

HP:0005997.label: Neck joint contracture
exact_synonyms: Restricted neck mobility due to contractures
Restricted neck movement due to contractures

HP:0005999.label: Ureteral atresia
HP:0005999.definition: A developmental defect defined by the failure of the formation of the lumen (tube) of the ureter.

HP:0006000.label: Ureteral obstruction
HP:0006000.definition: Obstruction of the flow of urine through the ureter.

HP:0006006.label: Hypotrophy of the small hand muscles

HP:0006009.label: Broad phalanx
HP:0006009.definition: Increased side-to-side width of one or more phalanges of the fingers or toes.

HP:0006011.label: Cuboidal metacarpal
HP:0006011.definition: Severely shortened metacarpal with a cuboidal appearance.
HP:0006011.comment: The metacarpals are normally tubular in appearance.
exact_synonyms: Short, cube shaped long bone of hand

HP:0006012.label: Widened metacarpal shaft
exact_synonyms: Broad shaft of long bone of hand

HP:0006016.label: Delayed phalangeal epiphyseal ossification
HP:0006016.definition: Delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more phalanx.
related_synonyms: Delayed bone maturation of end part of digital bone

HP:0006028.label: Metaphyseal cupping of metacarpals
HP:0006028.definition: Metaphyseal cupping affecting the metacarpal bones.
exact_synonyms: Cupping of wide portion of long bone of hand

HP:0006035.label: Cone-shaped epiphyses of phalanges 2 to 5
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of digital bones 2 to 5

HP:0006042.label: Y-shaped metacarpals
HP:0006042.definition: Y-shaped metacarpals are the result of a partial fusion of two metacarpal bones, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Y-shaped metacarpals may be seen in combination with polydactyly.

HP:0006048.label: Distal widening of metacarpals
HP:0006048.definition: Abnormal increase in width of the distal region of the metacarpal bones.
exact_synonyms: Wide outermost end of long bone

HP:0006059.label: Cone-shaped metacarpal epiphyses
HP:0006059.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphyses of the metacarpal bones, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphyses are located at the distal ends of the metacarpal bones.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of long bone

HP:0006067.label: Multiple carpal ossification centers
HP:0006067.definition: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more long bones.

HP:0006070.label: Metacarpophalangeal joint contracture
HP:0006070.definition: A chronic loss of joint motion in metacarpophalangeal joints due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.
HP:0006070.comment: In the literature this has been called metacarpophalangeal camptodactyly, but the term camptodactyly should be reserved for a painless flexion contracture of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint.

HP:0006077.label: Absent proximal finger flexion creases
HP:0006077.definition: Absence of the proximal interphalangeal flexion creases of the fingers.

HP:0006092.label: Malaligned carpal bone
HP:0006092.definition: Malalignement of carpal bone angles either with respect to each other, to the corresponding metacarpals or with respect to the wrist (radius and ulna).

HP:0006095.label: Wide tufts of distal phalanges
exact_synonyms: Wide tips of outermost digital bone

HP:0006097.label: 3-4 finger osseus syndactyly
HP:0006097.definition: Fusion of the third (middle) and fourth (ring) finger, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual finger bones.

HP:0006099.label: Metacarpophalangeal joint hyperextensibility
HP:0006099.definition: Increased mobility of one ore more metacarpophalangeal joint.

HP:0006101.label: Finger syndactyly
HP:0006101.definition: Webbing or fusion of the fingers, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "Symphalangism".

HP:0006107.label: Fingerpad telangiectases
HP:0006107.definition: Telangiectasia (small dilated blood vessels) located in the fingerpads at the tips of the fingers.
exact_synonyms: Small dilated blood vessels in fingerpads

HP:0006108.label: Tapered metacarpals
HP:0006108.definition: Metacarpal that becomes thinner toward the distal end.

HP:0006109.label: Absent phalangeal crease
HP:0006109.definition: Absence of one or more interphalangeal creases (i.e., of the transverse lines in the skin between the phalanges of the fingers).

HP:0006110.label: Shortening of all middle phalanges of the fingers
HP:0006110.definition: Short, hypoplastic middle phalanx of finger, affecting all fingers.

HP:0006112.label: Expanded phalanges with widened medullary cavities

HP:0006114.label: Multiple palmar creases
HP:0006114.definition: The presence of multiple creases on the palm of the hand (more than the normal three major creases (distal transverse crease, proximal transverse crease, and thenar crease).

HP:0006118.label: Shortening of all distal phalanges of the fingers
HP:0006118.definition: Hypoplasia of all of the distal phalanx of finger.
exact_synonyms: Shortening of all outermost bones of the fingers

HP:0006119.label: Proximal tapering of metacarpals
HP:0006119.definition: Some or all of the metacarpal bones (i.e., metacarpal II to V) have a pointed proximal appearance.
exact_synonyms: Pointed innermost long bone of hand

HP:0006121.label: Acral ulceration
HP:0006121.definition: A type of digital ulcer that manifests as an open sore on the surface of the skin at the tip of a finger or toe.

HP:0006127.label: Long proximal phalanx of finger
HP:0006127.definition: Increased length of the proximal phalanx of finger.

HP:0006129.label: Drumstick terminal phalanges
HP:0006129.definition: Rounding and broadening of the tufts of the distal phalanges.
HP:0006129.comment: This designation is supposed to refer to the widening of the meaty end of a chicken drumstick (lower leg).

HP:0006134.label: Enlarged metacarpal epiphyses
HP:0006134.definition: Abnormally large size of one or more growth plates (epiphyses) of the metacarpal bones (i.e., the tubular bones of the hand between the carpus and the phalanges).
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of long bone of hand

HP:0006140.label: Premature fusion of phalangeal epiphyses
HP:0006140.definition: Fusion of the epiphysis and metaphysis of one or more phalanges prior to the normal age or stage of growth.
exact_synonyms: Premature fusion of end part of digital bone

HP:0006143.label: Abnormal finger flexion crease
HP:0006143.definition: Anomalous flexion crease (i.e., a transverse line that crosses the skin of a finger).

HP:0006144.label: Shortening of all proximal phalanges of the fingers
HP:0006144.definition: Congenital hypoplasia of proximal phalanx of finger or all fingers.
exact_synonyms: Shortening of all innermost bones of the fingers

HP:0006145.label: Central Y-shaped metacarpal
HP:0006145.definition: A central Y-shaped metacarpal is the result of a partial fusion of two central metacarpals (i.e., metacarpals 2-4) of the hand, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Central Y-shaped metacarpals may be seen as a result of a central polydactyly with partial fusion of the duplicated metacarpal.
exact_synonyms: Y-shaped central long bones of hand

HP:0006146.label: Broad metacarpal epiphyses
HP:0006146.definition: Increased side-to-side width of the metacarpal epiphyses.
exact_synonyms: Broad end part of long bone of hand

HP:0006150.label: Swan neck-like deformities of the fingers
HP:0006150.definition: A swan neck deformity describes a finger with a hyperextended PIP joint and a flexed DIP joint. The most common cause for a swan neck-like deformity is a disruption of the end of the extensor tendon. Conditions that loosen the PIP joint and allow it to hyperextend, for example conditions that weaken the volar plate, can produce a swan neck deformity of the finger. One example is rheumatoid arthritis. Another cause are conditions that tighten up the small (intrinsic) muscles of the hand and fingers, for example hand trauma or nerve disorders, such as cerebral palsy, Parkinson's disease, or stroke.

HP:0006152.label: Proximal symphalangism of hands
HP:0006152.definition: The term proximal symphalangism refers to a bony fusion of the middle and proximal phalanges of the digits of the hand, in other words the proximal interphalangeal joint (PIJ) is missing which can be seen either on x-rays or as an absence of the proximal interphalangeal finger creases.

HP:0006155.label: Long phalanx of finger
HP:0006155.definition: Increased length of multiple or a single phalanx of finger.

HP:0006156.label: Ulnar deviation of thumb
HP:0006156.definition: Bending or curvature of a thumb towards the ulnar side (towards the ring finger).

HP:0006159.label: Mesoaxial hand polydactyly
HP:0006159.definition: The presence of a supernumerary finger (not a thumb) involving the third or fourth metacarpal with associated osseous syndactyly.

HP:0006160.label: Irregular metacarpals
HP:0006160.definition: Irregular morphology of one or more metacarpal bones.

HP:0006161.label: Short metacarpals with rounded proximal ends
exact_synonyms: Short long bone of hand with rounded innermost ends

HP:0006162.label: Soft tissue swelling of interphalangeal joints
exact_synonyms: Soft tissue swelling of hinge joints

HP:0006166.label: Tubular metacarpal bones
exact_synonyms: Cylindrical shaped long bones of hand

HP:0006170.label: Chess-pawn distal phalanges
HP:0006170.definition: A morphological abnormality of distal phalanges such that they have the appearance of chess pawns.

HP:0006172.label: Flattened, squared-off epiphyses of tubular bones
exact_synonyms: Flattened, squared-off end part of tubular bones

HP:0006174.label: Metacarpal diaphyseal endosteal sclerosis
HP:0006174.definition: Increase in bone density in the diaphyseal (shaft) region of a metacarpal bone.

HP:0006176.label: Two carpal ossification centers present at birth
exact_synonyms: Two carpal ossification centres present at birth

HP:0006179.label: Pseudoepiphyses of second metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Extra bone on end of second long bone of hand

HP:0006184.label: Decreased palmar creases
HP:0006184.definition: Poorly defined or shallow palmar creases.

HP:0006191.label: Deep palmar crease
HP:0006191.definition: Excessively deep creases of the palm.

HP:0006192.label: Tapered phalanx of finger
HP:0006192.definition: Phalanges of the fingers becoming thinner toward the distal end.

HP:0006193.label: Thimble-shaped middle phalanges of hand
HP:0006193.definition: The middle phalanx of finger resembles a thimble, a small metal cap to protect the finger while sewing that has a broad (proximal) base and narrower top, whereby both base and top are flat.

HP:0006201.label: Hypermobility of distal interphalangeal joints
exact_synonyms: Increased mobility of outermost hinge joint

HP:0006203.label: Decreased movement range in interphalangeal joints
exact_synonyms: Decreased range of movement range in hinge joints

HP:0006205.label: Irregular phalanges
HP:0006205.definition: Alteration of the normally smooth radiographic contour of phalanges producing an irregular appearance.

HP:0006206.label: Hypersegmentation of proximal phalanx of second finger
HP:0006206.definition: Presence of an additional phalanx-like bone, producing an extra, wedge-shaped bone at the base of the proximal phalanx of the second finger.
HP:0006206.comment: This anomaly is characteristic for brachydactyly type C.

HP:0006208.label: Metaphyseal cupping of proximal phalanges
HP:0006208.definition: Metaphyseal cupping affecting the proximal phalanges.

HP:0006213.label: Thin proximal phalanges with broad epiphyses of the hand
HP:0006213.comment: removed the logical def: 'has part' some (('decreased thickness' and ('inheres in' some 'proximal phalanx of manus') and ('has modifier' some abnormal)) and ('has part' some ('increased width' and ('inheres in' some 'epiphysis of proximal phalanx of manus'))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))
exact_synonyms: Thin innermost bone with broad end part of the hand bone

HP:0006216.label: Single interphalangeal crease of fifth finger
HP:0006216.definition: Presence of only one (instead of two, as normal) interphalangeal crease of the fifth finger.

HP:0006217.label: Limited mobility of proximal interphalangeal joint
exact_synonyms: Limited mobility of innermost hinge joint

HP:0006224.label: Tapering pointed ends of distal finger phalanges
HP:0006224.definition: A reduction in diameter of the distal phalanx of finger towards the distal end such that the tip of the phalanx comes to a point (this feature can be observed on radiograms).

HP:0006226.label: Osteoarthritis of the first carpometacarpal joint

HP:0006232.label: Expanded metacarpals with widened medullary cavities

HP:0006233.label: Osteoarthritis of the distal interphalangeal joint

HP:0006234.label: Osteolysis involving tarsal bones
HP:0006234.definition: An increased resorption of bone matrix by osteoclasts leading to bony defects involving the tarsal bones.

HP:0006236.label: Slender metacarpals
HP:0006236.definition: Decreased width of the metacarpal bones (that is, reduced diameter).

HP:0006239.label: Shortening of all middle phalanges of the toes
HP:0006239.definition: Abnormal shortening of all middle phalanges of toes.
exact_synonyms: Shortening of all the middle bones of the toes

HP:0006248.label: Limited wrist movement
HP:0006248.definition: An abnormal limitation of the mobility of the wrist.

HP:0006254.label: Elevated circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
HP:0006254.definition: Concentration of alpha-fetoprotein in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0006254.comment: An elevation of alpha-feto protein, which is produced by the fetal liver and the yolk sac and may be increased in the serum of pregnant women with a fetus with some types of developmental anomaly such as open neural tube defects and omphalocele.

HP:0006261.label: Abnormal phalangeal joint morphology of the hand
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the small joints of the hand
Abnormality of phalangeal joints of the hand

HP:0006263.label: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the 2nd finger
HP:0006263.definition: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges of the 2nd finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the index finger bone

HP:0006268.label: Fluctuating splenomegaly
HP:0006268.definition: Intermittently increased size of the spleen.

HP:0006273.label: Pancreatic lymphangiectasis
HP:0006273.definition: The presence of lymphangiectasis in the pancreas.

HP:0006274.label: Reduced pancreatic beta cells
HP:0006274.definition: Reduced number of beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.
HP:0006274.comment: The beta cells are responsible for producing insulin and amylin.

HP:0006277.label: Pancreatic hyperplasia
HP:0006277.comment: Hyperplasia is defined in MPATH as an increase in cell numbers in comparison to normal as a consequence of increased cell proliferation. Hyperplasia is a non -neoplastic process.

HP:0006278.label: Ectopic pancreatic tissue
HP:0006278.definition: The presence of pancreatic tissue outside the normal pancreas, in many cases along the foregut and proximal midgut.

HP:0006282.label: Generalized hypoplasia of dental enamel
HP:0006282.definition: A generalized form of developmental hypoplasia of the dental enamel.

HP:0006283.label: Multiple unerupted teeth
HP:0006283.definition: The presence of multiple embedded tooth germs which have failed to erupt.
exact_synonyms: Failure of eruption of multiple teeth

HP:0006285.label: Enamel hypomineralization
HP:0006285.definition: A decreased amount of enamel mineralization. Hypomineralized enamel has a brown discoloration and brittle aspect.
HP:0006285.comment: Enamel hypomineralization can be caused by genetic or environmental factors. It may occur in both deciduous and permanent dentitions, although more often in the permanent dentition. It may concern a single tooth, several teeth, or the complete dentition and may affect part or the complete surface of the tooth. Enamel hypomineralization is a qualitative defect of enamel, in which the enamel can be rough and softer. Affected teeth may be sensitive. Enamel hypomineralization can be part of molar incisor hypomineralization (hypomineralisation of systemic origin of one to four permanent first molars, frequently associated with affected incisors) and of hypomineralized second primary molars (or deciduous molar hypomineralisation, which indicates idiopathic hypomineralization of one to four second deciduous molars).
related_synonyms: White spot lesions of tooth enamel

HP:0006288.label: Advanced eruption of teeth
HP:0006288.definition: Premature tooth eruption, which can be defined as tooth eruption more than 2 SD earlier than the mean eruption age.
HP:0006288.comment: There are established norms for the timing of eruption in both deciduous and permanent teeth [Garn and Rohmann, [1966]; Lunt and Law, [1974]; McDonald et al. [2004]]. Eruption is defined by the appearance of a tooth that has pierced the gum.

HP:0006289.label: Agenesis of central incisor
HP:0006289.definition: Agenesis of one or more central incisors, i.e., of lower secondary incisor, lower primary incisor, upper secondary incisor, or of upper central primary incisor.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of central incisor

HP:0006290.label: Discolored lateral incisors
HP:0006290.definition: The presence of discolored lateral incisors.

HP:0006291.label: Marked delay in eruption of permanent teeth
exact_synonyms: Very late eruption of permanent teeth
Very late eruption of adult teeth
Severe delay of eruption of permanent teeth
Severe delay of eruption of adult teeth

HP:0006292.label: Abnormality of dental eruption
HP:0006292.comment: The average ages for eruption of the primary teeth are: 6 months: lower central incisor, 7 months: upper central incisor, 8 months: upper lateral incisor, 9 months: lower lateral incisor, 12 months first molars, 18 months, canines, 2 years, second molars.

HP:0006293.label: Agenesis of maxillary central incisor
HP:0006293.definition: Agenesis of upper secondary incisor or of upper central primary incisor.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of maxillary central incisor

HP:0006297.label: Enamel hypoplasia
HP:0006297.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the dental enamel.
HP:0006297.comment: Enamel hypoplasia can be caused by genetic or environmental factors. It may occur in both deciduous and permanent dentitions, although more often in the permanent dentition. Enamel hypoplasia may concern a single tooth, several teeth, or the complete dentition and may affect part or the complete surface of the tooth. Enamel hypoplasia regroups different clinical aspects: localized hypoplasia, generalized hypoplasia, enamel pits, enamel striae, and grooves defects. The term should be used to describe a quantitative defect of enamel. Enamel hypotrophy cannot be used as hypotrophy indicates loss of cells, whereas enamel is an acellular structure and thus not a tissue.

HP:0006298.label: Prolonged bleeding after dental extraction
HP:0006298.definition: Prolonged bleeding post dental extraction sufficient to require medical intervention.

HP:0006302.label: Dagger-shaped pulp calcifications
HP:0006302.definition: Dagger-shaped calcifications in the dental pulp.

HP:0006308.label: Atrophy of alveolar ridges
exact_synonyms: Resorption of alveolar processes of jaw
Atrophy of alveolar processes of jaw
related_synonyms: Flattening of alveolar processes of jaw

HP:0006313.label: Widely spaced primary teeth
HP:0006313.definition: Increased space between the primary teeth. Note this phenotype should be distinguished from increased space due purely to microdontia.

HP:0006315.label: Solitary median maxillary central incisor
HP:0006315.definition: A single maxillary central incisor positioned in the midline with morphological symmetry of the crown and bordered by lateral incisors.
HP:0006315.comment: The tooth differs from a normal central incisor in the symmetric formation of the crown. The tooth is present in both deciduous and permanent dentition. Solitary/single median maxillary central incisor syndrome indicates the presence of a single median maxillary central incisor together with other midline defects of development. A single maxillary central incisor not positioned in the midline indicates agenesis of the contralateral central incisor and can be differentiated furthermore by the morphology of the crown. A diagnosis of a solitary median maxillary central incisor typically requires X-ray examinations.

HP:0006316.label: Irregularly spaced teeth
HP:0006316.definition: Irregular distribution of the teeth along the dental arch, i.e., and irregular spatial pattern of teeth.

HP:0006321.label: Multiple non-erupting secondary teeth
exact_synonyms: Failure of eruption of multiple adult teeth
Failure of eruption of multiple permanent teeth

HP:0006323.label: Premature loss of primary teeth
HP:0006323.definition: Loss of the primary (also known as deciduous) teeth before the usual age.
HP:0006323.comment: The primary teeth are usually shed and replaced by the permanent teeth, usually by the age of six years. With premature loss of primary teeth, there is a delay between the loss of the primary teeth and the eruption of the permanent teeth.

HP:0006326.label: Buried teeth encased in mucopolysaccharide
exact_synonyms: Failure of tooth eruption due to mucopolysaccharidoses
Failure of dental eruption due to mucopolysaccharidoses

HP:0006329.label: Alveolar process hypoplasia
HP:0006329.definition: Underdevelopment of the alveolar process (also known as alveolar bone).
HP:0006329.comment: The alveolar process is a thickened ridge of bone that contains the tooth sockets on the mandible and maxilla.
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of alveolar process of jaw
Underdevelopment of alveolar process of jaw
related_synonyms: Deficiency of alveolar process of jaw

HP:0006332.label: Supernumerary maxillary incisor
HP:0006332.definition: The presence of a supernumerary, i.e., extra, maxillary incisor, either the primary maxillary incisor or the permanent maxillary incisor.

HP:0006333.label: Crowded maxillary incisors
HP:0006333.definition: A type of dental misalignment with crowded central incisors, i.e., of maxillary secondary incisor, or of maxillary central primary incisor.

HP:0006334.label: Hypoplasia of the primary teeth
HP:0006334.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the primary teeth.

HP:0006335.label: Persistence of primary teeth
HP:0006335.definition: Persistence of the primary teeth beyond the age by which they normally are shed and replaced by the permanent teeth.
HP:0006335.comment: The primary teeth are usually shed and replaced by the permanent teeth, usually by the age of six years. Persistence of primary teeth may be related to agenesis of the permanent teeth. Molar primary teeth may be persistent because of the agenesis of the premolars.

HP:0006336.label: Short dental root
HP:0006336.definition: Tooth root length more than 2 SD below mean, or subjectively apparently decreased tooth root length.

HP:0006337.label: Premature eruption of permanent teeth
HP:0006337.definition: Premature tooth eruption of the permanent dentition.

HP:0006338.label: Malformation of mandibular premolar
HP:0006338.definition: An abnormality of the morphology of secondary premolar tooth.

HP:0006339.label: Conical mandibular incisor
HP:0006339.definition: An abnormal conical morphology of the primary or permanent mandibular incisors.

HP:0006342.label: Peg-shaped maxillary lateral incisors
HP:0006342.definition: A tooth crown with its mesial and distal sides converging or tapering toward the incisal edge causing severe reduction of mesiodistal diameter
HP:0006342.comment: A peg shape appearance of a tooth occurs in lateral incisors only. A peg-shaped tooth is a microdont tooth and may occur isolated or associated with other dental anomalies, such as hypodontia and oligodontia; this should be assessed and coded separately.

HP:0006344.label: Abnormal primary molar morphology
HP:0006344.definition: An abnormality of morphology of primary molar.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of shape of baby molar
Abnormality of shape of primary molar

HP:0006346.label: Screwdriver-shaped incisors
HP:0006346.definition: An abnormality of morphology of the incisor tooth in which the tooth is shaped like a screwdriver blade, i.e., having a rhomboid shape.

HP:0006347.label: Microdontia of primary teeth
HP:0006347.definition: Decreased size of the primary teeth.

HP:0006349.label: Agenesis of permanent teeth
HP:0006349.definition: A congenital defect characterized by the absence of one or more permanent teeth, including oligodontia, hypodontia, and adontia of the of permanent teeth.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of permanent teeth
Failure of development of secondary teeth

HP:0006350.label: Pulp obliteration
HP:0006350.definition: Mineralized substance filling the entire dental pulp space.
HP:0006350.comment: The diagnosis pulp obliteration can be established using radiological studies. Gradual obliteration of the pulp is a physiologic process that occurs with aging. On radiographs the contours of the pulp disappear in part or totally, but histologically pulpal tissue remains present.
exact_synonyms: Reduced size of pulp chamber of tooth

HP:0006352.label: Failure of eruption of permanent teeth
HP:0006352.definition: Lack of tooth eruption of the secondary dentition.
exact_synonyms: Failure of eruption of adult teeth

HP:0006353.label: Hypoplasia of the tooth germ
HP:0006353.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the tooth germ, i.e., of the structure that forms in odontogenesis that will develop into a tooth.

HP:0006355.label: Agenesis of mandibular central incisor
HP:0006355.definition: Agenesis of lower secondary incisor or lower primary incisor.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of mandibular central incisor

HP:0006357.label: Premature loss of permanent teeth
HP:0006357.definition: Premature loss of the permanent teeth.

HP:0006358.label: Shovel-shaped maxillary central incisors
HP:0006358.definition: A tooth with a crown with marked lingual or palatal marginal ridges causing scooped lingual or palatal surfaces.

HP:0006367.label: Crumpled long bones
HP:0006367.definition: An crumpled radiographic appearance of the long bones, as if the long bone had been crushed together producing irregularities. This feature is the result of multiple fractures and repeated rounds of ineffective healing, as can be seen for instance in severe forms of osteogenesis imperfecta.

HP:0006369.label: Irregular patellae
HP:0006369.definition: An alteration of the normally relatively smooth margins of the kneecap in radiographic images leading to an irregular contour.

HP:0006370.label: Distal ulnar epiphyseal stippling
HP:0006370.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the distal epiphysis of the ulna.

HP:0006371.label: Broad long bone diaphyses
HP:0006371.definition: Increased width of the diaphysis of long bones.

HP:0006375.label: Dumbbell-shaped femur
HP:0006375.definition: The femur is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.

HP:0006379.label: Proximal tibial hypoplasia
HP:0006379.comment: Removed logical definition that used anonymous class. Requested new term from UBERON: 'proximal tibia'

HP:0006380.label: Knee flexion contracture
HP:0006380.definition: A type of knee joint contracture in which the knee is in a fixed bent (flexed) configuration such that it cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0006381.label: Rudimentary fibula
HP:0006381.definition: Absent or nearly absent fibula. (Does not include aplastic)

HP:0006383.label: Progressive bowing of long bones
HP:0006383.definition: Progressive bending or abnormal curvature of a long bone.

HP:0006384.label: Club-shaped distal femur
HP:0006384.definition: An abnormal conformation of the femur that becomes gradually enlarged towards the distal end. This feature affects the distal femoral metaphysis and epiphysis.
HP:0006384.comment: previous def: 'has part' some (clavate and ('inheres in' some 'Distal end of femur (adult human)') and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0006385.label: Short lower limbs
HP:0006385.definition: Shortening of the legs related to developmental hypoplasia of the bones of the leg.

HP:0006386.label: Hypoplastic distal radial epiphyses
HP:0006386.definition: Underdevelopment of the distal epiphysis of the radius.

HP:0006387.label: Wide distal femoral metaphysis
HP:0006387.definition: Increased width of the distal part of the shaft (metaphysis) of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Broad outermost wide portion of thighbone

HP:0006389.label: Limited knee flexion
HP:0006389.definition: Reduced ability to flex (bend) the knee joint.

HP:0006390.label: Anterior tibial bowing
HP:0006390.definition: An abnormal anterior bending or curvature of the tibia.

HP:0006391.label: Overtubulated long bones
HP:0006391.definition: Overconstriction, or narrowness of the diaphysis and metaphysis of long bones.

HP:0006392.label: Increased density of long bones
HP:0006392.definition: An abnormal increase in the bone density of the long bones.

HP:0006394.label: Limited pronation/supination of forearm
HP:0006394.definition: A limitation of the ability to place the forearm in a position such that the palm faces anteriorly (supination) and to place the forearm in a position such that the palm faces posteriorly (pronation).

HP:0006398.label: Flat distal femoral epiphysis
HP:0006398.definition: An abnormal flattening of the distal epiphysis of femur.
exact_synonyms: Flat end part of outermost thighbone

HP:0006406.label: Club-shaped proximal femur
HP:0006406.definition: An abnormal conformation of the femur that becomes gradually enlarged towards the proximal end. This feature affects the proximal femoral metaphysis and epiphysis.
HP:0006406.comment: previous def: 'has part' some (clavate and ('inheres in' some 'Proximal end of femur (adult human)') and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0006407.label: Irregular distal femoral epiphysis
HP:0006407.definition: Anomaly of the contour of the Distal epiphysis of femur such that its normally smooth appearance is irregular.

HP:0006408.label: Distal tapering femur
exact_synonyms: Tapering of outermost end of thighbone

HP:0006409.label: Progressive leg bowing
HP:0006409.definition: Progressive bending or abnormal curvature of the leg.

HP:0006414.label: Distal tibial bowing
HP:0006414.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the tibia.

HP:0006415.label: Cortically dense long tubular bones
HP:0006415.definition: Increased density of the compact bone of long bone.
HP:0006415.comment: Note that compact bone and cortical bone are synonymous.

HP:0006417.label: Wide femoral metaphysis
exact_synonyms: Broad wide portion of thigh bone

HP:0006423.label: Peg-like central prominence of distal tibial metaphyses

HP:0006429.label: Broad femoral neck
