HP:0006429.definition: An abnormally wide femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

HP:0006431.label: Abnormal proximal femoral metaphysis morphology
HP:0006431.definition: An anomaly of the metaphysis of the proximal femur (close to the hip).
exact_synonyms: Abnormal wide portion of innermost thighbone

HP:0006433.label: Radial ray deficiency
HP:0006433.definition: Radial dysplasia, also known as radial longitudinal deficiency, includes radial clubhand and is a disfiguring, and potentially disabling, congenital limb anomaly. The entire upper limb may be involved, although the defect is most evident in the forearm and hand. Affected children suffer a variable degree of hypoplasia or absence of the preaxial skeleton and soft tissues, in particular the thumb, radius, and dorsoradial soft tissues. The hand is usually radially deviated and subluxated off the distal aspect of the ulna, the ulna may be shortened and have a bow-shaped deformity, and there is no true wrist (radiocarpal) joint in Bayne2 type-III and IV radial dysplasia.
HP:0006433.comment: Bayne et al. classified radial ray deficiency into four types based on the radiographic severity of the radial ray deficiency: Type I, short distal radius (radius is slightly shorter than ulna, distal growth plate is present); Type II, hypoplastic radius (radius is smaller/thinner than ulna, no growth plate is present); Type III, partial absence of the radius (only a small proximal radial segment is present); and Type IV, total absence (radius is completely absent, ulna may be curved).

HP:0006434.label: Hypoplasia of proximal radius
HP:0006434.definition: Proximal radial shortening owing to a congenital defect of development.

HP:0006437.label: Disproportionate prominence of the femoral medial condyle

HP:0006438.label: Enlargement of the distal femoral epiphysis
HP:0006438.definition: An abnormal enlargement of the distal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Enlargement of the outermost thighbone end part

HP:0006439.label: Radioulnar dislocation
HP:0006439.definition: A dislocation is a separation of the radius and ulna bones where they normally meet. The radioulnar joints are two locations, proximal and distal, in which the radius and ulna articulate in the forearm. Both can dislocate.
HP:0006439.comment: This term refers to any kind of radioulnar joint dislocation (proximal, distal, both, or unknown).

HP:0006440.label: Increased density of long bone diaphyses
exact_synonyms: Increased density of shaft of long bone

HP:0006442.label: Hypoplasia of proximal fibula
HP:0006442.definition: Underdevelopment or shortening of the end of the fibula (calf bone) nearest the knee.
exact_synonyms: Underdeveloped innermost upper end of calf bone
Small innermost upper end of calf bone

HP:0006450.label: Multicentric ossification of proximal femoral epiphyses

HP:0006453.label: Lateral displacement of the femoral head
HP:0006453.definition: A developmental anomaly with lateral displacement of the femoral head.

HP:0006454.label: Delayed patellar ossification
HP:0006454.definition: Formation of bone in the patella later than normal.
HP:0006454.comment: The patella initially ossifies at between three and five years, commencing as multiple foci that rapidly coalesce. As the patellar ossification center enlarges the expanding margins may be irregular and associated with accessory ossification centers. These are most common superolaterally and may lead to the development of a bipartite patella. The bipartite patella has cartilaginous continuity despite the appearance of osseous discontinuity. The patella expands to all cartilaginous contours during late adolescence when the epiphyseal ossification centers around the knee are also in the final stages of maturation. The only cartilage not replaced is that occupying the superior two-thirds of the articular surface (the lower one-third is covered by the fat pad). The subchondral plate does not assume the actual articular contours until the late stages of osseous maturation (after ten to twelve years). Accordingly, typical measurements such as medial and lateral angulation cannot be accurately done prior to the final stages of patellar ossification expansion and maturation (PMID:6729496).
related_synonyms: Delayed bone maturation of the knee cap

HP:0006456.label: Irregular proximal tibial epiphyses
HP:0006456.definition: Anomaly of the contour of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia such that its normally smooth appearance is irregular.

HP:0006459.label: Dorsal subluxation of ulna
HP:0006459.definition: Partial dislocation of the ulna in the dorsal direction.

HP:0006460.label: Ankle hypermobility
HP:0006460.definition: The ankle joint can move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along its physiological axes.

HP:0006461.label: Proximal femoral epiphysiolysis
HP:0006461.definition: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is defined as a posterior and inferior slippage of the proximal epiphysis of the femur onto the metaphysis (femoral neck), occurring through the physeal plate during the early adolescent growth spurt.
exact_synonyms: Slipped end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0006462.label: Generalized bone demineralization
HP:0006462.definition: A generalized decrease in bone mineral density.
HP:0006462.comment: The terms Osteopenia or Osteoporosis should be preferred to this term, which may be obsoleted in the future.

HP:0006465.label: Periosteal thickening of long tubular bones
HP:0006465.definition: Thickening of the periosteum of long bone.

HP:0006467.label: Limited shoulder movement
HP:0006467.definition: A limitation of the range of movement of the shoulder joint.

HP:0006470.label: Thin long bone diaphyses
HP:0006470.definition: Decreased width of the diaphysis of long bones.

HP:0006473.label: Anterior bowing of long bones
HP:0006473.definition: An abnormal anterior curvature of a long bone.

HP:0006476.label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells
HP:0006476.definition: An abnormality of the islet of Langerhans, i.e., of the regions of the pancreas that contain its endocrine cells. These are the alpha cells, which produce glucagon, the beta cells, which produce insulin and amylin, the delta cells, which produce somatostatin, the PP cells, which produce pancreatic polypeptide, and the epsilon cells, which produce ghrelin.

HP:0006477.label: Abnormal alveolar ridge morphology
HP:0006477.definition: Any abnormality of the alveolar ridges (on the upper or lower jaws). The alveolar ridges contain the sockets (alveoli) of the teeth.
related_synonyms: Abnormality of alveolar processes of jaw

HP:0006479.label: Abnormal dental pulp morphology
HP:0006479.definition: An abnormality of the dental pulp.

HP:0006480.label: Premature loss of teeth
HP:0006480.definition: Exfoliation of a tooth more than 2 SD earlier than the normal age for the deciduous teeth and not related to traume or neglect. Exfoliation of a permanent tooth is per se abnormal.

HP:0006481.label: Abnormality of primary teeth
HP:0006481.definition: Any abnormality of the primary tooth.
HP:0006481.comment: Primary teeth are also called temporary teeth or deciduous teeth.

HP:0006482.label: Abnormal dental morphology
HP:0006482.definition: An abnormality of the morphology of the tooth.

HP:0006483.label: Abnormal number of teeth
HP:0006483.definition: The presence of an altered number of of teeth.
HP:0006483.comment: Humans usually have 20 primary teeth (also called deciduous teeth) and 32 permanent teeth. This term comprises anomalies with too many or too few teeth.

HP:0006485.label: Agenesis of incisor
HP:0006485.comment: Failure of one or more incisors to develop.

HP:0006486.label: Abnormal dental root morphology
HP:0006486.definition: An abnormality of the dental root.

HP:0006487.label: Bowing of the long bones
HP:0006487.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of a long bone.
HP:0006487.comment: Curvatures of a long bone such as femur, tibia, or fibula.

HP:0006488.label: Bowing of the arm
HP:0006488.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature affecting a long bone of the arm.

HP:0006489.label: Abnormal femoral metaphysis morphology
HP:0006489.definition: An anomaly of the femoral metaphysis.

HP:0006490.label: Abnormal lower-limb metaphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the wide portion of the lower-limb bone

HP:0006492.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fibula
HP:0006492.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the fibula.

HP:0006493.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the lower limbs
HP:0006493.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the lower limbs.

HP:0006494.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the feet

HP:0006495.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the ulna
HP:0006495.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the ulna.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia or unilateral/bilateral absence of ulna

HP:0006496.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the upper limbs
HP:0006496.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the upper limbs.
exact_synonyms: Absent/underdeveloped bones of the upper limbs
Absent/small bones of the upper limbs

HP:0006498.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the patella
HP:0006498.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the patella.

HP:0006499.label: Abnormal femoral epiphysis morphology
HP:0006499.definition: An anomaly of a growth plate of a femur.

HP:0006500.label: Abnormal lower limb epiphysis morphology
HP:0006500.definition: An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of one or both legs.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of lower limb epiphysis morphology
Abnormal shape of end part of lower limb end bone
Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the lower limbs

HP:0006501.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the radius
exact_synonyms: Absence or underdevelopment of the radius bone of the arm

HP:0006502.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the carpal bones
HP:0006502.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the carpal bones.

HP:0006503.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving forearm bones
HP:0006503.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of one or more forearm bones.

HP:0006504.label: obsolete Anomaly of the limb diaphyses morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of shaft of long bone of the limbs

HP:0006505.label: Abnormal limb epiphysis morphology
HP:0006505.definition: An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of a limb.
HP:0006505.comment: An epiphysis is the expanded articular end of a long bone that developes from a secondary ossification center, and which during the period of growth is either entirely cartilaginous or is separated from the shaft by a cartilaginous disk.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the limbs
Abnormal shape of end part of limb bones

HP:0006507.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the humerus
HP:0006507.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the humerus.
exact_synonyms: Absent/small long bone in upper arm
Absent/underdeveloped long bone in upper arm

HP:0006508.label: Abnormality of tibial epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of shinbone

HP:0006509.label: Diverticulosis of trachea
HP:0006509.definition: Tracheal diverticula are blind-ended outpouchings arising from the trachea. They are usually an incidental finding. Occasionally they can mimic pneumomediastinum. Tracheal diverticula are either congenital or acquired, in the latter case the most common causes are prolonged increased intraluminal pressure, e.g. chronic cough, COPD, tracheomalacia, and iatrogenic (e.g. post-surgical).

HP:0006510.label: Chronic pulmonary obstruction
HP:0006510.definition: An anomaly that is characterized progressive airflow obstruction that is only partly reversible, inflammation in the airways, and systemic effects or comorbities.
HP:0006510.comment: COPD is usually conceptualized as a disease entity. It is heterogeneous histologically and pathogenically, and conventionally includes emphysema and chronic bronchitis, It is included as a phenotype term as COPD is often annotated as a feature of other diseases.

HP:0006511.label: Laryngeal stridor
HP:0006511.definition: An abnormal high-pitched noisy sound, occurring during inhalation or exhalation caused by the incomplete obstruction in the throat.
HP:0006511.comment: The laryngeal stridor sound is usually heard during inspiratory phase, also called inspiratory stridor, and may accompanied by inspiratory difficulty in breathing. It may be due to abnormal flaccidity of the epiglottis or arytenoids.

HP:0006516.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
HP:0006516.definition: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis involves inhalation of an antigen. This leads to an exaggerated immune response and a following inflammation of the alveoli within the lungs. The main feature of chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis on lung biopsies is expansion of the interstitium by lymphocytes accompanied by an occasional multinucleated giant cell or loose granuloma. After exposure to the provoking antigen, following symptoms can be seen: fever, chills, malaise, cough, hemoptysis, chest tightness, dyspnea, rash, swelling and headache and can be completely reversible, based on the duration of the illness, categorized as acute (HP:0011009), subacute (HP:0011011), and chronic (HP:0011010).
HP:0006516.comment: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis may also be called many different names, based on the provoking antigen.

HP:0006517.label: Intraalveolar phospholipid accumulation
HP:0006517.definition: Accumulation of amorphous PAS-positive material in the space between alveolar macrophages, sometimes as condensed form (oval bodies) are typically found in alveolar proteinosis.
HP:0006517.comment: The periodic acid Schiff (PAS) staining is a staining method that detects polysaccharidese and mucosubstances, for example: glycogen, glyolipids, glyoproteins and mucins. It is one of the commonly used procedures in the histophathology laboratory and is easy to perform. It may help in discriminating different forms of interstitial lung disease (ILD), especially pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP).
exact_synonyms: Detection of PAS-positive extracellular material in broncho-alveolar lavage

HP:0006518.label: Pulmonary venous occlusion
HP:0006518.definition: Substantial narrowing or blockage of small pulmonary veins as a result of disorganized smooth muscle hypertrophy and collagen matrix deposition.
HP:0006518.comment: This feature can be observed by histological examination of lung tissue. The feature can be seen in pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD). PVOD is characterized by diffuse occlusion of the pulmonary veins by fibrous tissue, pulmonary venous congestion and associated complications including severe pulmonary hypertension (pHTN), non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, hypoxia and right-ventricular failure. Clinical presentation is typically non-specific, including dyspnea, fatigue and cough.

HP:0006521.label: Pulmonary lymphangiectasia
HP:0006521.definition: Abnormal dilatation of the pulmonary lymphatic vessels. Lymphatic fluid in the lung is derived from normal leakage of fluid out of the blood capillaries in the lung. In pulmonary lymphangiectasia, the pulmonary lymphatics are not properly connected and become dilated with fluid.

HP:0006527.label: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
HP:0006527.definition: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis is a benign lymphoproliferative disorder of the lung that is characterized by the presence of a dense, predominantly lymphocytic interstitial infiltrate (lymphocytes, plasma cells, other elements of the lymphoreticular system) that expands the alveolar septa.
HP:0006527.comment: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis is assumed to be a pathological immunologic response to different triggers and are particularly associated with autoimmune and infectious diseases as well as immunodeficiency. Associated clinical manifestations often include fever, cough, and shortness of breath.

HP:0006528.label: Chronic lung disease
HP:0006528.definition: According to the definitions of the American and British Thoracic Societies, including pulmonary functional tests, X-rays, and CT scans for items such as fibrosis, bronchiectasis, bullae, emphysema, nodular or lymphomatous abnormalities.

HP:0006529.label: Abnormal pulmonary lymphatics
HP:0006529.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary lymphatic chain.

HP:0006530.label: Abnormal pulmonary interstitial morphology
HP:0006530.definition: Abnormality of the lung parenchyma extending to the pulmonary interstitium and leading to diffuse pulmonary fibrosis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality in area between air sacs in lung

HP:0006532.label: Recurrent pneumonia
HP:0006532.definition: An increased susceptibility to pneumonia as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of pneumonia.
HP:0006532.comment: Recurrent pneumonia is defined as two or more episodes in a single year, or at least three episodes ever, with radiographic clearing of densities between occurrences.

HP:0006535.label: Recurrent intrapulmonary hemorrhage
HP:0006535.definition: A recurrent hemorrhage occurring within the lung.

HP:0006536.label: Airway obstruction
HP:0006536.definition: Obstruction of conducting airways of the lung.

HP:0006538.label: Recurrent bronchopulmonary infections
HP:0006538.definition: An increased susceptibility to bronchopulmonary infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bronchopulmonary infections.

HP:0006541.label: obsolete Chronic obstructive airway disease from birth

HP:0006544.label: Extrapulmonary lobar sequestration
HP:0006544.definition: A type of pulmonary sequestration that is completely enclosed in its own pleural sac, occurring above, within, or below the diaphragm, and without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.
HP:0006544.comment: Extralobar sequestration (ELS) may be asymptomatic. Infants with symptomatic lesions may present with respiratory distress, pneumonia, feeding difficulties, hemorrhage, or even congestive heart failure. The sequestered lobe may cause substantial arteriovenous shunting, leading to high-output cardiac failure. Extrapulmonary sequestra nearly all appear on the left side.

HP:0006548.label: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
HP:0006548.definition: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation, a condition most commonly associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, is an abnormal communication between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary communication. HRCT images usually show a coarse spidery appearance of the peripheral vascular markings in the lungs. More specific findings are obtained in the pulmonary angiogram where the normally invisible capillary phase is replaced by irregular vascular channels bridging the peripheral branches of pulmonary arteries and veins.

HP:0006554.label: Acute hepatic failure
HP:0006554.definition: Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as acute if there is onset of encephalopathy within 8 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.

HP:0006555.label: Diffuse hepatic steatosis
HP:0006555.definition: A diffuse form of hepatic steatosis.

HP:0006558.label: Decreased mitochondrial complex III activity in liver tissue
HP:0006558.definition: Decreased activity of complex III of the mitochondrion in the liver.
HP:0006558.comment: Complex III, also known as ubiquinol-cytochrome c oxidoreductase or cytochrome bc1 complex, is a multisubunit integral membrane complex of the mitochondrial transport chain, which catalyzes electron transfer from ubiquinol to cytochrome c and couples this process to electrogenic translocation of protons across the mitochondrial inner membrane. Mitochondrial complex III is integrated in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

HP:0006559.label: Hepatic calcification
HP:0006559.definition: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition in the liver.

HP:0006560.label: Biliary hyperplasia
HP:0006560.definition: Hyperplasia of the biliary tree, as manifested by increased size of bile ducts, dilated lumen, and histologically by an increased number of epithelial cells or hyperplasia.

HP:0006562.label: Viral hepatitis
HP:0006562.definition: Inflammation of the liver due to infection with a virus.

HP:0006563.label: Malformation of the hepatic ductal plate

HP:0006564.label: Fluctuating hepatomegaly
HP:0006564.definition: Intermittently increased size of the liver.

HP:0006565.label: Increased hepatocellular lipid droplets
HP:0006565.definition: An abnormal increase in the amount of intracellular lipid droplets in hepatocytes.
HP:0006565.comment: Lipid droplets, rich in triglycerides and cholesterol esters, are cellular lipid storage organelles.

HP:0006568.label: Increased hepatic glycogen content
HP:0006568.definition: An increase in the amount of glycogen stored in hepatocytes compared to normal.
HP:0006568.comment: Glycogen acts as secondary long-term energy storage in the liver and other organs. Its intracellular concentration can be increased in some disease states such as obesity.

HP:0006571.label: Reduced number of intrahepatic bile ducts
HP:0006571.definition: The presence of reduced numbers of intrahepatic bile duct than normal.

HP:0006573.label: Acute hepatic steatosis
HP:0006573.definition: An acute form of hepatic steatosis.

HP:0006577.label: Macronodular cirrhosis
HP:0006577.definition: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of large regenerative nodules.
HP:0006577.comment: In macronodular cirrhosis (post-necrotic cirrhosis), the nodules are larger than 3 mm.

HP:0006579.label: Prolonged neonatal jaundice
HP:0006579.definition: Neonatal jaundice refers to a yellowing of the skin and other tissues of a newborn infant as a result of increased concentrations of bilirubin in the blood. Neonatal jaundice affects over half of all newborns to some extent in the first week of life. Prolonged neonatal jaundice is said to be present if the jaundice persists for longer than 14 days in term infants and 21 days in preterm infants.
exact_synonyms: Prolonged yellowing of skin in newborn

HP:0006580.label: Portal fibrosis
HP:0006580.definition: Fibroblast proliferation and fiber expansion from the portal areas to the lobule.
HP:0006580.comment: Portal fibrosis can be seen in viral hepatitis and other types of liver disease.

HP:0006581.label: Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in liver
HP:0006581.definition: An abnormal reduction in the number of mitochondria in hepatocytes.

HP:0006582.label: Reye syndrome-like episodes
HP:0006582.definition: Repeated occurrences of acute noninflammatory encephalopathy and fatty degenerative liver failure.
HP:0006582.comment: This feature has been observed in individuals withe mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome-6 (MTDPS6), also known as Navajo neurohepatopathy [MIM:256810].

HP:0006585.label: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle
HP:0006585.definition: The two portions of the clavicle (corresponding to the two primary ossification centers of the clavicle) are connected by a fibrous bridge that is contiguous with the periosteum, and a synovial membrane develops, resulting in a clavicle with a bipartite appearance radiographically. Congenital pseudarthrosis of the clavicle generally presents as a painless mass or swelling over the clavicle.
HP:0006585.comment: In congenital pseudarthrosis of the clavicle, the two primary ossification centers fail to unite, probably due to a disruption of diaphyseal membranous ossification. See PMID:22295044, Figure 1, for the radiographic appearance of this feature.

HP:0006587.label: Straight clavicles
HP:0006587.definition: An abnormally straight configuration of the clavicle, a tubular bone which normally is doubly curved .

HP:0006591.label: Absent glenoid fossa
HP:0006591.definition: Lack of development of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.

HP:0006595.label: Scapulohumeral synostosis
HP:0006595.definition: Bony fusion between the humerus and scapula, leading to an impairment in mobility of the affected shoulder joint.
exact_synonyms: Fusion of shoulder blade to long bone in upper arm

HP:0006597.label: Diaphragmatic paralysis
HP:0006597.definition: The presence of a paralyzed diaphragm.
HP:0006597.comment: Loss of the ability to move the diaphragm for respiratory motions. Patients with complete diaphragm paralysis complain of gross orthopnoea, disturbed sleep and early morning headaches. They have shortness of breath on minimal exertion and, because they sleep poorly, they experience daytime fatigue.

HP:0006598.label: Irregular ossification at anterior rib ends

HP:0006606.label: Irregular chondrocostal junctions
HP:0006606.definition: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth border between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.
HP:0006606.comment: The first seven pairs of ribs are connected with the sternum; the next three ribs are each articulated with the lower border of the cartilage of the preceding rib; the last two ribs have pointed extremities, which do not connect with the sternum.

HP:0006607.label: Precocious costochondral ossification
HP:0006607.definition: Early ossification of the costochondral junction, which is the joint between the ribs and costal cartilage in the front of the rib cage.
HP:0006607.comment: The costal cartilage typically calcifies with advancing age and is therefore easier to identify on radiographs obtained in older patients.

HP:0006608.label: Midclavicular hypoplasia
HP:0006608.definition: Underdevelopment of the middle portion of the clavicle.
exact_synonyms: Underdeveloped middle portion of the collarbone

HP:0006610.label: Wide intermamillary distance
HP:0006610.definition: A larger than usual distance between the left and right nipple.

HP:0006611.label: Decreased number of sternal ossification centers
HP:0006611.definition: A less than normal number of sternal ossification centers. The sternum is initially formed from bilateral sternal plates that chondrify and begin to fuse with ribs at 10 weeks gestational age. Ossification starts in the manubrium and upper part of the sternal body at the 6th month, in the middle of the sternal body at the 7th month, in the lower part of the body during the 1st postnatal year and in the xiphoid process between years 5 and 18. The number of ossification centers vary up to six, and it is the ossification centers that are visualized by prenatal ultrasound. This term describes a reduction in the number of ossification centers compared with age-related norms.
exact_synonyms: Decreased number of sternal ossification centres

HP:0006615.label: Absent in utero rib ossification
HP:0006615.definition: Lack of formation and mineralization of the ribs in utero.

HP:0006619.label: Anterior rib punctate calcifications
HP:0006619.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in point-like foci within the anterior portion of one or more ribs.

HP:0006623.label: Costochondral joint sclerosis
HP:0006623.definition: Abnormal increase in density of the tissue at the costochondral junctions.

HP:0006625.label: Multifocal breast carcinoma
HP:0006625.definition: Breast carcinoma that is bilateral or otherwise multifocal.

HP:0006628.label: Absent sternal ossification
HP:0006628.definition: Lack of formation of mineralized bony tissue of the sternum.

HP:0006631.label: Hypoplastic distal segments of scapulae
exact_synonyms: Small distal segments of the shoulder blade
Underdeveloped outermost segments of shoulder blade

HP:0006633.label: Glenoid fossa hypoplasia
HP:0006633.definition: Underdevelopment of the glenoid fossa, which is the cavity in the lateral part of the scapula which articulates with the head of the humerus.

HP:0006634.label: Osteosclerosis of ribs
HP:0006634.definition: Osteosclerosis of ribs (increased density related to increased bone mass).

HP:0006638.label: Midclavicular aplasia
HP:0006638.definition: Developmental defect resulting in congenital absence of the middle portion of the clavicle.

HP:0006640.label: Multiple rib fractures
HP:0006640.definition: More than one fracture of the ribs. Callus formation around multiple rib fractures can produce a row of multiple rounded expansions (beadlike prominences) giving the appearance of beaded ribs. Note that rachitic rosary would have one bead per rib (a swelling at the costochondral junction), while beaded ribs in the context of multiple rib fractures have multiple beads (fractures) along the same rib.

HP:0006645.label: Thin clavicles
HP:0006645.definition: Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles.

HP:0006646.label: Costal cartilage calcification
HP:0006646.definition: Calcification of the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage found at the anterior ends of the ribs which serve to prolong the ribs forward and contribute to the elasticity of the walls of the thorax.

HP:0006649.label: Costochondral pain
HP:0006649.definition: Chest wall pain in the area of the costochondral junctions.
HP:0006649.comment: Costochondral pain is in the differential diagnosis of chest pain, being a relatively benign cause compared to myocardial ischemia. Costochondral pain can be caused by costochondritis.

HP:0006650.label: Thickening of the lateral border of the scapula
exact_synonyms: Thickening of the lateral border of the shoulder blade

HP:0006660.label: Aplastic clavicle
HP:0006660.definition: Absence of the clavicles as a developmental defect.

HP:0006665.label: Coat hanger sign of ribs
HP:0006665.definition: An abnormal morphology of the ribs consisting of shorted, abnormally curved ribs. On posteroanterior chest radiography, the ribs show a curvature resembling that of a coat hanger (clothes hanger).
HP:0006665.comment: The coat hanger abnormality of the ribs is said to be a useful diagnostic marker of paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 14.

HP:0006677.label: Prolonged QRS complex
HP:0006677.definition: Increased time for the complex comprised of the Q wave, R wave, and S wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).. In adults, normal values are 0.06 - 0.10 sec.

HP:0006679.label: Granulomatous coronary arteritis
HP:0006679.definition: Inflammation of the coronary arteries involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.
HP:0006679.comment: A granuloma is a compact (organized) collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes (macrophages and/or epithelioid cells) which may or may not be accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis or the infiltration of other inflammatory leukocytes (Adams DO. The granulomatous inflammatory response. Am J Pathol 1976:84:163-192).

HP:0006682.label: Premature ventricular contraction
HP:0006682.definition: Premature ventricular contractions (PVC) or ventricular extrasystoles are premature contractions of the heart that arise in response to an impulse in the ventricles rather than the normal impulse from the sinoatrial (SA) node.
HP:0006682.comment: A premature ventricular contraction (PVC) may be perceived as a skipped beat or as palpitations. Although they may cause symptoms such as palpitations or dizziness, incidental PVCs are generally considered benign. Highly frequent PVCs, however, can have detrimental effects on the left ventricular function over time and may cause or worsen heart failure. During a PVC, the heartbeat is initiated by the Purkinje fibers rather than the SA node. Given that a PVC occurs before a regular heartbeat, there is a pause before the next regular heartbeat. PVCs can occur in isolation or in repeated patterns. Two consecutive PVCs are termed doublets while three consecutive PVCs are named triplets. It is important to note that three or more consecutive PVCs are classified as ventricular tachycardia.

HP:0006683.label: Abnormal ventricular filling
HP:0006683.definition: An abnormality of filling of a ventricle with blood during diastole.
HP:0006683.comment: Two diastolic properties, the rate of ventricular relaxation and the ventricular compliance are especially important determinants of ventricular filling.

HP:0006684.label: Ventricular preexcitation with multiple accessory pathways
HP:0006684.definition: A form of ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of multiple accessory pathways for cardiac conduction.

HP:0006685.label: Endocardial fibrosis
HP:0006685.definition: The presence of excessive connective tissue in the endocardium.

HP:0006687.label: Aortic tortuosity
HP:0006687.definition: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the aorta.

HP:0006689.label: Bacterial endocarditis
HP:0006689.definition: A bacterial infection of the endocardium, the inner layer of the heart, which usually involves the heart valves.

HP:0006690.label: Myocardial calcification
HP:0006690.comment: Calcification affecting the muscle layer of the heart.

HP:0006691.label: Pulmonic valve myxoma
HP:0006691.definition: A benign tumor of connective tissue containing mucous or gelatinous material (myxoma) localized in the pumonic valve.

HP:0006692.label: Short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
HP:0006692.definition: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve.
HP:0006692.comment: The chordae tendineae connect the papillary muscles to the tricuspid valve and the mitral valve.

HP:0006694.label: Early progressive calcific cardiac valvular disease

HP:0006695.label: Atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0006695.definition: A defect of the atrioventricular septum of the heart.
HP:0006695.comment: During atrioventricular valvuloseptal morphogenesis, the endocardial cushions expand as they are infiltrated by extracellular matrix secreted from the surrounding myocardium. The cushions then fuse and are remodeled to form the atrioventricular valves and septa. Failure of this process results in AVSD, with the degree of severity dependent on the stage at which the developmental failure occurs. AVSD are a spectrum of cardiac malformations that result in a persistent common atrioventricular canal.

HP:0006698.label: Dilatation of the ventricular cavity
HP:0006698.definition: A localized outpouching of ventricular cavity that is generally associated with dyskinesia and paradoxical expansion during systole.
HP:0006698.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation. Ventricular aneurysms may have rim of calcium in the affected regions of the ventricular wall (which can become fibrotic). Thromboembolism is a potential complication. Ventricular aneurysms can be diagnosed by ventriculography.

HP:0006699.label: Premature atrial contractions
HP:0006699.definition: A type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature atrial contractions or beats caused by signals originating from ectopic atrial sites.

HP:0006702.label: Coronary artery dissection
HP:0006702.definition: Acute occurrence of a dissection (tear within the tunica intima and entry of blood into the tunica media) of a coronary artery.

HP:0006704.label: Abnormal coronary artery morphology
HP:0006704.definition: Any structural abnormality of the coronary arteries.

HP:0006705.label: Abnormal atrioventricular valve morphology
HP:0006705.definition: An abnormality of an atrioventricular valve.

HP:0006707.label: Abnormality of the hepatic vasculature
HP:0006707.definition: An abnormality of the hepatic vasculature.

HP:0006710.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the clavicles
HP:0006710.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the clavicles (collar bones).

HP:0006711.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the thorax

HP:0006721.label: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
HP:0006721.definition: A form of acute leukemia characterized by excess lympoblasts.

HP:0006725.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
HP:0006725.definition: The presence of an adenocarcinoma of the pancreas.

HP:0006727.label: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemias
HP:0006727.definition: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia of T-cell origin. It comprises about 15% of childhood cases and 25% of adult cases. It is more common in males than females.

HP:0006729.label: Retroperitoneal paraganglioma
HP:0006729.definition: A paraganglioma (previously referred to as chemodectoma) located in the retroperitoneal space. Paragangliomas (also known as extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas) are rare tumors that arise from extra-adrenal chromaffin cells. Paragangliomas are characterized by secretions of excessive catecholamines, including epinephrine, norepinephrine and dopamine, which may lead to clinical symptoms, including episodic hypertension, tachycardia and diaphoresis. However, between 40 and 50% of paragangliomas are non-functional.
HP:0006729.comment: The retroperitoneum is an anatomical space located behind the abdominal or peritoneal cavity. Abdominal organs that are not suspended by the mesentery and lie between the abdominal wall and parietal peritoneum are said to lie within the retroperitoneum. Several individual spaces make up the retroperitoneum. These spaces are the anterior pararenal space, posterior pararenal space, and the perirenal space.

HP:0006731.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
HP:0006731.definition: The presence of an follicular adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland.

HP:0006732.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 2
HP:0006732.definition: A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma in which the papillae are covered by large eosinophilic cells with pleomorphic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and nuclear pseudostratification.
HP:0006732.comment: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 2 is a common feature of hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer; HLRCC (OMIM 150800).

HP:0006733.label: Acute megakaryocytic leukemia
HP:0006733.definition: A rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia evolving from primitive megakaryoblasts.

HP:0006735.label: Renal cortical adenoma
HP:0006735.definition: The presence of an adenoma in the cortex of the kidney.

HP:0006737.label: Extraadrenal pheochromocytoma
HP:0006737.definition: Pheochromocytoma not originating from the adrenal medulla but from another source such as from chromaffin cells in or about sympathetic ganglia.

HP:0006739.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
HP:0006739.definition: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is a malignant tumor of squamous epithelium.

HP:0006740.label: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
HP:0006740.definition: The presence of a carcinoma of the urinary bladder with origin in a transitional epithelial cell.

HP:0006744.label: Adrenocortical carcinoma
HP:0006744.definition: A malignant neoplasm of the adrenal cortex that may produce hormones such as cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen, or testosterone.

HP:0006748.label: Adrenal pheochromocytoma
HP:0006748.definition: Pheochromocytoma originating from the adrenal medulla.

HP:0006751.label: Paraspinal neurofibroma
HP:0006751.definition: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized adjacent to the spine.

HP:0006753.label: Neoplasm of the stomach
HP:0006753.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the stomach.

HP:0006755.label: Cutaneous leiomyosarcoma
HP:0006755.definition: The presence of leiomyosarcoma of the skin.

HP:0006758.label: Malignant genitourinary tract tumor
HP:0006758.definition: The presence of a malignant neoplasm of the genital system.

HP:0006762.label: Renal pelvic carcinoma
HP:0006762.definition: The presence of a carcinoma in the renal pelvis.

HP:0006765.label: Chondrosarcoma
HP:0006765.definition: A slowly growing malignant neoplasm derived from cartilage cells.

HP:0006766.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
HP:0006766.definition: The presence of renal cell carcinoma in the renal papilla.

HP:0006767.label: Pituitary prolactin cell adenoma
HP:0006767.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma originating in prolactin secreting cells. This kind of adenoma is characterized by overproduction of prolactin, and may cause loss of menstrual periods and breast milk production in women.

HP:0006770.label: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
HP:0006770.definition: A subtype of renal cell carcinoma thought to originate from mature renal tubular cells in the proximal tubule of the nehpron.

HP:0006772.label: Renal angiomyolipoma
HP:0006772.definition: A benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.
HP:0006772.comment: Angiomyolipoma is a benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.

HP:0006774.label: Ovarian papillary adenocarcinoma
HP:0006774.definition: The presence of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the ovary.

HP:0006775.label: Multiple myeloma
HP:0006775.definition: A malignant plasma cell tumor growing within soft tissue or within the skeleton.

HP:0006778.label: Benign genitourinary tract neoplasm
HP:0006778.definition: A non-malignant neoplasm of the genitourinary system.

HP:0006780.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
HP:0006780.definition: A malignancy of the parathyroid glands. Parathyroid carcinoma usually secretes parathyroid hormone, leading to hyperparathyroidism.

HP:0006781.label: Hurthle cell thyroid adenoma
HP:0006781.definition: A kind of thyroid adenoma characterized by the presence of oxyphil cells.
HP:0006781.comment: Oxyphil cells of thyroid, defined by the Cell Ontology as oncocytes located in the thyroid, are also known as Hurthle cells.

HP:0006785.label: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
HP:0006785.definition: Muscular dystrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle (the hips and shoulders).

HP:0006794.label: Loss of ability to walk in first decade
exact_synonyms: Loss of ability to walk in first decade

HP:0006799.label: Basal ganglia cysts
exact_synonyms: Cystic lesions in the basal ganglia

HP:0006802.label: Abnormal anterior horn cell morphology
HP:0006802.definition: Any anomaly of the anterior horn cell.
HP:0006802.comment: Anterior horn cells are efferent neurons that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle. They conduct nerve impulses that lead to movement of muscles.
exact_synonyms: Anomaly of the anterior horn cells
Abnormality of the anterior horn cells

HP:0006803.label: Vivid hallucination
HP:0006803.definition: Perceptual experiences that are vivid, intense, and sensory in nature occur in the absence of corresponding stimuli from the external environment.

HP:0006808.label: Cerebral hypomyelination
HP:0006808.definition: Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the white matter of the central nervous system.

HP:0006812.label: Abnormal posterior periventricular white matter morphology
HP:0006812.definition: An anomaly of the white matter of the brain localized in the region posterior to the cerebral ventricles.
exact_synonyms: White matter abnormalities in the posterior periventricular region

HP:0006813.label: Focal hemiclonic seizure
HP:0006813.definition: A type of focal clonic seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking rapidly involves one side of the body at seizure onset.
HP:0006813.comment: A seizure type typically occurring in certain epilepsy syndromes, such as Dravet syndrome and self-limited neonatal seizures.

HP:0006817.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis
HP:0006817.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

HP:0006818.label: 4-layered lissencephaly
HP:0006818.definition: A form of lissencephaly in which the cortex is thickened and has four more or less disorganized layers rather than six normal layers resulting from incomplete neuronal migration during brain development. At neuropathological examination, a 4-layered cortex consists of an upper molecular layer, a second thin cellular layer containing pyramidal neurons usually observed in layer V, a third pale poorly cellular layer and a fourth thick deep layer made up of neurons which had failed to migrate. Radiologocally would manifest as agyria or pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm.

HP:0006821.label: Frontal polymicrogyria
HP:0006821.definition: A type of polymicrogyria with a gradient of severity (anterior more severe than posterior) extending from frontal poles posteriorly to precentral gyrus and inferiorly to frontal operculum.

HP:0006825.label: Pallor of dorsal columns of the spinal cord
HP:0006825.definition: An abnormally pale appearance of the dorsal portion of the gray substance of the spinal cord. This finding can be observed by histological examination.

HP:0006829.label: Severe muscular hypotonia
HP:0006829.definition: A severe degree of muscular hypotonia characterized by markedly reduced muscle tone.

HP:0006830.label: obsolete Severe neonatal hypotonia in males

HP:0006834.label: Developmental stagnation at onset of seizures
HP:0006834.definition: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills, following the onset of epilepsy.

HP:0006837.label: Congenital Horner syndrome
HP:0006837.definition: A type of Horner syndrome with congenital onset.

HP:0006844.label: Absent patellar reflexes
HP:0006844.definition: Absence of the knee jerk reflex, which can normally be elicited by tapping the patellar tendon with a reflex hammer just below the patella.

HP:0006849.label: Hypodysplasia of the corpus callosum
HP:0006849.definition: Developmental defect characterized by a small and malformed corpus callosum.

HP:0006850.label: Hypoplasia of the ventral pons
HP:0006850.definition: Underdevelopment of the ventral portion of the pons.

HP:0006851.label: Symmetric spinal nerve root neurofibromas
HP:0006851.definition: Multiple neurofibromas of the spinal nerve roots with a symmetric distribution.
exact_synonyms: Spinal nerve root neurofibromas, symmetric, multiple

HP:0006852.label: Episodic generalized hypotonia
HP:0006852.definition: The occurrence of repeated episodes of generalized muscular hypotonia.

HP:0006855.label: Cerebellar vermis atrophy
HP:0006855.definition: Wasting (atrophy) of the vermis of cerebellum.
HP:0006855.comment: This sign can be visualized with brain MRI.

HP:0006858.label: Impaired distal proprioception
HP:0006858.definition: A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position occurring at distal joints.

HP:0006863.label: Severe expressive language delay
HP:0006863.definition: A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

HP:0006865.label: Sensorimotor polyneuropathy affecting arms more than legs

HP:0006870.label: Lobar holoprosencephaly
HP:0006870.definition: A type of holoprosencephaly in which most of the right and left cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles are separated but the most rostral aspect of the telencephalon, the frontal lobes, are fused, especially ventrally.

HP:0006873.label: Symmetrical progressive peripheral demyelination
HP:0006873.definition: A symmetric and progressive loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

HP:0006879.label: Pontocerebellar atrophy
HP:0006879.definition: Atrophy affecting the pons and the cerebellum.

HP:0006881.label: Diffuse peripheral demyelination
HP:0006881.definition: A diffuse loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

HP:0006886.label: Impaired distal vibration sensation
HP:0006886.definition: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the distal portions of the limbs.

HP:0006889.label: Borderline intellectual disability
HP:0006889.definition: Borderline intellectual disability is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 70-85.
HP:0006889.comment: We choose to define the concept of borderline intellectual disability onthe basis of the commonly used range of 70-85 (IQ), but note that in DSM-5, IQ boundaries are no longer part of the classification.

HP:0006892.label: Frontotemporal cerebral atrophy
HP:0006892.definition: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the frontotemporal cerebrum.

HP:0006893.label: obsolete Severely dysplastic cerebellum
HP:0006893.comment: Use Cerebellar dysplasia (HP:0007033) with the modifier Severe.

HP:0006896.label: Hypnopompic hallucination
HP:0006896.definition: Hallucinations occurring during the transition from sleep to wakefulness.

HP:0006897.label: Abducens palsy
HP:0006897.definition: Malfunction of the abducens nerve as manifested by impairment of the ability of the affected eye to be moved outward. Patients who develop abducens nerve palsy often present with binocular horizontal diplopia, which is a double vision when looking at objects side by side. There will be a notable weakness of the ipsilateral lateral rectus muscle leading to a deficit in of eye abduction on the affected side. Some patients may present with a constant head turning movement to maintain binocular fusion and to lessen the degree of diplopia.
HP:0006897.comment: Affected individuals may experience diplopia as well as esotropia or convergent strabismus.

HP:0006906.label: Congenital intracerebral calcification
HP:0006906.definition: The presence of calcium deposition within brain structures that is present already at the time of birth.

HP:0006916.label: Intraaxonal accumulation of curvilinear autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0006916.definition: Curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material within axons.

HP:0006919.label: obsolete Abnormal aggressive, impulsive or violent behavior

HP:0006921.label: Axial muscle stiffness
HP:0006921.definition: Stiffness (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) of the axial musculature.

HP:0006927.label: Unilateral polymicrogyria
HP:0006927.definition: Excessive number of small gyri (convolutions) on the surface of one side of the brain.

HP:0006929.label: Hypoglycemic encephalopathy
HP:0006929.definition: Brain damage related to a lowering of blood glucose below a critical level (around 30 mg/dl), which may lead to confusion, lethargy and delirium followed by seizures and coma. Prolonged hypoglycemia may lead to irreversible brain damage.

HP:0006930.label: Frontoparietal cortical dysplasia
HP:0006930.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cortex of frontal lobe and the cortex of parietal lobe.

HP:0006931.label: Pericallosal lipoma
HP:0006931.definition: Pericallosal lipomas are congenital soft masses of adipose cells encapsulated by a thin layer of fibrous tissue, appearing adjacent to the corpus callosum of the brain.

HP:0006932.label: Transient psychotic episodes
HP:0006932.definition: Relatively short-lived periods of psychosis are characterized by the sudden onset of severe disturbances in perception, thinking, and behavior. These episodes typically last for a brief duration, generally ranging from a few days to a few weeks, and are often triggered by a significant stressor or traumatic event.

HP:0006934.label: Congenital nystagmus
HP:0006934.definition: Nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

HP:0006937.label: Impaired distal tactile sensation
HP:0006937.definition: A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation) on the skin of the distal limbs. This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.

HP:0006938.label: Impaired vibration sensation at ankles
HP:0006938.definition: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration at the ankles. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to the malleoli of the ankles.

HP:0006944.label: Abolished vibration sense
HP:0006944.definition: A complete loss of the ability to perceive vibration.

HP:0006946.label: Recurrent meningitis
HP:0006946.definition: An increased susceptibility to meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of meningitis.

HP:0006955.label: Olivopontocerebellar hypoplasia
HP:0006955.definition: Hypoplasia of the cerebellum, pontine nuclei, and inferior olivary nucleus.

HP:0006957.label: obsolete Loss of ability to walk

HP:0006958.label: Abnormal auditory evoked potentials
HP:0006958.definition: An abnormality of the auditory evoked potentials, which are used to trace the signal generated by a sound, from the cochlear nerve, through the lateral lemniscus, to the medial geniculate nucleus, and to the cortex.
HP:0006958.comment: Auditory brainstem response audiometry typically uses a click stimulus that generates a response from the basilar region of the cochlea.

HP:0006959.label: Proximal spinal muscular atrophy
HP:0006959.definition: Proximal spinal muscular atrophy, i.e., muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

HP:0006960.label: Choroid plexus calcification
HP:0006960.definition: The presence of calcium deposition in the choroid plexus.

HP:0006962.label: Gait instability, worse in the dark
exact_synonyms: Unstable walking, worse in the dark

HP:0006970.label: Periventricular leukomalacia
HP:0006970.definition: Periventricular leukomalacia is characterized by diffuse injury of deep cerebral white matter, accompanied in its most severe form by focal necrosis. The neuropathologic hallmarks of PVL are microglial activation and focal and diffuse periventricular depletion of premyelinating oligodendroglia.
HP:0006970.comment: Periventricular leukomalacia is the leading known cause of cerebral palsy. Magnetic resonance imaging-based neuroimaging techniques provide greater diagnostic sensitivity for PVL than does head ultrasonography and often document the involvement of telencephalic gray matter and long tracts in addition to periventricular white matter.

HP:0006976.label: Necrotizing encephalopathy
HP:0006976.definition: A type of encephalopathy (brain disease, damage, or malfunction accompanied by an altered mental state) that is characterized by evidence of necrosis of brain tissue.
HP:0006976.comment: The disease acute necrotizing encephalopathy is characterized by acute onset encephalopathy with rapid, progressive neurologic deterioration, seizures and symmetric multifocal brain lesions. This term is kept for convenience. For new annotations, it is recommended that the specific phenotypic abnormalities be noted.

HP:0006977.label: Deficit in grammar
HP:0006977.definition: Deficit in grammar, including syntax and morphology.

HP:0006979.label: Sleep-wake cycle disturbance
HP:0006979.definition: Any abnormality of an individual's circadian rhythm that affects the timing of sleeping and being awake is referred to as a sleep-wake disorder.
HP:0006979.comment: Often, patients complain of insomnia when their desired sleep-wake cycle is inconsistent with their intrinsic rhythms.

HP:0006980.label: Progressive leukoencephalopathy
HP:0006980.definition: Leukoencephalopathy that gets more severe with time.

HP:0006984.label: obsolete Distal sensory loss of all modalities

HP:0006988.label: Alobar holoprosencephaly
HP:0006988.definition: A type of holoprosencephaly characterized by the presence of a single ventricle and no separation of the cerebral hemisphere. The single midline ventricle is often greatly enlarged.

HP:0006989.label: Dysplastic corpus callosum
HP:0006989.definition: Dysplasia and dysgenesis of the corpus callosum are nonspecific descriptions that imply defective development of the corpus callosum. The term dysplasia is applied when the morphology of the corpus callosum is altered as a congenital trait. For instance, the corpus callosum may be hump-shaped, kinked, or a striped corpus callosum that lacks an anatomically distinct genu and splenium.

HP:0006990.label: Myelin-dependent gliosis
HP:0006990.definition: A type of gliosis that occurs in the vicinity of injured neurons.

HP:0006999.label: Basal ganglia gliosis
HP:0006999.definition: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the basal ganglia.
HP:0006999.comment: Gliosis refers to a proliferation of astrocytes in an area of damage of nervous tissue.

HP:0007001.label: Loss of Purkinje cells in the cerebellar vermis

HP:0007002.label: Motor axonal neuropathy
HP:0007002.definition: Progressive impairment of function of motor axons with muscle weakness, atrophy, and cramps. The deficits are length-dependent, meaning that muscles innervated by the longest nerves are affected first, so that for instance the arms are affected at a later age than the onset of deficits involving the lower leg.
HP:0007002.comment: Distal motor neuropathy is a bundled term that should not be used if more detailed information about the phenotype is available.

HP:0007007.label: Cavitation of the basal ganglia
HP:0007007.definition: The formation of small cavities in the tissue of the basal ganglia.
HP:0007007.comment: This feature can be observed in tissue upon autopsy or in magnetic resonance tomography (MRI) images.

HP:0007010.label: Poor fine motor coordination
HP:0007010.definition: An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of small muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Fine motor skills are required to mediate movements of the wrists, hands, fingers, feet, and toes.

HP:0007011.label: Fourth cranial nerve palsy
HP:0007011.definition: Paralysis of the fourth cranial (trochlear) nerve manifested as weakness of the superior oblique muscle which causes vertical diplopia that is maximal when the affected eye is adducted and directed inferiorly.
HP:0007011.comment: The fourth cranial nerve crosses as it exits the midbrain dorsally and may be injured along its course through the intracranial space, cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, or orbit.

HP:0007015.label: Poor gross motor coordination
HP:0007015.definition: An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of large muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Gross motor skills are required to mediate movements of the arms, legs, and other large body parts.

HP:0007018.label: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
HP:0007018.definition: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. The main symptoms are distractibility, impulsivity, hyperactivity, and often trouble organizing tasks and projects, difficulty going to sleep, and social problems from being aggressive, loud, or impatient.

HP:0007021.label: Pain insensitivity
HP:0007021.comment: The word Anesthesia is occasionally used to refer to lack of pain sensation, although it is more usually used to denote a medical procedure design to relieve pain.

HP:0007023.label: Antenatal intracerebral hemorrhage
HP:0007023.definition: Cerebral hemorrhage that occurs before birth.

HP:0007024.label: Pseudobulbar paralysis
HP:0007024.definition: Bilateral impairment of the function of the cranial nerves 9-12, which control musculature involved in eating, swallowing, and speech. Pseudobulbar paralysis is characterized clinically by dysarthria, dysphonia, and dysphagia with bifacial paralysis, and may be accompanied by Pseudobulbar behavioral symptoms such as enforced crying and laughing.

HP:0007027.label: Poorly formed metencephalon
HP:0007027.definition: A morphological abnormality of the metencephalon.
HP:0007027.comment: The metencephalon comprises the pons and the cerebellum; contains a portion of the fourth ventricle; and the trigeminal nerve, abducens nerve, facial nerve, and a portion of the vestibulocochlear nerve. The metencephalon is part of the hindbrain.

HP:0007029.label: Cerebral berry aneurysm
HP:0007029.definition: A small, sac-like aneurysm (outpouching) of a cerebral blood vessel.
HP:0007029.comment: Saccular aneurysms are often said to have a berry-shaped appearance, whence the name.

HP:0007033.label: Cerebellar dysplasia
HP:0007033.definition: Cerebellar dysplasia (abnormal growth or development) is defined by abnormal cerebellar foliation, white matter arborization, and gray-white matter junction. Cerebellar dysplasia is a neuroimaging finding that describes abnormalities of both the cerebellar cortex and white matter and is associated with variable neurodevelopmental outcome. Dysplasia may globally involve the cerebellum or affect only one cerebellar hemisphere. In addition, cerebellar dysplasia may be associated with cortical/subcortical cysts.
HP:0007033.comment: Any part of the cerebellum can be dysplastic, from small focal regions within one hemisphere to abnormal foliation throughout the cerebellum. Hypoplastic cerebella are frequently also dysmorphic, as observed in tubulinopathies and cobblestone malformations.

HP:0007035.label: Anterior encephalocele
HP:0007035.definition: A type of congenital malformation in which brain tissue protrudes through a defect in the anterior (front) part of the skull.
HP:0007035.comment: Anterior encephalocele development occurs from abnormal development of the foramen cecum. A diverticulum of dura usually projects anteriorly between the developing nasal and frontal bones at the fonticulus frontalis/foramen cecum. Later in embryogenesis, the diverticulum regresses, and the bone closes. However, if it does not regress, the brain can herniate through the bone defect and form an encephalocele.

HP:0007039.label: Symmetric T2-signal increase with T1-signal decrease in the putamen
HP:0007039.definition: A symmetric magnetic resonance imaing (MRI) abnormality of the basal ganglia characterized by an increase of signal intensity in T2-weighted images and a corresponding signal decrease on T1-weighted images.
HP:0007039.comment: Pathological processes characterized by increased tissue water content show signal loss on T1-weighted images and a signal increase on T2-weighted images.

HP:0007041.label: Chronic lymphocytic meningitis
HP:0007041.definition: Meningitis that persists for more than 4 weeks, and lymphocytes are present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP:0007047.label: Atrophy of the dentate nucleus
HP:0007047.definition: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of dentate nucleus.

HP:0007048.label: Large basal ganglia
HP:0007048.definition: Increased size of the basal ganglia.

HP:0007054.label: Proximal hyperreflexia
HP:0007054.definition: Hyperactive stretch reflexes of muscles that move proximal joints (elbow, knee).

HP:0007058.label: Generalized cerebral atrophy/hypoplasia
HP:0007058.definition: Generalized atrophy or hypoplasia of the cerebrum.

HP:0007063.label: Aplasia of the inferior half of the cerebellar vermis
exact_synonyms: Absent inferior half of the cerebellar vermis

HP:0007064.label: Progressive language deterioration
HP:0007064.definition: Progressive loss of previously present language abilities.

HP:0007065.label: Disorganization of the anterior cerebellar vermis
exact_synonyms: Disorganisation of the anterior cerebellar vermis

HP:0007066.label: Proximal limb muscle stiffness
HP:0007066.definition: Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in the proximal limb muscle.
HP:0007066.comment: Removed logical definition that used an anonymous class. Requested new term in UBERON: proximal musculature of limb

HP:0007067.label: Distal peripheral sensory neuropathy
HP:0007067.definition: Peripheral sensory neuropathy affecting primarily distal sensation.

HP:0007068.label: Inferior cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
HP:0007068.definition: Underdevelopment of the inferior portion of the vermis of cerebellum.

HP:0007074.label: Thick corpus callosum
HP:0007074.definition: Increased vertical dimension of the corpus callosum. This feature can be visualized by sagittal sections on magnetic resonance tomography imaging of the brain.

HP:0007076.label: Extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
HP:0007076.definition: Muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).
HP:0007076.comment: This is a classic type of extrapyramidal movement disorder.

HP:0007078.label: Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials
HP:0007078.definition: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

HP:0007082.label: Dilated third ventricle
HP:0007082.definition: An increase in size of the third ventricle.
HP:0007082.comment: The third ventricle is midline between the two lateral ventricles, and it communicates between them and the fourth ventricle.

HP:0007089.label: Facial-lingual fasciculations
HP:0007089.definition: Fasciculations affecting the tongue muscle and the musculature of the face.

HP:0007098.label: Paroxysmal choreoathetosis
HP:0007098.definition: Episodes of choreoathetosis that can occur following triggers such as quick voluntary movements.

HP:0007099.label: Chiari type I malformation
HP:0007099.definition: Arnold-Chiari type I malformation refers to a relatively mild degree of herniation of the posteroinferior region of the cerebellum (the cerebellar tonsils) into the cervical canal with little or no displacement of the fourth ventricle. It is characterized by one or both pointed (not rounded) cerebellar tonsils that project 5 mm below the foramen magnum, measured by a line drawn from the basion to the opisthion (McRae Line)

HP:0007103.label: Hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
HP:0007103.definition: A darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter.

HP:0007105.label: Infantile encephalopathy
HP:0007105.definition: Encephalopathy with onset in the infantile period.

HP:0007107.label: Segmental peripheral demyelination
HP:0007107.definition: A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers from segments of the peripheral nervous system.

HP:0007108.label: Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy
HP:0007108.definition: Demyelinating neuropathy is characterized by slow nerve conduction velocities with reduced amplitudes of sensory/motor nerve conduction and prolonged distal latencies.

HP:0007115.label: Naso-orbital encephalocele
HP:0007115.definition: A type of encephalocele that occurs along the medial orbit wall at the level of the frontal process of the maxilla and the ethmoid-lacrimal bone junction.

HP:0007123.label: Subcortical dementia
HP:0007123.definition: A particular type of dementia characterized by a pattern of mental defects consisting prominently of forgetfulness, slowness of thought processes, and personality or mood change.

HP:0007126.label: Proximal amyotrophy
HP:0007126.definition: Amyotrophy (muscular atrophy) affecting the proximal musculature.
HP:0007126.comment: Proximal amyotrophy usually has a roughly symmetric distribution.
exact_synonyms: Wasting of muscles near the body

HP:0007131.label: Acute demyelinating polyneuropathy
HP:0007131.definition: Acute progressive areflexic weakness and mild sensory changes resulting from myelin breakdown and axonal degeneration.
HP:0007131.comment: This is a bundled term used to refer to the symptomatology associated with the Guillain-Barre syndrome.

HP:0007132.label: Pallidal degeneration
HP:0007132.definition: Neurodegeneration involving the globus pallidus,a part of the basal ganglia that is involved in the regulation of voluntary movement.

HP:0007141.label: Sensorimotor neuropathy
exact_synonyms: Nerve damage causing decreased feeling and movement

HP:0007149.label: Distal upper limb amyotrophy
HP:0007149.definition: Muscular atrophy of distal arm muscles.

HP:0007156.label: Asymmetric limb muscle stiffness
HP:0007156.definition: Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in an asymmetric pattern.

HP:0007158.label: Progressive extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
HP:0007158.definition: A progressive degree of muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).

HP:0007159.label: Fluctuations in consciousness
HP:0007159.definition: Changes in one's level of awareness and responsiveness to their environment.

HP:0007162.label: Diffuse demyelination of the cerebral white matter
HP:0007162.definition: A diffuse loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

HP:0007163.label: obsolete Corticospinal tract disease in lower limbs

HP:0007165.label: Periventricular heterotopia
HP:0007165.definition: A form of gray matter heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is typically located periventricularly, also sometimes called subependymal heterotopia. Periventricular means beside the ventricles. This is by far the most common location for heterotopia. Subependymal heterotopia present in a wide array of variations. There can be a small single node or a large number of nodes, can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, can be small or large, single or multiple, and can form a small node or a large wavy or curved mass.
HP:0007165.comment: Periventricular gray matter heterotopia can be seen for example in patients with Smith-Lemli-Opitz-Syndrome.

HP:0007166.label: Paroxysmal dyskinesia
HP:0007166.definition: Episodic bouts of involuntary movements with dystonic, choreic, ballistic movements, or a combination thereof. There is no loss of consciousness during the attacks.

HP:0007179.label: Absent smooth pursuit
HP:0007179.definition: A complete lack of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.

HP:0007181.label: Interosseus muscle atrophy
HP:0007181.definition: Atrophy of the interosseus muscles (including the palmar interossei that lie on the anterior aspect of the metacarpals, the dorsal interosseus muscles of the hand, which lie between the intercarpals, the plantar interosseus muscles, which lie underneath the metatarsal bones, and the dorsal interossei, which are located between the metatarsal bones.
HP:0007181.comment: This term needs disambiguation. Palmar, plantar, or dorsal interosseus muscles.

HP:0007182.label: Peripheral hypomyelination
HP:0007182.definition: Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the peripheral nervous system.
HP:0007182.comment: This finding can be demonstrated by nerve biopsy.

HP:0007183.label: Focal T2 hyperintense basal ganglia lesion
HP:0007183.definition: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the basal ganglia.
related_synonyms: Hyperintense lesions in the basal ganglia on MRI

HP:0007185.label: Loss of consciousness
HP:0007185.definition: Loss of awareness of oneself or one's surroundings, involving (i) a loss of normal motor control is evident as flaccidity or stiffness, either of which can be accompanied by jerking movements, and postural control is lost so that patients fall if they are in an upright position; (ii) normal responsiveness is lost; and (iii) the patient experiences amnesia for the event. Loss of consciousness my be transitory (e.g., syncope) or prolonged.

HP:0007187.label: Focal lissencephaly
HP:0007187.definition: A congenital absence of the convolutions of the cerebral cortex and a poorly formed sylvian fissure that affects a particular part of the cortex.

HP:0007188.label: Congenital facial diplegia
HP:0007188.definition: Facial diplegia (that is, bilateral facial palsy) with congenital onset.

HP:0007190.label: Neuronal loss in the cerebral cortex

HP:0007193.label: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure on awakening
HP:0007193.definition: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure of either generalized or focal onset occurring on or soon after wakening (typically within 90 minutes of waking, regardless of the time of day).

HP:0007200.label: Episodic hypersomnia
HP:0007200.definition: Recurrent episodes of hypersomnia (sleeping 16 or more hours a day) over a period of days or weeks.
HP:0007200.comment: This feature is characteristic of Kleine-Levin syndrome.

HP:0007201.label: Cerebral artery atherosclerosis
HP:0007201.definition: The formation of the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the wall of an artery located in the brain.

HP:0007204.label: Diffuse white matter abnormalities
HP:0007204.comment: This finding is demonstrated by cerebral computer tomography or magnetic resonance imaging.

HP:0007206.label: Hemimegalencephaly
HP:0007206.definition: Enlargement of all or parts of one cerebral hemisphere.
HP:0007206.comment: The affected hemisphere may have focal or diffuse neuronal migration defects, with areas of polymicrogyria, pachygyria, and heterotopia.

HP:0007207.label: Photosensitive tonic-clonic seizure
HP:0007207.definition: Generalized-onset tonic-clonic seizures that are provoked by flashing or flickering light.

HP:0007208.label: Irregular myelin loops
HP:0007208.definition: Presence of irregular redundant loops of focally folded myelin in a peripheral nerve.

HP:0007209.label: Facial paralysis
HP:0007209.definition: Complete loss of ability to move facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (i.e., the seventh cranial nerve).
HP:0007209.comment: Facial paralysis can be caused by compression of the facial nerve.The main difference between facial paralysis and Palsy is cause for the paralysis can be identified, be it a tumor, infection, or nerve damage. Facial paralysis, in most cases, also appears more permanent than Bell's Palsy, with cases lasting for years to life if a patient doesn't seek treatment.

HP:0007210.label: Lower limb amyotrophy
HP:0007210.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting the lower limb.

HP:0007215.label: Periodic hyperkalemic paralysis
HP:0007215.definition: Episodes of muscle weakness associated with elevated levels of potassium in the blood.

HP:0007220.label: Demyelinating motor neuropathy
HP:0007220.comment: Demyelinating motor neuropathy demonstrates slow motor nerve conduction velocities with reduced amplitudes of motor nerve conduction and prolonged distal latencies.

HP:0007229.label: Intracerebral periventricular calcifications
HP:0007229.definition: The presence of calcium deposition in the cerebral white matter surrounding the cerebral ventricles.

HP:0007230.label: Decreased distal sensory nerve action potential
HP:0007230.definition: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential in distal nerve segments. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

HP:0007232.label: Spinocerebellar tract disease in lower limbs

HP:0007233.label: Clusters of axonal regeneration
HP:0007233.definition: Groups of small caliber axons in peripheral nerve biospies indicative of axonal regeneration.

HP:0007240.label: Progressive gait ataxia
HP:0007240.definition: A type of gait ataxia displaying progression of clinical severity.

HP:0007249.label: Decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
exact_synonyms: Decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibres

HP:0007250.label: Recurrent external ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007250.definition: Alternating and recurrent weakness of the external ocular muscles.

HP:0007256.label: Abnormal pyramidal sign
HP:0007256.definition: Functional neurological abnormalities related to dysfunction of the pyramidal tract.
HP:0007256.comment: pyramidal signs are a subset of long-tract signs that specifically indicate corticospinal tract involvement. The more general term long-tract sign refers to a clinical findings related to damage to the long white matter tracts of the CNS, particularly the corticospinal tract, dorsal columns, and the spinothalamic tract.

HP:0007258.label: Severe demyelination of the white matter
HP:0007258.definition: A severe loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

HP:0007260.label: Type II lissencephaly
HP:0007260.definition: A form of lissencephaly characterized by an uneven cortical surface with a so called 'cobblestone' appearace. There are no distinguishable cortical layers.

HP:0007262.label: Symmetric peripheral demyelination
HP:0007262.definition: A symmetric loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

HP:0007263.label: Spinocerebellar atrophy
HP:0007263.definition: Atrophy affecting the cerebellum and the spinocerebellar tracts of the spinal cord.

HP:0007266.label: Cerebral dysmyelination
HP:0007266.definition: Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths of the white matter of the brain.

HP:0007267.label: Chronic axonal neuropathy
HP:0007267.definition: An abnormality characterized by chronic impairment of the normal functioning of the axons.
HP:0007267.comment: This feature is assayed with sural nerve biopsy and is generally taken to be indicative of neuropathy in other peripheral nerves.

HP:0007269.label: Spinal muscular atrophy
HP:0007269.definition: Muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

HP:0007270.label: Atypical absence seizure
HP:0007270.definition: An atypical absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by interruption of ongoing activities and reduced responsiveness. In comparison to a typical absence seizure, changes in tone may be more pronounced, onset and/or cessation may be less abrupt, and the duration of the ictus and post-ictal recovery may be longer. Although not always available, an EEG often demonstrates slow (<3 Hz), irregular, generalized spike-wave activity.
HP:0007270.comment: in 2017 the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology recommended classifying a seizure as having focal or generalized onset only when there is a high degree of confidence (over 80%, arbitrarily chosen to parallel the usual allowable beta error) in the accuracy of this determination; see Dialeptic seizure.

HP:0007274.label: Recurrent bacterial meningitis
HP:0007274.definition: An increased susceptibility to bacterial meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of bacterial meningitis.

HP:0007277.label: Paucity of anterior horn motor neurons

HP:0007281.label: Developmental stagnation
HP:0007281.definition: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills.

HP:0007285.label: Facial palsy secondary to cranial hyperostosis
HP:0007285.definition: Paralysis of the facial nerves on the basis of overgrowth of the cranial bones causing impingement upon the seventh cranial nerve.
exact_synonyms: Facial palsy caused by excessive growth of facial bones
Facial palsy caused by enlargement of cranial bones
Facial palsy caused by overgrowth of cranial bones
Facial palsy secondary to hypertrophy of cranial bones

HP:0007286.label: Horizontal jerk nystagmus
HP:0007286.definition: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.
HP:0007286.comment: Pendular nystagmus refers to the situation in which the eye appeared to oscillate with equal speed in either direction, in contrast to jerk nystagmus, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.

HP:0007289.label: Limb fasciculations
HP:0007289.definition: Fasciculations affecting the musculature of the arms and legs.

HP:0007291.label: Posterior fossa cyst
