HP:0007291.definition: A discrete posterior fossa cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collection that does not communicate directly with the fourth ventricle.

HP:0007301.label: Oromotor apraxia
HP:0007301.definition: Oral-motor apraxia is the inability to volitionally sequence oral movements of the speech structure for nonspeech tasks in the absence of neuromuscular deficits such as paralysis or muscle weakness. Oral-motor apraxia is diagnosed when, despite intact sensory motor function an individual is unable to use these effector systems under voluntary control.
HP:0007301.comment: Affected individuals may experience difficulty in performing movements involving the muscles that also are involved in speech (e.g., clicking the tongue, licking the lips, whistling).

HP:0007302.label: Bipolar affective disorder
HP:0007302.definition: Bipolar disorder is an illness of mood characterized by alternating episodes of elevated and depressed moods, which are interspersed with euthymic periods.

HP:0007305.label: CNS demyelination
HP:0007305.definition: A loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.
HP:0007305.comment: CNS demyelination affects the white matter, which consists mostly of axons with their envelope of myelin, along with two types of neuroglia: oligo-dendrocytes and astrocytes.

HP:0007307.label: Rapid neurologic deterioration
HP:0007307.definition: Loss of neurological function in a time frame that is considered relatively quick, for instance, loss of a develomental milestone or substantial exacerbation of neurological complications such as seizures or feeding difficulties within a few months.

HP:0007321.label: Deep white matter hypodensities
HP:0007321.definition: Multiple areas of darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the deep cerebral white matter.
HP:0007321.comment: See also definition for "Periventricular white matter hypodensities". These two entities are in contra-distinction to each other.

HP:0007325.label: Generalized dystonia
HP:0007325.definition: A type of dystonia that affects all or most of the body.

HP:0007328.label: Impaired pain sensation
HP:0007328.definition: Reduced ability to perceive painful stimuli.

HP:0007330.label: Frontoethmoidal encephalocele
HP:0007330.definition: A type of anterior encephalocele in which there is a protrusion of the contents of the skull through a breach at the point where the frontal and ethmoidal bones meet. Frontoethmoidal encephalocele can be divided further into three distinct categories: nasofrontal, nasoethmoidal, and nasoorbital.

HP:0007332.label: Focal hemifacial clonic seizure
HP:0007332.definition: Focal seizure characterized at onset by clonic movements affecting half of the face.
HP:0007332.comment: A seizure type typically occurring in childhood epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes.

HP:0007333.label: Hypoplasia of the frontal lobes
HP:0007333.definition: Underdevelopment of the frontal lobe of the cerebrum.

HP:0007334.label: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset
HP:0007334.definition: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset is a focal-onset seizure which progresses into a bilateral tonic-clonic phase.
HP:0007334.comment: The ILAE 2017 classification refers to this seizure type as a focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizure. Previously it has been known as a secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The focal features of the seizure may be clinically manifest or alternatively, the spread in brain networks may be so rapid that no preceding focal symptom or sign is identified with demonstration of the focal onset resting on investigations. Note that not all instances of a Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset will be a Focal motor seizure, some will be a Focal non-motor seizure, thus one can only say that there is a Focal-onset.
exact_synonyms: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizure with partial onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizures with focal onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with partial onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizures with focal onset

HP:0007335.label: Recurrent encephalopathy
HP:0007335.definition: Recurrent episodes of brain dysfunction that may be triggered by factors such as metabolic disturbances or infections.

HP:0007338.label: Hypermetric saccades
HP:0007338.definition: A saccade that overshoots the target with the dynamic saccade.

HP:0007340.label: Lower limb muscle weakness
HP:0007340.definition: Weakness of the muscles of the legs.
HP:0007340.comment: Inability to perform rapid, alternating movements.

HP:0007341.label: Diffuse swelling of cerebral white matter

HP:0007343.label: Abnormal morphology of the limbic system
HP:0007343.definition: Any structural anomaly of the limbic system, a set of midline structures surrounding the brainstem of the mammalian brain, originally described anatomically, e.g., hippocampal formation, amygdala, hypothalamus, cingulate cortex. Although the original designation was anatomical, the limbic system has come to be associated with the system in the brain subserving emotional functions. As such, it is very poorly defined and doesn't correspond closely to the anatomical meaning any longer. [BirnLex].

HP:0007344.label: Atrophy/Degeneration involving the spinal cord
exact_synonyms: Atrophic and degenerative changes in the spinal cord

HP:0007350.label: Upper limb hyperreflexia
HP:0007350.definition: Increased intensity of the a reflex in the arm.

HP:0007351.label: Upper limb postural tremor
HP:0007351.definition: A type of tremors that is triggered by holding an arm in a fixed position.

HP:0007359.label: Focal-onset seizure
HP:0007359.definition: A focal-onset seizure is a type of seizure originating within networks limited to one hemisphere. They may be discretely localized or more widely distributed, and may originate in subcortical structures.
HP:0007359.comment: In 2017 the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology recommended classifying a seizure as having focal or generalized onset only when there is a high degree of confidence (>80%, arbitrarily chosen to parallel the usual allowable beta error) in the accuracy of this determination; see Dialeptic seizure.
exact_synonyms: Seizure affecting one half of brain

HP:0007361.label: Abnormal pons morphology
HP:0007361.definition: A structural abnormality of the pons.
HP:0007361.comment: The pons is the portion of the brainstem superior to the medulla oblongata.

HP:0007367.label: Atrophy/Degeneration affecting the central nervous system

HP:0007369.label: Atrophy/Degeneration affecting the cerebrum
HP:0007369.definition: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the cerebrum, also known as the telencephalon, the largest and most highly developed part of the human brain.

HP:0007370.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the corpus callosum
HP:0007370.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the corpus callosum.
exact_synonyms: Complete or partial absence of the corpus callosum
Hypoplasia or absence of the corpus callosum

HP:0007371.label: Corpus callosum atrophy
HP:0007371.definition: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the corpus callosum.

HP:0007375.label: Abnormal septum pellucidum morphology
HP:0007375.definition: An abnormality of the septum pellucidum, which is a thin, triangular, vertical membrane separating the lateral ventricles of the brain.

HP:0007376.label: Abnormal choroid plexus morphology
HP:0007376.definition: An abnormality of the choroid plexus, which is the area in the cerebral ventricles in which cerebrospinal fluid is produced by modified ependymal cells.
HP:0007376.comment: The choroid plexus is a structure in the ventricles of the brain where cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is produced.

HP:0007377.label: Abnormality of somatosensory evoked potentials
HP:0007377.definition: An abnormality of somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP), i.e., of the electrical signals of sensation going from the body to the brain in response to a defined stimulus. Recording electrodes are placed over the scalp, spine, and peripheral nerves proximal to the stimulation site. Clinical studies generally use electrical stimulation of peripheral nerves to elicit potentials. SSEP testing determines whether peripheral sensory nerves are able to transmit sensory information like pain, temperature, and touch to the brain. Abnormal SSEPs can result from dysfunction at the level of the peripheral nerve, plexus, spinal root, spinal cord, brain stem, thalamocortical projections, or primary somatosensory cortex.

HP:0007378.label: Neoplasm of the gastrointestinal tract
HP:0007378.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the gastrointestinal tract.

HP:0007379.label: Neoplasm of the genitourinary tract
HP:0007379.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the genitourinary system.

HP:0007380.label: Facial telangiectasia
HP:0007380.definition: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin of the face.

HP:0007385.label: Aplasia cutis congenita of scalp
HP:0007385.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp.

HP:0007395.label: Postnatal-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma
HP:0007395.definition: A type of ichthyosiform erythroderma with postnatal onset.

HP:0007396.label: Early cutaneous photosensitivity
HP:0007396.definition: Photosensitivity of the skin occurring early in life.
exact_synonyms: Sun sensitivity occurring early in life

HP:0007397.label: Axillary apocrine gland hypoplasia
HP:0007397.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the apocrine sweat glands in the region of the axilla.

HP:0007401.label: Macular atrophy
HP:0007401.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells in the macula.

HP:0007402.label: Areas of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation that do not follow Blaschko lines

HP:0007404.label: Nonepidermolytic palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007404.definition: Abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles charactersized by hyperkeratosis of the stratum corneum with no evidence of epidermolysis characteristic of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

HP:0007407.label: Excessive skin wrinkling on dorsum of hands and fingers
exact_synonyms: Excessive skin wrinkling on back of hands and fingers

HP:0007408.label: Tegumentary leishmaniasis susceptibility
HP:0007408.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection by the protozan parasite of the genus Leishmania.

HP:0007409.label: obsolete Absence of subcutaneous fat over entire body except buttocks, hips, and thighs

HP:0007410.label: Palmoplantar hyperhidrosis
HP:0007410.definition: An abnormally increased perspiration on palms and soles.
exact_synonyms: Excessive sweating of palms and soles

HP:0007413.label: Nevus flammeus of the forehead
HP:0007413.definition: Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the forehead.

HP:0007414.label: Neonatal wrinkled skin of hands and feet
exact_synonyms: Wrinkled skin of hands and feet in newborn

HP:0007417.label: Discoid lupus rash
HP:0007417.definition: Cutaneous lesion that develops as a dry, scaly, red patch that evolves to an indurated and hyperpigmented plaque with adherent scale. Scarring may result in central white patches (loss of pigmentation) and skin atrophy.
HP:0007417.comment: This lesion is characteristic of discoid lupus erythematosus, but similar lesions may be observed in other diseases.

HP:0007420.label: Spontaneous hematomas
HP:0007420.definition: Spontaneous development of hematomas (hematoma) or bruises without significant trauma.

HP:0007421.label: Telangiectases of the cheeks
HP:0007421.definition: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin of the cheeks.

HP:0007428.label: Telangiectasia of the oral mucosa
HP:0007428.definition: Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the oral mucosa.
exact_synonyms: Spider veins of the oral mucosa
Angioectasia of the oral mucous membrane
Telangiectasia of the oral mucous membrane

HP:0007429.label: Few cafe-au-lait spots
HP:0007429.definition: The presence of two to five cafe-au-lait macules.

HP:0007430.label: Generalized edema
HP:0007430.definition: Generalized abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.

HP:0007431.label: Congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
HP:0007431.definition: An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin with congenital onset.

HP:0007434.label: Plaque-like facial hemangioma
HP:0007434.definition: Hemangioma is a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells. This term refers to facial hemangiomas that have a plaque-like morphology.

HP:0007437.label: Multiple cutaneous leiomyomas
HP:0007437.definition: The presence of multiple leiomyomas of the skin.

HP:0007438.label: Mottled pigmentation of the trunk and proximal extremities

HP:0007443.label: Partial albinism
HP:0007443.definition: Absence of melanin pigment in various areas, which is found at birth and is permanent. The lesions are known as leucoderma and are often found on the face, trunk, or limbs.
exact_synonyms: Congenital partial albinism on face, trunk, or limbs

HP:0007446.label: Palmoplantar blistering
HP:0007446.definition: A type of blistering that affects the skin of the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet.

HP:0007447.label: Diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007447.definition: Diffuse abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles.
HP:0007447.comment: The terms hyperkeratosis and keratoderma have been used interchangeably throughout the literature.

HP:0007450.label: Increased groin pigmentation with raindrop depigmentation

HP:0007451.label: Ipsilateral lack of facial sweating
HP:0007451.definition: Inability to sweat on the same side of the face that is affected by ptosis and miosis. This is a feature of Horner syndrome.

HP:0007453.label: Flexural lichenification
HP:0007453.definition: Lichenification affecting primarily flexural areas of the skin.
HP:0007453.comment: The parts of the skin that touch when a joint flexes (bends) are called the flexural surfaces.

HP:0007460.label: Autoamputation of digits
HP:0007460.definition: The spontaneous detachment of a digit (finger or toe) from the body due to long standing pathology.

HP:0007462.label: Bitot spots of the conjunctiva
HP:0007462.definition: Keratinization of the bulbar conjunctiva near the limbus (corneoscleral junction), resulting in a raised spot.
HP:0007462.comment: Bitot spots can be a feature of vitamin A deficiency.

HP:0007464.label: Sparse facial hair
HP:0007464.definition: Reduced number or density of facial hair.

HP:0007465.label: Honeycomb palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007465.definition: Abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles with an honeycomb pattern.

HP:0007468.label: Perifollicular hyperkeratosis
HP:0007468.definition: Increased amount of keratin (visible as white scales) surrounding hair follicles.

HP:0007469.label: Palmoplantar cutis gyrata
HP:0007469.definition: Cutis gyrata of palms and soles.
exact_synonyms: Cutis gyrata of palms and soles

HP:0007470.label: Periarticular subcutaneous nodules
HP:0007470.definition: Subcutaneous nodules that are located in the vicinity of joints.

HP:0007471.label: Axillary and groin hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation

HP:0007475.label: Congenital bullous ichthyosiform erythroderma
HP:0007475.definition: An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin that presents at birth or shortly thereafter with generalized erythema, blistering, erosions, and peeling. In the subsequent months, erythema and blistering improves but patients go on to develop hyperkeratotic scaling that is especially prominent along the joint flexures, neck, hands and feet.
HP:0007475.comment: Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis can refer to the disease caused by mutations in the genes keratin 1 or keratin 10, but is here used to refer to the characteristic skin manifestations as a phenotypic feature.

HP:0007477.label: Abnormal dermatoglyphics
HP:0007477.definition: An abnormality of dermatoglyphs (fingerprints), which are present on fingers, palms, toes, and soles.

HP:0007479.label: Congenital nonbullous ichthyosiform erythroderma
HP:0007479.definition: The term collodion baby applies to newborns who appear to have an extra layer of skin (known as a collodion membrane) that has a collodion-like quality. It is a descriptive term, not a specific diagnosis or disorder (as such, it is a syndrome). Affected babies are born in a collodion membrane, a shiny waxy outer layer to the skin. This is shed 10-14 days after birth, revealing the main symptom of the disease, extensive scaling of the skin caused by hyperkeratosis. With increasing age, the scaling tends to be concentrated around joints in areas such as the groin, the armpits, the inside of the elbow and the neck. The scales often tile the skin and may resemble fish scales.
HP:0007479.comment: A collodion membrane is characterized by thick scaling of the skin, frequently associated with fissures and hyperkeratosis. Also, eclabium and ectropion are often seen, as are contractures of fingers and toes. A collodion membrane is mainly associated with underlying congenital ichthyosis (congenital epidermal differentiation disorders).

HP:0007480.label: Decreased sweating due to autonomic dysfunction

HP:0007485.label: Absence of subcutaneous fat
exact_synonyms: Lack of fatty tissue below the skin

HP:0007489.label: Diffuse telangiectasia
HP:0007489.definition: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) with a diffuse localization.

HP:0007490.label: Linear arrays of macular hyperkeratoses in flexural areas

HP:0007494.label: Discrete 2 to 5-mm hyper- and hypopigmented macules

HP:0007497.label: Focal friction-related palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007497.definition: Hyperkeratosis affecting the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot in areas exposed to friction.

HP:0007499.label: Recurrent staphylococcal infections
HP:0007499.definition: Increased susceptibility to staphylococcal infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of staphylococcal infections.

HP:0007500.label: Decreased number of sweat glands
HP:0007500.definition: The presence of fewer than normal sweat glands.

HP:0007501.label: Streaks of hyperkeratosis along each finger onto the palm

HP:0007502.label: Follicular hyperkeratosis
HP:0007502.definition: A skin condition characterized by excessive development of keratin in hair follicles, resulting in rough, cone-shaped, elevated papules resulting from closure of hair follicles with a white plug of sebum.

HP:0007506.label: Congenital absence of skin of limbs
exact_synonyms: Missing skin on limbs since birth

HP:0007508.label: Punctate palmar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007508.definition: Tiny bumps of thickened skin (hyperkeratosis) on the palms of the hands.

HP:0007514.label: Edema of the dorsum of hands
HP:0007514.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the back of the hands.
exact_synonyms: Oedema of the dorsum of hands

HP:0007516.label: Redundant skin on fingers
HP:0007516.definition: Loose and sagging skin of the fingers.

HP:0007517.label: Palmoplantar cutis laxa
HP:0007517.definition: Loose, wrinkled skin of hands and feet.
exact_synonyms: Excessive wrinkled skin of palms and soles
Increased wrinkles of palms and soles
Wrinkled skin of hands and feet

HP:0007519.label: obsolete Lack of subcutaneous fatty tissue

HP:0007525.label: Yellow subcutaneous tissue covered by thin, scaly skin

HP:0007526.label: Hypopigmented skin patches on arms
exact_synonyms: Patchy loss of skin color on arms
Patchy loss of skin colour on arms

HP:0007534.label: Congenital posterior occipital alopecia
HP:0007534.definition: Loss of hair in the occipital region of the scalp with congenital onset.

HP:0007536.label: Aplasia cutis congenita of midline scalp vertex

HP:0007537.label: Severe photosensitivity
HP:0007537.definition: A severe degree of photosensitivity of the skin.

HP:0007541.label: Frontal cutaneous lipoma
HP:0007541.definition: Presence of a cutaneous lipoma on the forehead.

HP:0007542.label: Absent pigmentation of the ventral chest
HP:0007542.definition: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the anterior chest.

HP:0007544.label: Piebald skin depigmentation
HP:0007544.definition: Congenital large depigmented (white) macule of irergular rhomboid shape. Piebald skin depigmentation generally presents with multiple such macules in the affected individual. There may be smaller (5-15mm), discrete, skin-colored and hyperpigmented macules interspersed within the depigmented macules.
HP:0007544.comment: Piebaldism (OMIM:172800) generally is characterized by both Piebald skin depigmentation and White forelock, which should be coded separately.

HP:0007545.label: Congenital palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007545.definition: Abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles that is present at birth.

HP:0007548.label: obsolete Palmoplantar keratosis with erythema and scale

HP:0007549.label: Desquamation of skin soon after birth

HP:0007550.label: Hypohidrosis or hyperhidrosis
exact_synonyms: Lack of sweating or excessive sweating

HP:0007552.label: Abnormal subcutaneous fat tissue distribution
exact_synonyms: Abnormal fat tissue distribution below the skin

HP:0007554.label: Confetti hypopigmentation pattern of lower leg skin
exact_synonyms: Confetti hypopigmentation pattern of lower leg skin

HP:0007556.label: Plantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0007556.definition: Hyperkeratosis affecting the sole of the foot.

HP:0007561.label: obsolete Telangiectases in sun-exposed and nonexposed skin

HP:0007565.label: Multiple cafe-au-lait spots
HP:0007565.definition: The presence of six or more cafe-au-lait spots.

HP:0007569.label: Generalized seborrheic dermatitis
HP:0007569.definition: Seborrheic dermatitis that is not localized to any one particular region.

HP:0007570.label: Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans
HP:0007570.definition: Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans (HLP), also known as Flegel disease, is a keratinization abnormality characterized by small, asymptomatic erythematous papules that leave characteristic punctate bleeding when they become detached. The lesions generally occur symmetrically along the top of the foot and on the legs, appearing more rarely on the arms, forearms, palms, and soles, and even on the oral mucosa.

HP:0007573.label: Late onset atopic dermatitis
HP:0007573.definition: A form of atopic dermatitis with onset in adulthood characterized by atopic red face, chronic lichenified eczema on the trunk, subacute or psoriasiform dermatitis.

HP:0007576.label: Palmar neurofibroma
HP:0007576.definition: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the palm of the hand.

HP:0007588.label: Reticular hyperpigmentation
HP:0007588.definition: Increased pigmentation of the skin with a netlike (reticular) pattern.

HP:0007589.label: Aplasia cutis congenita on trunk or limbs
HP:0007589.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the trunk or the limbs.
HP:0007589.comment: In future versions of the HPO this term will be made obsolete and will be replaced by terms for Aplasia cutis congenita on trunk and a term for Aplasia cutis congenita on the limbs.

HP:0007590.label: Aplasia cutis congenita over posterior parietal area

HP:0007592.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the eccrine sweat glands
HP:0007592.definition: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the eccrine sweat glands.

HP:0007596.label: Painful subcutaneous lipomas
HP:0007596.definition: The presence of multiple subcutaneous lipoma that cause pain.
exact_synonyms: Painful noncancerous fat tissue tumour under the skin
Painful noncancerous fat tissue tumor under the skin

HP:0007598.label: Bilateral single transverse palmar creases
HP:0007598.definition: The distal and proximal transverse palmar creases are merged into a single transverse palmar crease on both hands.

HP:0007609.label: Hypoproteinemic edema
HP:0007609.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body because of decreased osmotic pressure of plasma (hypoproteinemia).

HP:0007613.label: Spinous keratoses of palms and soles

HP:0007616.label: Nevus flammeus nuchae
HP:0007616.definition: Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the neck. This is one of the most common birthmarks and present in approximately 25% of all newborns.
HP:0007616.comment: The salmon patch is the most common capillary malformation, occurring in up to 50% of all neonates. It is a pinkish macule that typically affects the back of the neck (stork bite) or the glabella (angel's kiss), although it can affect the eyelids, the nose, the upper lip, and the sacral area.

HP:0007618.label: Subcutaneous calcification
HP:0007618.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in subcutaneous tissue (i.e., the the lowermost layer of the integument).

HP:0007620.label: Cutaneous leiomyoma
HP:0007620.definition: The presence of leiomyoma of the skin.
HP:0007620.comment: Cutaneous leiomyomata are benign soft tissue neoplasms that arise from smooth muscle cells in the skin.

HP:0007627.label: Mandibular condyle aplasia
exact_synonyms: Underdevelopment of condylar process of mandible
related_synonyms: Agenesis of condylar process of mandible
Agenesis of condylar head of mandible
Agenesis of condylar neck of mandible

HP:0007628.label: Mandibular condyle hypoplasia
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of subcondylar region of mandible
Hypoplasia of condylar process of mandible
Decreased size of condylar process of mandible

HP:0007633.label: Bilateral microphthalmos
HP:0007633.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of both eyes.
exact_synonyms: Abnormally small eyeball on both sides

HP:0007634.label: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
HP:0007634.definition: An acute condition characterized by sudden visual loss (usually discovered in the morning), optic disc edema at onset, optic disc-related visual field defects. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy can be associated with flame hemorrhages on the swollen disk or nearby neuroretinal layer, and sometimes with nearby cotton-wool exudates.
HP:0007634.comment: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is caused by infarction of the laminar or retrolaminar portion of the optic nerve head supplied by the short posterior ciliary arteries. Clinically NAION is characterized by sudden, usually painless, loss of vision in one or both eyes. Examination findings include decreased visual acuity, a visual field defect, decreased color vision, a relative afferent pupillary defect, and optic disc swelling.

HP:0007641.label: Dyschromatopsia
HP:0007641.definition: A form of colorblindness in which only two of the three fundamental colors can be distinguished due to a lack of one of the retinal cone pigments.

HP:0007642.label: Early-onset non-progressive night blindness
HP:0007642.definition: A usually nonprogressive (i.e., stationary) form of night blindness with early (presumed to be congenital) onset.
HP:0007642.comment: Congenital stationary night blindness is the result of either dysfunction of the rod photoreceptors or synaptic transmission. This term was previously called Congenital stationary night blindness. The terms hemeralopia and nyctalopia are deliberately not used, as they mean different things in different languages. The fundus can be either normal or abnormal, such as fundus with white dots in fundus albipunctatus, or a golden sheen in light-adapted state in Oguchi disease, which disappears with dark-adaptation (Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon).

HP:0007643.label: Peripheral tractional retinal detachment
HP:0007643.definition: Tractional retinal detachment at the periphery of the retina.
exact_synonyms: Tractional retinal detachment at the periphery of the retina

HP:0007646.label: Absent lower eyelashes
HP:0007646.definition: Lack of eyelashes on the lower lid.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of lower eyelashes

HP:0007647.label: Congenital extraocular muscle anomaly
HP:0007647.definition: Congenital abnormality of the extraocular muscles.

HP:0007648.label: Punctate cataract
HP:0007648.definition: A type of cataract with punctate opacities of the lens.

HP:0007649.label: Congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
HP:0007649.definition: Sharply demarcated, congenital hyperpigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium. It can be solitary, clustered or multifocal, uni- or bilateral.
HP:0007649.comment: This feature is found in around 1-2% of the population and is of no functional significance.

HP:0007655.label: Eversion of lateral third of lower eyelids

HP:0007656.label: Lacrimal gland aplasia
HP:0007656.definition: A congenital defect of development characterized by absence of the lacrimal gland.

HP:0007657.label: Diffuse nuclear cataract
HP:0007657.definition: Opacity of the entire lens nucleus.

HP:0007659.label: obsolete Decreased retinal pigmentation with dispersion

HP:0007667.label: Peripheral cystoid retinal degeneration
HP:0007667.definition: Degenerative changes of the peripheral retina consisting of close-packed tiny cystic spaces at the outer plexiform/inner nuclear retinal level. The degeneration is common in adult eyes and starts adjacent to the ora serrata and extends circumferentially and posteriorly.

HP:0007670.label: Abnormal vestibulo-ocular reflex
HP:0007670.definition: An abnormality of the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR). The VOR attempts to keep the image stable on the retina. Ideally passive or active head movements in one direction are compensated for by eye movements of equal magnitude.

HP:0007677.label: Vitelliform macular lesion
HP:0007677.definition: Egg yolk-like (vitelliform) maculopathy is a lesion caused by the accumulation of material, often lipofuscin, in the subretinal space underlying the macula. Lesions may be singular or multiple, and may be either sharply or poorly demarcated.
HP:0007677.comment: Vitelliform macular lesions can be observed in Bestrophinopathies (Best vitelliform macular dystrophy and Autosomal recessive Bestrophinopathy), IMPG1 and IMPG2-related maculopathies, paraneoplastic or idiopathic vitelliform maculopathies, serous chorioretinopathy, dome-shaped maculopathy and toxic maculopathies (e.g. MEK-inhibitors induced).

HP:0007678.label: Lacrimal duct stenosis
HP:0007678.definition: Narrowing of a tear duct (lacrimal duct).

HP:0007686.label: Abnormal pupillary function
HP:0007686.definition: A functional abnormality of the pupil.
HP:0007686.comment: It is preferable to describe the functional defect precisely.

HP:0007688.label: Undetectable light- and dark-adapted electroretinogram
HP:0007688.definition: Absence of the combined rod-and-cone response on electroretinogram.
exact_synonyms: Absent cone and rod functions by electroretinogram
Absent rod-and cone-mediated responses on ERG

HP:0007695.label: Abnormal pupillary light reflex
HP:0007695.definition: An abnormality of the reflex that controls the diameter of the pupil, in response to the intensity of light that falls on the retina of the eye.

HP:0007700.label: Ocular anterior segment dysgenesis
HP:0007700.definition: Abnormal development (dysgenesis) of the anterior segment of the eye globe. These structures are mainly of mesenchymal origin.
HP:0007700.comment: In anterior segment mesenchymal ocular dysgenesis (ASMOD), multiple tissues are affected, including the iris, cornea, and lens as well as the Schlemm's canal and trabecular meshwork drainage structures located at the anterior segment angle where the iris and cornea meet. These abnormalities may result from a primary defect in the migration and/or differentiation of the mesenchymal cells that contribute to development of the cornea, iris, and drainage structures.

HP:0007703.label: Abnormal retinal pigmentation
HP:0007703.definition: Any deviation from the normal pigmentation of the retina.
HP:0007703.comment: This includes abnormalities of the pigmentation of the RPE and intraretinal pigment migration. An abnormality of the retina characterized by pigment deposition. It is typically associated with migration and proliferation of macrophages or retinal pigment epithelial cells into the neuroretina; melanin from these cells causes the pigmentary changes. Pigmentary retinopathy is a common final pathway of many retinal conditions and is often associated with visual loss.
related_synonyms: Abnormality of the retinal pigment epithelium

HP:0007704.label: Paroxysmal involuntary eye movements
HP:0007704.definition: Sudden-onset episode of abnormal, involuntary eye movements.

HP:0007707.label: Congenital aphakia
HP:0007707.definition: Absence of the crystalline lens of the eye as a result of a developmental defect.

HP:0007709.label: Band-shaped corneal dystrophy
HP:0007709.definition: A type of genetically determined disease of the cornea with corneal lesions with a band-like shape.

HP:0007716.label: Uveal melanoma
HP:0007716.definition: A malignant melanoma originating within the eye. The tumor originates from the melanocytes in the uvea (which comprises the iris, ciliary body, and choroid).
HP:0007716.comment: WIth intraocular melanoma, the melanoma originates from melanocytic cells in the uveal layer, comprising the iris, ciliary body, and choroid.

HP:0007717.label: Chronic irritative conjunctivitis
HP:0007717.definition: A chronic irritative conjunctivitis, which commonly presents with general irritation and redness of the eyes, with a burning, dry, or foreign-body sensation of the eyes.

HP:0007720.label: Flat cornea
HP:0007720.definition: Cornea plana is an abnormally flat shape of the cornea such that the normal protrusion of the cornea from the sclera is missing. The reduced corneal curvature can lead to hyperopia, and a hazy corneal limbus and arcus lipoides may develop at an early age.

HP:0007721.label: Saccular conjunctival dilatations
HP:0007721.definition: Presence of multiple dilatations (sac-like outpouchings) in the blood vessels of the conjunctiva.

HP:0007722.label: Retinal pigment epithelial atrophy
HP:0007722.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE).

HP:0007727.label: Opacification of the corneal epithelium
HP:0007727.definition: Lack of transparency of the corneal epithelium.

HP:0007728.label: Congenital miosis
HP:0007728.definition: Abnormal (non-physiological) constriction of the pupil of congenital onset.

HP:0007730.label: Iris hypopigmentation
HP:0007730.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of pigmentation of the iris.

HP:0007731.label: Chorioretinal dysplasia
HP:0007731.definition: Abnormal development of the choroid and retina.

HP:0007737.label: Spicular pigmentation of the retina
HP:0007737.definition: Pigment migration into the retina in a bone-spicule configuration (resembling the nucleated cells within the lacuna of bone).
HP:0007737.comment: Spicular pigmentation of the retina is typically associated with migration of microglia or retinal pigment epithelial cells into the neuroretina secondary to photoreceptor cell death; melanin from these cells causes the pigmentary changes.
exact_synonyms: Bone spicule pigmentation of the retina

HP:0007754.label: Macular dystrophy
HP:0007754.definition: Macular dystrophy is a nonspecific term for retinal degeneration, generally confined to the macula, usually presumed of genetic origin.

HP:0007756.label: obsolete Slitlike anterior chamber angles in children

HP:0007759.label: Opacification of the corneal stroma
HP:0007759.definition: Reduced transparency of the stroma of cornea.

HP:0007761.label: Pericentral scotoma
HP:0007761.definition: A scotoma (area of diminished vision within the visual field) that surrounds the central fixation point.

HP:0007763.label: Retinal telangiectasia
HP:0007763.definition: Localized, irregular dilatation of small tortuous intraretinal blood vessels.

HP:0007765.label: Deep anterior chamber
HP:0007765.definition: Increased depth of the anterior chamber, i.e., the anteroposterior distance between the cornea and the iris is increased.
HP:0007765.comment: Deep anterior chamber can be seen in disorders such as congenital microphakia and buphthalmos.

HP:0007766.label: Optic disc hypoplasia
HP:0007766.definition: Underdevelopment of the optic disc, that is of the optic nerve head, where ganglion cell axons exit the eye to form the optic nerve.

HP:0007768.label: Central retinal vessel vascular tortuosity
HP:0007768.definition: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of retinal blood vessels (arteries, arterioles, veins, venules).

HP:0007769.label: Peripheral retinal degeneration
HP:0007769.definition: Progressive loss of peripheral retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and/or neurosensory retinal cells.

HP:0007772.label: Impaired smooth pursuit
HP:0007772.definition: An impairment of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.

HP:0007773.label: Vitreoretinopathy
HP:0007773.definition: Ocular abnormality characterized by premature degeneration of the vitreous and the retina that may be associated with increased risk of retinal detachment.

HP:0007777.label: Chorioretinal scar
HP:0007777.definition: Fibrous connective tissue resulting from incomplete healing of a wound (i.e., a scar) located in the choroid and retina or the eye.

HP:0007778.label: Posterior retinal neovascularization
HP:0007778.definition: A type of retinal neovascularization that affects the posterior pole of the retina.
exact_synonyms: Neovascularization of peripheral and posterior retina

HP:0007780.label: Cortical pulverulent cataract
HP:0007780.definition: A type of cataract characterized by punctate, dust-like opacities within the cortical region of the lens.

HP:0007783.label: obsolete Butterfly retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy

HP:0007787.label: Posterior subcapsular cataract
HP:0007787.definition: A type of cataract affecting the posterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to ('beneath') the Lens capsule.
exact_synonyms: Posterior subcapsular opacities of the lens

HP:0007791.label: Patchy atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium
HP:0007791.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) that occurs in small, isolated areas.

HP:0007793.label: Granular macular appearance
HP:0007793.definition: Mottled (spotted or blotched with different shades) pigmentary abnormality of the macula.

HP:0007795.label: Anterior cortical cataract
HP:0007795.definition: A cataract that affects the anterior part of the cortex of the lens.

HP:0007797.label: Developmental retinal vascular malformation
HP:0007797.definition: A group of development abnormalities of retinal blood vessels.

HP:0007799.label: Conjunctival whitish salt-like deposits
HP:0007799.definition: The presence of whitish deposits in the conjunctiva resembling salt. May be related to calcinosis.

HP:0007800.label: Increased axial length of the globe
HP:0007800.definition: Abnormal largeness of the eye with an axial length > 2.5 standard deviations from population mean.
exact_synonyms: Increased front to back length of eyeball

HP:0007802.label: Granular corneal dystrophy
HP:0007802.definition: The presence of central, fine, whitish granular lesions in the stroma of the cornea. This type of corneal dystrophy is usually asymptomatic and begins in childhood and shows a slow progression. Later in the course, the corneal epithelium and Bowman's layer may be affected. Histologically, the cornea shows a uniform deposition of hyaline material.

HP:0007803.label: Monochromacy
HP:0007803.definition: Complete color blindness, a complete inability to distinguish colors. Affected persons cannot perceive colors, but only shades of gray.
HP:0007803.comment: Rod monochromacy is the condition of having only rods in the retina. A rod monochromat is truly unable to see any color and can see only shades of gray.

HP:0007811.label: Horizontal pendular nystagmus
HP:0007811.definition: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements of equal velocity.
HP:0007811.comment: Pendular nystagmus refers to the situation in which the eye appeared to oscillate with equal speed in either direction, in contrast to jerk nystagmus, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.

HP:0007812.label: Herpetiform corneal ulceration
HP:0007812.definition: The presence of one or more dendritic corneal epithelial ulcers characterized by a treelike branching linear pattern with feathery edges and terminal bulbs. Herpetiform corneal ulcers can be identified by fluorescein staining.

HP:0007813.label: Nongranulomatous uveitis
HP:0007813.definition: A form of uveitis that is not associated with the formation of granulomas.

HP:0007814.label: Retinal pigment epithelial mottling
HP:0007814.definition: Mottling (spots or blotches of different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium, i.e., localized or generalized fundus pigment granularity associated with processes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium.
exact_synonyms: Focal hypopigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium

HP:0007815.label: Abnormal distribution of retinal arterioles and venules

HP:0007817.label: Horizontal supranuclear gaze palsy
HP:0007817.definition: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a horizontal direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.

HP:0007818.label: Central heterochromia
HP:0007818.definition: The presence of distinct colors in the central (pupillary) zone of the iris than in the mid-peripheral (ciliary) zone.

HP:0007819.label: Presenile cataracts
HP:0007819.definition: Presenile cataract is a kind of cataract that occurs in early adulthood, that is, at an age that is younger than usual.
HP:0007819.comment: Presenile cataract is rare. Some cases have a hereditary cause; others result from trauma or chromosomal, endocrine, metabolic, or systemic disorders. Many cases are idiopathic. The term 'presenile' is used differently in the literature. The HPO defines it to mean a cataract that is diagnosed after the age of 20 years but before old age.

HP:0007820.label: Lacrimal punctal atresia
HP:0007820.definition: Congenital absence or closure of the opening of the lacrimal punctum.

HP:0007824.label: Total ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007824.definition: Paralysis of both the extrinsic and intrinsic ocular muscles.

HP:0007825.label: obsolete Cataracts develop in second or third decade

HP:0007830.label: Adult-onset night blindness
HP:0007830.definition: Inability to see well at night or in poor light with onset in adulthood.

HP:0007831.label: Nonprogressive restrictive external ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007831.definition: Nonprogressive restriction of movement of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position. Residual eye movements are significantly limited.

HP:0007834.label: Progressive cataract
HP:0007834.definition: A kind of cataract that progresses with age.

HP:0007840.label: Long upper eyelashes
HP:0007840.definition: Increased length of the upper eyelashes.

HP:0007841.label: Amyloid deposition in the vitreous humor
HP:0007841.definition: Deposition of hyaline extracellular material (amyloid) into the vitreous humor, which can manifest as vitreous opacities and reduced visual acuity.
exact_synonyms: Amyloid deposition in the vitreous humour

HP:0007843.label: Attenuation of retinal blood vessels
HP:0007843.definition: Narrowing of the retinal blood vessels, both arterioles and venules.
HP:0007843.comment: Attenuation of retinal blood vessels is commonly seen in conditions with reduced photoreceptor cell metabolism and intact choroid, such as Retinitis Pigmentosa or vitamin A deficiency, or loss of inner retina, such as after central retinal artery occlusion. Narrowing may also be seen in accelerated hypertension and chronic hypertension.
exact_synonyms: Narrowing of blood vessels in back of eye

HP:0007856.label: Punctate opacification of the cornea
HP:0007856.definition: Punctate opacification (reduced transparency) of the corneal stroma.

HP:0007858.label: Chorioretinal lacunae
HP:0007858.definition: Punched out lesions in the pigmented layer of the retina.
HP:0007858.comment: A chorioretinal lacuna can have the appearance of a pseudodisk in the retina.

HP:0007859.label: Congenital horizontal nystagmus
HP:0007859.definition: Horizontal nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

HP:0007862.label: Retinal calcification
HP:0007862.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in the retina.
HP:0007862.comment: Retinal calcium deposits can be observed in pseudoxanthoma elasticum, retinoblastoma, calcified druse,n and phthisical eyes.

HP:0007867.label: Restrictive partial external ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007867.definition: Fibrosis of only some of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position.

HP:0007872.label: Choroidal hemangioma
HP:0007872.definition: Benign choroidal tumour, seen in the fundus as a reddish or orange choroidal lesion and usually associated with cystoid edema, and less commonly with Subretinal fluid.
HP:0007872.comment: Choroidal hemangiomas can cause hyperopia or other visual symptoms such as blurred or distorted vision. Some choroidal hemangiomas are asymptomatic, and only diagnosed after angiography. Diffuse choroidal hemangioma is seen associated with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

HP:0007874.label: Almond-shaped palpebral fissure
HP:0007874.definition: A shape created by an acute downward arching of the upper eyelid and upward arching of the lower eyelid, toward the medial canthus, which gives the outline of the palpebral fissures the configuration of an almond. Thus, the maximum distance between the fissures is offset from, and medial to, the center point.
HP:0007874.comment: The almond configuration tends to dissipate with time, as the surrounding tissues (e.g., eyelid, nasal bridge) grow.

HP:0007879.label: Allergic conjunctivitis
HP:0007879.definition: Allergic Conjunctivitis is an allergic inflammation of the conjunctiva.

HP:0007885.label: Slowed horizontal saccades
HP:0007885.definition: An abnormally slow velocity of horizontal saccadic eye movements.
HP:0007885.comment: Saccades are rapid eye movements that align the fovea with the target.

HP:0007886.label: Absent extraocular muscles
HP:0007886.definition: Congenital absence of the extraocular muscles.

HP:0007889.label: Iridescent posterior subcapsular cataract
HP:0007889.definition: A type of posterior subcapsular cataract characterized by an iridescent color.

HP:0007894.label: Fundus hypopigmentation
HP:0007894.definition: Generalized or focal reduced pigmentation of the fundus, evaluated in the context of skin and hair color. Fundoscopy may reveal a low level pigment.
HP:0007894.comment: Fundus hypopigmentation is consistently observed in albinism. Pigmentation is also reduced with age in some individuals, high myopia, and in chronic inflammation, such as Harada disease. Ocular pigmentation is essential for normal vision, and persons with ocular albinism tend to have severely reduced visual acuity often associated with nystagmus, strabismus, and photophobia.

HP:0007899.label: Retinal nonattachment
HP:0007899.definition: Failure of attachment of the retina during development.

HP:0007902.label: Vitreous hemorrhage
HP:0007902.definition: Bleeding within the vitreous compartment of the eye.
HP:0007902.comment: The most common causes include proliferative diabetic retinopathy, vitreous detachment with or without retinal breaks, and trauma. Less common causes include vascular occlusive disease, retinal arterial macroaneurysm, hemoglobinopathies, age-related macular degeneration, intraocular tumors, and others.

HP:0007903.label: Paravenous chorioretinal atrophy
HP:0007903.definition: Chorioretinal atrophy along the retinal veins.

HP:0007906.label: Ocular hypertension
HP:0007906.definition: Intraocular pressure that is 2 standard deviations above the population mean.

HP:0007911.label: Congenital bilateral ptosis
exact_synonyms: Congenital drooping of both upper eyelids

HP:0007913.label: Reticular retinal dystrophy
HP:0007913.definition: A type of of patterned retinal dystrophy that shows a reticular pattern of pigmentation.

HP:0007915.label: Polymorphous posterior corneal dystrophy
HP:0007915.definition: This corneal dystrophy affects the posterior limiting membrane of the cornea and is characterized by polymorphous plaques of calcium deposits in the deep stromal layers of the cornea, and occasionally by vesicular lesions of the endothelium and edema of the deep corneal stroma.

HP:0007916.label: obsolete Small anterior lens surface opacities

HP:0007917.label: Tractional retinal detachment
HP:0007917.definition: A type of retinal detachment arising due to a combination of contracting retinal membranes, abnormal vitreoretinal adhesions, and vitreous changes, in the absence of a full-thickness retinal defect.
HP:0007917.comment: Tractional retinal detachment can be seen in the context of diseases that induce a fibrovascular response, e.g. diabetes or conditions associated with abnormal vitreoretinal adhesions. This can be in the posterior pole and the retinal periphery

HP:0007922.label: Hypermyelinated retinal nerve fibers
HP:0007922.definition: Myelinated retinal nerve fiber (MRNF) layer is a rare and mostly benign congenital anomaly in which the retinal nerve fibers anterior to the lamina cribrosa have a myelin sheath.

HP:0007924.label: Slow decrease in visual acuity
exact_synonyms: Slow decrease in sharpness of vision

HP:0007925.label: Lacrimal duct aplasia
HP:0007925.definition: A congenital defect resulting in absence of the lacrimal duct.

HP:0007928.label: Abnormal flash visual evoked potentials
HP:0007928.definition: Anomaly of the visual evoked potentials elicited by a flash stimulus, generally a flash of light subtending an angle of at least 20 degrees of the visual field and presented in a dimly lit room.

HP:0007929.label: Peripheral retinal detachment
HP:0007929.definition: Separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium occurring near the outer limit (periphery) of the retina.

HP:0007932.label: Bilateral congenital mydriasis
HP:0007932.definition: Congenital abnormal dilation of the pupil on both sides.

HP:0007933.label: Broad lateral eyebrow
HP:0007933.definition: Regional increase in the width (height) of the lateral eyebrow.

HP:0007936.label: Restrictive external ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007936.definition: Fibrosis of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position. Residual eye movements are significantly limited.

HP:0007937.label: Reticular pigmentary degeneration
HP:0007937.definition: A pattern of peripheral netlike retinal pigmentation that forms a polygonal arrangement of hyperpigmented lines forming geometric patterns in the fundus.

HP:0007939.label: Blue cone monochromacy
HP:0007939.definition: A form of monochromacy in which vision is derived from the remaining preserved blue (S) cones and rod photoreceptors.

HP:0007941.label: Limited extraocular movements
HP:0007941.definition: Limited mobility of the eye within its socket.

HP:0007942.label: Internal ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007942.definition: Paralysis of the iris and ciliary apparatus.
HP:0007942.comment: Paralysis of the internal ocular muscles, the iris and ciliary apparatus.

HP:0007943.label: Congenital stapes ankylosis
HP:0007943.definition: A form of stapes ankylosis with congenital onset.

HP:0007946.label: Unilateral narrow palpebral fissure
HP:0007946.definition: A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures on one side only.
related_synonyms: Unequal size of opening between the eyelids

HP:0007947.label: Pericentral retinitis pigmentosa
HP:0007947.definition: A subtype of retinitis pigmentosa in which, instead of the pathology starting in the mid-periphery like typical retinitis pigmentosa, the disease starts in the near periphery closer to the vascular arcades and tends to spare the far periphery.

HP:0007948.label: Dense posterior cortical cataract
HP:0007948.definition: A type of posterior cortical cataract characterized by dense lenticular opacities.

HP:0007950.label: Peripapillary chorioretinal atrophy
HP:0007950.definition: Chorioretinal atrophy concentrated around the optic papilla (i.e., the optic nerve head).

HP:0007957.label: Corneal opacity
exact_synonyms: Scarring or clouding of the cornea of the eye

HP:0007958.label: Optic atrophy from cranial nerve compression

HP:0007963.label: Pattern dystrophy of the retina
HP:0007963.definition: A spectrum of fundoscopic appearances characterized by the development of a variety of patterns of deposits predominantly in the macular area. The deposits are typically bilateral, relatively symmetrical, yellow/white and associated with changes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium. With time, retinal atrophy may occur. A number of pattern dystrophy subtypes have been described including butterfly-shaped dystrophy, reticular dystrophy (net-like pattern) and fundus pulverulentus (granular, mottled pigmentation).

HP:0007968.label: Remnants of the hyaloid vascular system
HP:0007968.definition: Persistence of the hyaloid artery, which is the embryonic artery that runs from the optic disc to the posterior lens capsule may persist; the site of attachment may form an opacity. The hyaloid artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery, and usually regresses completely before birth. This features results from a failure of regression of the hyaloid vessel, which supplies the primary vitreous during embryogenesis and normally regresses in the third trimester of pregnancy, leading to a particular form of posterior cataract.
exact_synonyms: Persistent posterior foetal fibrovascular sheath of the lens
Persistent posterior fetal fibrovascular sheath of the lens

HP:0007971.label: Lamellar cataract
HP:0007971.definition: A congenital cataract in which opacity is limited to layers of the lens external to the nucleus (i.e., the perinuclear region), i.e., between the nuclear and cortical layers of the lens.

HP:0007973.label: Retinal dysplasia
HP:0007973.definition: Abnormal growth and differentiation, structure and appearance of the retina present from birth.
HP:0007973.comment: This feature is a congenital developmental anomaly of the retina characterized by abnormal growth and differentiation. The retina contains numerous tubular structures and rosettes. Retinal dysplasia (synonym: retinal dysgenesis) is often accompanied by retinal detachment and micropthalmos, but the latter features should be coded separately.

HP:0007975.label: Hypometric horizontal saccades
HP:0007975.definition: Saccadic undershoot of horizontal saccadic eye movements, i.e., a horizontal saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

HP:0007976.label: Cerulean cataract
HP:0007976.definition: Cerulean cataracts are a kind of congenital cataract having peripheral bluish and white opacifications in concentric layers with occasional central lesions arranged radially. Although the opacities may be observed during fetal development and childhood, usually visual acuity is only mildly reduced until adulthood, when lens extraction is generally necessary.

HP:0007979.label: Gaze-evoked horizontal nystagmus
HP:0007979.definition: Horizontal nystagmus made apparent by looking to the right or to the left.

HP:0007980.label: Absent retinal pigment epithelium
HP:0007980.definition: Discrete areas of pallor in which the pigment epithelium, choriocapillaris and choroidal pigment are absent.
HP:0007980.comment: Absence of the retinal pigment epithelium occurs in a number of monogenic disorders, such as choroideremia, gyrate atrophy, and Bietti chorioretinal dystrophy.

HP:0007981.label: obsolete Concentric narrowing of visual field

HP:0007984.label: Electronegative electroretinogram
HP:0007984.definition: A dark-adapted bright flash electroretinogram in which the b-wave that is of markedly lower amplitude than the associated a-wave (source: Holder GE., Inherited Chorioretinal Dystrophies: A Textbook and Atlas; 2014; p.17; ISBN 978-3-540-69466-3).
HP:0007984.comment: Flashes will elicit an a-wave with an initial negative deflection followed by a b-wave with positive deflection. This feature refers to a reduction in the amplitude primarily of the b-wave.
exact_synonyms: Reduced amplitude of dark-adapted bright flash electroretinogram b-wave

HP:0007985.label: Retinal arteriolar occlusion
HP:0007985.definition: Blockage of retinal arteriole, generally associated with interruption of blood flow and oxygen delivery to affected regions of the retina. This can affect the inner or mid-retinal structures.
HP:0007985.comment: This can be due to embolic, inflammatory, or hyperviscosity disorders. This can be associated with Cotton wool spots. It is often referred to as Branch retinal artery occlusion.

HP:0007988.label: Macular hypopigmentation
HP:0007988.definition: Decreased amount of pigmentation in the macula.

HP:0007989.label: Intraretinal exudate
HP:0007989.definition: Retinal exudate within the retinal tissue itself.

HP:0007990.label: Hypoplastic iris stroma
HP:0007990.definition: Underdevelopment of the stroma of iris.

HP:0007992.label: Lattice retinal degeneration
HP:0007992.definition: A pattern of white lines and dots in the far periphery of the retina.

HP:0007993.label: Malformed lacrimal duct
HP:0007993.definition: Congenital malformation of the lacrimal duct associated with incomplete development of the bony nasolacrimal canal or craniofacial anomalies.

HP:0007994.label: Peripheral visual field loss
HP:0007994.definition: Loss of peripheral vision with retention of central vision, resulting in a constricted circular tunnel-like field of vision.

HP:0008000.label: Decreased corneal reflex
HP:0008000.definition: An abnormally reduced response to stimulation of the cornea (by touch, foreign body, blowing air). The corneal reflex (also known as the blink reflex, normally results in an involuntary blinking of the eyelids.

HP:0008001.label: Foveal hyperpigmentation
HP:0008001.definition: Increased amount of pigmentation in the fovea.

HP:0008002.label: Abnormal macular pigmentation
HP:0008002.definition: Any deviation from the normal, uniform distribution or appearance of pigment within the macular region of the retina.

HP:0008011.label: Peripheral opacification of the cornea
HP:0008011.definition: Reduced transparency of the peripheral region of the cornea.

HP:0008017.label: obsolete Depigmented lesions of the retinal pigment epithelium

HP:0008019.label: Superior lens subluxation
HP:0008019.definition: Partial dislocation of the lens in a superior direction.

HP:0008028.label: Cystoid macular degeneration
HP:0008028.definition: A form of macular degeneration characterized by the presence of multiple cystoid spaces in the macula.

HP:0008031.label: Posterior Y-sutural cataract
HP:0008031.definition: A type of sutural cataract in which the opacity follows the posterior Y suture.

HP:0008035.label: Retinitis pigmentosa inversa
HP:0008035.definition: Retinitis pigmentosa inversa is form of retinal degeneration characterized by areas of retinal/chorioretinal degeneration with pigment migration in the macular area (in contrast to retinitis pigmentosa which, at early disease stages, predominantly affects the retinal periphery).

HP:0008037.label: Absent anterior chamber of the eye
HP:0008037.definition: Absence of the anterior chamber of the eye owing to a developmental defect.

HP:0008038.label: Aplastic/hypoplastic lacrimal glands
HP:0008038.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the lacrimal gland.

HP:0008043.label: Focal retinal arteriolar constriction
HP:0008043.definition: Focal decreased retinal arteriolar diameters, which may decrease blood flow and slow oxygen delivery to regions of the retina.
HP:0008043.comment: Usually after the first branch, the retinal arteries contain no elastic fibers and the term retinal arteriole is more appropriate. The main changes seen in diseases such as hypertension affect mainly the retinal arterioles rather than the retinal artery.

HP:0008046.label: Abnormal retinal vascular morphology
HP:0008046.definition: A structural abnormality of retinal vasculature.

HP:0008047.label: Abnormality of the vasculature of the eye

HP:0008048.label: Abnormal line of Schwalbe morphology
HP:0008048.definition: An abnormality of the line of Schwalbe.
HP:0008048.comment: Schwalbe's line is the anatomical line found on the posterior surface of the cornea, delineating the outer limit of the corneal endothelium layer.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the line of Schwalbe

HP:0008049.label: Abnormality of the extraocular muscles
HP:0008049.definition: An abnormality of an extraocular muscle.
HP:0008049.comment: There are six extraocular muscles that control the movements of the eye.

HP:0008050.label: Abnormality of the palpebral fissures
HP:0008050.definition: An anomaly of the space between the medial and lateral canthi of the two open eyelids.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the opening between the eyelids

HP:0008051.label: obsolete Abnormality of the retinal pigment epithelium

HP:0008052.label: Retinal fold
HP:0008052.definition: A wrinkle of retinal tissue projecting outward from the surface of the retina and visible as a line on fundoscopy.

HP:0008053.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the iris
HP:0008053.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the iris.

HP:0008054.label: Abnormal morphology of the conjunctival vasculature
HP:0008054.definition: Any abnormality of the blood vessels of the conjunctiva.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the vasculature of the conjunctiva
Abnormal vasculature of the conjunctiva morphology
Abnormal morphology of the conjunctiva vasculature

HP:0008055.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the uvea
HP:0008055.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the uvea, the pigmented middle layer of the eye consisting of the iris and ciliary body together with the choroid.

HP:0008057.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the fundus
HP:0008057.definition: A developmental defect characterized by lack of development or underdevelopment of the fundus/fovea.

HP:0008060.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fovea
HP:0008060.definition: Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the fovea.

HP:0008062.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the anterior segment of the eye
HP:0008062.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the anterior segment of the eye.

HP:0008063.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the lens
HP:0008063.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the lens.

HP:0008064.label: Ichthyosis
HP:0008064.definition: An abnormality of the skin characterized the presence of excessive amounts of dry surface scales on the skin resulting from an abnormality of keratinization.
HP:0008064.comment: The ichthyoses are a group of skin diseases characterized by drying and scaling of skin with the accumulation of thick scales and cracks that may be painful or bleed. The abnormality in ichthyosis lies in am imbalance in the normal lifecycle of skin in which growth is matched with dying and shedding of skin cells. In ichthyosis, skin cells reproduce at a rate faster than dead skin cells can be shed or reproduce at a normal rate with a reduction in the rate of shedding. Either abnormality leads to a build up of dry and scaly skin. Note that this term refers to the morphological abnormality of the skin and not the disorder. Ichthyosis can have a congenital onset or be acuqired, e.g., paraneoplastic ichthyosis.

HP:0008066.label: Abnormal blistering of the skin
HP:0008066.definition: The presence of one or more bullae on the skin, defined as fluid-filled blisters more than 5 mm in diameter with thin walls.
HP:0008066.comment: A bulla is a large vesicle described as a rounded or irregularly shaped blister containing serous or seropurulent fluid, equal to or greater than 10mm. In approaching blistering diseases, there are 3 fundamental criteria to consider: (1) the site or level of the blister (or the lowest level of vesiculation): subcorneal, midepidermis, suprabasal, subepidermal; (2) the findings that implicate the mechanism of blister formation (spongiosis, acantholysis, blistering degeneration, or epidermolysis); and (3) the type of inflammation (neutrophilic, lymphocytic, eosinophilic, mixed), if present.

HP:0008069.label: Neoplasm of the skin
HP:0008069.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the skin.

HP:0008070.label: Sparse hair
HP:0008070.comment: This term applies if the number of hair shafts per unit area is reduced. The term fine hair is used to describe hair with a reduced diameter.

HP:0008071.label: Maternal hypertension
HP:0008071.definition: Increased blood pressure during a pregnancy.

HP:0008072.label: Maternal virilization in pregnancy
HP:0008072.definition: Virilization (deepening of voice, facial hirsutism and scalp hair loss) with onset during pregnancy (usually towards the end of the first trimester) and regression several months post-partum.

HP:0008073.label: Low maternal circulating estriol concentration
HP:0008073.definition: An abnormally low concentration of serum conjugated estriol as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

HP:0008076.label: Osteoporotic tarsals
HP:0008076.definition: Reduction in bone mineral density affecting any or all of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

HP:0008079.label: Absent fifth metatarsal
HP:0008079.definition: A developmental abnormality characterized by the absence of the fifth metatarsal bone.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone

HP:0008080.label: Hallux varus
HP:0008080.definition: Medial deviation of the great toe owing to a deformity of the great toe joint causing the hallux to deviate medially.

HP:0008081.label: Pes valgus
HP:0008081.definition: An outward deviation of the foot at the talocalcaneal or subtalar joint.
HP:0008081.comment: Valgus refers to the twisting outward of a bone or joint is twisted outward from the center of the body, whereas varus is a twisting toward the center of the body.

HP:0008087.label: Nonossified fifth metatarsal
HP:0008087.definition: The presence of a fifth metatarsal bone that has not undergone ossification at an age when ossification is usually visible.

HP:0008089.label: Abnormality of the fifth metatarsal bone
HP:0008089.definition: An anomaly of the fifth metatarsal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 5th long bone of foot

HP:0008094.label: Widely spaced toes
HP:0008094.definition: An overall widening of the spaces between the digits.
HP:0008094.comment: This description is based on the width of the gap between the toes. It is usually used when the width of the toes remains normal rather than to describe a situation where the toes are thin or narrow. This term should not be used for the situation where the finding is limited to a gap between T1,2 (see Sandal gap).

HP:0008096.label: Medially deviated second toe
HP:0008096.definition: Medial deviation of the second toe.

HP:0008102.label: Expanded metatarsals with widened medullary cavities

HP:0008103.label: Delayed tarsal ossification
HP:0008103.definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

HP:0008107.label: Plantar crease between first and second toes
HP:0008107.definition: The presence of unusually deep creases (ridges/wrinkles) on the skin of sole of foot located between the first and second toe.

HP:0008108.label: Advanced tarsal ossification
HP:0008108.definition: Precocious (accelerated) maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

HP:0008112.label: Plantar flexion contracture
HP:0008112.definition: A type of contracture in which the plantar flexion muscles are contracted.
HP:0008112.comment: Plantar flexion is the movement of the top of the foot away from the leg in a downward motion. With plantar flexion contracture, the abiliuty to passively or actively move the tip of the toe back closer to the leg is limited.

HP:0008114.label: Metatarsal diaphyseal endosteal sclerosis
HP:0008114.definition: Osteosclerosis of the endosteal surface of the diaphyses (shafts) of the metatarsal bones.

HP:0008115.label: Clinodactyly of the 3rd toe
HP:0008115.definition: Bending or curvature of a third toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

HP:0008116.label: Flexion limitation of toes
HP:0008116.definition: Limitation of the ability to bend the toes.

HP:0008122.label: Calcaneonavicular fusion
HP:0008122.definition: Synostosis of the calcaneus with the navicular bone.

HP:0008124.label: Talipes calcaneovarus
HP:0008124.definition: A congenital deformity characterized by a dorsiflexed, inverted, and adducted foot, i.e., a combination of talipes calcaneus and talipes varus.

HP:0008127.label: Bipartite calcaneus
HP:0008127.definition: A two-part calcaneus, a finding that probably results from delayed coalescence of two primary calcaneal centers of ossification.
exact_synonyms: Delayed coalescence of calcaneal ossification centers
Delayed coalescence of calcaneal ossification centres

HP:0008131.label: Tarsal stippling
HP:0008131.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more tarsal bones.

HP:0008132.label: Medial rotation of the medial malleolus
HP:0008132.definition: Hindfoot valgus (posterior part of the foot turns outward) in combination with forefoot abduction (front part of the foot (the forefoot) is angled outwards away from the midline of the body, relative to the hindfoot) and lowering of the midfoot.
HP:0008132.comment: In the context of Marfan syndrome, this anomaly is sometimes referred to as hindfoot deformity, but in general, the term hindfoot deformity is also used to describe other findings.

HP:0008134.label: Irregular tarsal ossification
HP:0008134.definition: Defective ossification in an irregular pattern of the seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

HP:0008138.label: Equinus calcaneus
HP:0008138.definition: Abnormal plantar flexion of the calcaneus relative to the longitudinal axis of the tibia. This results in the angle between the long axis of the tibia and the long axis of the heel bone (calcaneus) being greater than 90 degrees.

HP:0008142.label: Delayed calcaneal ossification
HP:0008142.definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of the calcaneus.

HP:0008148.label: Impaired epinephrine-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0008148.definition: Abnormal response to epinephrine as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of epinephrine.

HP:0008150.label: Elevated serum transaminases during infections
HP:0008150.definition: Elevations of the levels of SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) that occur during infections.

HP:0008151.label: Prolonged prothrombin time
HP:0008151.definition: Increased time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.
HP:0008151.comment: The prothrombin time (PT) and the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) are the most requested tests to investigate patients with congenital or acquired coagulopathies and drug monitoring. They are defined as the time (seconds) needed to clot platelet-poor plasma upon addition of coagulation triggers, such as tissue factor in complex with phospholipids and calcium chloride (in the PT), or negatively charged phospholipids-activators and calcium chloride (in the APTT). They can hence be considered as global coagulation tests sensitive to deficiencies of many coagulation factors. In brief, they are both sensitive to factor X, V, II and fibrinogen, whereas the PT is only sensitive to factor VII deficiency and the APTT is sensitive to pre-kallikrein, high molecular weight kininogen (HMWK), factor XII, XI, IX and VIII deficiencies. Normal plasma in the PT clots approximately within 10-12 s upon triggering coagulation, and the normal reference range is (usually) narrow. PT results have been reported as clotting time, percentage activity, PT-ratio (patient-to-normal clotting time) and as international normalized ratio (INR). The INR scale has been devised to harmonize results stemming from different thromboplastins from patients on treatment with vitamin K antagonists. Some recommend abandoning the approach of using percentage activity to assess PR.

HP:0008153.label: Periodic hypokalemic paresis
HP:0008153.definition: Episodes of muscle weakness associated with reduced levels of potassium in the blood.

HP:0008155.label: Mucopolysacchariduria
HP:0008155.definition: Excessive amounts of mucopolysaccharide in the urine.
HP:0008155.comment: This finding is suggestive of the diagnosis of a mucopolysaccharidosis.

HP:0008158.label: Hyperapobetalipoproteinemia
HP:0008158.definition: Hyperapobetalipoproteinemia is defined as the combination of a normal low density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol in the face of an increased LDL apolipoprotein B (apoB) protein.

HP:0008160.label: 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria
HP:0008160.definition: The concentration of 2-hydroxydicarboxylic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0008161.label: Absent leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
HP:0008161.definition: Alkaline phosphatase levels measured within leukocytes is below detectable levels.

HP:0008162.label: Asymptomatic hyperammonemia
HP:0008162.definition: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood not associated with symptoms such as encephalopathy.

HP:0008163.label: Decreased circulating cortisol level
HP:0008163.definition: Abnormally reduced concentration of cortisol in the blood.

HP:0008165.label: obsolete Decreased helper T cell proportion

HP:0008166.label: Decreased beta-galactosidase activity
HP:0008166.definition: Abnormally decreased rate of beta-galactosidase activity. Beta-galactosidase activity can be measured in leukocyte, fibroblast, or plasma.
exact_synonyms: Beta-galactosidase deficiency in fibroblasts and white blood cells

HP:0008167.label: Very long chain fatty acid accumulation

HP:0008169.label: Reduced factor VII activity
HP:0008169.definition: Reduced activity of coagulation factor VII. Factor VII is part of the extrinsic coagulation pathway, which is initiated at the site of injury in response to the release of tissue factor (fIII). Tissue factor and activated factor VII catalyze the activation of factor X.

HP:0008179.label: Decreased Arden ratio of electrooculogram
HP:0008179.definition: An abnormal reduction in the Arden ratio, which is the ratio between the light peak and the dark trough of the smoothed (physiologic) EOG record.

HP:0008180.label: Mildly elevated creatine kinase
HP:0008180.comment: 'has part' some ('increased amount' and ('inheres in' some blood) and (towards some IMR_0002602) and ('has modifier' some 'mild intensity') and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0008181.label: Abetalipoproteinemia
HP:0008181.definition: An absence of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
HP:0008181.comment: Beta-lipoprotein cholesterol is a synonym for low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol.

HP:0008185.label: Precocious puberty in males
HP:0008185.definition: The onset of puberty before the age of 9 years in boys.
exact_synonyms: Early onset of puberty in males

HP:0008186.label: Adrenocortical cytomegaly
HP:0008186.definition: The presence of large polyhedral cells with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and enlarged nuclei in the adrenal cortex.
HP:0008186.comment: This feature is common in Beckwith Wiedemann syndrome.

HP:0008187.label: Absence of secondary sex characteristics
HP:0008187.definition: No secondary sexual characteristics are present at puberty.
exact_synonyms: No secondary sexual characteristics at puberty

HP:0008188.label: Thyroid dysgenesis
HP:0008188.definition: Thyroid dysgenesis is a descriptive term that should be avoided if more precise information is available. However, the HPO keeps retains this term because it is commonly used in the medical literature. In humans, the process of thyroid morphogenesis occurs from the 3rd to 16th week of gestation. Alterations occurring during this period may result in a thyroid gland that is absent (thyroid agenesis or athyreosis), hypoplastic (thyroid hypoplasia), or located in an unusual position (thyroid ectopy). All these entities are grouped under the term thyroid dysgenesis.

HP:0008191.label: Thyroid agenesis
HP:0008191.definition: The congenital absence of the thyroid gland.

HP:0008194.label: Multiple pancreatic beta-cell adenomas
HP:0008194.definition: The presence of multiple pancreatic islet cell adenomas.

HP:0008198.label: Congenital hypoparathyroidism
HP:0008198.definition: Deficiency of parathyroid hormone with congenital onset.

HP:0008200.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
HP:0008200.definition: A type of hyperparathyroidism caused by a primary abnormality of the parathyroid glands (e.g., adenoma, carcinoma, hyperplasia). Primary hyperparathyroidism is associated with hyercalcemia.

HP:0008202.label: Reduced circulating prolactin concentration
HP:0008202.definition: A reduced level of prolactin in the blood circulation. Prolactin is a protein hormone that is secreted by lactotrophs in the anterior pituitary and that stimulates mammary gland development and milk production.

HP:0008204.label: Precocious puberty with Sertoli cell tumor
exact_synonyms: Precocious puberty with Sertoli cell tumour

HP:0008205.label: Insulin-dependent but ketosis-resistant diabetes
HP:0008205.definition: Ketosis-resistant diabetes is a synonym for type II diabetes. This term thus refers to a form of type II diabetes in which patients are dependent on insulin.

HP:0008207.label: Primary adrenal insufficiency
HP:0008207.definition: Insufficient production of steroid hormones (primarily cortisol) by the adrenal glands as a result of a primary defect in the glands themselves.
HP:0008207.comment: Deficiency of both glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.

HP:0008208.label: Parathyroid hyperplasia
HP:0008208.comment: An absolute increase in the mass of the parenchymal cells of the parathyroid gland leading to an enlargement of the parathyroid glands.

HP:0008209.label: Premature ovarian insufficiency
