HP:0008209.definition: Amenorrhea due to loss of ovarian function before the age of 40. Primary ovarian insuficiency (POI) is a state of female hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. It can manifest as primary amenorrhea with onset before menarche or secondary amenorrhea.
HP:0008209.comment: The causes of primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) include chromosomal and genetic defects, autoimmune processes, chemotherapy, radiation, infections and surgery, but many are unidentified (idiopathic). The age of 40 is set by convention but is supported by clinical observations. From a statistical point of view, the age limit of 40 is approximately two standard deviations (SD) below the average age at natural menopause (50 plus/minus 4 years).

HP:0008213.label: Gonadotropin deficiency
HP:0008213.definition: A reduced ability to secrete gonadotropins, which are protein hormones secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary gland, including the hormones follitropin (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

HP:0008214.label: Decreased serum estradiol
HP:0008214.definition: A reduction below normal concentration of estradiol in the circulation.

HP:0008216.label: Adrenal gland dysgenesis
HP:0008216.definition: Abnormal development of the adrenal gland.

HP:0008223.label: Compensated hypothyroidism
HP:0008223.definition: Condition associated with a raised serum concentration of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) but a normal serum free thyroxine (FT4).

HP:0008227.label: Pituitary resistance to thyroid hormone
HP:0008227.definition: A condition in which the pituitary gland is partially resistant to thyroid hormone, so that it continues to secrete thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) until the blood level of thyroid hormone rises higher than normal.

HP:0008229.label: Thyroid lymphangiectasia
HP:0008229.definition: The presence of lymphangiectasis of the thyroid gland.
HP:0008229.comment: A stretching and widening of the lymphatic vessels of the thyroid gland.

HP:0008232.label: Elevated circulating follicle stimulating hormone level
HP:0008232.definition: An elevated concentration of follicle-stimulating hormone in the blood.
exact_synonyms: Increased circulating follicle stimulating hormone level

HP:0008233.label: Decreased circulating progesterone
HP:0008233.definition: An reduced concentration of progesterone in the blood.
HP:0008233.comment: Progesterone is a steroid hormone secreted by the corpus luteum after ovulation during the second half of the menstrual cycle.

HP:0008237.label: Hypothalamic hypothyroidism
HP:0008237.definition: A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in thyrotropin-releasing hormone activity.
HP:0008237.comment: The simultaneous occurrence a low thyroid hormone level and a normal or low serum level of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) in a patient with hypothyroidism establishes the diagnosis of secondary hypothyroidism. The administration of thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH), which is normally synthesized and released by the hypothalamus, enables the physician to distinguish between pituitary and hypothalamic causes of hypothyroidism. TRH will normally cause the release of TSH from the pituitary gland. When the hypothalamus does not synthesize or release TRH, the administration of exogenous TRH will result in prompt rise of serum TSH. To date, the cases reported of pituitary hypothyroidism. Hypothalamic hypothyroidism, on the other hand, may either be idiopathic or result from demonstrable hypothalamic disease.

HP:0008239.label: Adrenal medullary hypoplasia
HP:0008239.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the adrenal medulla.

HP:0008242.label: Pseudohypoaldosteronism
HP:0008242.definition: A state of renal tubular unresponsiveness or resistance to the action of aldosterone.
HP:0008242.comment: Pseudohypoaldosteronism is characterized by hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and normal glomerular filtration rate. This term refers to the phenotypic finding of pseudohypoaldosteronism rather than the disease of idiopathic pseudohypoaldosteronism.

HP:0008244.label: Congenital adrenal hypoplasia
HP:0008244.definition: A type of adrenal hypoplasia with congenital onset.

HP:0008245.label: Pituitary hypothyroidism
HP:0008245.definition: A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion.
exact_synonyms: Low thyroid gland function due to abnormal pituitary gland

HP:0008247.label: Euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia
HP:0008247.definition: Increased levels of thyroxine without evidence of clinical thyroid disease.
HP:0008247.comment: Any functional abnormality of the thyroid gland and the systems that control its rate of production of thyroid hormone (hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis) and the peripheral reactivity to thyroid hormone.

HP:0008251.label: Congenital goiter
HP:0008251.definition: An enlargement of the thyroid gland with congenital onset.

HP:0008256.label: Adrenocortical adenoma
HP:0008256.definition: Adrenocortical adenomas are benign tumors of the adrenal cortex.

HP:0008258.label: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
HP:0008258.definition: A type of adrenal hyperplasia with congenital onset.

HP:0008259.label: Adrenocorticotropin receptor defect
HP:0008259.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the ACTH receptor.

HP:0008261.label: Pancreatic islet cell adenoma
HP:0008261.definition: The presence of an adenoma of the pancreas with origin in a pancreatic B cell.

HP:0008263.label: Thyroid defect in oxidation and organification of iodide

HP:0008264.label: Neutrophil inclusion bodies
HP:0008264.definition: The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neutrophils. Cytoplasmic neutrophil inclusions (oval, basophilic) are also known as Doehle bodies.

HP:0008269.label: Increased red cell hemolysis by shear stress

HP:0008271.label: Abnormal cartilage collagen
HP:0008271.definition: Abnormal morphology of collagen fibers in cartilage. In cartilage, collagen II, actually a collagen II:IX:XI heterofibril, is by far the most important type of collagen. A number of abnormalities may be appreciated by electron micrography or biochemical investigations, including sparse collagen fibers in the cartilage matrix.

HP:0008277.label: Abnormal blood zinc concentration
HP:0008277.definition: An abnormality of zinc ion homeostasis.

HP:0008278.label: Cerebellar cortical atrophy
HP:0008278.comment: Cerebellar cortical atrophy may be associated with vacuolated or binucleated Purkinje cells.

HP:0008281.label: Acute hyperammonemia
HP:0008281.definition: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood with sudden onset.

HP:0008282.label: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
HP:0008282.definition: An increased amount of unconjugated (indirect) bilurubin in the blood.

HP:0008283.label: Fasting hyperinsulinemia
HP:0008283.definition: An increased concentration of insulin in the blood in the fasting state, i.e., not as the response to food intake.
exact_synonyms: High blood insulin levels while fasting

HP:0008290.label: Partial complement factor H deficiency
HP:0008290.definition: A partial reduction in level of the complement component Factor H in circulation.

HP:0008291.label: Pituitary corticotropic cell adenoma
HP:0008291.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).

HP:0008293.label: Long-chain dicarboxylic aciduria
HP:0008293.definition: An increase in the level of long-chain dicarboxylic acid in the urine.

HP:0008297.label: Transient hyperphenylalaninemia
HP:0008297.definition: A condition of not having consistently high levels of phenylalanine in the blood but of experiencing temporary hyperphenylalaninemia following ingestion of large quantities of phenylalanine (for instance, following an oral loading test with phenylalanine).

HP:0008301.label: Dermatan sulfate excretion in urine
HP:0008301.definition: An increased concentration of dermatan sulfate in the urine.
HP:0008301.comment: Dermatan sulfate is a a glycosaminoglycan (mucopolysaccharide) found in skin, blood vessels, heart valves, tendons, and lungs.

HP:0008303.label: Olivary degeneration
HP:0008303.definition: Degeneration of the olivary bodies, prominent oval structures in the medulla oblongata.

HP:0008305.label: Exercise-induced myoglobinuria
HP:0008305.definition: Presence of myoglobin in the urine following exercise.

HP:0008309.label: Medium chain dicarboxylic aciduria
HP:0008309.definition: An increase in the level of medium chain dicarboxylic acid in the urine.

HP:0008311.label: Spinal cord dorsal column hypomyelination
HP:0008311.definition: Lower than normal amount of myelin in the dorsal (posterior) tract of the spinal cord white matter.
exact_synonyms: Spinal cord posterior columns myelin loss

HP:0008314.label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex II
HP:0008314.definition: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex II, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.

HP:0008315.label: Decreased plasma free carnitine
HP:0008315.definition: A decreased concentration of free (unbound) carnitine in the blood.

HP:0008316.label: Abnormal mitochondria in muscle tissue
HP:0008316.definition: An abnormality of the mitochondria in muscle tissue.
HP:0008316.comment: This finding is typically demonstrated by muscle biopsy.

HP:0008318.label: Elevated leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
HP:0008318.definition: Increased alkaline phosphatase measured within leukocytes.

HP:0008320.label: Impaired collagen-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0008320.definition: Abnormal response to collagen or collagen-mimetics as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition collagen or collagen-mimetics.

HP:0008321.label: Reduced factor X activity
HP:0008321.definition: Reduced activity of coagulation factor X. The extrinsic and intrinsic pathways converge at factor X (fX). The extrinsic pathway activates fX by means of d factor VII with its cofactor, tissue factor. The intrinsic pathway activates fX by means of the tenase complex (Ca2+ and factors VIIIa, IXa and X) on the surface of activated platelets. Factor Xa in turn activates prothrombin (factor II) to thrombin (factor IIa).

HP:0008322.label: Abnormal mitochondrial morphology
HP:0008322.definition: Any structural anomaly of the mitochondria.
HP:0008322.comment: This feature may be assessed by means of electron microscopy.

HP:0008323.label: Abnormal light- and dark-adapted electroretinogram
HP:0008323.definition: An abnormality of the combined rod-and-cone response on electroretinogram.
HP:0008323.comment: The dark-adapted 3.0 ERG can be used to elicit a combined rod-cone response.

HP:0008326.label: Reduced circulating vitamin B6 circulating
HP:0008326.definition: An abnormally decreased concentration of vitamin B6 in the blood circulation.

HP:0008327.label: Microscopic nephrocalcinosis
HP:0008327.definition: The presence of microscopic crystalline calcium precipitates in the form of oxalate and/or phosphate in the renal parenchyma.
HP:0008327.comment: The qualifier microscopic is used to indicate that the nephrocalcinosis cannot be observed on visual or radiologic examination without further magnification (as can macroscopic nephrocalcinosis).

HP:0008330.label: Reduced von Willebrand factor activity
HP:0008330.definition: Decreased activity of von Willebrand factor. Von Willebrand factor mediates the adhesion of platelets to the collagen exposed on endothelial cell surfaces.
HP:0008330.comment: Von Willebrand factor (VWF) is a key hemostatic protein, but documenting its function through laboratory tests is not always straightforward. VWF serves as a carrier protein for factor VIII (FVIII), and also facilitates platelet adhesion through its interaction with platelet GPIb on the platelet surface and through its binding to the subendothelial matrix. This interaction is driven in vivo by shear stress, which induces a conformational change in VWF that allows it to bind platelet GPIb. In vitro, however, this interaction is induced by the antibiotic ristocetin, which enables VWF and platelet GPIb to interact in the absence of shear forces. Laboratory testing of VWF utilizes ristocetin in the VWF ristocetin cofactor activity assay (VWF:RCo), which is a measure of VWF binding to platelets, or by ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation (RIPA).

HP:0008338.label: Partial functional complement factor D deficiency
HP:0008338.definition: A partial reduction in level of the complement component Factor D in circulation.

HP:0008339.label: Diaminoaciduria
HP:0008339.definition: An increased urine level of any amino acid carrying two amino groups (Asparagine, glutamine and lysine, cystine, ornithine).

HP:0008341.label: Distal renal tubular acidosis
HP:0008341.definition: A type of renal tubular acidosis characterized by a failure of acid secretion by the alpha intercalated cells of the cortical collecting duct of the distal nephron. The urine cannot be acidified below a pH of 5.3, associated with acidemia and hypokalemia.

HP:0008344.label: Elevated circulating branched chain amino acid concentration
HP:0008344.definition: Concentration of a branched chain amino acid in the blood above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0008345.label: Hypoplasia of the iris dilator muscle
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the pupil dilator muscle

HP:0008347.label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex IV
HP:0008347.definition: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.

HP:0008348.label: Decreased circulating IgG2 concentration
HP:0008348.definition: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG2 subclass in the blood circulation.

HP:0008352.label: Impaired platelet adhesion
HP:0008352.definition: An abnormality of adhesion of thrombocytes. Normally, platelets adhere to collagen in the vascular subendothelium within seconds of injury via a receptor made up of glycoprotein Ia and IIa and GPVI and to vWF via receptor GPIb/IX/V. The adherent platelets then release granules that lead to platelet activation and aggregation.

HP:0008353.label: Neutral hyperaminoaciduria
HP:0008353.definition: The presence of an abnormally increased concentration of neutral amino acids in the urine. The neutral amino acids are tryptophan, alanine, asparagine, glutamine, histidine, isoleucine, leucine, phenylalanine, serine, threonine, tyrosine and valine.

HP:0008354.label: Factor X activation deficiency
HP:0008354.definition: Reduced ability to transform factor X into its activated form factor Xa.

HP:0008357.label: Reduced factor XIII activity
HP:0008357.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XIII (also known as fibrin stabilizing factor). Activated Factor XIII cross-links fibrin polymers solidifying the clot.

HP:0008358.label: Hyperprolinemia
HP:0008358.definition: An increased concentration of proline in the blood.

HP:0008360.label: Neonatal hypoproteinemia
HP:0008360.definition: A neonatal decreased concentration of proteins in the blood.

HP:0008362.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the hallux
HP:0008362.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the big toe.

HP:0008363.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the tarsal bones
HP:0008363.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the tarsal bones.

HP:0008364.label: Abnormality of the calcaneus
HP:0008364.definition: An abnormality of the calcaneus, also known as the heel bone, one of the or heel bone, one of the components of the tarsus of the foot which make up the heel.

HP:0008366.label: Foot joint contracture
HP:0008366.definition: Contractures of one or more joints of the feet meaning chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.
exact_synonyms: Contractures involving the joints of the feet
Joint contractures involving the joints of the feet

HP:0008368.label: Tarsal synostosis
HP:0008368.definition: Synostosis (bony fusion) involving one or more bones of the tarsus (calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, cuneiiform bones).

HP:0008369.label: Abnormal tarsal ossification
HP:0008369.definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

HP:0008371.label: Abnormal metatarsal ossification
HP:0008371.definition: Any abnormal process of ossification of the metatarsal bones, which normally are each ossified from two centers: one for the body, and one for the head (metatarsal II,III,IV, and V) and one for the body and one for the base (metatarsal I). The ossification process begins in the center of the body about the ninth week, and extends toward either extremity. The center for the base of the first metatarsal appears about the third year, and the centers for the heads of the other bones between the fifth and eighth years. They join the bodies between the eighteenth and twentieth years.
related_synonyms: Abnormal maturation of long bone of foot

HP:0008372.label: Abnormal circulating vitamin A concentration
HP:0008372.definition: Concentration of vitamin A in the blood circulation outside limits of normal.

HP:0008383.label: Slow-growing nails
HP:0008383.definition: Nails whose growth is slower than normal.

HP:0008386.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the nails
HP:0008386.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the nail.

HP:0008390.label: Recurrent loss of toenails and fingernails
HP:0008390.definition: Repeated loss, or shedding, of the nails of the fingers and toes.
exact_synonyms: Recurrent shedding of toenails and fingernails
Recurrent loss of toenails and fingernails

HP:0008391.label: Dystrophic fingernails
HP:0008391.definition: The presence of misshapen or partially destroyed nail plates, often with accumulation of soft, yellow keratin between the dystrophic nail plate and nail bed, resulting in elevation of the nail plate.

HP:0008392.label: Subungual hyperkeratosis
HP:0008392.definition: A thickening of the stratum corneum in the region beneath the nails.

HP:0008393.label: Congenital curved nail of fourth toe

HP:0008396.label: Chronic monilial nail infection
HP:0008396.definition: Chronic infection of the nails by Candida species.

HP:0008398.label: Hypoplastic fifth fingernail
HP:0008398.definition: A nail of the fifth finger that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail of little finger.

HP:0008399.label: Circumungual hyperkeratosis
HP:0008399.definition: A thickening of the stratum corneum, the outer layer of the skin, in the region surrounding the nails.

HP:0008400.label: Onycholysis of distal fingernails
HP:0008400.definition: Detachment of the distal fingernails from the nail bed.

HP:0008402.label: Ridged fingernail
HP:0008402.definition: Longitudinal, linear prominences in the fingernail plate.

HP:0008404.label: Nail dystrophy
HP:0008404.definition: Onychodystrophy (nail dystrophy) refers to nail changes apart from changes of the color (nail dyschromia) and involves partial or complete disruption of the various keratinous layers of the nail plate.
HP:0008404.comment: Onychodystrophy is a widely used, yet rarely defined term. Onychodystrophy can be caused by congenital nail diseases, systemic disorders, fungal and nonfungal infections, various noninfectious inflammatory dermatologic diseases of the nail unit and tumors. Onychodystrophy can also occur secondarily to systemic drug use.

HP:0008419.label: Intervertebral disk degeneration
HP:0008419.definition: The presence of degenerative changes of intervertebral disk.

HP:0008420.label: Punctate vertebral calcifications
HP:0008420.definition: The presence of punctiform calcification of the bone of the vertebral bodies.

HP:0008422.label: Vertebral wedging
HP:0008422.definition: An abnormal shape of the vertebral bodies whereby the vertebral bodies are thick on one side and taper to a thin edge at the other.

HP:0008423.label: Spinal dysplasia
HP:0008423.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the vertebral column.

HP:0008428.label: Vertebral clefting
HP:0008428.definition: Schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.
HP:0008428.comment: Cleft vertebrae result when there are two, instead of one, primary ossification centers in a vertebral body. An unossified cartilaginous brdige may be observed radiographically with the shape of a cleft. If the two ossification centers are ventral/dorsal, a coronal cleft is observed, and if the two ossification centers are left/right, than a sagittal cleft is observed.

HP:0008430.label: Anterior beaking of lumbar vertebrae
HP:0008430.definition: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the vertebral bodies of the lumbar spine.
exact_synonyms: Anterior tongue-like protrusion of lumbar vertebral bodies

HP:0008432.label: Anterior wedging of L1
HP:0008432.definition: An abnormality of the shape of the lumbar vertebra L1 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).

HP:0008435.label: Absent in utero ossification of vertebral bodies

HP:0008438.label: Vertebral arch anomaly
HP:0008438.definition: A morphological abnormality of the vertebral arch, i.e., of the posterior part of a vertebra.
HP:0008438.comment: A vertebral arch is the posterior part of a vertebra and forms the canal through which the spinal cord passes. A vertebral arch consists of (i) a pair of vertebral pedicles, which are short thick processes that extend from the vertebral body to connect the body to the vertebral arch; (ii) a pari of vertebral laminae (broad plates that extending dorsally and medially from the pedicles fusing with one another to complete the roof of the vertebral arch); (iii) the spinous process (a process that is directed backward and downward from the junction of the laminae and to which muscles and ligaments attach); (iv) two superior articular processes and two inferior articular processes that articulate between two adjacent vertebrae); and (v) two transverse processes that extend at either side from the point where the lamina joins the pedicle, between the superior and inferior articular processes and allow the attachment of muscles and ligaments.

HP:0008439.label: Lumbar hemivertebrae
HP:0008439.definition: Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the lumbar spine.

HP:0008440.label: C1-C2 vertebral abnormality
HP:0008440.definition: Any abnormality of the atlas and the axis.
HP:0008440.comment: The atlas is the first cervical vertebral body and the axis is the second vertebral body.

HP:0008441.label: Herniation of intervertebral nuclei
HP:0008441.definition: The presence of one or more herniated nucleus pulposus of intervertebral disk.

HP:0008442.label: Vertebral hyperostosis
HP:0008442.definition: Excessive growth of the bones of the vertebral bodies.

HP:0008443.label: Neuropathic spinal arthropathy
HP:0008443.definition: A progressive disorder of vertebral joint degeneration that occurs in the setting of any condition characterized by decreased afferent innervation, involving loss of deep pain and proprioceptive sensation in the vertebral column. Patients most commonly present with symptoms of lower back pain, sitting imbalance, progressive spinal deformity (usually kyphosis), and an audible clicking sound on changing postures.
HP:0008443.comment: Neuropathic spinal arthropathy presents almost exclusively in patients who have suffered traumatic spinal cord injury or less commonly, secondary to syringomyelia, meningocele, myelomeningocele, diabetes mellitus, peripheral neuropathies, anesthetic leprosy, congenital analgesia, Parkinson's disease, arachnoiditis, transverse myelitis, and others.

HP:0008444.label: Posterior wedging of vertebral bodies
HP:0008444.definition: An abnormality of the shape of vertebrae, such that they are wedge-shaped (narrow towards the back).

HP:0008445.label: Cervical spinal canal stenosis
HP:0008445.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the cervical spinal canal.

HP:0008450.label: Narrow vertebral interpedicular distance
HP:0008450.definition: A reduction of the distance between vertebral pedicles, which are the two short, thick processes, which project backward, one on either side, from the upper part of the vertebral body, at the junction of its posterior and lateral surfaces.

HP:0008454.label: Lumbar kyphosis
HP:0008454.definition: Over curvature of the lumbar region.

HP:0008455.label: Dysplastic sacrum
HP:0008455.definition: A developmental defect of the sacrum characterized by partial or disordered development of the sacrum in which portions of the sacrum, which normally is formed by fusion of five sacral vertebrae S1-S5, fail to form or fail to form normally.
exact_synonyms: Absence of some of the sacral and coccygeal bones

HP:0008456.label: C2-C3 subluxation
HP:0008456.definition: A partial dislocation of the intervertebral joint between the second and third cervical vertebrae.

HP:0008457.label: Caudal interpedicular narrowing
HP:0008457.definition: Narrowing (becoming gradually narrower) of the distance between vertebral pedicles that gets progressively more severe towards to caudal (lower) end of the vertebral column. Note that normally, the interpedicular distances get progressively wider as one proceeds down the spine.

HP:0008458.label: Progressive congenital scoliosis
HP:0008458.definition: A progressive form of scoliosis with congenital onset.

HP:0008459.label: Cervical vertebral agenesis
HP:0008459.definition: Agenesis of one or more vertebrae of the cervical vertebral column.

HP:0008464.label: Absent spinous processes of lower thoracic and lumbar vertebrae

HP:0008465.label: Absent vertebra
HP:0008465.definition: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies.

HP:0008467.label: Thoracic hemivertebrae
HP:0008467.definition: Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the thoracic spine.

HP:0008468.label: Abnormal sacral segmentation
HP:0008468.definition: An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation of sacral vertebrae during development.

HP:0008469.label: Cervical vertebral dysplasia
HP:0008469.definition: Dysplasia of the cervical vertebral column.

HP:0008470.label: Lower thoracic interpediculate narrowness
HP:0008470.definition: A reduction of the distance between the lower thoracic vertebral pedicles.
exact_synonyms: Narrowness of interpediculate distances in lower thoracic regions

HP:0008473.label: Narrow anterio-posterior vertebral body diameter
HP:0008473.definition: An abnormal reduction of the anterioposterior diameter of the vertebral body.
exact_synonyms: Reduced anterior-posterior diameter of vertebral bodies

HP:0008477.label: Poorly ossified cervical vertebrae
HP:0008477.definition: Decreased ossification of the cervical vertebral bodies, i.e., of the Cervical vertebrae set.

HP:0008480.label: Cervical spondylosis
HP:0008480.definition: Arthrosis, i.e., of degenerative joint disease, affecting the cervical vertebral column.
HP:0008480.comment: When osteoarthritis affects the spine, it is known as spondylosis.

HP:0008483.label: Cervical vertebral bodies with decreased anteroposterior diameter

HP:0008484.label: Thoracolumbar interpediculate narrowness
HP:0008484.definition: A reduction of the distance between thoracolumbar vertebral pedicles.

HP:0008486.label: Lumbar interpedicular narrowing
HP:0008486.definition: Narrowing (becoming gradually narrower) of the distance between lumbar vertebral pedicles that gets progressively more severe towards to caudal (lower) end of the vertebral column.

HP:0008489.label: Spondylolisthesis at L5-S1
HP:0008489.definition: Complete bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis resulting in the anterior slippage of the fifth lumbar vertebral body (L5) onto the sacrum (level S1).

HP:0008491.label: Premature anterior fontanel closure
HP:0008491.definition: Early closure (ossification) of the anterior fontanelle, which generally undergoes closure around the 18th month of life.

HP:0008494.label: Inferior lens subluxation
HP:0008494.definition: Partial displacement of the lens in the inferior direction.

HP:0008499.label: High hypermetropia
HP:0008499.definition: A severe form of hypermetropia with over +5.00 diopters.

HP:0008501.label: obsolete Median cleft lip and palate

HP:0008504.label: Moderate sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008504.definition: The presence of a moderate form of sensorineural hearing impairment.

HP:0008511.label: Central posterior corneal opacity
HP:0008511.definition: Reduced transparency of the central posterior portion of the corneal stroma.

HP:0008513.label: Bilateral conductive hearing impairment
HP:0008513.definition: A bilateral type of conductive hearing impairment.

HP:0008516.label: Abnormality of the vertebral spinous processes

HP:0008517.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the sacrum
HP:0008517.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the sacral bone.

HP:0008519.label: Abnormal coccyx morphology
HP:0008519.definition: Any structural abnormality of the coccyx.

HP:0008523.label: Posterior helix pit
HP:0008523.definition: Permanent indentation on the posteromedial aspect of the helix that may be sharply or indistinctly delineated.
HP:0008523.comment: They are usually linear to a narrow oval in shape and may be single or multiple.
exact_synonyms: Indentation in back of outer ear
Pits in posterior aspect of ear helices

HP:0008527.label: Congenital sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008527.definition: A type of hearing impairment caused by an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve with congenital onset.

HP:0008528.label: Long hairs growing from helix of pinna
exact_synonyms: Long hairs growing from helix of ear

HP:0008529.label: Absence of acoustic reflex
HP:0008529.definition: Absence of the acoustic reflex, an involuntary contraction of the stapedius muscle that occurs in response to high-intensity sound stimuli.
HP:0008529.comment: Note that the acoustic reflex is also referred to as stapedius reflex, attenuation reflex, or auditory reflex.
exact_synonyms: Absence of acoustic middle ear muscle reflexes

HP:0008537.label: Cleft at the superior portion of the pinna
HP:0008537.comment: This term is used for Auriculocondylar syndrome (MIM:602483). Not clear if there is a clean delineation against cleft helix.
exact_synonyms: Cleft at the superior portion of the ear

HP:0008542.label: Low-frequency hearing loss
HP:0008542.definition: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the low frequencies of sound (125 Hz to 1000 Hz).

HP:0008544.label: Abnormally folded helix
HP:0008544.definition: Any structural anomaly of the border of the helix, which usually forms a rolled rim but is highly variable in shape.

HP:0008551.label: Microtia
HP:0008551.comment: The definitions of microtia follow a widely used, surgically based, classification of ear anomalies outlined by Weerda 1988. As microtia indicates at least both decreased length and width, and in more severe forms it includes abnormal shape of structures, all forms are acknowledged to be bundled terms, but are retained here because they are well established.

HP:0008554.label: Cochlear malformation
HP:0008554.definition: The presence of a malformed cochlea.
HP:0008554.comment: A cochlear malformation may include a membranous abnormality, a bony abnormality, or a combination of the two.

HP:0008555.label: Absent vestibular function
HP:0008555.definition: Complete lack of functioning of the vestibular apparatus.

HP:0008568.label: Vestibular areflexia
HP:0008568.definition: Vestibular areflexia can be measured as the absence of the caloric nystagmus response in electronystagmography.

HP:0008569.label: Microtia, second degree
HP:0008569.definition: Median longitudinal length of the ear more than two standard deviations below the mean in the presence of some, but not all, parts of the normal ear.

HP:0008573.label: Low-frequency sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008573.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects primarily the lower frequencies.

HP:0008577.label: Underfolded helix
HP:0008577.definition: Underdevelopment of the helix that either affects the entire helix, or is localized.
HP:0008577.comment: Helix folding is highly variable, and the range is illustrated in Figures 29 and 30. To use this term, the affected area must be too long to be considered a Cleft helix. Underdevelopment of part of the helix can lead to the impression that the scaphal area is enlarged.

HP:0008583.label: Underfolded superior helices
HP:0008583.definition: A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a lesser degree than normal.

HP:0008587.label: Mild neurosensory hearing impairment
HP:0008587.definition: The presence of a mild form of sensorineural hearing impairment.
HP:0008587.comment: A neurosensory hearing loss with a deficit of 21-40 dB.

HP:0008588.label: Slit-like opening of the exterior auditory meatus
HP:0008588.definition: A type of stenosis of the external auditory meatus in which the opening of the external auditory meatus appears as a vertical slit.

HP:0008589.label: Hypoplastic helices
HP:0008589.definition: Underdevelopment of the helix, i.e., of the outer rim of the pinna.

HP:0008591.label: Congenital conductive hearing impairment
HP:0008591.definition: A type of conductive deafness with congenital onset.

HP:0008593.label: Prominent antitragus
HP:0008593.definition: Increased anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.

HP:0008596.label: Postlingual sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008596.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment with onset after the acquisition of speech.

HP:0008598.label: Mild conductive hearing impairment
HP:0008598.definition: A mild form of conductive hearing impairment.
HP:0008598.comment: Conductive hearing impairment with 21-40 dB deficit.

HP:0008605.label: Unilateral external ear deformity
exact_synonyms: Deformed external ear on one side

HP:0008606.label: Supraauricular pit
HP:0008606.definition: Benign congenital lesion of the supraauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.

HP:0008607.label: Progressive conductive hearing impairment
HP:0008607.definition: A progressive type of conductive deafness.

HP:0008609.label: Abnormal middle ear morphology
HP:0008609.definition: An abnormality of the morphology or structure of the middle ear.
exact_synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the middle ear

HP:0008610.label: Infantile sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008610.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment with infantile onset.

HP:0008615.label: Adult onset sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008615.definition: The presence of sensorineural deafness with late onset.

HP:0008619.label: Bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008619.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects both ears.

HP:0008625.label: Severe sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0008625.definition: A severe form of sensorineural hearing impairment.

HP:0008628.label: Abnormal stapes morphology
HP:0008628.definition: An abnormality of the stapes, a stirrup-shaped ossicle in the middle ear.

HP:0008629.label: Pulsatile tinnitus
HP:0008629.definition: Pulsatile tinnitus is generally classified a kind of objective tinnitus, meaning that it is not only audible to the patient but also to the examiner on auscultation of the auditory canal and/or of surrounding structures with use of an auscultation tube or stethoscope. Usually, pulsatile tinnitus is heard as a lower pitched thumping or booming, a rougher blowing sound which is coincidental with respiration, or as a clicking, higher pitched rhythmic sensation.
HP:0008629.comment: Pulsatile tinnitus may be associated with vascular abnormalities such as arterioevenous shunts or glomus tumors or the jugular vein, arterial bruits related to a high-riding carotid artery (close to the auditory areas) or carotid stenosis, or venous abnormalities such as a dehiscent jugular bulb or to hypertension. Finally, in some patients, mechanical abnormalities such patulous eustachian tubes, palatomyoclonus (small spasms of muscles in the soft palate area), or idiopathic stapedial muscle spasm may represent the underlying cause of pulsatile tinnitus.

HP:0008631.label: Ureteral dysgenesis
HP:0008631.definition: A developmental anomaly of the ureter.
HP:0008631.comment: If possible, a more specific term describing the precise type of ureteral dysgenesis should be chosen.

HP:0008633.label: Agonadism
HP:0008633.definition: Absence of sex glands (gonads are the organs that produce gametes; testis in males and ovary in females).
HP:0008633.comment: Gonadal agenesis refers to the lack of development of gonads during fetal development; it may not be possible clinically to determine if gonal tissue was present at any point of development. For this reason, we regard agonadism and gonadal agenesis as synonymous.

HP:0008635.label: Urinary bladder wall hypertrophy
HP:0008635.definition: Increase in thickness of the wall of the urinary bladder. This finding may be seen in conditions such as bladder outlet obstruction and may be accompanied by increased trabeculation of the bladder wall musculature.
exact_synonyms: Hypertrophy of the urinary bladder wall

HP:0008643.label: Nephroblastomatosis
HP:0008643.definition: Presence of persistent islands of renal blastema in the postnatal kidney. Nephroblastomatosis represents a complex abnormality of nephrogenesis and has been defined as the persistence of metanephricblastema into infancy and childhood.

HP:0008651.label: Uric acid urolithiasis independent of gout

HP:0008652.label: Autonomic erectile dysfunction
HP:0008652.definition: Impotence (inability to develop or maintain an erection) resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.

HP:0008653.label: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
HP:0008653.definition: A type of extracapillary glomerulonephritis characterized by the formation of crescent-like cellular proliferation.

HP:0008655.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fallopian tube
HP:0008655.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the fallopian tube.

HP:0008659.label: Multiple small medullary renal cysts
HP:0008659.definition: The presence of many cysts in the medulla of the kidney.
HP:0008659.comment: This feature is the cardinal sign of medullary cystic disease, also known as medullary sponge disease.

HP:0008660.label: Renotubular dysgenesis
HP:0008660.definition: A developmental defect characterized by absence or poor development of proximal renal tubules.
HP:0008660.comment: Renotubular dysgenesis is generally accompanied by early onset and persistent oligohydramnios that leads to the Potter sequence.

HP:0008668.label: Gonadal dysgenesis, male
HP:0008668.definition: Unusual gonadal development in a person with a 46,XY male karyotype, leading to an unassigned sex differentiation.

HP:0008669.label: Abnormal spermatogenesis
HP:0008669.definition: Incomplete maturation or aberrant formation of the male gametes.

HP:0008672.label: Calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis
HP:0008672.definition: The presence of calcium- and oxalate-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

HP:0008676.label: Congenital megaureter
HP:0008676.definition: A developmental disturbance with extreme ureteral dilatation.
HP:0008676.comment: The cause of congenital megaloureter is thought to be aperistalsis of the distal ureter, leading to dilatation. The defect in peristalsis may be due to faulty development of muscle layers of ureter, that is, there is a functional, not a mechanical cause of obstruction.

HP:0008677.label: Congenital nephrotic syndrome
HP:0008677.definition: Nephrotic syndrome with onset within the first three months of life.

HP:0008678.label: Renal hypoplasia/aplasia
HP:0008678.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the kidney.

HP:0008682.label: Renal tubular epithelial necrosis
HP:0008682.definition: Coagulative necrosis of tubular epithelial cells, defined as cells with increased cytoplasmic eosinophilia and nucleus that has a condensed chromatin pattern with fuzzy nuclear contour or has barely visible nuclear basophilic staining. The extent of cortical tubular necrosis is scoredsemiquantitatively as none, mild (less than 25% tubules with necrosis), moderate (25-50 percent), and severe (over 50%).
HP:0008682.comment: Renal tubular epithelial necrosis is a histomorphological definition that corresponds to the clinical term of acture tubular necrosis. Acute death of renal tubular cells that usually results from prolonged renal ischemia, nephrotoxins, or sepsis. The clinical course of acute tubular necrosis may be divided into initiation, maintenance, and recovery phases.

HP:0008683.label: Enlarged labia minora
HP:0008683.definition: Increase in size of the folds of skin between the outer labia.

HP:0008684.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the uterus
HP:0008684.definition: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the uterus.

HP:0008689.label: Bilateral cryptorchidism
HP:0008689.definition: Absence of both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

HP:0008691.label: Solitary bladder diverticulum
HP:0008691.definition: Presence of a single diverticulum (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urinary bladder.

HP:0008696.label: Renal hamartoma
HP:0008696.definition: A disordered proliferation of mature tissues that are native to the kidneys.

HP:0008697.label: Hypoplasia of the fallopian tube
HP:0008697.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the fallopian tube.

HP:0008703.label: Gonadal calcification
HP:0008703.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in gonadal tissue.

HP:0008707.label: Absent scrotum
HP:0008707.comment: Both the sac and rugae are absent. This finding may be accompanied by an (Apparently) absent testis and Cryptorchidism, which should be coded separately.

HP:0008708.label: Partial development of the penile shaft
HP:0008708.definition: A congenital condition of the external male genitalia in which the shaft of the penis fails to fully develop.
HP:0008708.comment: This feature is based on a description in PMID:15273283 for Sudden infant death with dysgenesis of the testes syndrome (OMIM:608800).

HP:0008711.label: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
HP:0008711.definition: The presence of non-malignant hyperplasia of the prostate.

HP:0008716.label: Urethrovaginal fistula
HP:0008716.definition: The presence of a fistula between the vagina and the urethra.

HP:0008717.label: Unilateral renal atrophy
HP:0008717.definition: A unilateral form of atrophy of the kidney.

HP:0008718.label: Unilateral renal dysplasia
HP:0008718.definition: A unilateral form of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.

HP:0008722.label: Urethral diverticulum
HP:0008722.definition: The presence of a diverticulum (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urethra.

HP:0008723.label: Gonadal dysgenesis with female appearance, male
HP:0008723.definition: Unusual gonadal development in a person with a 46,XY male karyotype, leading to a more female sex differentiation.
HP:0008723.comment: Very bad term - try to get rid of it later.

HP:0008730.label: Female external genitalia in individual with 46,XY karyotype
HP:0008730.definition: The presence of female external genitalia in a person with a male karyotype.

HP:0008732.label: Renal hypophosphatemia
HP:0008732.definition: Renal hypophosphatemia is defined as reduced serum phosphate (e.g., below 0.70 mmol/l) and an inappropriately high renal phosphate excretion.
HP:0008732.comment: Three primary mechanisms of hypophosphatemia exist: increased renal excretion, decreased intestinal absorption, and movement of phosphate from the extracellular to intracellular compartments. The initial step in diagnosis involves determining whether hypophosphatemia is renal or nonrenal.

HP:0008733.label: Dysplastic testis
HP:0008733.definition: A descriptive term denoting a developmental anomaly of the male gonad characterized by architectural disorganization of the testicular parenchyma, which may include irregular or poorly formed seminiferous tubules, a thinned tunica albuginea, and increased or fibrotic interstitial tissue. Macroscopically, the testis may range from near-normal in size and appearance to a small, firm, or streak-like structure.

HP:0008734.label: Decreased testicular size
HP:0008734.definition: Reduced volume of the testicle (the male gonad).

HP:0008738.label: Partially duplicated kidney
HP:0008738.definition: The presence of a partially duplicated kidney.

HP:0008740.label: Longitudinal vaginal septum
HP:0008740.definition: The presence of a longitudinal vaginal septum, thereby creating a vaginal duplication.

HP:0008743.label: Coronal hypospadias
HP:0008743.definition: A mild form of hypospadias in which the urethra opens just under the corona glandis, that is, where the head of the penis meets the shaft.

HP:0008744.label: Abnormal aryepiglottic fold morphology
HP:0008744.definition: An abnormality of the aryepiglottic fold.
HP:0008744.comment: The aryepiglottic fold is a fold of mucous membrane extending on each side between the lateral border of the epiglottis and the summit of the arytenoid cartilage.

HP:0008747.label: Cartilaginous ossification of larynx
HP:0008747.definition: Ossification affecting the set of cartilages of larynx.
HP:0008747.comment: This term describes abnormal ossification affecting one or more of the cartilages of the larnyx (cricoid cartilage, thyroid cartilage, epiglottic cartilage, arytenoid cartilage, corniculate cartilage, cuneiform cartilage, triticeal cartilage, and sesamoid cartilage).

HP:0008750.label: Laryngeal atresia
HP:0008750.definition: Congenital absence of the lumen of the larynx. Laryngeal atresia is a rare condition. If the laryngeal opening fails to develop, fluid secreted by the lungs cannot be expelled. In a fetus with laryngeal atresia, the lungs are either normal or hyperplastic, not hypoplastic. Mortality is reported as 100%. At obstetric US examination, views of the fetal neck demonstrate a dilated trachea filled with trapped fluid. Views of the fetal chest show enlarged, hyperechoic lungs, with dilated fluid-filled bronchi. Fetal ascites is usually present.
HP:0008750.comment: Laryngeal atresia results from failure of recanalization of the laryngotracheal tube during the third month of gestation. Laryngeal atresia manifests as acute airway obstruction in the newborn immediately following clamping of the umbilical cord and is fatal without immediate airway management with a tracheotomy. Congenital laryngeal atresia is a rare anomaly that is mostly incompatible with life. Most authors claim that this malformation is related to an arrest of the sixth brachial arch at different gestational stages during normal embryologic development. Complete laryngeal atresia results in a desperate emergency during the first few moments of life, and surgical intervention must occur within 2 to 5 minutes of birth to enable respiration. The most dramatic physical finding is that the child is aphonic, with absence of any cry or gasp at birth.

HP:0008751.label: Laryngeal cleft
HP:0008751.definition: Presence of a gap in the posterior laryngotracheal wall with a continuity between the larynx and the esophagus.
HP:0008751.comment: Embryologically, the trachea and esophagus share a common lumen until they are separated by the development of the tracheoesophageal septum. Failure of this fusion and incomplete development of the tracheoesophageal septum may lead to congenital abnormalities such as isolatedlaryngeal cleft, tracheoesophageal fistula, and esophageal atresia, depending on the severity of the abnormality. Patients with laryngeal cleft may present with feeding difficulty, chronic cough, stridor, pneumonia or respiratory distress, depending on the size of the cleft.

HP:0008752.label: Laryngeal cartilage malformation
HP:0008752.definition: A malformation of the laryngeal cartilage.
exact_synonyms: Vocal impairment, severe, due to laryngeal cartilage abnormalities

HP:0008754.label: Laryngeal calcification
HP:0008754.definition: Calcification (abnormal deposits of calcium) in the laryngeal tissues.

HP:0008756.label: Bowing of the vocal cords
HP:0008756.definition: Bowing (abnormal curvature) of the vocal folds.

HP:0008757.label: Unilateral vocal cord paralysis
HP:0008757.definition: A loss of the ability to move the vocal fold on one side.
exact_synonyms: Unilateral paralysis of the vocal cord

HP:0008760.label: Violent behavior
HP:0008760.definition: Conduct and/or behavior, both verbal and non-verbal, including but not limited to verbal and/or physical aggression, attacks, threats, harassment, intimidation, and other disruptive behaviors in any form or through any medium, that cause or have the potential to cause a reasonable person to fear physical harm from any individual(s) or group(s) towards any person(s) or property. This is commonly defined as a violent act characterized by the use of physical force, anger, or sudden intense activity.

HP:0008763.label: No social interaction
HP:0008763.definition: Lack of intentional participation in interactions with another person.

HP:0008765.label: Auditory hallucination
HP:0008765.definition: Perception of sounds without auditory stimulus.

HP:0008767.label: Self-mutilation of tongue and lips due to involuntary movements
HP:0008767.definition: Uncontrolled movements result in tissue damage to the tongue and lips.
exact_synonyms: Self-mutilation of tongue and lips due to involuntary movements

HP:0008768.label: Abnormal sexual behavior
HP:0008768.definition: A deviation of sexual behaviors from the personal norms of the individual in the context of socially and culturally recognized patterns of human sexual behaviors.

HP:0008770.label: Obsessive-compulsive trait
HP:0008770.definition: The presence of one or more obsessive-compulsive personality traits. Obsessions refer to persistent intrusive thoughts, and compulsions to intrusive behaviors, which the affected person experiences as involuntary, senseless, or repugnant.
HP:0008770.comment: Obsessions have been defined as intrusive and unwanted thoughts that are subjectively experienced as unacceptable.

HP:0008771.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the ear
HP:0008771.definition: The presence of aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the ear.

HP:0008772.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the external ear
HP:0008772.definition: The presence of aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of all or part of the external ear.

HP:0008773.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the middle ear
HP:0008773.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of all or part of the middle ear.

HP:0008774.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the inner ear
HP:0008774.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the inner ear.

HP:0008776.label: Abnormal renal artery morphology
HP:0008776.definition: Any structural abnormality of the renal artery.

HP:0008777.label: Abnormal vocal cord morphology
HP:0008777.definition: An abnormality of the vocal cord.
HP:0008777.comment: The vocal cords, also known as the vocal folds, represent a subdivision of the larynx, and consist of twin infoldings of mucous membrane stretched horizontally across the larynx.

HP:0008783.label: Wide proximal femoral metaphysis
HP:0008783.definition: Increased width of the proximal part of the shaft (metaphysis) of the femur.

HP:0008784.label: Wide capital femoral epiphyses
HP:0008784.definition: Abnormally wide morphology of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Wide end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0008785.label: Delayed ossification of pubic rami
HP:0008785.definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of the rami (branches) of the pubic bone.

HP:0008786.label: Iliac crest serration
HP:0008786.definition: Irregularities of the iliac crest that produce the appearance of a lace border around it.

HP:0008788.label: Delayed pubic bone ossification
HP:0008788.definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of the pubic bone.

HP:0008789.label: Cone-shaped capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0008789.definition: A cone-shaped deformity of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of innermost thighbone

HP:0008794.label: Dysplastic iliac wing
HP:0008794.definition: A general term that describes a congenital defect in the iliac wing resulting from abnormal development.

HP:0008796.label: Femoral retroversion
HP:0008796.definition: An abnormal backward rotation of the hip relative to the knee such that the hips are externally rotated with the foot pointed outward instead of straight ahead (out-toeing).
HP:0008796.comment: Femoral torsion, also known as femoral rotation or femoral version, refers to the twist between the proximal and distal parts of the femur on the transverse plane. Femoral anteversion averages between 30-40 degrees at birth, and between 8-14 degrees in adults. This term applies if the amount of femoral torsion is below this range.

HP:0008797.label: Early ossification of capital femoral epiphyses
HP:0008797.definition: Developmental acceleration of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.

HP:0008798.label: Widened greater sciatic notch
HP:0008798.definition: The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a increase in the lateral dimension of the notch.

HP:0008800.label: Limited hip movement
HP:0008800.definition: A decreased ability to move the femur at the hip joint associated with a decreased range of motion of the hip.

HP:0008804.label: Broad femoral head
HP:0008804.definition: Increased width of the femoral head.

HP:0008807.label: Acetabular dysplasia
HP:0008807.definition: A smaller than normal acetabulum that has insufficient femoral head coverage leading to abnormal hip joint contact pressures, instability and pain.
HP:0008807.comment: Acetabular dysplasia can lead to hip pain and early-onset hip osteoarthritis.
related_synonyms: Decreased femoral head coverage by acetabulum

HP:0008808.label: High iliac wing
HP:0008808.definition: Increased height of the wing (or ala) of the ilium (which is the large expanded portion which bounds the greater pelvis laterally).

HP:0008817.label: Aplastic pubic bone
HP:0008817.definition: A developmental defect characterized by lack of development of the pubis bone.

HP:0008818.label: Large iliac wing
HP:0008818.definition: Increased size of the ilium ala.

HP:0008819.label: Narrow femoral neck
HP:0008819.definition: An abnormally reduced diameter of the femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

HP:0008820.label: Absent ossification of capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0008820.definition: Lack of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
HP:0008820.comment: The ossification center of the capital femoral epiphysis appears at the end of the first year after birth.
exact_synonyms: Absent ossification of femoral capital epiphyses

HP:0008822.label: Hypoplastic ischiopubic ramus
HP:0008822.definition: Underdevelopment of the ischiopubic ramus, which is comprised of the inferior pubic ramus and the inferior ramus of the ischium.

HP:0008823.label: Inferior pubic ramus hypoplasia
HP:0008823.definition: Underdevelopment of the lower branch of the pubis bone (inferior pubic ramus).
HP:0008823.comment: The pubis is the anterior part of the hip bone and forms the anterior and inferior borders of the obturator foramen (the obturator foramen is the opening between the ischium and pubic bones). It is divisible into a body, a superior and an inferior ramus.

HP:0008824.label: Hypoplastic iliac body
HP:0008824.definition: Underdevelopment of the body of ilium.

HP:0008826.label: obsolete Dislocation of the femoral head

HP:0008828.label: Delayed proximal femoral epiphyseal ossification
HP:0008828.definition: Developmental delay of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
HP:0008828.comment: The proximal femoral epiphyseal ossification center normally appears at about age 6 months.
exact_synonyms: Delayed ossification of the proximal femoral epiphysis

HP:0008829.label: Delayed femoral head ossification
HP:0008829.definition: Delayed ossification of the femoral head.
related_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the head of the thigh bone

HP:0008830.label: Hypoplastic pubic ramus
HP:0008830.definition: Underdevelopment of a ramus (branch) of the pubic bone.

HP:0008835.label: Multicentric femoral head ossification
HP:0008835.definition: There is normally one ossification center in the head of the femur. This term applies if there are multiple such centers.
HP:0008835.comment: Additionally, the ossification center of the capital femoral epiphysis appears at the end of the first year after birth. This is not what this term refers to.

HP:0008838.label: Stippled calcification proximal humeral epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in end part of innermost long bone of upper arm

HP:0008845.label: Mesomelic short stature
HP:0008845.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by disproportionate shortening of the medial parts of the extremities (forearm or lower leg).

HP:0008846.label: Severe intrauterine growth retardation
HP:0008846.definition: Intrauterine growth retardation that is 4 or more standard deviations below average, corrected for sex and gestational age.

HP:0008848.label: Moderately short stature
HP:0008848.definition: A moderate degree of short stature, more than -3 SD but not more than -4 SD from mean corrected for age and sex.

HP:0008850.label: Severe postnatal growth retardation
HP:0008850.definition: Severely slow or limited growth after birth, being four standard deviations or more below age- and sex-related norms.

HP:0008855.label: Moderate postnatal growth retardation
HP:0008855.definition: A moderate degree of slow or limited growth after birth, being between three and four standard deviations below age- and sex-related norms.

HP:0008857.label: Neonatal short-trunk short stature
HP:0008857.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with congenital onset recognizable at birth.

HP:0008866.label: Failure to thrive secondary to recurrent infections
HP:0008866.definition: Insufficient weight gain or inappropriate weight loss for a child, that is attributed to an endogenous recurrent infections.
exact_synonyms: Faltering weight secondary to recurrent infections
Weight faltering secondary to recurrent infections

HP:0008872.label: Feeding difficulties in infancy
HP:0008872.definition: Impaired feeding performance of an infant as manifested by difficulties such as weak and ineffective sucking, brief bursts of sucking, and falling asleep during sucking. There may be difficulties with chewing or maintaining attention.

HP:0008873.label: Disproportionate short-limb short stature
HP:0008873.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short limbs but an average-sized trunk.
HP:0008873.comment: A type of dwarfism (marked short stature with adult height below 147 cm) in which the limbs are disproportionately affected. Note that brachymelia is a general term referring to shortening of the limbs. Micromelia refers to the shortening of entire limbs (in contrast to rhizomelia, mesomelia, and acromelia, which refer to shortening of the proximal, middle, or distal portions of the limbs).

HP:0008883.label: Mild intrauterine growth retardation
HP:0008883.definition: Intrauterine growth retardation that is at least 2 standard deviations (SD) below average, but not as low as 3 SD, corrected for sex and gestational age.

HP:0008887.label: Adipose tissue loss
HP:0008887.definition: A reduction in the amount of adipose tissue (fat) compared with the amount previously present in an individual.

HP:0008897.label: Postnatal growth retardation
HP:0008897.definition: Slow or limited growth after birth.

HP:0008905.label: Rhizomelia
HP:0008905.definition: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of limbs (i.e. the femur and humerus).
exact_synonyms: Disproportionately short upper portion of limb

HP:0008915.label: Childhood-onset truncal obesity
HP:0008915.definition: Truncal obesity with onset during childhood, defined as between 2 and 10 years of age.

HP:0008921.label: Neonatal short-limb short stature
HP:0008921.definition: A type of short-limbed dwarfism that is manifest beginning in the neonatal period.
exact_synonyms: Short limb dwarfism recognisable at birth
Short limb dwarfism recognizable at birth

HP:0008922.label: Childhood-onset short-trunk short stature
HP:0008922.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with onset in childhood.
exact_synonyms: Disproportionate short-trunk short stature, identifiable in childhood

HP:0008935.label: Generalized neonatal hypotonia
HP:0008935.definition: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) manifesting in the neonatal period and affecting the entire musculature.
exact_synonyms: Generalized low muscle tone in neonate
Generalised low muscle tone in neonate

HP:0008936.label: Axial hypotonia
HP:0008936.definition: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) affecting the musculature of the trunk.

HP:0008940.label: Generalized lymphadenopathy
exact_synonyms: Swollen lymph nodes affecting all regions of the body

HP:0008944.label: Distal lower limb amyotrophy
HP:0008944.definition: Muscular atrophy of distal leg muscles.
HP:0008944.comment: Distal lower limb muscle atrophy is commonly due to peripheral neuropathy.

HP:0008945.label: Loss of ability to walk in early childhood

HP:0008946.label: Pelvic girdle amyotrophy
HP:0008946.definition: Atrophy of the muscles of the pelvic girdle (also known as hip girdle), i.e., the gluteal muscles, the lateral rotators, the adductors, the psoas major and the iliacus muscle.

HP:0008947.label: Floppy infant
HP:0008947.definition: Floppiness/hypotonia is defined as reduced resistance to passive movement of joints. Physical examination of floppy/hypotonic infants shows head lag, lack of shoulder and elbow muscle contraction on traction response, inability to tighten the shoulder girdle muscles (or slipping through) when held under the axillae, scarf sign (when the arm is pulled to the opposite side, the arm wraps around the neck with the elbow crossing midline), hyperdorsiflexion of the feet, easy apposition of the thumb against the forearm, feet touching the cheek with ease and without discomfort, frog leg position, and inverted U sign on ventral suspension (head, arms, and legs hanging down without elbow or knee flexion and the trunk rounded in a dome shape).
HP:0008947.comment: This term should not be used for new annotations. Instead, state the type of onset of hypotonia more exactly.

HP:0008948.label: Proximal upper limb amyotrophy
HP:0008948.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting proximally located muscles of the arms.
exact_synonyms: Proximal muscle atrophy in upper limbs

HP:0008952.label: Shoulder muscle hypoplasia
HP:0008952.definition: Underdevelopment of muscles of the shoulder.

HP:0008953.label: Pectoralis major hypoplasia
HP:0008953.comment: The pectoralis major is a thick, fan-shaped muscle of the anterior chest.

HP:0008954.label: Intrinsic hand muscle atrophy
HP:0008954.definition: Atrophy of the intrinsic muscle groups of the hand, comprising the thenar and hypothenar muscles; the interossei muscles; and the lumbrical muscles.

HP:0008955.label: Progressive distal muscular atrophy
HP:0008955.definition: Progressive muscular atrophy affecting muscles in the distal portions of the extremities.

HP:0008956.label: Proximal lower limb amyotrophy
HP:0008956.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting proximally located muscles of the legs, i.e., of the thigh.

HP:0008959.label: Distal upper limb muscle weakness
HP:0008959.definition: Reduced strength of the distal musculature of the arms.

HP:0008962.label: Calf muscle hypoplasia
HP:0008962.definition: Underdevelopment of the muscuklature of the calf.

HP:0008963.label: Tibialis muscle weakness
HP:0008963.definition: Muscle weakness affecting the tibialis anterior muscle.
HP:0008963.comment: This is a bundled term which should be made obsolete.

HP:0008964.label: Nonprogressive muscular atrophy
HP:0008964.definition: Muscular atrophy that does not display a progression in severity with time.

HP:0008967.label: Exercise-induced muscle stiffness
HP:0008967.definition: A type of muscle stiffness that occurs following physical exertion.

HP:0008968.label: Muscle hypertrophy of the lower extremities
HP:0008968.definition: Muscle hypertrophy primarily affecting the legs.

HP:0008972.label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain
HP:0008972.definition: Decreased activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
related_synonyms: Decreased activities of mitochondrial-encoded respiratory chain complexes
Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory complexes

HP:0008981.label: Calf muscle hypertrophy
HP:0008981.definition: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the calf muscles.
exact_synonyms: Muscular hypertrophy of the calf muscles

HP:0008984.label: Neck muscle hypoplasia
HP:0008984.definition: Underdevelopment of muscles of the neck.

HP:0008985.label: Increased intramuscular fat
HP:0008985.definition: An abnormal increase in the amount of intramuscular fat tissue.

HP:0008986.label: Agenesis of the diaphragm
HP:0008986.definition: Congenital lack, i.e., aplasia of the diaphragm.
HP:0008986.comment: An extremely large diaphragmatic defect, or apparent absence of the hemidiaphragm, is called agenesis of the diaphragm; this defect probably represents the severe end of the Bochdalek hernia spectrum rather than a distinct entity.

HP:0008988.label: Pelvic girdle muscle atrophy
HP:0008988.definition: Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles that attach to the pelvic girdle (the gluteal muscles, the lateral rotators, adductor magnus, adductor brevis, adductor longus, pectineus, and gracilis muscles).

HP:0008991.label: Exercise-induced leg cramps
HP:0008991.definition: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles of the leg brought on by physical exertion.

HP:0008993.label: Increased intraabdominal fat
HP:0008993.definition: An abnormal increase in the amount of intraabdominal fat tissue.

HP:0008994.label: Proximal lower limb muscle weakness
HP:0008994.definition: A lack of strength of the proximal muscles of the legs.
exact_synonyms: Proximal muscle weakness in lower limbs

HP:0008997.label: Proximal upper limb muscle weakness
HP:0008997.definition: A lack of strength of the proximal muscles of the arms.
exact_synonyms: Proximal muscle weakness in upper limbs

HP:0009002.label: Loss of truncal subcutaneous adipose tissue
HP:0009002.definition: Loss (reduction of previously present) of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the region of the trunk.
exact_synonyms: Loss of subcutaneous truncal adipose tissue
Loss of fat tissue in trunk

HP:0009003.label: Increased subcutaneous truncal adipose tissue
HP:0009003.definition: The presence of an abnormally increased amount of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the trunk of the body.
exact_synonyms: Increased fat below the skin in trunk

HP:0009005.label: Weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles

HP:0009011.label: Hypoplasia of serratus anterior muscle
HP:0009011.definition: Underdevelopment of the serratus anterior muscle, which is involved in abduction, upward Rotation, and elevation of the scapula.

HP:0009016.label: Upper limb muscle hypoplasia
HP:0009016.definition: Underdevelopment of muscles of the arm.

HP:0009017.label: Loss of gluteal subcutaneous adipose tissue
HP:0009017.definition: Loss (reduction of previously present) of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the gluteal region.
exact_synonyms: Loss of fat tissue below the skin in gluts

HP:0009019.label: Progressive loss of facial adipose tissue
exact_synonyms: Progressive loss of facial subcutaneous adipose tissue
Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face, progressive
Progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face

HP:0009020.label: Exercise-induced muscle fatigue
HP:0009020.definition: An abnormally increased tendency towards muscle fatigue induced by physical exercise.

HP:0009023.label: Abdominal wall muscle weakness
HP:0009023.definition: Decreased strength of the abdominal musculature.
HP:0009023.comment: This may be associated with protuberance of the abdomen.

HP:0009025.label: Increased connective tissue
HP:0009025.definition: The presence of an abnormally increased amount of connective tissue.

HP:0009026.label: Hypoplasia of latissimus dorsi muscle
HP:0009026.definition: Underdevelopment of the latissimus dorsi muscle, which is involved in adduction, extension, internal rotation, and transverse extension of the shoulder and assists in movement of the scapula.

HP:0009027.label: Foot dorsiflexor weakness
HP:0009027.definition: Weakness of the muscles responsible for dorsiflexion of the foot, that is, of the movement of the toes towards the shin. The foot dorsiflexors include the tibialis anterior, the extensor hallucis longus, the extensor digitorum longus, and the peroneus tertius muscles.
HP:0009027.comment: Dorsiflexion of the foot extends the foot superiorly, as if taking the foot off the gas pedal.

HP:0009028.label: Generalized weakness of limb muscles
HP:0009028.definition: Generalized weakness of the muscles of the arms and legs.

HP:0009031.label: Amyotrophy of ankle musculature
HP:0009031.definition: Atrophy of the muscles of the ankle.

HP:0009049.label: Peroneal muscle atrophy
HP:0009049.definition: Atrophy of the peroneous muscles, peroneus longus (also known as Fibularis longus), Peroneus brevis (also known as fibularis brevis, and Peroneus tertius (also known as fibularis tertius).
HP:0009049.comment: The peroneus muscles (longus, brevis, and tertius) originate on the fibula and insert on the metatarsals.

HP:0009050.label: Quadriceps muscle atrophy
HP:0009050.definition: Muscular atrophy involving the quadriceps muscle.

HP:0009051.label: Increased muscle glycogen content
HP:0009051.definition: An increased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.

HP:0009053.label: Distal lower limb muscle weakness
HP:0009053.definition: Reduced strength of the distal musculature of the legs.
HP:0009053.comment: This finding can be due to peripheral neuropathy.
exact_synonyms: Distal muscle weakness in lower limbs

HP:0009055.label: Generalized limb muscle atrophy
HP:0009055.definition: Generalized (unlocalized) atrophy affecting muscles of the limbs in both proximal and distal locations.
exact_synonyms: Generalized muscle atrophy, proximal and distal
Generalised muscle atrophy, proximal and distal

HP:0009056.label: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Loss of fat tissue below the skin from upper limbs

HP:0009058.label: Increased muscle lipid content
HP:0009058.definition: An abnormal accumulation of lipids in skeletal muscle.
HP:0009058.comment: Increased neutral lipid content may be observed on muscle biopsies specimen with the specific staining of Sudan black or oil red O techniques by optic microscopy.

HP:0009060.label: Scapular muscle atrophy
HP:0009060.definition: Atrophy of the muscles that are responsible for moving the scapula, which are the levator scapulae, the infraspinatus muscle, the teres major, the teres minor, and the supraspinatus muscle.
HP:0009060.comment: Need to add new UBERON term for scapula muscle

HP:0009063.label: Progressive distal muscle weakness
HP:0009063.definition: Progressively reduced strength of the distal musculature.

HP:0009064.label: Generalized lipodystrophy
HP:0009064.definition: Generalized degenerative changes of the fat tissue.

HP:0009067.label: Progressive spinal muscular atrophy
HP:0009067.definition: Progressive spinal muscular atrophy, i.e., muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

HP:0009071.label: Inflammatory myopathy
HP:0009071.definition: Chronic muscle inflammation accompanied by muscle weakness.

HP:0009072.label: Decreased Achilles reflex
HP:0009072.definition: Decreased intensity of the Achilles reflex (also known as the ankle jerk reflex), which can be elicited by tapping the tendon is tapped while the foot is dorsiflexed.

HP:0009073.label: Progressive proximal muscle weakness
HP:0009073.definition: Lack of strength of the proximal muscles that becomes progressively more severe.
HP:0009073.comment: Removed logical definition that used anonymous class. Outstanding term request in UBERON for proximal muscle organ.

HP:0009077.label: Weakness of long finger extensor muscles

HP:0009084.label: Midline notch of upper alveolar ridge
exact_synonyms: Midline cleft of maxillary alveolar process
Midline notch of maxillary alveolar process
Midline cleft of upper alveolar ridge
Midline notch of upper gum ridge
Midline notch of maxillary alveolar ridge

HP:0009085.label: Alveolar ridge overgrowth
HP:0009085.definition: Increased width of the alveolar ridges.
HP:0009085.comment: This finding may or may not be accompanied by increased height of the alveolar ridge. This is not to be confused with Prominent palatal ridges or gingival overgrowth. This distinction of gingival from alveolar ridge overgrowth may be difficult, especially in milder degrees of the finding.
exact_synonyms: Hyperplasia of alveolar process of jaw

HP:0009088.label: Speech articulation difficulties
HP:0009088.definition: Impairment in the physical production of speech sounds.
HP:0009088.comment: Speech articulation difficulties can result from abnormalities of the vocal tract (the larynx and the pharyngeal, oral, and nasal cavities).

HP:0009092.label: Progressive alveolar ridge hypertrophy
exact_synonyms: Progressive hypertrophy of alveolar process of jaw

HP:0009098.label: Chronic oral candidiasis
HP:0009098.definition: Chronic accumulation and overgrowth of the fungus Candida albicans on the mucous membranes of the mouth, generally manifested as associated with creamy white lesions on the tongue or inner cheeks, occasionally spreading to the gums, tonsils, palate or oropharynx.

HP:0009099.label: Median cleft palate
HP:0009099.definition: Cleft palate of the midline of the palate.

HP:0009100.label: Thick anterior alveolar ridges
exact_synonyms: Thick anterior alveolar process of jaw

HP:0009101.label: Submucous cleft lip
HP:0009101.definition: A cleft of the lip with overlying mucous membrane.
HP:0009101.comment: Submucous cleft lip may lead to increased nasal resonance.

HP:0009102.label: Anterior open-bite malocclusion
HP:0009102.definition: Anterior open bite is a malocclusion characterized by a gap between the anterior teeth (incisors), that is, by a deficiency in the normal vertical overlap between antagonist incisal edges when the posterior teeth are in occlusion.
exact_synonyms: Gap between upper and lower front teeth when biting
Anterior open bite between upper and lower teeth
Absence of overlap of anterior upper and lower teeth

HP:0009104.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the pubic bone
HP:0009104.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the pubic bone.

HP:0009105.label: Abnormal ossification of the pubic bone
HP:0009105.definition: Abnormal ossification (bone tissue formation) affecting the pubic bone, also known as the pubis.
related_synonyms: Abnormal maturation of the pubic bone

HP:0009106.label: Abnormal pelvis bone ossification
HP:0009106.definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the bony pelvis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal ossification involving the bones of the pelvis
related_synonyms: Abnormal maturation of the pelvis bone

HP:0009107.label: Abnormal ossification involving the femoral head and neck
related_synonyms: Abnormal maturation of thigh bone head and neck

HP:0009108.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the femoral head and neck
exact_synonyms: Absent/small head and neck of thighbone
Absent/underdeveloped head and neck of thighbone

HP:0009109.label: Denervation of the diaphragm
HP:0009109.definition: Interruption of the innervation of the diaphragm.

HP:0009110.label: Diaphragmatic eventration
HP:0009110.definition: A congenital failure of muscular development of part or all of one or both hemidiaphragms, resulting in superior displacement of abdominal viscera and altered lung development.

HP:0009112.label: Aplasia of the left hemidiaphragm
HP:0009112.definition: Congenital absence of the left half of the diaphragm.

HP:0009113.label: Diaphragmatic weakness
HP:0009113.definition: A decrease in the strength of the diaphragm.
HP:0009113.comment: Diaphragmatic paralysis is an extreme form of diaphragmatic weakness. Weakness of the diaphragm can result from abnormalities at any site along its neuromuscular axis, although it most frequently arises from diseases in the phrenic nerves or from myopathies affecting the diaphragm itself. Presence of diaphragmatic weakness may be suspected from the complaint of dyspnea (particularly on exertion) or orthopnea; or the presence of rapid, shallow breathing or, more importantly, paradoxical inward motion of the abdomen during inspiration on physical examination.

HP:0009115.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving the skeleton
HP:0009115.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of one or more components of the skeleton.

HP:0009116.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the skull

HP:0009117.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the maxilla
HP:0009117.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the maxilla.

HP:0009118.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the mandible
HP:0009118.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the mandible.

HP:0009119.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the frontal sinuses
HP:0009119.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of frontal sinus.

HP:0009120.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the sinuses
HP:0009120.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of a cranial sinus or sinuses.

HP:0009121.label: Abnormal axial skeleton morphology
HP:0009121.definition: An abnormality of the axial skeleton, which comprises the skull, the vertebral column, the ribs and the sternum.

HP:0009122.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia affecting bones of the axial skeleton
HP:0009122.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of bones of the axial skeleton.

HP:0009123.label: Mixed hypo- and hyperpigmentation of the skin

HP:0009124.label: Abnormal adipose tissue morphology
HP:0009124.definition: An abnormality of adipose tissue, which is loose connective tissue composed of adipocytes.

HP:0009125.label: Lipodystrophy
HP:0009125.definition: Degenerative changes of the fat tissue.
exact_synonyms: Inability to make and keep healthy fat tissue

HP:0009126.label: Increased adipose tissue
HP:0009126.definition: An increase in adipose tissue mass by hyperplastic growth (increase in the number of adipocytes) or by hypertrophic growth (increase in the size of adipocytes occurring primarily by lipid accumulation within the cell).

HP:0009127.label: Abnormality of the musculature of the limbs
exact_synonyms: Muscle issues in the arms and/or legs

HP:0009128.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the musculature of the extremities

HP:0009129.label: Upper limb amyotrophy
HP:0009129.definition: Muscular atrophy involving the muscles of the upper limbs.

HP:0009130.label: Hand muscle atrophy
HP:0009130.definition: Muscular atrophy involving the muscles of the hand.
HP:0009130.comment: This term can be used to described bilateral amyotrophy of the musculature of the hand.
