exact_synonyms: Amyotrophy involving the musculature of the hand

HP:0009131.label: Abnormality of the musculature of the thorax
HP:0009131.definition: A disease or lesion affecting the muscles of the thorax.

HP:0009132.label: Abnormal tarsal bone mineral density
HP:0009132.definition: This term applies to all changes in bone mineral density of the tarsal bones, which (depending on severity) can be seen on x-rays as a change in density and or structure of the bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of bone mineral density involving tarsal bones

HP:0009134.label: Osteolysis involving bones of the feet

HP:0009136.label: Duplication involving bones of the feet
exact_synonyms: Duplication involving bones of the feet

HP:0009138.label: Synostosis involving bones of the lower limbs
HP:0009138.definition: An abnormal union between bones or parts of bones lower limbs.
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving the bones of the lower limbs

HP:0009139.label: Osteolysis involving bones of the lower limbs

HP:0009140.label: Synostosis involving bones of the feet
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving the bones of the feet

HP:0009141.label: Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in muscle tissue
exact_synonyms: Depletion of mitochondrial dna in skeletal muscle tissue

HP:0009142.label: Duplication of bones involving the upper extremities
exact_synonyms: Duplication of bones involving the upper extremities

HP:0009144.label: Supernumerary bones of the axial skeleton

HP:0009145.label: Abnormal cerebral artery morphology
HP:0009145.definition: Any structural anomaly of a cerebral artery. The cerebral arteries comprise three main pairs of arteries and their branches, which supply the cerebrum of the brain. These are the anterior cerebral artery, the middle cerebral artery, and the posterior cerebral artery.

HP:0009147.label: Enlarged epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009147.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger
Enlarged end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Enlarged end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009148.label: Small epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009148.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Small end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger
Small end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009149.label: Triangular epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009149.definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the little finger of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat.
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Delta-shaped epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
Triangular end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger
Triangular end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009150.label: Abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009150.definition: Abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the little (5th) finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the innermost bone pinky finger
Abnormality of the innermost bone little finger
Abnormality of the innermost bone pinkie finger

HP:0009152.label: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the 5th finger
HP:0009152.definition: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of little finger bone
Abnormality of end part of pinky finger bone
Abnormality of end part of pinkie finger bone

HP:0009153.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009153.definition: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the fifth finger. This epiphysis is located on the proximal end of the phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Abnormality of end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Abnormality of end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009154.label: Triangular epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009154.definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat.
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Delta-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
Triangular end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Triangular end part of the innermost bone of little finger

HP:0009155.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009155.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger of the hand, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of the phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Cone-shaped end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Cone-shaped end part of the innermost bone of little finger
related_synonyms: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger
Angel-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger

HP:0009157.label: Ivory epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009157.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
related_synonyms: Ivory epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the little finger

HP:0009158.label: Enlarged epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009158.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger
Enlarged end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Enlarged end part of the innermost bone of little finger

HP:0009159.label: Small epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009159.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Small end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Small end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009160.label: Absent epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009160.definition: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of the innermost bone of little finger
Absent end part of the innermost bone of pinky finger
Absent end part of the innermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009161.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009161.definition: Absence or underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the middle phalanx of the little (5th) finger.
exact_synonyms: Absent/underdeveloped middle bone of pinkie finger
Absent/underdeveloped middle bone of pinky finger
Absent/underdeveloped middle bone of little finger
Absent/small middle bone of pinky finger

HP:0009162.label: Absent middle phalanx of 5th finger
HP:0009162.definition: Absence of the middle phalanx of the little (5th) finger.
exact_synonyms: Absent middle bone of pinkie finger
Absent middle bone of little finger
Aplasia of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger
Absent middle bone of pinky finger

HP:0009163.label: obsolete Abnormal form of the 5th finger

HP:0009164.label: Abnormal calcification of the carpal bones
exact_synonyms: Abnormal calcification of the wrist bones

HP:0009165.label: Stippling of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009165.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger
Speckled calcifications in end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Speckled calcifications in end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger

HP:0009166.label: Fragmentation of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009166.definition: Fragmented appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger
Fragmentation of end part of the outermost bone of little finger
Fragmentation of end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger

HP:0009167.label: Irregular epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009167.definition: Irregular radiographic opacity of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of the outermost bone of pinky finger
Irregular end part of the outermost bone of pinkie finger
Irregular end part of the outermost bone of little finger

HP:0009168.label: Bullet-shaped middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009168.definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally . Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the middle phalanx of the 5th finger is affected.

HP:0009169.label: Broad middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009169.definition: Increased width of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Broad middle bone of pinkie finger
Wide middle phalanx of the 5th finger
Broad middle bone of little finger
Broad middle bone of pinky finger

HP:0009170.label: Osteolytic defects of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009170.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger.

HP:0009171.label: Triangular epiphyses of the metacarpals
HP:0009171.definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphyses of the metacarpals. These epiphyses are located at the distal end of the metacarpals.
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of the long bone of hand

HP:0009172.label: Abnormal 4th finger phalanx morphology
HP:0009172.definition: Abnormality of the phalanges of the 4th (ring) finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the phalanges of the ring finger

HP:0009173.label: Curved middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009173.definition: Curved appearance of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Curved middle bone of pinkie finger
Curved middle bone of pinky finger
Curved middle bone of little finger

HP:0009174.label: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the 4th finger
HP:0009174.definition: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges of the 4th finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the ring finger

HP:0009175.label: Patchy sclerosis of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009175.definition: Patchy increase in bone density of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in the middle bone of the little finger
Uneven increase in bone density in the middle bone of the pinkie finger
Uneven increase in bone density in the middle bone of the pinky finger

HP:0009177.label: Proximal/middle symphalangism of 5th finger
HP:0009177.definition: Fusion of the proximal and middle phalanges of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Fused innermost and middle bones of pinkie finger
Symphalangism of the proximal and middle phalanges of the 5th finger
Fused innermost and middle bones of pinky finger
Fused innermost and middle bones of little finger

HP:0009178.label: Symphalangism of middle phalanx of 5th finger
HP:0009178.definition: Fusion of the middle phalanx of the 5th finger with another bone.
exact_synonyms: Fused middle bones of little finger
Fused middle bones of pinkie finger
Fused middle bones of pinky finger

HP:0009179.label: Deviation of the 5th finger
HP:0009179.definition: Displacement of the 5th finger from its normal position.

HP:0009180.label: Ulnar deviation of the 5th finger
HP:0009180.definition: Displacement of the 5th finger towards the ulnar side.

HP:0009182.label: Triangular shaped middle phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009182.definition: Triangular shaped middle phalanx of the 5th (little) finger. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped middle pinky finger bone
Triangular shaped middle pinkie finger bone
Triangular shaped middle little finger bone

HP:0009183.label: Joint contracture of the 5th finger
HP:0009183.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion in the 5th finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. The term camptodactyly of the 5th finger is used if the distal and/or proximal interphalangeal joints are affected.

HP:0009184.label: Contracture of the distal interphalangeal joint of the 5th finger
HP:0009184.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the distal interphalangeal joint of the 5th finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

HP:0009185.label: Contracture of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the 5th finger
HP:0009185.definition: Proximal interphalangeal (PIP) flexion deformity of the little finger. That is, the PIP joint of a little finger is bent (flexed) and cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.

HP:0009186.label: Contracture of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the 5th finger
HP:0009186.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the 5th finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

HP:0009187.label: Bracket epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009187.definition: An abnormality of the distal phalanx of the fifth finger in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of the outermost pinkie finger bone
Bracket shaped end part of the outermost little finger bone
Bracket shaped end part of the outermost pinky finger bone

HP:0009188.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009188.definition: A secondary ossification center in the distal phalanx of the fifth finger that is distinct from the normal epiphysis that does not contribute to the longitudinal growth of a tubular bone.

HP:0009189.label: Fragmented metacarpal epiphysis
HP:0009189.definition: Fragmented appearance of the epiphyses of the metacarpals.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of end part of the long bone of hand

HP:0009190.label: Irregular epiphyses of the metacarpals
HP:0009190.definition: Irregular radiographic opacity of the epiphyses of the metacarpals.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of the long bone of hand

HP:0009191.label: Ivory epiphyses of the metacarpals
HP:0009191.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphyses of the metacarpals, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the long bone of hands

HP:0009192.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009192.definition: Absence or underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the proximal phalanx of the little (5th) finger.

HP:0009193.label: Metacarpal pseudoepiphysis
HP:0009193.definition: A pseudoepiphysis is a secondary ossification center distinct from the normal epiphysis. The normal metacarpal epiphyses are located at the distal ends of the metacarpal bones. Accessory epiphyses (which are also known as pseudoepiphyses) can also occasionally be observed at the proximal ends of the metacarpals, usually involving the 2nd metacarpal bone.

HP:0009194.label: Small epiphyses of the metacarpals
HP:0009194.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphyses located at the distal end of the metacarpals in respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of the long bone of hand

HP:0009195.label: Epiphyseal stippling of the metacarpals
HP:0009195.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphyses of the metacarpals.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in end part of the long bone of hand
Stippling of the epiphyses of the metacarpals

HP:0009196.label: Absent metacarpal epiphyses
HP:0009196.definition: Absence of the epiphyses of the metacarpal bones, which are normally located at the distal ends of the metacarpals.
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of the long bone of hand

HP:0009197.label: Bracket epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009197.definition: An abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the fifth finger in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of the innermost bone of the pinky finger
Bracket shaped end part of the innermost bone of the little finger
Bracket shaped end part of the innermost bone of the pinkie finger

HP:0009198.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009198.definition: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the fifth finger. This epiphysis is located on the proximal end of the phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the terminal phalanx of the little finger
Abnormality of end part of the outermost bone of the pinkie finger
Abnormality of end part of the outermost bone of the pinky finger
Abnormality of end part of the outermost bone of the little finger

HP:0009199.label: Irregular epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0009199.definition: Irregular radiographic opacity of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of the innermost pinky finger bone

HP:0009548.label: Bullet-shaped phalanges of the 2nd finger
HP:0009548.definition: A second finger with short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.

HP:0009553.label: Abnormality of the hairline
HP:0009553.definition: The hairline refers to the outline of hair of the head. An abnormality of the hairline can refer to an unusually low or high border between areas of the scalp with and without hair or to abnormal projections of scalp hair.

HP:0009554.label: Preauricular hair displacement
HP:0009554.definition: An tongue-like extension of hair towards the cheeks, in which hair growth extends in front of the ear to the lateral cheekbones.
exact_synonyms: Projection of scalp hair onto lateral cheek
Hair displacement, preauricular, towards lateral cheekbone

HP:0009558.definition: Increased width of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

HP:0009559.label: Bullet-shaped distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009559.definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally . Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger is affected.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped outermost bone of the index finger

HP:0009560.label: Curved distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009560.definition: Curved appearance of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

HP:0009561.label: Osteolytic defects of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger

Osteolytic defects of the outermost bone of the 2nd finger

HP:0009562.label: Patchy sclerosis of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009562.definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of the distal phalanx of the second finger.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in the outermost bone of the 2nd finger

HP:0009563.label: Distal/middle symphalangism of 2nd finger
HP:0009563.definition: Fusion of the terminal/distal and middle phalanges of the 2nd finger.

Fused outermost and middle index finger bones

HP:0009564.label: Triangular shaped distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009564.definition: Triangular shaped distal phalanx of the 2nd finger. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx.

HP:0009566.definition: Hypoplasia (congenital reduction in size) of the distal phalanx of the second finger.

HP:0009569.definition: Increased width of the middle phalanx of the second finger.

HP:0009570.label: Bullet-shaped middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009570.definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger is affected.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped middle bone of index finger

HP:0009571.label: Curved middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009571.definition: Curved appearance of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger.
exact_synonyms: Curved middle bone of the index finger

HP:0009572.label: Osteolytic defects of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009572.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger.
exact_synonyms: Lytic defects of middle index finger phalanx

HP:0009573.label: Patchy sclerosis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009573.definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of the middle phalanx of the second finger.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in the middle bone of the index finger

HP:0009574.label: Symphalangism of middle phalanx of 2nd finger
HP:0009574.definition: Fusion of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger with another bone.
exact_synonyms: Fused middle bone of index finger

HP:0009575.label: Triangular shaped middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009575.definition: Triangular shaped middle phalanx of the 2nd finger. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped middle bone of index finger

HP:0009576.label: Absent middle phalanx of 2nd finger
HP:0009576.definition: Absence of the middle phalanx of the index (2nd) finger.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
Absent middle phalanx of index finger
Absent middle bone of index finger

HP:0009577.label: Short middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009577.definition: Hypoplasia (congenital reduction in size) of the middle phalanx of the second finger, also known as the index finger.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplastic/small middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
Short middle bone of index finger

HP:0009579.label: Proximal/middle symphalangism of the 2nd finger
HP:0009579.definition: Fusion of the proximal and middle phalanges of the 2nd finger.
exact_synonyms: Fused innermost and middle index finger bones

HP:0009581.definition: Increased width of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

HP:0009582.definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger is affected.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped innermost bone of index finger

HP:0009583.label: Curved proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009583.definition: Curved appearance of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger.
exact_synonyms: Curved innermost bone of index finger

HP:0009584.label: Osteolytic defects of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009584.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

HP:0009585.label: Patchy sclerosis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009585.definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of the proximal phalanx of the second finger.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in innermost index finger bone

HP:0009586.label: Symphalangism affecting the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009586.definition: Fusion of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger with another bone.
exact_synonyms: Fused innermost bone of index finger

HP:0009587.label: Triangular shaped proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009587.definition: Triangular shaped proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped innermost bone of index finger

HP:0009588.label: Vestibular schwannoma
HP:0009588.definition: A vestibular schwannoma (also known as acoustic neuroma, acoustic neurinoma, or acoustic neurilemoma) is a benign, usually slow-growing tumor that develops from the VIIIth cranial nerve supplying the inner ear.

HP:0009591.label: Abnormal vestibulocochlear nerve morphology
HP:0009591.definition: Any structural anomaly of the vestibulocochlear nerve. The vestibulocochlear nerve consists of the vestibular and cochlear nerves, also known as cranial nerve eight (CN VIII). Each nerve has distinct nuclei within the brainstem. The vestibular nerve is primarily responsible for maintaining body balance and eye movements, while the cochlear nerve is responsible for hearing.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the VIIIth cranial nerve

HP:0009592.label: Astrocytoma
HP:0009592.definition: Astrocytoma is a neoplasm of the central nervous system derived from astrocytes. Astrocytes are a type of glial cell, and thus astrocytoma is a subtype of glioma.

HP:0009593.label: Peripheral schwannoma
HP:0009593.definition: The presence of a peripheral schwannoma.
HP:0009593.comment: A Peripheral schwannoma (also known as neurilemoma) is a benign, usually encapsulated neoplasm derived from Schwann cells.

HP:0009594.label: Retinal hamartoma
HP:0009594.definition: A hamartoma (a benign, focal malformation consisting of a disorganized mixture of cells and tissues) of the retina.

HP:0009596.label: Aplasia of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009596.definition: Absence of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger.
exact_synonyms: Absent innermost bone of index finger

HP:0009597.label: Short proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
HP:0009597.definition: Hypoplasia (congenital reduction in size) of the proximal phalanx of the second finger.
exact_synonyms: Short proximal phalanx of the second finger
Hypoplastic/small proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger

HP:0009598.label: Symphalangism of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger with the 2nd metacarpal
HP:0009598.definition: Fusion of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger with the 2nd metacarpal.
exact_synonyms: Fused innermost bone of index finger with 2nd long bone of hand

HP:0009599.label: Abnormality of thumb epiphysis
HP:0009599.definition: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the proximal, and distal phalanges of the thumb and/or the 1st metacarpal.
HP:0009599.comment: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5 (whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits).
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of thumb long bone
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the thumb

HP:0009600.label: Thumb contracture
HP:0009600.definition: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the thumb joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin. The term camptodactyly is used if the distal and/or proximal interphalangeal joints are affected.

HP:0009602.label: Abnormality of thumb phalanx
HP:0009602.definition: A structural anomaly of one or more phalanges of the thumb.

HP:0009603.label: Deviation of the thumb
HP:0009603.definition: Displacement of the thumb from its normal position.

HP:0009606.label: Complete duplication of distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009606.definition: Complete duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb. On x-ray two separate bones appear side to side.
exact_synonyms: Complete duplication of outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009608.label: Complete duplication of proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009608.definition: Complete duplication of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. On x-ray two separate bones appear side to side. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Complete duplication of the innermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009609.label: Duplication of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0009609.definition: Partail or complete duplication of the first metacarpal bone.
HP:0009609.comment: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin. This term applies if the first metacarpal is completely or partially duplicated. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched metacarpal (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the metacarpal), a partially fused appearance of the two bones (in most cases the fused bone resembles a Y-shape), or two separate metacarpal bones appearing side to side.
exact_synonyms: Partial/complete duplication of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0009611.label: Bifid distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009611.definition: Partial duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx) to a partially fused appearance of the two bones.
HP:0009611.comment: Note that with bifid distal phalanx, the terminal phalanx of the thumb is clefted but is still one bone. With duplication of the terminal phalanx of the thumb, the distal phalanx is split into two bones that are located side by side. With triphalangeal thumb, the thumb has three phalanxes located one after the other.
exact_synonyms: Notched outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009612.label: Duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009612.definition: Complete or partial duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx), a partially fused appearance of the two bones, or two separate bones appearing side to side.
exact_synonyms: Duplication of the outermost bone of the thumb
Partial/complete duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009613.label: Duplication of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009613.definition: Complete or partial duplication of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx), a partially fused appearance of the two bones, or two separate bones appearing side to side. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Partial/complete duplication of the proximal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009614.label: Bifid proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009614.definition: This term applies if the proximal phalanx of the thumb is partially duplicated. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx) to a partially fused appearance of the two bones. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0009615.label: Complete duplication of the first metacarpal
HP:0009615.definition: Complete duplication of the first metacarpal bone.
HP:0009615.comment: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin, equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits. This term applies if the first metacarpal is completely duplicated. On x-ray two separate metacarpal bones appear side to side. This term applies if the first metacarpal is completely duplicated.
exact_synonyms: Complete duplication of the first long bone of hand

HP:0009616.label: Bifid first metacarpal
HP:0009616.definition: Partial duplication of the first metacarpal bone.
HP:0009616.comment: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin (equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits). This term applies if the first metacarpal is partially duplicated. Depending on the severity the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched metacarpal (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the metacarpal) to a partially fused appearance of the two bones. In most cases the fused bone resembles a Y-shape.
exact_synonyms: Notched first long bone of hand
partial duplication of the first metacarpal

HP:0009617.label: Abnormality of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009617.definition: Any anomaly of the distal phalanx of thumb.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009618.label: Abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009618.definition: An anomaly of the shape or form of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
HP:0009618.comment: In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0009620.label: obsolete Radial deviation of the thumb

HP:0009621.label: obsolete Ulnar deviation of the thumb

HP:0009622.label: Distally placed thumb
HP:0009622.definition: Insertion of thumb at a more distal location than normal.

HP:0009623.label: Proximal placement of thumb
HP:0009623.comment: Thumb placement index greater than 0.55; or, the base of the thumb appears closer to the wrist than is typical. The technique for the thumb placement index is described in detail [Malina et al., 1973; Hall et al., 2007]. Briefly, the thumb placement index is the distance from the proximal crease of the index finger to the angle of the first interdigital space divided by the distance from the proximal crease of the index finger to the wrist flexion crease at the base of the thumb. This term should not be used with Preaxial polydactyly.
exact_synonyms: Attachment of thumb close to wrist

HP:0009624.label: Carpometacarpal thumb joint contracture
HP:0009624.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. This joint is formed by the first metacarpal and the trapezial bone and is also called Articulatio carpometacarpalis pollicis, carpometacarpal articulation of thumb, carpometacarpal joint of thumb or first carpometacarpal articulation. Seldom referred to as thumb saddle joint.
exact_synonyms: Contracture of the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb

HP:0009625.label: Metacarpophalangeal thumb joint contracture
HP:0009625.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. This joint is also called Articulatio metacarpophalangealis pollicis.
exact_synonyms: Contracture of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb

HP:0009626.label: Interphalangeal thumb joint contracture
HP:0009626.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the interphalangeal joint of the thumb due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. This joint is also called Articulatio interphalangealis pollicis.
exact_synonyms: Contracture of the interphalangeal joint of the thumb

HP:0009629.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009629.definition: This term applies if the proximal phalanx of the thumb is either small/hypoplastic or absent. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0009630.label: Broad proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009630.definition: Increased width of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0009631.label: Bullet-shaped proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009631.definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the proximal phalanx of the thumb is affected.

HP:0009632.label: Curved proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009632.definition: A deviation from the normal straight shape of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.

HP:0009633.label: Osteolytic defect of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009633.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Osteolytic defects of the proximal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009634.label: Patchy sclerosis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009634.definition: An uneven increase in bone density of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in the innermost thumb bone

HP:0009635.label: Synostosis of thumb phalanx
HP:0009635.definition: Fusion of a phalanx of the thumb with another bone.

HP:0009636.label: Triangular shaped proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009636.definition: Triangular shaped proximal phalanx of the thumb.

HP:0009637.label: Absent proximal phalanx of thumb
HP:0009637.definition: Absence of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the proximal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009638.label: Short proximal phalanx of thumb
HP:0009638.definition: Hypoplastic (short) proximal phalanx of the thumb. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplastic/small proximal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009640.label: Synostosis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb with the 1st metacarpal
HP:0009640.definition: Fusion of the proximal phalanx of the thumb with the 1st metacarpal.
exact_synonyms: Ankylosis of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb
Fusion of the innermost bone of the thumb with the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0009641.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the distal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009642.label: Broad distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009642.definition: Increased width of the distal phalanx of thumb.
exact_synonyms: Broad outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009643.label: Bullet-shaped distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009643.definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the distal phalanx of the thumb is affected.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009644.label: Curved distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009644.definition: A deviation from the normal straight shape of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Curved outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009645.label: Osteolytic defect of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009645.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Osteolytic defects of the distal phalanx of the thumb
Osteolytic defects of the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009646.label: Patchy sclerosis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009646.definition: An uneven increase in bone density of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009648.label: Triangular shaped distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009648.definition: Triangular shaped distal phalanx of the thumb. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009649.label: Aplasia of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009649.definition: Absence of the distal/terminal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Absence of the outermost bone of the thumb
Aplasia of the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009650.label: Short distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009650.definition: Hypoplastic (short) distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Short outermost bone of the thumb
Hypoplastic/small distal phalanx of the thumb

HP:0009652.label: Bullet-shaped thumb phalanx
HP:0009652.definition: An abnormal morphology of one or more phalanges of the thumb, with a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.

HP:0009653.label: Curved thumb phalanx
HP:0009653.definition: A deviation from the normal straight shape of a thumb phalanx.

HP:0009654.label: Osteolytic defect of thumb phalanx
HP:0009654.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of one or more phalanges of the thumb.
HP:0009654.comment: Osteolytic lesions are visible on radiography as demarcated areas of radiolucency ('darkness').
exact_synonyms: Osteolytic defects of the phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009655.label: Patchy sclerosis of thumb phalanx
HP:0009655.definition: An uneven increase in bone density of one or more of the phalanges of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in thumb bone
Patchy sclerosis of the phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009656.label: Symphalangism of the thumb
HP:0009656.definition: Congenital fusion (ankylosis) of the interphalangeal joint of the thumb.
HP:0009656.comment: Symphalangism is caused by a failure of segmentation that occurs during early fetal development.
exact_synonyms: Symphalangism of the distal and proximal phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009657.label: Triangular shaped thumb phalanx
HP:0009657.definition: Abnormal shape of one or more phalanges of the thumb such that affected phalanges resemble a triangle.
HP:0009657.comment: A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx (in this case metacarpal, see explanation above).
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009658.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009659.label: Partial absence of thumb
HP:0009659.definition: The absence of a phalangeal segment of a thumb.
related_synonyms: Aplasia of the phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009662.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009662.definition: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb. This epiphysis is located on the proximal end of the phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009663.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009663.definition: This term applies if the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, which is located at the proximal end of the phalanx, does not appear in concordance with gender and age dependant norms as seen on x-rays. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009664.label: Absent epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009664.definition: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009665.label: Bracket epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009665.definition: An abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the thumb in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009666.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009666.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb of the hand, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of the phalanx. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009667.label: Enlarged epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009667.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009668.label: Fragmentation of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009668.definition: Epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb having multiple bony fragments.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009669.label: Irregular epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009669.definition: Irregular radiographic opacity of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009670.label: Ivory epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009670.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the innermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009671.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009671.definition: A pseudoepiphysis (which is a secondary ossification center distinct from the normal epiphysis) of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.

HP:0009672.label: Small epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009672.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009673.label: Stippling of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009673.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009674.label: Triangular epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009674.definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the thumb of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of thumb innermost long bone

HP:0009675.label: Absent epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009675.definition: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of thumb outermost long bone

HP:0009676.label: Bracket epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009676.definition: An abnormality of the distal phalanx of the thumb in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of thumb outermost long bone

HP:0009677.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009677.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb of the hand, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of the phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of thumb outermost long bone

HP:0009678.label: Enlarged epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009678.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of thumb outermost long bone

HP:0009679.label: Fragmentation of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009679.definition: Epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb having multiple bony fragments.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of end part thumb outermost long bone

HP:0009680.label: Irregular epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009680.definition: Uneven radiographic opacity of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of thumb outermost bone

HP:0009681.label: Ivory epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009681.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009682.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009682.definition: A pseudoepiphysis (which is a secondary ossification center distinct from the normal epiphysis) of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Pseudoepiphysis of the outermost bone of the thumb

HP:0009683.label: Small epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009683.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of thumb outermost bone

HP:0009684.label: Stippling of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009684.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in the end part of the outermost thumb bone

HP:0009685.label: Triangular epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb
HP:0009685.definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the thumb of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat.
exact_synonyms: Triangular epiphysis of the outermost bone of the thumb
Triangular end part of thumb outermost bone

HP:0009686.label: Absent epiphyses of the thumb
HP:0009686.definition: Absence of one or more epiphyses of the thumb.

HP:0009687.label: Bracket epiphyses of the thumb
HP:0009687.definition: An abnormality of the thumb in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of the thumb bone

HP:0009688.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the thumb
HP:0009688.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphyses of the thumb, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of a phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of thumb long bone

HP:0009689.label: Enlarged thumb epiphysis
HP:0009689.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphyses of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of thumb long bone

HP:0009690.label: Fragmentation of thumb epiphysis
HP:0009690.definition: Epiphysis of the thumb having multiple bony fragments.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of the epiphyses of the thumb
Fragmentation of end part of long bone of thumb

HP:0009691.label: Irregular thumb epiphysis
HP:0009691.definition: Uneven radiographic opacity of the one or more epiphyses of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of thumb long bone

HP:0009692.label: Ivory epiphysis of the thumb
HP:0009692.definition: Sclerosis of one or more of the epiphyses of the thumb, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the thumb

HP:0009693.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the thumb
HP:0009693.definition: A pseudoepiphysis (which is a secondary ossification center distinct from the normal epiphysis) of one or more phalanges of the thumb.

HP:0009694.label: Small thumb epiphysis
HP:0009694.definition: Abnormally small size of one or more of the epiphyses of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of thumb long bone

HP:0009695.label: Stippling of thumb epiphysis
HP:0009695.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more of the epiphyses of the thumb.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in end part of thumb bone
Stippling of the epiphyses of the thumb

HP:0009696.label: Triangular epiphyses of the thumb
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of the thumb bone

HP:0009697.label: Contracture of the distal interphalangeal joint of the fingers
HP:0009697.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion in one or more distal interphalangeal joints of the fingers.

HP:0009699.label: Osteolytic defects of the hand bones

HP:0009700.label: Finger symphalangism
HP:0009700.definition: An abnormal union between bones or parts of bones of the fingers. The synonymous term "symphalangism of the hand" may be translated as fusions of bones of varying digree, that involve at least one phalangeal bone of the hand. If bony fusions are referred to as "Symphalangism" the fusion occurs in a proximo-distal axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers in a radio-ulnar axis are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly.
exact_synonyms: Synostosis involving bones of the fingers

HP:0009701.label: Metacarpal synostosis
HP:0009701.definition: Fusion involving two or more metacarpal bones (A synostosis of the first metacarpal and the proximal phalanx of the thumb can also be observed, note that the first metacarpal bone corresponds to a proximal phalanx).

HP:0009702.label: Carpal synostosis
HP:0009702.definition: Synostosis (bony fusion) involving one or more bones of the carpus (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate, pisiform).

HP:0009703.label: Synostosis involving the 1st metacarpal
HP:0009703.definition: Fusion of the 1st metacarpal with another bone. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2 to 5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving 1st long bone of hand

HP:0009704.label: Chronic CSF lymphocytosis
HP:0009704.definition: Chronic cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) lymphocytosis is defined as the finding, in at least two serial CSF examinations, of more than 5 cells per cubic millimeter.

HP:0009705.label: Synostosis involving the 2nd metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving the 2nd long bone of hand

HP:0009706.label: Synostosis involving the 3rd metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving the 3rd long bone of hand

HP:0009707.label: Synostosis involving the 4th metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving the 4th long bone of hand

HP:0009708.label: Synostosis involving the 5th metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Fusion involving the 5th long bone of hand

HP:0009709.label: Increased CSF interferon alpha
HP:0009709.definition: Increased concentration of interferon alpha in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP:0009710.label: Chilblains
HP:0009710.definition: Chilblains, also called perniosis, are an inflammatory skin condition related to an abnormal vascular response to the cold. We are unaware of a reliable estimate of incidence. It typically presents as tender, pruritic red or bluish lesions located symmetrically on the dorsal aspect of the fingers, toes, ears and nose. Less commonly, reports describe involvement of the thighs and buttocks. The lesions present hours after exposure to cold and usually resolve spontaneously in one to three weeks.

HP:0009711.label: Retinal capillary hemangioma
HP:0009711.definition: A benign vascular tumor of the retina without any neoplastic characteristics.

HP:0009713.label: Spinal hemangioblastoma
HP:0009713.definition: A hemangioblastoma of the spinal cord.

HP:0009714.label: Abnormal epididymis morphology
HP:0009714.comment: The epididymis is the structure that connects efferent ductules to vas deferens.

HP:0009715.label: Papillary cystadenoma of the epididymis
HP:0009715.definition: A cystadenoma, an epithelial tumor, that originates within the head of the epididymis.
HP:0009715.comment: Papillary cystadenomas of the epididymis are partially or completely cystic or solid lesions, between 1-3 cm in diameter and arise from the efferent duct epithelium of the head of epididymis.

HP:0009716.label: Subependymal nodules
HP:0009716.definition: Small nodular masses which originate in the subependymal region of the lateral ventricles and protrude into the ventricular cavity. They may represent subependymal hamartomas of tuberous sclerosis.

HP:0009717.label: Cortical tubers
HP:0009717.definition: Cortical tubers in the brain are hamartomatous lesions typically located at the gray-white matter interface, commonly in the frontal and parietal lobes. Cortical tubers are composed of abnormal glial and neural cells, and the size, number, and location vary among patients.

HP:0009718.label: Subependymal giant-cell astrocytoma
HP:0009718.definition: A demarcated, largely intraventricular tumor in the region of the foramen of Monro composed of spindle to large plump or ganglion-like cells with eosinophilic to amphophilic cytoplasm and somewhat pleomorphic nuclei with occasional prominent nucleoli. These tumors are almost always associated with tuberous sclerosis.

HP:0009719.label: Hypomelanotic macule
HP:0009719.definition: Hypomelanotic macules ("ash leaf spots") are white or lighter patches of skin that may appear anywhere on the body and are caused by a lack of melanin. White ash leaf-shaped macules are considered to be characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.
HP:0009719.comment: While hypopigmentation is a general term that refers to any form of decreased or absent skin pigmentation, hypomelanosis more specifically refers to a reduction of epidermal melanin.

HP:0009720.label: Adenoma sebaceum
HP:0009720.definition: The presence of a sebaceous adenoma with origin in the sebum secreting cells of the skin.
HP:0009720.comment: Facial angiofibromas, also known as adenoma sebaceum, are reddish papillary lesions (fibrous skin tumors) that are found around the nose, cheeks, and chin and considered to be characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.

HP:0009721.label: Shagreen patch
HP:0009721.definition: A plaque representing a connective-tissue nevus. Connective tissue naevi are uncommon skin lesions that occur when the deeper layers of the skin do not develop correctly or the components of these layers occur in the wrong proportion. Shagreen patches are oval-shaped and nevoid, skin-colored or occasionally pigmented, smooth or crinkled. The word shagreen refers to a type of roughened untanned leather.

HP:0009722.label: Dental enamel pits
HP:0009722.definition: The presence of small depressions in the dental enamel.

HP:0009723.label: Abnormal subungual morphology
HP:0009723.definition: A lesion located beneath a fingernail or toenail.

HP:0009724.label: Subungual fibromas
HP:0009724.definition: The presence of fibromata beneath finger or toenails.

HP:0009725.label: Bladder neoplasm
HP:0009725.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary bladder.

HP:0009726.label: Renal neoplasm
HP:0009726.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the kidney.

HP:0009727.label: Achromatic retinal patches
HP:0009727.definition: Areas of the retina lacking pigmentation. Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation less than 1 disk diameter in size and tending to be located in the midperiphery of the retina.
exact_synonyms: Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation

HP:0009728.label: Neoplasm of striated muscle
HP:0009728.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) originating in striated muscle, either skeletal muscle or cardiac muscle.

HP:0009729.label: Cardiac rhabdomyoma
HP:0009729.definition: A benign tumor of cardiac striated muscle.

HP:0009730.label: Rhabdomyoma
HP:0009730.definition: A benign tumor of striated muscle.

HP:0009731.label: Cerebral hamartoma
HP:0009731.definition: The presence of a hamartoma of the cerebrum.
HP:0009731.comment: Hamartomatous lesions (benign focal lesions composed of disorganized tissue elements) affecting and sometimes originating from the cerebrum.

HP:0009732.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
HP:0009732.definition: A neurofibroma in which Schwann cells proliferate inside the nerve sheath, producing an irregularly thickened, distorted, tortuous structure.

HP:0009733.label: Glioma
HP:0009733.definition: The presence of a glioma, which is a neoplasm of the central nervous system originating from a glial cell (astrocytes or oligodendrocytes).
HP:0009733.comment: Gliomas can be classified as 1) ependymomas, 2) astrocytomas (including glioblastoma multiforme), 3 oligodendrogliomas, and 4) mixed gliomas, such as oligoastrocytomas.

HP:0009734.label: Optic nerve glioma
HP:0009734.definition: A glioma originating in the optic nerve or optic chiasm.

HP:0009735.label: Spinal neurofibroma
HP:0009735.definition: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the spine.
HP:0009735.comment: Spinal neurofibromas can affect the spinal cord or the spinal nerve roots. Spinal neurofibromas can occur at cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral levels.

HP:0009736.label: Tibial pseudarthrosis
HP:0009736.definition: Pseudarthrosis, or "false joint" of the tibia is the result of a developmental failure in the tibia progressing to spontaneous fracture and subsequent fibrous nonunion. The fracture is rarely present at birth but commonly develops during the first 18 months of life.

HP:0009737.label: Lisch nodules
HP:0009737.definition: The presence of pigmented, oval and dome-shaped raised hamartomatous nevi of the iris..

HP:0009738.label: Abnormal antihelix morphology
HP:0009738.comment: An abnormal form of the antihelix, which is the curved prominence of cartilage, parallel with and in front of the helix, and which divides into the crura antihelicis, between which is a triangular depression, the fossa triangularis.

HP:0009741.label: Nephrosclerosis
HP:0009741.definition: Nephrosclerosis refers to thickening or scarring ("sclerosis") resulting from damage to the renal arterioles, also referred to as arteriosclerosis of the kidney arteries.

HP:0009742.label: Stiff shoulders
HP:0009742.definition: Shoulder joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in shoulders when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

HP:0009743.label: Distichiasis
HP:0009743.comment: Distichiasis can be defined as the abnormal growth of lashes from the orifices of the Meibomian glands on the posterior lamella of the tarsal plate, resulting in a double row of eyelashes.

HP:0009744.label: Abnormal spinal dura mater morphology
HP:0009744.definition: An abnormality of the spinal dura mater, which is the outermost of the three layers of the meninges surrounding the spinal cord.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the spinal dura mater

HP:0009745.label: Spinal arachnoid cyst
HP:0009745.definition: Presence of arachnoid cysts of the spinal canal extradurally in the epidural space.
exact_synonyms: Epidural arachnoid cysts of the spinal canal

HP:0009746.label: Thick nasal septum
HP:0009746.definition: Abnormally increased thickness of the nasal septum.

HP:0009747.label: Lumbosacral hirsutism
HP:0009747.definition: Abnormally increased hair growth in the lumbosacral region.

HP:0009748.label: Large earlobe
HP:0009748.definition: Increased volume of the earlobe, that is, abnormally prominent ear lobules.
HP:0009748.comment: All gradations in size of the earlobe may be seen from absent to clearly enlarged compared to average. This finding is highly variable. Lobe size increases throughout adulthood.

HP:0009751.label: Aplasia of the pectoralis major muscle
HP:0009751.definition: Absence of the pectoralis major muscle.

HP:0009752.label: Cleft in skull base
HP:0009752.definition: A bony defect in the skull base.

HP:0009754.label: Fibrous syngnathia
HP:0009754.definition: Complete or nearly complete soft tissue fusion of the alveolar ridges.
HP:0009754.comment: This finding is associated with severely reduced mobility, or lack of mobility, between the upper and lower jaws. This finding is the severe end of a spectrum that includes oral synechiae.

HP:0009755.label: Ankyloblepharon
HP:0009755.definition: Partial fusion of the upper and lower eyelid margins by single or multiple bands of tissue.
HP:0009755.comment: A minimally expressed form, especially when located fully laterally, may be more difficult to ascertain and would be a subjective feature. A band may break and leave no evidence of its presence. Note that the term is distinct from cryptophthalmos.

HP:0009756.label: Popliteal pterygium
HP:0009756.definition: A pterygium (or pterygia) occurring in the popliteal region (the back of the knee).

HP:0009757.label: Intercrural pterygium
HP:0009757.definition: A pterygium (or pterygia) in the intercrural (groin) region.

HP:0009758.label: Pyramidal skinfold extending from the base to the top of the nails
HP:0009758.definition: Pyramidal skinfold extending from the base to the top of the nails is a rare and distinctive anomaly seen in popliteal pterygia syndrome.

HP:0009760.label: Antecubital pterygium
HP:0009760.definition: Pterygium affecting the elbow. This is a cutaneous web that can lead to severe flexion contracture of the elbow joint. Antecubital pterygium can be unilateral, bilateral, symmetric, or asysmmetric.

HP:0009761.label: Anterior clefting of vertebral bodies
HP:0009761.definition: Anterior schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.

HP:0009762.label: Facial wrinkling
HP:0009762.definition: Excessive wrinkling of the skin of the face.

HP:0009763.label: Limb pain
HP:0009763.definition: Chronic pain in the limbs with no clear focal etiology.

HP:0009765.label: Low hanging columella
HP:0009765.definition: Columella extending inferior to the level of the nasal base, when viewed from the side.
exact_synonyms: Extension of the columella below the ala nasi
related_synonyms: Columella extends below the ala nasi

HP:0009767.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0009767.definition: Small or missing phalangeal bones of the fingers of the hand.

HP:0009768.label: Broad phalanges of the hand
HP:0009768.definition: Increased width of the phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Widening of phalanges of the hand

HP:0009769.label: Bullet-shaped phalanges of the hand
HP:0009769.definition: The presence of short and wide phalanges which taper distally ("bullet shaped").
exact_synonyms: Conical bullet-shaped distal ends of phalanges

HP:0009771.label: Osteolytic defects of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0009771.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Breakdown of small bones of fingers

HP:0009772.label: Patchy sclerosis of finger phalanx
HP:0009772.definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in finger bone
Patchy sclerosis of the phalanges of the hand

HP:0009773.label: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand
HP:0009773.definition: Fusion of two or more phalangeal bones of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Synostosis involving phalanges of the hand
Fused finger bones of the hand

HP:0009774.label: Triangular shaped phalanges of the hand

HP:0009775.label: Amniotic constriction ring
HP:0009775.definition: Annular constrictions around the digits, limbs, or trunk, occurring congenitally (sometimes causing intrauterine autoamputation) and also associated with a wide variety of disorders. Constrictive amniotic bands are the result of primary amniotic rupture, which can lead to entanglement of fetal tissue (especially limbs) in fibrous amniotic strands.
HP:0009775.comment: Pseudoainhum is a rare condition of unknown etiology that produces digital constricting rings, most commonly on the small fingers.

HP:0009776.label: Adactyly
HP:0009776.definition: The absence of all phalanges of all the digits of a limb and the associated soft tissues.
HP:0009776.comment: This descriptor does not require absence of the metacarpal or metatarsal bones. A qualifying phrase is added to specify which limb has the attribute of adactyly.

HP:0009777.label: Absent thumb
HP:0009777.definition: Absent thumb, i.e., the absence of both phalanges of a thumb and the associated soft tissues.

HP:0009778.label: Short thumb
HP:0009778.definition: Hypoplasia (congenital reduction in size) of the thumb.

HP:0009779.label: 3-4 toe syndactyly
HP:0009779.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes three and four.

HP:0009780.label: Iliac horns
HP:0009780.definition: Horn-like malformations of the iliac crests with symmetrical bilateral central posterior iliac processes. A characteristic finding in the Nail-Patella syndrome. Iliac horns are visible on X-ray and may be palpable, but are asymptomatic.

HP:0009781.label: Lester's sign
HP:0009781.definition: A zone of darker pigmentation around the central part of the iris with a roughly cloverleaf or flower shape.

HP:0009782.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the biceps
HP:0009782.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the biceps muscle.

HP:0009784.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the triceps
HP:0009784.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the triceps muscle.

HP:0009786.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the musculature of the thigh
HP:0009786.definition: Absence or underdevelopment involving the musculature of the thigh.

HP:0009787.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the quadriceps
HP:0009787.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the quadriceps muscle.

HP:0009789.label: Perianal abscess
HP:0009789.definition: The presence of an abscess located around the anus.

HP:0009790.label: Hemisacrum
HP:0009790.definition: A hemisacral defect involving the sacral vertebrae S2 to S5. In hemisacrum, the first sacral vertebra is intact and there is agenesis involving only S2-S5.

HP:0009791.label: Bifid sacrum
HP:0009791.definition: Presence of a bifid sacral bone.

HP:0009792.label: Teratoma
HP:0009792.comment: Teratomas are germ-cell tumors commonly composed of multiple cell types derived from one or more of the three germ layers. They derive from embryonic pluripotent cells and may have various degrees of maturation, according to which they are classified as mature, immature, and malignant. Teratomas are found with decreasing frequency in the ovaries and testis, mediastinum, retroperitoneal space, sacrococcygeal zone, pineal and other intracranial locations.

HP:0009793.label: Presacral teratoma
HP:0009793.definition: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma located anterior to the sacrum and entirely inside the body (Altman type IV).
HP:0009793.comment: Sacrococcygeal teratomas are thought to originate from multipotential cells in Henson's node, which migrates caudally to rest in the coccyx.

HP:0009794.label: Branchial anomaly
HP:0009794.definition: Congenital developmental defect arising from the primitive branchial apparatus.
HP:0009794.comment: During embryonic development the major head and neck structures are formed from the five pharyngeal arches (bands of tissue). Incomplete, failed or persistent embryonic development of these arches results in several anomalies or defects in the neck.

HP:0009795.label: Branchial fistula
HP:0009795.definition: A congenital fistula in the neck resulting from incomplete closure of a branchial cleft.

HP:0009796.label: Branchial cyst
HP:0009796.definition: A branchial cyst is a remnant of embryonic development resulting from a failure of obliteration of a branchial cleft and consists of a subcutaneous cystic mass. Cysts are located anterior or posterior to the ear or in the submandibular region.
HP:0009796.comment: Branchial cyst have to be distinguished from the preauricular cysts and sinuses, which are ectodermal remnants from an aberrant development of the auditory tubercles, tend to be bilateral, and are localized anterior to the tragus of the ear.

HP:0009797.label: Cholesteatoma
HP:0009797.definition: Cholesteatoma is a benign but potentially destructive growth consisting of keratinizing epithelium located in the middle ear and/or mastoid process. In cholesteatoma, a skin cyst grows into the middle ear and mastoid. The cyst is not cancerous but can erode tissue and cause destruction of the ear.

HP:0009798.label: Euthyroid goiter
HP:0009798.definition: A goiter that is not associated with functional thyroid abnormalities.

HP:0009799.label: Supernumerary spleens
HP:0009799.definition: The presence of two or more accessory spleens.

HP:0009800.label: Maternal diabetes
HP:0009800.definition: Maternal diabetes can either be a gestational, mostly type 2 diabetes, or a type 1 diabetes. Essential is the resulting maternal hyperglycemia as a non-specific teratogen, imposing the same risk of congenital malformations to pregnant women with both type 1 and type2 diabetes.

HP:0009802.label: Aplasia of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0009802.definition: Absence of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.
related_synonyms: Absent finger bone of the hand

HP:0009803.label: Short phalanx of finger
HP:0009803.definition: Short (hypoplastic) phalanx of finger, affecting one or more phalanges.

HP:0009804.label: Tooth agenesis
HP:0009804.definition: The absence of one or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop
HP:0009804.comment: Teeth agenesis needs to be confirmed by X-rays. Teeth agenesis encompasses hypodontia, oligodontia, and anodontia. The total number and the type of teeth missing should be added to the description. The clinical absence of a tooth due to a disturbed eruption should not be termed teeth agenesis but a missing tooth.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of some teeth

HP:0009805.label: Low-output congestive heart failure
HP:0009805.definition: A form of heart failure characterized by reduced cardiac output. This may be seen in patients with heart failure owing to ischemic heart disease, hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and other causes.

HP:0009806.label: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
HP:0009806.definition: A form of diabetes insipidus caused by failure of the kidneys to respond to vasopressin (AVP).

HP:0009808.label: Anomaly of the upper limb diaphyses
HP:0009808.definition: A structural abnormality of a diaphysis of the arm.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of shaft of long bone of the upper limbs
Abnormality involving the diaphyses of the upper limbs
Diaphyseal abnormality of the upper limbs

HP:0009809.label: Abnormal upper limb metaphysis morphology
HP:0009809.definition: An anomaly of one or more metaphyses of the arms.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the wide portion of upper limb bone
Metaphyseal abnormality of the upper limbs

HP:0009810.label: Abnormality of upper limb joint
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the joints of the upper limbs

HP:0009811.label: Abnormality of the elbow
HP:0009811.definition: An anomaly of the joint that connects the upper and the lower arm.

HP:0009812.label: Amelia involving the upper limbs
HP:0009812.definition: Amelia of one or both upper limbs.

HP:0009813.label: Upper limb phocomelia
