HP:0009813.definition: Missing or malformed long bones of the upper limbs with the distal parts (the hands) connected to the variably shortened or even absent upper extremity, leading to a flipper-like appearance, as opposed to other forms of limb malformations were either the whole limb is missing (such as amelia), or the distal part of a limb is absent (peromelia).

HP:0009814.label: Upper limb peromelia
HP:0009814.definition: Peromelia affecting only the upper limbs. That is, the distal parts of the arm are missing leading to stump formation.

HP:0009815.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the extremities
HP:0009815.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the extremities.

HP:0009816.label: Lower limb undergrowth
HP:0009816.definition: Leg shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the lower extremity.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia involving bones of the lower limbs

HP:0009817.label: Aplasia involving bones of the lower limbs
exact_synonyms: Absent bones of the lower limbs

HP:0009818.label: Amelia involving the lower limbs
HP:0009818.definition: Complete or near-complete absence of a leg.

HP:0009819.label: Lower limb phocomelia
HP:0009819.definition: Phocomelia affecting only the lower limbs.

HP:0009820.label: Lower limb peromelia
HP:0009820.definition: Peromelia affecting only the lower limbs. That is, the distal parts of the leg are missing leading to stump formation.

HP:0009821.label: Forearm undergrowth
HP:0009821.definition: Forearm shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the forearm.

HP:0009823.label: Aplasia involving bones of the upper limbs
exact_synonyms: Absent bones of the upper limbs

HP:0009824.label: Upper limb undergrowth
HP:0009824.definition: Arm shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the upper extremity.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia involving bones of the upper limbs

HP:0009825.label: Aplasia involving bones of the extremities

HP:0009826.label: Limb undergrowth
HP:0009826.definition: Limb shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the extremities.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia involving bones of the extremities

HP:0009827.label: Amelia
HP:0009827.definition: Congenital absence (aplasia) of one or more limbs.

HP:0009828.label: Peromelia
HP:0009828.definition: The distal parts of the limbs are missing leading to a stump formation.

HP:0009829.label: Phocomelia
HP:0009829.definition: Missing or malformed long bones of the extremities with the distal parts (such as hands and/or feet) connected to the variably shortened or even absent extremity, leading to a flipper-like appearance, as opposed to other forms of limb malformations were either the hole limb is missing (such as amelia), or the distal part of a limb is absent (peromelia).

HP:0009830.label: Peripheral neuropathy
HP:0009830.definition: Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.
HP:0009830.comment: Terms from this subhierarchy should be used to describe functional abnormalities seen in peripheral neuropathy. Morphological abnormalities should be coded separately.

HP:0009831.label: Mononeuropathy
HP:0009831.definition: A focal lesion of a single peripheral nerve. Damage to a sensory nerve is accompanied by sensory impairment of all modalities in the affected anatomic distribution.

HP:0009832.label: Abnormal distal phalanx morphology of finger
HP:0009832.definition: Any anomaly of distal phalanx of finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the distal phalanx of finger
Abnormality of the outermost finger bone
Abnormality of the distal phalanges of the hand
Abnormal terminal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009833.label: Abnormal middle phalanx morphology of the hand
HP:0009833.definition: An anomaly of middle phalanx of finger.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the middle finger bones of the hand
Abnormality of the middle phalanges of the hand

HP:0009834.label: Abnormal proximal phalanx morphology of the hand
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the proximal phalanges of the hand
Abnormality of the innermost finger bones of the hand

HP:0009835.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the distal phalanges of the hand
HP:0009835.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the distal phalanges.
exact_synonyms: Absent/small outermost finger bone of the hand
Absent/underdeveloped outermost finger bone of the hand

HP:0009836.label: Broad distal phalanx of finger
HP:0009836.definition: Abnormally wide (broad) distal phalanx of finger.
HP:0009836.comment: This term should be reserved for a radiological finding of increased width of the distal finger phalanx (bone). The term Broad fingertip should be used to denote a clinical impression of increased side to side width of the distance part of the finger.
exact_synonyms: Broad, square ends of distal phalanges
Broad distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009837.label: Bullet-shaped distal phalanges of the hand
HP:0009837.definition: Short and wide distal phalanges that taper distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped outermost finger bone of the hand

HP:0009838.label: Curved distal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Curved outermost finger bone of the hand

HP:0009839.label: Osteolytic defects of the distal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Osteolytic defects of the outermost finger bone of the hand

HP:0009840.label: Patchy sclerosis of distal phalanx of finger
HP:0009840.definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of the distal phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in outermost finger bone
Patchy sclerosis of the distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009843.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the middle phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Absent/underdeveloped middle finger bone of the hand
Absent/small middle finger bone of the hand

HP:0009844.label: Broad middle phalanx of finger
HP:0009844.definition: Increased width of the middle phalanx of finger.
exact_synonyms: Broad middle phalanges of the hand

HP:0009845.label: Bullet-shaped middle phalanges of the hand
HP:0009845.definition: Any of the middle phalanges with short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.

HP:0009846.label: Curved middle phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Curved middle finger bonds of the hand

HP:0009847.label: Osteolytic defects of the middle phalanges of the hand

HP:0009848.label: Patchy sclerosis of middle phalanx of finger
HP:0009848.definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of one or more of the middle phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in the middle finger bones of the hand
Patchy sclerosis of the middle phalanges of the hand

HP:0009849.label: Symphalangism of middle phalanx of finger
HP:0009849.definition: Fusion of a middle phalanx of a finger with another bone.

HP:0009850.label: Triangular shaped middle phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped middle finger bones of the hand

HP:0009851.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the proximal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Absent/small innermost finger bones of the hand
Absent/underdeveloped innermost finger bones of the hand

HP:0009852.label: Broad proximal phalanges of the hand
HP:0009852.definition: Increased width of the proximal phalanges of the finger.
exact_synonyms: Broad innermost finger bones of the hand
Wide innermost finger bones of the hand

HP:0009853.label: Bullet-shaped proximal phalanges of the hand
HP:0009853.definition: Short and wide proximal phalanges that taper distally . Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped innermost finger bones of the hand

HP:0009854.label: Curved proximal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Curved innermost finger bones of the hand

HP:0009855.label: Osteolytic defects of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009856.label: Patchy sclerosis of proximal phalanx of finger
HP:0009856.definition: Uneven increase in bone density of the proximal phalanges of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in innermost finger bone
Patchy sclerosis of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009857.label: Symphalangism affecting the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009858.label: Triangular shaped proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009875.label: Triangular shaped distal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped outermost bone of the hand

HP:0009878.label: Cerebellar ataxia associated with quadrupedal gait
HP:0009878.definition: The presence of cerebellar signs and symptoms such as lack of balance associated with quadrupedal gait (locomotion on all four extremities with a 'bear-like' gait with the legs held straight).

HP:0009879.label: Simplified gyral pattern
HP:0009879.definition: An abnormality of the cerebral cortex with fewer gyri but with normal cortical thickness. This pattern is usually often associated with congenital microcephaly.

HP:0009880.label: Broad distal phalanges of all fingers
HP:0009880.definition: Abnormally wide (broad) distal phalanx of finger of all fingers.

HP:0009881.label: Aplasia of distal finger phalanx
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the distal phalanges of the hand
Absent distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009882.label: Short distal phalanx of finger
HP:0009882.definition: Short distance from the end of the finger to the most distal interphalangeal crease or the distal interphalangeal joint flexion point. That is, hypoplasia of one or more of the distal phalanx of finger.
HP:0009882.comment: This term differs from Partial absence of the finger because in that term, the phalanx must be missing, whereas in this term it may be small, but present. Distal phalangeal lengths can be assessed subjectively by comparing that digit segment to the rest of the digit, to other normal digits in that patient, or to typical patients of that age or build. Regarding the subjective definition, for individuals who do not have flexion creases, one may determine this by flexing the DIP joint and estimating the length of the terminal segment of the digit. Alternatively, one may be able to palpate the joint.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009883.label: Duplication of the distal phalanx of hand
HP:0009883.definition: This term applies if one or more of the distal phalanges of the hand are either partially duplicated, depending on severity leading to a broad or bifid appearance of the phalanges, or completely duplicated.
exact_synonyms: Duplication of the outermost bone of hand
Partial/complete duplication of the distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009884.label: Tapered distal phalanges of finger
HP:0009884.definition: A reduction in diameter of the distal phalanx of finger towards the distal end.
exact_synonyms: Tapered distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0009886.label: Trichorrhexis nodosa
HP:0009886.definition: Trichorrhexis nodosa is the formation of nodes along the hair shaft through which breakage readily occurs. It is thus a focal defect in the hair fiber that is characterized by thickening or weak points (nodes) that cause the hair to break off easily. The result is defective, abnormally fragile hair.

HP:0009888.label: Abnormality of secondary sexual hair
HP:0009888.definition: Abnormality of the growth of secondary sexual hair, which normally ensues during puberty. In males, secondary sexual hair usually comprises body hair, including underarm, abdominal, chest, and pubic hair. In females, secondary sexual hair usually comprises a lesser degree of body hair, most prominently underarm and pubic hair.

HP:0009889.label: Localized hirsutism
HP:0009889.definition: Abnormally increased hair growth with a localized distribution.

HP:0009890.label: High anterior hairline
HP:0009890.definition: Distance between the hairline (trichion) and the glabella (the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose), in the midline, more than two SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between the hairline and the glabella.
HP:0009890.comment: This feature gives the appearance of a tall forehead, and may or may not include reduction of hair in the temporal areas. This can be distinguished from male pattern baldness as the hairline is the superior boundary of the muscular forehead, which can be actively wrinkled, in contrast to the scalp where no wrinkling can occur. In addition, texture of the skin of the scalp differs from the texture of the skin over the forehead.

HP:0009891.label: Underdeveloped supraorbital ridges
HP:0009891.definition: Flatness of the supraorbital portion of the frontal bones.

HP:0009892.label: Anotia
HP:0009892.definition: Complete absence of any auricular structures.
HP:0009892.comment: Complete absence of the auricle (external ear). The skin of the cheek passes smoothly over the aural area without definite elevation or depression.

HP:0009893.label: Telangiectasia of the ear
HP:0009893.definition: The presence of telangiectasia of the ear.

HP:0009894.label: Thickened ears
HP:0009894.definition: Increased thickness of the external ear.

HP:0009895.label: Abnormality of the crus of the helix
HP:0009895.definition: An abnormality of the crus of the helix, which is the horizontal piece of cartilage located outside the ear canal that divides the upper and lower parts of the ear.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the crus of the ear

HP:0009896.label: Abnormal antitragus morphology
HP:0009896.definition: An abnormality of the antitragus, which is a small tubercle opposite to the tragus of the ear. The antitragus and the tragus are separated by the intertragic notch.

HP:0009897.label: Horizontal crus of helix
HP:0009897.definition: An abnormal horizontal axis orientation of the crus of the helix. That is, the main axis of the crus of the helix is perpendicular to the medial longitudinal axis of the ear, instead of sloping inferoposteriorly.
HP:0009897.comment: The term 'railroad track sign' has been used to describe prominent horizontal crus of the helix in combination with prominent and parallel inferior crus of the antihelix. It is preferable to simply describe each component separately.
exact_synonyms: Horizontal orientation of the ear crus
Horizontal orientation of the crus of helix

HP:0009898.label: Underdeveloped crus of the helix
HP:0009898.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the crus of the helix. That is, flatter and/or shorter crus helix than average.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the crus of the ear

HP:0009899.label: Prominent crus of helix
HP:0009899.definition: The presence of an abnormally prominent of the crus of the helix. That is, development of the crus helix to the same degree as an average antihelix stem or helix.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal prominence of the crus of the ear

HP:0009900.label: Unilateral deafness
HP:0009900.definition: A unilateral absence of sensory perception of sound.

HP:0009901.label: Crumpled ear
HP:0009901.definition: Distortion of the course of the normal folds of the ear and the appearance of supernumerary crura and folds.
HP:0009901.comment: This is distinct from Stahl ear and Shell ear, with which the term has sometimes been conflated. The appearance often changes markedly after birth.

HP:0009902.label: Cleft helix
HP:0009902.definition: A notched form of the helix of the ear. That is, a defect in the continuity of the helix, which may occur at any point along its length.
HP:0009902.comment: This may take the form of a sharp cleft or a less well-demarcated area. This should be distinguished from a Question-mark ear. If the defect or notch occurs at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix, it should be coded as Darwin notch of the helix.

HP:0009903.label: Conjunctival nodule
HP:0009903.definition: Presence of nodules in the conjunctiva of the eye.

HP:0009905.label: Thin ear helix
HP:0009905.definition: Decreased thickness of the helix of the ear.

HP:0009906.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the earlobes
HP:0009906.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the ear lobes.

HP:0009907.label: Attached earlobe
HP:0009907.definition: Attachment of the lobe to the side of the face at the lowest point of the lobe without curving upward.
HP:0009907.comment: The earlobe does not have a dependent portion.

HP:0009908.label: Anterior creases of earlobe
HP:0009908.definition: Sharply demarcated, typically linear and approximately horizontal, indentations in the outer surface of the ear lobe.
HP:0009908.comment: Shallow grooves or indentations are quite common, especially in large lobes. Ear lobe creases may arise postnatally. Posterior helical pits can be a related finding but should be assessed and coded separately.

HP:0009909.label: Uplifted earlobe
HP:0009909.definition: An abnormal orientation of the earlobes such that they point out- and upward. That is, the lateral surface of ear lobe faces superiorly.
HP:0009909.comment: This finding is characteristic of Mowat-Wilson syndrome.

HP:0009910.label: Aplasia of the middle ear ossicles
HP:0009910.definition: Absence of the middle ear ossicles, malleus, incus, and stapes.

HP:0009911.label: Abnormal temporal bone morphology
HP:0009911.definition: Abnormality of the temporal bone of the skull, which is situated at the sides and base of the skull roughly underlying the region of the face known as the temple.

HP:0009912.label: Abnormal tragus morphology
HP:0009912.comment: The tragus is the small pointed eminence of the external ear, situated in front of the concha, and projecting backward over the auditory canal.

HP:0009913.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the tragus
HP:0009913.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the tragus.

HP:0009914.label: Cyclopia
HP:0009914.definition: Cyclopia is a congenital abnormality in which there is only one eye. That eye is centrally placed in the area normally occupied by the root of the nose.

HP:0009915.label: Corneal asymmetry
HP:0009915.definition: The presence of a size difference between the left and right cornea.

HP:0009916.label: Anisocoria
HP:0009916.definition: Anisocoria, or unequal pupil size, may represent a benign physiologic variant or a manifestation of disease.
HP:0009916.comment: Pathologic anisocoria can reflect an abnormality of the musculature of the iris or of the sympathetic or prasympathetic innervation of the iris.

HP:0009917.label: Persistent pupillary membrane
HP:0009917.definition: The presence of remnants of a fetal membrane that persist as strands of tissue crossing the pupil.
HP:0009917.comment: The tunica vasculosa lentis anterior (pupillary membrane) normally undergoes atrophy in the third trimester of pregnancy. If the membrane does not completely atrophy, then remnants of membranous structures can be observed to emrge from the iris.

HP:0009918.label: Ectopia pupillae
HP:0009918.definition: A malposition of the pupil owing to a developmental defect of the iris.

HP:0009919.label: Retinoblastoma
HP:0009919.definition: A tumor of the eye originating from cells of the retina.

HP:0009920.label: Nevus of Ota
HP:0009920.definition: A dermal melanocytic hamartoma that presents as bluish hyperpigmentation on the face along the first or second branches of the trigeminal nerve. Nevus of Ota may involve the sclera.

HP:0009921.label: Duane anomaly
HP:0009921.definition: A condition associated with a limitation of the horizontal ocular movement with retraction of the globe and narrowing of the palpebral fissure on adduction
exact_synonyms: Limited eye movement from Duane anomaly
Limited eye motility from Duane anomaly
related_synonyms: Globe retraction and deviation on adduction

HP:0009922.label: Vascular remnant arising from the disk
HP:0009922.definition: Persistence of the hyaloid artery, which is the embryonic artery that runs from the optic disc to the posterior lens capsule may persist; the site of attachment may form an opacity. The hyaloid artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery, and usually regresses completely before birth.

HP:0009924.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the nose
HP:0009924.definition: Underdevelopment or absence of the nose or parts thereof.

HP:0009926.label: Epiphora
HP:0009926.definition: Abnormally increased lacrimation, that is, excessive tearing (watering eye).
HP:0009926.comment: Epiphora or tearing is the presence of a watering eye, which is a common complaint for referrals to oculoplastics clinics for evaluation. The etiology of tearing can be divided into two categories: reflex tearing and reduced tear outflow. Reflex tearing is usually secondary to dry eye, inflammation, allergy or other ocular surface disorders, whereas primary hypersecretion of the lacrimal glands is rare. Reduced tear outflow is due to eyelid malposition, tear pump dysfunction caused by eyelid laxity, or obstruction at any portion of the nasaolacrimal drainage system.

HP:0009927.label: Aplasia of the nose
HP:0009927.definition: Complete absence of all nasal structures.

HP:0009928.label: Thick nasal alae
HP:0009928.definition: Increase in bulk of the ala nasi.

HP:0009929.label: Abnormal columella morphology
HP:0009929.definition: A structural abnormality of the columella.
HP:0009929.comment: The columella is the fleshy external end of the nasal septum.

HP:0009930.label: Asymmetry of the nares
HP:0009930.definition: Asymmetry or size difference between the left and right nostril.

HP:0009931.label: Enlarged naris
HP:0009931.comment: The nostrils or nares are typically symmetric, wide openings. They should be assessed with the face at rest to avoid the effect of flared alae nasi that occurs with distress. Note that the nares change with age, from rounded in infancy to elongated at a later age.

HP:0009932.label: Single naris
HP:0009932.definition: The presence of only a single nostril.
HP:0009932.comment: The single opening may occur in the midline or it can occur on one side, that is, it can be symmetric or asymmetric. Although the columella is invariably absent, this is implicit and does not need to be separately specified.

HP:0009933.label: Narrow naris
HP:0009933.definition: Slender, slit-like aperture of the nostril.

HP:0009934.label: Supernumerary naris
HP:0009934.definition: The presence of more than two nostrils.

HP:0009935.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the nasal septum
HP:0009935.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the nasal septum.

HP:0009938.label: Sunken cheeks
HP:0009938.definition: Lack or loss of the soft tissues between the zygomata and mandible.

HP:0009939.label: Mandibular aplasia
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the lower jaw bone
Failure of development of lower jaw

HP:0009940.label: Asymmetry of the mandible
HP:0009940.definition: Lack of symmetry between the left and right mandible.
exact_synonyms: Lower jaw shifted to one side

HP:0009941.label: Asymmetry of the mouth
HP:0009941.definition: The presence of an asymmetric mouth.

HP:0009942.label: Duplication of thumb phalanx
HP:0009942.definition: Complete or partial duplication of the phalanges of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx), a partially fused appearance of the two bones (bifid), two separate bones appearing side to side, or completely duplicated phalanges (proximal and distal phalanx of the thumb and/or 1st metacarpal). In contrast to the phalanges of the digits 2-5 (proximal, middle and distal), the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Complete/partial duplication of phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009943.label: Complete duplication of thumb phalanx
HP:0009943.definition: A complete duplication affecting one or more of the phalanges of the thumb. As opposed to a partial duplication were there is still a variable degree of fusion between the duplicated bones, a complete duplication leads to two separate bones appearing side to side (radio-ulnar axis) as seen on x-rays. A duplication leading to an accessory bone appearing in the proximo-distal axis on x-rays, this is actually a different entity called a Pseudoepiphyses (see according terms) sometimes also referred to as Hyperphalangism.
exact_synonyms: Complete duplication of the phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009944.label: Partial duplication of thumb phalanx
HP:0009944.definition: A partial duplication, depending on severity leading to a broad or bifid appearance, affecting one or more of the phalanges of the thumb. As opposed to a complete duplication there is still a variable degree of fusion between the duplicated bones.
exact_synonyms: Partial duplication of the thumb bones
Partial duplication of the phalanges of the thumb

HP:0009945.label: Duplication of phalanx of 2nd finger
HP:0009945.definition: This term applies if one or more of the phalanges of the 2nd finger are either partially duplicated, depending on severity leading to a broad or bifid appearance of the phalanges, or completely duplicated.

HP:0010009.label: Abnormal 1st metacarpal morphology
HP:0010009.definition: A structural anomaly of the first metacarpal.
HP:0010009.comment: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010010.label: Abnormal 2nd metacarpal morphology
HP:0010010.definition: Any abnormality of the second metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 2nd long bone of hand

HP:0010011.label: Abnormal 3rd metacarpal morphology
HP:0010011.definition: Any abnormality of the third metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 3rd long bone of hand

HP:0010012.label: Abnormal 4th metacarpal morphology
HP:0010012.definition: Any abnormality of the fourth metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 4th long bone of hand

HP:0010013.label: Abnormal 5th metacarpal morphology
HP:0010013.definition: Any abnormality of the fifth metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 5th long bone of hand

HP:0010014.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010014.definition: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5 (whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits). The epiphysis of the first metacarpal is localized at the proximal end (as seen in the proximal phalanges of the other digits), whereas the epiphyses of the other metacarpal bones are located at the distal end. This term applies if the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal is in any way abnormal, referring to age and gender depending norms, as seen on x-rays.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010015.label: Absent epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010016.label: Bracket epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010016.definition: An epiphysis that curves around from its transverse orientation to a longitudinal one from proximal to distal along one side of the phalanx, thus resembling the letter 'C' and forming a bracket around the diaphysis. This results in a so called delta phalanx characterized by a triangular or trapezoidal shaped bone with a C-shaped epiphyseal plate.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010017.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010017.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010018.label: Enlarged epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010018.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphyses of the 1st metacarpal with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010019.label: Fragmentation of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010019.definition: Epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal having multiple bony fragments.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of the end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010020.label: Irregular epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010020.definition: Uneven radiographic opacity of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010021.label: Ivory epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010021.definition: The epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal appears hard and dense like ivory. An ivory epiphysis has a uniformly dense appearance on radiographs.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010022.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010022.definition: The epiphysis of the first metacarpal is localized at the proximal end of the metacarpal bone although an accessory epiphysis may be located at the distal end of the metacarpal.
HP:0010022.comment: This feature can be seen for example in Holt-Oram Syndrome.

HP:0010023.label: Small epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010023.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010024.label: Epiphyseal stippling of the first metacarpal
HP:0010024.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphyses of the first metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in the end part of the first long bone of hand
Stippling of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal

HP:0010025.label: Triangular epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of the 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010026.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010026.definition: Aplasia or Hypoplasia affecting the 1st metacarpal. In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5 (whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits).

HP:0010027.label: Broad 1st metacarpal
HP:0010027.definition: Increased width of the 1st metacarpal. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0010028.label: Bullet-shaped 1st metacarpal
HP:0010028.definition: The presence of short and wide 1st metacarpal which tapers distally ("bullet shaped").

HP:0010029.label: Curved 1st metacarpal
HP:0010029.definition: A deviation from the normal straight shape of the first metacarpal.

HP:0010030.label: Osteolytic defects of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010030.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the 1st metacarpal.
HP:0010030.comment: Osteolytic lesions are visible on radiography as demarcated areas of radiolucency ('darkness').

HP:0010031.label: Patchy sclerosis of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010031.definition: Uneven increase in bone density within the 1st metacarpal.
exact_synonyms: Uneven increase in bone density in 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010033.label: Triangular shaped 1st metacarpal
HP:0010033.definition: This term applies to a triangular shaped 1st metacarpal.
HP:0010033.comment: In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx (in this case metacarpal, see explanation above).
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped 1st long bone of hand

HP:0010034.label: Short 1st metacarpal
HP:0010034.definition: A developmental defect characterized by reduced length of the first metacarpal (long bone) of the hand.
HP:0010034.comment: In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0010035.label: Aplasia of the 1st metacarpal
HP:0010035.definition: Absent first metacarpal (long bone) of the hand.
HP:0010035.comment: In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.

HP:0010036.definition: Aplasia or Hypoplasia affecting the 2nd metacarpal.

HP:0010037.label: Aplasia of the 2nd metacarpal
HP:0010037.definition: Absence of the second long bone of the hand.

HP:0010038.label: Short 2nd metacarpal
HP:0010038.definition: Short second metacarpal bone because of developmental hypoplasia.

HP:0010039.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the 3rd metacarpal
HP:0010039.definition: Aplasia or Hypoplasia affecting the 3rd metacarpal.

HP:0010040.definition: Absence of the third long bone of the hand.

HP:0010043.definition: Absence of the fourth long bone of the hand.

HP:0010045.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the 5th metacarpal
HP:0010045.definition: Aplasia or Hypoplasia affecting the 5th metacarpal.

HP:0010046.definition: Absence of the fifth long bone of the hand.

HP:0010048.label: Aplasia of metacarpal bones
HP:0010048.definition: Developmental defect associated with absence of one or more metacarpal bones.

HP:0010049.label: Short metacarpal
HP:0010049.definition: Diminished length of one or more metacarpal bones in relation to the others of the same hand or to the contralateral metacarpal.
HP:0010049.comment: Short metacarpals can involve any of the metacarpal bones, and the affected ray should be specified. The assessment of isolated short metacarpal can be made by viewing the dorsum of the hand when clenched. Note that if metacarpals F2-5 are affected, the correct term is Short palm.

HP:0010051.label: Deviation of the hallux
HP:0010051.definition: Displacement of the big toe from its normal position.

HP:0010052.label: Abnormal morphology of the proximal phalanx of the hallux
HP:0010052.definition: An abnormal shape or form of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
HP:0010052.comment: In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, the proximal phalanx of the big toe is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metatarsal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the proximal phalanx of the hallux

HP:0010053.label: Abnormality of the distal phalanx of the hallux
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the outermost bone of the big toe

HP:0010054.label: Abnormality of the first metatarsal bone
HP:0010054.definition: An anomaly of the first metatarsal bone.
HP:0010054.comment: In contrast to the metatarsals 2-5, the first metatarsal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5, whereas the proximal phalanx of the big toe is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits. This term applies to abnormalities of the first metatarsal.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 1st long bone of foot

HP:0010055.label: Broad hallux
HP:0010055.definition: Visible increase in width of the hallux without an increase in the dorso-ventral dimension.
HP:0010055.comment: Note that girth may be increased in a broad hallux, but this must be distinguished from Macrodactyly because there the length is also increased. This assessment may be difficult when the hallux is short.

exact_synonyms: Broad middle bones of the toes

HP:0010196.label: Bullet-shaped middle phalanx of toe
HP:0010196.definition: An abnormal morphology of one or more middle phalanges of the toes, with a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped middle phalanges of the toes
Bullet-shaped middle bones of the toes

HP:0010197.label: Curved middle phalanx of toe
HP:0010197.definition: A deviation from the normal straight form of one or more middle toe phalanges.
exact_synonyms: Curved middle bones of the toes
Curved middle phalanges of the toes

HP:0010198.label: Osteolytic defects of the middle phalanges of the toes

HP:0010199.label: Patchy sclerosis of middle phalanx of toe
HP:0010199.definition: Patchy (irregular) increase in bone density of one or more of the middle phalanges of the toes. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.
exact_synonyms: Patchy sclerosis of the middle phalanges of the toes
Uneven increase in bone density in middle toe bone

HP:0010200.label: Symphalangism affecting the middle phalanges of the toes

HP:0010201.label: Triangular shaped middle phalanges of the toes
exact_synonyms: Triangular shaped middle bones of toes

HP:0010202.label: Duplication of middle phalanx of toe
HP:0010202.definition: Partial or complete duplication of a middle phalanx of toe.
exact_synonyms: Partial/complete duplication of the middle phalanges of the toes
Partial/complete duplication of the middle bones of the toes

HP:0010203.label: Aplasia/hypoplasia of proximal toe phalanx
HP:0010203.definition: Absence (agenesis) or underdevelopment of the proximal phalanx of the toe.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010204.label: Broad proximal phalanx of toe
HP:0010204.definition: An increase in width of one ore more proximal toe phalanges.

HP:0010205.label: Bullet-shaped proximal toe phalanx
HP:0010205.definition: An abnormal morphology of one or more of the proximal phalanges of the toes, with a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.
exact_synonyms: Bullet-shaped proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010206.label: Curved proximal toe phalanx
HP:0010206.definition: A deviation from the normal straight shape of a proximal phalanx of one or more toes.
exact_synonyms: Curved proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010207.label: Osteolytic defect of the proximal toe phalanx
HP:0010207.definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the proximal toe phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Osteolytic defects of the proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010208.label: Patchy sclerosis of proximal toe phalanx
HP:0010208.definition: Patchy (irregular) increase in bone density of one or more of the proximal phalanges of the toes. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.
exact_synonyms: Patchy sclerosis of the proximal phalanges of the toes
Uneven increase in bone density in innermost toe bone

HP:0010209.label: Symphalangism affecting the proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010210.label: Triangular shaped proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010211.label: Duplication of proximal phalanx of toe
HP:0010211.definition: Partial/complete duplication of a proximal phalanx of toe.
exact_synonyms: Partial/complete duplication of the proximal phalanges of the toes

HP:0010212.label: Flexion contracture of the hallux
HP:0010212.definition: One or more bent (flexed) joints of the first (big) toe that cannot be straightened actively or passively.
exact_synonyms: Joint contracture of the big toe

HP:0010213.label: Contracture of the tarsometatarsal joint of the hallux
HP:0010213.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion in the tarsometatarsal joint of the hallux due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. The tarsometatarsal joints of the feet are also called Lisfranc's joints.

HP:0010214.label: Contracture of the interphalangeal joint of the hallux
HP:0010214.definition: The interphalangeal joint of the big toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0010215.label: Contractures of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux
HP:0010215.definition: The joint between the first metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the first (big) toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0010219.label: Structural foot deformity
HP:0010219.definition: A foot deformity resulting due to an abnormality affecting the bones of the foot (as well as muscle and soft tissue). In contrast if only the muscle and soft tissue are affected the term positional foot deformity applies.

HP:0010220.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the 2nd metacarpal
HP:0010220.definition: Any abnormality of the epiphysis of the second metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the 2nd long bone of hand

HP:0010222.label: Abnormal 3rd metacarpal epiphysis morphology
HP:0010222.definition: Any abnormality of the epiphysis of the third metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the 3rd long bone of hand
Abnormality of the epiphysis of the 3rd metacarpal

HP:0010223.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the 3rd metacarpal
HP:0010223.definition: The normal epiphysis of the third metacarpal is localized at the distal end of the metacarpal bone. This term applies if an accessory epiphysis, located at the proximal end of the metacarpal bone, is present.

HP:0010224.label: Abnormal 4th metacarpal epiphysis morphology
HP:0010224.definition: Any abnormality of the epiphysis of the 4th metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the 4th metacarpal
Abnormality of the end part of the 4th long bone of hand

HP:0010225.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the 4th metacarpal
HP:0010225.definition: The normal epiphysis of the fourth metacarpal is localized at the distal end of the metacarpal bone. This term applies if an accessory epiphysis, located at the proximal end of the metacarpal bone, is present.

HP:0010226.label: Abnormal 5th metacarpal epiphysis morphology
HP:0010226.definition: Any abnormality of the epiphysis of the fifth metacarpal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the long bone of pinkie finger
Abnormality of the end part of the long bone of pinky finger
Abnormality of the epiphysis of the 5th metacarpal
Abnormality of the end part of the long bone of little finger

HP:0010227.label: Pseudoepiphysis of the 5th metacarpal
HP:0010227.definition: The normal epiphysis of the fifth metacarpal is localized at the distal end of the metacarpal bone. This term applies if an accessory epiphysis, located at the proximal end of the metacarpal bone, is present.

HP:0010228.label: Absent epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010228.definition: Absence of one or more epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers.

HP:0010229.label: Bracket epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010229.definition: Bracket epiphysis refers to an abnormality in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of finger bones

HP:0010230.label: Cone-shaped epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010230.definition: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphyses of the fingers of the hand, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of a phalanx.
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of finger bones

HP:0010231.label: Enlarged epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010231.definition: Abnormally large size of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of finger bones

HP:0010232.label: Fragmented finger phalanx epiphysis
HP:0010232.definition: Fragmented appearance of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers.
exact_synonyms: Fragmentation of end part of finger bones
Fragmentation of the epiphyses of the fingers
Fragmentation of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand

HP:0010233.label: Irregular epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010233.definition: Irregular radiographic opacity of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of finger bones

HP:0010234.label: Ivory epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010234.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density of end part of the hand bones

HP:0010235.label: Pseudoepiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010235.definition: A secondary ossification center in the phalanges of the hand that is distinct from the normal epiphysis that does not contribute to the longitudinal growth of a tubular bone.

HP:0010236.label: Small epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010236.definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers with respect to age-dependent norms.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of finger bones

HP:0010237.label: Epiphyseal stippling of finger phalanges
HP:0010237.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphyses of phalanges of the fingers.
exact_synonyms: Stippling of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
Stippling of the epiphyses of the fingers
Speckled calcifications in end part of finger bones

HP:0010238.label: Triangular epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand
HP:0010238.definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers of the hand.
exact_synonyms: Triangular end part of finger bones

HP:0010239.label: Aplasia of the middle phalanx of the hand
HP:0010239.definition: Absence of one or more middle phalanx of a finger.

HP:0010241.label: Short proximal phalanx of finger
HP:0010241.definition: Congenital hypoplasia of one or more proximal phalanx of finger.
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010243.definition: Any anomaly of distal epiphysis of phalanx of finger.

HP:0010245.label: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the innermost hand bones

HP:0010246.label: Absent epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Absent end part of the outermost hand bones

HP:0010247.label: Bracket epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand
HP:0010247.definition: An abnormality of the distal phalanges of the hand in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of the outermost hand bones

HP:0010248.label: Cone-shaped epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Cone-shaped end part of the outermost hand bones

HP:0010249.label: Enlarged epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand
exact_synonyms: Enlarged end part of the outermost hand bones

HP:0010250.label: Fragmentation of the epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010251.label: Irregular epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010252.label: Ivory epiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand
HP:0010252.definition: Distal epiphyses of the hand are hard and dense like ivory. Such an epiphysis has a uniformly dense appearance on radiographs.

HP:0010253.label: Pseudoepiphyses of the distal phalanges of the hand
HP:0010253.definition: A secondary ossification center in the distal phalanges of the hand that is distinct from the normal epiphysis that does not contribute to the longitudinal growth of a tubular bone.

HP:0010258.definition: An abnormality of the middle phalanges of the hand in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.

HP:0010261.definition: Fragmented appearance of the epiphyses of the middle phalanges of the hand.

HP:0010263.definition: Epiphyses of the middle phalanges of the hand are hard and dense like ivory. Such an epiphysis has a uniformly dense appearance on radiographs.

HP:0010264.definition: A secondary ossification center in the middle phalanges of the hand that is distinct from the normal epiphysis that does not contribute to the longitudinal growth of a tubular bone.

HP:0010269.label: Bracket epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand
HP:0010269.definition: An abnormality of the proximal phalanges of the hand in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.

HP:0010274.definition: Epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand are hard and dense like ivory. Such an epiphysis has a uniformly dense appearance on radiographs.

HP:0010275.label: Pseudoepiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand
HP:0010275.definition: A secondary ossification center in the proximal phalanges of the hand that is distinct from the normal epiphysis that does not contribute to the longitudinal growth of a tubular bone.

HP:0010276.label: Small epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010277.label: Stippling of the epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010278.label: Triangular epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010280.label: Stomatitis
HP:0010280.definition: Stomatitis is an inflammation of the mucous membranes of any of the structures in the mouth.

HP:0010281.label: Cleft lower lip
HP:0010281.definition: A gap in the lower lip.

HP:0010282.label: Thin lower lip vermilion
HP:0010282.definition: Height of the vermilion of the medial part of the lower lip more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the lower lip in the frontal view (subjective).
HP:0010282.comment: Normal values for the height of the vermilion are available [Farkas, 1981] but measurements are not commonly used. Most clinicians determine this feature subjectively. The height of the vermilion of the lower lip varies considerably among ethnic groups, and the vermilion should be compared to a population of same ethnic background. If the lower lip vermilion is thin, the inferior border of the vermilion is less curved, and on a profile view, the lower lip vermilion is less convex than usual.
exact_synonyms: Thin vermilion border of lower lip
Decreased height of lower lip vermilion
Decreased volume of lower lip vermilion

HP:0010284.label: Intra-oral hyperpigmentation
HP:0010284.definition: Increased pigmentation, either focal or generalized, of the mucosa of the mouth.
HP:0010284.comment: Pigmentation of alveolar ridges is common in people with dark skin pigmentation. This term encompasses a range of pigmentary findings, from freckles to generalized hyperpigmentation.

HP:0010285.label: Oral synechia
HP:0010285.definition: Fibrous band between the mucosal surfaces of the upper and lower alveolar ridges.
HP:0010285.comment: These bands must be distinguished from synechiaee between the tongue and palate (glossopalatal ankylosis) and from synechiae arising from the floor of the mouth (as in the subglossopalatal membrane), oropharyngeal isthmus (as in persistent buccopharyngeal membrane) or from the lower lip. If there is a complete soft tissue contiguity between the upper and lower alveolar ridges, the term, Fibrous syngnathia should be used instead.

HP:0010286.label: Abnormal salivary gland morphology
HP:0010286.definition: Any abnormality of the salivary glands, the exocrine glands that produce saliva.

HP:0010287.label: Abnormality of the submandibular glands
HP:0010287.definition: Any abnormality of the submandibular glands, which are the salivary glands that are located beneath the floor of the mouth, superior to the digastric muscles.

HP:0010288.label: Abnormality of the sublingual glands
HP:0010288.definition: Any abnormality of the sublingual glands, which are the salivary glands that are located beneath the floor of the mouth anterior to the submandibular glands.

HP:0010289.label: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
HP:0010289.definition: A gap (cleft) affecting one of the alveolar ridges, which are the protuberances in the mouth that contain the sockets (alveoli) of the teeth. An alveolar cleft can affect all structures of the alveolar ridge, including the gingiva, other mucosa, periosteum, alveolar bone, and teeth. Alveolar cleft occurs in response to divergence from normal development during frontonasal prominence growth, contact, and fusion. The most common alveolar portion of the cleft is located between the lateral incisor and the canine.
HP:0010289.comment: The palate develops from the frontonasal and maxillary prominences between 4 and 12 weeks of gestation. During gestational weeks 4 to 7, the primary palate originates from the median palatine process, which itself originated from frontonasal prominence. The lip, alveolus, and hard palate anterior to the incisive foramen all share this origin in development. During this period, disruptions of palatal development process can result in primary palate clefting. The secondary palate develops from the lateral palatine processes originating from the maxillary prominences between 7 and 12 weeks, and the hard palate posterior to incisive foramen and the soft palate are developmental products of this process. As such, disruptions during this time will result in secondary palate clefts. The alveolus is a component of the primary palate, and alveolar cleft results from mal-development of the frontonasal prominence. As such, it is most closely related to cleft lip and cleft palate. Generally, alveolar clefts are located between the lateral incisor and canine.
exact_synonyms: Cleft of alveolar ridge of maxilla

HP:0010290.label: Short hard palate
HP:0010290.definition: Distance between the labial point of the incisive papilla to the midline junction of the hard and soft palate more than 2 SD below the mean (objective) or apparently decreased length of the hard palate (subjective).
HP:0010290.comment: Objective measurement of the hard palate requires special instrumentation [Hall JG, Froster-Iskenius UG, Allanson JE, Gripp K, Slavotinek A. 2006. Handbook of Normal Physical Measurements. 2nd edition. Oxford Medical, publishers]. A short hard palate may be associated with velopharyngeal incompetence.

HP:0010291.label: Prominent palatine ridges
HP:0010291.definition: Increased size and/or number of soft tissue folds on the palatal side of the maxillary alveolar ridge.
HP:0010291.comment: Soft tissue folds are typically present on the lateral sides of the palate, especially anteriorly.

HP:0010292.label: Absent uvula
HP:0010292.comment: Sometimes accompanies a Submucous cleft palate, but this should be coded separately.

HP:0010293.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the uvula
HP:0010293.definition: Underdevelopment or absence of the uvula.

HP:0010294.label: Palate fistula
HP:0010294.definition: A fistula which connects the oral cavity and the pharyngeal area via the aspects of the soft palate.

HP:0010295.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the tongue
HP:0010295.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the tongue.

HP:0010296.label: Ankyloglossia
HP:0010296.definition: Short or anteriorly attached lingual frenulum, associated with limited mobility of the tongue.
HP:0010296.comment: The anterior third of the tongue is usually free or is partially attached to the floor of the mouth by the lingual frenulum. There is a spectrum ranging from fusion of the tongue to the floor of the mouth (ankyloglossia inferiorum) to a lingual frenulum that is short or anchored toward the tip of the tongue (sometimes called tongue tie). Ankyloglossia may be associated with a mild indentation of the tip of the tongue, which should not be coded as a Bifid tongue.

HP:0010297.label: Bifid tongue
HP:0010297.definition: Tongue with a median apical indentation or fork.
HP:0010297.comment: Bifid tongue can be associated with ankyloglossia, but this should be assessed and coded separately. Small indentations of the tip of the tongue should not be coded as a bifid tongue.

HP:0010298.label: Smooth tongue
HP:0010298.definition: Glossy appearance of the entire tongue surface.
HP:0010298.comment: This is due to reduction in number and/or size of the filiform papillae. A geographic tongue has localized areas of smoothening, but not sufficient to warrant use of the term Smooth tongue.

HP:0010299.label: Abnormal dentin morphology
HP:0010299.comment: Dentin is a calcified tissue of teeth that is covered by enamel on the crown and cementum on the root and surrounds the entire pulp.

HP:0010300.label: Abnormally low-pitched voice
HP:0010300.definition: A persistent (minutes to hours) abnormal decrease in the pitch of the voice for the context or social situation or significantly different from the baseline of the individual.

HP:0010301.label: Spinal dysraphism
HP:0010301.definition: A heterogeneous group of congenital spinal anomalies that result from defective closure of the neural tube early in fetal life.
HP:0010301.comment: Spinal dysraphism, or neural tube defect comprises a heterogeneous group of congenital spinal anomalies that result from defective closure of the neural tube early in fetal life and anomalous development of the caudal cell mass. The anatomic features common to the entire group is an anomaly in the midline structures of the back, especially the absence of some of the neural arches, and defects of the skin, filum terminale, nerves, and spinal cord. Open forms of spinal dysraphism include myelocele, meningocele, and myelomeningocele. These open forms are often associated with hydrocephalus and Arnold-Chiari malformation type II and may be classified as spina bifida aperta. Closed forms of spinal dysraphism include spina bifida occulta.
exact_synonyms: Incomplete closure of the vertebral arch

HP:0010302.label: Spinal cord tumor
HP:0010302.definition: A neoplasm affecting the spinal cord.

HP:0010303.label: Abnormal spinal meningeal morphology
HP:0010303.definition: Any abnormality of the spinal meninges, the system of membranes (dura mater, the arachnoid mater, and the pia mater) which envelops the spinal cord.

HP:0010304.label: Spinal meningeal diverticulum
HP:0010304.definition: An outpouching of the spinal meninges.

HP:0010306.label: Short thorax
HP:0010306.definition: Reduced inferior to superior extent of the thorax.
exact_synonyms: Shorter than typical length between neck and abdomen

HP:0010307.label: Stridor
HP:0010307.definition: Stridor is a high pitched sound resulting from turbulent air flow in the upper airway.
HP:0010307.comment: Stridor is different from wheezing by the following reasons. It is louder over the neck than chest wall. Secondly; stridor is mainly inspiratory. If occurs in expiration, it is usually biphasic. On the other hand; wheeze is mainly expiratory and occurs during both phases. It indicates extrathoracic upper-airway obstruction (supraglottic lesions like laryngomalacia, vocal cord lesion) when heard on inspiration. It occurs in expiration if associated with intrathoracic tracheobronchial lesions (tracheomalacia, bronchomalacia, and extrinsic compression). It occurs in both phases if lesion is fixed, for example, stenosis. Stridor is caused by the turbulent flow passing through a narrowed segment of the upper respiratory tract.

HP:0010308.label: Asternia
HP:0010308.definition: The congenital absence of the sternum.

HP:0010309.label: Bifid sternum
HP:0010309.definition: The sternal cleft is a rare congenital anomaly resulting from a fusion failure of the sternum.
HP:0010309.comment: Various degrees of bifid sternum may occur, varying from an enlarged suprasternal notch to complete separation of the two halves of the sternum. Ectopia cordis may or may not accompany this defect in its more severe form.

HP:0010310.label: Chylothorax
HP:0010310.definition: Accumulation of excessive amounts of lymphatic fluid (chyle) in the pleural cavity.

HP:0010311.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the breasts
HP:0010311.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the breasts.

HP:0010313.label: Breast hypertrophy
HP:0010313.definition: The presence of hypertrophy of the breast.

HP:0010315.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the diaphragm
HP:0010315.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the diaphragm.

HP:0010316.label: Ebstein anomaly of the tricuspid valve
HP:0010316.definition: Ebstein's anomaly refers to an abnormally placed and deformed tricuspid valve characterized by apical displacement of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets, leading to atrialization of the right ventricle with a variable degree of malformation and displacement of the anterior leaflet.
HP:0010316.comment: Ebstein's anomaly is often associated with a hypoplastic right ventricle, patent foramen ovale, and a degree of cyanosis dependent on the amount if inadequacy of the tricuspid valve. Ebstein's anomaly may be associated with Wolf-Parkinson-White syndrome or other arrythmias.
exact_synonyms: Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve

HP:0010318.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
HP:0010318.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the abdominal musculature.

HP:0010319.label: Abnormal second toe morphology
HP:0010319.definition: An anomaly of the second toe.

HP:0010320.label: Abnormal third toe morphology
HP:0010320.definition: An anomaly of the third toe.

HP:0010321.label: Abnormal fourth toe morphology
HP:0010321.definition: An anomaly of the fourth toe.

HP:0010322.label: Abnormal fifth toe morphology
HP:0010322.definition: An anomaly of the little toe.

HP:0010323.label: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the 2nd toe

HP:0010438.label: Abnormal ventricular septum morphology
HP:0010438.definition: A structural abnormality of the interventricular septum.

HP:0010440.label: Ectopic accessory toe-like appendage
HP:0010440.definition: In contrast to forms of polydactyly where the supernumerary digit (this can either be a rudimentary or a completely 'normal' digit) is either located postaxial (on the fibular side of the foot, next top the little toe), preaxial (on the tibial side of the foot, next to the big toe) or mesoaxial (somewhere central, between big and little toe), a supernumerary digit may also be placed ectopically, meaning anywhere else except post-,meso- or preaxial. In the literature this is sometimes referred to as Disorganisation-like Syndrome (OMIM223200).

HP:0010441.label: Ectopic accessory finger-like appendage
HP:0010441.definition: In contrast to forms of polydactyly where the supernumerary digit (this can either be a rudimentary or a completely 'normal' digit) is either located postaxial (on the ulnar side of the hand, next to the little finger), preaxial (on the radial side of the hand, next to the thumb) or mesoaxial (somewhere central, between thumb and little finger), a supernumerary digit may also be placed ectopically, meaning anywhere else except post-,meso- or preaxial. In the literature this is sometimes referred to as Disorganisation-like Syndrome (OMIM223200).

HP:0010442.label: Polydactyly
HP:0010442.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of supernumerary fingers or toes.
exact_synonyms: More than five fingers or toes on hands or feet

HP:0010443.label: Bifid femur
HP:0010443.definition: A bifid or bifurcated appearance of the femur as seen on x-rays, possible appearing as a more or less severe bowing of the upper leg. Might be associated with hip dysplasia on the affected side.

HP:0010444.label: Pulmonic regurgitation
HP:0010444.definition: The retrograde (backwards) flow of blood through the pulmonary valve into the right ventricle during diastole.
HP:0010444.comment: The pulmonary valve directs blood from the right ventricle (RV) towards the pulmonary arteries during systole.

HP:0010445.label: Primum atrial septal defect
HP:0010445.definition: An ostium primum atrial septal defect is located in the most anterior and inferior aspect of the atrial septum. The ostium primum refers to an anterior and inferior opening (ostium) within the septum primum, which divides the rudimentary atrium during fetal development. The ostium primum is normally sealed by fusion of the superior and inferior endocardial cushions around 5 weeks' gestation. Ostium primum defects result from a failure of the fusion of the embryologic endocardial cushion and septum primum.
HP:0010445.comment: With this type of ASD, communication persists when the septum primum fails to fuse with the endocardial cushions, thus leaving an opening between both atria near the atrial floor, being a mid/late event in atrial septation. Due to the association with endocardial cushion abnormalities, this defect may be associated with either atrioventricular valve anomalies, such as mitral valve cleft, or a complete atrioventricular septal defect.

HP:0010446.label: Tricuspid stenosis
HP:0010446.definition: A narrowing of the orifice of the tricuspid valve of the heart.
HP:0010446.comment: Tricuspid stenosis results in characteristic changes in the jugular venous pulse in the form of leisurely V to Y descent and prominent a-waves. The liver is enlarged with a firm edge and is pulsatile in presystole. This is best appreciated with one hand on the liver edge and one on the precordium. Auscultation reveals a low- to medium-pitched diastolic rumble with inspiratory accentuation. This is usually localized to the lower sternal border.

HP:0010447.label: Anal fistula
HP:0010447.definition: An abnormal connection between the epithelialised surface of the anal canal and the perianal skin.

HP:0010448.label: Colonic atresia
HP:0010448.definition: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the colon. That is, there is an abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the colon.

HP:0010450.label: Esophageal stenosis
HP:0010450.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the lumen of the esophagus.

HP:0010451.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the spleen
HP:0010451.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the spleen.

HP:0010452.label: Ectopia of the spleen
HP:0010452.definition: An abnormal (non-anatomic) location of the spleen.

HP:0010453.label: Pelvic bone asymmetry
HP:0010453.definition: Pelvic asymmetry refers to asymmetric positioning of landmarks on the two sides of the pelvis and may have a structural or functional etiology.

HP:0010454.label: Acetabular spurs
HP:0010454.definition: The presence of osteophytes (bone spurs), i.e., of bony projections originating from the acetabulum.

HP:0010455.label: Steep acetabular roof
HP:0010455.definition: An exaggeration of the normal arched form of the acetabular roof such that it takes on a steep appearance.

HP:0010456.label: Abnormal greater sciatic notch morphology
HP:0010456.definition: An abnormality of the sacrosciatic notch, i.e., the deep indentation in the posterior border of the hip bone at the point of union of the ilium and ischium.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the greater sacrosciatic notch

HP:0010457.label: obsolete Widening of the sacrosciatic notch

HP:0010458.label: Female pseudohermaphroditism
HP:0010458.definition: Hermaphroditism refers to a discrepancy between the morphology of the gonads and that of the external genitalia. In female pseudohermaphroditism, the genotype is female (XX) and the gonads are ovaries, but the external genitalia are virilized.

HP:0010459.label: True hermaphroditism
HP:0010459.definition: The presence of both ovarian and testicular tissues either in the same or in opposite gonads. Affected persons have ambiguous genitalia and may have 46,XX or 46,XY karyotypes or 46,XX/XY mosaicism.
HP:0010459.comment: In true hermaphroditism, the testicular tissue must have well developed seminiferous tubules, and the ovarian tissue primordial follicles. The external genitalia are usually associated with variable degrees of sexual ambiguity, depending on the amount of functioning testicular tissue. Internally, a uterus is almost always present, but the development of Mullerian and Wolffian structures is variable and generally depends on the adjacent gonad. Usually there is a vas deferens on the side of the testis, and a Fallopian tube on the side of the ovary. Both types of ducts can occur next to an ovotestis. An ovotestis is the most common gonad found in true hermaphroditism and can be coded with HP:0012861.

HP:0010460.label: Abnormality of the female genitalia
HP:0010460.definition: Abnormality of the female genital system.
HP:0010460.comment: Abnormality of the female internal or external genitalia.

HP:0010461.label: Abnormality of the male genitalia
HP:0010461.definition: Abnormality of the male genital system.

HP:0010462.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the ovary
HP:0010462.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the ovary.

HP:0010463.label: Aplasia of the ovary
HP:0010463.definition: Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the ovary.

HP:0010464.label: Streak ovary
HP:0010464.definition: A developmental disorder characterized by the progressive loss of primordial germ cells in the developing ovaries of an embryo, leading to hypoplastic ovaries composed of wavy connective tissue with occasional clumps of granulosa cells, and frequently mesonephric or hilar cells.

HP:0010465.label: Precocious puberty in females
HP:0010465.definition: The onset of puberty before the age of 8 years in girls.

HP:0010468.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the testes
HP:0010468.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the testes.

HP:0010469.label: Absent testis
HP:0010469.definition: Testis not palpable in the scrotum or inguinal canal.
HP:0010469.comment: Absence can be congenital or not (vanishing testis). Definitive assessment can only be made by imaging or surgical studies, in order to exclude an intra-abdominal testis, which should be coded as Cryptorchidism. True absence of a testis can be difficult to prove. Anorchia is true absence of both testes, and can only be determined by imaging or surgical studies.

HP:0010470.label: Supernumerary testes
HP:0010470.definition: The presence of more than two testes.

HP:0010471.label: Oligosacchariduria
HP:0010471.definition: Increased urinary excretion of oligosaccharides (low molecular weight carbohydrate chains composed of at least three monosaccharide subunits), derived from a partial degradation of glycoproteins.

HP:0010472.label: Abnormal circulating porphyrin concentration
HP:0010472.definition: An abnormality in the synthesis or catabolism of heme. Heme is composed of ferrous iron and protoporphyrin IX and is an essential molecule as the prosthetic group of hemeproteins such as hemoglobin, myoglobin, mitochondrial and microsomal cytochromes.

HP:0010473.label: Porphyrinuria
HP:0010473.definition: Abnormally increased excretion of porphyrins in the urine.
HP:0010473.comment: Porphyrins are natural pigments containing a fundamental skeleton of four pyrrole nuclei united through the alpha-positions by four methine groups to form a macrocyclic structure. One of the best-known porphyrins is heme.

HP:0010474.label: Bladder stones
HP:0010474.definition: Buildups of minerals that form in the urinary bladder.

HP:0010475.label: Cloacal exstrophy
HP:0010475.definition: Cloacal exstrophy is a severe anterior abdominal wall defect in which the two hemibladders are visible and are separated by a midline intestinal plate, an omphalocele, and an imperforate anus.

HP:0010476.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the bladder
HP:0010476.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the urinary bladder.

HP:0010478.label: Abnormality of the urachus
HP:0010478.comment: The urachus is a vestigial embryonic structure, a canal that connects the urinary bladder of the fetus with the allantois (a structure involved in the development of the umbilical cord). During embryonic development, the lumen of the urachus is normally obliterated, transforming the urachus into a solid cord.

HP:0010479.label: Patent urachus
HP:0010479.definition: Persistence of the urachal canal resulting in a canal between the bladder and the umbilicus.

HP:0010480.label: Urethral fistula
HP:0010480.definition: The presence of an abnormal connection between the urethra and another organ or the skin.

HP:0010481.label: Urethral valve
HP:0010481.definition: The presence of an abnormal membrane obstructing the urethra.

HP:0010482.label: Acromelia of the upper limbs
HP:0010482.definition: Shortening of the arms predominantly affecting terminal parts of the arm in relation to the upper and middle limb segments.

HP:0010483.label: Amniotic constriction rings of arms
HP:0010483.definition: Amniotic constriction rings affecting the arms.

HP:0010484.label: Hypertrophy of the upper limb
HP:0010484.definition: Abnormal increase in size of the upper limbs (due to an increase of the size of cells).

HP:0010485.label: Hyperextensibility at elbow
HP:0010485.definition: The ability of the elbow joint to move beyond its normal range of motion.

HP:0010486.label: Abnormality of the hypothenar eminence
HP:0010486.definition: An abnormality of the hypothenar eminence, i.e., of the muscles on the ulnar side of the palm of the hand (i.e., on the side of the little finger).

HP:0010487.label: Small hypothenar eminence
HP:0010487.definition: Reduced muscle mass on the ulnar side of the palm, that is, reduction in size of the hypothenar eminence.

HP:0010488.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the palmar creases
HP:0010488.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the palmar creases.

HP:0010489.label: Absent palmar crease
HP:0010489.definition: The absence of the major creases of the palm (distal transverse crease, proximal transverse crease, or thenar crease).

HP:0010490.label: Abnormality of the palmar creases
HP:0010490.definition: An abnormality of the creases of the skin of palm of hand.

HP:0010491.label: Digital constriction ring
HP:0010491.definition: A narrow segment of significantly reduced circumference of a digit.
HP:0010491.comment: The description should specify the hand and digit that is affected and the approximate location of the band relative to the phalanges. It may be described as partial, if it does not involve the entire circumference of the digit.

HP:0010492.label: Osseous finger syndactyly
HP:0010492.definition: Webbing or fusion of the fingers, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual finger bones.
HP:0010492.comment: Bony fusions are referred to as bony syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as symphalangism.

HP:0010493.label: Long metacarpals
HP:0010493.definition: An abnormally increased length of the metacarpal bones.

HP:0010494.label: Acromelia of the lower limbs
HP:0010494.definition: Shortening of the legs predominantly affecting terminal parts of the leg in relation to the upper and middle arm segments.

HP:0010495.label: Amniotic constriction rings of legs
HP:0010495.definition: Amniotic constriction rings affecting the legs.

HP:0010496.label: Hypertrophy of the lower limb
HP:0010496.definition: Abnormal increase in size of the lower limbs (due to an increase of the size of cells).

HP:0010497.label: Sirenomelia
HP:0010497.definition: A developmental defect in which the legs are fused together.

HP:0010498.label: Bipartite patella
HP:0010498.definition: A developmental defect that occurs if the two halves of the patella fail to fuse in early childhood.

HP:0010499.label: Patellar subluxation
HP:0010499.definition: The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar subluxation refers to an unstable kneecap that does not slide centrally within its groove, i.e., a partial dislocation of the patella.

HP:0010500.label: Hyperextensibility of the knee
HP:0010500.definition: The ability of the knee joint to extend beyond its normal range of motion (the lower leg is moved beyond a straight position with respect to the thigh).

HP:0010501.label: Limitation of knee mobility
HP:0010501.definition: An abnormal limitation of knee joint mobility.
HP:0010501.comment: The knee permits four types of movement: (i) Extension (straightening the lower leg); (ii) Flexion (bending the knee); (iii) Lateral rotation (turning outwards); and (iv) Medial rotation (turning inward)

HP:0010502.label: Fibular bowing
HP:0010502.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of the fibula.
HP:0010502.comment: A developmental defect with posteromedial fibular angulation.

HP:0010503.label: Fibular duplication
HP:0010503.definition: Duplication of the fibula. This may occur as a part of diplopodia (accessory tarsal or metatarsal bone). Diplopodia with double fibula is an extremely rare condition.

HP:0010504.label: Increased length of the tibia
HP:0010504.definition: An abnormal increase in the length of the tibia.

HP:0010505.label: Limitation of movement at ankles
HP:0010505.definition: An abnormal limitation of the mobility of the ankle joint.

HP:0010506.label: Abnormal plantar dermatoglyphics
HP:0010506.definition: An abnormality of dermatoglyphs on the toes and soles, i.e., an abnormality of the patterns of ridges of the skin of sole of foot.

HP:0010507.label: Foot asymmetry
HP:0010507.definition: A difference in size or shape between the left and right foot.

HP:0010508.label: Metatarsus valgus
HP:0010508.definition: A condition in which the anterior part of the foot rotates outward away from the midline of the body and the heel remains straight.

HP:0010510.label: Hypermobility of toe joints
HP:0010510.definition: An ability of the toe joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

HP:0010511.label: Long toe
HP:0010511.definition: Toes that appear disproportionately long compared to the foot.
HP:0010511.comment: This finding must be distinguished from digits that are thin but of normal length and that of a short mid and hind foot with normal digit lengths. The affected digits should be specified. If only a subset of the digits of a limb is lengthened, the affected digits should be specified.

HP:0010512.label: Adrenal calcification
HP:0010512.comment: This condition may occur in a wide variety of pathologies, some serious and some with no obvious consequence. Adrenal hemorrhage may be detected as an incidental finding in children in radiographic studies of the abdomen. Etiologies include hemorrhage into the adrenals at or immediately after birth, neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, cortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and cysts.

HP:0010513.label: Pituitary calcification
HP:0010513.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in the pituitary gland.

HP:0010514.label: Hyperpituitarism
HP:0010514.definition: Hypersecretion of one or more pituitary hormones. This can occur in conditions in which deficiency in the target organ leads to decreased hormonal feedback, or as a primary condition most usually in connection with a pituitary adenoma.

HP:0010515.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the thymus
