HP:0010515.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the thymus.

HP:0010517.label: Ectopic thymus tissue
HP:0010517.definition: The presence of ectopic thymus tissue. Normally, cells of the ventral bud of the third pharyngeal pouch detach and migrate in the eighth gestational week caudally and medially towards the location of the mature thyroid. They migrate further retrosternally into the superior mediastinum. There are two main ways ectopic thymus tissue can develop. Either cells detach along the descensus path and proliferate, thereby forming accessory thymus tissue, or the entire gland fails to descend.

HP:0010518.label: Thyroglossal cyst
HP:0010518.definition: An abnormality of the thyroid gland owing to the presence of a fibrous cyst resulting from the persistence of the thyroglossal duct.
HP:0010518.comment: A developmental defect resulting in the presence of a thyroglossal cyst, a fibrous cyst that forms from a persistent thyroglossal duct. During the embryologic development of the thyroid gland, the precursor of the thyroid migrates from the base of the tongue inferiorly though the thyroglossal duct. This duct normally disappears following the development and migration of the thyroid gland, but if a portion of the duct remain it can form a thyroglossal cyst.

HP:0010519.label: Increased fetal movement
HP:0010519.definition: An abnormal increase in quantity or strength of fetal movements.

HP:0010521.label: Gait apraxia
HP:0010521.definition: Gait apraxia affecting the ability to make walking movements with the legs.

HP:0010522.label: Dyslexia
HP:0010522.definition: A learning disorder characterized primarily by difficulties in learning to read and spell. Dyslectic children also exhibit a tendency to read words from right to left and to confuse letters such as b and d whose orientation is important for their identification. Children with dyslexia appear to be impaired in phonemic skills (the ability to associate visual symbols with the sounds they represent).

HP:0010523.label: Alexia
HP:0010523.definition: An acquired type of sensory aphasia where damage to the brain leads to the loss of the ability to read.
HP:0010523.comment: Note that dyslexia refers to a developmental reading disability, whereas alexi arefers to an acquired reading disability related to damage to the brain in an individual in whom reading ability had previously been developed.

HP:0010524.label: Disturbed sensory perception
HP:0010524.definition: Alteration or impairment in the processing or interpretation of sensory information can lead to abnormal perceptions or experiences.

HP:0010525.label: Finger agnosia
HP:0010525.definition: The examiner identified the inability to name, move, or touch specific fingers.

HP:0010526.label: Dysgraphia
HP:0010526.definition: A writing disability in the absence of motor or sensory deficits of the upper extremities, resulting in an impairment in the ability to write regardless of the ability to read and not due to intellectual impairment.

HP:0010527.label: Astereognosis
HP:0010527.definition: Tactile agnosia refers to the inability to recognize objects by touch, while the inability to discriminate shape and size by touch is also a related condition.

HP:0010528.label: Prosopagnosia
HP:0010528.definition: Inability to recognize faces of familiar persons.

HP:0010529.label: Echolalia
HP:0010529.definition: Echolalia is the automatic imitative repetition of sounds, words, or phrases in the absence of explicit awareness. The repeated words or phrases are typically odd or used in a non-social manner. These can be words or phrases that the affected individual has heard or invented.

HP:0010530.label: Palatal tremor
HP:0010530.definition: Palatal tremor (PT) is an involuntary, rhythmic and oscillatory movement of the soft palate. PT is a rare type of tremor involving the soft palate. It can be unilateral or bilateral.
HP:0010530.comment: Previously, PT was known as palatal myoclonus but it was subsequently renamed palatal tremor during the First International Congress of Movement Disorders to acknowledge the continuous and rhythmic nature of the palatal movement. Palatal tremors do not oscillate around a point, unlike any other type of tremor. Palatal tremors can have huge variability in frequency, unlike other commonly-described tremors.

HP:0010531.label: Spinal myoclonus
HP:0010531.definition: Spinal myoclonus is generally due to a tumor, infection, injury, or degenerative process of the spinal cord, and is characterized by involuntary rhythmic muscle contractions, usually at a rate of more than one per second. Myoclonus occurs synchronously in several muscles and can be increased in severity and frequency by fatigue or stress, but is usually unaffected by sensory stimuli. Spinal myoclonus ceases during sleep or anesthesia.

HP:0010533.label: Spasmus nutans
HP:0010533.definition: The combination of pendular nystagmus, head nodding, and torticollis.

HP:0010534.label: Transient global amnesia
HP:0010534.definition: A paroxysmal, transient loss of memory function with preservation of immediate recall and remote memory but with a severe impairment of memory for recent events and ability to retain new information.

HP:0010535.label: Sleep apnea
HP:0010535.definition: An intermittent cessation of airflow at the mouth and nose during sleep is known as sleep apnea. Apneas that last at least 10 seconds are considered significant, but individuals with sleep apnea may experience apneas lasting from 20 seconds up to 2 or 3 minutes. Patients may have up to 15 events per hour of sleep.

HP:0010536.label: Central sleep apnea
HP:0010536.definition: Sleep apnea results from a temporary loss of the central drive to the muscles responsible for breathing.

HP:0010537.label: Wide cranial sutures
HP:0010537.definition: An abnormally increased width of the cranial sutures for age-related norms (generally resulting from delayed closure).

HP:0010539.label: Thin calvarium
HP:0010539.definition: The presence of an abnormally thin calvarium.

HP:0010540.label: Advanced pneumatization of cranial sinuses
HP:0010540.definition: A degree of pneumatization that is increased compared to age-related norms.

HP:0010541.label: Cutis gyrata of scalp
HP:0010541.definition: The presence of convoluted folds and furrows formed from thickened skin of the scalp, resembling cerebriform pattern. The scalp has convoluted and elevated folds, 1 to 2 cm in thickness. The convolutions generally cannot be flattened by traction.
exact_synonyms: Furrows in thickened skin on top of scalp
Thickened folds on top of scalp

HP:0010542.label: Vestibular nystagmus
HP:0010542.definition: Nystagmus due to disturbance of the vestibular system; eye movements are rhythmic, with slow and fast components.

HP:0010543.label: Opsoclonus
HP:0010543.definition: Bursts of large-amplitude multidirectional saccades without intersaccadic interval
HP:0010543.comment: Spontaneous, non-rhythmic, multi-directional, chaotic movements of the eyes, giving the appearance of agitation. There may be bursts of conjugate movement of the eyes in varying directions and of varying amplitude.

HP:0010544.label: Vertical nystagmus
HP:0010544.definition: Vertical nystagmus may present with either up-beating or down-beating eye movements or both. When present in the straight-ahead position of gaze it is referred to as upbeat nystagmus or downbeat nystagmus.

HP:0010545.label: Downbeat nystagmus
HP:0010545.definition: Downbeat nystagmus is a type of fixation nystagmus with the fast phase beating in a downward direction. It generally increases when looking to the side and down and when lying prone.

HP:0010546.label: Muscle fibrillation
HP:0010546.definition: Fine, rapid twitching of individual muscle fibers with little or no movement of the muscle as a whole as ascertained by electromyography (EMG). If a motor neuron or its axon is destroyed, the muscle fibers it innervates undergo denervation atrophy. This leads to hypersensitivity of individual muscle fibers to acetyl choline so that they may contract spontaneously. Isolated activity of individual muscle fibers is generally so fine it cannot be seen through the intact skin, although it can be recorded as a short-duration spike in the EMG.

HP:0010547.label: Muscle flaccidity
HP:0010547.definition: A type of paralysis in which a muscle becomes soft and yields to passive stretching, which results from loss of all or practically all peripheral motor nerves that innervated the muscle. Muscle tone is reduced and the affected muscles undergo extreme atrophy within months of the loss of innervation.

HP:0010548.label: Percussion myotonia
HP:0010548.definition: A localized myotonic contraction in a muscle in reaction to percussion (tapping with the examiner's finger, a rubber percussion hammer, or a similar object).
exact_synonyms: Transient swelling of muscle induced by percussion

HP:0010549.label: Weakness due to upper motor neuron dysfunction
HP:0010549.definition: Paralysis of voluntary muscles means loss of contraction due to interruption of one or more motor pathways from the brain to the muscle fibers. Although the word paralysis is often used interchangeably to mean either complete or partial loss of muscle strength, it is preferable to use paralysis or plegia for complete or severe loss of muscle strength, and paresis for partial or slight loss. Paralysis due to lesions of the principle motor tracts is related to a lesion in the corticospinal, corticobulbar or brainstem descending (subcorticospinal) neurons.
exact_synonyms: Paralysis due to lesions of the principle motor tracts

HP:0010550.label: Paraplegia
HP:0010550.definition: Severe or complete weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities.

HP:0010551.label: Paraplegia/paraparesis
HP:0010551.definition: Weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities. Paraplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas paraparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.

HP:0010553.label: Oculogyric crisis
HP:0010553.definition: An acute dystonic reaction with blepharospasm, periorbital twitches, and protracted fixed staring episodes. There may be a maximal upward deviation of the eyes in the sustained fashion. Oculogyric crisis can be triggered by a number of factors including neuroleptic medications.

HP:0010554.label: Cutaneous finger syndactyly
HP:0010554.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints, or a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two fingers that lies significantly distal to the flexion crease that overlies the metacarpophalangeal joint of the adjacent fingers.
HP:0010554.comment: We have set an arguably arbitrary threshold to distinguish the object form the subjective finding. While severe degrees of cutaneous syndactyly are clearly objective, more subtle degrees are subjective. We set this threshold to distinguish these two situations. The digits (or parts of) are joined together by tissue that is not normally present between the digits at that point in the P/D axis. A modifier of "complete" may be used if the cutaneous syndactyly extends to the distal end of the nail bed of the digits. The affected digits should be specified. Note that the unqualified term "syndactyly" is no longer allowed as it is unclear whether this refers to bony or cutaneous syndactyly.

HP:0010557.label: Overlapping fingers
HP:0010557.definition: A finger resting on the dorsal surface of an adjacent digit when the hand is at rest.
HP:0010557.comment: Overlapping of the fingers occurring as the result of a deviation of the fingers from their normal position. Fingers that are laterally deviated, but do not rest on top of adjacent fingers should be coded as Clinodactyly.

HP:0010558.label: Abnormality of the clivus
HP:0010558.definition: An abnormality of the clivus, which is the inclined bony region of the posterior cranial fossa located between the sella turcica and the foramen magnum.

HP:0010559.label: Vertical clivus
HP:0010559.definition: An abnormal vertical orientation of the clivus (which normally forms a kind of slope from the sella turcica down to the region of the foramen magnum).

HP:0010560.label: Undulate clavicles
HP:0010560.definition: An abnormally wavy surface or edge of the clavicles.

HP:0010561.label: Undulate ribs
HP:0010561.definition: An abnormally wavy surface or edge of the ribs.

HP:0010564.label: Bifid epiglottis
HP:0010564.definition: A midline anterior-posterior cleft of the epiglottis that involves at least two-thirds of the epiglottic leaf. It is a useful feature for clinical diagnosis because it appears to be very rare in syndromes other than Pallister-Hall-Syndrome and is also rare as an isolated malformation.

HP:0010565.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the Epiglottis
HP:0010565.definition: This term applies if the Epiglottis is absent or hypoplastic.

HP:0010566.label: Hamartoma
HP:0010566.definition: A disordered proliferation of mature tissues that is native to the site of origin, e.g., exostoses, nevi and soft tissue hamartomas. Although most hamartomas are benign, some histologic subtypes, e.g., neuromuscular hamartoma, may proliferate aggressively such as mesenchymal cystic hamartoma, Sclerosing epithelial hamartoma, Sclerosing metanephric hamartoma.

HP:0010567.label: Y-shaped metatarsals
HP:0010567.definition: Y-shaped metatarsals are the result of a partial fusion of two metatarsal bones, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Y-shaped metatarsals may be seen in combination with polydactyly.

HP:0010568.label: Hamartoma of the eye
HP:0010568.definition: A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) which can originate from any tissue of the eye.

HP:0010569.label: Elevated circulating 7-dehydrocholesterol concentration
HP:0010569.definition: Concentration of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0010569.comment: Elevated 7-dehydrocholesterol levels occur as the result of a deficiency of the enzyme delta-7-sterol reductase, the penultimate enzyme of mammalian sterol biosynthesis that converts 7-dehydrocholesterol (7-DHC) to cholesterol. This enzyme removes the C(7-8) double bond introduced by the sterol delta8-delta7 isomerases. In addition, its role in drug-induced malformations is known: inhibitors of the last step of cholesterol biosynthesis such as AY9944 and BM15766 severely impair brain development. Homozygous mutations in the gene encoding for this enzyme are the molecular genetic cause of Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome.

HP:0010570.label: Low maternal circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
HP:0010570.definition: An abnormally low concentration of serum alpha-fetoprotein as compared to normal values for gestational-age.
HP:0010570.comment: Reduced levels of alpha-fetoprotein can be seen in some fetal disorders such as Down syndrome.

HP:0010571.label: Elevated circulating phytanic acid concentration
HP:0010571.definition: An abnormal elevation of phytanic acid.
HP:0010571.comment: Phytanic acid (3,7,11,15-tetramethyl hexadecanoic acid) is a fatty acid that is derived from chlorophyll and present in the diet. The metabolism of phytanic acid involves alpha-oxidation in the peroxisome, which converts phytanic acid to pristanic acid. Peroxisomes involved in the catabolism of very long chain fatty acids and phytanic acid. Peroxisomal malfunctioning can lead to over-accumulation of very long chain fatty acids and phytanic acid, among other things.

HP:0010574.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the femoral head
HP:0010574.definition: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
HP:0010574.comment: Note that the proximal epiphysis of the femur is often referred to as the capital femoral epiphysis from the Latin word caput for head.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the proximal femoral epiphysis
Abnormality of the end part of the innermost thighbone

HP:0010575.label: Dysplasia of the femoral head
HP:0010575.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the femoral head.

HP:0010576.label: Intracranial cystic lesion
HP:0010576.definition: A cystic lesion originating within the brain.

HP:0010578.label: Bracket epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of long bone

HP:0010579.label: Cone-shaped epiphysis
HP:0010579.definition: Cone-shaped epiphyses (also known as coned epiphyses) are epiphyses that invaginate into cupped metaphyses. That is, the epiphysis has a cone-shaped distal extension resulting from increased growth of the central portion of the epiphysis relative to its periphery.

HP:0010582.label: Irregular epiphyses
HP:0010582.definition: An alteration of the normally smooth contour of the epiphysis leading to an irregular appearance.
exact_synonyms: Irregular end part of long bone

HP:0010583.label: Ivory epiphyses
HP:0010583.definition: Sclerosis of the epiphyses, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
exact_synonyms: Increased bone density in end part of bone

HP:0010585.label: Small epiphyses
HP:0010585.definition: Reduction in the size or volume of epiphyses.

HP:0010587.label: Triangular epiphysis
HP:0010587.definition: Longitudinal epiphyseal bracket or bracket epiphysis is an uncommon disorder of growth. Alternatively known as a delta phalanx, it is due to an anomalous secondary ossification center that extends longitudinally along the diaphysis. Although rare, longitudinal epiphyseal bracket most commonly manifests in the hands as clinodactyly and in the feet as hallux varus.

HP:0010588.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion
HP:0010588.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at each end of a long bone, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.
HP:0010588.comment: The epiphysis is the rounded end of a long bone, at its joint with adjacent bone.

HP:0010590.label: Abnormality of the distal femoral epiphysis
HP:0010590.definition: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the femur.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the outermost thighbone

HP:0010591.label: Abnormality of the proximal tibial epiphysis
HP:0010591.definition: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of innermost shankbone
Abnormality of the end part of innermost shinbone

HP:0010592.label: Abnormality of the distal tibial epiphysis
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of outermost shankbone
Abnormality of the end part of outermost shinbone

HP:0010593.label: Abnormal fibular epiphysis morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the calf bone

HP:0010594.label: Abnormality of the proximal fibular epiphysis
HP:0010594.definition: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the fibula.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the innermost end part of calf bone

HP:0010595.label: Abnormality of the distal fibular epiphysis
HP:0010595.definition: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the fibula.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the outermost end part of calf bone

HP:0010596.label: Abnormal proximal radial epiphysis morphology
HP:0010596.definition: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the proximal radial epiphysis

HP:0010597.label: Abnormality of the distal radial epiphysis
HP:0010597.definition: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the radius.

HP:0010598.label: Abnormality of the proximal humeral epiphysis
HP:0010598.definition: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the humerus.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the innermost long bone in upper arm

HP:0010599.label: Abnormal distal humeral epiphysis morphology
HP:0010599.definition: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the humerus.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the outermost long bone in upper arm
Abnormality of the distal humeral epiphysis

HP:0010600.label: Abnormal distal ulnar epiphysis morphology
HP:0010600.definition: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the ulna.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the distal ulnar epiphysis

HP:0010601.label: Abnormal proximal ulnar epiphysis morphology
HP:0010601.definition: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the ulna.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the proximal ulnar epiphysis

HP:0010602.label: Type 2 muscle fiber predominance
HP:0010602.definition: An abnormal predominance of type II muscle fibers (in general, this feature can only be observed on muscle biopsy).

HP:0010603.label: Odontogenic keratocysts of the jaw
HP:0010603.definition: A benign uni- or multicystic, intraosseous tumor of odontogenic origin, with a characteristic lining of parakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium and potential for aggressive, infiltrative behavior.
HP:0010603.comment: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor (KCOT) most commonly affects the mandible, but may also be localized in the maxilla.

HP:0010605.label: Chalazion
HP:0010605.definition: A chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland. A chalazion or meibomian cyst appears as a painless tuberous swelling in the upper lid without loss of eyelashes.

HP:0010606.label: Hordeolum
HP:0010606.definition: An acute purulent infection of the sebaceous glands of Zeis at the base of the eyelashes, of the apocrine sweat glands of Moll or the meibomian sebacious glands often caused by staphylococcus infections. Hordeola can either occur as Hordeola externa affecting the sebaceous glands of Zeis or the apocrine sweat glands of Moll or as Hordeola interna affecting the meibomian sebacious glands. In contrast to chalazia, hordeola are extremely painful and can cause extreme local swelling.

HP:0010607.label: Hordeolum externum
HP:0010607.definition: Hordeola externa are acute purulent infections affecting the sebaceous glands of Zeis or the apocrine sweat glands of Moll, often caused by staphylococcus infections. In contrast to chalazia, hordeola are extremely painfull and can cause extreme local swelling.

HP:0010608.label: Hordeolum internum
HP:0010608.definition: Hordeola interna are acute purulent infections affecting the meibomian sebacious glands, often caused by staphylococcus infections. In contrast to chalazia (chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland), hordeola are extremely painfull and can cause extreme local swelling.

HP:0010609.label: Skin tags
HP:0010609.definition: Cutaneous skin tags also known as acrochorda or fibroepithelial polyps are small benign tumors that may either form secondarily over time primarily in areas where the skin forms creases, such as the neck, armpit or groin or may also be present at birth, in which case they usually occur in the periauricular region.

HP:0010612.label: Plantar pits
HP:0010612.definition: The presence of multiple pits (small, pinpoint-large indentations on the surface of the skin) located on the skin of sole of foot.

HP:0010614.label: Fibroma
HP:0010614.definition: Benign tumors that are composed of fibrous or connective tissue. They can grow in all organs, arising from mesenchyme tissue. The term "fibroblastic" or "fibromatous" is used to describe tumors of the fibrous connective tissue. When the term fibroma is used without modifier, it is usually considered benign, with the term fibrosarcoma reserved for malignant tumors.

HP:0010615.label: Angiofibromas
HP:0010615.definition: Angiofibroma consist of many often dilated vessels.

HP:0010616.label: Lung fibroma
HP:0010616.definition: The presence of a lung fibroma, a benign neoplasm that can present as a mass causing airway obstruction, cough, and hemoptysis, or present without symptoms as a solitary pulmonary nodule.

HP:0010618.label: Ovarian fibroma
HP:0010618.definition: The presence of a fibroma of the ovary.
HP:0010618.comment: Ovarian fibromas belong to the sex cord-stromal tumor group of ovarian neoplasms. Ovarian fibromas are most frequent during middle age, and rare in children. Upon gross pathological inspection, ovary fibromas are firm and white or tan.

HP:0010619.label: Fibroadenoma of the breast
HP:0010619.definition: A benign biphasic tumor of the breast with epithelial and stromal components.
HP:0010619.comment: A connective tissue tumor of the breast which is usually benign and painless. Fibromas of the breast are more common in young woman.

HP:0010620.label: Malar prominence
HP:0010620.definition: Prominence of the malar process of the maxilla and infraorbital area appreciated in profile and from in front of the face.
HP:0010620.comment: Increased prominence of the malar region (cheeks), as manifested by anterior positioning of the infraorbital and perialar regions or increased convexity of the face or increased naso-labial angle.

HP:0010621.label: Cutaneous syndactyly of toes
HP:0010621.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between adjacent foot digits that involves at least half of the proximodistal length of one of the two involved digits; or, a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits of the foot that does not meet the prior objective criteria.

HP:0010622.label: Neoplasm of the skeletal system
HP:0010622.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the skeleton.

HP:0010624.label: Aplastic/hypoplastic toenail
HP:0010624.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the toenail.

HP:0010625.label: Anterior pituitary dysgenesis
HP:0010625.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis.

HP:0010626.label: Anterior pituitary agenesis
HP:0010626.definition: Absence of the anterior pituitary gland resulting from a developmental defect.

HP:0010627.label: Anterior pituitary hypoplasia
HP:0010627.definition: Underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland.

HP:0010628.label: Facial palsy
HP:0010628.definition: Facial nerve palsy is a dysfunction of cranial nerve VII (the facial nerve) that results in inability to control facial muscles on the affected side with weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure. This can either be present in unilateral or bilateral form.
HP:0010628.comment: Several conditions can cause a facial paralysis, e.g. brain tumor, stroke, and Lyme disease. However, if no specific cause can be identified, the condition is known as Bell's palsy. Named after Scottish anatomist Charles Bell, who first described it. Bell's palsy is the most common acute mononeuropathy (disease involving only one nerve) and is the most common cause of acute facial nerve paralysis.
related_synonyms: Facial muscle weakness of muscles innervated by CN VII

HP:0010629.label: Abnormal morphology of the cortex of the humerus
HP:0010629.definition: Any abnormality affecting the cortex of the humerus.

HP:0010630.label: Abnormal metatarsal epiphysis morphology
HP:0010630.definition: Any abnormality of a metatarsal bone epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of end part of long bone of foot
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the metatarsals

HP:0010631.label: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the feet
HP:0010631.definition: Any abnormality of the epiphyses of the feet.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the end part of the foot bone

HP:0010632.label: Total anosmia
HP:0010632.definition: Inability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.

HP:0010633.label: Partial anosmia
HP:0010633.definition: Inability to perceive certain odorants (implies that the sense of smell is maintained for other classes of odorants).

HP:0010634.label: Total hyposmia
HP:0010634.definition: Reduced ability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.

HP:0010635.label: Partial hyposmia
HP:0010635.definition: Reduced ability to perceive certain odorants (implies that the sense of smell is maintained for other classes of odorants).

HP:0010636.label: Schizencephaly
HP:0010636.definition: The presence of a cleft in the cerebral cortex unilaterally or bilaterally, usually located in the frontal area.

HP:0010637.label: Conjunctival amyloidosis
HP:0010637.definition: A form of amyloidosis that affects the conjunctiva.
HP:0010637.comment: The deposition of amyloid, a noncollagenous protein, in the conjunctiva, which presents as a discrete, nontender, nonulcerative, waxy, yellow-white subconjunctival tissue.

HP:0010638.label: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
HP:0010638.definition: An abnormally increased level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

HP:0010639.label: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
HP:0010639.definition: An abnormally increased level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
HP:0010639.comment: Bone alkaline phosphatase (BALP) is encoded by the tissue non-specific form of alkaline phosphatase and thus is an isoform of this isoenzyme.
exact_synonyms: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin

HP:0010640.label: Abnormal nasal cavity morphology
HP:0010640.definition: Abnormality of the nasal cavity (the cavity includes and starts at the nares and reaches all the way through to the and includes the choanae, the posterior nasal apertures).

HP:0010641.label: Abnormality of the midnasal cavity
HP:0010641.definition: Abnormality of the midnasal cavity which includes the cavity between the nares and the choanae.

HP:0010643.label: Midnasal atresia
HP:0010643.definition: Absence or abnormal closure of the midnasal cavity.

HP:0010644.label: Midnasal stenosis
HP:0010644.definition: Abnormal narrowing (stenosis) of the midnasal cavity, i.e., of the middle nasal meatus, which in neonates can cause respiratory distress.

HP:0010645.label: Aplasia of the distal phalanges of the toes
HP:0010645.definition: Absence of the distal phalanges of the toes.
exact_synonyms: Absent outermost bone of the toes

HP:0010646.label: Cervical spine instability
HP:0010646.definition: An abnormal lack of stability of the cervical spine.
HP:0010646.comment: The cervical spine is made up of two anatomically and functionally distinct segments: the upper cervical spine (C1and C2), which possesses the most rotational mobility with some degrees of frontal and sagittal plane mobility, and the lower cervical spine, which allows for two types of movements - flexion-extension and inclination-rotation. Cervical instability mainly involves the upper cervical spine, particularly between C1 and C2. Craniocervical ligaments are the main determinants of cervical spine stability.

HP:0010647.label: Abnormal elasticity of skin
HP:0010647.definition: Any abnormal increase or reduction in skin elasticity.

HP:0010648.label: Dermal translucency
HP:0010648.definition: An abnormally increased ability of the skin to permit light to pass through (translucency) such that subcutaneous structures such as veins display an increased degree of visibility.

HP:0010649.label: Flat nasal alae
HP:0010649.definition: An abnormal degree of flatness of the Ala of nose, which can be defined as a reduced nasal elevation index (lateral depth of the nose from the tip of the nose to the insertion of the nasal ala in the cheek x 100 divided by the side-to-side breadth of the nasal alae).

HP:0010650.label: Hypoplasia of the premaxilla
HP:0010650.definition: An abnormality of the premaxilla (the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla) causing it to appear relatively small in size compared to the other parts of the maxilla or other facial structures.
exact_synonyms: Underdevelopment of the primary palate bone
Decreased size of the primary palate bone
Hypoplasia of the primary palate bone

HP:0010651.label: Abnormal meningeal morphology
HP:0010651.definition: An abnormality of the Meninges, including any abnormality of the Dura mater, the Arachnoid mater, and the Pia mater.

HP:0010652.label: Abnormal dura mater morphology
HP:0010652.definition: An abnormality of the Dura mater.

HP:0010653.label: Abnormality of the falx cerebri
HP:0010653.definition: An abnormality of the Falx cerebri.
HP:0010653.comment: The falx cerebri refers to the fold of dura mater which descends vertically in the longitudinal fissure between the cerebral hemispheres.

HP:0010654.label: Aplasia of the falx cerebri
HP:0010654.definition: A developmental defect characterized by aplasia of the Falx cerebri.

HP:0010655.label: Epiphyseal stippling
HP:0010655.definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more epiphyses.
HP:0010655.comment: Stippling resolves with maturation of the epiphysis but is often replaced by some permanent epiphyseal abnormality.
exact_synonyms: Speckled calcifications in end part of bone

HP:0010656.label: Abnormal epiphyseal ossification
HP:0010656.definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of an epiphysis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the mineralisation or ossification of the epiphyses
related_synonyms: Abnormal maturation of the end part of a bone

HP:0010657.label: Patchy reduction of bone mineral density
HP:0010657.definition: Patchy (irregular) reduction in bone density. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.

HP:0010658.label: Patchy changes of bone mineral density
HP:0010658.definition: Patchy (irregular) changes in bone mineral density. These changes can either be patchy reduction or increase of mineral density as seen on x-rays. Depending on the pathomechanism and the underlying disease, these changes can either appear solely as reduction or increase or as a combination of both (patches of bone showing an increased density while others are affected by reduction of mineral density).

HP:0010659.label: Patchy variation in bone mineral density
HP:0010659.definition: Patchy (irregular) changes in bone mineral density with patches of bone showing an increased density side to side with patches that are affected by reduction of mineral density. This is sometimes referred to as a moth-eaten appearance on x-rays.
exact_synonyms: Patchy increased and decreased bone mineral density

HP:0010660.label: Abnormal hand bone ossification
HP:0010660.definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the skeleton of hand.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bones of the hand
related_synonyms: Abnormal maturation of the hand bones

HP:0010661.label: Absence of the third cerebral ventricle
HP:0010661.definition: A developmental defect characterized by the absence of the third ventricle.

HP:0010662.label: Abnormal diencephalon morphology
HP:0010662.definition: An abnormality of the Diencephalon, which together with the cerebrum (telencephalon) makes up the forebrain.
HP:0010662.comment: The diencephalon comprises the thalamus, hypothalamus, epithalamus, prethalamus or subthalamus and pretectum.

HP:0010664.label: Fusion of the left and right thalami
HP:0010664.definition: A developmental defect characterized by fusion of the left and right halves of the thalamus.

HP:0010665.label: Bilateral coxa valga
HP:0010665.definition: The presence of bilateral coxa valga.

HP:0010666.label: Hypoplasia of the anterior nasal spine
HP:0010666.definition: Underdevelopment of the anterior nasal spine of maxilla.
exact_synonyms: Decreased projection of anterior nasal spine
Decreased size of anterior nasal spine

HP:0010667.label: Aplasia of the maxilla
HP:0010667.definition: A congenital defect characterized by absence of the Maxilla.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the upper jaw bones

HP:0010668.label: Abnormal zygomatic bone morphology
HP:0010668.definition: An abnormality of the zygomatic bone.

HP:0010669.label: Hypoplasia of the zygomatic bone
HP:0010669.definition: Underdevelopment of the zygomatic bone. That is, a reduction in size of the zygomatic bone, including the zygomatic process of the temporal bone of the skull, which forms part of the zygomatic arch.

HP:0010672.label: Abnormality of the third metatarsal bone
HP:0010672.definition: An abnormality of the third metatarsal bone.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the 3rd long bone of foot

HP:0010674.label: Abnormal curvature of the vertebral column
HP:0010674.definition: The presence of an abnormal curvature of the vertebral column.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the curvature of the vertebral column

HP:0010675.label: Abnormal foot bone ossification
HP:0010675.definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the skeleton of foot.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bones of the feet
related_synonyms: Abnormal ossification involving bones of the feet

HP:0010678.label: Enuresis diurna
HP:0010678.definition: Enuresis occurring during waking hours of the day.

HP:0010679.label: Elevated tissue non-specific alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010679.definition: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
HP:0010679.comment: Tissue non-specific alkaline phosphatase (ALPP) is one of four distinct but related alkaline phosphatases. Entrez Gene ID 249, Uniprot P05186 (PPBT_HUMAN). The gene is also known as alkaline phosphatase, liver/bone/kidney (ALPL).

HP:0010680.label: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
HP:0010680.definition: An abnormally increased level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

HP:0010681.label: Elevated intestinal alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010681.definition: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.
HP:0010681.comment: Intestinal alkaline phosphatase (IAP) is one of four distinct but related alkaline phosphatases. Entrez Gene ID:248, Uniprot ID: P09923 (PPBI_HUMAN).

HP:0010682.label: Elevated placental alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010682.definition: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.
HP:0010682.comment: Placental alkaline phosphatase (ALPP) is one of four distinct but related alkaline phosphatases. Entrez Gene ID 250, Uniprot P05187 (PPB1_HUMAN).

HP:0010683.label: Low tissue non-specific alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010683.definition: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

HP:0010684.label: Low alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
HP:0010684.definition: An abnormally reduced level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

HP:0010685.label: Low alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
HP:0010685.definition: An abnormally reduced level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

HP:0010686.label: Low alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
HP:0010686.definition: An abnormally reduced level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

HP:0010687.label: Low intestinal alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010687.definition: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.

HP:0010688.label: Low placental alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010688.definition: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.

HP:0010689.label: Mirror image polydactyly
HP:0010689.definition: A hand or foot with more than five digits that has a recognizable A/P axis of symmetry. The axis can lie within a normally formed or partially duplicated digit resembling a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe, or hallux. Alternatively, the axis can be in an interdigital space with a flanking pair of digits that resemble a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe or hallux. The most lateral digits on each side of the hand/foot typically resemble fifth fingers/toes.
HP:0010689.comment: Transplantation of the ZPA (zone of polarized activity) to the anterior margin of a limb bud in the chick results in mirror image duplication of limb elements (Tabin, 1991). Similarly, mirror image duplication in the forelimb of the mouse has been observed with ectopic expression of Hox b-8 (Charit6 et al, 1994). Mirror hand anomaly in humans has been shown to be due to either aberrant positioning of the ZPA or altered inductive interactions of the Shh gene resulting in impairment of the mechanism responsible for the organization and differentiation of the limb bud, rather than a primary duplication event. In other words, the primary event results in failure of the radial ray to develop. The ulnar area will then induce the differentiation of two groups of ulnar rays. Timing of this insult could play a critical role in severity of this phenotypic feature. Syndromal mirror hand is probably due to agene mutation of the Shh gene (Hersh et al, 1995). Finally, the multiple hand deformity may be explained by true duplication of the ZPA.

HP:0010690.label: Mirror image hand polydactyly
HP:0010690.definition: Mirror image duplication of digits affecting the hands only.

HP:0010691.label: Mirror image foot polydactyly
HP:0010691.definition: Mirror image duplication of digits affecting the feet.

HP:0010693.label: Pulverulent cataract
HP:0010693.definition: A kind of congenital cataract that is characterized by a hollow sphere of punctate opacities involving the fetal nucleus and that usually occurs bilaterally.
HP:0010693.comment: The word "pulverulent " means dust-like and refers to the dustlike appearance of the punctate opacities in this type of cataract. The word pulverulent refers to the very small size of the punctate opacities (like flecks of dust) rather than to a dust-like color.

HP:0010694.label: Lamellar pulverulent cataract
HP:0010694.definition: A Lamellar cataract with a pulverulent (punctate, "dust-like" opacities) appearance.
HP:0010694.comment: Opacities located in the perinuclear (lamellar) zones of the lens.

HP:0010695.label: Sutural cataract
HP:0010695.definition: A type of congenital cataract in which the opacity follows the anterior or posterior Y suture.
HP:0010695.comment: During lens terminal differentiation, the originally cuboidal lens vesicle cells elongate into long fiber-like cells, or fibers. Y-shaped sutures form because of how the lens epithelial cells proliferate during formation. The Y sutures demarcate the boundaries between the lens cortex, which is peripheral to the Y sutures, and the lens nucleus, which is within and includes the Y sutures. The anterior Y suture is oriented upright, and the posterior Y suture is inverted.

HP:0010696.label: Polar cataract
HP:0010696.definition: A type of Congenital cataract in which the opacities occupy the subcapsular cortex at the anterior or posterior pole of the lens.

HP:0010697.label: Anterior pyramidal cataract
HP:0010697.definition: A type of anterior polar cataract which projects as a conical opacity into the anterior chamber.

HP:0010698.label: Nuclear pulverulent cataract
HP:0010698.definition: A type of nuclear cataract involving congenital dust-like (pulverulent) opacity of the embryonal and fetal nucleus.

HP:0010699.label: Triangular nuclear cataract
HP:0010699.definition: A nuclear cataract with a triangular form.

HP:0010701.label: Abnormal circulating immunoglobulin concentration
HP:0010701.definition: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of immunoglobulins in blood.
HP:0010701.comment: 'has part' some (amount and ('inheres in' some (IMR_0002090 and ('part of' some blood))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

HP:0010702.label: Increased circulating immunoglobulin concentration
HP:0010702.definition: An increased level of gamma globulin (immunoglobulin) in the blood.
HP:0010702.comment: In humans, immunoglobulins comprise the five antibody isotypes IgA, IgD, IgE, IgG and IgM.

HP:0010704.label: 1-2 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0010704.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the index finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

HP:0010705.label: 4-5 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0010705.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the fourth (ring) to the fifth (little) finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

HP:0010706.label: 1-3 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0010706.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the middle finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

HP:0010707.label: 1-4 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0010707.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the ring finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

HP:0010708.label: 1-5 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0010708.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the little finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints (complete syndactyly of all fingers of the hand).

HP:0010709.label: 2-4 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0010709.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second (index) to the fourth (ring) finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
exact_synonyms: Syndactyly of second to fourth fingers

HP:0010710.label: 3-5 finger syndactyly
HP:0010710.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the middle to little fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
exact_synonyms: Webbed third, fourth and fifth toes

HP:0010711.label: 1-2 toe syndactyly
HP:0010711.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one and two.

HP:0010712.label: 1-4 toe syndactyly
HP:0010712.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to four.

HP:0010713.label: 1-5 toe syndactyly
HP:0010713.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to five (complete syndactyly of all toes of the foot).

HP:0010714.label: 2-4 toe syndactyly
HP:0010714.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to four.

HP:0010715.label: 2-5 toe syndactyly
HP:0010715.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to five.

HP:0010716.label: 3-5 toe syndactyly
HP:0010716.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes three to five.

HP:0010717.label: Osseous syndactyly of toes
HP:0010717.definition: Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual bones of the toes. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a tibial-fibular axis. Fusions of bones of the toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "Symphalangism".

HP:0010719.label: Abnormality of hair texture
HP:0010719.definition: An abnormality of the texture of the hair.

HP:0010720.label: Abnormal hair pattern
HP:0010720.definition: An abnormality of the distribution of hair growth.

HP:0010721.label: Abnormal hair whorl
HP:0010721.definition: An abnormal hair whorl (that is, a patch of hair growing in the opposite direction of the rest of the hair).

HP:0010722.label: Asymmetry of the ears
HP:0010722.definition: An asymmetriy, i.e., difference in size, shape or position between the left and right ear.

HP:0010724.label: Advanced pneumatization of the mastoid process
HP:0010724.definition: An abnormally advanced degree of pneumatization (i.e., formation of air cells) in the mastoid process with respect to age-dependent norms.

HP:0010726.label: Prominent corneal nerve fibers
HP:0010726.definition: Abnormal prominence of the corneal nerve fibers.

HP:0010727.label: Spontaneous rupture of the globe
HP:0010727.definition: Rupture of the eyeball not due to trauma.

HP:0010728.label: Aplasia of the retina
HP:0010728.definition: A developmental defect characterized by absence of the retina.

HP:0010729.label: Cherry red spot of the macula
HP:0010729.definition: Pallor of the perifoveal macula of the retina with appearance of a small circular reddish choroid shape as seen through the fovea centralis due to relative transparency of the macula.

HP:0010730.label: Double eyebrow
HP:0010730.definition: This may present as a partial or complete duplication of the eyebrows.
HP:0010730.comment: Double eyebrow is commonly a feature of Mowat Wilson syndrome.

HP:0010731.label: Extension of eyebrows towards upper eyelid
HP:0010731.definition: The eyebrows extend towards - or even all the way down to - the margin of the upper eyelid.
HP:0010731.comment: This is commonly a feature of Jacobson syndrome.
exact_synonyms: Extension of eyebrows towards upper eyelid

HP:0010732.label: Nodular changes affecting the eyelids
HP:0010732.definition: Nodular changes affecting the eyelids may have many different causes such as cystic lesions (chalaziae, hordeolae), lipogranulomas, melanomas, infectious diseases (Molluscum contagiosum) and many more.

HP:0010733.label: Naevus flammeus of the eyelid
HP:0010733.definition: Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the eyelid.

HP:0010734.label: Fibrous dysplasia of the bones
HP:0010734.definition: Tumor-like growths that consist of replacement of the medullary bone with fibrous tissue, causing the expansion and weakening of the areas of bone involved. Especially when involving the skull or facial bones, the lesions can cause externally visible deformities. The skull is often, but not necessarily, affected, and any other bone or bones may be involved. Fibrous dysplasia can either effect isolated bones (Monostotic fibrous dysplasia) or also generalized all bones of the body (Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia).

HP:0010735.label: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
HP:0010735.definition: Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in many bones throughout of the body. Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia is a cardinal feature of McCune-Albright syndrome.

HP:0010736.label: Monostotic fibrous dysplasia
HP:0010736.definition: Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in only one bone.

HP:0010739.label: Osteopoikilosis
HP:0010739.definition: Osteopoikilosis is a benign, asymptomatic sclerotic dysplasia of the bones. It affects both male and female and may be seen at any age. Radiographically sclerotic circular or ovoid lesions are usually symmetrically distributed in a periarticular location. Lesions can increase or decrease in size and number in serial radiographs or even disappear and do not have increased bone radiotracer uptake.

HP:0010740.label: Osteopathia striata
HP:0010740.definition: A lamellar pattern visible on radiographs and mainly localized at the metaphyses of the long tubular bones. Pathologic-anatomical studies revealed that these benign signs on x-rays are the result of a juvenile metaphyseal bone necrosis. Calcifications in the necrotic marrow lead to this lamellar or lattice-like appearance.

HP:0010741.label: Pedal edema
HP:0010741.definition: An abnormal accumulation of excess fluid in the lower extremity resulting in swelling of the feet and extending upward to the lower leg.

HP:0010742.label: Edema of the upper limbs
HP:0010742.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin of the arms.

HP:0010743.label: Short metatarsal
HP:0010743.definition: Diminished length of a metatarsal bone, with resultant proximal displacement of the associated toe.
HP:0010743.comment: This is a subjective assessment and one generally compares the position of the MTP joint to that of the contralateral digit or the putatively shortened ray in proportion to the other rays. The affected digits should be specified.

HP:0010744.label: Absent metatarsal bone
HP:0010744.definition: A developmental abnormality characterized by the absence (aplasia) of a metatarsal bone.

HP:0010745.label: Aplasia of the phalanges of the toes
HP:0010745.definition: Absence of a digit or of one or more phalanges of a toe.

HP:0010746.label: Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the toes

HP:0010747.label: Medial flaring of the eyebrow
HP:0010747.definition: An abnormal distribution of eyebrow hair growth in the medial direction.

HP:0010748.label: Ectopic lacrimal punctum
HP:0010748.definition: Positioning of a lacrimal punctum other than at the medial margins of the eyelid.
HP:0010748.comment: The openings of the tear ducts are normally located at the medial margin of each eyelid. The opening on the lower eyelid border is more visible than the opening on the upper eyelid border. Ectopic positions can include the upper eyelid, nasal bridge, or inferior to medial aspect of the lower lid.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal position of the lacrimal punctum

HP:0010749.label: Blepharochalasis
HP:0010749.definition: Blepharochalasis is characterized by recurrent, non-painful, nonerythematous episodes of eyelid edema. It has been divided into hypertrophic and atrophic forms. In the hypertrophic form recurrent edema results in orbital fat herniation through a weakened orbital septum. Most patients who have blepharochalasis present in an atrophic condition with atrophy of redundant eyelid skin and superior nasal fat pads.
HP:0010749.comment: Most patients who have blepharochalasis present in an atrophic condition with atrophy of redundant eyelid skin and superior nasal fat pads. Most of these atrophic patients do not go through a hypertrophic phase. Multiple attacks of eyelid edema result in thinning, stretching, and atrophy of eyelid tissues. The eyelid skin becomes redundant, discolored, and atrophic, appearing like wrinkled cigarette paper. The upper eyelids are more commonly affected, but the lower eyelids may also be involved. Blepharochalasis is not synonymous with dermatochalasis.

HP:0010750.label: Dermatochalasis
HP:0010750.definition: Loss of elasticity of the upper and lower eyelids causing the skin to sag and bulge.

HP:0010751.label: Dimple chin
HP:0010751.definition: A persistent midline depression of the skin over the fat pad of the chin.

HP:0010752.label: Cleft mandible
HP:0010752.definition: Midline deficiency of the mandible and some or all overlying tissues.

HP:0010754.label: Abnormality of the temporomandibular joint
HP:0010754.definition: An anomaly of the temporomandibular joint.

HP:0010755.label: Asymmetry of the maxilla
HP:0010755.definition: Asymmetry between the left and right sides of the maxilla.
exact_synonyms: Asymmetry of right and left side of the maxilla

HP:0010756.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the premaxilla
HP:0010756.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the premaxilla.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the primary palate bone

HP:0010757.label: Aplasia of the premaxilla
HP:0010757.definition: Absence of the premaxilla, which is the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of the primary palate bone
Aplasia of the primary palate bone
Absence of the primary palate bone

HP:0010758.label: Abnormality of the premaxilla
HP:0010758.definition: An abnormality of the premaxilla, the most anterior part of the maxilla that usually bears the central and lateral incisors and includes the anterior nasal spine and inferior aspect of the piriform rim. The premaxilla contains the bone and teeth of the primary palate.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the intermaxillary segment of the maxilla
Abnormality of the primary palate bone

HP:0010759.label: Prominence of the premaxilla
HP:0010759.definition: Prominent positioning of the premaxilla in relation to the rest of the maxilla, the facial skeleton, or mandible. Not necessarily caused by an increase in size (hypertrophy of) the premaxilla.
HP:0010759.comment: As a consequence of prominence of the premaxilla, the overlying structures, the nose and philtrum, may appear prominent. There is increased convexity of the face and an increased nasolabial angle. In the presence of a normal sized mandible, retrognathia may be appreciated.
exact_synonyms: Prominence of the primary palate bone
Anterior position of the primary palate bone

HP:0010760.label: Absent toe
HP:0010760.definition: Aplasia of a toe. That is, absence of all phalanges of a non-hallux digit of the foot and the associated soft tissues.
HP:0010760.comment: This descriptor does NOT require absence of the metatarsal. The definition excludes partial absent hallux.

HP:0010762.label: Chordoma
HP:0010762.definition: A chordoma is a tumor that arises from embryonic remnants of the notochord along the length of the neuraxis. Chordomas generally occur in the sacrum, intracranially at the clivus, or along the spinal axis.
HP:0010762.comment: The notochord is a mesodermal embryonic structure that defines the primitive axis of the embryo and which survives in the adult vertebral column as the intervertebral disks.

HP:0010763.label: Low insertion of columella
HP:0010763.definition: Insertion of the posterior columella below the nasal base.
HP:0010763.comment: This feature is different from a convex Low hanging columella that has a normal insertion. It may be associated with a Short philtrum, but this should be assessed and coded separately. A low insertion is best appreciated when viewed from the side.

HP:0010764.label: Short eyelashes
HP:0010764.comment: Normal values are 7.99 - 1.05 mm in boys and 7.76 - 1.03 mm in girls.

HP:0010765.label: Palmar hyperkeratosis
HP:0010765.definition: Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand.

HP:0010766.label: Ectopic calcification
HP:0010766.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in a tissue or location in which calcification does not normally occur.

HP:0010767.label: Sacrococcygeal pilonidal abnormality
HP:0010767.definition: The presence of a cyst, fistula, or abscess in the sacrococcygeal region (gluteal crease) characteristically accompanied by hair and skin folds.

HP:0010769.label: Pilonidal sinus
HP:0010769.definition: A sinus in the coccygeal region (the region of the intergluteal cleft). A pilonidal sinus often contains hair and skin debris.

HP:0010771.label: Pilonidal abscess
HP:0010771.definition: A hair-containing cyst or sinus usually in the coccygeal region.

HP:0010772.label: Anomalous pulmonary venous return
HP:0010772.definition: A developmental defect characterized by abnormal connection of one or more pulmonary veins to the superior or inferior vena cava, the right atrium, or the coronary sinus, resulting in a left-to-right shunt of oxygenated blood.

HP:0010773.label: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return
HP:0010773.definition: A form of anomalous pulmonary venous return in which not all pulmonary veins drain abnormally. Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return frequently involves one or both of the veins from one lung.

HP:0010774.label: Cor triatriatum
HP:0010774.definition: The presence of an additional membrane in the left or right cardiac atrium which results in the subdivision of the affected atrium (and thus in total three atria, whence the name).

HP:0010775.label: Vascular ring
HP:0010775.definition: A developmental defect of the aortic arch system in which the trachea and esophagus are completely encircled by connected segments of the aortic arch and its branches. This occurs if the normal process of regression and persistence of the bilateral embryonic aortic arches fails.

HP:0010776.label: Tracheobronchmegaly
HP:0010776.definition: Marked widening of the trachea and major bronchi that may be predispose to chronic respiratory tract infection.
HP:0010776.comment: Tracheobronchmegaly is typically characterized by atrophy or absence of elastic fibers and thinning of smooth muscle layers in the trachea and main bronchi.

HP:0010777.label: Bronchomegaly
HP:0010777.definition: Marked widening of the major bronchi that may be predispose to chronic respiratory tract infection.

HP:0010779.label: Large pelvis bone
HP:0010779.definition: The presence of an abnormally large pelvis.

HP:0010780.label: Hyperacusis
HP:0010780.definition: Over-sensitivity to certain frequency ranges of sound.
HP:0010780.comment: Hyperacusis refers to a general hypersensitivity to sound of any frequency, and phonophobia to an anxious sensitivity towards specific sound largely independent of its volume. Hyperacusis and phonophobia represent disturbances of central auditory processing without peripheral pathology, often combined with psychosomatic reactions. Listeners with hearing loss often struggle to detect low-level sounds, but as the sound intensity rises above threshold, loudness initially grows at a faster than normal rate, but the growth rate slows with increasing intensity so that normal loudness is achieved at high intensities. This phenomenon is referred to as loudness recruitment. However, in some hearing-impaired listeners,loudness continues to grow more rapidly than normal at suprathreshold intensities causing moderately intense sounds to be perceived as louder than normal, a debilitating condition known as hyperacusis or loudness intolerance.

HP:0010781.label: Skin dimple
HP:0010781.definition: Skin dimples are cutaneous indentations that are the result of tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) causing an indentation.

HP:0010782.label: Shoulder dimple
HP:0010782.definition: A subtype of skin dimples occurring in the shoulder region.
HP:0010782.comment: Symmetrical dimples of the skin overlying the acromial process of the scapulae are called bi-acromial dimples.

HP:0010783.label: Erythema
HP:0010783.definition: Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
exact_synonyms: Redness of skin or mucous membrane

HP:0010784.label: Uterine neoplasm
HP:0010784.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the uterus.

HP:0010785.label: Gonadal neoplasm
HP:0010785.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of a gonad.

HP:0010786.label: Urinary tract neoplasm
HP:0010786.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary system.

HP:0010787.label: Genital neoplasm
HP:0010787.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the genital system.

HP:0010788.label: Testicular neoplasm
HP:0010788.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the testis.

HP:0010790.label: Hypoplasia of the Leydig cells
HP:0010790.definition: Underdevelopment of the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis. These cells produce testosterone.

HP:0010791.label: Hyperplasia of the Leydig cells
HP:0010791.definition: Hypertrophy or overdevelopment of the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis. These cells produce testosterone.

HP:0010793.label: Bifid nail
HP:0010793.definition: A digit with two nails, with at least some soft tissue between them.

HP:0010794.label: Impaired visuospatial constructive cognition
HP:0010794.definition: Reduced ability affecting mainly visuospatial cognition which may be tested using pattern construction (for example by Differential Ability Scales, which test a person's strengths and weaknesses across a range of intellectual abilities).
HP:0010794.comment: The ability to see an object or picture as a set of parts and then to construct a replica of the original from these parts is known as visuospatial constructive cognition. Impaired visuospatial constructive cognition is one of the characteristic featrues of most patients with Williams-Beuren Syndrome.

HP:0010797.label: Hemangioblastoma
HP:0010797.definition: A hemangioblastoma is a benign vascular neoplasm that arises almost exclusively in the central nervous system. Hemangioblastomas consist of a tightly packed cluster of small blood vessels forming a mass of up to 1 or 2 cm in diameter.

HP:0010798.label: Lip freckle
HP:0010798.definition: Increased focal pigmentation of the vermilion of the lips.
HP:0010798.comment: Lip freckles may be accompanied by Perioral hyperpigmentation, but this should be assessed separately. Lentigo is commonly used as a synonym for freckle in reference to the vermilion, but these are distinct terms when referring to the skin.

HP:0010799.label: Pinealoma
HP:0010799.definition: A neoplasm of the pineal gland.
HP:0010799.comment: Pineal tumors are a rare and heterogeneous group of primary central nervous system neoplasms, including pineal parenchymal tumors (pineocytomas, pineal parenchymal tumors of intermediate differentiation, and pineoblastomas), germ cell tumors, and neuroepithelial tumors, such as astrocytomas, ependymomas, and papillary tumor of the pineal region.

HP:0010800.label: Absent cupid's bow
HP:0010800.definition: Lack of paramedian peaks and median notch of the upper lip vermilion.
HP:0010800.comment: This bow is often absent in a Thin vermilion of the upper lip, but that should be assessed separately. This finding is commonly associated with Smooth philtrum, but that should be coded separately.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of cupid's bow

HP:0010801.label: Underdeveloped nasolabial fold
HP:0010801.definition: Reduced bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion or commissure).

HP:0010802.label: Perioral hyperpigmentation
HP:0010802.definition: Increased pigmentation, either focal or generalized, of the skin surrounding the vermilion of the lips.
HP:0010802.comment: Periorbital hyperpigmentation may be accompanied by Lip freckles, but this should be assessed separately.
exact_synonyms: Darkening of skin around the mouth

HP:0010803.label: Everted upper lip vermilion
HP:0010803.definition: Inner aspect of the upper lip vermilion (normally apposing the teeth) visible in a frontal view, i.e., the presence of an everted upper lip.
HP:0010803.comment: In frontal view, with the face relaxed, the apparent height of the upper lip vermilion is excessive and the upper incisors may be visible. On profile view, the vermilion is more convex than usual. An everted upper lip may be associated with a short philtrum, and may be secondary to protruded upper teeth, but these should be assessed and described separately.

HP:0010804.label: Tented upper lip vermilion
HP:0010804.definition: Triangular appearance of the oral aperture with the apex in the midpoint of the upper vermilion and the lower vermilion forming the base.
HP:0010804.comment: This finding is distinguished from an Exaggerated Cupid's bow by the alteration of the shape of the oral aperture.

HP:0010805.label: Upturned corners of mouth
HP:0010805.definition: Oral commissures positioned superior to the midline labial fissure.
HP:0010805.comment: This finding should be assessed with the mouth closed, the lips in relaxed contact, and the face relaxed. The finding may be difficult to assess if the upper lip is enlarged.

HP:0010806.label: U-Shaped upper lip vermilion
HP:0010806.definition: Gentle upward curve of the upper lip vermilion such that the center is placed well superior to the commissures.
HP:0010806.comment: The U-shaped upper vermilion is a more rounded version of the Tented upper lip vermilion. In U-shaped upper vermilion there is loss of the central groove of the Cupid's bow. Replaces: Carpmouth; Fish mouth (pejorative terms).

HP:0010807.label: Open bite
HP:0010807.definition: Visible space between the dental arches in occlusion.
HP:0010807.comment: An open bite produces an absence of vertical overlap of the two dental arches. It may be associated with malocclusion, but this should be coded separately. Open bite can be accompanied by malocclusion, which is a complex bundled term. The Angle classification of malocclusion (Classes I-III) is widely used in the orthodontics community [Moyers, [1973]] for the characterization of malocclusion.
exact_synonyms: Open bite between upper and lower teeth
Absence of overlap of upper and lower teeth

HP:0010808.label: Protruding tongue
HP:0010808.definition: Tongue extending beyond the alveolar ridges or teeth at rest.
HP:0010808.comment: Protruding tongue may or may not be associated with a Large tongue, and that finding should be assessed and coded separately.

HP:0010809.label: Broad uvula
HP:0010809.definition: Increased width of the uvula (subjective finding).
HP:0010809.comment: This finding often accompanies a Submucous cleft palate, but this should be coded separately. A longitudinal groove indicating incomplete fusion of the two parts of the uvula may be present with a broadened uvula and has sometimes been called abortive cleft uvula.

HP:0010810.label: Long uvula
HP:0010810.comment: In clinical practice, the size of the uvula cannot be easily measured and is not static, since it depends on the position of the soft palate, the base of the tongue, and the head. Therefore, judgment of change in length of the uvula depends heavily on the experience of the observer.

HP:0010812.label: Short uvula
HP:0010812.comment: Objective measurement of the length of the uvula can be determined on a lateral cephalograms. However, in this series we are not relying on radiographs for assessment of findings. In clinical practice, the size of the uvula cannot be easily measured and is not static, since it depends on the position of the soft palate, the base of the tongue, and the head. Therefore, judgment of change in length of the uvula depends heavily on the experience of the observer.

HP:0010813.label: Abnormal number of hair whorls
HP:0010813.definition: More than two clockwise hair whorls.
HP:0010813.comment: Most individuals have one clockwise hair whorl at a single point on the scalp lateral to the midline but close to the vertex of the skull. Five percent of the population has two whorls. A double hair whorl is sometimes referred to as a double crown. In 10%, whorl direction is counter-clockwise.

HP:0010814.label: Abnormal position of hair whorl
HP:0010814.definition: Hair growth from a single point on the scalp in any location other than lateral to the midline and close to the vertex of the skull.
HP:0010814.comment: Placement of hair whorl should be described as parietal, vertex, eccentric, etc. In addition, the number of hair whorls should be noted. Five percent of the population has two whorls.

HP:0010815.label: Nevus sebaceous
HP:0010815.definition: A congenital, hairless plaque consisting of overgrown epidermis, sebaceous glands, hair follicles, apocrine glands and connective tissue. They are a variant of epidermal naevi. Sebaceous naevi most often appear on the scalp, but they may also arise on the face, neck or forehead. At birth, a sevaceous nevus typically appears as a solitary, smooth, yellow-orange hairless patch. Sebaceous naevi become more pronounced around adolescence, often appearing bumpy, warty or scaly.

HP:0010816.label: Epidermal nevus
HP:0010816.definition: Epidermal naevi are due to an overgrowth of the epidermis and may be present at birth (50%) or develop during childhood.
HP:0010816.comment: Epidermal nevus arises from a defect in the ectoderm and in general are due to an overgrowth of keratinocytes. Subclasses of epidermal nevus include Linear epidermal naevus, epidermolytic epidermal naevus, acantholytic epidermal naevus, linear porokeratosis, and systematized epidermal naevus. Several other conditions are also characterized by benign overgrowth of the epidermis and its appendages (organoid naevi), including inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal naevus, sebaceous naevus, sweat gland naevi, comedone naevus, and Becker naevus.

HP:0010817.label: Linear nevus sebaceous
HP:0010817.definition: A type of nevus sebaceous with a linear form, raised borders and yellowish color.

HP:0010818.label: Generalized tonic seizure
HP:0010818.definition: A generalized tonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by bilateral limb stiffening or elevation, often with neck stiffening without a subsequent clonic phase. The tonic activity can be a sustained abnormal posture, either in extension or flexion, sometimes accompanied by tremor of the extremities.
HP:0010818.comment: Characterized by a sudden increase in muscle tone whereby the body, arms, or legs make sudden stiffening movements and consciousness is usually preserved. Tonic seizures can occur during sleep. Tonic seizures usually affect both sides of the body, and cause a fall if the affected person was standing when the seizure started.

HP:0010819.label: Atonic seizure
HP:0010819.definition: Atonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by a sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic event lasting about 1 to 2 seconds, involving head, trunk, jaw, or limb musculature.
HP:0010819.comment: This term describes the initial semiology of the seizure without specifying whether the onset is focal or generalized. Thus it can be used for coding atonic seizures when the onset is not known.

HP:0010820.label: Focal emotional seizure with crying
HP:0010820.definition: Focal emotional seizure with crying (dacrystic) is characterized by the presence of stereotyped crying, this may be accompanied by lacrimation, sad facial expression and sobbing. The subjective emotion of sadness may or may not be present.
HP:0010820.comment: Crying is a rare feature of an epileptic seizure, and is more commonly a feature of a non-epileptic seizure. The word dacrystic is derived from the Greek word dakryon (tear).

HP:0010821.label: Focal emotional seizure with laughing
HP:0010821.definition: Focal emotional seizure with laughing (gelastic) is characterized by bursts of laughter or giggling, usually without appropriate related emotion of happiness, and described as 'mirthless'.
HP:0010821.comment: This seizure type is characteristic of seizures arising in the hypothalamus (see hypothalamic hamartoma), but can occur in seizures arising in the frontal or temporal lobes.

HP:0010822.label: Scintillating scotoma
HP:0010822.definition: A scintillating scotoma is a common visual aura that can precede a migraine, whereby a spot of flickering light near the center of the visual fields occurs. The spot prevents vision, and is thus termed scotoma. The scotoma can extend into one or more shimmering arcs of white or colored flashing lights.

HP:0010823.label: Ridged cranial sutures
HP:0010823.definition: An overlap of the bony plates of the skull in an infant, with or without early closure.

HP:0010824.label: Abnormal fifth cranial nerve morphology
HP:0010824.definition: Any structural abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve

HP:0010825.label: Abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve
HP:0010825.definition: Abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve.

HP:0010826.label: Abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve
HP:0010826.definition: Abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve.

HP:0010827.label: Abnormal seventh cranial physiology
HP:0010827.definition: Abnormality of the seventh cranial nerve sometimes also referred to as the facial nerve.

HP:0010828.label: Hemifacial spasm
HP:0010828.definition: Intermittent clonic or tonic contraction of muscles supplied by facial nerve. Muscles are relaxed in between contractions.
HP:0010828.comment: Hemifacial spasm presents in the fifth or sixth decade of life, and is almost always unilateral. An attack usually begins with brief clonic movements of the orbicularis oculi and spreads over years to other facial muscles. Hemifacial spasm is often the result of chronic irritation of the facial nerve or nucleus.
exact_synonyms: Spasms on one side of the face

HP:0010829.label: Impaired temperature sensation
HP:0010829.definition: A reduced ability to discriminate between different temperatures.
HP:0010829.comment: Temperature sensation can be tested by touching the skin several seconds with a water flask filled to the desired temperature. Persons with normal temperature sensation should at least be able to identify as warm a flask that is 35-36 degrees C and identify as cool a flask at 28-32 degrees C.

HP:0010830.label: Impaired tactile sensation
HP:0010830.definition: A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation). This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.

HP:0010831.label: Impaired proprioception
HP:0010831.definition: A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position.

HP:0010832.label: Abnormality of pain sensation
HP:0010832.definition: Pain is an unpleasant sensation that can range from mild, localized discomfort to agony, whereby the physical part of pain results from nerve stimulation and is often accompanied by an emotional component. This term groups abnormalities in pain sensation presumed to result from abnormalities related to the specific nerve fibers that carry the pain impulses to the brain.

HP:0010833.label: Spontaneous pain sensation
HP:0010833.definition: Spontaneous pain is a kind of neuropathic pain which occurs without an identifiable trigger.

HP:0010834.label: Trophic changes related to pain
HP:0010834.definition: Trophic changes is a term used to describe abnormalities in the area of pain that include primarily wasting away of the skin, tissues, or muscle, thinning of the bones, and changes in how the hair or nails grow, including thickening or thinning of hair or brittle nails.

HP:0010835.label: Dissociated sensory loss
HP:0010835.definition: A pattern of sensory loss with selective loss of touch sensation and proprioception without loss of pain and temperature, or vice-versa.
HP:0010835.comment: Dissociated sensory loss indicates a focal lesion within the spinal cord or brainstem.

HP:0010836.label: Abnormal circulating copper concentration
HP:0010836.comment: An abnormality in the concentration of copper, which normally occurs as a cofactor for a number of proteins including amine oxidases and chaperone proteins.

HP:0010837.label: Decreased circulating ceruloplasmin concentration
HP:0010837.definition: Decreased concentration of ceruloplasmin in the blood.
HP:0010837.comment: Ceruloplasmin is the major copper-carrying protein in the serum. Decreased serum ceruloplasmin levels can indicate other defects in copper metabolism.

HP:0010838.label: High nonceruloplasmin-bound serum copper
HP:0010838.definition: An increased concentration of non ceruloplasmin bound copper in the blood.

HP:0010839.label: Increased urinary copper concentration
HP:0010839.definition: An increased concentration of copper in the urine.

HP:0010841.label: Multifocal epileptiform discharges
HP:0010841.definition: An abnormality in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG) and being identified at multiple locations (foci).

HP:0010843.label: EEG with focal slow activity
HP:0010843.definition: Focal (localized) slow activity reflects focal dysfunction, not diffuse dysfunction (i.e., encephalopathy).

HP:0010844.label: EEG with multifocal slow activity
HP:0010844.definition: Multifocal slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

HP:0010845.label: EEG with generalized slow activity
HP:0010845.definition: Diffuse slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
HP:0010845.comment: Generalized slow activity in the EEG typically signifies serious dysfunction of the entire brain.

HP:0010846.label: EEG with persistent abnormal rhythmic activity

HP:0010847.label: EEG with spike-wave complexes (<2.5 Hz)
HP:0010847.definition: The presence of complexes of slow spikes and slow waves (<2.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).
HP:0010847.comment: Spikes (<70 ms) and sharp waves (70-200 ms) are sharp transient waves that have a strong association with epilepsy. No difference is noted in terms of clinical significance of spikes and sharp waves. Significant spikes usually are followed by a slow wave.
