HP:0010848.label: EEG with spike-wave complexes (2.5-3.5 Hz)
HP:0010848.definition: The presence of complexes of spikes and waves (2.5-3.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).

HP:0010849.label: EEG with spike-wave complexes (>3.5 Hz)
HP:0010849.definition: The presence of complexes of spikes and waves (>3.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).

HP:0010850.label: EEG with spike-wave complexes
HP:0010850.definition: Complexes of spikes (<70 ms) and sharp waves (70-200 ms), which are sharp transient waves that have a strong association with epilepsy, in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

HP:0010851.label: EEG with burst suppression
HP:0010851.definition: The burst suppression pattern in electroencephalography refers to a characteristic periodic pattern of low voltage (<10 microvolts) suppressed background and a relatively shorter pattern of higher amplitude slow, sharp, and spiking complexes.
HP:0010851.comment: Burst suppression can occur in a generalized or lateralized distribution and is often a sign of severe encephalopathy. Generally, an interburst interval of 30 seconds or less is associated with a better prognosis than longer interburst intervals (>30 sec). Burst suppression is an electroencephalogram (EEG) pattern in which high voltage activity (burst) and flatline (suppression) periods alternate systematically but quasiperiodically (almost periodic but with variations in inter- and intra-burst duration) is a state of profound brain inactivation.

HP:0010852.label: EEG with photoparoxysmal response
HP:0010852.definition: EEG abnormalities (epileptiform discharges) evoked by flashing lights or black and white striped patterns.
HP:0010852.comment: In some patients, seizures can be provoked by specific external factors (reflex epilepsy), including flickering lights and patterns. These patients commonly show epileptiform discharges in the EEG when stimulated with flashing lights, black and white striped patterns and television. These evoked EEG abnormalities are called photoparoxysmal responses.

HP:0010853.label: EEG with periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges
HP:0010853.definition: Periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs)are periodic, lateralized, and epileptiform. PLEDs show a relatively constant interval between discharges (0.5 to 3 seconds).
HP:0010853.comment: The epileptiform morphology of the discharges is not invariable, as PLEDS are often closer to slow waves than to sharp waves in morphology. PLEDs are often are caused by acute destructive focal lesions. PLEDs are often a transitory phenomenon, disappearing in a matter of weeks, even if the causal lesion persists, and often transforming into a less specific but more persistent focal slow appearance.

HP:0010854.label: EEG with generalized low amplitude activity
HP:0010854.definition: An abnormal generalized reduction in amplitude of the cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised low amplitude activity

HP:0010855.label: EEG with localized low amplitude activity
HP:0010855.definition: An abnormal localized reduction in amplitude of the cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
exact_synonyms: EEG with localised low amplitude activity

HP:0010857.label: EEG with periodic abnormalities
HP:0010857.definition: Periodically recurring abnormalities in the EEG.

HP:0010858.label: EEG with hyperventilation-induced epileptiform discharges
HP:0010858.definition: Epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
HP:0010858.comment: Hyperventilation (overbreathing) is widely used as a diagnostic procedure to activate epileptiform EEG discharges.

HP:0010859.label: Frank breech presentation
HP:0010859.definition: A kind of breech presentation in which the hips are flexed and the knees are extended.

HP:0010860.label: Complete breech presentation
HP:0010860.definition: A kind of breech presentation in which the hips are flexed and the knees are flexed.

HP:0010861.label: Incomplete breech presentation
HP:0010861.definition: A kind of breech presentation in which one or both hips are extended and one or both of the fetus' feet are pointing down and entering the birth canal.

HP:0010862.label: Delayed fine motor development
HP:0010862.definition: A type of motor delay characterized by a delay in acquiring the ability to control the fingers and hands.

HP:0010863.label: Receptive language delay
HP:0010863.definition: A delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

HP:0010864.label: Severe intellectual disability
HP:0010864.definition: Severe intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by severely sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 20-34.
HP:0010864.comment: Persons with severe mental retardation can be taught basic life skills and simple tasks with supervision.

HP:0010865.label: Oppositional defiant disorder
HP:0010865.definition: An enduring pattern of uncooperative, defiant, and hostile behavior towards authority figures that does not involve major antisocial violations, is not accounted for by the child's developmental stage, and results in significant functional impairment. A certain level of oppositional behavior is common in children and adolescents.
HP:0010865.comment: Oppositional defiant disorder is essentially a persistent pattern of tantrums, arguments, and angry or disruptive behavior that exceeds what can be considered normal.

HP:0010866.label: Abdominal wall defect
HP:0010866.definition: An incomplete closure of the abdominal wall.

HP:0010867.label: Dyssynergia
HP:0010867.definition: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to smoothly perform the elements of a voluntary movement in the appropriate order and speed. With dyssynergia, a voluntary movement appears broken down into its component parts.

HP:0010868.label: Ocular dyssynergia
HP:0010868.definition: A type of dyssynergia affecting eye movements and characterized by the inability to smoothly follow a visual target across the visual field.

HP:0010869.label: Asynergia
HP:0010869.definition: A type of dyssynergy characterized by the lack of the ability to smoothly perform the elements of a voluntary movement in the appropriate order and speed.

HP:0010871.label: Sensory ataxia
HP:0010871.definition: Incoordination of movement caused by a deficit in the sensory nervous system. Sensory ataxia can be distinguished from cerebellar ataxia by asking the patient to close his or her eyes. Persons with cerebellar ataxia show only a minimal worsening of symptoms, whereas persons with sensory ataxia show a marked worsening of symptoms.
HP:0010871.comment: Afferent (seonsory) ataxia is caused by lackof proprioceptive feedback during gait and stance. It can be caused by lesions to the peripheral nerves, the dorsal root ganglia, or the spinal cord. It can be distinguished from cerebellar ataxia by (1) heavy dependence of the affected individual on visual guidance; (2) a minor degree of oculomotor deficits; and (3) the absence of dysarthria. Afferent ataxia may be associated with impaired tendon reflexes and sensory deficits.

HP:0010872.label: T-wave inversion
HP:0010872.definition: An inversion of the T-wave (which is normally positive).

HP:0010873.label: Cervical spinal cord atrophy
HP:0010873.definition: Atrophy of the cervical segment of the spinal cord.

HP:0010874.label: Tendon xanthomatosis
HP:0010874.definition: The presence of xanthomas (intra-and extra-cellular accumulations of cholesterol) extensor tendons (typically over knuckles, Achilles tendon, knee, and elbows).

HP:0010875.label: Chaddock reflex
HP:0010875.definition: A diagnostic reflex elicited by stimulation of the skin over the surface of the lateral malleolus of the foot. The Chaddock refelx is present if there is extension of one or more or all of the toes with or without fanning of them when the external inframalleolar skin is stimulated. The Chaddock sign, similar to the Babinski sign, is taken to be an indication of disease of the spinocortical (pyramidal) tract.

HP:0010876.label: Abnormal circulating protein concentration
HP:0010876.definition: An abnormal level of a circulating protein in the blood.

HP:0010877.label: Monocular strabismus
HP:0010877.definition: A type of strabismus in which the fixating eye is always the same one, while the other eye is constantly deviated. Monocular strabismus is to be distinguished from alternating strabismus, in which either of the eyes 'squints' at different times.

HP:0010878.label: Fetal cystic hygroma
HP:0010878.definition: The presence during the prenatal period of a cystic mass with multiple septa with multiple, asymmetric, thin-walled cysts near the posterior aspect of the neck. Fetal cystic hygroma can be defined as nuchal translucency with or without septations measuring greater than 3.0 mm. Increased NT refers to a measurement above the 95th centile, and the term is used irrespective of whether the collection of fluid is septated or not, and whether it is confined to the neck or envelopes the whole fetus. After 14 weeks, increased NT usually resolves, but in some cases it evolves into nuchal edema or cystic hygromas.
HP:0010878.comment: Upon ultrasound examination, fetal cystic hygroma presents as a cystic mass with multiple septa with multiple, asymmetric, thin-walled cysts related to the posterior aspect of the neck. Cystic hygromas can range from increased nuchal translucency to thin-walled cystic masses that may become larger than the fetal head. The cysts may result from a lymphatic abnormality, possibly one caused by absent or inefficient connections between the lymphatic and venous systems. Depending on the site, the cut off may vary from site to site. Lowest would be 2.5 mm and highest 3.5 mm.

HP:0010880.label: Increased nuchal translucency
HP:0010880.definition: Nuchal translucency is the sonographic appearance of subcutaneous accumulation of liquid in the back of the fetal neck in the first trimester of pregnancy (11-14 gestational weeks of pregnancy).
HP:0010880.comment: Increased nuchal translucency may be related to a cystic hygroma or to mesenchymal edema. Increased nuchal translucency can be classified into three categories: 1) cardiac abnormalities, combined with abnormal ductus venosus flow velocities, is found, leading to the theory that cardiac failure causes nuchal translucency enlargement; 2) various types of abnormalities are found in the extracellular matrix of the nuchal skin of fetuses with increased nuchal translucency; 3) abnormal lymphatic development is demonstrated in fetuses with increased nuchal translucency.

HP:0010881.label: Abnormality of the umbilical cord
HP:0010881.definition: An abnormality of the umbilical cord, which is the cord connecting the developing embryo or fetus to the placenta.

HP:0010882.label: Pulmonary valve atresia
HP:0010882.definition: A congenital disorder of the pulmonary valve in which the orifice of the valve fails to develop.

HP:0010883.label: Aortic valve atresia
HP:0010883.definition: A congenital disorder of the aortic valve in which the orifice of the valve fails to develop.

HP:0010884.label: Acromelia
HP:0010884.definition: Shortening of the extremities affecting primarily the distal parts of the limbs (hands and feet) in relation to the other segments of the limbs.

HP:0010885.label: Avascular necrosis
HP:0010885.definition: A disease where there is cellular death (necrosis) of bone components due to interruption of the blood supply.
HP:0010885.comment: The interruption of the blood supply may have many different causes such as rapid growth, heredity causes, trauma or overuse, anatomic conformation, dietary imbalances or secondary effects of other diseases.
exact_synonyms: Death of bone due to decreased blood supply

HP:0010886.label: Osteochondritis dissecans
HP:0010886.definition: A joint disorder caused by blood deprivation in the subchondral bone causing the subchondral bone to die in a process called avascular necrosis. The bone is then reabsorbed by the body, leaving the articular cartilage it supported prone to damage. The result is fragmentation (dissection) of both cartilage and bone, and the free movement of these osteochondral fragments within the joint space, causing pain and further damage.
HP:0010886.comment: Joints that are most often affected by Osteochondrosis dissecans are elbow and hip, but also wrist and ankel joints.

HP:0010888.label: Morbus Koehler
HP:0010888.definition: Morbus Koehler is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Os naviculare pedis.

HP:0010889.label: Morbus Kienboeck
HP:0010889.definition: Morbus Kienboeck is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Os lunatum.
HP:0010889.comment: Results most often from a stress-fracture and consecutive devascularisation of the Os lunatum.

HP:0010890.label: Morbus Osgood-Schlatter
HP:0010890.definition: Morbus Osgood-Schlatter is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Tuberositas tibiae.
HP:0010890.comment: Painfull irritation and localized bony necrosis affecting the Tuberositas tibiae, where the patellar tendon inserts.

HP:0010891.label: Morbus Scheuermann
HP:0010891.definition: A developmental growth retardation of the vertebral end plates that may lead to secondary destruction of the vertebral end plates and protrusion of the nucleus pulposus into the vertebral body (so called Schmorl's nodes as seen on x-rays).
HP:0010891.comment: Scheuermann's disease usually manifests during the 2nd decade and leads to the appearance of the so called adolescence kyphosis. Late manifestations may be wedge-shaped vertebrae, platyspondyly and arthrosis affecting the verterbal collum.

HP:0010892.label: Abnormal circulating branched chain amino acid concentration
HP:0010892.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a branched chain family amino acid in the blood circulation.

HP:0010893.label: Abnormal circulating phenylalanine concentration
HP:0010893.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of phenylalanine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010894.label: Abnormal circulating serine family amino acid concentration
HP:0010894.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a serine family amino acid in the blood circulation.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of serine family amino acid metabolism

HP:0010895.label: Abnormal circulating glycine concentration
HP:0010895.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glycine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010896.label: Hypersarcosinemia
HP:0010896.definition: An elevated plasma concentration of sarcosine.
HP:0010896.comment: Sarcosine is the N-methyl derivative of glycine.

HP:0010897.label: Hypersarcosinuria
HP:0010897.definition: An elevated urinary concentration of sarcosine.

HP:0010898.label: Abnormal circulating sarcosine concentration
HP:0010898.definition: An deviation from the normal concentration of sarcosine in the blood circulation.
HP:0010898.comment: Sarcosine, which is also known as N-methylglycine, is an intermediate and byproduct in glycine synthesis and degradation.

HP:0010899.label: Abnormal circulating aspartate family amino acid concentration
HP:0010899.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of an aspartate family amino acid in the blood circulation.

HP:0010900.label: Abnormal circulating threonine concentration
HP:0010900.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of threonine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010901.label: Abnormal circulating methionine concentration
HP:0010901.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of methionine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010902.label: Abnormal circulating glutamine family amino acid concentration
HP:0010902.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a glutamine family amino acid in the blood circulation.

HP:0010903.label: Abnormal circulating glutamine concentration
HP:0010903.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glutamine in the blood circulation.
HP:0010903.comment: Glutamine is a charge-neutral, polar amino acid.

HP:0010904.label: Abnormal circulating histidine concentration
HP:0010904.definition: An abnormality of a histidine metabolic process.

HP:0010906.label: Hyperhistidinemia
HP:0010906.definition: An increased concentration of histidine in the blood.
HP:0010906.comment: Blood histidine levels over 500 micromole per liter. Normal blood histidine levels are around 80-90 micromole per liter.

HP:0010907.label: Abnormal circulating proline concentration
HP:0010907.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of proline or a proline metabolite in the blood circulation.

HP:0010908.label: Abnormal circulating lysine concentration
HP:0010908.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of lysine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010909.label: Abnormal circulating arginine concentration
HP:0010909.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of arginine in the blood circulation.
HP:0010909.comment: Arginine is a charged, aliphatic amino acid.

HP:0010910.label: Hypervalinemia
HP:0010910.definition: An increased concentration of valine in the blood.

HP:0010911.label: Hyperleucinemia
HP:0010911.definition: An increased concentration of leucine in the blood.
HP:0010911.comment: Normal leucine blood levels are around 120-160 micromole per liter.

HP:0010912.label: Abnormal circulating isoleucine concentration
HP:0010912.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of isoleucine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010913.label: Hyperisoleucinemia
HP:0010913.definition: An increased concentration of isoleucine in the blood.
HP:0010913.comment: Normal isoleucine blood levels are around 60-80 micromole per liter.

HP:0010914.label: Abnormal circulating valine concentration
HP:0010914.definition: Any deviation from the normal circulation of valine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010915.label: Abnormal circulating pyruvate family amino acid concentration
HP:0010915.definition: An abnormality of a pyruvate family amino acid metabolic process.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of pyruvate family amino acid metabolism

HP:0010916.label: Abnormal circulating alanine concentration
HP:0010916.definition: An abnormality of an alanine metabolic process.

HP:0010917.label: Abnormal circulating tyrosine concentration
HP:0010917.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of tyrosine in the blood circulation.

HP:0010918.label: Abnormal circulating cysteine concentration
HP:0010918.definition: An abnormality of a cysteine metabolic process.

HP:0010919.label: Abnormal circulating homocysteine concentration
HP:0010919.definition: An abnormality of a homocysteine metabolic process.

HP:0010920.label: Zonular cataract
HP:0010920.definition: Zonular cataracts are defined to be cataracts that affect specific regions of the lens.
HP:0010920.comment: Zonular cataracts include specific regions of the lens and include nuclear cataracts, which affect the fetal or embryonic lens nucleus and lamellar cataracts. These tend to affect lens fibers that are formed at the same time, resulting in a shell like opacity. Zonular cataracts can also be characterized as dense or pulverulent (dusty appearing), and can be accompanied by arcuate opacities extending into the lens cortex, called cortical riders.

HP:0010921.label: Coralliform cataract
HP:0010921.definition: A 'coral-like' pattern of opacity in the lens of the eye. That is, a cataract with an irregular, stellate form.

HP:0010922.label: Membranous cataract
HP:0010922.definition: A form of cataract in which the lens substance has shrunk, leaving a collapsed, flattened capsule with little or no cortex or epithelium on the lens.

HP:0010923.label: Anterior subcapsular cataract
HP:0010923.definition: A type of cataract affecting the anterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to ('beneath') the lens capsule.

HP:0010924.label: Posterior cortical cataract
HP:0010924.definition: A cataract that affects the posterior part of the cortex of the lens.

HP:0010926.label: Aculeiform cataract
HP:0010926.definition: A kind of nuclear cataract characterized by fiberglasslike or needlelike crystals projecting in different directions, through or close to the axial region of the lens.
HP:0010926.comment: This phenotype is characterized by fiberglasslike or needlelike crystals projecting in different directions, through or close to the axial region of the lens. Some crystals may be 11 mm in length, and their biochemical composition is not known. This type of cataract is considered to be different from the corraliform cataract, which does not show the needlelike projections. This opacity does not appear to respect the sutures or the direction of the lens fibers (Francois 1963) and appears to originate from the fetal and postnatal nuclei, suggesting a congenital origin with some postnatal progression, if any. See Figure 1 of PMID:10521291.

HP:0010927.label: Abnormal blood inorganic cation concentration
HP:0010927.definition: An abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis

HP:0010928.label: obsolete Increased urinary orotic acid concentration

HP:0010930.label: Abnormal blood monovalent inorganic cation concentration
HP:0010930.definition: An abnormality of monovalent inorganic cation homeostasis.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of monovalent inorganic cation homeostasis

HP:0010932.label: Abnormal circulating nucleobase concentration
HP:0010932.definition: An abnormality of a nucleobase metabolic process.
HP:0010932.comment: This term is used to refers to abnormality in chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleobase, a nitrogenous base that is a constituent of a nucleic acid, e.g. the purines: adenine, guanine, hypoxanthine, xanthine and the pyrimidines: cytosine, uracil, thymine.

HP:0010933.label: Hyperxanthinemia
HP:0010933.definition: An increased level of xanthine in the blood circulation.
HP:0010933.comment: Xanthine is a purine base that is a product of purine degradation.

HP:0010934.label: Xanthinuria
HP:0010934.definition: An increased concentration of xanthine in the urine.
HP:0010934.comment: Xanthinuria is generally caused by a defect in the xanthine oxidase, an enzyme that catalyzes the oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine and can further catalyze the oxidation of xanthine to uric acid. The formation of xanthine stones in the urinary tract is the main evidence of this abnormality.

HP:0010935.label: Abnormality of the upper urinary tract
HP:0010935.definition: An abnormality of the upper urinary tract.
HP:0010935.comment: The upper urinary tract is a subdivision of urinary system which consists of the kidney and the ureters.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the upper urinary tract

HP:0010936.label: Abnormality of the lower urinary tract
HP:0010936.definition: An abnormality of the lower urinary tract.
HP:0010936.comment: The lower urinary tract is a subdivision of urinary system which consists of the urinary bladder and the urethra.

HP:0010937.label: Abnormal nasal skeleton morphology
HP:0010937.definition: An abnormality of the nasal skeleton.

HP:0010938.label: Abnormal external nose morphology
HP:0010938.definition: An abnormality of the external nose.

HP:0010939.label: Abnormal nasal bone morphology
HP:0010939.definition: An abnormality of the nasal bone, comprising the left nasal bone and the right nasal bone.

HP:0010940.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the nasal bone
HP:0010940.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the nasal bone.

HP:0010941.label: Aplasia of the nasal bone
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of the nasal bone
Lack of development of the nasal bone

HP:0010942.label: Echogenic intracardiac focus
HP:0010942.definition: A finding of a focus of increased echogenicity upon prenatal ultrasound examination of the fetus. The foci may be present in one or both ventricles. Echogenic intracardiac focus (EICF) is defined as a focus of echogenicity comparable to bone, in the region of the papillary muscle in either or both ventricles of the fetal heart.
HP:0010942.comment: An echogenic intracardiac focus (EIF) is generally believed to be a normal variant, observed in 5% of all fetuses during second trimester sonography, but the risk of aneuploidies such as Down syndrome is increased in fetuses with EIF.

HP:0010943.label: Echogenic fetal bowel
HP:0010943.definition: Echogenic bowel is defined as fetal bowel with homogenous areas of echogenicity that are equal to or greater than that of surrounding bone.
HP:0010943.comment: Echogenic fetal bowel may be observed in fetuses with normal outcomes, but may also be a marker for diseases such as cystic fibrosis, congenital infection, chromosomal anomalies, and intraamniotic bleeding. This finding can be observed on prenatal ultrasound. The echogenicity has been classified as either focal or multifocal. Grade 2 suggests that echogenicity is equal to bone whereas grade 3 suggests that it is greater.

HP:0010944.label: Abnormal renal pelvis morphology
HP:0010944.definition: An abnormality of the renal pelvis.

HP:0010945.label: Fetal pyelectasis
HP:0010945.definition: Mild pyelectasis is defined as a hypoechoic spherical or elliptical space within the renal pelvis that measures at least 5mm and not more than 10 mm. The measurement is taken on a transverse section through the fetal renal pelvis using the maximum anterior-to-posterior measurement.
HP:0010945.comment: The renal pelvis is the part of the kidney that collects urine. Fetal pyelectasis is a prenatal ultrasound finding that is diagnosed with enlargement of the renal pelvis from 4 to 10 millimeters. In many cases, fetal pyelectasis resolves spontaneously. Note that dilatation of the renal pelvis to more than 10 mm is referred to as severe pyelectasis or hydronephrosis. Measurements less than 5mm are normal, should not be designated as pyelectasis, and should not be reported (PMID:16100637).

HP:0010946.label: Dilatation of the renal pelvis
HP:0010946.definition: The presence of dilatation of the renal pelvis.

HP:0010947.label: Abnormality of ductus venosus blood flow
HP:0010947.definition: A first-trimester prenatal ultrasound finding of abnormal blood flow in the ductus venosus.
HP:0010947.comment: The ductus venosus is a bypass between the umbilical vein and the inferior vena cava in the fetus. The blood flow through this bypass decreases immediately after birth. Functional closure, which is followed by anatomic closure, is virtually complete within a few weeks of birth. The typical abnormal finding in abnormal ductus venosus flow is a reversed a-wave.

HP:0010948.label: Abnormal fetal cardiovascular morphology
HP:0010948.definition: A structural abnormality of the fetal circulation system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the fetal cardiovascular system
Abnormality of the fetal circulation system
Abnormality of the foetal cardiovascular system
Abnormality of the foetal circulation system

HP:0010949.label: Abnormality of umbilical vein blood flow
HP:0010949.definition: A first-trimester prenatal ultrasound finding of abnormal blood flow in the umbilical vein.
HP:0010949.comment: Umbilical vein blood flow (UVBF) is closely related to the mass of placental cotyledons and is considered an expression of the amount of oxygen and nutrients transferred from the mother to the fetus.

HP:0010950.label: Abnormal fourth ventricle morphology
HP:0010950.definition: An abnormality of the fourth ventricle.
HP:0010950.comment: The fourth ventricle is the cerebral ventricle that extends from the cerebral aqueduct to the obex, and is located within the pons and the upper part of the medulla oblongata.

HP:0010951.label: Abnormal third ventricle morphology
HP:0010951.definition: An abnormality of the third ventricle.
HP:0010951.comment: The third ventricle is the cerebral ventricle that is located in the midline between the left and right lateral ventricles.

HP:0010952.label: Mild fetal ventriculomegaly
HP:0010952.definition: A kind of ventriculomegaly occurring in the fetal period and usually diagnosed by prenatal ultrasound. Cerebral ventriculomegaly is defined by atrial measurements 10 mm or more. Mild ventriculomegaly (MVM) is defined as measurements between 10 and 15 mm. Measurements are obtained from an axial plane at the level of the thalamic nuclei just below the standard image to measure the BPD (PMID:16100637).
HP:0010952.comment: A ventricular atrial diameter of more than 10 mm at 20-24 weeks of gestation has been accepted as defining ventriculomegaly because it represents at least 3 standard deviations above the mean (which is roughly 5 mm at 20-24 weeks of gestation). If the diameter is above 15 mm, the ventriculomegaly is considered to be severe. Amongst the most common causes of ventriculomegaly are impaired absorption of CSF, developmental cerebral defects, and destroyed brain tissue.

HP:0010953.label: Noncommunicating hydrocephalus
HP:0010953.definition: A form of hydrocephalus in which the flow of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) within the cerebral ventricular system or in the outlets of the CSF to the arachnoid space is obstructed.
HP:0010953.comment: The most common form of noncommunicating hydrocephalus is obstructive and is caused by intraventricular or extraventricular mass-occupying lesions that disrupt the ventricular anatomy.

HP:0010954.label: Hypoplastic right ventricle
HP:0010954.comment: Hypoplastic right ventricle generally occurs as part of the Hypoplastic right heart syndrome (HRHS), which causes inadequate blood flow to the lungs postnatally and thus leads to cyanosis. HRHS involves pulmonary valve atresia, hypoplasia of the right ventricle, hypoplasia of the tricuspid valve, and a small, hypoplastic pulmonary artery. As the ductus arteriosus closes postnatally, infants with HRHS become critically ill.

HP:0010955.label: Dilatation of the bladder
HP:0010955.definition: The presence of a dilated urinary bladder.

HP:0010956.label: Fetal megacystis
HP:0010956.definition: Fetal megacystis is an abnormally enlarged bladder identified at any gestational age.
HP:0010956.comment: Abnormal enlargement of the fetal bladder can be detected by prenatal ultrasound by fourteen weeks of gestation. In some cases, dilatation of the fetal bladder is transient and resolves without sequelae, and in other cases it is the earliest manifestation of bladder outlet obstruction.

HP:0010957.label: Congenital posterior urethral valve
HP:0010957.definition: A developmental defect resulting in an obstructing membrane in the posterior male urethra.
HP:0010957.comment: Congenital posterior urethral valve is a cause of bladder outlet obstruction in male newborns. It results from a failure of resorption of the caudal end of the Wolffian duct into the primitive cloaca at the site of the future verumontanum in the posterior urethra (Following normal resorption of the posterior urethral valve there remain the posterior urethral folds, also called plicae colliculi).

HP:0010958.label: Bilateral renal agenesis
HP:0010958.definition: A bilateral form of agenesis of the kidney.

HP:0010959.label: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP:0010959.definition: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) - previously known as congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM) - is a relatively rare developmental malformation of the lower respiratory tract. It is a hamartomatous, dysplastic developmental abnormality of the lung characterized by abnormal airway patterning during lung branching morphogenesis and is formed by abnormal branching of the immature bronchioles.
HP:0010959.comment: The term CPAM has been recommended as being preferable to the term congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation, since the lesions are cystic or adenomatoid in only a limited number of cases. Only three types of CPAMs are distinguished at imaging: large cyst CPAM (type I) and small cyst CPAM (type II), which constitute macrocystic CPAMs; and microcystic or solid type (type III) lesions, which have cysts that are smaller than 5 mm in diameter, with no discernible cystic spaces.
exact_synonyms: Congenital cystic disease of the lung
Congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung

HP:0010963.label: Absence of stomach bubble on fetal sonography
HP:0010963.definition: By the 14th week of gestation it is nearly always possible to visualized the fluid-filled fetal stomach bubble on prenatal sonography. This term refers to the absence of a normal fetal stomach bubble on fetal ultrasonography performed at around 16 to 20 weeks' gestation.
HP:0010963.comment: The absence of stomach bubble on fetal sonography can be an indication of malformations such as esophageal atresia, especially in combination with polyhydramnios.
exact_synonyms: Absence of stomach bubble on foetal sonography

HP:0010964.label: Abnormal circulating long-chain fatty-acid concentration
HP:0010964.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a long-chain fatty acid in the blood circulation.
HP:0010964.comment: A long-chain fatty-acid is defined as an aliphatic monocarboxylic acid with a chain length of C13 to C18.

HP:0010965.label: Abnormal circulating phytanic acid concentration
HP:0010965.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of phytanic acid in the blood circulation.
HP:0010965.comment: Phytanic acid is a branched-chain saturated fatty acid consisting of hexadecanoic acid carrying methyl substituents at positions 3, 7, 11 and 15.

HP:0010966.label: Abnormal circulating fatty-acid anion concentration
HP:0010966.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a fatty acid anion in the blood circulation.
HP:0010966.comment: A fatty acid anion is the conjugate base of a fatty acid.

HP:0010967.label: Abnormal circulating carnitine concentration
HP:0010967.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation.
HP:0010967.comment: L-carnitine (3-hydroxy-4-N.trimethylammonium butyrate) plays a key role in facilitating the transport of long-chain fatty acids from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix, where they undergo 13-oxidation.

HP:0010970.label: Blood group antigen abnormality
HP:0010970.definition: An abnormality of an erythrocyte cell surface molecule.
HP:0010970.comment: During development, the human immune system recognizes antigens of the body as 'self' and does not generate antibodies against them.

HP:0010971.label: Absence of Lutheran antigen on erythrocytes
HP:0010971.definition: Absence of the Lutheran antigen (a type I integral membrane glycoprotein) from the surface of red blood cells.

HP:0010972.label: Anemia of inadequate production
HP:0010972.definition: A kind of anemia characterized by inadequate production of erythrocytes.

HP:0010974.label: Abnormal myeloid leukocyte morphology
HP:0010974.comment: A myeloid leukocyte refers to a cell of the monocyte, granulocyte, or mast cell lineage.

HP:0010975.label: Abnormal B cell count
HP:0010975.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of total B cells or any deviation of the propoortion of a B cell subtype. B cells are commonly characterized as CD19+ or CD20+ lymphocytes, or their subpopulations, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, measured ex vivo.

HP:0010976.label: Decreased total B cell count
HP:0010976.definition: The absolute number of B cells in the blood, per microlitre is below the lower limit of normal of the reference range for the appropriate sex and age-group.
HP:0010976.comment: Plasma B cells differentiate from B cells and secrete large amounts of antibodies.

HP:0010977.label: Abnormal phagocytosis
HP:0010977.definition: An abnormal functioning of phagocytosis. Phagocytosis is an elegant but complex process for the ingestion and elimination of pathogens, but it is also important for the elimination of apoptotic cells and hence fundamental for tissue homeostasis. Phagocytosis can be divided into four main steps: (i) recognition of the target particle, (ii) signaling to activate the internalization machinery, (iii) phagosome formation, and (iv) phagolysosome maturation.

HP:0010978.label: Abnormality of immune system physiology
HP:0010978.definition: A functional abnormality of the immune system.

HP:0010979.label: Abnormality of lipoprotein cholesterol concentration
HP:0010979.definition: An abnormal increase or decrease in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
HP:0010979.comment: Lipoproteins transport fats (lipids) in the blood circulation. Lipids are insoluble in water, meaning that they could not be transported in the blood circulation on their own. There are five major types of lipoproteins: (i) chylomicrons; VLDL (very low-density lipoprotein); (iii) IDL (intermediate-density lipoprotein); (iv) LDL (low-density lipoprotein); and (v) HDL (high-density lipoprotein). Clinical measures assess the amount of cholesterol carried by different lipoproteins. For instance, LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) is the maount of cholesterol carried by LDL.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the level of lipoprotein cholesterol

HP:0010980.label: Hyperlipoproteinemia
HP:0010980.definition: An abnormal increase in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0010981.label: Hypolipoproteinemia
HP:0010981.definition: An abnormal decrease in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

HP:0010982.label: Polygenic inheritance
HP:0010982.definition: A mode of inheritance that depends on a mixture of major and minor genetic determinants possibly together with environmental factors. Diseases inherited in this manner are termed complex diseases.

HP:0010983.label: Oligogenic inheritance
HP:0010983.definition: A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of a few gene loci. It is recommended this term be used for traits governed by three loci, although it is noted that usage of this term in the literature is not uniform.

HP:0010984.label: Digenic inheritance
HP:0010984.definition: A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of two gene loci.

HP:0010987.label: Abnormal cellular immune system morphology
HP:0010987.definition: An abnormality of the morphology or counts of the cells that make up the immune system.

HP:0010988.label: Abnormality of the extrinsic pathway
HP:0010988.definition: An abnormality of the extrinsic pathway (also known as the tissue factor pathway) of the coagulation cascade.
HP:0010988.comment: The extrinsic pathway is a protein activation cascade that contributes to blood coagulation and consists of the self-limited process linking exposure and activation of tissue factor to the activation of clotting factor X.

HP:0010989.label: Abnormality of the intrinsic pathway
HP:0010989.definition: An abnormality of the intrinsic pathway (also known as the contact activation pathway) of the coagulation cascade.
HP:0010989.comment: The intrinsic pathway requires coagulation factors VIII, IX, X, XI, and XII, as well as the proteins prekallikrein (PK) and high-molecular-weight kininogen (HK or HMWK), in addition to calcium ions and phospholipids secreted from platelets.

HP:0010990.label: Abnormality of the common coagulation pathway
HP:0010990.definition: An abnormality of blood coagulation, common pathway.
HP:0010990.comment: The common pathway is a protein activation cascade that contributes to blood coagulation and consists of events leading from the formation of activated factor X to the formation of active thrombin, the cleavage of fibrinogen by thrombin, and the formation of cleaved fibrin into a stable multimeric, cross-linked complex.

HP:0010991.label: Abnormal morphology of the abdominal musculature
HP:0010991.definition: An abnormality of the abdominal musculature.

HP:0010992.label: Stress urinary incontinence
HP:0010992.definition: Involuntary urine leakage synchronous with exertion, or actions such as sneezing, or coughing.

HP:0010993.label: Abnormal cerebral subcortex morphology
HP:0010993.definition: An abnormality of the cerebral subcortex.
HP:0010993.comment: The cerebral subcortex contains the basal ganglia and the cerebral white matter.

HP:0010994.label: Abnormal corpus striatum morphology
HP:0010994.definition: Abnormality of the striatum, which is the largest nucleus of the basal ganglia, comprising the caudate, putamen and ventral striatum, including the nucleus accumbens.
HP:0010994.comment: The striatum (also known as the neostriatum or striate nucleus) contains the caudate nucleus and putamen, which are separated from one another by a white matter tract called the internal capsule. The striatum is part of the basal ganglia and receives input from the cerebral cortex. Essentially all cortical areas (sensory, motor and associational) project to the striatum. The other major input to the striatum comes from the thalamus, particularly the intralaminar thalamic nuclei.

HP:0010995.label: Abnormal circulating dicarboxylic acid concentration
HP:0010995.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a dicarboxylic acid in the blood circulation.
HP:0010995.comment: A dicarboxylic acid is an oxoacid containing two carboxy groups.

HP:0010996.label: Abnormal circulating monocarboxylic acid concentration
HP:0010996.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a monocarboxylic acid in the blood circulation.

HP:0010997.label: Chromosomal breakage induced by ionizing radiation
HP:0010997.definition: Increased amount of chromosomal breaks in cultured blood lymphocytes or other cells induced by treatment with ionizing radiation.
HP:0010997.comment: Increased tendency to chromosomal breakage induced by crosslinking agents is typical for several disorders including ataxia teleangiectasia and Nijmegen breakage syndrome.
exact_synonyms: Chromosomal breakage induced by ionising radiation

HP:0010998.label: Increased susceptibility to spontaneous sister chromatid exchange
HP:0010998.definition: An increase in the number of spontaneous sister chromatid exchanges observed in cell culture of lymphocytes or other cells.
HP:0010998.comment: Increased susceptibility to spontaneous sister chromatid exchange is characteristic for Bloom syndrome.

HP:0011001.label: Increased bone mineral density
HP:0011001.definition: An abnormal increase of bone mineral density, that is, of the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones which is often referred to as osteosclerosis. Osteosclerosis can be detected on radiological examination as an increased whiteness (density) of affected bones.
HP:0011001.comment: This term may be merged with Increased bone density in the future or made obsolete.

HP:0011002.label: Osteopetrosis
HP:0011002.definition: Abnormally increased formation of dense trabecular bone tissue. Despite the increased density of bone tissue, osteopetrotic bones tend to be more fracture-prone than normal.

HP:0011003.label: High myopia
HP:0011003.definition: A severe form of myopia with greater than -6.00 diopters.

HP:0011004.label: Abnormal systemic arterial morphology
HP:0011004.definition: An abnormality of the systemic arterial tree, which consists of the aorta and other systemic arteries.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the systemic arterial tree

HP:0011005.label: Mixed cirrhosis
HP:0011005.definition: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of regenerative nodules of a variety of sizes.
HP:0011005.comment: In mixed cirrhosis, there are regenerating nodules under and over 3 mm in size.

HP:0011006.label: Abnormal morphology of the musculature of the neck
HP:0011006.definition: An abnormality of the neck musculature.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the musculature of the neck

HP:0011008.label: Temporal pattern
HP:0011008.definition: The speed at which disease manifestations appear and develop.

HP:0011009.label: Acute
HP:0011009.definition: Sudden appearance of disease manifestations over a short period of time.
HP:0011009.comment: The word acute is applied to different time scales depending on the disease or manifestation and does not have an exact definition in minutes, hours, or days.

HP:0011010.label: Chronic
HP:0011010.definition: Slow, creeping onset, slow progress and long continuance of disease manifestations.
HP:0011010.comment: According to the U.S. National Center for Health Statistics, a chronic condition is one lasting 3 months or more.

HP:0011011.label: Subacute
HP:0011011.definition: Somewhat rapid onset and change of disease manifestations.
HP:0011011.comment: Subacute is between acute and chronic.

HP:0011012.label: Abnormal circulating polysaccharide concentration
HP:0011012.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of a polysaccharide in the blood circulation.

HP:0011013.label: Abnormal circulating carbohydrate concentration
HP:0011013.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of a carbohydrate in the blood circulation.
HP:0011013.comment: An abnormality of the metabolism (include abnormality of the concentration) of a carbohydrate, including monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides, and substances derived from them.

HP:0011014.label: Abnormal glucose homeostasis
HP:0011014.comment: An abnormality of any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of glucose within an organism or cell.

HP:0011015.label: Abnormal blood glucose concentration
HP:0011015.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of glucose in the blood.

HP:0011016.label: obsolete Abnormality of urine glucose concentration

HP:0011017.label: Abnormal cellular physiology
HP:0011017.definition: An abnormality in a cellular process.

HP:0011018.label: Abnormality of the cell cycle
HP:0011018.definition: An abnormality of the cell cycle.

HP:0011020.label: Abnormality of mucopolysaccharide metabolism
HP:0011020.definition: An abnormality of the metabolism of mucopolysaccharide.

HP:0011021.label: Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration
HP:0011021.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of an enzyme in the blood circulation.

HP:0011022.label: Abnormal circulating unsaturated fatty acid concentration
HP:0011022.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of an unsaturated fatty acid in the blood circulation.

HP:0011023.label: Abnormal circulating prostaglandin circulation
HP:0011023.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a prostaglandin in the blood circulation.

HP:0011024.label: Abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
HP:0011024.definition: An abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract.

HP:0011025.label: Abnormal cardiovascular system physiology
HP:0011025.definition: Abnormal functionality of the cardiovascular system.

HP:0011026.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the vagina
HP:0011026.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the vagina.

HP:0011027.label: Abnormal fallopian tube morphology
HP:0011027.definition: An abnormality of the fallopian tube.
HP:0011027.comment: The Fallopian tubes (also known as oviducts, uterine tubes, and salpinges) are ducts that lead from the ovaries into the uterus.

HP:0011029.label: Internal hemorrhage
HP:0011029.definition: The presence of hemorrhage within the body.

HP:0011030.label: Abnormal blood transition element cation concentration
HP:0011030.definition: An abnormality of the homeostasis (concentration) of transition element cation.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of transition element cation homeostasis

HP:0011031.label: Abnormality of iron homeostasis
HP:0011031.definition: An abnormality of the homeostasis (concentration) of iron cation.

HP:0011032.label: Abnormality of fluid regulation
HP:0011032.definition: An abnormality of the regulation of body fluids.

HP:0011033.label: Impairment of fructose metabolism
HP:0011033.definition: An impairment of a fructose metabolic process.

HP:0011034.label: Amyloid deposition
HP:0011034.definition: Pathologic deposits of specific fibrillar protein aggregates with distinct microscopic properties, particularly affinity for the dye Congo red with typical birefringence.
HP:0011034.comment: Amyloid deposition is associated with amyloidosis, the pathologic process or disease caused by the tissue deposition of amyloid, often leading to organ dysfunction. This term, and its descendents, refer to the amyloid deposition (the phenotypic feature). Other clinical manifestations of amyloidosis should be coded separately.

HP:0011035.label: Abnormal renal cortex morphology
HP:0011035.definition: An abnormality of the cortex of the kidney.

HP:0011036.label: Abnormality of renal excretion
HP:0011036.definition: An altered ability of the kidneys to void urine and/or specific substances.

HP:0011037.label: Decreased urine output
HP:0011037.definition: A decreased rate of urine production.
HP:0011037.comment: A reduction in the overall amount of urine output.

HP:0011039.label: Abnormal helix morphology
HP:0011039.definition: An abnormality of the helix. The helix is the outer rim of the ear that extends from the insertion of the ear on the scalp (root) to the termination of the cartilage at the earlobe.

HP:0011040.label: Abnormal intrahepatic bile duct morphology
HP:0011040.definition: An abnormality of the intrahepatic bile duct.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the intrahepatic bile duct

HP:0011041.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the cervical spine
HP:0011041.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the cervical vertebral column.

HP:0011043.label: Abnormal circulating adrenocorticotropin concentration
HP:0011043.definition: An abnormal concentration of corticotropin in the blood.
HP:0011043.comment: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), also known as corticotropin, is a polypeptide hormone produced and secreted by the pituitary gland comprising 39 amino acid residues coupled in a linear sequence. . It is a component of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and stimulates increased production and release of corticosteroids and cortisol from the adrenal cortex.
related_synonyms: Abnormality of circulating adrenocorticotropic hormone level

HP:0011044.label: Abnormal number of permanent teeth
HP:0011044.definition: The presence of an altered number of of permanent teeth.

HP:0011045.label: Agenesis of permanent maxillary central incisor
HP:0011045.comment: This feature is to be distinguished from single central upper incisor, which is median.
exact_synonyms: Agenesis of adult maxillary central incisor
Failure of development of permanent maxillary central incisor
related_synonyms: Absence of permanent upper front tooth
Absence of permanent upper central incisor
Absence of permanent maxillary central incisor

HP:0011046.label: Agenesis of primary maxillary central incisor
HP:0011046.definition: Agenesis of upper central primary incisor.
HP:0011046.comment: This feature is to be distinguished from single central upper incisor, which is median.
exact_synonyms: Agenesis of deciduous maxillary central incisor
Failure of development of deciduous maxillary central incisor
Failure of development of primary maxillary central incisor
related_synonyms: Absence of upper front baby tooth
Absence of primary maxillary central incisor
Absence of deciduous maxillary central incisor

HP:0011047.label: Agenesis of primary mandibular central incisor
exact_synonyms: Agenesis of primary lower central incisor
Failure of development of deciduous mandibular central incisor
Agenesis of deciduous lower central incisor
Failure of development of primary mandibular central incisor
related_synonyms: Absence of deciduous mandibular central incisor
Absence of primary mandibular central incisor
Missing lower central incisor milk tooth

HP:0011048.label: Agenesis of permanent mandibular central incisor
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of permanent mandibular central incisor
Agenesis of adult mandibular central incisor
related_synonyms: Absence of permanent lower central incisor
Absence of permanent lower front tooth
Absence of permanent mandibular central incisor

HP:0011049.label: Agenesis of primary maxillary lateral incisor
HP:0011049.definition: Agenesis of one or more maxillary lateral incisor, comprising the maxillary lateral primary incisor.
exact_synonyms: Agenesis of deciduous maxillary lateral incisor
Failure of development of deciduous maxillary lateral incisor
Failure of development of primary maxillary lateral incisor
related_synonyms: Absence of primary maxillary lateral incisor
Absence of deciduous maxillary lateral incisor

HP:0011050.label: Agenesis of permanent maxillary lateral incisor
HP:0011050.definition: Agenesis of one or more upper lateral secondary incisor.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of permanent maxillary lateral incisor
Agenesis of permanent upper lateral incisor
Failure of development of permanent upper lateral incisor
related_synonyms: Absence of permanent maxillary lateral incisor

HP:0011051.label: Agenesis of premolar
HP:0011051.comment: Note that premolar teeth occur only in the permanent dentition.

HP:0011052.label: Agenesis of maxillary premolar
HP:0011052.comment: Note that premolar teeth occur only in the permanent dentition.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of maxillary bicuspid
Failure of development of maxillary premolar

HP:0011053.label: Agenesis of mandibular premolar
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of mandibular premolar

HP:0011055.label: Agenesis of permanent molar
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of secondary molar
Failure of development of permanent molar

HP:0011056.label: Agenesis of first permanent molar tooth
HP:0011056.definition: Agenesis of either maxillary first permanent molar or mandibular first permanent molar or both.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of six year molar
Failure of development of first permanent molar

HP:0011057.label: Agenesis of second permanent molar
HP:0011057.definition: Agenesis of either mandibular second permanent molar or maxillary second permanent molar.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of twelve year molar
Failure of development of second permanent molar

HP:0011060.label: Dentinogenesis imperfecta limited to primary teeth
HP:0011060.definition: Developmental dysplasia of dentin affecting only the primary dentition.

HP:0011061.label: Abnormality of dental structure
HP:0011061.definition: An abnormality of the structure or composition of the teeth.

HP:0011063.label: Abnormal incisor morphology
HP:0011063.definition: An abnormality of morphology of the incisor tooth.

HP:0011064.label: Abnormal number of incisors
HP:0011064.definition: The presence of an altered number of the incisor teeth.

HP:0011065.label: Conical incisor
HP:0011065.definition: An abnormal conical morphology of the incisor tooth.
HP:0011065.comment: Conical incisors are incisors that are round in cross-sectional views of the crown or that have a rounded appearance. Conical incisors may have a pointed shape that tapers to a point at the tip of the tooth. One speaks of conical incisor for a conical shaped tooth that is located in the region where incisors normally are.

HP:0011067.label: Mesiodens
HP:0011067.definition: A supernumerary tooth in the midline between the maxillary central incisors.
HP:0011067.comment: A mesiodens is not a supernumerary incisor (i.e., it does not have the morphology of an incisor). Rather, it is a conoid, extra tooth located between the maxillary central incisors. Mesiodens is the most common supernumerary tooth. Typically, they are small. They are usually conical in shape but may have heterogeneous forms. Mesiodens may remain unerupted and cause failure of a permanent incisor to erupt. Mesiodens may develop in an inverted position.

HP:0011068.label: Odontoma
HP:0011068.comment: MPATH defines odontoma as a hamartomatous malformation of odontogenic tissue. It may vary from nondescript masses of dental tissue (complex odontoma) to multiple well-formed teeth (compound odontoma).

HP:0011069.label: Supernumerary tooth
HP:0011069.definition: The presence of one or more teeth additional to the normal number.
HP:0011069.comment: Age-related physiological sequential eruption should be taken into account during evaluation. The type and the location of the additional tooth/teeth should be added to the description. Supernumerary teeth are uncommon (in 0.21% of deciduous dentitions and in 0.9% of permanent dentitions), and often abnormal positioning of a normal number of teeth is wrongly classified as supernumerary teeth. Supernumerary teeth are most frequent in the upper maxilla, and typically, a single additional tooth is present. We discourage the use of distodens, distomolars (an extra fourth molar posterior to the third molar), paramolars (supernumerary tooth in the molar region) but rather to mention the presence of the supernumerary tooth mesial to or distal to a tooth from the normal series. Diagnosing a supernumerary tooth may require radiographic examination. A supernumerary tooth present between the maxillary central incisors is called mesiodens.

HP:0011070.label: Abnormal molar morphology
HP:0011070.definition: An abnormality of morphology of molar tooth.

HP:0011071.label: Abnormal permanent molar morphology
HP:0011071.definition: An abnormality of morphology of permanent molar.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of shape of adult molar
Abnormality of shape of permanent molar

HP:0011072.label: Rootless teeth
related_synonyms: Tooth with dentin dysplasia type i

HP:0011073.label: Abnormality of dental color
HP:0011073.definition: A developmental defect of tooth color.

HP:0011074.label: Localized hypoplasia of dental enamel
HP:0011074.definition: A localized form of developmental hypoplasia of the dental enamel.

HP:0011075.label: Green teeth
HP:0011075.comment: Green teeth are a rare finding in children with neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to blood group incompatibility, sepsis-induced cholestasis or biliary atresia. Rarely, green staining of the teeth may be seen with cholestasis and sepsis.

HP:0011079.label: Impacted tooth
HP:0011079.definition: A tooth that has not erupted because of local impediments (overcrowding or fibrous gum overgrowth).

HP:0011080.label: Abnormal premolar morphology
HP:0011080.definition: An abnormality of morphology of premolar tooth.

HP:0011081.label: Incisor macrodontia
HP:0011081.definition: Increased size of the incisor tooth.

HP:0011082.label: Conical primary incisor
HP:0011082.definition: An abnormal conical morphology of the primary incisor.

HP:0011083.label: Conical maxillary incisor
HP:0011083.definition: An abnormal conical morphology of either maxillary primary incisor tooth or maxillary permanent incisor tooth or both.

HP:0011084.label: Hypocalcification of dental enamel
HP:0011084.definition: A form of hypomineralization of enamel characterized by reduced calcification.

HP:0011085.label: Hypomature dental enamel
HP:0011085.definition: A form of hypomineralization of enamel characterized by a chalky appearance of the enamel with orange, brown, or white color.
HP:0011085.comment: Radiographically there is normal thickness of enamel and the enamel is slightly more radiolucent than dentin.

HP:0011086.label: Dentinogenesis imperfecta of primary and permanent teeth
HP:0011086.definition: Developmental dysplasia of dentin or both the primary dentition and the permanent dentition.
exact_synonyms: Dentinogenesis imperfecta of both sets of teeth
Dentinogenesis imperfecta of adult and baby teeth

HP:0011087.label: Talon cusp
HP:0011087.definition: Talon cusp is an accessory cusp located near the cingulum (the portion of the lingual or palatal aspect of the tooth that forms a convex protuberance at the cervical third of the anatomic crown).

HP:0011088.label: Dens in dente
HP:0011088.definition: An abnormality of the incisor characterized by invagination of the enamel, giving a radiographic appearance that suggests a tooth within a tooth.
HP:0011088.comment: Dens in dente is Latin for tooth inside of tooth. Dens in dente results from an invagination of the enamel organ into the dental papilla, extending into the root before initiation of mineralization. The permanent maxillary lateral incisors are the most frequently involved teeth, but it can occur in any tooth type. It occurs more frequently in the permanent dentition and in maxillary teeth. The diagnosis dens in dente needs to be confirmed by X-rays.

HP:0011089.label: Double tooth
HP:0011089.comment: The fusion can be complete or be limited to the crown or the root. Typically, incisors and canines form double teeth. Double teeth are more common in the deciduous dentition and rare in the permanent dentition. Double teeth encompasses fusion, concrescence, and gemination of teeth, which some authors describe with the twinning.

HP:0011090.label: Fused teeth
HP:0011090.definition: The union of two separately developing tooth germs typically leading to one less tooth than normal in the affected dental arch.

HP:0011091.label: Gemination
HP:0011091.definition: The development of two teeth from a single tooth bud, leading to a larger fused tooth.
HP:0011091.comment: If the fused tooth is counted singly, then the total number of teeth is normal with gemination. Usually, there is a larger dental crown with a single root and single canal.

HP:0011092.label: Mulberry molar
HP:0011092.definition: Mulberry molars are irregular teeth generally affecting the first molars and are characterized by a grossly deformed crown imitating, as the name implies, the surface of a mulberry.

HP:0011093.label: Molarization of premolar
HP:0011093.definition: Increased size and molar morphology of premolar tooth.

HP:0011094.label: Increased overbite
HP:0011094.definition: Maxillary teeth cover the mandibular teeth when biting to an increased degree. The feature is defined as a vertical overlap of the maxillary incisors over the mandibular incisors that exceeds 2 mm.
exact_synonyms: Increased overlap of upper and lower incisors

HP:0011095.label: Overjet
HP:0011095.definition: An abnormal anteroposterior extension of the maxillary teeth beyond the plane of the mandibular teeth upon jaw closure.
exact_synonyms: Protrusion of upper teeth in front of lower teeth

HP:0011096.label: Peripheral demyelination
HP:0011096.definition: A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.
HP:0011096.comment: This feature is generally diagnosed on the basis of a sural nerve biopsy. Demyelination is associated with slowed nerve conduction, increased refractoriness, and conduction block.

HP:0011097.label: Epileptic spasm
HP:0011097.definition: A sudden flexion, extension, or mixed extension-flexion of predominantly proximal and truncal muscles that is usually more sustained than a myoclonic movement but not as sustained as a tonic seizure. Limited forms may occur: Grimacing, head nodding, or subtle eye movements. Epileptic spasms frequently occur in clusters. Infantile spasms are the best known form, but spasms can occur at all ages
HP:0011097.comment: The maximum age of onset is between 3 and 12 months, the peak being at 6 months. However, spasms may start from birth, or appear long after the age of 12 months, including into adulthood. Infantile spasms represent a specific type of seizure seen in an epilepsy syndrome of infancy and childhood known as West Syndrome. West Syndrome is characterized by infantile spasms, developmental regression, and hypsarrhythmia (as demonstrated by electroencephalography).

HP:0011098.label: Speech apraxia
HP:0011098.definition: A type of apraxia that is characterized by difficulty or inability to execute speech movements because of problems with coordination and motor problems, leading to incorrect articulation. An increase of errors with increasing word and phrase length may occur.
HP:0011098.comment: Speech apraxia may co-occur with oral apraxia and limb apraxia.

HP:0011099.label: Spastic hemiparesis
HP:0011099.definition: Unilateral paresis (weakness) with spasticity of the affected muscles and increased tendon reflexes.

HP:0011100.label: Intestinal atresia
HP:0011100.definition: An abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the intestine.
HP:0011100.comment: Intestinal atresia is a broad term used to describe a complete blockage or obstruction anywhere in the intestine, in contrast to stenosis, which refers to a partial obstruction that results in a narrowing of the intestinal lumen.

HP:0011102.label: Ileal atresia
HP:0011102.definition: An abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the ileum.

HP:0011103.label: Abnormal left ventricular outflow tract morphology
HP:0011103.definition: An abnormality of the outflow tract of the left ventricle.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the left ventricular outflow tract

HP:0011104.label: Abnormality of blood volume homeostasis
HP:0011104.definition: An abnormality in the amount of volume occupied by intravascular blood.

HP:0011105.label: Hypervolemia
HP:0011105.definition: An increase in the amount of intravascular fluid, particularly in the volume of the circulating blood.

HP:0011106.label: Hypovolemia
HP:0011106.definition: An decrease in the amount of intravascular fluid, particularly in the volume of the circulating blood.

HP:0011107.label: Recurrent aphthous stomatitis
HP:0011107.definition: Recurrent episodes of ulceration of the oral mucosa, typically presenting as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a hyperemic border.
HP:0011107.comment: Recurrent aphthous stomatitis can be classified into three forms, with minor ulcers (over 80% of RAS cases) being less than 1 cm in diameter and self-limiting; major ulcers being over 1 cm in diameter with potential scar formation; and herpetiform ulcers manifesting as recurrent episodes with multiple small ulcers throughout the oral mucosa.

HP:0011108.label: Recurrent sinusitis
HP:0011108.comment: Recurring inflammation of the paranasal sinuses.

HP:0011110.label: Recurrent tonsillitis
HP:0011110.definition: Inflammation of the tonsils that has occurred repeatedly. The definition of recurrent may vary somewhat, but the criteria used recently as a measure of severity were five or more episodes of true tonsillitis per year, symptoms recurring for at least a year, and episodes that are disabling and that prevent normal functioning. In some cases recurrent tonsillitis may be related to immunosusceptibility. Evidence exists for a genetic predisposition for recurrent tonsillitis.

HP:0011111.label: Abnormal immune serum protein physiology
HP:0011111.definition: An abnormality of the concentration or function of circulating immune proteins.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of immune serum protein physiology

HP:0011112.label: Abnormal circulating cytokine concentration
HP:0011112.definition: Abnormality of the cytokine levels in the blood, i.e., an abnormality of any of the non-antibody proteins made by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells that affect the behavior of other cells.

HP:0011113.label: Abnormality of cytokine secretion
HP:0011113.definition: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of a cytokine (i.e., any of the non-antibody proteins made by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells that affect the behavior of other cells).

HP:0011114.label: Defective production of NFKB1-dependent cytokines
HP:0011114.definition: An impairment in the production by leukocytes of NFKB1-dependent cytokines such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interferon-alpha.

HP:0011115.label: Abnormal circulating chemokine concentration
HP:0011115.definition: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of a chemokine (a class of cytokines).

HP:0011116.label: Abnormal circulating interferon concentration
HP:0011116.definition: The concentration of an interferon is outside the limits of normal.

HP:0011117.label: Abnormal circulating interleukin concentration
HP:0011117.definition: The concentration of an interleukin (a class of cytokines) is outside the limits of normal.

HP:0011118.label: Abnormality of tumor necrosis factor secretion
HP:0011118.definition: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of tumor necrosis factor.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of tumour necrosis factor secretion

HP:0011119.label: Abnormal nasal dorsum morphology
HP:0011119.definition: An abnormality of the nasal dorsum, also known as the nasal ridge.
HP:0011119.comment: The nasal ridge is the midline prominence of the nose, extending from the nasal root to the tip.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the dorsum of nose

HP:0011120.label: Concave nasal ridge
HP:0011120.definition: Nasal ridge curving posteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip.
HP:0011120.comment: A saddle-nose deformity can be congenital or acquired (e.g., traumatic) and is associated with structural compromise of the nasoseptal cartilage leading to decreased dorsal nasal structural support. A depression of the dorsum of the nose with loss of nasal tip support and definition, shortened (vertical) nasal length, overrotation of the nasal tip, and retrusion of the nasal spine and caudal septum.

HP:0011121.label: Abnormal skin morphology
HP:0011121.definition: Any morphological abnormality of the skin.

HP:0011122.label: Abnormality of skin physiology
HP:0011122.definition: Any abnormality of the physiological function of the skin.

HP:0011123.label: Inflammatory abnormality of the skin
HP:0011123.definition: The presence of inflammation of the skin. That is, an abnormality of the skin resulting from the local accumulation of fluid, plasma proteins, and leukocytes.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal tendency to infections of the skin

HP:0011124.label: Abnormal epidermal morphology
HP:0011124.definition: An abnormality of the morphology of the epidermis.

HP:0011125.label: Abnormality of dermal melanosomes
HP:0011125.definition: An abnormality of the melanosomes, i.e., of the cellular organelles in which melanin pigments are synthesized and stored within melanocytes (the cells that produce pigment in the dermis).

HP:0011126.label: Nephroptosis
HP:0011126.definition: A significant descent of the kidney as the patient moves from the supine to the erect position.
HP:0011126.comment: Nephroptosis is diagnosed if the descent of the kidney is greater than 5 cm or two vertebral bodies on intravenous urogram. The kidney is capable of moving back to the normal position, which differentiates it from an ectopic kidney, which constantly remains in an abnormal position. Nephroptosis may be asymptomatic or may cause symptoms including pain and intermittent ureteric obstruction with hydronephrosis, and ischemia due to elongation, narrowing, or kinking of a renal artery.

HP:0011127.label: Perioral eczema
HP:0011127.definition: A type of eczema that occurs in the lips and perioral area.

HP:0011128.label: Acute esophageal necrosis
HP:0011128.definition: A condition characterized by necrosis of the mucosal and submucosal layers of the esophagus not related to ingestion of caustic or other injurious agents. Endoscopically, there is a dark lesion ('black esophagus') distributed in a circumferential manner in the distal one-third of the esophagus with or without exudates. There is involvement of the distal esophagus ending sharply at the gastroesophageal junction.

HP:0011129.label: Bilateral fetal pyelectasis
HP:0011129.definition: A bilateral form of fetal pyelectasis.

HP:0011130.label: Abnormal renal calyx morphology
HP:0011130.definition: Any abnormality of the morphology of the major calices or minor calices of the kidney.

HP:0011131.label: Perianal dermatitis
HP:0011131.definition: The presence of a rash (change of color and texture) of the perianal skin.

HP:0011132.label: Chronic furunculosis
HP:0011132.definition: A furuncle (boil) is a skin infection involving an entire hair follicle and nearby skin tissue. Chronic furunculosis refers to recurrent episodes of furuncles, often caused by recurrent staphylococcus infection.
HP:0011132.comment: Note that a confluence of several furuncles results in a carbuncle.

HP:0011133.label: Increased sensitivity to ionizing radiation
HP:0011133.definition: An abnormally increased sensitivity to the effects of ionizing radiation.
HP:0011133.comment: Ionizing radiation can lead to the production of free radicals, break chemical bonds, and damage DNA; RNA, and proteins. Cellular damage related to low doses such as that received from normal background radiation is rapidly repaired under normal conditions.

HP:0011134.label: Low-grade fever
HP:0011134.definition: Mild fever that does not exceed 38.5 degrees centigrade.

HP:0011135.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the sweat glands
HP:0011135.definition: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the sweat glands.

HP:0011137.label: Non-pruritic urticaria
HP:0011137.definition: Pale reddish slightly elevated papules and plaques of 0.5-3 cm in diameter and not accompanied by pruritus.
HP:0011137.comment: Although the English-language names for uritcaria and non-pruritic urticaria are very similar these are treated as distinct lesions. Non-pruritic urticaria should not be considered to be a subclass of urticaria, because the latter is characterized by pruritus.

HP:0011138.label: Abnormal skin adnexa morphology
HP:0011138.definition: An abnormality of the skin adnexa (skin appendages), which are specialized skin structures located within the dermis and focally within the subcutaneous fatty tissue, comprising three histologically distinct structures: (1) the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle and sebaceous glands); (2) the eccrine sweat glands; and (3) the apocrine glands.

HP:0011139.label: Gastric duplication
HP:0011139.definition: Gastric duplication is a usually cystic malformation of gastrointestinal tract, usually attached to the greater curvature of the stomach and has no communication with the stomach.
HP:0011139.comment: Gastric duplication usually presents as gastric outlet obstruction. They are usually spherical in form, do not communicate with the stomach, and are generally localized at the greater curvature. In some cases they may exhibit adhesion to the pancreas and even communicate with aberrant pancreatic ducts. Gastric duplication is more frequent in females. It is generally either diagnosed in infancy because of symptoms of gastric outlet obstruction or is an incidental finding in adulthood.

HP:0011140.label: Gastrointestinal duplication
HP:0011140.definition: A spherical hollow structure with a smooth muscle coat, lined by a mucous membrane, and attached to any part of the gastrointestinal tract, from the base of the tongue to the anus.

HP:0011141.label: Age-related cataract
HP:0011141.definition: A type of cataract (opacification of the lens) that forms during the course of aging.
HP:0011141.comment: The lens is formed from ectodermal tissue and contains epithelial cells that give rise to lens fibers throughout life, so with increasing age the lens becomes more compact and thicker.
exact_synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye with age

HP:0011142.label: Age-related nuclear cataract
HP:0011142.definition: A type of age-related cataract that primarily affects the nucleus of the lens.
HP:0011142.comment: As the lens ages, new layers of fibers are added and the lens nucleus is compressed and becomes harder (nuclear sclerosis cataract), with associated yellowing of the lens. Nuclear sclerosis typically progresses slowly.

HP:0011143.label: Age-related cortical cataract
HP:0011143.definition: A type of age-related cataract that primarily affects the cortex of the lens.
HP:0011143.comment: The cortex of the lens is made of the newest lens fibers. With aging, discrete opacities can develop within the cortex of the lens that typically cause no visual symptoms unless they involve the visual axis or the entire cortex, in which case the lens becomes white and is said to be mature.

HP:0011144.label: Age-related posterior subcapsular cataract
HP:0011144.definition: A type of age-related cataract consisting of granular opacities occurring mainly in the central posterior cortex just under the posterior capsule.

HP:0011145.label: Symptomatic seizures
HP:0011145.definition: A seizure that occurs in the context of a brain insult (systemic, toxic, or metabolic) and may not recur when the underlying cause has been removed or the acute phase has elapsed.
HP:0011145.comment: While all patients with epilepsy experience seizures, not all individuals with seizures have epilepsy. One or more epileptic seizures may occur in the context of a brain insult (systemic, toxic, or metabolic). These events (defined acute symptomatic seizures, provoked seizures, or situation-related seizures) are presumed to be an acute manifestation of the insult and may not recur when the underlying cause has been removed or the acute phase has elapsed.

HP:0011146.label: Dialeptic seizure
HP:0011146.definition: A dialeptic seizure is a type of seizure characterized predominantly by reduced responsiveness or awareness and with subsequent at least partial amnesia of the event.
HP:0011146.comment: The main ictal manifestation of dialeptic seizures is an alteration of consciousness rather than motor or sensory features. The term describes the pure clinical semiology of a seizure and is used independently of the ictal electrographic findings: it could describe a seizure of focal, generalized or unknown onset. In 2017 the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology recommended classifying a seizure as having focal or generalized onset only when there is a high degree of confidence (>80%, arbitrarily chosen to parallel the usual allowable beta error) in the accuracy of this determination.
exact_synonyms: Behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
Behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
Unknown onset behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness
Unknown onset behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness

HP:0011147.label: Typical absence seizure
HP:0011147.definition: A typical absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by its sudden onset, interruption of ongoing activities, a blank stare, possibly a brief upward deviation of the eyes. Usually the patient will be unresponsive when spoken to. Duration is a few seconds to half a minute with very rapid recovery. Although not always available, an EEG would usually show 3 Hz generalized epileptiform discharges during the event.
HP:0011147.comment: In 2017 the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology recommended classifying a seizure as having focal or generalized onset only when there is a high degree of confidence (>80%, arbitrarily chosen to parallel the usual allowable beta error) in the accuracy of this determination; see Dialeptic seizure. Typical absences have 2 essential components: (1) clinically the impairment of consciousness (absence), and (2) EEG generalized 3 Hz to 4 Hz (less than 2.5 Hz) spike and slow wave discharges.

HP:0011148.label: obsolete Absence seizures with special features

HP:0011149.label: Absence seizure with eyelid myoclonia
HP:0011149.definition: An absence with eyelid myoclonia seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by forced upward jerking of the eyelids during an absence seizure.
