HP:0011149.comment: This type of seizure was classified as a type of generalized non-motor seizure by the ILAE in 2017 because the absence predominates over the eyelid myoclonia. However, eyelid myoclonia can occur as a generalized-onset seizure without any absence, in which they may be better considered a motor seizure: see Eyelid myoclonia seizure.

HP:0011150.label: Myoclonic absence seizure
HP:0011150.definition: Myoclonic absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by an interruption of ongoing activities, a blank stare and rhythmic three-per-second myoclonic movements, causing ratcheting abduction of the upper limbs leading to progressive arm elevation, and associated with 3 Hz generalized spike-wave discharges on the electroencephalogram. Duration is typically 10-60 s. Whilst impairment of consciousness may not be obvious the ILAE classified this seizure as a generalized non-motor seizure in 2017.

HP:0011151.label: Atypical absence status epilepticus
HP:0011151.definition: Atypical absence status epilepticus is a type of generalized non-convulsive status epilepticus without coma that is semiologically a prolonged atypical absence seizure.
HP:0011151.comment: In comparison to a typical absence seizure, changes in tone may be more pronounced, onset and/or cessation may be less abrupt, and the duration of the ictus and post-ictal recovery may be longer. Although not always available, an EEG often demonstrates slow (<3 Hz), irregular, generalized spike-wave activity. This form of seizure may be observed in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.

HP:0011152.label: Early onset absence seizures
HP:0011152.definition: Typical absence seizures starting before the age of 4 years.

HP:0011153.label: Focal motor seizure
HP:0011153.definition: A type of focal-onset seizure characterized by a motor sign as its initial semiological manifestation.
HP:0011153.comment: A motor onset seizure involves motor activity (movement) and may be due to either an increase or decrease in contraction in a muscle or group of muscles. Depending on the muscle groups involved and the way they are affected, the movement features of a motor onset seizure may be simple or more complex.

HP:0011154.label: Focal autonomic seizure
HP:0011154.definition: An autonomic seizure is a type of focal non-motor seizure characterized by alteration of autonomic nervous system function as the initial semiological feature.
HP:0011154.comment: Focal seizures with a subjective or objectively documented alteration of autonomic nervous system function at onset, involving but not limited to, cardiovascular, pupillary, gastrointestinal, sudomotor, vasomotor and thermoregulatory functions. Focal autonomic seizure is not a child of Epileptic aura (HP:0033348) as many Focal autonomic seizures are not purely subjective (required to be called an aura).

HP:0011155.label: obsolete Focal autonomic seizures with altered responsiveness

HP:0011156.label: obsolete Focal autonomic seizures without altered responsiveness

HP:0011157.label: Focal sensory seizure
HP:0011157.definition: A focal sensory seizure is a type seizure beginning with a subjective sensation.
HP:0011157.comment: A focal sensory seizure involves a sensation being experienced at seizure onset, without objective clinical signs of a seizure evident to the observer.

HP:0011158.label: Focal sensory seizure with auditory features
HP:0011158.definition: A seizure characterized by elementary auditory phenomena including buzzing, ringing, drumming or single tones as its first clinical manifestation.
HP:0011158.comment: More complex auditory hallucinations such as voices are considered a focal cognitive seizure. Focal sensory auditory seizures involve auditory cortex in the lateral superior temporal lobe.

HP:0011159.label: Focal autonomic seizure with epigastric sensation/nausea/vomiting/other gastrointestinal phenomena
HP:0011159.definition: A type of focal autonomic seizure characterized by symptoms or signs pertaining to the gastrointestinal system as the initial semiological feature.
HP:0011159.comment: This includes epigastric sensations (which may rise up to the chest or throat) such as upper abdominal discomfort, emptiness, tightness, churning, or hunger, as well as ictal nausea and ictal vomiting.

HP:0011160.label: Focal sensory seizure with gustatory features
HP:0011160.definition: A seizure characterized by taste phenomena including acidic, bitter, salty, sweet, or metallic tastes as its first clinical manifestation.
HP:0011160.comment: These seizures involve the parietal operculum and the insula.

HP:0011161.label: Focal sensory seizure with olfactory features
HP:0011161.definition: Seizures characterized by olfactory phenomena as its first clinical manifestation.
HP:0011161.comment: These seizures involve the mesial temporal or orbitofrontal regions.

HP:0011163.label: Focal sensory seizure with somatosensory features
HP:0011163.definition: A seizure characterized by sensory phenomena including tingling, numbness, electric-shock like sensation, pain, sense of movement, or desire to move as its first clinical manifestation.
HP:0011163.comment: These seizures involve the sensorimotor cortex.

HP:0011165.label: Focal sensory seizure with visual features
HP:0011165.definition: A seizure characterized by elementary visual hallucinations such as flashing or flickering lights/colors, or other shapes, simple patterns, scotomata, or amaurosis as its first clinical manifestation.
HP:0011165.comment: More complex visual hallucinations such as seeing formed images are considered a focal cognitive seizure. Focal sensory visual seizures arise in the occipital lobe. Note that there is a distinction between Visual aura and Simple partial occipital seizures. See HPO term HP:0025121 for comments.

HP:0011166.label: Focal myoclonic seizure
HP:0011166.definition: A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction(s) of muscles(s) or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.

HP:0011167.label: Focal tonic seizure
HP:0011167.definition: A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained increase in muscle contraction, lasting a few seconds to minutes.
HP:0011167.comment: The abnormal movements of dystonia resulting from co-contraction of agonist and antagonist muscles differentiates these from tonic seizures, see focal dystonic seizure.

HP:0011168.label: Focal seizure with eyelid myoclonia
HP:0011168.definition: Focal seizure with eyelid myoclonia, not eyelid myoclonias in the context of absence seizures.

HP:0011169.label: Generalized clonic seizure
HP:0011169.definition: Generalized clonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by sustained bilateral jerking, either symmetric or asymmetric, that is regularly repetitive and involves the same muscle groups.
HP:0011169.comment: Generalized clonic seizures are much less common than are tonic-clonic seizures, usually occur in infants, and should be distinguished from jitteriness or shuddering attacks.

HP:0011170.label: Generalized myoclonic-atonic seizure
HP:0011170.definition: A generalized myoclonic-atonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by a myoclonic jerk followed by an atonic motor component.
HP:0011170.comment: A myoclonic-tonic seizure was previously called a myoclonic-astatic seizure. ILAE2017 does not currently consider myoclonic-atonic seizures to be a form of myoclonic seizure which is why it is classified as a motor seizure.

HP:0011171.label: Simple febrile seizure
HP:0011171.definition: A short generalized seizure, of a duration of <15 min, not recurring within 24 h, occurring during a febrile episode not caused by an acute disease of the nervous system intracranial infection or severe metabolic disturbance.
HP:0011171.comment: Fever may not be detected before the seizure, but it must be present at least in the immediate postacute period. In most cases these seizures are of a generalized tonic-clonic semiology.

HP:0011172.label: Complex febrile seizure
HP:0011172.definition: A febrile seizure that has any of the following features: focal semiology (or associated with post-ictal neurologic abnormalities beyond drowsiness, such as a Todd's paresis), prolonged seizure beyond 15 minutes, or recurring (occurring more than once) in a 24 hour period.
HP:0011172.comment: Children presenting with a prolonged seizure stopped with anticonvulsive therapy (i.e., diazepam) before the 15th minute should be classified within this group.

HP:0011173.label: Focal behavior arrest seizure
HP:0011173.definition: A type of focal non-motor seizure characterized by an arrest or pause of activities, freezing, or immobilization as the predominant semiological feature throughout the seizure.
HP:0011173.comment: The word 'focal' is explicit in the term title to emphasize the difference between these seizures and absence (generalized non-motor) seizures. Because brief behavior arrest is common and difficult to identify at the start of many seizures, the arrest must be persistent and dominant through the entire seizure. If the patient is able to identify that fear is the primary onset feature of the seizure, and results in immobility, the seizure is a focal emotional seizure with fear, and the immobility is then considered a descriptive feature, due to the fear. If the focal seizure is not characterized by this feature at the very outset of the seizure, it is not used to classify the seizure, it is instead used as a seizure descriptor, after the seizure is classified according to its onset feature.

HP:0011174.label: Focal hyperkinetic seizure
HP:0011174.definition: A focal seizure characterized at onset by predominantly proximal limb or axial muscles producing irregular sequential ballistic movements, such as pedaling, pelvic thrusting, thrashing, rocking movements.
HP:0011174.comment: The 2017 ILAE classification arbitrarily groups pedaling activity with hyperkinetic seizures, rather than with automatism seizures. However, some automatisms overlap other motor behaviors and where pedaling is slow and coordinated it may be considered an automatism.

HP:0011175.label: Focal motor seizure with version
HP:0011175.definition: A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained, forced conjugate ocular, cephalic, and/or truncal rotation or lateral deviation from the midline as the initial semiological manifestation.

HP:0011176.label: EEG with constitutional variants
HP:0011176.definition: An EEG with constitutional variants contains waves that are rare or unusual but not generally pathologic.

HP:0011177.label: EEG with 4-5/second background activity
HP:0011177.comment: EEG background activity at 4-5/second is rare and unusual but not generally pathologic.

HP:0011178.label: Alpha-EEG
HP:0011178.comment: Alpha-EEG is a rare finding but not generally pathologic.

HP:0011179.label: Beta-EEG
HP:0011179.definition: EEG dominated by diffuse beta-waves (>13 Hz).
HP:0011179.comment: Beta-EEG is a rare finding but not generally pathologic.

HP:0011180.label: Partial beta-EEG
HP:0011180.definition: EEG dominated by diffuse beta waves (>13 Hz) with occipitally localized alpha waves (8-13 Hz).
HP:0011180.comment: A partial beta-EEG is a rare finding but not generally pathologic.

HP:0011181.label: Low voltage EEG
HP:0011181.definition: EEG with an amplitude less than 30 microvolts without observable occipital alpha rhythm (8-13 Hz).
HP:0011181.comment: A low voltage EEG is a rare finding but not generally pathologic.

HP:0011182.label: Interictal epileptiform activity
HP:0011182.definition: Epileptiform activity refers to distinctive EEG waves or complexes distinguished from background activity found in in a proportion of human subjects with epilepsy, but which can also be found in subjects without seizures. Interictal epileptiform activity refers to such activity that occurs in the absence of a clinical or subclinical seizure.
HP:0011182.comment: Epileptiform EEG discharges include small sharp spikes (SSSs), wicket spikes, 14- and 6-Hz positive spikes, phantom spike and waves, psychomotor variant, subclinical rhythmic EEG discharges of adults (SREDA), and midline theta rhythm.

HP:0011183.label: EEG with hyperventilation-induced focal epileptiform discharges
HP:0011183.definition: Focal epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

HP:0011184.label: EEG with hyperventilation-induced generalized epileptiform discharges
HP:0011184.definition: Generalized epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
exact_synonyms: EEG with hyperventilation-induced generalised epileptiform discharges

HP:0011185.label: EEG with focal epileptiform discharges
HP:0011185.definition: EEG discharges recorded in particular areas of a localized (focal) abnormality in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
HP:0011185.comment: Note that a focal EEG abnormality is not synonymous with "focal epileptiform discharges" because a focal EEG abnormality is not necessarily epileptiform (e.g., it could be a focal slowing).

HP:0011186.label: Focal epileptiform discharges with limited propagation to contralateral hemisphere
HP:0011186.definition: Focal epileptiform discharges with spreading to contralateral hemisphere but without secondary generalization.

HP:0011187.label: Focal EEG discharges with propagation to ipsilateral hemisphere
HP:0011187.definition: Focal epileptiform discharges with spreading to the hemisphere on the same side of the brain.

HP:0011188.label: Focal EEG discharges with secondary generalization
HP:0011188.definition: Focal EEG discharges that secondarily spread to both hemispheres and can then be recorded over the entire scalp.
exact_synonyms: Focal EEG discharges with secondary generalisation

HP:0011189.label: Bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
HP:0011189.definition: Epileptiform discharges being identified at multiple locations in both hemispheres.

HP:0011190.label: Uni- and bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
HP:0011190.definition: Epileptiform discharges identified at multiple locations temporarily in both hemispheres and temporarily in one hemisphere.

HP:0011191.label: Unilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
HP:0011191.definition: Epileptiform discharges being identified at multiple locations in one hemisphere.

HP:0011192.label: Polymorphic focal epileptiform discharges
HP:0011192.definition: Focal epileptiform discharges of different shapes and frequencies.

HP:0011193.label: EEG with focal spikes
HP:0011193.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec.

HP:0011194.label: EEG with series of focal spikes
HP:0011194.definition: Focal spikes occurring for several seconds.

HP:0011195.label: EEG with focal sharp slow waves
HP:0011195.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011196.label: EEG with focal sharp waves
HP:0011196.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

HP:0011197.label: EEG with focal spike waves
HP:0011197.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011198.label: EEG with generalized epileptiform discharges
HP:0011198.definition: EEG discharges recorded on the entire scalp typically seen in persons with epilepsy.
HP:0011198.comment: Spikes (<70 ms) and sharp waves (70-200 ms) are sharp transient waves that have a strong association with epilepsy. No difference is noted in terms of clinical significance of spikes and sharp waves. Significant spikes usually are followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011199.label: EEG with generalized sharp slow waves
HP:0011199.definition: EEG with generalized sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised sharp slow waves

HP:0011200.label: EEG with generalized polymorphic epileptiform discharges
HP:0011200.definition: Generalized epileptiform discharges of different shapes and frequencies.
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised polymorphic epileptiform discharges

HP:0011204.label: EEG with continuous slow activity
HP:0011204.definition: EEG showing diffuse slowing without interruption.

HP:0011205.label: EEG with intermittent slow activity
HP:0011205.definition: Non-continuous diffuse slowing of electroencephalographic patterns.

HP:0011206.label: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 1
HP:0011206.definition: Slowing at frequencies between 7.5 and 8.5 Hz.
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 1

HP:0011207.label: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 2
HP:0011207.definition: Generalized slowing of EEG activity at frequencies between 4-7 Hz.
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 2

HP:0011208.label: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 3
HP:0011208.definition: Generalized slowing of EEG activity at frequencies between 0.5-3 Hz.
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 3

HP:0011209.label: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 4
exact_synonyms: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 4

HP:0011210.label: EEG with occipital slowing
HP:0011210.definition: Slowing in occipital areas of the scalp EEG.

HP:0011211.label: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade I
HP:0011211.definition: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital regions during photic stimulation.

HP:0011212.label: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade II
HP:0011212.definition: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital and central regions during photic stimulation.

HP:0011213.label: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade III
HP:0011213.definition: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital, central, temporal and parietal regions during photic stimulation.

HP:0011214.label: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade IV
HP:0011214.definition: Occurrence of generalized epileptiform discharges during photic stimulation.

HP:0011217.label: Abnormal shape of the occiput
exact_synonyms: Abnormal shape of the back of the skull

HP:0011218.label: Abnormal shape of the frontal region
HP:0011218.definition: An abnormal shape of the frontal part of the head.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal morphology of the frontal region

HP:0011219.label: Short face
HP:0011219.definition: Facial height (length) is more than two standard deviations below the mean (objective); or an apparent decrease in the height (length) of the face (subjective).
HP:0011219.comment: Objective measurement of face height is made with sliding calipers from the nasion, just above the depth of the nasal root to the gnathion, the inferior border of the mandible, both in the midline. Note that short face is distinct from wide face.

HP:0011220.label: Prominent forehead
HP:0011220.definition: Forward prominence of the entire forehead, due to protrusion of the frontal bone.
HP:0011220.comment: Not to be confused with frontal bossing.

HP:0011221.label: Vertical forehead creases
HP:0011221.definition: Vertical soft tissue creases in the midline of the forehead, often extending from the hairline to the brow, and seen with facial expression or when the face is at rest.

HP:0011222.label: Depressed glabella
HP:0011222.definition: Posterior positioning of the glabella, i.e., of the midline forehead between the supraorbital ridges.
HP:0011222.comment: The glabella is the area of the forehead in the midline between the supraorbital ridges, just above the nasal root.

HP:0011223.label: Metopic depression
HP:0011223.definition: Linear vertical groove in the midline of the forehead, extending from hairline to glabella.

HP:0011224.label: Ablepharon
HP:0011224.comment: In ablepharon, the globe is continuously exposed. It is arguable whether true aplasia of the eyelid exists, or whether this represents severe hypoplasia. Nevertheless, as it is difficult or impossible to make this distinction on clinical grounds, the term was felt to be useful.

HP:0011225.label: Epiblepharon
HP:0011225.definition: Redundant eyelid skin pressing the eyelashes against the cornea and/or conjunctiva.
HP:0011225.comment: Epiblepharon should be distinguished from entropion.

HP:0011226.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the eyelid
HP:0011226.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the eyelid.

HP:0011227.label: Elevated circulating C-reactive protein concentration
HP:0011227.definition: An abnormal elevation of the C-reactive protein level in the blood circulation.
HP:0011227.comment: C-reactive protein (CRP) is produced by the liver, and increases in concentration in response to inflammation.

HP:0011228.label: Horizontal eyebrow
HP:0011228.definition: An eyebrow that extends straight across the brow, without curve.

HP:0011229.label: Broad eyebrow
HP:0011229.definition: Regional increase in the width (height) of the eyebrow.
HP:0011229.comment: Broadening or flaring can be medial or lateral. Flaring is used to describe a widening with a change in direction of the eyebrow hairs.

HP:0011230.label: Laterally extended eyebrow
HP:0011230.definition: An eyebrow that extends laterally beyond the orbital rim rather than turning gently downward at that location.
HP:0011230.comment: The degree of extension beyond the obital rim that is considered abnormal has not been established.

HP:0011231.label: Prominent eyelashes
HP:0011231.definition: Eyelashes that draw the attention of the viewer due to increased density and/or length and/or curl without meeting the criteria of trichomegaly.

HP:0011232.label: Infra-orbital fold
HP:0011232.definition: Elevated ridge(s) of skin starting well below the medial aspect of the lower lid that curves gradually upward toward and/or across the nasal bridge.

HP:0011233.label: Antihelical shelf
HP:0011233.definition: Antihelix protrusion directed more anteriorly than laterally, forming a shelf overlying the posterior concha.
HP:0011233.comment: In marked cases this often appears to be associated with lack of lateral protrusion of the antihelix.

HP:0011234.label: Absent antihelix
HP:0011234.definition: No discernible ridge between concha and triangular fossa and helix.
HP:0011234.comment: This finding is common in a protruding and cupped ear, where the superior and inferior parts of the antihelix are often absent. This is distinct from partial absence of the antihelix as may occur in, for example, underdeveloped inferior crus of the antihelix.

HP:0011235.label: Additional crus of antihelix
HP:0011235.definition: Supernumerary ridge or crus of the ear arising from the antihelix.
HP:0011235.comment: The supernumerary crus usually emanates posteriorly from the antihelix at, or just above, the point of its bifurcation but may have a different origin. In the former case, the finding is termed Stahl ear.

HP:0011236.label: Angulated antihelix
HP:0011236.definition: Antihelical ridge that forms an acute angle between the antitragus and its bifurcation (stem) instead of a gently curving arc.

HP:0011237.label: Broad inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011237.definition: Increased width of the inferred cross-section of the inferior crus.
HP:0011237.comment: This finding is highly variable. The inferior crus is usually sharply folded giving a narrow profile.

HP:0011238.label: Prominent inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011238.definition: Increased protrusion of the inferior crus relative to the prominence of the antihelix stem.

HP:0011239.label: Underdeveloped inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011239.definition: Decreased protrusion of the inferior crus relative to the prominence of the antihelix stem.

HP:0011240.label: Prominent stem of antihelix
HP:0011240.definition: Increased protrusion of the antihelical ridge, proximal to its bifurcation, relative to the prominence of the helix.
HP:0011240.comment: This finding is highly variable. The relative prominence is attributable to either increased volume of the cartilage and/or the acuteness of the folding angle. Interpretation of relative antihelical prominence may be difficult when the conchal anatomy is distorted, for example, with a cupped ear.

HP:0011241.label: Serpiginous stem of antihelix
HP:0011241.definition: Posterior curving of the antihelix from its origin at the antitragus, traveling initially almost perpendicular to the descending helix and obscuring some of the concha.

HP:0011242.label: Underdeveloped stem of antihelix
HP:0011242.definition: Decreased protrusion of the antihelical ridge, proximal to its bifurcation, relative to the prominence of a normal helix.
HP:0011242.comment: The degree of prominence of the stem is highly variable and is attributable to the volume of the cartilage and/or the acuteness of the folding angle. Interpretation of degree of antihelical prominence may be difficult when the conchal anatomy is distorted, e.g., in cupped ear.

HP:0011243.label: Abnormality of inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011243.definition: An abnormality of the inferior crus of the antihelix is the lower cartilaginous ridge arising at the bifurcation of the antihelix that ends beneath the fold of the ascending helix, and separates the concha from the triangular fossa.
HP:0011243.comment: The inferior antihelical crus runs in an anterior and slightly superior direction, and is usually sharply defined, and appears less variable than its superior counterpart. A synonym is anterior crus of the antihelix.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of anterior crus of antihelix

HP:0011244.label: Abnormality of stem of antihelix
HP:0011244.definition: An abnormality of the stem of the antihelix, which is the part below the bifurcation of the antihelix into the inferior and superior crura.

HP:0011245.label: Abnormality of superior crus of antihelix
HP:0011245.definition: An abnormality of the superior crus of the antihelix is the upper cartilaginous ridge arising at the bifurcation of the antihelix that ends beneath the fold of the ascending helix, and separates the concha from the triangular fossa.
HP:0011245.comment: The inferior antihelical crus runs in an anterior and slightly superior direction, and is usually sharply defined, and appears less variable than its superior counterpart. A synonym is anterior crus of the antihelix.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of posterior crus of antihelix

HP:0011246.label: Underdeveloped superior crus of antihelix
HP:0011246.definition: Decreased protrusion of the superior crus relative to the prominence of a normal antihelix stem.
HP:0011246.comment: This finding is highly variable. There may be an inverse relationship between the relative sizes of the superior and inferior crura, but these findings should be coded separately.

HP:0011247.label: Prominent superior crus of antihelix
HP:0011247.definition: Increased protrusion of the superior crus relative to the prominence of a normal antihelix stem.
HP:0011247.comment: This finding is highly variable. There may be an inverse relationship between the relative sizes of the superior and inferior crura, but these findings should be coded separately.

HP:0011248.label: Everted antitragus
HP:0011248.definition: Positioning of the antitragus at an angle perpendicular to the plane of the ear (oriented away from the plane of the ear).

HP:0011249.label: Absent antitragus
HP:0011249.definition: Absence of the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.
HP:0011249.comment: The size of the antitragus is highly variable.

HP:0011250.label: Bifid antitragus
HP:0011250.definition: Double rather than single peak of the antitragus.

HP:0011251.label: Underdeveloped antitragus
HP:0011251.definition: Reduction in the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.

HP:0011252.label: Cryptotia
HP:0011252.definition: Invagination of the superior part of the auricle under a fold of temporal skin.
HP:0011252.comment: There are associated anomalies of the upper antihelix and crura. The upper one-third of the auricle is primarily affected and there is an inferomedial displacement of the Helical Darwin tubercle. Two types are recognized. Type I: the antihelix and superior crus are reduced in size; type II: it is the antihelix and inferior crus that are affected.

HP:0011253.label: Type I cryptotia
HP:0011253.definition: A type of cryptotia associated with reduction in size of the antihelix and superior crus.

HP:0011254.label: Type II cryptotia
HP:0011254.definition: A type of cryptotia associated with reduction in size of the antihelix and inferior crus that are affected.

HP:0011255.label: Absent crus of helix
HP:0011255.definition: Continuum between the tragus and ascending helix, without any evidence of a posterior extension (crus) towards the concha.

HP:0011256.label: Crus of helix connected to antihelix
HP:0011256.definition: Extension of the ridge of the crus helix across the ear and connection of the crus to the antihelix.

HP:0011257.label: Serpiginous crus of helix
HP:0011257.definition: Curving course of the crus of the helix, approaching or joining the antitragus.

HP:0011258.label: Tragal bridge of crus of helix
HP:0011258.definition: The anterior origin of the crus encompasses the superior margin of the tragus, the crus overrides the upper portion of the conchal cavum and ends at the antihelix.

HP:0011259.label: Expanded terminal portion of crus of helix
HP:0011259.definition: Widening, rather than tapering, of the crus at its posterior border near the antihelix.

HP:0011260.label: Darwin notch of helix
HP:0011260.definition: Small defect of the helical fold that lies at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix.

HP:0011261.label: Darwin tubercle of helix
HP:0011261.definition: Small expansion of the helical fold at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix.

HP:0011262.label: Crimped helix
HP:0011262.definition: Linear, circumferential indentation in the convexity of the outer surface of the helix.
HP:0011262.comment: The crimp is usually found in the middle third of the descending helix. The helix has the appearance of having been pinched or flattened along its posterior margin. The crimp may distort the free margin of the helix.

HP:0011263.label: Forward facing earlobe
HP:0011263.definition: Positioning of the anterior surface of the ear lobe in a more coronal plane than the remainder of the ear.
HP:0011263.comment: The lobe should be viewed from the front. This feature is distinct from the situation where the entire ear is forward facing and prominent. The lobe normally lies more or less in the same plane as the remainder of the ear. This feature should be distinguished from Uplifted lobe.

HP:0011264.label: Discontinuous ascending root of helix
HP:0011264.definition: Interruption between the ascending helix and the crus helix, allowing the ascending helix to be attached directly to the mastoid.

HP:0011265.label: Cleft earlobe
HP:0011265.definition: Discontinuity in the convexity of the inferior margin of the lobe.
HP:0011265.comment: The cleft is often more visible if the lobe is pulled forward or when seen from behind. Tears acquired from earrings should be distinguished.

HP:0011266.label: Microtia, first degree
HP:0011266.definition: Presence of all the normal ear components and the median longitudinal length more than two standard deviations below the mean.

HP:0011267.label: Microtia, third degree
HP:0011267.definition: Presence of some auricular structures, but none of these structures conform to recognized ear components.
HP:0011267.comment: This malformation is commonly associated with atresia of the external canal, but that anomaly should be coded separately. Complete absence of the ear should be coded as Anotia.

HP:0011268.label: Absent tragus
HP:0011268.definition: Lack of convexity or prominence of the contour of the ridge between the bottom of the incisura and the confluence of the ascending helix and crus helix.
HP:0011268.comment: This appears to be unusual in an otherwise normal ear, and is most often seen in microtia with atretic auditory meatus, but those findings should be coded separately.

HP:0011269.label: Bifid tragus
HP:0011269.definition: Increased height of the tragal ridge with a shallow indentation at the apex, giving the appearance of a double peak.

HP:0011270.label: Duplicated tragus
HP:0011270.definition: A complete or partial duplication of the tragus; expected to lie anterior to the normal tragus.
HP:0011270.comment: It is unclear how often, or even whether, this feature which would represent a duplication of mandibular components, occurs. More common occurrences in this region would include preauricular tags and pretragial duplications of hyoid origin.

HP:0011271.label: Prominent tragus
HP:0011271.definition: Increase posterolateral protrusion of the tragus.

HP:0011272.label: Underdeveloped tragus
HP:0011272.definition: Decreased posterolateral protrusion of the tragus.

HP:0011273.label: Anisocytosis
HP:0011273.definition: Abnormally increased variability in the size of erythrocytes.
exact_synonyms: Unequal size of red blood cells

HP:0011274.label: Recurrent mycobacterial infections
HP:0011274.definition: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of mycobacterial infection.
HP:0011274.comment: Mycobacteria represent a family of slowly growing bacteria, including M. tuberculosis, the agent of tuberculosis, M. leprae, the agent of leprosy, M. avium complex species, and others. Mycobacteria infection can be asymptomatic or not, and are typically difficult to treat with antibiotics.

HP:0011275.label: Recurrent mycobacterium avium complex infections
HP:0011275.definition: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial avium complex infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of mycobacterial infection.
HP:0011275.comment: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) is a group of species including M. avium, M. avium paratuberculosis, and others. Disseminated MAC infections can be seen associated with HIV infection. Pulmonary disease and cervical adenitis are other sequellae of MAC infection.

HP:0011277.label: Abnormality of the urinary system physiology

HP:0011278.label: Intrapulmonary lobar sequestration
HP:0011278.definition: A type of pulmonary sequestration that occurs within the visceral pleura of normal lung tissue, usually without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.
HP:0011278.comment: Intralobar sequestration (ILS) may be diagnosed on antenatal ultrasound screening. ILS can be asymptomatic in later life or can lead to signs and symptoms related to inadequate tracheobronchial drainage caused by the lesion of adjacent atelectatic lung.

HP:0011279.label: Abnormality of urine bicarbonate level
HP:0011279.definition: An abnormal amount of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.

HP:0011280.label: Abnormality of urine calcium concentration
HP:0011280.definition: An abnormality of calcium concentration in the urine.

HP:0011281.label: Abnormality of urine catecholamine level
HP:0011281.definition: An abnormal amount of urinary catecholamine concentration.
HP:0011281.comment: Any anomaly in the urinary amount of catecholamines, including adrenaline, noradrenaline and L-dopamine.

HP:0011282.label: Abnormal hindbrain morphology
HP:0011282.definition: An abnormality of the hindbrain, also known as the rhombencephalon.
HP:0011282.comment: The hindbrain consists of two main structures: The pons and the cerebellum.

HP:0011283.label: Abnormal metencephalon morphology
HP:0011283.definition: An abnormality of the metencephalon. The metencephalon is the part of the hindbrain that consists of the pons and the cerebellum.

HP:0011284.label: Short-segment aganglionic megacolon
HP:0011284.definition: A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment does not extend beyond the upper sigmoid.

HP:0011285.label: Long-segment aganglionic megacolon
HP:0011285.definition: A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment extends proximal to the sigmoid.

HP:0011286.label: Total colonic aganglionosis
HP:0011286.definition: A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment comprises the entire colon.

HP:0011287.label: EEG with occipital sharp slow waves
HP:0011287.definition: EEG with sharp slow waves in the occipital region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011288.label: EEG with parietal sharp slow waves
HP:0011288.definition: EEG with sharp slow waves in the parietal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011289.label: EEG with temporal sharp slow waves
HP:0011289.definition: EEG with sharp slow waves in the temporal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011290.label: EEG with frontal sharp slow waves
HP:0011290.definition: EEG with sharp slow waves in the frontal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011291.label: EEG with central sharp slow waves
HP:0011291.definition: EEG with sharp slow waves in the central region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0011292.label: EEG with occipital sharp waves
HP:0011292.definition: EEG with sharp waves in the occipital region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

HP:0011293.label: EEG with central sharp waves
HP:0011293.definition: EEG with sharp waves in the central region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

HP:0011294.label: EEG with frontal sharp waves
HP:0011294.definition: EEG with sharp waves in the frontal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

HP:0011295.label: EEG with parietal sharp waves
HP:0011295.definition: EEG with sharp waves in the parietal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

HP:0011296.label: EEG with temporal sharp waves
HP:0011296.definition: EEG with sharp waves in the temporal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

HP:0011297.label: Abnormal digit morphology
HP:0011297.definition: A morphological abnormality of a digit, i.e., of a finger or toe.

HP:0011298.label: Prominent digit pad
HP:0011298.definition: A soft tissue prominence of the ventral aspects of the fingertips or toe tips.
HP:0011298.comment: The prominence of the finger or toe pads varies throughout life, being greater in neonates and dependent on the state of hydration. This term should not be used if the digit has clubbing. Note that the synonym "fetal fingertip pads" should not be interpreted to mean that the prominent pad necessarily was present in this individual since fetal life. We do not endorse the use of the term "Persistent fetal pads" as this term implies knowledge of the natural history of this finding, which may or may not be known.

HP:0011299.label: Partial absence of finger
HP:0011299.definition: The absence of a phalangeal segment of a finger.
HP:0011299.comment: The part that is absent may be specified. The distal modifier specifies the loss of the distal phalanx; clinically this is defined by the absence of the nail. The proximal modifier specifies the loss of the proximal or middle phalanx with the nail still present and/or the radiographic finding of a remaining phalanx that is similar to a distal phalanx. It may be difficult to determine which phalanx is absent without x-rays and even then, there are circumstances where the missing bone may not be exactly identified (note that no attempt is made to distinguish missing middle from proximal phalanges). In this situation the location adjective will have to be removed. This finding is distinct from Short fingers.

HP:0011300.label: Broad fingertip
HP:0011300.definition: Increased width of the distal segment of a finger.
HP:0011300.comment: This term should be reserved for use when the distal digit is significantly broader than the middle part. It should not be used if the digit has Clubbing or Macrodactyly or if the entire finger is broad. The distinction to the term Broad distal phalanx of finger is that this term is a clinical impression while Broad distal phalanx of finger refers to the objectively measured width of the distal phalane (bone), a radiological finding.

HP:0011301.label: Absent foot
HP:0011301.definition: The total absence of the foot, with no bony elements distal to the tibia or fibula.

HP:0011302.label: Long palm
HP:0011302.definition: For children from birth to 16 years of age the length of the palm is more than the 97th centile; or, the length of the palm appears relatively long compared to the finger length or the limb length.

HP:0011303.label: Convex contour of sole
HP:0011303.definition: The contour of the foot in lateral profile has a convex shape.
HP:0011303.comment: This term was established as the convex contour may occur without the prominent heel, which together comprise the bundled term Rocker-bottom foot.

HP:0011304.label: Broad thumb
HP:0011304.definition: Increased thumb width without increased dorso-ventral dimension.
HP:0011304.comment: Note that this term should not be used for thumbs that meet the definition for Macrodactyly.

HP:0011305.label: Partial absence of toe
HP:0011305.definition: The absence of a phalangeal segment of a toe or hallux.
HP:0011305.comment: The part that is absent may be specified. The "distal" modifier specifies the loss of the distal phalanx; clinically this is defined by the absence of the nail. The "proximal" modifier specifies the loss of the proximal or middle phalanx with the nail still present. It may be difficult to know which phalanx is absent without X-rays and even then, the missing bone may not be identified (note no attempt is made to distinguish missing middle from proximal phalanges). In this situation the location adjective should be removed. Note that this finding is distinct from Short toes, (which are reduced in length but have the normal number of phalangeal segments). Partial absence of the hallux is an alternative term that may be used for the first toe.

HP:0011307.label: Splayed toes
HP:0011307.definition: Divergence of digits along the anteroposterior axis (in the plane of the sole).

HP:0011308.label: Slender toe
HP:0011308.definition: Toes that are disproportionately narrow (reduced girth) for the hand/foot size or build of the individual.

HP:0011309.label: Tapered toe
HP:0011309.definition: The gradual reduction in girth of the toe from proximal to distal.

HP:0011310.label: Bridged palmar crease
HP:0011310.definition: A crease that connects the proximal and distal transverse palmar creases.
HP:0011310.comment: The crease that connects the two transverse creases should itself be more in the transverse (antero-posterior) than longitudinal (proximo-distal) orientation.

HP:0011311.label: Sydney crease
HP:0011311.definition: Extension of the proximal transverse crease (five finger crease) to the ulnar edge of the palm.
HP:0011311.comment: The proximal transverse (five finger) crease starts on the radial side of the hand near the base of the index finger and extends toward the ulnar side of the palm, but does not reach the ulnar side. In this finding, the crease extends completely to the ulnar margin of the palm.

HP:0011312.label: Fused nails
HP:0011312.definition: A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation with partially separated nails, each with a separate lateral radius of curvature.
HP:0011312.comment: The use of the word "fused" is not meant to imply that pathogenetically these nails were separate and merged. This is distinct from a split or cleaved nail, where the two parts of the nails share the same radius of curvature. The involved digits should be specified. It may be associated with underlying syndactylous digits, but these are coded separately.

HP:0011314.label: Abnormal long bone morphology
HP:0011314.definition: An abnormality of size or shape of the long bones.

HP:0011315.label: Unicoronal synostosis
HP:0011315.definition: Synostosis affecting only one of the coronal sutures.

HP:0011316.label: Left unicoronal synostosis
HP:0011316.definition: Synostosis affecting only the left coronal suture.

HP:0011317.label: Right unicoronal synostosis
HP:0011317.definition: Unicoronal synostosis affecting only the right coronal suture.

HP:0011318.label: Bicoronal synostosis
HP:0011318.definition: Synostosis affecting the right and the left coronal suture.

HP:0011319.label: Bilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011319.definition: Premature synostosis of both lambdoid sutures.

HP:0011320.label: Unilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011320.definition: Premature synostosis of only one lambdoid suture.

HP:0011321.label: Left unilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011321.definition: Premature synostosis of only the left lambdoid suture.

HP:0011322.label: Right unilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011322.definition: Premature synostosis of only the right lambdoid suture.

HP:0011323.label: Cleft of chin
HP:0011323.definition: Incomplete fusion of the chin, resulting from a developmental defect and manifesting as a midline cleft or fissure of the chin.

HP:0011324.label: Multiple suture craniosynostosis
HP:0011324.definition: Craniosynostosis involving at least 2 cranial sutures, where the exact pattern of sutures fused has not been precisely specified.
HP:0011324.comment: If possible, it is preferable to annotate the precise pattern of involvement of the cranial sutures involved in craniosynostosis. This term may be chosen if more information is not available.

HP:0011326.label: Anterior plagiocephaly
HP:0011326.definition: Asymmetry of the anterior part of the skull.
HP:0011326.comment: Anterior plagiocephaly may have synostotic or non-synostotic causes.

HP:0011327.label: Posterior plagiocephaly
HP:0011327.definition: Asymmetry of the posterior part of the skull.
HP:0011327.comment: Anterior plagiocephaly may have synostotic or non-synostotic causes.

HP:0011328.label: Abnormal fontanelle morphology
HP:0011328.comment: The fontanelles are the regions in an infant's calvaria that are covered by a thick membrane that normally ossify in the first two years of life.

HP:0011329.label: Abnormality of cranial sutures
HP:0011329.definition: Any anomaly of a cranial suture, that is one of the six membrane-covered openings in the incompletely ossified skull of the fetus or newborn infant.

HP:0011330.label: Metopic synostosis
HP:0011330.definition: Premature fusion of the metopic suture.

HP:0011331.label: Hemifacial atrophy
HP:0011331.definition: Unilateral atrophy of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.
exact_synonyms: Atrophy of one side of the face

HP:0011332.label: Hemifacial hypoplasia
HP:0011332.definition: Unilateral underdevelopment of the facial tissues, including muscles and bones.
exact_synonyms: Decreased size of half of the face
Decrease in size of half of face
Decreased size of one side of the face
Decrease in size of one side of the face
Shrinking of one side of the face

HP:0011333.label: Asymmetric crying face
HP:0011333.definition: Asymmetry observed in the face of a neonate or infant whose face appears symmetric at rest and asymmetric during crying as the mouth is pulled downward on one side while not moving on the other side.
HP:0011333.comment: Asymmetric crying facies is caused by underdevelopment of the depressor anguli oris muscle or compression of one of the branches of the facial nerve.
related_synonyms: Hypoplasia of depressor angula oris muscle

HP:0011335.label: Frontal hirsutism
HP:0011335.definition: Excessive amount of hair growth on forehead.

HP:0011336.label: Bitemporal forceps marks
HP:0011336.definition: Bilateral temporal scarlike defects, which are said to resemble forceps marks.
HP:0011336.comment: Congenital, bilateral, scarlike facial lesions have been reported under several titles, such as hereditary symmetric systemic aplastic nevi, congenital ectodermal dysplasia of the face, familial focal facial dermal dysplasia, bitemporal aplasia cutis congenita, and focal facial dermal dysplasia (FFDD). The findings are congenital, bilateral scarlike facial lesions in the preauricular or cheek areas. The lesions may present as slightly depressed hypopigmented scarlike oval plaques measuring about 1 cm and may have a surrounding rim of fine lanugo-like hair. Skin biopsy can reveal an atrophic epidermis with a thinned dermis devoid of adnexal structures. Elastic fibers are absent in the affected areas, as can be shown by Verhoeff-van Giesen staining.
exact_synonyms: Congenital ectodermal dysplasia of the face

HP:0011338.label: Abnormality of mouth shape
HP:0011338.definition: An abnormality of the outline, configuration, or contour of the mouth.

HP:0011339.label: Abnormality of upper lip vermillion
HP:0011339.definition: An abnormality of the vermilion border, the sharp demarcation between the lip (red colored) and the adjacent normal skin.

HP:0011340.label: Incomplete cleft of the upper lip
HP:0011340.definition: Cleft of the upper lip that does not go all the way from the bottom of the upper lip until the nasal cavity.
HP:0011340.comment: If the cleft lip is on only one side, use 'Incomplete unilateral cleft lip' (HP:5201000). This term was created to be used in association with a left (HP:0012835) or right (HP:0012834) modifier to annotate completeness of a cleft lip.
exact_synonyms: Partial cleft of the upper lip
Notched cleft of the upper lip
Incomplete cleft of the upper lip

HP:0011341.label: Long upper lip
HP:0011341.definition: Increased width of the upper lip.
exact_synonyms: Increased vertical length of upper lip

HP:0011342.label: Mild global developmental delay
HP:0011342.definition: A mild delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.

HP:0011343.label: Moderate global developmental delay
HP:0011343.definition: A moderate delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.

HP:0011344.label: Severe global developmental delay
HP:0011344.definition: A severe delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.

HP:0011345.label: Moderate expressive language delay
HP:0011345.definition: A moderate delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

HP:0011346.label: Mild expressive language delay
HP:0011346.definition: A mild delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

HP:0011347.label: Abnormality of ocular abduction
HP:0011347.definition: An abnormality involving the movement of the eye outwards.

HP:0011348.label: Abnormal sixth cranial nerve morphology
HP:0011348.definition: Any structural abnormality of the abducens nerve.
HP:0011348.comment: The abducens nerve (also known as the sixth cranial nerve or cranioal nerve VI) controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle of the eye, which moves the eyeball in the outward direction (towards the side of the head).
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the sixth cranial nerve

HP:0011350.label: Mild receptive language delay
HP:0011350.definition: A mild delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

HP:0011351.label: Moderate receptive language delay
HP:0011351.definition: A moderate delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

HP:0011352.label: Severe receptive language delay
HP:0011352.definition: A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

HP:0011353.label: Arterial intimal fibrosis
HP:0011353.definition: Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries.

HP:0011354.label: Generalized abnormality of skin
HP:0011354.definition: An abnormality of the skin that is not localized to any one particular region.

HP:0011355.label: Localized skin lesion
HP:0011355.definition: A lesion of the skin that is located in a specific region rather than being generalized.

HP:0011356.label: Regional abnormality of skin
HP:0011356.definition: An abnormality of the skin that is restricted to a particular body region.

HP:0011359.label: Dry hair
HP:0011359.definition: Hair that lacks the luster (shine or gleam) of normal hair.

HP:0011360.label: Acquired abnormal hair pattern
HP:0011360.definition: An abnormality of the distribution of hair growth that is acquired during the course of life.

HP:0011361.label: Congenital abnormal hair pattern
HP:0011361.definition: A congenital abnormality of the distribution of hair growth.

HP:0011363.label: Abnormality of hair growth rate
HP:0011363.definition: Hair whose growth rate deviates from the norm.
HP:0011363.comment: Hair growth rate is normally about 1.25 centimeters per month.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of speed of hair growth
Abnormality of pace of hair growth

HP:0011365.label: Patchy hypopigmentation of hair
HP:0011365.definition: Reduced pigmentation of hair in patches.

HP:0011368.label: Epidermal thickening
HP:0011368.definition: Thickening of the epidermal layer of the skin.

HP:0011369.label: Mongolian blue spot
HP:0011369.definition: Congenital deep dermal melanosis in the sacral area.

HP:0011370.label: Recurrent cutaneous fungal infections
HP:0011370.definition: Increased susceptibility to cutaneous fungal infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of cutaneous fungal infections.

HP:0011371.label: Recurrent viral skin infections
HP:0011371.definition: Increased susceptibility to viral skin infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral skin infections.

HP:0011372.label: Aplasia of the inner ear
HP:0011372.definition: Absence of the inner ear due to a developmental defect.
HP:0011372.comment: Aplasia of the inner ear is usually diagnosed on MR or CT imaging.

HP:0011373.label: Incomplete partition of the cochlea
HP:0011373.definition: Incomplete formation of the cochlear partition. The scala vestibuli and scala tympani separated by the cochlear partition, except in the apical turn where the two scalae are in continuity via the helicotrema.

HP:0011374.label: Incomplete partition of the cochlea type I
HP:0011374.definition: Incomplete partition I is also known as cystic cochleovestibular malformation, where the cochlea has no bony modiolus, resulting in an empty cystic cochlea. This is accompanied by a dilated cystic vestibule with developmental arrest at the fifth week of gestation.

HP:0011375.label: Cochlear aplasia
HP:0011375.definition: Absence of the cochlea, a spiral shaped cavity in the inner ear, owing to a developmental defect.

HP:0011376.label: Abnormal morphology of the vestibule of the inner ear
HP:0011376.definition: A morphological abnormality of the vestibule, the central part of the osseous labyrinth that is situated medial to the tympanic cavity, behind the cochlea, and in front of the semicircular canals.
HP:0011376.comment: The vestibular system consists of five distinct components, three semicircular canals that are sensitive to angular acceleration and two otolith organs that are sensitive to linear acceleration.
exact_synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the vestibule of the inner ear

HP:0011377.label: Aplasia of the vestibule
HP:0011377.definition: Complete absence of the vestibule of the inner ear.

HP:0011378.label: Hypoplasia of the vestibule of the inner ear
HP:0011378.definition: Underdevelopment of the vestibule of the inner ear.

HP:0011379.label: Dilated vestibule of the inner ear
HP:0011379.definition: Dilatation of the vestibule of the inner ear.

HP:0011380.label: Abnormal semicircular canal morphology
HP:0011380.definition: An abnormality of the morphology of the semicircular canal.
exact_synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the semicircular canal

HP:0011383.label: Enlarged semicircular canal
HP:0011383.definition: Increased size of the semicircular canal.

HP:0011384.label: Abnormality of the internal auditory canal
HP:0011384.definition: An abnormality of the Internal acoustic meatus, i.e., of the canal in the petrous part of the temporal bone through which the cranial nerve VII and cranial nerve VIII traverse.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the internal acoustic meatus

HP:0011385.label: Absent internal auditory canal
HP:0011385.definition: Aplasia of the internal auditory canal.

HP:0011386.label: Narrow internal auditory canal
HP:0011386.definition: Reduction in diameter of the internal auditory canal.

HP:0011387.label: Enlarged vestibular aqueduct
HP:0011387.definition: Increased size of the vestibular aqueduct.
HP:0011387.comment: Enlarged vestibular aqueduct is commonly seen in Pendred syndrome.

HP:0011388.label: Enlarged cochlear aqueduct
HP:0011388.definition: Increased size of the cochlear duct, i.e., of a duct that communicates between the perilymphatic space and the subarachnoid space, and transmits a vein from the cochlea to join the internal jugular.
HP:0011388.comment: The cochlear aqueduct surrounds the perilymphatic (periotic duct). Enlargement of the cochlear aqueduct may be seen in POU3F4 X-linked deafness with Gusher.

HP:0011389.label: Functional abnormality of the inner ear
HP:0011389.definition: An abnormality of the function of the inner ear.
HP:0011389.comment: The inner ear comprises the cochlea, three semicircular canals and the vestibule (labyrinth), and is directly responsible for hearing. Additionally, the vestibule and semicircular canals function to maintain balance or equilibrium.
exact_synonyms: Functional abnormality of the inner ear

HP:0011390.label: Abnormal inner ear morphology
HP:0011390.definition: A structural anomaly of the internal part of the ear.
HP:0011390.comment: The inner ear contains the cochlea and the semicircular canals.
exact_synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the inner ear

HP:0011391.label: Abnormal inner ear nerve morphology
exact_synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the nerves of the inner ear

HP:0011393.label: Aplasia of the vestibular nerve
HP:0011393.comment: May be seen in CHARGE syndrome.
exact_synonyms: Aplasia of the eighth cranial nerve

HP:0011394.label: Hypoplasia of the vestibular nerve
exact_synonyms: Hypoplasia of the eighth cranial nerve

HP:0011395.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the cochlea
HP:0011395.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the cochlea, a spiral shaped cavity in the inner ear, owing to a developmental defect.

HP:0011396.label: Abnormality of the cochlear nerve
HP:0011396.definition: Any anomaly of the cohclear nerve, which is the part of the vestibulocochlear nerve that is responsible for transmitting auditory signals from the inner ear to the cochlear nuclei within the brainstem and ultimately to the primary auditory cortex within the temporal lobe.

HP:0011397.label: Abnormal spinal cord dorsal column morphology
HP:0011397.definition: An abnormality of the dorsal columns, i.e., of the dorsal portion of the gray substance of the spinal cord. The dorsal column consists of the fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus and itself is part of the dorsal funiculus.
HP:0011397.comment: The dorsal column represents an ascending pathway mediating well-localized fine touch and conscious proprioception.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the dorsal column of the spinal cord

HP:0011399.label: Tibialis anterior muscle atrophy
HP:0011399.definition: Wasting of the tibialis anterior muscle.
HP:0011399.comment: The tibialis anterior muscle is located in the front of the lower leg. The shin may appear prominent because of atrophy of the tibialis anterior muscle (sharp shin sign).

HP:0011400.label: Abnormal CNS myelination
HP:0011400.definition: An abnormality of myelination of nerves in the central nervous system.
HP:0011400.comment: In the CNS, myelin is the product of oligodendrocytes (and not of Schwann cells, as in the PNS). This term refers to an abnormality of the process in which myelin sheaths are formed and maintained around neurons or the result of such an abnormality.

HP:0011401.label: Delayed peripheral myelination
HP:0011401.definition: Delayed myelination in the peripheral nervous system.

HP:0011403.label: Abnormal umbilical cord blood vessel morphology

HP:0011404.label: Lethal short-trunk short stature
HP:0011404.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs that is lethal at birth.

HP:0011406.label: Infancy onset short-trunk short stature
HP:0011406.definition: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with onset in infancy.

HP:0011408.label: Moderate intrauterine growth retardation
HP:0011408.definition: Intrauterine growth retardation that is at least 3 standard deviations (SD) below average, but not as low as 4 SD, corrected for sex and gestational age.

HP:0011409.label: Abnormal placental membrane morphology
HP:0011409.definition: Structural anomaly of the fetal membranes (also known as the amniochorionic or placental membranes), which comprise a vital intrauterine compartment, where they perform mechanical, immune, and endocrine functions to promote growth of the fetus and protection from environmental adversity. Amniochorionic membranes anatomically consist of a single layer of cuboidal amnion epithelial cells, chorionic trophoblasts, and scattered fibroblasts connected by a layer of type IV collagen-rich extracellular matrix.

HP:0011410.label: Caesarean section
HP:0011410.definition: Delivery of a fetus through surgical incisions made through the abdominal wall (laparotomy) and the uterine wall (hysterotomy).

HP:0011412.label: Ventouse delivery
HP:0011412.definition: Delivery of newborn by means of a ventouse, a vacuum device used to assist the delivery of a baby when the second stage of labor has not progressed adequately.

HP:0011413.label: Shoulder dystocia
HP:0011413.definition: Shoulder dystocia occurs when the fetal anterior shoulder impacts against the maternal symphysis following delivery of the vertex.
HP:0011413.comment: Adelivery in which additional maneuvers are required to deliver the fetus after normal gentle downward traction has failed.

HP:0011414.label: Hydropic placenta
HP:0011414.definition: An abnormality of the placenta in which there are numerous cystic spaces within the placenta as well as placental enlargement.

HP:0011417.label: Long umbilical cord
HP:0011417.definition: Increased length of the umbilical cord.

HP:0011418.label: Abnormal insertion of umbilical cord
HP:0011418.definition: Anomalous location of the insertion of umbilical cord in the placenta. Normally, the insertion is at least two centimers distant from the edge of the placenta.

HP:0011419.label: Placental abruption
HP:0011419.definition: Separation of the placenta from the uterus wall before delivery.

HP:0011420.label: Age of death
HP:0011420.definition: The age group when the cessation of life happens.

HP:0011421.label: Death in adolescence
HP:0011421.definition: Death during adolescence, the period between childhood and adulthood (roughly between the ages of 10 and 16 years).

HP:0011422.label: Abnormal blood chloride concentration
HP:0011422.definition: An abnormality of chloride homeostasis or concentration in the body.

HP:0011423.label: Hyperchloremia
HP:0011423.definition: An abnormally increased chloride concentration in the blood.

HP:0011424.label: Increased serum zinc
HP:0011424.definition: An increased concentration of zinc in the blood.

HP:0011425.label: Fetal ultrasound soft marker
HP:0011425.definition: An finding upon obstetric ultrasound examination performed at around 16 to 20 weeks of gestation that is abnormal but not clearly identifiable as a fetal anatomic malformation or growth restriction. Such findings are known as soft markers since they are associated with increased risk for fetal aneuploidy or other disorders.
HP:0011425.comment: The screening ultrasound at 16 to 20 weeks should evaluate 8 markers, 5 of which (thickened nuchal fold, echogenic bowel, mild ventriculomegaly, echogenic focus in the heart, and choroid plexus cyst) are associated with an increased risk of fetal aneuploidy, and in some cases with nonchromosomal problems, while 3 (single umbilical artery, enlarged cisterna magna, and pyelectasis) are only associated with an increased risk of nonchromosomal abnormalities when seen in isolation (PMID:16100637).

HP:0011426.label: Fetal choroid plexus cysts
HP:0011426.definition: Fetal choroid plexus cysts (CPCs) are sonographically discrete, small cysts found in the choroid plexus within the lateral cerebral ventricles of the developing fetus at 14 to 24 weeks gestation. Imaging of the choroid plexus is performed in the transverse plane of the fetal head at the same level that the lateral cerebral ventricle is evaluated. The choroid plexus should be inspected bilaterally for the presence of cysts. The size of CPCs is not of clinical relevance (PMID:16100637).
HP:0011426.comment: There is agreement that ultrasound characteristics of CPC, such as bilaterality, size, number, complexity, and resolution, are not related to the risk of aneuploidy. However, cysts with diameters less than 5 mm may not be linked with trisomy and large cysts in excess of 10 mm may impart a higher risk.

HP:0011427.label: Enlarged fetal cisterna magna
HP:0011427.definition: The cisterna magna is measured on a transaxial view of the fetal head angled 15 degrees caudal to the canthomeatal line. The anterior/posterior diameter is taken between the inferior/posterior surface of the vermis of the cerebellum to the inner surface of the cranium. An enlarged cisternal magna is defined by an anterior/posterior diameter of 10 mm or more (PMID:16100637).

HP:0011428.label: Short fetal femur length
HP:0011428.definition: A short femur length is defined as either a measurement below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or a measurement that is less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The femur should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).

HP:0011429.label: Short fetal humerus length
HP:0011429.definition: A short humerus length is defined as a length below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or as a measurement less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The humerus should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).
exact_synonyms: Short fetal long bone in upper arm length
Short foetal long bone in upper arm length

HP:0011430.label: Hypoplasia of fetal nasal bone
HP:0011430.definition: On prenatal ultrasound, the nasal bone is a thin echogenic line within the bridge of the fetal nose. The fetus is imaged facing the transducer with the fetal face strictly in the midline. The angle of insonation is 90 degrees, with the longitudinal axis of the nasal bone as the reference line. Calibres are placed at each end of the nasal bone. Absence of the nasal bone or measurements below 2.5th percentile are considered significant (PMID:16100637).

HP:0011431.label: Fetal fifth finger clinodactyly
HP:0011431.definition: Fifth finger clinodactyly is defined by a hypoplastic or absent mid-phalanx of the fifth digit. Ultrasound identification of the fetal hand must first be undertaken and then appropriate magnification accomplished. The evaluation requires stretching of the 5 fingers. The diagnosis is established when the middle phalanx of the fifth finger is markedly smaller than normal or absent, which often causes the finger to be curved inward (PMID:16100637).

HP:0011432.label: Elevated maternal circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
HP:0011432.definition: Increase in the levels of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein levels during pregnancy.
HP:0011432.comment: Increased levels of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein is often part of the triple (AFP, Estriol, and human chorionic gonadotropin) or quadruple screening tests (AFP, estriol, human chorionic gonadotropin and Inhibin A) for congenital birth defects. It can be seen in fetal neural tube defects (NTD), abdominal wall defects, congenital renal disease, esophageal atresia, other fetal distress situations (eg, threatened abortion and fetal demise), multiple pregnancy, placental chorioangioma and placental lakes and other fetal and maternal conditions. Association with various adverse pregnancy outcomes reported. Usually assessed in second trimester and values above 2.5 MoM considered as significantly increased. For NTD, a screen-negative result indicates that the calculated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) multiple of the median (MoM) falls below the established cutoff of 2.50 MoM. A negative screen does not guarantee the absence of neural tube defects. A screen-positive result indicates that the calculated AFP MoM is 2.50 or greater and may indicate an increased risk for open NTD. The actual risk depends on the level of AFP and the individual's pretest risk of having a child with NTD based on family history, geographical location, maternal conditions such as diabetes and epilepsy, and use of folate prior to conception. A screen-positive result does not infer a definitive diagnosis of a NTD but indicates that further evaluation should be considered. Reduced levels of alpha-fetoprotein can be seen in some fetal disorders such as Down syndrome.

HP:0011433.label: High maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
HP:0011433.definition: An abnormally high concentration of maternal serum human chorionic gonadotropin as compared to normal values for gestational-age.
HP:0011433.comment: Reduced levels of alpha-fetoprotein can be seen in some fetal disorders such as Down syndrome.

HP:0011434.label: Low maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
HP:0011434.definition: An abnormally low concentration of maternal serum human chorionic gonadotropin as compared to normal values for gestational-age.
HP:0011434.comment: Reduced levels of alpha-fetoprotein can be seen in some fetal disorders such as Down syndrome.

HP:0011435.label: Low maternal circulating PAPP-A concentration
HP:0011435.definition: An abnormally low concentration of serum PAPP-A (pregnancy associated plasma protein A), as compared to normal values for gestational-age.
HP:0011435.comment: Reduced levels of alpha-fetoprotein can be seen in some fetal disorders such as Down syndrome.

HP:0011436.label: Abnormal maternal serum screening
HP:0011436.definition: An abnormally elevated or decreased level of a maternal serum marker analytes used in screening for aneuploidy.

HP:0011437.label: Maternal autoimmune disease
HP:0011437.definition: A medical history of a fetus or child born to a mother with an autoimmune disease.
HP:0011437.comment: Maternal autoimmune diseases with potential adverse effects for the fetus include autoimmune forms of hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism, myasthenia gravis, systemic lupus erythematodes, and autoimmune forms of thrombocytopenia.

HP:0011438.label: Maternal teratogenic exposure
HP:0011438.definition: A medical history of exposure of the mother of a child or fetus to a teratogenic substance during pregnancy.
HP:0011438.comment: Commonly encountered maternal teratogens include alcohol, antiepileptic drugs, antihypertensive and antithyroid medications, aspirin, bisphosphonates, chemotherapy, monoclonal antibodies, ionizing radiation, recreational drugs, and serotonin-specific reuptake inhibitors (a class of antidepressants).

HP:0011440.label: Alcohol-induced rhabdomyolysis
HP:0011440.definition: Rhabdomyolysis induced by intake of alcohol.

HP:0011441.label: Abnormal medulla oblongata morphology
HP:0011441.definition: An abnormality of the medulla oblongata, the lower half of the brainstem.
HP:0011441.comment: The medulla oblongata, which is often referred to simply as the medulla, comprises the medullary reticular formation, inferior olivary complex and cochlear nuclear complex, among other structures.

HP:0011442.label: Abnormal central motor function
HP:0011442.definition: An anomaly of the control or production of movement in the central nervous system.

HP:0011444.label: Decorticate rigidity
HP:0011444.definition: A type of rigidity in which the arms are in flexion and adduction and the legs are extended. This signifies a lesion in the cerebral white matter, internal capsules, or thalamus.

HP:0011445.label: Athetoid cerebral palsy
HP:0011445.definition: A type of cerebral palsy characterized by slow, involuntary muscle movement and mixed muscle tone.
HP:0011445.comment: Athetoid cerebral palsy is caused by damage to the basal ganglia.

HP:0011446.label: Abnormality of mental function
HP:0011446.comment: This includes abnormalities in speech, mood, emotions, behavior, and cognition.

HP:0011447.label: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei
HP:0011447.comment: Hyposegmented cells are neutrophils with fewer than three nuclear lobes.
exact_synonyms: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood

HP:0011448.label: Ankle clonus
HP:0011448.definition: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Ankle clonus is tested by rapidly flexing the foot upward.
HP:0011448.comment: Ankle clonus is generally caused by corticospinal disease.

HP:0011449.label: Knee clonus
HP:0011449.definition: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Knee clonus can be tested by rapidly pushing the patella towards the toes.

HP:0011450.label: Unusual CNS infection
HP:0011450.definition: A type of infection of the central nervous system that can be regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection.

HP:0011451.label: Primary microcephaly
HP:0011451.definition: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender at birth.
exact_synonyms: Decreased head circumference present at birth
related_synonyms: Head circumference small for gestational age

HP:0011452.label: Functional abnormality of the middle ear
HP:0011452.definition: An abnormality of the function of the middle ear.
HP:0011452.comment: The middle ear comprises the tympanic cavity in the temporal bone of the skull behind the eardrum, and is separated from the outer ear by the ear drum. The tympanic cavity contains the auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) that vibrate when exposed to sound, forming a chain that extends to the oval window of the inner ear and whose main function is to amplify sound. Additionally, the middle ear connects to the back of the throat and nose through the Eustachian tube.
exact_synonyms: Functional abnormality of the middle ear

HP:0011453.label: Abnormal incus morphology
HP:0011453.definition: An abnormality of the incus, an ossicle in the middle ear.

HP:0011454.label: Abnormal malleus morphology
HP:0011454.definition: An abnormality of the malleus, an ossicle in the middle ear.

HP:0011457.label: Loss of eyelashes
HP:0011457.definition: This term refers to the loss of eyelashes that were previously present.
HP:0011457.comment: Common causes of loss of eyelashes include inflammation, autoimmunity, tumors,endocrine disorders, drugs and medications, and a number of congenital conditions.

HP:0011458.label: Abdominal symptom
HP:0011458.definition: A subjective manifestation of disease localized to the abdomen.

HP:0011459.label: Esophageal carcinoma
HP:0011459.definition: The presence of a carcinoma of the esophagus.

HP:0011460.label: Embryonal onset
HP:0011460.definition: Onset of disease at up to 8 weeks following fertilization (corresponding to 10 weeks of gestation).
HP:0011460.comment: The time interval of a gestation is called the gestation period. In human obstetrics, gestational age refers to the fertilization age plus two weeks. This is approximately the duration since the woman's last menstrual period began.

HP:0011461.label: Fetal onset
HP:0011461.definition: Onset prior to birth but after 8 weeks of embryonic development (corresponding to a gestational age of 10 weeks).
HP:0011461.comment: The time interval of a gestation is called the gestation period. In human obstetrics, gestational age refers to the fertilization age plus two weeks. This is approximately the duration since the woman's last menstrual period began.

HP:0011462.label: Young adult onset
HP:0011462.definition: Onset of disease at the age of between 16 and 40 years.

HP:0011463.label: Childhood onset
HP:0011463.definition: Onset of disease at the age of between 1 and 5 years.
HP:0011463.comment: This term refers to ages up to but not including the fifth birthday (see Juvenile onset).

HP:0011464.label: Aganglionosis of the small intestine
HP:0011464.definition: A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the small intestine.

HP:0011465.label: Duodenal aganglionosis
HP:0011465.definition: A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the duodenum.

HP:0011466.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the gallbladder
HP:0011466.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the gallbladder.

HP:0011467.label: Absent gallbladder
HP:0011467.definition: A developmental defect in which the gallbladder fails to form.

HP:0011468.label: Facial tics
HP:0011468.definition: Sudden, repetitive, nonrhythmic motor movements (spasms), involving the eyes and muscles of the face.

HP:0011469.label: Nasal regurgitation
HP:0011469.definition: Regurgitation of milk through the nose.

HP:0011470.label: Nasogastric tube feeding in infancy
HP:0011470.definition: Feeding problem necessitating nasogastric tube feeding.
HP:0011470.comment: This is a severe form of feeding problems in infancy.

HP:0011471.label: Gastrostomy tube feeding in infancy
HP:0011471.definition: Feeding problem necessitating gastrostomy tube feeding.
HP:0011471.comment: This is an extremely severe form of feeding problems in infancy.

HP:0011472.label: Abnormal small intestinal villus morphology
exact_synonyms: Abnormal shape of small intestinal villus
Abnormality of small intestinal villus morphology

HP:0011473.label: Villous atrophy
HP:0011473.definition: The enteric villi are atrophic or absent.
related_synonyms: Small intestine biopsy shows villous atrophy

HP:0011474.label: Childhood onset sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0011474.definition: Sensorineural hearing impairment with childhood onset.

HP:0011475.label: Persistent stapedial artery
HP:0011475.definition: Persistence of the stapedial artery, which normally regresses during embryonic life.

HP:0011476.label: Profound sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0011476.definition: Complete loss of hearing related to a sensorineural defect.

HP:0011477.label: Upbeat nystagmus
HP:0011477.definition: In primary position, the eyes drift slowly downward and then spontaneously beat upward. Upward gaze accentuates the nystagmus. The associated oscillopsias are often very irritating, but the symptoms are usually transient.
