HP:0011761.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that is of unknown cellular origin and that lacks immunocytochemical or fine structural markers. Null cell adenomas are not associated with hormone excess.

HP:0011762.label: Pituitary thyrotropic cell adenoma
HP:0011762.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH).

HP:0011763.label: Pituitary carcinoma
HP:0011763.definition: A pituitary tumor with subarachnoid, brain, or systemic metastasis. The diagnosis of a pituitary carcinoma requires evidence of metastatic disease, either outside the central nervous system (CNS) or as separate noncontiguous foci within the CNS.

HP:0011764.label: Pituitary spindle cell oncocytoma
HP:0011764.definition: A spindled-to-epithelioid, oncocytic, nonendocrine neoplasm of the anterior hypophysis that manifests in adults and follows a benign clinical course. Pituitary spindle cell oncocytomas are firm, fibrous, and adherent to surrounding structures and are highly vascular.

HP:0011766.label: Abnormal parathyroid morphology
HP:0011766.definition: A structural abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

HP:0011767.label: Abnormality of the parathyroid physiology
HP:0011767.definition: A functional abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

HP:0011768.label: Parathyroid dysgenesis
HP:0011768.definition: Abnormal embryonic development of the parathyroid gland.

HP:0011769.label: Ectopic parathyroid
HP:0011769.definition: An abnormal anatomical location of the parathyroid gland.

HP:0011770.label: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
HP:0011770.definition: A type of hyperparathyroidism that occurs following kidney transplantation, which is a treatment for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Although kidney transplantation leads to a normalization of serum calcium and parathyroid hormone in most patients. The state of persistent hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism is referred to as tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

HP:0011771.label: Autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
HP:0011771.definition: A type of hypoparathyroidism with circulating antiparathyroid or anti-calcium sensing receptor antibodies indicative of autoimmunity.

HP:0011772.label: Abnormal thyroid morphology
HP:0011772.definition: A structural abnormality of the thyroid gland.

HP:0011773.label: Uninodular goiter
HP:0011773.definition: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to a singular nodule in the thyroid gland.

HP:0011780.label: Thyroid hemiagenesis
HP:0011780.definition: Absence of a lobe of the thyroid gland related to a failure of its embryologic development.

HP:0011781.label: Thyroid C cell hyperplasia
HP:0011781.definition: An abnormal growth of parafollicular (C-cells) cells.
HP:0011781.comment: Thyroid C cell hyperplasia usually occurs before the development of familial forms of medullary thyroid cancer and is considered a pre-cancerous condition.

HP:0011786.label: Thyrotoxicosis with toxic single thyroid nodule

HP:0011787.label: Central hypothyroidism
HP:0011787.definition: A type of hypothyroidism due to an insufficient stimulation of an otherwise normal thyroid gland. Central hypothyroidism is caused by either pituitary (secondary hypothyroidism) or hypothalamic (tertiary hypothyroidism) defects.

HP:0011788.label: Increased circulating free T3
HP:0011788.definition: An elevated concentration of free 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine in the blood circulation.

HP:0011789.label: Impaired sensitivity to thyroid stimulating hormone
HP:0011789.definition: Reduced sensitivity of thyroid follicle cells to stimulation by biologically active thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).

HP:0011792.label: Neoplasm by histology
HP:0011792.definition: Neoplasm categorized according to type of histological abnormality.

HP:0011793.label: Neoplasm by anatomical site
HP:0011793.definition: Neoplasm categorized according to the anatomical site of origin of the neoplasm.

HP:0011794.label: Embryonal renal neoplasm
HP:0011794.definition: The presence of an embryonal neoplasm of the kidney that primarily affects children.

HP:0011795.label: Intralobar nephroblastomatosis
HP:0011795.definition: Presence of persistent islands of renal blastema in the postnatal kidney, anywhere within a renal lobe (a portion of a kidney consisting of a renal pyramid and the renal cortex above it).

HP:0011796.label: Perilobar nephroblastomatosis
HP:0011796.definition: Abnormally persistent foci of embryonal immature blastema located in the superficial cortical region (perilobar).

HP:0011797.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 1
HP:0011797.definition: A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma that is characterized by small cuboidal cells covering thin papillae with a single line of uniform nuclei and small nucleoli.

HP:0011798.label: Renal oncocytoma
HP:0011798.definition: A renal tumor originating from an oncocyte, which is an epithelial cell characterized by an excessive amount of mitochondria, resulting in an abundant acidophilic, granular cytoplasm.
HP:0011798.comment: Renal oncocytoma is seen in Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome (OMIM 135150).

HP:0011800.label: Midface retrusion
HP:0011800.definition: Posterior positions and/or vertical shortening of the infraorbital and perialar regions, or increased concavity of the face and/or reduced nasolabial angle.

HP:0011801.label: Enlargement of parotid gland
HP:0011801.definition: Increased size of the parotid gland.

HP:0011802.label: Hamartoma of tongue
HP:0011802.definition: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the tongue.

HP:0011803.label: Bifid nose
HP:0011803.definition: Visually assessable vertical indentation, cleft, or depression of the nasal bridge, ridge and tip.
HP:0011803.comment: This is a bundled term, but as it is useful in practice it is kept here. If it is only an indentation or cleft of the nasal tip, this should be coded as Bifid nasal tip.
exact_synonyms: Indentation or clefting of the nose

HP:0011804.label: Abnormal muscle physiology
HP:0011804.definition: A functional abnormality of a skeletal muscle.

HP:0011805.label: Abnormal skeletal muscle morphology
HP:0011805.definition: A structural abnormality of a skeletal muscle.

HP:0011807.label: Type 1 muscle fiber atrophy
HP:0011807.definition: Atrophy (wasting) affecting primary type 1 muscle fibers. This feature in general can only be observed on muscle biopsy.

HP:0011808.label: Decreased patellar reflex
HP:0011808.definition: Decreased intensity of the patellar reflex (also known as the knee jerk reflex).

HP:0011809.label: Paradoxical myotonia
HP:0011809.definition: A type of myotonia that worsens with repeated muscle contractions.
HP:0011809.comment: In classic myotonia the myotonia improves as muscles warm up, whereas in paradoxical myotonia (paramyotonia) it worsens with repeated muscle contractions.

HP:0011810.label: Impaired two-point discrimination
HP:0011810.definition: A reduced ability to distinguish tactile sensations at points that are very close to one another. This can be tested by using special calipers whose points can be set from 2mm to several centimeters apart.
HP:0011810.comment: A normal individual can sense about a 3 mm separation of points on the fingertips.

HP:0011811.label: Impaired touch localization
HP:0011811.definition: A reduced ability to identify precisely the site of a touch. This test is usually carried out by asking a patient, whose eyes are closed or covered, to touch the same site with a fingertip.

HP:0011812.label: Agraphesthesia
HP:0011812.definition: Impaired ability to recognize letters or numbers drawn by an examiner's fingertip on the patient's skin (the patients eyes are closed or covered throughout this examination).

HP:0011813.label: Increased cerebral lipofuscin
HP:0011813.definition: Lipofuscin (age pigment) is a brown-yellow, electron-dense, autofluorescent material that accumulates progressively over time in lysosomes of postmitotic cells, such as neurons and cardiac myocytes. This term pertains if there is an increase in the accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.

HP:0011814.label: Increased urinary hypoxanthine level
HP:0011814.definition: The concentration of hypoxanthine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0011815.label: Cephalocele
HP:0011815.definition: A congenital defect in the skull, whereby there is a protrusion of part of the cranial contents through a congenital defect in the cranium, usually covered with skin or mucous membrane. The term encephalocele refers to a subclass of these lesions in which brain tissue protrudes through the defect.
HP:0011815.comment: A cephalocele is a rare birth defect that is characterized by a sac-like mass protruding through a defective opening in the skull. The sac varies in size that typically consists of herniated meninges and brain tissue (meningoencephalocele or encephalocele) or fragments of disorganized neural tissue. Alternatively, the sac may contain only the meninges (cranial meningocele) or it may include part of the ventricle filled with CSF (encephalocystocele) covered by skin (from PMID:24931720).

HP:0011816.label: Parietal encephalocele
HP:0011816.definition: An encephalocele located between bregma and lambda.

HP:0011817.label: Basal encephalocele
HP:0011817.definition: Basal encephalocele is an encephalocele that occurs along the cribriform plate or through the sphenoid bone. The mass may appear in the nasal cavity, nasopharynx, epipharynx, sphenoid sinus, posterior orbit, or pterygopalatine fossa. The important distinction from other types is that no external tumor is visible except in those rare instances of herniations so large that they protrude through the mouth or nares.
HP:0011817.comment: The skull base is made up of the ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, paired frontal, and paired parietal bones, and is subdivided into 3 regions: the anterior, middle, and posterior cranial fossae.

HP:0011819.label: Submucous cleft soft palate
HP:0011819.definition: A cleft of the muscular (soft) portion of the palate that is covered by mucous membrane. Soft-palate submucous clefts are characterized by a midline deficiency or lack of muscle tissue.
HP:0011819.comment: Often, submucous cleft palate is associated with bifid uvula, but this should be coded separately. The muscles of the soft palate may not function properly, leading to speech problems, middle ear disease, and swallowing difficulties.

HP:0011820.label: Membranous choanal atresia
HP:0011820.definition: Absence of the normal opening of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture) as a result of an obstructing choanal membrane that may be thin and strandlike or thick and pluglike.

HP:0011821.label: Abnormal facial skeleton morphology
HP:0011821.definition: An abnormality of one or more of the set of bones that make up the facial skeleton.
HP:0011821.comment: The facial skeleton comprises the mandible, maxilla, frontal bone, nasal bones, and zygoma, as well as the inferior nasal concha, the lacrimal bones, the palatine bone, and the vomer.

HP:0011822.label: Broad chin
HP:0011822.definition: Increased width of the midpoint of the mandible (mental protuberance) and overlying soft tissue.

HP:0011823.label: Chin with horizontal crease
HP:0011823.definition: Horizontal crease or fold situated below the vermilion border of the lower lip and above the fatty pad of the chin, with the face at rest.

HP:0011824.label: Chin with H-shaped crease
HP:0011824.definition: H-shaped crease in the fat pad of the chin.
HP:0011824.comment: The H-shape must be distinguished from Vertical crease of the chin.

HP:0011825.label: Tented philtrum
HP:0011825.definition: Prominence of a triangular soft tissue area of the philtrum with the apex to the columella.
HP:0011825.comment: A tented philtrum may accompany a Smooth philtrum. If present this should be coded separately.

HP:0011826.label: Philtrum with midline raphe
HP:0011826.definition: Narrow ridge in the midline of the philtral groove.
HP:0011826.comment: The ridge may be very subtly elevated.

HP:0011827.label: Malaligned philtral ridges
HP:0011827.definition: Absence of the usual parallel position of philtral ridges.
HP:0011827.comment: Hajnis [1972] has described downwards convergent, downwards divergent (trapezoid or triangular), convex (ovoid), and concave philtral configurations. Any of these findings may be coded using this term.

HP:0011828.label: Midline sinus of philtrum
HP:0011828.definition: Pit in the midline of the philtral groove.
HP:0011828.comment: Although congenital sinuses of the lips generally occur in the lower lip, in rare instances they may appear in the philtrum of the upper lip, commonly close to the insertion of the columella.

HP:0011829.label: Narrow philtrum
HP:0011829.definition: Distance between the philtral ridges, measured just above the vermilion border, more than 2 standard deviations below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased distance between the ridges of the philtrum.
HP:0011829.comment: Although congenital sinuses of the lips generally occur in the lower lip, in rare instances they may appear in the philtrum of the upper lip, commonly close to the insertion of the columella.

HP:0011831.label: Deviated nasal tip
HP:0011831.definition: Nasal tip positioned to one side of the midline.
HP:0011831.comment: There is no specific minimal angle before the tip can be determined to be deviated. The assessment of a mild degree of deviation is highly dependant on the experience of the observer. A deviated nasal septum can accompany a deviated nasal tip.

HP:0011832.label: Narrow nasal tip
HP:0011832.definition: Decrease in width of the nasal tip.
HP:0011832.comment: Nasal tip width is assessed at the anterior junction of the alae and the tip. This is easier in persons with a somewhat squared shape of the nasal tip. This may be best viewed from the inferior aspect of the nose. No objective measures are available.

HP:0011833.label: Overhanging nasal tip
HP:0011833.definition: Positioning of the nasal tip inferior to the nasal base.
HP:0011833.comment: This finding is often associated with a long nasal ridge. It is best appreciated in profile. This may also coexist with a Depressed nasal tip and Low insertion of the columella and should be coded separately.

HP:0011834.label: Moyamoya phenomenon
HP:0011834.definition: A noninflammatory, progressive occlusion of the intracranial carotid arteries owing to the formation of netlike collateral arteries arising from the circle of Willis.
HP:0011834.comment: Cerebral angiography shows puff-of-smoke (moyamoya) collaterals at the base of the brain.

HP:0011836.label: Delayed talus ossification
HP:0011836.definition: Delayed maturation and calcification of the talus.

HP:0011837.label: Partial IgA deficiency
HP:0011837.definition: Detectable but decreased IgA levels that are more than 2 standard deviations below normal age-adjusted means.

HP:0011838.label: Sclerodactyly
HP:0011838.definition: Localized thickening and tightness of the skin of the fingers or toes.

HP:0011839.label: Abnormal total T cell count
HP:0011839.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number of T cells or of a subset of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

HP:0011840.label: Abnormal T cell physiology
HP:0011840.definition: A functional anomaly of T cells.

HP:0011841.label: Ventricular flutter
HP:0011841.definition: A potentially lethal cardiac arrhythmia characterized by an extremely rapid, hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia (150-300 beats/min) with a large oscillating sine-wave appearance.
HP:0011841.comment: If untreated, ventricular flutter typically progresses to ventricular fibrillation.

HP:0011842.label: Abnormal skeletal morphology
HP:0011842.definition: An abnormality of the form, structure, or size of the skeletal system.

HP:0011843.label: Abnormal musculoskeletal physiology
HP:0011843.definition: An abnormality of the function of the skeletal system.

HP:0011844.label: Abnormal appendicular skeleton morphology
HP:0011844.definition: An abnormality of the appendicular skeletal system, consisting of the of the limbs, shoulder and pelvic girdles.

HP:0011846.label: Osteoblastoma
HP:0011846.definition: A benign, painful, tumor of bone characterized by the formation of osteoid tissue, primitive bone and calcified tissue.

HP:0011847.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
HP:0011847.definition: A bone tumor composed of cellular spindle-cell stroma containing scattered multinucleated giant cells resembling osteoclasts.

HP:0011848.label: Abdominal colic
HP:0011848.definition: A type of abdominal pain that comes and goes in waves, most often starting and ending suddenly and being of severe intensity.
HP:0011848.comment: Colicky abdominal pain can be caused by kidney stones and gallstones, among other etiologies. This type of pain is thought to be caused by spasm, obstruction, or distension of any of the hollow viscera of the gastrointestinal system.

HP:0011849.label: Abnormal bone ossification
HP:0011849.definition: Any anomaly in the formation of bone or of a bony substance, or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.
HP:0011849.comment: All bones are formed by the replacement by osteocytes of mesenchyme-derived connective tissue. Intramembranous ossification refers to the direct replacement of primitive mesenchyme with bone, and is responsible for bones such as the calvarium (e.g., frontals, parietals, interparietal) and the clavicula. In endochondral ossification, the mesenchyme differentiates into a cartilaginous intermediate, which serves as a template (anlange) that is subsequently removed and replaced by bone. Most bones are formed via endochondral ossification, including those at the base of the skull, the vertebral column, pectoral and pelvic regions and long bones of the extremities. A reduction in the amount of mineralized bone compared with that expected for a given developmental age. In clinicakl parlance, reduced ossification and delayed ossification are often used synonymously, but in principle a bone delayed ossification in a child can display normal ossification at a later developmental stage. The HPO will therefore treat poor, reduced, and decreased officiation as synonymous, and delayed ossification as a specific kind of reduced ossification.

HP:0011851.label: Hemopericardium
HP:0011851.definition: Accumulation of blood within the pericardial sac.

HP:0011852.label: Chylopericardium
HP:0011852.definition: Accumulation of chyle (the whitish fluid taken up by the lacteals in the intestine, consisting of an emulsion of lymph and triglyceride fat thatpasses into the veins by the thoracic duct) in the pericardium. Chylopericardium is generally caused by obstruction of or trauma to the thoracic duct.

HP:0011853.label: Serous pericardial effusion
HP:0011853.definition: Accumulation of serous fluid (pale yellow and transparent fluid) in the pericardial sac.

HP:0011854.label: Hemoperitoneum
HP:0011854.definition: Accumulation of blood in the peritoneal cavity owing to internal hemorrhage.

HP:0011855.label: Pharyngeal edema
HP:0011855.definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid leading to swelling of the pharynx.

HP:0011856.label: Pica
HP:0011856.definition: An appetite for and the persistent ingestion of non-food substances such as clay. In order to diagnose pica, this behavior must have persisted over a period of at least one month.

HP:0011857.label: Plasmacytoma
HP:0011857.definition: A discrete mass of neoplastic monoclonal plasma cells either in the bone marrow or in an extramedullary location.
HP:0011857.comment: Plasmacytoma often generalizes to multiple myeloma over the course of several years.

HP:0011858.label: Reduced factor IX activity
HP:0011858.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor IX. Factor IX, which itself is activated by factor Xa or factor VIIa to form factor IXa, activates factor X into factor Xa.
HP:0011858.comment: Severe deficiency of factor IX underlies hemophilia B.

HP:0011859.label: Punctate keratitis
HP:0011859.definition: A type of keratitis characterized by inflammation in pinpoint areas of the corneal epithelium.

HP:0011860.label: Metaphyseal dappling
HP:0011860.definition: The presence of spots or rounded patches of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
HP:0011860.comment: This finding is characteristic of Strudwick type of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.

HP:0011861.label: Bilateral trilobed lung
HP:0011861.definition: Both lungs have three lobes. Normally, the left lung has two lobes, whereas the right lung has three lobes.

HP:0011862.label: Abnormal bone collagen fibril morphology
HP:0011862.definition: Any structural anomaly of the connective tissue bundles in the extracellular matrix of bone tissue that are composed of collagen, and play a role in tissue strength and elasticity.

HP:0011863.label: Abnormal sternal ossification
HP:0011863.definition: Any anomaly in the formation of the bony substance of the sternum.
HP:0011863.comment: The sternum develops from two cartilaginous bars, situated one on either side of the median plane and connected with the cartilages of the upper nine ribs of its own side. During development, the two cartilaginous bars fuse with each other to form the cartilaginous sternum. This in turn is ossified from six centers: one in the manubrium, four in the body of the sternum, and one in the xiphoid process.

HP:0011864.label: Elevated plasma pyrophosphate
HP:0011864.definition: An abnormally increased diphosphate(4-) concentration in the blood. Diphosphate(4-), as ester with two phosphate groups, is also known as pyrophosphate.

HP:0011867.label: Abnormal iliac wing morphology
HP:0011867.definition: An anomaly of the ilium ala. This is the large expanded portion of the ilum which bounds the greater pelvis laterally.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the wing of the ilium

HP:0011868.label: Sciatica
HP:0011868.definition: Pain in the lower back and hip radiating in the distribution of the sciatic nerve.

HP:0011869.label: Abnormal platelet function
HP:0011869.definition: Any anomaly in the function of thrombocytes.

HP:0011870.label: Impaired arachidonic acid-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0011870.definition: Abnormal response to arachidonic acid as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of arachidonic acid.

HP:0011871.label: Impaired ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0011871.definition: Abnormal response to ristocetin as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ristocetin.

HP:0011872.label: Impaired thrombin-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0011872.definition: Abnormal response to thrombin or thrombin mimetics as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of thrombin (or thrombin mimetics).

HP:0011873.label: Abnormal platelet count
HP:0011873.definition: Abnormal number of platelets per volume of blood. In a healthy adult, a normal platelet count is between 150,000 and 450,000 per microliter of blood.

HP:0011874.label: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
HP:0011874.definition: Low platelet count following administration of unfractionated or (less commonly) low-molecular weight heparin.
HP:0011874.comment: A delay of 5-10 days following administration of heparin is common in patients with no previous (or remote) exposure to heparin, but the drop in platelet count may be precipitous in patients with recent exposure. Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is caused by antibodies against platelet factor 4.

HP:0011875.label: Abnormal platelet morphology
HP:0011875.definition: An anomaly in platelet form, ultrastructure, or intracellular organelles.

HP:0011876.label: Abnormal platelet volume
HP:0011876.definition: Anomalous size of platelets. Most normal sized platelets are 1.5 to 3 micrometers in diameter. Large platelets are 4 to 7 micrometers. Giant platelets are larger than 7 micrometers and usually 10 to 20 micrometers.

HP:0011877.label: Increased mean platelet volume
HP:0011877.definition: Average platelet volume above the upper limit of the normal reference interval.
HP:0011877.comment: Mean platelet volume (MPV) is a measure of the average size of platelets, with a typical reference range of 7.5 to 11.5 femtoliters (fL).

HP:0011878.label: Abnormal platelet membrane protein expression
HP:0011878.definition: Presence of reduced amount of a membrane protein on the cell membrane of platelets. This feature is typically measured by flow cytometry.

HP:0011879.label: Decreased platelet glycoprotein Ib-IX-V
HP:0011879.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of the glycoprotein complex Ib-IX-V.
HP:0011879.comment: The glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex forms a specific platelet membrane adhesion receptor, which binds the adhesive glycoprotein, von Willebrand factor (vWF), in the vessel wall or plasma.

HP:0011880.label: Acute disseminated intravascular coagulation
HP:0011880.definition: An acute form of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Acute DIC can occur following sudden exposure of blood to procoagulants, with the compensatory hemostatic mechanisms becoming overwhelmed.

HP:0011881.label: Decreased platelet glycoprotein VI
HP:0011881.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of glycoprotein VI.
HP:0011881.comment: The glycoprotein VI is a glycoprotein receptor for collagen.

HP:0011882.label: Decreased platelet P2Y12 receptor
HP:0011882.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of P2Y12 receptor.
HP:0011882.comment: The P2Y12 receptor is activated by ADP and plays a central role in platelet activation.

HP:0011883.label: Abnormal platelet granules
HP:0011883.definition: An anomaly of alpha or dense granules or platelet lysosomes.
HP:0011883.comment: Platelets contain two classes of granule: the alpha granules and the dense granules. During platelet activation, the contents of the granules are discharged into the lumen of the open canalicular system, from which they are then released to the extracellular space.

HP:0011884.label: Abnormal umbilical stump bleeding
HP:0011884.definition: Abnormal bleeding of the umbilical stump following separation of the cord at approximately 7-10 days after birth.

HP:0011885.label: Hemorrhage of the eye
HP:0011885.definition: Bleeding from vessels of the various tissues of the eye.

HP:0011886.label: Hyphema
HP:0011886.definition: Bleeding in the anterior chamber of the eye.

HP:0011887.label: Choroid hemorrhage
HP:0011887.definition: Hemorrhage from the vessels of the choroid.

HP:0011888.label: Bleeding requiring red cell transfusion
HP:0011888.definition: Bleeding sufficiently severe as to require red cell transfusion (WHO Grade 3 or 4).

HP:0011889.label: Bleeding with minor or no trauma
HP:0011889.definition: Significant bleeding or hemorrhage without significant precipitating factor.
exact_synonyms: Bleeding with minor or no trauma

HP:0011890.label: Prolonged bleeding following procedure
HP:0011890.definition: Prolonged or protracted bleeding following an invasive procedure or intervention.

HP:0011891.label: Post-partum hemorrhage
HP:0011891.definition: Significant maternal hemorrhage/blood loss following deilvery of a child.

HP:0011892.label: Decreased circulating vitamin K concentration
HP:0011892.definition: The concentration of vitamin K in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0011893.label: Abnormal leukocyte count
HP:0011893.definition: Number of leukocytes per volume of blood beyond normal limits.

HP:0011894.label: Impaired thromboxane A2 agonist-induced platelet aggregation
HP:0011894.definition: Abnormal response to thromboxane as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of thromboxane A2 receptor agonists.

HP:0011895.label: Anemia due to reduced life span of red cells
HP:0011895.definition: A type of anemia related to a reduction in the average life span of red blood cells in the peripheral circulation, which is normally around 120 days.
exact_synonyms: Anaemia due to reduced life span of red cells

HP:0011896.label: Subconjunctival hemorrhage
HP:0011896.definition: Bleeding beneath the mucous membrane that lines the inner surface of the eyelid.

HP:0011897.label: Increased total neutrophil count
HP:0011897.definition: Abnormal increase of absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

HP:0011898.label: Abnormality of circulating fibrinogen
HP:0011898.definition: An abnormality of the level of activity of circulating fibrinogen.
HP:0011898.comment: Fibrinogen is an essential hemostatic factor that is converted to fibrin (a final product of the hemostatic pathway) by activated thrombin.

HP:0011899.label: Hyperfibrinogenemia
HP:0011899.definition: Increased concentration of fibrinogen in the blood.

HP:0011900.label: Hypofibrinogenemia
HP:0011900.definition: Decreased concentration of fibrinogen in the blood.

HP:0011902.label: Abnormal hemoglobin
HP:0011902.definition: Anomaly in the level or the function of hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein of erythrocytes.

HP:0011903.label: HbH hemoglobin
HP:0011903.definition: Hemoglobin H (HbH) contains four beta-globin chains. It is normally not present at all in blood, but may make up about 1-40 percent of all hemoglobin in HbH disease, a subform of alpha thalassemia.

HP:0011904.label: Persistence of hemoglobin F
HP:0011904.definition: Hemoglobin F (HbF) contains two globin alpha chains and two globin gamma chains. It is the main form of hemoglobin in the fetus during the last seven months of intrauterine development and in the half year of postnatal life. In adults it normally makes up less than one percent of all hemoglobin. This term refers to an increase in HbF above this limit. In beta thalassemia major, it may represent over 90 percent of all hemoglobin, and in beta thalassemia minor it may make up between 0.5 to 4 percent.

HP:0011905.label: Reduced hemoglobin A
HP:0011905.definition: Hemoglobin A (HbA) contains two globin alpha chains and two globin beta chains. HbA is normally the main adult hemoglobin, representing about 96-98 percent of all hemoglobin. This term represents a decreased in the proportion of HbA below this limit, and can be seen in various forms of thalassemia.

HP:0011906.label: Reduced beta/alpha synthesis ratio
HP:0011906.definition: A reduction in the ratio of production of beta globin to that of alpha globin. This is the major abnormality in the various forms of beta thalassemia.

HP:0011907.label: Reduced alpha/beta synthesis ratio
HP:0011907.definition: A reduction in the ratio of production of alpha globin to that of beta globin. This is the major abnormality in the various forms of alpha thalassemia.

HP:0011908.label: Unilateral radial aplasia
HP:0011908.definition: Missing radius bone on one side only associated with congenital failure of development.

HP:0011909.label: Flattened metacarpal heads
HP:0011909.definition: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metacarpal bones.
HP:0011909.comment: The metacarpal heads articulate with the proximal phalanges of the fingers.
exact_synonyms: Flattened head of long bone of hand

HP:0011910.label: Shortening of all phalanges of fingers
HP:0011910.definition: Abnormal reduction in length affecting all phalanges.

HP:0011911.label: Abnormal metacarpophalangeal joint morphology
HP:0011911.definition: An anomaly of a metacarpophalangeal joint.

HP:0011912.label: Abnormality of the glenoid fossa
HP:0011912.definition: An anomaly of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.

HP:0011913.label: Lumbar hypertrichosis
HP:0011913.definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the lumbar region.

HP:0011914.label: Thoracic hypertrichosis
HP:0011914.definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the thoracic region.

HP:0011915.label: Cardiovascular calcification
HP:0011915.definition: Abnormal calcification in the cardiovascular system.

HP:0011916.label: Toe extensor amyotrophy
HP:0011916.definition: Atrophy of the extensor digitorum longus muscles, which mediate extension of the toes.

HP:0011918.label: Clinodactyly of the 4th toe
HP:0011918.definition: Bending or curvature of a fourth toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

HP:0011919.label: Pleural empyema
HP:0011919.definition: Accumulation of pus in the pleural cavity.

HP:0011920.label: Transudative pleural effusion
HP:0011920.definition: A type of pleural effusion with a transudate (extravascular fluid with low protein content and a low specific gravity). Pleural effusions can be classified as transudates or exudates based on Light's criteria, which classify an effusion as exudate if one or more of the following are present: (1) the ratio of pleural fluid protein to serum protein is greater than 0.5, (2) the ratio of pleural fluid lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) to serum LDH is greater than 0.6, or (3) the pleural fluid LDH level is greater than two thirds of the upper limit of normal for serum LDH.
HP:0011920.comment: Transudates result from imbalances in hydrostatic and oncotic forces and are caused by a limited number of recognized clinical conditions such as heart failure and cirrhosis. Less common causes include nephrotic syndrome, atelectasis, peritoneal dialysis, constrictive pericarditis, superior vena caval obstruction, and urinothorax.

HP:0011921.label: Exudative pleural effusion
HP:0011921.definition: A type of pleural effusion with a exudate (extravascular fluid that has exuded out of a tissue or its capillaries due to injury or inflammation). Pleural effusions can be classified as transudates or exudates based on Light's criteria, which classify an effusion as exudate if one or more of the following are present: (1) the ratio of pleural fluid protein to serum protein is greater than 0.5, (2) the ratio of pleural fluid lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) to serum LDH is greater than 0.6, or (3) the pleural fluid LDH level is greater than two thirds of the upper limit of normal for serum LDH.
HP:0011921.comment: Transudates result from pneumonia, malignancy, thromboembolism, and other causes.

HP:0011922.label: Abnormal activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain
HP:0011922.definition: An increased or decreased activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.

HP:0011923.label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I
HP:0011923.definition: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.

HP:0011924.label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex III
HP:0011924.definition: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.

HP:0011925.label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial ATP synthase complex
HP:0011925.definition: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial proton-transporting ATP synthase complex, which makes ATP via oxidative phosphorylation, and is sometimes described as Complex V of the electron transport chain.
exact_synonyms: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex V

HP:0011926.label: Proximal placement of hallux
HP:0011926.definition: Proximal mislocalization of the big toe from its normal position.
HP:0011926.comment: Thumb placement index greater than 0.55; or, the base of the thumb appears closer to the wrist than is typical. The technique for the thumb placement index is described in detail [Malina et al., 1973; Hall et al., 2007]. Briefly, the thumb placement index is the distance from the proximal crease of the index finger to the angle of the first interdigital space divided by the distance from the proximal crease of the index finger to the wrist flexion crease at the base of the thumb. This term should not be used with Preaxial polydactyly.

HP:0011927.label: Short digit
HP:0011927.definition: One or more digit that appears disproportionately short compared to the hand/foot, whereby either the entire digit or a specific phalanx is shortened.
HP:0011927.comment: Note that the term brachydactyly is reserved for specific patterns of short digits, see HP:0001156.

HP:0011928.label: Short proximal phalanx of toe
HP:0011928.definition: Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of proximal phalanx of toe.

HP:0011929.label: Hypersegmentation of proximal phalanx of third finger
HP:0011929.definition: Presence of an additional phalanx-like bone, producing an extra, wedge-shaped bone at the base of the proximal phalanx of the third finger.
HP:0011929.comment: This anomaly is characteristic for brachydactyly type C.

HP:0011931.label: Abnormal cerebellar peduncle morphology
HP:0011931.definition: An anomaly of the cerebellar peduncles. The superior, middle, and inferior cerebellar peduncles emerge from the cerebellum. The superior cerebellar penduncles connect the cerebellum to the midbrain, the middle cerebellar peduncles connect the cerebellum to the pons, and the inferior cerebellar peduncle connects the medulla spinalis and medulla oblongata with the cerebellum.

HP:0011932.label: Abnormal superior cerebellar peduncle morphology
HP:0011932.definition: An anomaly of the superior cerebellar peduncle.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the superior cerebellar peduncle

HP:0011933.label: Elongated superior cerebellar peduncle
HP:0011933.definition: Increased length of the superior cerebellar peduncle.

HP:0011934.label: Dilatation of mesenteric artery
HP:0011934.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the inferior mesenteric artery or superior mesenteric artery .
HP:0011934.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0011935.label: Decreased urinary urate
HP:0011935.definition: Decreased concentration of urate in the urine.
HP:0011935.comment: Xanthine oxidase oxidizes oxypurines such as xanthine and hypoxanthine to uric acid. Uric acid is the final oxidation product of purine catabolism.

HP:0011936.label: Decreased plasma total carnitine
HP:0011936.definition: A decreased concentration of total carnitine in the blood.

HP:0011937.label: Hypoplastic fifth toenail
HP:0011937.definition: Underdeveloped nails of the fifth toes.

HP:0011939.label: 3-4 finger cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0011939.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between fingers 3 and 4.

HP:0011940.label: Anterior wedging of T12
HP:0011940.definition: An abnormality of the shape of the thoracic vertebra T12 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).
exact_synonyms: Anterior wedging of the 12th thoracic vertebra

HP:0011941.label: Anterior wedging of L2
HP:0011941.definition: An abnormality of the shape of the lumbar vertebra L2 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).

HP:0011942.label: Increased urinary sulfite level
HP:0011942.definition: The concentration of SO3(2-), i.e., sulfite, in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0011943.label: Increased urinary thiosulfate
HP:0011943.definition: Increased concentration of thiosulfate(2-) in the urine.

HP:0011944.label: Small vessel vasculitis
HP:0011944.definition: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) that affects blood vessels that are smaller than arteries, i.e., arterioles, venules, and capilllaries.

HP:0011945.label: Bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia
HP:0011945.definition: Bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP) is and interstitial lung abnormalitiy characterized histopathologically by plugs of granulation tissue lying within small airways, alveolar ducts, and alveoli and by chronic inflammatory cell infiltration in alveolar walls. Patients with BOOP generally present with subacute illness, including shortness of breath, fever, malaise, and weight loss.

HP:0011946.label: Bronchiolitis obliterans
HP:0011946.definition: Inflammation and fibrosis of the bronchioles leading to partial or complete obstruction of these airways.
HP:0011946.comment: Note that Bronchiolitis obliterans is not to be confused with the similarly named feature Bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia.

HP:0011947.label: Respiratory tract infection
HP:0011947.definition: An infection of the upper or lower respiratory tract.

HP:0011948.label: Recurrent acute respiratory tract infection
HP:0011948.definition: A history of repeated acute infections of the upper or lower respiratory tract.

HP:0011949.label: Acute infectious pneumonia
HP:0011949.definition: Acute inflammation of the lung due to an infection.

HP:0011951.label: Aspiration pneumonia
HP:0011951.definition: Pneumonia due to the aspiration (breathing in) of food, liquid, or gastric contents into the upper respiratory tract.

HP:0011952.label: Acute aspiration pneumonia
HP:0011952.definition: An acute episode of pneumonia due to the aspiration (breathing in) of food, liquid, or gastric contents into the upper respiratory tract.

HP:0011954.label: Nodular regenerative hyperplasia of liver
HP:0011954.definition: Diffuse benign transformation of the hepatic parenchyma into small regenerative nodules with minimal or no fibrosis.

HP:0011955.label: Hepatic granulomatosis
HP:0011955.definition: The presence of multiple granulomas in the liver as based on pathological examination. Granulomas are small 0.5 to 2 mm collections of modified macrophages called epithelioid cells usually surrounded by lymphocytes.

HP:0011956.label: Intestinal lymphoid nodular hyperplasia
HP:0011956.definition: A lymphoproliferative abnormality of the intestine characterized by numerous visible mucosal nodules measuring up to, and rarely exceeding, 0.5 cm in diameter Histologically, hyperplastic lymphoid follicles with large germinal centers are seen in the lamina propria and superficial submucosa. There is enlargement of the mucosal B cell follicles caused by hyperplasia of the follicle centers; surrounded by a normal appearing mantle zone. Disease may involve the stomach, the entire small intestine, and the large intestine.

HP:0011957.label: Abnormal pectoral muscle morphology
HP:0011957.definition: An abnormality of the pectoral muscle, comprising the pectoralis major, a thick, fan-shaped muscle of the anterior chest and the pectoralis minor, a thin, triangular muscle situated underneath the pectoralis major.

HP:0011958.label: Retinal perforation
HP:0011958.definition: A hole through the whole thickness of the retina, associated with trauma.
HP:0011958.comment: Retinal perforations can be cause by inflammation, trauma, degeneration, or other factors, and comprise retinal breaks, tears, dialyses, and holes.

HP:0011959.label: Unilateral hypoplasia of pectoralis major muscle
HP:0011959.definition: Hypoplasia (underdevelopment) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.
exact_synonyms: Underdeveloped pec muscle on one side
Small pec muscle on one side

HP:0011960.label: Substantia nigra gliosis
HP:0011960.definition: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the substantia nigra.

HP:0011961.label: Non-obstructive azoospermia
HP:0011961.definition: Absence of any measurable level of sperm in his semen, resulting from a defect in the production of spermatozoa in the testes. This can be differentiated from obstructive azoospermia on the basis of testicular biopsy.

HP:0011962.label: Obstructive azoospermia
HP:0011962.definition: Absence of any measurable level of sperm in his semen, resulting from post-testicular obstruction or retrograde ejaculation. This can be differentiated from obstructive azoospermia on the basis of testicular biopsy.

HP:0011963.label: Pretesticular azoospermia
HP:0011963.definition: Absence of any measurable level of sperm in his semen, due to a hypothalamic or pituitary abnormality diagnosed with hypo-gonadotropic-hypogonadism. The diagnosis is made on the basis of low LH and FSH levels and low or normal testosterone levels.

HP:0011964.label: Intermittent painful muscle spasms
HP:0011964.definition: History of repeated intermittent involuntary muscle contractions that were painful.

HP:0011965.label: Abnormal circulating citrulline concentration
HP:0011965.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of citrulline in the blood circulation.
HP:0011965.comment: Citrulline is an alpha-amino acid that is a key intermediate in the urea cycle.

HP:0011966.label: Elevated plasma citrulline
HP:0011966.definition: An increased concentration of citrulline in the blood.

HP:0011967.label: Decreased circulating copper concentration
HP:0011967.definition: A reduced concentration of copper in the blood.

HP:0011968.label: Feeding difficulties
HP:0011968.definition: Impaired ability to eat related to problems gathering food and getting ready to suck, chew, or swallow it.
HP:0011968.comment: Difficulties with eating and drinking, resulting in decreased oral nutrition

HP:0011969.label: Elevated circulating luteinizing hormone level
HP:0011969.definition: An elevated concentration of luteinizing hormone in the blood.

HP:0011970.label: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
HP:0011970.definition: Amyloid deposition in the walls of leptomeningeal and cortical arteries, arterioles, and less often capillaries and veins of the central nervous system.
HP:0011970.comment: Vascular beta-amyloid deposition in the walls of small to medium-sized, blood vessels (mostly arterial) of the central nervous system. Cerebral amyloid angiopathy mostly occurs in the sporadic form in the elderly, while rare familial forms occur in younger patients and are generally lead to more severe clinical manifestations. Extracellular deposition of the amyloid protein in the brain is associated with neurologic and physiological disease progression.

HP:0011971.label: Dermatographic urticaria
HP:0011971.definition: An exaggerated whealing tendency when the skin is stroked, that is, formation of red, itchy bumps and lines on the skin as a result of pressure on the skin (for instance, stroking the skin with a pen or tongue depressor).

HP:0011972.label: Hypoglycorrhachia
HP:0011972.definition: Abnormally low glucose concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid.
exact_synonyms: Low glucose levels in cerebral spinal fluid

HP:0011973.label: Paroxysmal lethargy
HP:0011973.definition: Repeated episodes of sudden-onset and transient lethargy.

HP:0011974.label: Myelofibrosis
HP:0011974.definition: Replacement of bone marrow by fibrous tissue.

HP:0011975.label: Aminoglycoside-induced hearing loss
HP:0011975.definition: Partial or complete loss of hearing following ingestion of aminoglycoside antibiotics.
HP:0011975.comment: The ototoxicity of aminoglycoside antibiotics is related to the destruction of sensory hair cells in the cochlea and vestibular labyrinth.

HP:0011976.label: Elevated urinary catecholamine level
HP:0011976.definition: The concentration of a catecholamine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0011977.label: Elevated urinary homovanillic acid
HP:0011977.definition: An increased concentration of homovanillic acid in the urine.
HP:0011977.comment: Homovanillic acid is the main metabolite produced from dopamine degradation by the action of monoamine oxidase. Increased levels of catecholamines or catecholamine metabolites, including dopamine, homovanillic acid (HVA) and/or vanillylmandelic acid (VMA), can be detected in the urine of 90% of all patients with neuroblastoma.

HP:0011978.label: Elevated urinary vanillylmandelic acid
HP:0011978.definition: An increased concentration of vanillylmandelic acid in the urine.

HP:0011979.label: Elevated urinary dopamine level
HP:0011979.definition: The concentration of dopamine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0011980.label: Cholesterol gallstones
HP:0011980.definition: Gallstones composed primarily of cholesterol, usually about 2-3 cm in length with an oval form and a yellow or green/brown color.

HP:0011981.label: Pigment gallstones
HP:0011981.definition: Gallstones composed primarily of bilirubin and calcium salts (calcium bilirubinate) with a low cholesterol concentration.

HP:0011982.label: Black pigment gallstones
HP:0011982.definition: A type of pigment gallstone that is hard and black, containing calcium carbonate and calcium phosphates.

HP:0011983.label: Brown pigment gallstones
HP:0011983.definition: A type of pigment gallstone that is brown, containing calcium fatty acids. These stones are softer than black pigment gallstones.

HP:0011984.label: Atretic gallbladder
HP:0011984.definition: Failure of formation of the lumen of the gallbladder, often associated with gallbladder hypoplasia.

HP:0011985.label: Acholic stools
HP:0011985.definition: Clay colored stools lacking bile pigment.

HP:0011986.label: Ectopic ossification
HP:0011986.definition: Formation of abnormal, extraskeletal bony tissue, i.e., the presence of bone in soft tissue where bone normally does not exist.

HP:0011987.label: Ectopic ossification in muscle tissue
HP:0011987.definition: Formation of abnormal bony tissue within muscle tissue.

HP:0011988.label: Ectopic ossification in tendon tissue
HP:0011988.definition: Formation of abnormal bony tissue within tendon tissue.

HP:0011989.label: Ectopic ossification in ligament tissue
HP:0011989.definition: Formation of abnormal bony tissue within ligament tissue.

HP:0011990.label: Abnormal neutrophil physiology
HP:0011990.comment: Abnormal response of granulocytes to stimuli.

HP:0011991.label: Abnormal total neutrophil count
HP:0011991.definition: A deviation from the normal range of neutrophil cell counts in the circulation.

HP:0011992.label: Abnormal neutrophil morphology
HP:0011992.definition: An abnormal form or size of neutrophils.

HP:0011993.label: Impaired neutrophil bactericidal activity
HP:0011993.definition: A reduction in the ability of neutrophils to kill bacteria.

HP:0011994.label: Abnormal atrial septum morphology
HP:0011994.definition: An abnormality of the interatrial septum.

HP:0011995.label: Atrial septal dilatation
HP:0011995.definition: A bulging of the interatrial septum towards one side. In adults, atrial septal aneurysm can be defined as a protrusion of the aneurysm of >10 mm beyond the plane of the atrial septum as measured by transesophageal echocardiography.
HP:0011995.comment: Atrial septal aneurysm formation may be secondary to raised interatrial pressure gradients, producing a bulging septal shift toward the low-pressure side. However, it has been also found in patients with normal atrial pressures, suggesting a primary (congenital) malformation.

HP:0011996.label: Elevated coagulation factor V activity
HP:0011996.definition: Increased activity of coagulation factor V, Factor V, which is activated to factor Va by means of minute amounts of thrombin (and inactivated by larger amounts of thrombin). Activated factor V (fVa) is a cofactor in the formation of the prothrombinase complex.

HP:0011997.label: Postprandial hyperlactemia
HP:0011997.definition: Abnormally increased level of blood lactate following a meal.

HP:0011998.label: Postprandial hyperglycemia
HP:0011998.definition: An increased concentration of glucose in the blood following a meal.

HP:0011999.label: Paranoia
HP:0011999.definition: The feeling and belief that one is being targeted or is a focus of negative or untoward actions, overt or covert, from others. The affected individual expresses a concern that people are in general against the individual and are engaging in subtle behaviors to make things difficult for them. The origins of such thinking may arise from real events and become amplified over time. Paranoia may also arise in the absence of any action or interaction between the person and their environment.
HP:0011999.comment: Paranoia is defined as a non-delusional state characterized by a vague sense that 'everyone and anyone' is unfavorable towards one as in 'the whole world hates me'. A persecutory delusion is, in contrast, typically fixed and focused - as in 'my neighbor is pumping poison into my house'.

HP:0012000.label: EEG with generalized spikes
HP:0012000.definition: EEG with generalized sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec.

HP:0012001.label: EEG with generalized polyspikes
HP:0012001.definition: EEG with repetitive generalized sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec.

HP:0012002.label: Experiential epileptic aura
HP:0012002.definition: Affective, mnemonic or composite perceptual auras with subjective qualities similar to those experienced in life but are recognized by the subject as occurring outside of actual context.

HP:0012003.label: Affective epileptic aura
HP:0012003.definition: Affective auras with subjective qualities similar to those experienced in life but are recognized by the subject as occurring outside of actual context.

HP:0012004.label: Focal cognitive seizure with deja vu/jamais vu
HP:0012004.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by memory phenomena such as feelings of familiarity (deja vu) and unfamiliarity (jamais vu) as the initial semiological manifestation.
HP:0012004.comment: See the Glossary of Descriptive Terminology for Ictal Semiology at http://www.ilae.org.

HP:0012005.label: Deja vu aura
HP:0012005.definition: A subjective feeling that an experience which is occurring for the first time has been experienced before.

HP:0012006.label: Jamais vu aura
HP:0012006.definition: A subjective feeling that an experience which has occurred before is being experienced for the first time.

HP:0012007.label: Focal cognitive seizure with hallucination
HP:0012007.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by hallucination as the initial semiological manifestation.
HP:0012007.comment: Hallucination is the creation of composite perceptions without the presence of external sensory stimuli, these may be visual (e.g. formed images), auditory (e.g. hearing voices) or involve other sensory modalities, without change in awareness. The sensory phenomena may be accompanied by associated emotion or interpretation e.g. a formed visual image may be accompanied by fear, or may be experienced as persecutory or with paranoia (i.e. with unjustified suspicion / mistrust). These features distinguish focal seizures with hallucinations from focal sensory seizures.

HP:0012008.label: Focal cognitive seizure with illusion
HP:0012008.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by an alteration of actual perception involving visual, auditory, somatosensory, olfactory, and/or gustatory phenomena as the initial semiological manifestation.

HP:0012009.label: EEG with central focal spike waves
HP:0012009.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the central region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0012010.label: EEG with frontal focal spike waves
HP:0012010.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the frontal region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0012011.label: EEG with occipital focal spike waves
HP:0012011.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the occipital region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0012012.label: EEG with parietal focal spike waves
HP:0012012.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the parietal region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0012013.label: EEG with temporal focal spike waves
HP:0012013.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the temporal region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0012014.label: EEG with central focal spikes
HP:0012014.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec in the central region.

HP:0012015.label: EEG with frontal focal spikes
HP:0012015.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec in the frontal region.

HP:0012016.label: EEG with occipital focal spikes
HP:0012016.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec in the occipital region.

HP:0012017.label: EEG with parietal focal spikes
HP:0012017.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec in the parietal region.

HP:0012018.label: EEG with temporal focal spikes
HP:0012018.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec in the temporal region.

HP:0012019.label: Lens luxation
HP:0012019.definition: Complete dislocation of the lens of the eye.

HP:0012020.label: Right aortic arch
HP:0012020.definition: Aorta descends on right instead of on the left.
HP:0012020.comment: The are several types of right aortic arch (RAA). RAA can recognized radiographically by leftward displacement of barium-filled esophagus or of an air-filled trachea. The aortic knob is absent from left side, and the para-aortic stripe returns to left side of spine just above diaphragm.

HP:0012021.label: Persistent patent ductus venosus
HP:0012021.definition: Persistence of blood flow through the ductus venosus for longer than the normal time after birth.
HP:0012021.comment: The ductus venosus is a bypass between the umbilical vein and the inferior vena cava in the fetus. The blood flow through this bypass decreases immediately after birth. Functional closure, which is followed by anatomic closure, is virtually complete within a few weeks of birth.

HP:0012022.label: Congenital portosystemic venous shunt
HP:0012022.definition: A congenital defect of the vasculature such that there is a shunt (by-pass) of blood directly from the portal vein to the vena cava (i.e., the blood from the portal vein is not filtered through the liver).

HP:0012023.label: Galactosuria
HP:0012023.definition: Elevated concentration of galactose in the urine.

HP:0012024.label: Hypergalactosemia
HP:0012024.definition: Elevated concentration of galactose in the blood.
HP:0012024.comment: Hypergalactosemia is used here to mean the increased concentration of galactose in the blood. Note that the word galactosemia is occasionally used with the same meaning but more commonly denotes the disease entity called galactosemia caused by mutations in the galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase gene (MIM:230400).

HP:0012025.label: Abnormal circulating ornithine concentration
HP:0012025.definition: Deviation from the normal concentration of ornithine in the blood circulation.
HP:0012025.comment: Ornithine is an amino acid produced in the urea cycle by the splitting off of urea from arginine. Ornithine is a naturally occurring, non-proteinogenic amino acid found in meat, fish, dairy and eggs.

HP:0012026.label: Hyperornithinemia
HP:0012026.definition: Increased concentration of ornithine in the blood.

HP:0012027.label: Laryngeal edema
HP:0012027.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid and swelling in the tissues of the larynx.

HP:0012028.label: Hepatocellular adenoma
HP:0012028.definition: A benign tumor of the liver of presumably epithelial origin.

HP:0012029.label: Abnormal urine hormone level
HP:0012029.definition: An abnormal concentration of a hormone in the urine.

HP:0012030.label: Increased urinary cortisol level
HP:0012030.definition: Abnormally increased concentration of cortisol in the urine.

HP:0012032.label: Lipoma
HP:0012032.definition: Benign neoplasia derived from lipoblasts or lipocytes of white or brown fat. May be angiomatous or hibernomatous.

HP:0012033.label: Sacral lipoma
HP:0012033.definition: Presence of a lipoma in the region of the sacrum.
HP:0012033.comment: For an example, see Figure 1 of PMID:30264029.

HP:0012034.label: Liposarcoma
HP:0012034.definition: Malignant neoplasms which probably originate in primitive mesenchymal stem cell populations differentiating down a lipomatous pathway.

HP:0012035.label: Steatocystoma multiplex
HP:0012035.definition: Multiple, localized or widespread, asymptomatic or inflammatory dermal cysts involving the pilosebaceous units. Lesions can appear anywhere on the body, but steatocystoma multiplex is more commonly involved with those areas of the skin with a high density of developed pilosebaceous units (e.g., the axilla, groin, neck, and proximal extremities).
HP:0012035.comment: Steatocystoma multiplex can present with localized, generalized, facial, acral, or suppurative involvement.

HP:0012036.label: Sternocleidomastoid amyotrophy
HP:0012036.definition: Wasting of the sternocleidomastoid muscle, the muscle in the anterior part of the neck that acts to flex and rotate the head.

HP:0012037.label: Pectoralis amyotrophy
HP:0012037.definition: Wasting of the pectoral muscles, i.e., of the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor. This finding is often manifested by prominent axillary creases or double axillary creases.

HP:0012038.label: Corneal guttata
HP:0012038.definition: Corneal guttata are droplet-like accumulations of non-banded collagen on the posterior surface of Descemet's membrane. The presence of focal thickenings of Descemet's membrane histologically named guttae. Cornea guttata can be easily diagnosed in vivo and ex vivo by means of specular microscopy as it gives dark areas where no endothelial cells are visible.
HP:0012038.comment: Corneal guttata are often observed in elderly people and are known to be associated with Fuchs corneal endothelial dystrophy, and also with trauma, congenital glaucoma, and macular dystrophy.

HP:0012039.label: Descemet Membrane Folds
HP:0012039.definition: Presence of folds in the Descemet membrane, which is the basement membrane of the endothelial (inner) cell layer of the cornea. Descemet membrane folds are generally a manifestation of inflammation or edema of the cornea.

HP:0012040.label: Corneal stromal edema
HP:0012040.definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid and swelling of the stroma of cornea.

HP:0012042.label: Aspirin-induced asthma
HP:0012042.definition: A type of asthma in which aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that inhibit cyclooxygen-ase 1 (COX-1) exacerbate bronchoconstriction.

HP:0012043.label: Pendular nystagmus
HP:0012043.definition: Rhythmic, involuntary sinusoidal oscillations of one or both eyes. The waveform of pendular nystagmus may occur in any direction.

HP:0012044.label: Seesaw nystagmus
HP:0012044.definition: Seesaw nystagmus is a type of pendular nystagmus where a half cycle consists of the elevation and intorsion of one eye, concurrently with the depression and extortion of the fellow eye. In the other half cycle, there is an inversion of the ocular movements.
HP:0012044.comment: Seesaw nystagmus can be a manifestation of lesions of the optic chiasma.

HP:0012045.label: Retinal flecks
HP:0012045.definition: Presence of multiple yellowish-white lesions of various size and configuration on the retina not related to vascular lesions.

HP:0012046.label: Areflexia of upper limbs
HP:0012046.definition: Inability to elicit tendon reflexes in the upper limbs.

HP:0012047.label: Hemeralopia
HP:0012047.definition: A visual defect characterized by the inability to see as clearly in bright light as in dim light. The word hemeralopia literally means day blindness.

HP:0012048.label: Oromandibular dystonia
HP:0012048.definition: A kind of focal dystonia characterized by forceful contractions of the face, jaw, and/or tongue causing difficulty in opening and closing the mouth and often affecting chewing and speech.

HP:0012049.label: Laryngeal dystonia
HP:0012049.definition: A form of focal dystonia that affects the vocal cords, associated with involuntary contractions of the vocal cords causing interruptions of speech and affecting the voice quality and often leading to patterned, repeated breaks in speech.

HP:0012050.label: Anasarca
HP:0012050.definition: An extreme form of generalized edema with widespread and massive edema due to effusion of fluid into the extracellular space.

HP:0012051.label: Reactive hypoglycemia
HP:0012051.definition: Hypoglycermia following a meal (or more generally, after intake of glucose).
HP:0012051.comment: Reactive hypoglycemia may be the result of an exaggerated insulin response.
exact_synonyms: Low blood sugar after a meal

HP:0012052.label: Low serum calcitriol
HP:0012052.definition: A reduced concentration of calcitriol in the blood. Calcitriol is also known as 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol or 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3.

HP:0012053.label: Decreased circulating calcifediol concentration
HP:0012053.definition: A reduced concentration of calcifediol in the blood. Calcifediol is also known as calcidiol, 25-hydroxycholecalciferol and 25-Hydroxyvitamin D3.

HP:0012054.label: Choroidal melanoma
HP:0012054.definition: Malignant tumor of melanocytes of the choroid. The classic appearance of choroidal melanoma is a pigmented dome-shaped or collar button-shaped tumor with an associated exudative retinal detachment. Choroidal melanoma is usually pigmented, but can be variably pigmented and even amelanotic (non-pigmented).

HP:0012055.label: Ciliary body melanoma
HP:0012055.definition: Malignant tumor of melanocytes of the ciliary body.

HP:0012056.label: Cutaneous melanoma
HP:0012056.definition: The presence of a melanoma of the skin.
HP:0012056.comment: The phenotypic presentation of melanomas is often described using the ABCDE mnemomic: A) Asymmetry; B) Borders of the lesion are irregular; C) Color changes from one area of the lesion to another, with shades of tan, brown, or black, and sometimes white, red, or blue; D) Diameter of the lesionis usually larger than 6 mm; E) Evolution of the appearance of the lesion with time. These rules do not, however, apply to every melanoma.

HP:0012057.label: Superficial spreading melanoma
HP:0012057.definition: A type of melanoma that is flat and irregular in shape and color, with different shades of black and brown.

HP:0012058.label: Nodular melanoma
HP:0012058.definition: A type of melanoma that starts as a raised area that is usually dark blackish-blue or bluish-red but may not have any color.

HP:0012059.label: Lentigo maligna melanoma
HP:0012059.definition: A subtype of melanoma in situ that typically develops on sun-damaged skin. The lesion is typically a large, irregularly pigmented macule that has developed from an ordinary lentigo (a small pigmented spot on the skin with a clearly-defined edge). Change to a malignant lentigo typically takes place over 20 years or more, and many patients accept the change as a consequence of aging.

HP:0012060.label: Acral lentiginous melanoma
HP:0012060.definition: A type of cutaneous melanoma localized to the palm, sole, or beneath the nail (subungual melanoma). Acral lentiginous melanoma starts as a slowly-enlarging flat patch of discolored skin and usually displays a size above 6 mm and often several centimeters or more in diameter upon diagnosis and variable pigmentation with a mixutre of colors including brown, and blue-grey, black and red. The surface of the lesion is initially smooth but later in the course may become thicker and irregular, and may ulcerate or bleed.

HP:0012061.label: Urinary excretion of sialylated oligosaccharides
HP:0012061.definition: Excretion of oligosaccharides conjugated to sialic acid in the urine.

HP:0012062.label: Bone cyst
HP:0012062.definition: A fluid filled cavity that develops with a bone.
HP:0012062.comment: Many bone cysts are asymptomatic. However, larger cysts can make the bone more susceptible to fracture.

HP:0012063.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
HP:0012063.definition: Radiographic features include a dilated, radiolucent lesion typically located eccentrically within the metaphyseal portion of the bone, with fluid levels visible on magnetic resonance imaging.

HP:0012064.label: Unicameral bone cyst
HP:0012064.definition: A benign fluid filled simple cyst of bone filled with serous fluid.

HP:0012065.label: Multiple bony cystic lesions
HP:0012065.definition: Presence of multiple cystic changes in multiple areas or multiple bones.

HP:0012066.label: Increased urinary disaccharide excretion
HP:0012066.definition: Increased concentration of disaccharide in the urine.
HP:0012066.comment: Excess amount of disaccharides such as mannosyl-N-acetylglucosamine excreted in the urine.

HP:0012067.label: Glycopeptiduria
HP:0012067.definition: Increased excretion of glycopeptides in the urine. Glycopeptides are peptides with carbohydrate moieties covalently attached to the side chains of the amino acid residues.
HP:0012067.comment: This feature is often the result of a defect in glycosidase activate. Glycosidases catalyze the release of sugar moieties.

HP:0012068.label: Aspartylglucosaminuria
HP:0012068.definition: Excretion of excess amounts of aspartylglucosamine in the urine.

HP:0012069.label: Keratan sulfate excretion in urine
HP:0012069.definition: An increased concentration of keratan sulfate in the urine.
HP:0012069.comment: Keratan sulfate is a a glycosaminoglycan.

HP:0012070.label: Chondroitin sulfate excretion in urine
HP:0012070.definition: An increased concentration of chondroitin sulfate (CHEBI:37397) in the urine.
HP:0012070.comment: Chondroitin sulfate refers to a class of 10-60 kDa glycosaminoglycan sulfates, which are widely distributed in cartilage.

HP:0012071.label: Abnormal circulating acylcarnitine concentration
HP:0012071.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of an acylcarnitine, which is produced by reversible esterification of the 3-hydroxyl group of carnitine.
HP:0012071.comment: Acylcarnitines are esters of l-carnitine and fatty acids. Therefore, it is inferred that the number of acylcarnitines that may be formed with these fatty acids is very considerable. Similar to fatty acids, acylcarnitines are also differed by length of the acyl groups, often categorized as short, medium and long-chain acylcarnitines (simply marked as SCACs, MCACs and LCACs). Carnitine fundergoes reversible esterification of its 3-hydroxyl group producing acylcarnitine, which can enter the mitochondria with the assistance of specific translocases.

HP:0012072.label: Aciduria
HP:0012072.definition: Excretion of urine with an acid pH, i.e., having an increased hydrogen ion concentration.

HP:0012073.label: Abnormal urinary acylglycine profile
HP:0012073.definition: An abnormal distribution of N-acylglycines in the urine. There are numerous different N-acylglycines, and this term refers to pathological alterations in their level or distribution.
HP:0012073.comment: N-acylglycines result from glycine conjugation with exogenous compounds to enhance their excretion in urine. Glycine conjugation is also an effective detoxification system for preventing accumulation of acyl-CoA esters in several inherited metabolic disorders.

HP:0012074.label: Tonic pupil
HP:0012074.definition: An abnormality of the pupillary light reaction characterized by a marked slowing of the light reaction of usually just one pupil. The pupil tends to be relatively dilated, and there is reduced accommodation.

HP:0012075.label: Personality disorder
HP:0012075.definition: A personality disorder is a deeply ingrained pattern of behavior of a specified kind that deviates markedly from the norms of generally accepted behavior. It is typically apparent by the time of adolescence and causes long-term difficulties in personal relationships or functioning in society.
HP:0012075.comment: A personality disorder is generally associated with significant problems and limitations in relationships, social encounters, work, and school. It usually manifests since childhood or adolescence and continues throughout adulthood.

HP:0012076.label: Borderline personality disorder
HP:0012076.definition: A personality disorder characterized by impulsive behavior and unpredictable, capricious mood. Affected individuals show a tendency to have outbursts of emotion and an inability to control these behavioral explosions. They generally experience an intense fear of abandonment or instability and also struggle with feelings of emptiness.

HP:0012077.label: Histrionic personality disorder
HP:0012077.definition: A personality disorder characterized by shallow and labile affectivity, self-dramatization, theatricality, exaggerated expression of emotions, suggestibility, egocentricity, self-indulgence, lack of consideration for others, easily hurt feelings, and continuous seeking for appreciation, excitement and attention.

HP:0012078.label: Motor conduction block
HP:0012078.definition: Blockade of impulses at a focal site along the course of a motor axon.

HP:0012079.label: Abnormality of central motor conduction
HP:0012079.definition: Any anomaly of the conduction of motor nerve impulses in the central nervous system.
HP:0012079.comment: Nerve conduction velocity in the central motor pathways of the brain and spinal cord can be studied by methods including transcutaneous electrical stimulation of the cortex, cervical cord, thoracic cord and conus medullaris and determination of motor latencies to various muscles. This measure is thought to represent conduction in large diameter fibers in the corticospinal tracts.

HP:0012080.label: Cerebellar granular layer atrophy
HP:0012080.definition: Atrophy of the cerebellum affecting primarily the granular cell layer.

HP:0012081.label: Enlarged cerebellum
HP:0012081.definition: An abnormally increased size of the cerebellum compared to other brain structures.

HP:0012082.label: Cerebellar Purkinje layer atrophy
HP:0012082.definition: Atrophy of the cerebellum affecting primarily the Purkinje cell layer.

HP:0012083.label: Ubiquitin-positive cerebral inclusion bodies
HP:0012083.definition: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates that show positive staining with antibodies against ubiquitin within cells of the brain.

HP:0012084.label: Abnormality of skeletal muscle fiber size
HP:0012084.definition: Any abnormality of the size of the skeletal muscle cell.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of skeletal muscle fibre size

HP:0012085.label: Pyuria
HP:0012085.definition: The presence of 10 or more white cells per cubic millimeter in a urine specimen, 3 or more white cells per high-power field of unspun urine, a positive result on Gram staining of an unspun urine specimen, or a urinary dipstick test that is positive for leukocyte esterase.

HP:0012086.label: Abnormal urinary color
HP:0012086.definition: An abnormal color of the urine, that is, the color of the urine appears different from the usual straw-yellow color.

HP:0012087.label: Abnormal mitochondrial shape
HP:0012087.definition: An anomaly in the surface contour of mitochondria.

HP:0012088.label: Abnormal urinary odor
HP:0012088.definition: A deviation from the normal odor of the urine.
HP:0012088.comment: Urine does not usually have a strong smell, but the odor may be altered by a number of factors including some diseases. Foul-smelling urine may be due to bacteria that have caused a urinary tract infection. Sweet-smelling urine may be a sign of uncontrolled diabetes or more rarely a disease of metabolism. Liver disease and certain metabolic disorders may cause musty-smelling urine.

HP:0012091.label: Abnormality of pancreas physiology
HP:0012091.definition: An anomaly of the function of the pancreas.

HP:0012092.label: Abnormality of exocrine pancreas physiology
HP:0012092.definition: A functional anomaly of the acinar gland portion of the pancreas that secretes digestive enzymes.

HP:0012093.label: Abnormality of endocrine pancreas physiology
HP:0012093.definition: A function abnormality of the endocrine pancreas.

HP:0012094.label: Abnormal pancreas size
HP:0012094.definition: A deviation from the normal size of the pancreas.

HP:0012096.label: Intracranial epidermoid cyst
HP:0012096.definition: A congenital inclusion cysts that arises from ectodermal cells that normally form skin cells being left behind in the nervous system during development.
HP:0012096.comment: See Figure 8 in PMID:16714456. Epidermoid cysts arise from ectodermal inclusion during neural tube closure in the 3rd-5th week of embryogenesis. The microscopic cyst lining consists of stratified squamous epithelium supported by an outer layer of collagenous connective tissue. Cystic contents usually include debris, keratin, water, and cholesterol laid down in a lamellar fashion. Epidermoid cysts do not contain dermal appendages.

HP:0012097.label: Intracranial dermoid cyst
HP:0012097.definition: A congenital inclusion cysts that arises from the inclusion of ectodermally committed cells at the time of neural tube closure (3rd-5th week of embryogenesis). The capsule of dermoid cysts consists of simple epithelium supported by collagen. In thicker parts, the lining is supplemented with dermis containing hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and apocrine glands.
HP:0012097.comment: See Figure 9 in PMID:16714456. These cysts increase in size by means of glandular secretion and epithelial desquamation. Growth can lead to rupture of the cyst contents, causing a chemical meningitis that may lead to vasospasm, infarction, and even death.

HP:0012098.label: Edema of the dorsum of feet
HP:0012098.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the back of the feet.
exact_synonyms: Oedema of the dorsum of feet

HP:0012099.label: Abnormality of circulating catecholamine level
HP:0012099.definition: An abnormal catecholamine concentration in the blood.

HP:0012100.label: Abnormal circulating creatinine concentration
HP:0012100.definition: An abnormal concentration of creatinine in the blood.

HP:0012101.label: Decreased serum creatinine
HP:0012101.definition: An abnormally reduced amount of creatinine in the blood.

HP:0012102.label: Abnormal mitochondrial number
HP:0012102.definition: A deviation from the normal number of mitochondria per cell.

HP:0012103.label: Abnormality of the mitochondrion
HP:0012103.definition: An anomaly of the mitochondrion, the membranous cytoplasmic organelle the interior of which is subdivided by cristae. The mitochondrion is a self replicating organelle that is the site of tissue respiration.

HP:0012106.label: Rhizomelic leg shortening
HP:0012106.definition: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the leg (i.e. the femur).
HP:0012106.comment: This term implies that the fibula and tibia are not substantially shortened.

HP:0012107.label: Increased fibular diameter
HP:0012107.definition: Increased width of the cross sectional diameter of the fibula.

HP:0012108.label: Open angle glaucoma
HP:0012108.definition: A type of glaucoma defined by an open, normal appearing anterior chamber angle and raised intraocular pressure,
HP:0012108.comment: Evidence of optic nerve damage can include s optic disc abnormalities (Vertical cup:disk ratio over the 97. 5th percentile in the normal population), visual field defects. The role of increased intraocular pressure (IOP) in glaucoma is debated, but an IOP exceeding the 99. 5th percentile of the normal population may be considered to support the diagnosis.

HP:0012109.label: Angle closure glaucoma
HP:0012109.definition: A type of glaucomatous optic neuropathy in an eye that has evidence of angle closure (i.e. significant iridotrabecular contact).
HP:0012109.comment: Evidence of optic nerve damage can include s optic disc abnormalities (Vertical cup:disk ratio over the 97. 5th percentile in the normal population), visual field defects.
