The role of increased intraocular pressure (IOP) in glaucoma is debated, but an IOP exceeding the 99. 5th percentile of the normal population may be considered to support the diagnosis.

HP:0012111.label: Abnormality of circulating glucocorticoid level
HP:0012111.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of a glucocorticoid in the blood.

HP:0012112.label: Abnormal circulating corticosterone level
HP:0012112.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

HP:0012113.label: Abnormal circulating creatine concentration
HP:0012113.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of creatine in the blood circulation. Creatine is a derivative of glycine having methyl and amidino groups attached to the nitrogen. Creatine is naturally produced from amino acids, primarily in liver and kidney, and acts as an energy source for cells, primarily for muscle cells.

HP:0012114.label: Endometrial carcinoma
HP:0012114.definition: A carcinoma of the endometrium, the mucous lining of the uterus.

HP:0012116.label: Abnormal circulating albumin concentration
HP:0012116.definition: Concentration of albumin in the blood circulation outside of the normal range.

HP:0012117.label: Hyperalbuminemia
HP:0012117.definition: Concentration of albumin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0012118.label: Laryngeal carcinoma
HP:0012118.comment: Laryngeal carcinoma often is related to a history of smoking and may manifest by hoarseness, a lump in the neck, persistent cough, stridor and other symptoms.

HP:0012119.label: Methemoglobinemia
HP:0012119.definition: Abnormally increased levels of methemoglobin in the blood. In this form of hemoglobin, there is an oxidized ferric iron (Fe +3) rather than the reduced ferrous form (Fe 2+) that is normally found in hemoglobin. Methemoglobin has a reduced affinity for oxygen, resulting in a reduced ability to release oxygen to tissues.

HP:0012120.label: Methylmalonic aciduria
HP:0012120.definition: Increased concentration of methylmalonic acid in the urine.
HP:0012120.comment: Methylmalonic aciduria is a genetically heterogeneous disorder of methylmalonate and cobalamin (cbl; vitamin B12) metabolism.

HP:0012121.label: Panuveitis
HP:0012121.definition: Inflammation of the uveal tract in which inflammation affects the anterior chamber, vitreous, retina or choroid.

HP:0012122.label: Anterior uveitis
HP:0012122.definition: Inflammation of the uveal tract in which the primary site of inflammation is the anterior chamber.

HP:0012123.label: Posterior uveitis
HP:0012123.definition: Inflammation of the uveal tract in which the primary site of inflammation is the retina or choroid.

HP:0012124.label: Intermediate uveitis
HP:0012124.definition: Inflammation of the uveal tract in which the primary site of inflammation is the vitreous.

HP:0012126.label: Stomach cancer
HP:0012126.definition: A cancer arising in any part of the stomach.

HP:0012127.label: Uraciluria
HP:0012127.definition: Increased concentration of uracil in the urine.

HP:0012128.label: Basal ganglia necrosis
HP:0012128.definition: Death of cells in the basal ganglia. This finding can be confirmed by autopsy. It can be suspected with hyperintensities within the basal ganglia on FLAIR and T2-sequences on magnetic resonance imaging.

HP:0012129.label: Abnormality of bone marrow stromal cells

HP:0012130.label: Abnormal erythroid lineage cell morphology
HP:0012130.definition: An anomaly of erythroid lineage cells, that is, of the erythropoietic cells in the lineage leading to and including erythrocytes.
HP:0012130.comment: Proerythroblasts are the earliest recognizable erythroid precursors. They are followined during the process of hematopoiesis by basophilic erythroblasts, polychromatic (polychromatophilic) erythroblasts, orthochromatic erythroblasts (normoblasts), reticulocytes, and finally mature erythrocytes (red blood cells). This term encompasses structural anomalies of erythroblast precursors in the bone marrow.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of cells of the erythroid lineage

HP:0012131.label: Abnormal number of erythroid precursors
HP:0012131.definition: A deviation from the normal count of erythroid precursor cells, that is, erythroid lineage cells in the bone marrow.

HP:0012132.label: Erythroid hyperplasia
HP:0012132.definition: Increased count of erythroid precursor cells, that is, erythroid lineage cells in the bone marrow.
related_synonyms: Bone marrow biopsy shows erythroid hyperplasia
Bone marrow smear shows erythroid hyperplasia

HP:0012133.label: Erythroid hypoplasia
HP:0012133.definition: Decreased count of erythroid precursor cells, that is, erythroid lineage cells in the bone marrow.
related_synonyms: Erythroid hypoplasia in the bone marrow

HP:0012135.label: Abnormal granulocytopoietic cell morphology
HP:0012135.definition: An anomaly of cells involved in the formation of a granulocytes, that is, of the granulocytopoietic cell.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of cells of the granulocytic lineage

HP:0012139.label: Granulocytic hypoplasia
HP:0012139.definition: Decreased number of granulocyte precursors in the bone marrow.

HP:0012140.label: obsolete Abnormality of cells of the lymphoid lineage

HP:0012142.label: Pancreatic squamous cell carcinoma
HP:0012142.definition: A subtype of ductal pancreatic carcinoma that is thought to originate from squamous metaplasia of pancreatic ductal epithelium.
exact_synonyms: Squamous cell carcinoma of the pancreas

HP:0012143.label: Abnormal megakaryocyte morphology
HP:0012143.definition: Any structural anomaly of megakaryocytes. Mature blood platelets are released from the cytoplasm of megakaryocytes, which are bone-marrow resident cells.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of cells of the megakaryocyte lineage

HP:0012144.label: Abnormal monocyte morphology
HP:0012144.definition: Any structural anomaly of a myeloid mononuclear recirculating leukocyte that can act as a precursor of tissue macrophages, osteoclasts and some populations of tissue dendritic cells.

HP:0012145.label: Abnormality of multiple cell lineages in the bone marrow

HP:0012146.label: Abnormality of von Willebrand factor
HP:0012146.definition: Decreased quantity or activity of von Willebrand factor. Von Willebrand factor mediates the adhesion of platelets to the collagen exposed on endothelial cell surfaces.

HP:0012147.label: Reduced quantity of Von Willebrand factor
HP:0012147.definition: Decreased quantity of von Willebrand factor.

HP:0012148.label: Multiple lineage myelodysplasia
HP:0012148.definition: Myelodysplasia with dysplastic changes in two or more of the myeloid lineages: erythroid, granulocytic, megakaryocytic.

HP:0012149.label: Bilineage myelodysplasia
HP:0012149.definition: Myelodysplasia with dysplastic changes in two of the myeloid lineages: erythroid, granulocytic, megakaryocytic.

HP:0012150.label: Single lineage myelodysplasia
HP:0012150.definition: Abnormality/dysplasia of a single myeloid cell (erythroid, granulocytic, or megakaryocytic).

HP:0012151.label: Hemothorax
HP:0012151.definition: The presence of blood in the pleural space.
HP:0012151.comment: Hemothorax may result from hemorrhage in the chest wall, lung parenchyma, heart, or great vessels.

HP:0012152.label: Foveoschisis
HP:0012152.definition: Splitting of the retinal layers in the macula and involving the fovea.

HP:0012153.label: Hypotriglyceridemia
HP:0012153.definition: An decrease in the level of triglycerides in the blood.

HP:0012154.label: Anhedonia
HP:0012154.definition: Decreased ability or inability to experience, feel, or anticipate pleasure from activities, experiences, or stimuli that are typically found pleasurable by the individual. This may involve diminished enjoyment of previously rewarding experiences (e.g., hobbies, social interactions, or sexual activity) or reduced pleasure in response to stimuli processed through the senses (e.g., music, food, or tactile contact). Anhedonia is a disruption in the capacity to derive emotional reward and is not due to primary sensory deficits or medical conditions (e.g., anosmia from viral illness). The phenomenon involves altered affective processing rather than impaired sensory perception.
exact_synonyms: Loss of ability to enjoy things
Loss of interest in pleasurable activities

HP:0012155.label: Decreased corneal sensation
HP:0012155.definition: Reduced ability of the cornea to respond to stimulation.
HP:0012155.comment: Corneal sensitivity to touch can be assessed by an aesthesiometer, which measures the corneal touch threshold. Decreased corneal sensation is associated with a decreased corneal reflex (HP:0008000); however, impairment of the corneal reflex can have other causes such as trigeminal nerve compression or a cerebellopontine angle lesion. Well known causes of decreased corneal sensation include Herpes simplex keratitis, neuroparalytic keratitis, leprosy, acoustic neuroma, and absolute glaucoma.

HP:0012156.label: Hemophagocytosis
HP:0012156.definition: Phagocytosis by macrophages of erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets, and their precursors in bone marrow and other tissues.
HP:0012156.comment: Hemophagocytosis is a nonspecific phenotypic feature observed in several conditions including hemolytic anemia, malignant disease, infections, and hemophagocytic syndrome (also known as hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, a rare hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by severe hypercytokinemia due to a highly stimulated but ineffective immune process).

HP:0012157.label: Subcortical cerebral atrophy
HP:0012157.definition: Atrophy of the cerebral subcortical white and gray matter, termed subcortical atrophy, reflects loss of nerve cells in the basal ganglia or fibers in the deep white matter.

HP:0012158.label: Carotid artery dissection
HP:0012158.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the carotid artery wall.

HP:0012159.label: Internal carotid artery dissection
HP:0012159.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the internal carotid artery wall.
HP:0012159.comment: The internal carotid begins at the bifurcation of the common carotid, opposite the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, and runs perpendicularly upward. It supplies the anterior part of the brain, the eye and its appendages, and sends branches to the forehead and nose. Interstitial hemorrhage into the media of the vessel wall can lead to occlusion of the internal carotid artery and aneurysm formation.

HP:0012160.label: Intracranial internal carotid artery dissection
HP:0012160.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the intracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.

HP:0012161.label: External carotid artery dissection
HP:0012161.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the external carotid artery wall.

HP:0012162.label: Common carotid artery dissection
HP:0012162.definition: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the common carotid artery wall.

HP:0012163.label: Carotid artery dilatation
HP:0012163.definition: A dilatation (balooning or bulging out of the vessel wall) of a carotid artery.

HP:0012164.label: Asterixis
HP:0012164.definition: A clinical sign indicating a lapse of posture and is usually manifest by a bilateral flapping tremor at the wrist, metacarpophalangeal, and hip joints.
HP:0012164.comment: The examiner can test for asterixis by asking the patient to extend the arms, spread the fingers, dorsiflex the wrist and observe for the abnormal "flapping" tremor at the wrist. Asterixis represents the failure to actively maintain a position and is caused by the abnormal function of diencephalic motor centers that regulate the tone of the agonist and antagonist muscles involved in maintaining posture.

HP:0012165.label: Oligodactyly
HP:0012165.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the presence of fewer than the normal number of digits.

HP:0012166.label: Skin-picking
HP:0012166.definition: Repetitive and compulsive picking of skin which results in tissue damage.

HP:0012167.label: Hair-pulling
HP:0012167.definition: A phenomenon in which persons repetitively pull out their own hair, resulting in noticeable hair loss.

HP:0012168.label: Head-banging
HP:0012168.definition: Habitual striking of one's own head against a surface such as a mattress or wall of a crib.

HP:0012169.label: Self-biting
HP:0012169.definition: Habitual biting of one's own body.
HP:0012169.comment: Biting of one's own arms, lip, check, finger etc.

HP:0012170.label: Nail-biting
HP:0012170.definition: Habitual biting of one's own fingernails.

HP:0012171.label: Stereotypical hand wringing
HP:0012171.definition: Habitual clasping and wringing of the hands in the middle of the body, similar to a hand-washing movement.

HP:0012172.label: Stereotypical body rocking
HP:0012172.definition: Habitual repetitive movement of the entire body, front to back or side to side.

HP:0012173.label: Orthostatic tachycardia
HP:0012173.definition: An increase in heart rate with standing of 30 beats per minute or more.

HP:0012174.label: Glioblastoma multiforme
HP:0012174.definition: A tumor arising from glia in the central nervous system with macroscopic regions of necrosis and hemorrhage. Microscopically, glioblastoma multiforme is characterized by regions of pseudopalisading necrosis, pleomorphic nuclei and cells, and microvascular proliferation.

HP:0012175.label: Resistance to activated protein C
HP:0012175.definition: Poor anticoagulant response to activated protein C. A plasma is termed 'APC resistant' when the addition of exogenous APC fails to prolong its clotting time in an activated partial thromboplastin time assay.
HP:0012175.comment: The protein C pathway is a major anticoagulant mechanism that down-regulates the prothrombin- and intrinsic factor X (FX)-activating complexes via inactivation of their respective cofactors, activated factors V (FVa) and VIII (FVIIIa). Cofactor inactivation occurs by limited proteolysis at certain amino acid positions in FVa and in FVIIIa. These reactions are catalyzed by the serine protease activated protein C (APC) and stimulated by the APC cofactor protein S. Functional defects of the protein C pathway determine a plasma phenotype known as APC resistance, which is a prevalent and important risk factor for venous thrombosis. A plasma is termed 'APC resistant' when the addition of exogenous APC fails to prolong its clotting time in an activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) assay.

HP:0012176.label: Abnormal natural killer cell morphology
HP:0012176.definition: An anomaly of the natural killer cell, which is a lymphocyte that can spontaneously kill a variety of target cells without prior antigenic activation via germline encoded activation receptors. It also regulates immune responses via cytokine release and direct contact with other cells.

HP:0012177.label: Abnormal natural killer cell physiology
HP:0012177.definition: Abnormal response of natural killer (NK) cells to stimuli.

HP:0012178.label: obsolete Reduced natural killer cell activity

HP:0012179.label: Craniofacial dystonia
HP:0012179.definition: A form of focal dystonia affecting the face and especially the jaw that is induced by the act of speaking. It is an involuntary contraction of the masticatory muscles, resulting in dysarthria or dysphagia.

HP:0012180.label: Cystic medial necrosis
HP:0012180.definition: A disorder of large arteries, in particular the aorta, characterized by an accumulation of basophilic ground substance in the media with cyst-like lesions associated with degenerative changes of collagen, elastin and the vascular smooth muscle cells.
HP:0012180.comment: The lesions of cystic medial necrosis are not true cysts.

HP:0012181.label: Entrapment neuropathy
HP:0012181.definition: Malfunction of a peripheral nerve resulting from mechanical compression of the nerve roots from internal or external causes and leading to a conduction block or axonal loss.
HP:0012181.comment: An entrapment neuropathy is an isolated peripheral nerve injury due to mechanical constriction in a fibrous or fibro-osseous tunnel or to deformation of the nerve by a fibrous band.

HP:0012182.label: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
HP:0012182.definition: A squamous cell carcinoma that originates in the oropharnyx.

HP:0012183.label: Hyperplastic colonic polyposis
HP:0012183.definition: Presence of multiple hyperplastic polyps in the colon. Hyperplastic polyps are generally about 5 mm in size and show hyperplastic mucosal proliferation.

HP:0012184.label: Increased HDL cholesterol concentration
HP:0012184.definition: An elevated concentration of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL) in the blood.
HP:0012184.comment: The major apolipoproteins of HDL are apolipoprotein (apo) A-I and apo A-II, also known as the alpha lipoproteins. Thus, hyperalphalipoproteinemia refers to an elevated concentration of apo A-I and apo A-II.

HP:0012185.label: Constrictive median neuropathy
HP:0012185.definition: Injury to the median nerve caused by its entrapment at the wrist as it traverses through the carpal tunnel. Clinically, constrictive median neuropathy is characterized by pain, paresthesia, and weakness in the median nerve distribution of the hand.
HP:0012185.comment: Constrictive median neuropathy is the major clinical feature of carpal tunnel syndrome.

HP:0012186.label: Entrapment neuropathy of the ulnar nerve at elbow
HP:0012186.definition: An entrapment neuropathy of the ulnar nerve in the cubital tunnel (in the elbow) characterized by numbness in the ring and little fingers and weakness of the intrinsic muscles in the hand.

HP:0012187.label: Increased erythrocyte protoporphyrin concentration
HP:0012187.definition: Concentration of protoporphyrins in erythrocytes above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0012188.label: Hyperemesis gravidarum
HP:0012188.definition: Excessive vomiting in early pregnancy, leading to the loss of 5% or more of body weight.

HP:0012189.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
HP:0012189.definition: A type of lymphoma characterized microscopically by multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells.

HP:0012190.label: T-cell lymphoma
HP:0012190.definition: A type of lymphoma that originates in T-cells.

HP:0012191.label: B-cell lymphoma
HP:0012191.definition: A type of lymphoma that originates in B-cells.

HP:0012192.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
HP:0012192.definition: A type of T-cell lymphoma that exhibits malignant infiltration of the skin.

HP:0012193.label: Anaplastic large-cell lymphoma
HP:0012193.definition: A type of T-cell lymphoma that is characterized by so-called hallmark cells with a pleomorphic appearance that express the CD30 antigen, are lobulated, and have indented nuclei.

HP:0012194.label: Episodic hemiplegia
HP:0012194.definition: Transient episodes of weakness of the arm, leg, and in some cases the face on one side of the body.

HP:0012196.label: Cheyne-Stokes respiration
HP:0012196.definition: An abnormal pattern of respiration characterized by cycles of respiration that are increasingly deeper then shallower with possible periods of apnea. Affected patients may display a 10 to 20 second episode of hypoventilation or apnea, followed by respiration of increased depth and frequency over the course of about one minute. The cycle repeats every 45 seconds to 3 minutes.

HP:0012197.label: Insulinoma
HP:0012197.definition: A type of tumor of the pancreatic beta cells that secretes excess insulin and can result in hypoglycemia.

HP:0012198.label: Juvenile colonic polyposis
HP:0012198.definition: The presence of more than 5 juvenile polyps of the colon. The term juvenile polyps refer to a special histopathology and not the age of onset as the polyp might be diagnosed at all ages. The juvenile polyp has a spherical appearance and is microscopically characterized by overgrowth of an oedematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells and cystic glands.
HP:0012198.comment: A juvenile polyp is a hamartomatous growth that projects from the lining of the intestine. It does not arise from the colonocytes themselves but from the tissues underneath the lining cells.

HP:0012199.label: Cluster headache
HP:0012199.definition: A type of headache characterized by repeated attacks of unilateral pain lasting 15 to 180 minutes and associated with local autonomic signs.
HP:0012199.comment: According to the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-II), the diagnosis of cluster headache can be made with at least five attacks fulfilling criteria B-D: (B) Severe or very severe unilateral orbital, supraorbital and/or temporal pain lasting 15-180 minutes if untreated. (C) Headache is accompanied by at least 1 of the following: (i) Ipsilateral conjunctival injection and/or lacrimation. (ii) Ipsilateral nasal congestion and/or rhinorrhea. (iii) Ipsilateral eyelid edema. (iv) Ipsilateral forehead and facial sweating. (v) Ipsilateral miosis and/or ptosis. (vi) A sense of restlessness or agitation. (D) Attacks have a frequency from 1 every other day to 8/day. Additionally, the headaches cannot attributed to another disorder.

HP:0012200.label: Abnormality of prothrombin
HP:0012200.definition: An anomaly of clotting factor II, which is known as prothrombin, a vitamin K-dependent proenzyme that functions in the blood coagulation cascade.

HP:0012202.label: Increased serum bile acid concentration
HP:0012202.definition: An increase in the concentration of bile acid in the blood.

HP:0012203.label: Onychomycosis
HP:0012203.definition: A fungal infection of the toenails or fingernails that tends to cause the nails to thicken, discolor, disfigure, and split.

HP:0012204.label: Recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis
HP:0012204.definition: Recurrent infection involving the vulva, vagina, and adjacent crural areas, whereby the causative agent belongs to the genus Candida.

HP:0012205.label: Globozoospermia
HP:0012205.definition: Any structural anomaly of the acrosome resulting in a round sperm head.

HP:0012206.label: Abnormal sperm motility
HP:0012206.definition: An anomaly of the mobility of ejaculated sperm.

HP:0012207.label: Reduced sperm motility
HP:0012207.definition: An abnormal reduction in the mobility of ejaculated sperm.

HP:0012208.label: Immotile sperm
HP:0012208.definition: A lack of mobility of ejaculated sperm.

HP:0012209.label: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
HP:0012209.definition: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is a lethal myeloproliferative disease of young childhood characterized clinically by overproduction of myelomonocytic cells and by the in vitro phenotype of hematopoietic progenitor hypersensitivity to granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor.

HP:0012210.label: Abnormal renal morphology
HP:0012210.definition: Any structural anomaly of the kidney.
exact_synonyms: Structural anomalies of the renal tract

HP:0012211.label: Abnormal renal physiology
HP:0012211.definition: An abnormal functionality of the kidney.

HP:0012212.label: Abnormal glomerular filtration rate
HP:0012212.definition: An abnormally increased or reduced amount of fluid filtered out of plasma through glomerular capillary walls into Bowman's capsules per unit of time.
HP:0012212.comment: Glomerular filtration, the first step in urine formation, is the passive process of ultrafiltration of plasma from blood into Bowman's space as it traverses the glomerular capillaries. Because GFR varies by body size, it is indexed relative to an average body surface area (BSA) of 1.73 m2 and expressed as ml/min/per 1.73 m2. GFR cannot be measured directly; it can be assessed from clearance measurements or estimated from serum levels of endogenous filtration markers, such as creatinine or cystatin C. Clearance measurements require either multiple measurements of serum concentrations or timed urine collections and are not routinely performed. GFR is usually estimated from serum concentrations of a marker of filtration using GFR estimating equations.

HP:0012213.label: Decreased glomerular filtration rate
HP:0012213.definition: An abnormal reduction in the volume of fluid filtered out of plasma through glomerular capillary walls into Bowman's capsules per unit of time.
HP:0012213.comment: Renal clearance is defined as the volume of plasma per minute needed to excrete the quantity of a solute appearing in the urine in a minute. Normal values for adults are 97 to 137 ml/min (male) and 88 to 128 ml/min (female). This term refers to a reduction below normal limits in the ability of the kidney to clear creatinine from the bloodstream.

HP:0012214.label: Increased glomerular filtration rate
HP:0012214.definition: An abnormal rise in the volume of water filtered out of plasma through glomerular capillary walls into Bowman's capsules per unit of time.

HP:0012215.label: Testicular microlithiasis
HP:0012215.definition: The deposition of calcium phosphate microliths within the seminiferous tubules.

HP:0012216.label: Entrapment neuropathy of suprascapular nerve
HP:0012216.definition: An entrapment neuropathy of the suprascapular nerve, presenting with shoulder weakness confined to the supraspinatus muscle (this muscle initiates shoulder abduction) or to the infraspinatus (this muscle externally rotates the arm), as well as with pain in the posterior part of the shoulder and upper periscapular region.

HP:0012217.label: Increased urinary porphobilinogen
HP:0012217.definition: The concentration of porphobilinogen in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0012217.comment: Increased porphobilinogen (PBG) in urine is pathognomonic of an attack of acute porphyria (acute intermittent porphyria, variegate porphyria, hereditary coproporphyria); the absence of increased urinary PBG in a suspected attack excludes the diagnosis.

HP:0012218.label: Alveolar soft part sarcoma
HP:0012218.definition: A type of soft tissue sarcoma with a histological appearance reminiscent of alveoli because of its reticulated fibrous stroma enclosing groups of sarcoma cells, which resemble epithelial cells and are enclosed in alveoli walled with connective tissue.

HP:0012219.label: Erythema nodosum
HP:0012219.definition: An erythematous eruption commonly associated with drug reactions or infection and characterized by inflammatory nodules that are usually tender, multiple, and bilateral.
HP:0012219.comment: The nodules of erythema nodosum are located predominantly on the shins with less common occurrence on the thighs and forearms. They undergo characteristic color changes ending in temporary bruise-like areas, and usually subside in 3-6 weeks without scarring or atrophy.

HP:0012220.label: Non-caseating epithelioid cell granulomatosis
HP:0012220.definition: The presence of multiple epithelioid cell granulomas consist of highly differentiated mononuclear phagocytes (epithelioid cells and giant cells) and lymphocytes, not exhibiting caseation (a form of necrosis in which the tissue changes into a dry, amorphous mass said to resemble cheese).
HP:0012220.comment: This feature is a hallmark of sarcoidosis.

HP:0012221.label: Pretibial blistering
HP:0012221.definition: A type of blistering that affects the skin of the tibial region.

HP:0012222.label: Arachnoid hemangiomatosis
HP:0012222.definition: The presence of multiple hemangiomas in the arachnoid.

HP:0012223.label: Splenic rupture
HP:0012223.definition: A breach of the capsule of the spleen.

HP:0012224.label: Circulating immune complexes
HP:0012224.definition: Persistence of immune complexes in the blood circulation.
HP:0012224.comment: Immune complexes are formed of interlocking antigens and antibodies and are normally are rapidly removed from the bloodstream by macrophages in the spleen and Kupffer cells in the liver. If they persist abnormally in the circulation, they may become trapped in various tissues and induce inflammatory reactions.

HP:0012225.label: Oligodontia of primary teeth
HP:0012225.comment: Primary teeth are also called temporary teeth or deciduous teeth.
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of some primary teeth
Failure of development of some deciduous teeth

HP:0012226.label: Ovarian teratoma
HP:0012226.definition: The presence of a teratoma in the ovary.

HP:0012227.label: Urethral stricture
HP:0012227.definition: Narrowing of the urethra associated with inflammation or scar tissue.
HP:0012227.comment: A urethral stricture may result from surgery, disease, or injury. The term should not be used for a congenital narrowing of the urethra (Consider the term Urethral stenosis, HP:0008661). All strictures result from injury to the epithelium of the urethra or underlying corpus spongiosum, which ultimately causes fibrosis during the healing process. The pathological changes associated with strictures show that the normal pseudostratified columnar epithelium is replaced with squamous metaplasia. Small tears in this metaplastic tissue result in urinary extravasation, which causes a fibrotic reaction within the spongiosum. At the time of injury, this fibrosis can be asymptomatic; however, over time, the fibrotic process can cause further narrowing of the lumen of the urethra, resulting in symptomatic obstructive voiding.

HP:0012228.label: Tension-type headache
HP:0012228.definition: A type of headache that last hours with continuous pain of mild or moderate intensity, bilateral location, a pressing/tightening (non-pulsating) quality and that is not aggravated by routine physical activity such as walking or climbing stairs.

HP:0012229.label: CSF pleocytosis
HP:0012229.definition: An increased white blood cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid.

HP:0012230.label: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
HP:0012230.definition: A type of retinal detachment associated with a full-thickness defect in the retina that allows fluid to pass from the vitreous space into the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.

HP:0012231.label: Serous retinal detachment
HP:0012231.definition: A type of retinal detachment such that fluid is present in the subretinal space and separate the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium. It is not associated with a full-thickness break nor a tractional component. Due to breakdown of outer blood-retina barrier or increased exudation from abnormal vasculature or defective outflow.

HP:0012232.label: Shortened QT interval
HP:0012232.definition: Decreased time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).

HP:0012233.label: Intramuscular hematoma
HP:0012233.definition: Blood clot formed within muscle tissue following leakage of blood into the tissue.

HP:0012234.label: Absence of circulating granulocytes
HP:0012234.definition: Absence of detectable circulating granulocytes in the blood. Usually a value of less than 50 cells per microliter is considered to be an absence.
HP:0012234.comment: Agranulocytosis is defined as an absolute neutrophil count less than 500 cells/microliter.

HP:0012235.label: Drug-induced agranulocytosis
HP:0012235.definition: Absence of detectable circulating granulocytes in the blood caused by an exposure to a drug. Usually a value of less than 50 granulocytes per microliter is considered to be an absence.

HP:0012236.label: Elevated sweat chloride
HP:0012236.definition: An increased concentration of chloride in the sweat.
HP:0012236.comment: Sweat chloride is notably increased in cystic fibrosis, but also in some other diseases.

HP:0012237.label: Urocanic aciduria
HP:0012237.definition: An increased concentration of urocanic acid in the urine.

HP:0012238.label: Increased circulating chylomicron concentration
HP:0012238.definition: Increased plasma concentrations of chylomicrons, the large lipid droplet (up to 100 mm in diameter) of reprocessed lipid synthesized in epithelial cells of the small intestine and containing triacylglycerols, cholesterol esters, and several apolipoproteins.

HP:0012239.label: Atransferrinemia
HP:0012239.definition: Absence of transferrin, a protein that transports iron, in the blood.

HP:0012240.label: Increased intramyocellular lipid droplets
HP:0012240.definition: An abnormal increase in intracellular lipid droplets In a muscle. The number and size of these drops can increase with somd disorders of lipid metabolism affecting muscle. See PMID 20691590 for histological images.
HP:0012240.comment: In normal muscle cells, lipid content takes the aspect of small droplets which concentration and size are usually higher in type 1 fibers than in type 2 fibers.

HP:0012241.label: Levator palpebrae superioris atrophy
HP:0012241.definition: Atrophy of the levator palpebrae superioris, the extraocular muscle that elevates the superior eyelid.

HP:0012242.label: Superior rectus atrophy
HP:0012242.definition: Atrophy of the superior rectus, the extraocular muscle whose primary function is to elevate the globe.

HP:0012243.label: Abnormal reproductive system morphology
HP:0012243.definition: A structural or developmental anomaly of any of the tissues involved in the genital system.

HP:0012244.label: Abnormal sex determination
HP:0012244.definition: Anomaly of primary or secondary sexual development or characteristics.

HP:0012245.label: Sex reversal
HP:0012245.definition: Development of the reproductive system is inconsistent with the chromosomal sex.
HP:0012245.comment: Sex reversal is present if an XX individual develops phenotypically as a male or if an XY individual develops as a female.

HP:0012246.label: Oculomotor nerve palsy
HP:0012246.definition: Reduced ability to control the movement of the eye associated with damage to the third cranial nerve (the oculomotor nerve).

HP:0012248.label: Prolonged PR interval
HP:0012248.definition: Increased time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex).
HP:0012248.comment: In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

HP:0012249.label: Abnormal ST segment
HP:0012249.definition: An electrocardiographic anomaly of the ST segment, which is the segment that connects the QRS complex and the T wave. The ST segment normally has a duration of 80 to 120 ms, is flat and at the same level (isoelectric) as the PR and TP segment.

HP:0012250.label: ST segment depression
HP:0012250.definition: An electrocardiographic anomaly in which the ST segment is observed to be located inferior to the isoelectric line.

HP:0012251.label: ST segment elevation
HP:0012251.definition: An electrocardiographic anomaly in which the ST segment is observed to be located superior to the isoelectric line.
HP:0012251.comment: ST segment elevation may have multiple causes including myocardial infaction, left ventricular aneurysm, and hyperkalemia.

HP:0012252.label: Abnormal respiratory system morphology
HP:0012252.definition: A structural anomaly of the respiratory system.

HP:0012253.label: Abnormal respiratory epithelium morphology
HP:0012253.definition: Any structural anomaly of the pseudostratified ciliated epithelium that lines much of the conducting portion of the airway, including part of the nasal cavity and larynx, the trachea, and bronchi.

HP:0012254.label: Ewing sarcoma
HP:0012254.definition: A malignant tumor of the bone which always arises in the medullary tissue, occurring more often in cylindrical bones.
HP:0012254.comment: Histologically, Ewing's sarcoma is composed of a homogeneous population of small round cells with high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratios that are arrayed in sheets. There is scant cytoplasms, which is pale, vacuolated and characterized by faded boundaries. In contrast, the nuclei are clearly visualized by their intense color. Mitotic activity is typically low.

HP:0012255.label: Dynein arm defect of respiratory motile cilia
HP:0012255.definition: An anomaly of the dynein arms of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.
HP:0012255.comment: The peripheral microtubules in the canonical 9 + 2 microtubular pattern of motile cilia are studded with dynein arms that contain adenosine triphosphatases and act as molecular motors to effect the sliding of the peripheral microtubular pairs relative to one another.

HP:0012256.label: Absent outer dynein arms
HP:0012256.definition: Absence of the outer dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, which normally are situated outside of the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.

HP:0012257.label: Absent inner dynein arms
HP:0012257.definition: Absence of the inner dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, which normally are situated within the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.

HP:0012258.label: Abnormal axonemal organization of respiratory motile cilia
HP:0012258.definition: Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the axoneme, which is the cytoskeletal structure that forms the inner core of the motile cilium and displays a canonical 9+2 microtubular pattern of motile cilia studded with dynein arms.
HP:0012258.comment: Abnormal axonemal organization comprises anomalies such as an eccentric central pair of microtubuli, abnormal radial spokes and nexin links, reduced number of inner dynein arms, and displacement of the outer doublet.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal axonemal organisation of respiratory motile cilia

HP:0012259.label: Absent inner and outer dynein arms
HP:0012259.definition: Complete absence of the dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, that is, absence of the inner and the outer dynein arms, which normally are situated inside and outside of the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.

HP:0012260.label: Abnormal central microtubular pair morphology of respiratory motile cilia
HP:0012260.definition: A structural anomaly of the two central microtubules of motile cilia with a 9+2 microtubuluar configuration.
HP:0012260.comment: The central microtubular pair is referred to as the central part of axoneme of cilium.

HP:0012261.label: Abnormal respiratory motile cilium physiology
HP:0012261.definition: Any functional anomaly of the respiratory motile cilia.
HP:0012261.comment: Abnormal respiratory motile cilium physiology may include alterations in ciliary beating pattern or frequency.

HP:0012262.label: Abnormal ciliary motility
HP:0012262.definition: Any anomaly of the normal motility of motile cilia. Evaluation of ciliary beat frequency and ciliary beat pattern requires high-speed videomicroscopy of freshly obtained ciliary biopsies that are maintained in culture media under controlled conditions.
HP:0012262.comment: Ciliated epithelial cells bear approximately 200 motile (9 + 2) cilia that move with both intracellular and intercellular synchrony. The pattern of beat in 9 + 2 motile cilia occurs in a waveform having a forward effective stroke followed by a return stroke. The direction of stroke is a function of the directional orientation of the central microtubules. In addition to moving in synchrony, individual cilia in normal cells are very plastic and move fluidly, sometimes deforming briefly upon encountering resistance and/or particles being transported over the mucosal surface. Cilia are embedded in a watery periciliary fluid of low viscosity, which facilitates the rapid beat cycle to move the more viscous overlying layer of mucus. Ciliary beat frequency ranges from approximately 8-20 Hz under normal conditions but may be accelerated by exposure to irritants such as tobacco smoke.

HP:0012264.label: Absent central microtubular pair morphology of respiratory motile cilia
HP:0012264.definition: Absence of the two central microtubules of motile cilia with a 9+2 microtubuluar configuration.

HP:0012265.label: Ciliary dyskinesia
HP:0012265.definition: A deviation from the normally well coordinated pattern of intracellular and intercellular synchrony of motile cilia. Dyskinetic cilia usually beat out of synchrony relative to neighboring cilia.
HP:0012265.comment: Typically, but not always, dyskinesia is characterized by markedly attenuated ciliary beat frequency.
exact_synonyms: Lack of coordinated beating of respiratory cilia

HP:0012266.label: T-wave alternans
HP:0012266.definition: A periodic beat-to-beat variation in the amplitude or shape of the T wave in an EKG.

HP:0012267.label: Absent respiratory ciliary axoneme radial spokes
HP:0012267.definition: Absence of the radial spokes of the axoneme of the respiratory cilium.

HP:0012268.label: Myxoid liposarcoma
HP:0012268.definition: A liposarcoma that contains myxomatous tissue.

HP:0012269.label: Abnormal muscle glycogen content
HP:0012269.definition: Any anomaly in the amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.
HP:0012269.comment: Glycogen functions as a secondary short term energy storage in muscle.

HP:0012270.label: Decreased muscle glycogen content
HP:0012270.definition: A decreased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.

HP:0012271.label: Episodic upper airway obstruction
HP:0012271.definition: Intermittent episodes of increased resistance to the passage of air in the upper airway.

HP:0012272.label: J wave
HP:0012272.definition: The J wave is a positive convex deflection that occurs at the junction of the QRS complex and ST segment, the J-point.
HP:0012272.comment: J waves can be seen in hypothermia when the core body temperature falls below 32 degrees C. Then, they occur most prominently in the inferior leads: II, III, and aVF and the precordial leads: V5-V6. J waves can also be observed in other conditions such as some forms of Brugada syndrome.

HP:0012273.label: Increased carotid artery intimal medial thickness
HP:0012273.definition: An increase in the combined thickness of the intima and media of the carotid artery.
HP:0012273.comment: This feature can be measured by ultrasonography and is thought to be a risk foctor for myocardial infarction and stroke.

HP:0012274.label: Autosomal dominant inheritance with paternal imprinting
HP:0012274.definition: A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that is imprinted with paternal silencing.
HP:0012274.comment: Since the paternally inherited copy of such genes is silenced normally, only a maternally transmitted mutation leads to disease in this kind of inheritance.

HP:0012275.label: Autosomal dominant inheritance with maternal imprinting
HP:0012275.definition: A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that is imprinted with maternal silencing.
HP:0012275.comment: Since the maternally inherited copy of such genes is silenced normally, only a paternally transmitted mutation leads to disease in this kind of inheritance.

HP:0012276.label: Digital flexor tenosynovitis
HP:0012276.definition: Inflammation of the flexor digitorum tendon, often associated with the Kanavel signs: (i) finger held in slight flexion, (ii) fusiform swelling, (iii) tenderness along the flexor tendon sheath, and (iv) pain with passive extension of the digit.
HP:0012276.comment: Tenosynovitis refers to inflammation of the protective sheath that surrounds a tendon. Stenosing tenosynovitis, or trigger finger, is diagnosed when a patient presents with a symptomatic locking or clicking of a finger or the thumb. It is caused by a mismatch between the volume of the flexor tendon sheath and its contents. As the flexor tendon attempts to glide through a relatively stenotic sheath, it catches, producing an inability to flex or extend the digit smoothly.

HP:0012277.label: Hypoglycinemia
HP:0012277.definition: An abnormally reduced concentration of glycine in the blood.

HP:0012278.label: Abnormal circulating serine concentration
HP:0012278.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of serine in the blood circulation.

HP:0012279.label: Hyposerinemia
HP:0012279.definition: Reduced concentration of serine in the blood.

HP:0012280.label: Hepatic amyloidosis
HP:0012280.definition: A form of amyloidosis that affects the liver.

HP:0012281.label: Chylous ascites
HP:0012281.definition: Extravasation of chyle into the peritoneal cavity.

HP:0012282.label: Morbilliform rash
HP:0012282.definition: An exanthema consisting of widespread pink-to-red macules (flat spots of 2-10 mm in diameter) or papules (red bumps) that blanch with pressure. The macules and papules may cluster and merge to form sheets over several days.
HP:0012282.comment: A morbilliform rash is said to resemble the rash of measles, rubella or scarlet fever, thus mimicking viral and bacterial exanthemas.

HP:0012283.label: Small distal femoral epiphysis
HP:0012283.definition: Reduced size of the Distal epiphysis of femur.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of outermost thighbone

HP:0012284.label: Small proximal tibial epiphyses
HP:0012284.definition: Reduced size of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia.
exact_synonyms: Small end part of innermost shankbone
Small end part of innermost shinbone

HP:0012285.label: Abnormal hypothalamus physiology
HP:0012285.definition: An abnormal functionality of the hypothalamus.
HP:0012285.comment: The hypothalamus is linked vascularly with the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland and thereby controls the secretion of pituitary hormones.

HP:0012286.label: Abnormal hypothalamus morphology
HP:0012286.definition: Any structural anomaly of the hypothalamus.
HP:0012286.comment: The hypothalamus is a cone-shaped cerebral structure that projects downward, ending in the pituitary (infundibular) stalk, a tubular connection to the pituitary gland. It is linked vascularly with the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland and thereby controls the secretion of pituitary hormones.

HP:0012287.label: Hypothalamic luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone deficiency
HP:0012287.definition: Decreased secretion of luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone by the hypothalamus.

HP:0012288.label: Neoplasm of head and neck
HP:0012288.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the head and neck region with origin in the lip, oral cavity, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, pharynx, or larynx.

HP:0012289.label: Facial neoplasm
HP:0012289.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the face.

HP:0012292.label: Fusion of gums
HP:0012292.definition: A congenital defect with an abnormal joining of the gums of the upper and lower jaw.
exact_synonyms: Upper and lower gums fused together

HP:0012293.label: Abnormal genital pigmentation
HP:0012293.definition: An abnormal pigmentation pattern of the external genitalia.

HP:0012294.label: Abnormal occipital bone morphology
HP:0012294.definition: Abnormality of the occipital bone of the skull.

HP:0012295.label: Slender middle phalanx of finger
HP:0012295.definition: Reduced diameter of the middle phalanx of finger.

HP:0012296.label: Slender distal phalanx of finger
HP:0012296.definition: Reduced diameter of the distal phalanx of finger.

HP:0012297.label: Slender proximal phalanx of finger
HP:0012297.definition: Reduced diameter of the proximal phalanx of finger.

HP:0012298.label: Long middle phalanx of finger
HP:0012298.definition: Increased length of the middle phalanx of finger.

HP:0012299.label: Long distal phalanx of finger
HP:0012299.definition: Increased length of the distal phalanx of finger.

HP:0012300.label: Ureteral agenesis
HP:0012300.definition: Failure of the ureter to undergo development.

HP:0012301.label: Type II transferrin isoform profile
HP:0012301.definition: Abnormal transferrin isoform profile consistent with a type II congenital disorder of glycosylation.
HP:0012301.comment: There are several methods in use with which this feature can be diagnosed. Using HPLC analysis increased mono- and trisialotransferrin and reduced tetrasialotransferrin are observed. Using immunoaffinity column analysis, the tri-sialo/di-oligosaccharide transferrin ratio is abnormal.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin, type II pattern
Isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin consistent with CDG type II
related_synonyms: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin, type 2 pattern

HP:0012302.label: Herpes simplex encephalitis
HP:0012302.definition: Infection of the brain parenchyma with herpes simplex virus, resulting in inflammation of the brain parenchyma with neurologic dysfunction.
HP:0012302.comment: Although infection with HSV is very common in the population, only a miniscule proportion of infected persons develop encephalitis, so that an occurrence of HSV encephalitis is interpreted as a sign of increased susceptibility to HSV. Herpes encephalitis may occur in immunocompromised patients, but HSV-1 is consistently the single most common cause of sporadic encephalitis worldwide.

HP:0012303.label: Abnormal aortic arch morphology
HP:0012303.definition: An anomaly of the arch of aorta.

HP:0012304.label: Hypoplastic aortic arch
HP:0012304.definition: Underdevelopment of the arch of aorta.

HP:0012305.label: Coarctation of the descending aortic arch
HP:0012305.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized to the region of the descending trunk of arch of aorta.

HP:0012306.label: Abnormal rib ossification
HP:0012306.definition: An anomaly of the process of rib bone formation.

HP:0012307.label: Spatulate ribs
HP:0012307.definition: Ribs that are increased in width and taper to the posterior ends.
HP:0012307.comment: This morphological anomaly of the rib has been compared to a canoe panel or a spatula, whence the name.

HP:0012308.label: Decreased circulating complement C9 concentration
HP:0012308.definition: Concentration of the complement component C9 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0012309.label: Cutaneous amyloidosis
HP:0012309.definition: The presence of amyloid deposition in the superficial dermis.

HP:0012310.label: Abnormal monocyte count
HP:0012310.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of total monocytes, or their phenotype, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, measured ex vivo.
HP:0012310.comment: Mmonocytes are myeloid mononuclear recirculating leukocytes that can act as a precursor of tissue macrophages, osteoclasts and some populations of tissue dendritic cells.

HP:0012311.label: Increased total monocyte count
HP:0012311.definition: Abnormal increase of absolute number of monocytes in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

HP:0012312.label: Decreased total monocyte count
HP:0012312.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of monocytes in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

HP:0012313.label: Heberden node
HP:0012313.definition: Bony swelling of the distal interphalangeal joint (DIP) associated with the formation of osteophytes (calcific spurs) of the articular (joint) cartilage that are visible radiographically.
HP:0012313.comment: Heberden's nodes are nodular deformities at the distal interphalangeal joint of the fingers (usually the middle and index) and are commonly seen in the elderly. The deformity is created by osteophyte formation and synovial thickening at the margin ofan osteoarthritic joint. Significant functional problems are rarely encountered though patients may suffer with stiffness and pain. Surgical intervention is seldom indicated unless there is severe pain or instability. In such cases, a joint fusion may be appropriate.

HP:0012314.label: Bouchard node
HP:0012314.definition: Bony swelling of the proximal interphalangeal joint (PIP) associated with the formation of osteophytes (calcific spurs) of the articular (joint) cartilage that are visible radiographically.
HP:0012314.comment: Heberden's nodes are generally a sign of osteoarthritis.

HP:0012316.label: Fibrous tissue neoplasm
HP:0012316.definition: Any neoplasm composed of fibrous tissue.

HP:0012317.label: Sacroiliac arthritis
HP:0012317.definition: Inflammation of the sacroiliac joint, generally accompanied by lower back pain.

HP:0012318.label: Occipital neuralgia
HP:0012318.definition: A distinct type of headache characterized by piercing, throbbing, or electric-shock-like chronic pain in the upper neck, back of the head, and behind the ears, usually on one side.
HP:0012318.comment: Typically, the pain of occipital neuralgia begins at the base of the head and spreads upward within the distribution of the greater and lesser occipital nerves. Characteristically, it is neuropathic, with paroxysmal episodes of shooting electric shock-like symptoms.

HP:0012319.label: Absent pigmentation of the abdomen
HP:0012319.definition: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the abdomen.

HP:0012320.label: Absent pigmentation of the limbs
HP:0012320.definition: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the arms and legs.

HP:0012321.label: D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria
HP:0012321.definition: An increased concentration of 2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine.

HP:0012323.label: Sleep myoclonus
HP:0012323.definition: Myoclonus that occurs during the initial phases of sleep.

HP:0012324.label: Myeloid leukemia
HP:0012324.definition: A leukemia that originates from a myeloid cell, that is the blood forming cells of the bone marrow.

HP:0012325.label: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia
HP:0012325.definition: A myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm which is characterized by persistent monocytosis, absence of a Philadelphia chromosome and BCR/ABL fusion gene, fewer than 20 percent blasts in the bone marrow and blood, myelodysplasia, and absence of PDGFRA or PDGFRB rearrangement.

HP:0012326.label: Abnormal celiac artery morphology
HP:0012326.definition: An anomaly of the celiac artery.
HP:0012326.comment: The celiac artery (celiac trunk or truncus coeliacus) is the first major branch of the abdominal aorta.

HP:0012327.label: Celiac artery compression
HP:0012327.comment: This feature may be characterized by abdominal pain related to compression of the celiac artery by fibers of the median arcuate ligament.

HP:0012328.label: Cementoma
HP:0012328.definition: An odontogenic tumor of the cementum of tooth.

HP:0012329.label: Tufted angioma
HP:0012329.definition: A vascular tumor of the skin and subcutaneous tissues and characterized by slow angiomatous proliferation.

HP:0012330.label: Pyelonephritis
HP:0012330.definition: An inflammation of the kidney involving the parenchyma of kidney, the renal pelvis and the kidney calices.
HP:0012330.comment: Pyelonephritis may be unilateral or bilateral and is often characterized by abdominal pain, fever, nausea, and vomiting.

HP:0012331.label: Abnormal autonomic nervous system morphology
HP:0012331.definition: A structural abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.

HP:0012332.label: Abnormal autonomic nervous system physiology
HP:0012332.definition: A functional abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.

HP:0012333.label: Abnormal sudomotor regulation
HP:0012333.definition: An abnormal regulation of the sweat glands by the sympathetic nervous system associated with abnormal perspiration.
HP:0012333.comment: Normally, the cholinergic innervation via the sympathetic nervous system activates muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in sweat glands, thereby leading to perspiration. This terms refers to an abnormally increased or decreased activity of this system.

HP:0012334.label: Extrahepatic cholestasis
HP:0012334.definition: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in large bile ducts outside the liver.

HP:0012335.label: Abnormality of folate metabolism
HP:0012335.definition: An abnormality of the metabolism of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9.

HP:0012337.label: Abnormal homeostasis
HP:0012337.definition: An anomaly in the processes involved in the maintenance of an internal equilibrium.

HP:0012338.label: Abnormal energy expenditure
HP:0012338.definition: Any anomaly in the utilization of energy (calories).

HP:0012339.label: Increased resting energy expenditure
HP:0012339.definition: An increase in the number of calories used per unit time.

HP:0012340.label: Decreased resting energy expenditure
HP:0012340.definition: A reduction in the number of calories used per unit time.

HP:0012341.label: Microprolactinoma
HP:0012341.definition: A pituitary prolactin cell adenoma of less than 10 mm diameter.

HP:0012342.label: Macroprolactinoma
HP:0012342.definition: A pituitary prolactin cell adenoma of more than 10 mm diameter.

HP:0012343.label: Decreased circulating ferritin concentration
HP:0012343.definition: Abnormally reduced concentration of ferritin, a ubiquitous intracellular protein that stores iron, in the blood.
HP:0012343.comment: Ferritin levels measured in serum usually have a direct correlation with the total amount of iron stored in the body, but ferritin levels may also be increased with anemia of chronic disease or in the course of an acute phase reaction.

HP:0012345.label: Abnormal glycosylation
HP:0012345.definition: An anomaly of a glycosylation process, i.e., a process involved in the covalent attachment of a glycosyl residue to a substrate molecule.

HP:0012346.label: Abnormal protein glycosylation
HP:0012346.definition: An anomaly of a protein glycosylation process, i.e., of a protein modification process that results in the addition of a carbohydrate or carbohydrate derivative unit to a protein amino acid, e.g. the addition of glycan chains to proteins.

HP:0012347.label: Abnormal protein N-linked glycosylation
HP:0012347.definition: An anomaly of protein N-linked glycosylation, i.e., an abnormality of the protein glycosylation process in which a carbohydrate or carbohydrate derivative unit is added to a protein via a nitrogen atom in an amino acid residue in a protein.
HP:0012347.comment: Essentially, all proteins (except albumin) that travel through the ER-Golgi network undergo N-linked glycosylation. Glycans promote protein folding, stability, trafficking, localisation, and oligomerisation. They play vital parts in cell-cell interactions and intracellular signaling.

HP:0012348.label: Decreased galactosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012348.definition: A reduction in the amount of galactose residues of N-glycans.
HP:0012348.comment: The majority of complex and hybrid N-glycans have elongated branches that are made by the addition of a beta-linked galactose residue to the initiating N-acetylglucosamine to produce the ubiquitous building block Gal-beta-linked1-4GlcNAc, referred to as a type-2 N-acetyllactosamine (LacNAc) sequence.

HP:0012349.label: Abnormal sialylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012349.definition: An anomaly of the addition of sialic acids to N-linked glycans.
HP:0012349.comment: The most common sialic acids is N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac).

HP:0012350.label: Decreased sialylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012350.definition: Decreased addition of sialic acids to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012351.label: Increased sialylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012351.definition: Increased addition of sialic acids to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012352.label: Abnormal fucosylation of protein N-linked glycosylation
HP:0012352.definition: An anomaly of the addition of fucose sugar units to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012353.label: Decreased fucosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012353.definition: Decreased addition of fucose sugar units to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012354.label: Increased fucosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012354.definition: Increased addition of fucose sugar units to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012355.label: Abnormal mannosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012355.definition: An anomaly of the addition of mannose to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012356.label: Decreased mannosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012356.definition: Reduced addition of mannose to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012357.label: Increased mannosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012357.definition: Increased addition of mannose to N-linked glycans.

HP:0012358.label: Abnormal protein O-linked glycosylation
HP:0012358.definition: An anomaly of protein O-linked glycosylation, i.e., of the process in which a carbohydrate or carbohydrate derivative unit is added to a protein via the hydroxyl group of a serine or threonine residue.

HP:0012359.label: Abnormal fucosylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012359.definition: An anomaly of the addition of fucose sugar units to O-linked glycans.

HP:0012360.label: Decreased fucosylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012360.definition: A reduction of the addition of fucose sugar units to O-linked glycans.

HP:0012361.label: Increased fucosylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012361.definition: Increased addition of fucose sugar units to O-linked glycans.

HP:0012362.label: Abnormal sialylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012362.definition: An anomaly of the addition of sialic acids to O-linked glycans.

HP:0012363.label: Decreased sialylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
HP:0012363.definition: An reduced addition of sialic acids to O-linked glycans.

HP:0012364.label: Decreased urinary potassium
HP:0012364.definition: A decreased concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.

HP:0012365.label: Hypophosphaturia
HP:0012365.definition: An abnormally decreased phosphate concentration in the urine.

HP:0012366.label: Basilar invagination
HP:0012366.definition: Projection of the tip of the dens more than 5 mm above a line joining the hard palate to the posterior lip of the foramen magnum (Chamberlain's line) or the tip of the dens is greater than 7 mm above McGregor's line (the back of the hard palate to the lowest point of the occipital squama).

HP:0012367.label: Extra fontanelles
HP:0012367.definition: Bony defects situated along the cranial suture lines or at the junction of the bone plates of the skull.
HP:0012367.comment: Extra fontanelles include glabellar, metopic, sagittal (parietal) and cerebellar fontanelles.

HP:0012368.label: Flat face
HP:0012368.definition: Absence of concavity or convexity of the face when viewed in profile.
HP:0012368.comment: A useful guide is to imagine that a line connecting the glabella to the anterior most part of the mandible touches the top of the philtrum where it meets the base of the columella. The glabella is the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose. If the superior philtrum is anterior to this line the face is convex, if the superior philtrum is posterior to this line the face is concave.

HP:0012370.label: Prominence of the zygomatic bone
HP:0012370.definition: Large or prominent malar surface of the zygomatic bone of the skull, which is convex and forms the prominence of the 'cheek bones'.

HP:0012371.label: Hyperplasia of midface
HP:0012371.definition: Abnormally anterior positioning of the infraorbital and perialar regions, or increased convexity of the face, or increased nasolabial angle. The midface includes the maxilla, the cheeks, the zygomas, and the infraorbital and perialar regions of the face
HP:0012371.comment: This term represents increased size of the maxilla (upper jaw) in length (increased midface height) or anterior-posterior projection (midface prominence). In the presence of normal mandible size, maxillary prominence may give the appearance of retrognathia.

HP:0012372.label: Abnormal eye morphology
HP:0012372.definition: A structural anomaly of the globe of the eye, or bulbus oculi.

HP:0012373.label: Abnormal eye physiology
HP:0012373.definition: A functional anomaly of the eye.

HP:0012377.label: Hemianopia
HP:0012377.definition: Partial or complete loss of vision in one half of the visual field of one or both eyes.

HP:0012378.label: Fatigue
HP:0012378.definition: A subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation.
HP:0012378.comment: Fatigue is distinct from muscle weakness.

HP:0012379.label: Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity
HP:0012379.definition: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

HP:0012380.label: Reduced tissue carnitine O-palmitoyltransferase 2 activity
HP:0012380.definition: Reduced carnitine O-palmitoyltransferase (CPT II; EC 2.3.1.21) activity or level, leading to a reduced activity of the reaction: palmitoyl-CoA + L-carnitine = CoA + L-palmitoylcarnitine. (CPT II activity can be measured in tissues including fibroblasts, lymphoblasts, and skeletal muscle.

HP:0012381.label: Delayed self-feeding during toddler years
HP:0012381.definition: A delay in the development of skills required to feed oneself in the toddler period (between one and three years of age).

HP:0012382.label: Left-to-right shunt
HP:0012382.definition: Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from the left side of the heart to the right.

HP:0012383.label: Bidirectional shunt
HP:0012383.definition: Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from both right side of the heart to the left and vice versa.

HP:0012384.label: Rhinitis
HP:0012384.definition: Inflammation of the nasal mucosa with nasal congestion.

HP:0012385.label: Camptodactyly
HP:0012385.definition: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers or toes cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.
exact_synonyms: Permanent flexion of the finger or toe

HP:0012386.label: Absent hallux
HP:0012386.definition: Aplasia of the hallux, that is, a development defect such that the big toe does not develop.

HP:0012387.label: Bronchitis
HP:0012387.definition: Inflammation of the large airways in the lung including any part of the bronchi from the primary bronchi to the tertiary bronchi.

HP:0012388.label: Acute bronchitis
HP:0012388.definition: Inflammation of the large airways of the lung with rapid onset and short course usually associated with cough, mucus production, shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness.

HP:0012389.label: Appendicular hypotonia
HP:0012389.definition: Muscular hypotonia of one or more limbs.

HP:0012390.label: Anal fissure
HP:0012390.definition: A small tear in the thin, moist tissue (mucosa) that lines the anus. It appears as a crack or slit in the mucous membrane of the anus.

HP:0012391.label: Hyporeflexia of upper limbs
HP:0012391.definition: Reduced intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in the upper limbs. Reflexes are elicited by stretching the tendon of a muscle, e.g., by tapping.

HP:0012392.label: Jaw hyporeflexia
HP:0012392.definition: Reduced intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in jaw.
HP:0012392.comment: The jaw jerk is elicited by the examiner placing the tip of the index finger on a relaxed jaw, one that is about one-third open. One then taps briskly on the index finger with the other hand and notes the speed as the mandible is flexed.

HP:0012393.label: Allergy
HP:0012393.definition: An allergy is an immune response or reaction to substances that are usually not harmful.

HP:0012394.label: Iodine contrast allergy
HP:0012394.definition: Allergy to iodine contrast media used in radiological studies.

HP:0012395.label: Seasonal allergy
HP:0012395.definition: An allergy experienced at a particular time of year when trees or grasses pollinate and elicit an allergic reaction.

HP:0012396.label: Biliary dyskinesia
HP:0012396.definition: A motility disorder characterized by biliary colic in the absence of gallstones with a reduced gallbladder ejection fraction.

HP:0012397.label: Aortic atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0012397.definition: The presence of atheromas or atherosclerotic plaques in the aorta.

HP:0012398.label: Peripheral edema
HP:0012398.definition: An abnormal accumulation of interstitial fluid in the soft tissues of the limbs.

HP:0012399.label: Pressure ulcer
HP:0012399.definition: A type of ulcer that is caused when an area of skin is subject to pressure over a prolonged period of time, ranging in range in severity from patches of discolored skin to open wounds that expose the underlying bone or muscle. The most common sites are the sacrum, coccyx, heels and the hips.
HP:0012399.comment: Pressure ulcers tend to affect persons with reduced mobility who are bedridden or wheelchair-bound.

HP:0012400.label: Abnormal circulating aldolase concentration
HP:0012400.definition: An abnormal concentration of aldolase in the serum. Aldolase is an enzyme responsible for converting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into the triose phosphates dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.
HP:0012400.comment: The reaction catalyzed by aldolase is a component of the glycolysis pathway.

HP:0012401.label: Abnormal urine alpha-ketoglutarate concentration
HP:0012401.definition: A deviation from normal of the concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
HP:0012401.comment: Note that alpha-ketoglutaric acid is also known as 2-ketoglutaric acid, alpha-ketoglutaric acid, 2-xxoglutaric acid, and oxoglutaric acid.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of urine alpha ketoglutarate concentration

HP:0012402.label: Increased urine alpha-ketoglutarate concentration
HP:0012402.definition: A greater than normal concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
HP:0012402.comment: Note that alpha-ketoglutaric acid is also known as 2-ketoglutaric acid, alpha-ketoglutaric acid, 2-xxoglutaric acid, and oxoglutaric acid.

HP:0012403.label: Decreased urine alpha-ketoglutarate concentration
HP:0012403.definition: A lower than normal concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
HP:0012403.comment: Note that alpha-ketoglutaric acid is also known as 2-ketoglutaric acid, alpha-ketoglutaric acid, 2-xxoglutaric acid, and oxoglutaric acid.

HP:0012404.label: Abnormal urine citrate concentration
HP:0012404.definition: A deviation from normal of the concentration of citrate(3-) in the urine.

HP:0012405.label: Hypocitraturia
HP:0012405.definition: A lower than normal concentration of citrate(3-) in the urine.

HP:0012406.label: Hypercitraturia
HP:0012406.definition: A greater than normal concentration of citrate(3-) in the urine.

HP:0012407.label: Scissor gait
HP:0012407.definition: A type of spastic paraparetic gait in which the muscle tone in the adductors is marked. It is characterized by hypertonia and flexion in the legs, hips and pelvis accompanied by extreme adduction leading to the knees and thighs hitting, or sometimes even crossing, in a scissors-like movement. The opposing muscles (abductors) become comparatively weak from lack of use.
HP:0012407.comment: Scissor gait is a form of gait abnormality primarily associated with spastic cerebral palsy.

HP:0012408.label: Medullary nephrocalcinosis
HP:0012408.definition: The deposition of calcium salts in the parenchyma of the renal medulla (innermost part of the kidney).

HP:0012409.label: Cortical nephrocalcinosis
HP:0012409.definition: The deposition of calcium salts in the parenchyma of the renal cortex (the outer portion of the kidney between the renal capsule and the renal medulla).

HP:0012410.label: Pure red cell aplasia
HP:0012410.definition: A type of anemia resulting from suppression of erythropoiesis with little or no abnormality of leukocyte or platelet production. Erythroblasts are virtually absent in bone marrow; however, leukocyte and platelet production show little or no reduction.
HP:0012410.comment: Pure red cell aplasia results from a maturation arrest occurs in the formation of erythrocytes.

HP:0012411.label: Premature pubarche
HP:0012411.definition: The onset of growth of pubic hair at an earlier age than normal.

HP:0012412.label: Premature adrenarche
HP:0012412.definition: Onset of adrenarche at an earlier age than usual.
HP:0012412.comment: Adrenarche is an early sexual maturation stage that typically occurs at around 6 to 8 years of age, during which the adrenal cortex begins to secrete increased levels of androgens resulting from the development of the zona reticularis in the adrenal cortex. Note that pubarche refers to the development of pubic hair, axillary hair, and adult sweat gland (apocrine) odor. The physical features associated with pubarche reflect the onset of adrenarche, which refers to the pubertal maturation of the adrenal and is associated with increased secretion of an adrenal hormone called dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS).

HP:0012413.label: Notched primary central incisor
HP:0012413.definition: The presence of a V-shaped indentation (notch) in the primary central incisor.

HP:0012414.label: Duodenal atrophy
HP:0012414.definition: Wasting or decrease in size of all or part of the duodenum.

HP:0012415.label: Abnormal blood gas level
HP:0012415.definition: An abnormality of the partial pressure of oxygen or carbon dioxide in the arterial blood.

HP:0012416.label: Hypercapnia
HP:0012416.definition: Abnormally elevated blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level.

HP:0012417.label: Hypocapnia
HP:0012417.definition: Abnormally reduced blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level.
exact_synonyms: Reduced carbon dioxide in the blood

HP:0012418.label: Hypoxemia
HP:0012418.definition: An abnormally low level of blood oxygen.
HP:0012418.comment: Note that hypoxemia is defined as a condition where arterial oxygen tension is below normal (80-100mmHg). Hypoxia is defined as the failure of oxygenation at the tissue level. Hypoxia is not measured directly by a standard laboratory value.

HP:0012419.label: Hyperoxemia
HP:0012419.definition: An abnormally high level of blood oxygen.
HP:0012419.comment: Note that hyperoxemia is defined as a condition where arterial oxygen tension is above normal (80-100mmHg). Hyperoxia is defined as increased oxygen tension at the tissue level. Hyperoxia is not measured directly by a standard laboratory value.

HP:0012420.label: Meconium stained amniotic fluid
HP:0012420.definition: Amniotic fluid containing the earliest stools of a mammalian infant.
HP:0012420.comment: Meconium may be expelled into the amniotic fluid before birth in response to fetal distress. If meconium is aspirated by the fetus, it may lead to meconium aspiration syndrome.

HP:0012421.label: Congenital absence of foreskin
HP:0012421.definition: Congenital lack of the skin of prepuce of penis, that is, of the double-layered fold of skin and mucous membrane that covers the glans penis.
HP:0012421.comment: Absence of the foreskin can be accompanied by Cryptorchidism and Hypospadias, which should be coded separately.

HP:0012422.label: Villous hypertrophy of choroid plexus
HP:0012422.comment: The most common location for overgrowth is the lateral ventricles. The choroid plexus folds into many villi around capillaries, creating frond-like processes that project into the ventricles. The terms choroid plexus hypertrophy or choroid plexus hyperplasia are used interchangeably to refer to an increase in size of these structures. Diffuse villous hyperplasia of choroid plexus (DVHCP) is a rare condition which is characterized by the presence of diffuse enlargement of the entire choroid plexus throughout the length of the choroidal fissure and overproduction of CSF.
related_synonyms: Diffuse villous hypertrophy of choroid plexus

HP:0012423.label: Colonic inertia
HP:0012423.definition: The inability of the colon to modify stool to an acceptable consistency and move the stool from the cecum to the rectosigmoid area at least once every three days.

HP:0012424.label: Chorioretinitis
HP:0012424.definition: An inflammation of the choroid and retina.
HP:0012424.comment: Chorioretinitis is a form of posterior uveitis. Note that the term Chorioretinitis suggests that the origin of the process is predominantly in the choroid while Retinitis suggests that the process is mainly in the retina.

HP:0012425.label: Stercoral ulcer
HP:0012425.definition: An ulcer of the colon due to pressure and irritation from retained fecal masses.
HP:0012425.comment: Stercoral ulceration is the loss of bowel integrity from the pressure effects of inspissated feces. The lesion usually occurs in constipated, bedridden patients and presents as an isolated lesion in the rectosigmoid area.

HP:0012426.label: Optic disc drusen
HP:0012426.definition: Optic disc drusen are acellular, calcified deposits within the optic nerve head. Optic disc drusen are congenital and developmental anomalies of the optic nerve head, representing hyaline-containing bodies that, over time, appear as elevated, lumpy irregularities on the anterior portion of the optic nerve.
HP:0012426.comment: Optic disc drusen can lead to an elevated disk and thus mimic disk swelling (pseudopapilledema).

HP:0012427.label: Increased femoral anteversion
HP:0012427.definition: An increased degree of femoral version, which is defined as the angular difference between axis of femoral neck and transcondylar axis of the knee. Thus, femoral anteversion is an inward twisting of the femur that causes the knees and feet to turn inward.
HP:0012427.comment: Femoral neck anteversion (FNA), also called femoral torsion or femoral version, is the angle between the projection of two lines in the axial plane perpendicular to the femoral shaft; one line going through the proximal femoral neck region and the second one through the distal condylar region, indicating the degree of twist of the femur. Excessive femoral anteversion is a common cause of in-toeing that first presents in early childhood. See Figure 1 of PMID:32579722.

HP:0012429.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the cerebral white matter
HP:0012429.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the cerebral white matter.

HP:0012430.label: Cerebral white matter hypoplasia
HP:0012430.definition: Underdevelopment of the cerebral white matter.

HP:0012431.label: Episodic fatigue
HP:0012431.definition: Intermittent and recurrent bouts of a subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation.

HP:0012432.label: Chronic fatigue
HP:0012432.definition: Subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation that persists for six months or longer.
HP:0012432.comment: Note that chronic fatigue can be a symptom of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS), which is characterized by profound fatigue that is not improved by bed rest and that may be worsened by physical or mental activity. Symptoms of CFS may include weakness, muscle pain, impaired memory, impaired mental concentration, and insomnia, which can result in reduced participation in daily activities.

HP:0012433.label: Abnormal social behavior
HP:0012433.definition: An abnormality of actions or reactions of a person exhibited during social interactions with other individuals.

HP:0012434.label: Delayed early-childhood social milestone development
HP:0012434.definition: A failure to meet one or more age-related milestones of social behavior.
HP:0012434.comment: This term may be applied to describe a child whose social development is delayed compared to age-related norms. For instance, at the age of three months, a child smiles in response to social interaction;. aAt the age of seven months, a child responds to the facial expressions of others;. aAnd at the age of 12 months, a child is shy around strangers.

HP:0012435.label: Ventral shortening of foreskin
HP:0012435.definition: Reduction in length of the ventral (lower) skin of prepuce of penis.

HP:0012436.label: Nonocclusive coronary artery atherosclerosis
HP:0012436.definition: Coronary disease that has not progressed to the point of causing significant occlusion (blockage) of the coronary arteries.

HP:0012437.label: Abnormal gallbladder morphology
HP:0012437.definition: A structural anomaly of the gallbladder.

HP:0012438.label: Abnormal gallbladder physiology
HP:0012438.definition: A functional anomaly of the gallbladder.

HP:0012439.label: Abnormal biliary tract physiology
HP:0012439.definition: A functional abnormality of the biliary tree.

HP:0012440.label: Abnormal biliary tract morphology
