HP:0012440.definition: A structural abnormality of the biliary tree.

HP:0012441.label: Sphincter of Oddi dyskinesia
HP:0012441.definition: Reduced motility through the sphincter of Oddi, resulting in impedance of bile and pancreatic juice flow from the common bile duct into the duodenum.
HP:0012441.comment: The sphincter of Oddi (also known as sphincter of ampulla) is a muscular valve that controls the flow of bile and pancreatic juice through the ampulla of Vater into the second part of the duodenum. Increased tone of the sphincter or disturbance in the coordination of contraction of the biliary ducts prevents normal emptying of the biliary tree. This may result in biliary pain, common bile duct dilation and episodes of pancreatitis.

HP:0012442.label: Gallbladder dyskinesia
HP:0012442.definition: Reduced motility of the gallbladder with reduced emptying fraction.
HP:0012442.comment: Patients with this gallbladder dyskinesia present with biliary-type pain but no evidence of gallstones in the gallbladder. The diagnosis is made by performing a radionuclide investigation of the gallbladder ejection fraction. An abnormal gallbladder ejection fraction has a value less than 40 percent.

HP:0012443.label: Abnormal brain morphology
HP:0012443.definition: A structural abnormality of the brain, which has as its parts the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.

HP:0012444.label: Brain atrophy
HP:0012444.definition: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of brain tissue that was once present.

HP:0012446.label: Decreased CSF 5-methyltetrahydrofolate concentration
HP:0012446.definition: A reduced concentration of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate(2-) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). 5-methyltetrahydrofolate is the active folate metabolite.

HP:0012447.label: Abnormal myelination
HP:0012447.definition: Any anomaly in the process by which myelin sheaths are formed and maintained around neurons.

HP:0012449.label: Sacroiliac joint synovitis
HP:0012449.definition: Inflammation of the synovial membrane of the sacroiliac joint.

HP:0012450.label: Chronic constipation
HP:0012450.definition: Constipation for longer than three months with fewer than 3 bowel movements per week, straining, lumpy or hard stools, and a sensation of anorectal obstruction or incomplete defecation.

HP:0012451.label: Acute constipation
HP:0012451.definition: Constipation of sudden onset and lasting for less than three months.

HP:0012452.label: Restless legs
HP:0012452.definition: An irresistible urge to move the legs, usually accompanied by unpleasant sensations deep within the limbs. Symptoms typically begin or worsen during periods of rest or inactivity, are most pronounced in the evening or at night, and are temporarily relieved by movement such as walking or stretching. The disturbance often interferes with the initiation or maintenance of sleep.
HP:0012452.comment: Restless legs syndrome is a disorder characterized by aching or burning sensations in the legs that occur prior to sleep or may awaken the affected individuals. Complying with an irresistible urge to move the affected limbs brings temporary relief. Sleep may become disrupted, resulting in excessive daytime hypersomnolence.

HP:0012453.label: Bilateral wrist flexion contracture
HP:0012453.definition: A chronic loss of wrist joint motion on the right and left sides.

HP:0012454.label: Unilateral wrist flexion contracture
HP:0012454.definition: A chronic loss of wrist joint motion on one side only.

HP:0012456.label: Medial arterial calcification
HP:0012456.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of arteries.
HP:0012456.comment: Medial arterial calcification causes stiffening and decreased compliance of the affected arteries.

HP:0012457.label: Medial calcification of medium-sized arteries
HP:0012457.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of medium-sized (muscular or distributive) arteries.

HP:0012458.label: Medial calcification of small arteries
HP:0012458.definition: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of small arteries.
HP:0012458.comment: The general construction of small arteries is very similar to that of muscular arteries. The media is still muscular and has up to 8-10 layers of smooth muscle cells. A discussion on the logical definition can be found here: https://github.com/obophenotype/human-phenotype-ontology/issues/6877.

HP:0012459.label: Hypnic headache
HP:0012459.definition: A headache disorder that occurs exclusively at night, waking the affected individual from sleep.
HP:0012459.comment: Hypnic headache can be unilateral or bilateral, and is often but not always described as throbbing. The pain begins abruptly and can last from 15 minutes to 6 hours, although typically it is about 30-60 minutes.

HP:0012460.label: Dysmorphic inferior cerebellar vermis
HP:0012460.definition: A structural anomaly of the inferior portion of the vermis of cerebellum.

HP:0012461.label: Bacteriuria
HP:0012461.definition: The presence of bacteria in the urine.
HP:0012461.comment: The urine is normally bacteria-free. The term refers to bacteria from the urinary tract and not to bacteria found in the urine because of contamination from the surrounding tissues. Significant bacteriuria is a sign of urinary tract infection.

HP:0012462.label: Chin myoclonus
HP:0012462.definition: Involuntary and irregular twitches of the chin.

HP:0012463.label: Elevated transferrin saturation
HP:0012463.definition: An above normal level of saturation of serum transferrin with iron.
HP:0012463.comment: Transferrins are iron-binding blood plasma glycoproteins that control the level of free iron in biological fluids. The transferrin saturation test (TSAT) refers to the ratio of serum iron to total iron-binding capacity, expressed as a percentage. Transferrin saturations of less than 20% indicate iron deficiency, while transferrin saturations of more than 50% suggest iron overload. Note that the results of the TSAT can be influenced by inflammation.

HP:0012464.label: Decreased transferrin saturation
HP:0012464.definition: A below normal level of saturation of serum transferrin with iron.
HP:0012464.comment: Transferrins are iron-binding blood plasma glycoproteins that control the level of free iron in biological fluids. The transferrin saturation test (TSAT) refers to the ratio of serum iron to total iron-binding capacity, expressed as a percentage. Transferrin saturations of less than 20% indicate iron deficiency, while transferrin saturations of more than 50% suggest iron overload. Note that the results of the TSAT can be influenced by inflammation.

HP:0012465.label: Elevated hepatic iron concentration
HP:0012465.definition: An increased level of iron in liver tissues.
HP:0012465.comment: This abnormality can be measured by liver biopsy or by hepatic magnetic resonance imaging.

HP:0012466.label: Chronic respiratory acidosis
HP:0012466.definition: Longstanding impairment in ventilation such that the partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) is elevated above the upper limit of the reference range (more than 45 mm Hg), with a normal or near-normal pH secondary to renal compensation and an elevated serum bicarbonate levels (more than30 mEq/L).

HP:0012467.label: Acute respiratory acidosis
HP:0012467.definition: Sudden onset of impairment in ventilation such that the removal of carbon dioxide by the respiratory system is less than the production of carbon dioxide in the tissues, leading to an elevation of the partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) above the normal limits (more than 45 mm Hg) with an accompanying acidemia (pH less than 7.35).

HP:0012468.label: Chronic acidosis
HP:0012468.definition: Longstanding abnormal acid accumulation or depletion of base.

HP:0012469.label: Infantile spasms
HP:0012469.definition: Infantile spasms represent a subset of "epileptic spasms". Infantile Spasms are epileptic spasms starting in the first year of life (infancy).

HP:0012470.label: Setting-sun eye phenomenon
HP:0012470.definition: An ophthalmologic sign in young children resulting from upward-gaze paresis. In this condition, the eyes appear driven downward, the sclera may be seen between the upper eyelid and the iris, and part of the lower pupil may be covered by the lower eyelid.
HP:0012470.comment: Setting-sun eye phenomenon can also be transiently elicited in healthy infants up to 7 months of age by changes of position or removal of light (benign setting-sun phenomenon). When persistent, this sign is one of the most frequent markers of elevated intracranial pressure.

HP:0012471.label: Thick vermilion border
HP:0012471.definition: Increased width of the skin of vermilion border region of upper lip.

HP:0012472.label: Eclabion
HP:0012472.definition: A turning outward of the lip or lips, that is, eversion of the lips.

HP:0012474.label: Carotid artery occlusion
HP:0012474.definition: Complete obstruction of a carotid artery.
HP:0012474.comment: Carotid artery occlusion is usually caused by caused by atherosclerosis.

HP:0012475.label: Decreased circulating level of specific antibody
HP:0012475.definition: The presence of normal overall immunoglobulin levels with deficiency of specific immunoglobulins directed against a specific antigen or microorganism.

HP:0012476.label: Decreased specific pneumococcal antibody level
HP:0012476.definition: The presence of normal overall immunoglobulin levels with deficiency of specific immunoglobulins directed against pneumococci.

HP:0012477.label: Vocal tremor
HP:0012477.definition: A wavering, unsteady voice that reflects involuntary and approximately sinusoidal oscillation of motor unit firings of laryngeal muscles. Vocal tremor results in low frequency modulations of voice frequency or amplitude and intermittent voice instability.

HP:0012478.label: Temporomandibular joint ankylosis
HP:0012478.definition: Bony fusion of the mandibular condyle to the base of the skull, resulting in limitation of jaw opening.

HP:0012479.label: Temporomandibular joint crepitus
HP:0012479.definition: Noises from the temporomandibular joint during mandibular movement (e.g., chewing). Temporomandibular joint crepitus is often described as a clicking, popping, grating sound.

HP:0012481.label: Cerebral venous angioma
HP:0012481.definition: A congenital malformation of veins which drain normal brain characterized by a caput medusae or an umbrellalike convergence of multiple venules on a single, or occasionally multiple, enlarged parenchymal or medullary vein, like the trunk of a tree or the shank of an umbrella. This dilated terminal vein penetrates the cortex to drain either (a) superficially to cortical veins or sinuses, (b) deeply to subependymal veins of the lateral ventricle and then into the galenic system, (c) to the fourth ventricle and then to the pontomesencephalic vein, or (d) to the precentral cerebellar vein and into the galenic system.
HP:0012481.comment: DVA is characterized by a caput medusae or an umbrellalike convergence of multiple venules on a single, or occasionally multiple, enlarged parenchymal or medullary vein, like the trunk of a tree or the shank of an umbrella. This dilated terminal vein penetrates the cortex to drain either (a) superficially to cortical veins or sinuses, (b) deeply to subependymal veins of the lateral ventricle and then into the galenic system, (c) to the fourth ventricle and then to the pontomesencephalic vein, or (d) to the precentral cerebellar vein and into the galenic system.

HP:0012482.label: Frontal venous angioma
HP:0012482.definition: A venous angioma of the frontal lobe of the brain.

HP:0012483.label: Abnormal alpha granules
HP:0012483.definition: Defective structure, size or content of alpha granules, platelet organelles that contain several growth factors destined for release during platelet activation at sites of vessel wall injury.
HP:0012483.comment: This feature can be observed by electron microscopy. Alpha granules normally contain a number of proteins including von Willebrand factor, and fibrinogen.

HP:0012484.label: Abnormal dense granules
HP:0012484.definition: Defective structure, size or content of dense granules, platelet organelles that contain granules proaggregatory factors such as adenosine diphosphate (ADP), adenosine triphosphate (ATP), ionized calcium, histamine and serotonin.
HP:0012484.comment: This feature can be observed by electron microscopy.

HP:0012485.label: Abnormal surface-connected open canalicular system
HP:0012485.definition: An anomaly of the invaginations of the surface membrane that form the open canalicular system (OCS). The OCS serve as the pathway for transport of substances into the cells and as conduits for the discharge of alpha granule products secreted during the platelet release reaction.

HP:0012487.label: Cerebellopontine angle arachnoid cyst
HP:0012487.definition: An arachnoid cyst located at the margin of the cerebellum and pons.
HP:0012487.comment: The cerebellopontine angle is in the posterior fossa.

HP:0012488.label: Intraventricular arachnoid cyst
HP:0012488.definition: An arachnoid cyst located within the ventricular system.
HP:0012488.comment: Arachnoid cysts very rarely occur within the ventricular system, where no arachnoid tissue exists.

HP:0012489.label: Suprasellar arachnoid cyst
HP:0012489.definition: An arachnoid cyst that progressively enlarges from an abnormality in the membrane of Liliequist or in the interpeduncular cistern, and typically, expands from the prepontine space, displacing the floor of the third ventricle upwards, the pituitary stalk and optic chiasm upwards and forwards, and the mammillary bodies upwards and backwards.
HP:0012489.comment: As the cyst increases in size it fills and occludes the third ventricle, and distorts and blocks the aqueduct, which finally results in hydrocephalus.

HP:0012490.label: Panniculitis
HP:0012490.comment: Panniculitis most commonly affects the skin and characterized by reddened subcutaneous nodules.

HP:0012491.label: Abnormal dense tubular system
HP:0012491.definition: An anomaly of the intracellular membrane complexes known as the dense tubular system.
HP:0012491.comment: The dense tubular system (DTS) functions to regulate platelet activation by sequestering or releasing calcium, similar to the sarcotubules of skeletal muscle. In resting platelets, the DTS exists as thin elongated membranes. Within 10 seconds of the addition of thrombin, platelets show a major ultrastructural change in their DTS: from the thin elongated form to a rounded vesicular form.

HP:0012492.label: Cerebral artery stenosis
HP:0012492.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of a cerebral artery.

HP:0012493.label: Middle cerebral artery stenosis
HP:0012493.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of the middle cerebral artery.

HP:0012494.label: Anterior cerebral artery stenosis
HP:0012494.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of the anterior cerebral artery.

HP:0012495.label: Posterior cerebral artery stenosis
HP:0012495.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of the posterior cerebral artery.

HP:0012496.label: Reduced maximal inspiratory pressure
HP:0012496.definition: A decrease in the maximum amount of negative pressure a person can generate during an inhalation.

HP:0012497.label: Reduced maximal expiratory pressure
HP:0012497.definition: A decrease in the maximum amount of pressure of expired air achieved by a person after a full inspiration.

HP:0012498.label: Nuchal cord
HP:0012498.definition: A complication of pregnancy and delivery in which the umbilical cord wraps around the fetal neck once or multiple times.

HP:0012499.label: Descending aortic dissection
HP:0012499.definition: A separation of the layers within the wall of the descending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.
HP:0012499.comment: According to the Stanford classification, type B aortic dissection begins beyond brachiocephalic vessels (begins distal to the left subclavian artery).

HP:0012500.label: Verrucous papule
HP:0012500.definition: A wartlike (with multiple small elevated projections) papule.

HP:0012501.label: Abnormal brainstem white matter morphology
HP:0012501.definition: An anomaly of the white matter of brainstem.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the brainstem white matter

HP:0012502.label: Abnormality of the internal capsule
HP:0012502.definition: An anomaly of the internal capsule, which is an area of white matter in the brain that separates the caudate nucleus and the thalamus from the putamen and the globus pallidus.

HP:0012503.label: Abnormal pituitary gland morphology
HP:0012503.definition: An anomaly of the pituitary gland.

HP:0012504.label: Abnormal size of pituitary gland
HP:0012504.definition: A deviation from the normal size of the pituitary gland.

HP:0012505.label: Enlarged pituitary gland
HP:0012505.definition: An abnormally increased size of the pituitary gland.

HP:0012506.label: Small pituitary gland
HP:0012506.definition: An abnormally decreased size of the pituitary gland.

HP:0012507.label: Weakness of orbicularis oculi muscle
HP:0012507.definition: Reduced strength of the orbicularis oculi, the circumorbital muscle in the face that closes the eyelid.

HP:0012508.label: Metamorphopsia
HP:0012508.definition: A visual anomaly in which images appear distorted. A grid of straight lines appears wavy and parts of the grid may appear blank.

HP:0012510.label: Extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid accumulation
HP:0012510.definition: An increased amount of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the subarachnoid space.

HP:0012511.label: Temporal optic disc pallor
HP:0012511.definition: A pale yellow discoloration of the temporal (lateral) portion of the optic disc.
HP:0012511.comment: Temporal pallor is seen in conditions that selectively affect the papillo-macular bundle. The word temporal refers to the temporal bone at the side of the head.

HP:0012512.label: Diffuse optic disc pallor
HP:0012512.definition: A pale yellow discoloration of the entire optic disc.
HP:0012512.comment: Temporal pallor is seen in conditions that selectively affect the papillo-macular bundle. The word temporal refers to the temporal bone at the side of the head.

HP:0012513.label: Upper limb pain
HP:0012513.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the arm.

HP:0012514.label: Lower limb pain
HP:0012514.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the leg.

HP:0012515.label: Hip flexor weakness
HP:0012515.definition: Reduced ability to flex the femur, that is, to pull the knee upward.
HP:0012515.comment: Hip flexion is mediated by multiple muscles including the iliopsoas, the rectus femoris, the sartorius, and several muscles from the medial compartment of thigh.

HP:0012516.label: Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia
HP:0012516.definition: An extreme form of tetralogy of Fallot characterized by absence of flow from the right ventricle to the pulmonary arteries.
HP:0012516.comment: Tetralogy of Fallot with Pulmonary Atresia (TOF/PA) is a complex lesion with many different anatomic variants. The primary source of variability in this lesion is in the anatomy of the pulmonary arteries, with the spectrum ranging from well-formed, confluent pulmonary artery branches to completely absent native pulmonary arteries and major aorto-pulmonary collaterals (MAPCA's) providing all the pulmonary blood flow. The majority of cases fall somewhere in between these two ends of the spectrum, with the total pulmonary blood flow provided by a combination of diminutive native pulmonary arteries and multiple MAPCA.

HP:0012517.label: Reduced circulating catalase activity
HP:0012517.definition: Activity or concentration of catalase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
HP:0012517.comment: Catalase catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen.

HP:0012518.label: Abnormal circle of Willis morphology
HP:0012518.definition: An anomaly of the circle of Willis, also known as the cerebral arterial circle.
HP:0012518.comment: The circle of Willis is a circulatory anastomosis in the brain comprised of the anterior cerebral arteries, the anterior communicating artery, the internal carotid arteries, the posterior cerebral arteries, and the posterior communicating arteries.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the cerebral arterial circle

HP:0012519.label: Hypoplastic posterior communicating artery
HP:0012519.definition: A developmental anomnaly characterized by underdevelopment of the posterior communicating artery.
HP:0012519.comment: The posterior communicating arteries connect the internal carotid artery just proximal to its bifurcation into the anterior cerebral artery and middle cerebral artery with the posterior cerebral artery. The posterior communicating artery is part of the circle of Willis.

HP:0012520.label: Dilation of Virchow-Robin spaces
HP:0012520.definition: Increased dimensions of the Virchow-Robin spaces (also known as perivascular spaces), which surround the walls of vessels as they course from the subarachnoid space through the brain parenchyma. Perivascular spaces are commonly microscopic, and not visible on conventional neuroimaging. This term refers to an increase of size of these spaces such that they are visible on neuroimaging (usually magnetic resonance imaging). The dilatations are regular cavities that always contain a patent artery.
HP:0012520.comment: Virchow-Robin spaces are commonly seen at magnetic resonance imaging. These perivascular spaces as fluid-filled spaces that follow the typical course of a vessel as it goes through gray or white matter. The spaces have signal intensity similar to that of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) on all magnetic resonance sequences.

HP:0012521.label: Optic nerve aplasia
HP:0012521.definition: Congenital absence of the optic nerve.

HP:0012522.label: Spider hemangioma
HP:0012522.definition: A form of telangiectasis characterized by a central elevated red dot the size of a pinhead, representing an arteriole, with numerous small blood vessels that radiate out thereby resembling the legs of a spider. Characteristically, compression of the central arteriole causes the entire lesion to blanch, and the lesion quickly refills once the compression is released.
HP:0012522.comment: Spider hemangiomas are up to a few centimeters in diameter.

HP:0012523.label: Oral aversion
HP:0012523.definition: Reluctance or refusal of a child to be breastfed or eat, manifested as gagging, vomiting, turning head away from food, or avoidance of sensation in or around the mouth (i.e. toothbrushing or face-washing).

HP:0012524.label: Abnormal platelet shape
HP:0012524.definition: A deviation from the normal discoid platelet shape.

HP:0012525.label: Abnormal alpha granule distribution
HP:0012525.definition: An anomalous location and arrangement of platelet alpha granules.

HP:0012526.label: Absence of alpha granules
HP:0012526.definition: A lack of platelet alpha granules. This typically results in the gray appearance of platelets in giemsa stained blood smears.

HP:0012527.label: Abnormal alpha granule content
HP:0012527.definition: A deviation from the normal contents of the platelet alpha granules, which normally contain hemostatic proteins such as fibrinogen, von Willebrand factor, and growth factors such as platelet-derived growth factor.
HP:0012527.comment: The alpha granules contain hemostatic proteins such as fibrinogen, von Willebrand factor, and growth factors such as platelet-derived growth factor.

HP:0012528.label: Abnormal number of alpha granules
HP:0012528.definition: A deviation from the normal count of alpha granules per thrombocyte.

HP:0012529.label: Abnormal dense granule content
HP:0012529.definition: A deviation from the normal contents of the platelet alpha granules, which normally contain adenosine triphosphate (ATP), adenosine diphosphate (ADP), serotonin, calcium, and pyrophosphate, which are secreted when platelets are activated.

HP:0012530.label: Abnormal number of dense granules
HP:0012530.definition: A deviation from the normal count of dense granules per thrombocyte.

HP:0012531.label: Pain
HP:0012531.definition: An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage, or described in terms of such damage.

HP:0012532.label: Chronic pain
HP:0012532.definition: Persistent pain, usually defined as pain that has lasted longer than 3 to 6 months.
HP:0012532.comment: Acute pain is provoked by a specific disease or injury, serves a useful biologic purpose, is associated with skeletal muscle spasm and sympathetic nervous system activation, and is self-limited. Chronic pain, in contrast, may be considered a disease state. It is pain that outlasts the normal time of healing.

HP:0012533.label: Allodynia
HP:0012533.definition: Pain due to a stimulus that does not normally provoke pain.

HP:0012534.label: Dysesthesia
HP:0012534.definition: Painful sensations elicited by a nonpainful cutaneous stimulus such as a light touch or gentle stroking over affected areas of the body. Sometimes referred to as hyperpathia or hyperalgesia. Often perceived as an intense burning, dyesthesias may outlast the stimulus by several seconds.

HP:0012535.label: Abnormal synaptic transmission
HP:0012535.definition: An anomaly in the communication from a neuron to a target across a synapse. This is a four step process, comprising (i) synthesis and storage of neurotransmitters; (ii) neurotransmitter release; (iii) activation of postsynaptic receptors by the neurotransmitter; and (iv) inactivation of the neurotransmitter. Thus, this term is defined as an anomaly of neurotransmitter metabolic process.

HP:0012536.label: Maternal anticardiolipin antibody positive
HP:0012536.definition: The presence of circulating autoantibodies to anticardiolipin in the mother.
HP:0012536.comment: There have been reports of cerebral infarction in a newborns in association with elevated maternal anticardiolipin antibodies.

HP:0012537.label: Food intolerance
HP:0012537.definition: A detrimental reaction to a food, beverage, food additive, or compound found in foods that produces symptoms in one or more body organs and systems that is not mediated by an immune reaction.

HP:0012538.label: Gluten intolerance
HP:0012538.definition: A detrimental reaction to the presence of gluten in food, which may include abdominal pain, fatigue, headaches and paresthesia, or celiac disease.

HP:0012539.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
HP:0012539.definition: A type of lymphoma characterized microscopically by the absence of multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells.

HP:0012540.label: Axillary epidermoid cyst
HP:0012540.definition: An epidermoid cyst in the armpit.

HP:0012541.label: Cephalohematoma
HP:0012541.definition: Hemorrhage between the skull and periosteum of a newborn resulting from rupture of blood vessels that cross the periosteum.
HP:0012541.comment: Cephalohematoma is generally caused by trauma during labor.

HP:0012543.label: Hemosiderinuria
HP:0012543.definition: The presence of hemosiderin in the urine.
HP:0012543.comment: Hemosiderinuria leads to a brown color of urine. It is a marker of chronic intravascular hemolysis, in which hemoglobin is released from RBCs into the bloodstream in excess of the binding capacity of haptoglobin.

HP:0012544.label: Elevated circulating aldolase concentration
HP:0012544.definition: Concentration of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
HP:0012544.comment: Aldolase is an enzyme responsible for converting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into the triose phosphates dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.

HP:0012545.label: Reduced circulating aldolase concentration
HP:0012545.definition: Concentration of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
HP:0012545.comment: Aldolase is an enzyme responsible for converting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into the triose phosphates dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.

HP:0012546.label: Skewed maternal X inactivation
HP:0012546.definition: A deviation from equal (50%) inactivation of each parental X chromosome in maternal cells.
HP:0012546.comment: X chromosome inactivation (XCI) is the process by which one of the two copies of the X chromosome present in females is inactivated in order to achieves dosage equivalency for X-linked genes between XY males and XX females. An individual cell's decision to inactivate either the paternal or maternal X is made early in development, at approximately the time of implantation, such that normally there is a roughly equal distribution of either X being active. A deviation from equality is known as skewing, with common criteria for "skewed" inactivation being arbitrarily defined as the observation of inactivation of the same allele in 75% or 80% of cells (and very skewed inactivation resulting in 90% or 95% of cells with the same allele inactive). For some X-linked diseases there is strong selection in the heterozygous carrier in favor of cells bearing the mutation on the silenced inactive X, and thus, assessment of XCI skewing in female family members can be suggestive of carrier status.

HP:0012547.label: Abnormal involuntary eye movements
HP:0012547.definition: Anomalous movements of the eyes that occur without the subject wanting them to happen.

HP:0012548.label: Fatty replacement of skeletal muscle
HP:0012548.definition: Muscle fibers degeneration resulting in fatty replacement of skeletal muscle fibers
HP:0012548.comment: Fatty infiltration of muscle tissue can be observed on muscle biopsy as well as through imaging by computed tomography and magnetic resonance tomography.

HP:0012549.label: Conjunctival lipoma
HP:0012549.definition: A lipoma (a benign tumor composed of adipose tissue) located in the conjunctiva.
HP:0012549.comment: Conjunctival lipoma displays yellowish-pink stromal mass, histologically with large lipid vacuoles surrounded by stellate cells.

HP:0012550.label: Colonic varices
HP:0012550.definition: The presence of varices (enlarged and convoluted blood vessels) in the colon.
HP:0012550.comment: Colonic varices are a rare cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding, most commonly associated with portal hypertension and more rarely with congestive heart failure, mesenteric vein thrombosis, pancreatitis with splenic vein thrombosis and adhesions, and mesenteric vein compression. Colonic varices are usually located in the rectosigmoid region and the cecum.

HP:0012551.label: Absent neutrophil specific granules
HP:0012551.definition: Lack of specific granules in neutrophils.
HP:0012551.comment: Neutrophil polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) contain two principal types of granules. Azurophil granules appear early in neutrophil development and contain lysosomal enzymes, lysozyme, and myeloperoxidase (MPO). Specific granules are formed later, lack MPO and hydrolases, but contain lactoferrin and the remainder of the cell's complement of lysozyme. Consequently, specific granules may be conveniently detected at the electron-microscopic (EM) level by the cytochemical demonstration of their lack of MPO, while at the optical level their presence can be inferred from their positive immunocytochemical staining for lactoferrin with the use of specific antiserums.

HP:0012552.label: Increased neutrophil nuclear projections
HP:0012552.definition: Presence of an elevated number of projections from nuclei of neutrophils. These projections can have the shape of hooks, tags, or clubs.

HP:0012553.label: Hypoplastic thumbnail
HP:0012553.definition: A thumbnail that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped thumb nail.

HP:0012556.label: Hyperbeta-alaninemia
HP:0012556.definition: Increased concentration of beta-alanine in the blood.

HP:0012557.label: EEG with centrotemporal focal spike waves
HP:0012557.definition: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the centrotemporal region of the brain (also known as the central sulcus), i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

HP:0012558.label: Abnormal T3/T4 ratio
HP:0012558.definition: A ratio of serum triiodothyronine (T3) to thyroxine (T4) in the blood that deviates from normal.

HP:0012559.label: Increased T3/T4 ratio
HP:0012559.definition: A ratio of serum triiodothyronine (T3) to thyroxine (T4) in the blood that is higher than normal.

HP:0012560.label: Decreased T3/T4 ratio
HP:0012560.definition: A ratio of serum triiodothyronine (T3) to thyroxine (T4) in the blood that is lower than normal.

HP:0012561.label: Unicuspid aortic valve
HP:0012561.definition: The presence of an aortic valve with one instead of the normal three cusps (flaps).
HP:0012561.comment: The aortic valve normally has three cusps (flaps), that is, it is normally tricuspid. Unicuspid aortic valve (UAV) shares many of the features of bicuspid aortic valve, including valvular dysfunction, aortic dilatation, aortic dissection, and dystrophic calcification, although these conditions develop at an earlier age and progress at a faster pace in UAV.

HP:0012562.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion in hand
HP:0012562.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the hand, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

HP:0012563.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion in foot
HP:0012563.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the foot, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

HP:0012564.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion in tibia
HP:0012564.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the tibia, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

HP:0012565.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion in fibula
HP:0012565.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the fibula, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

HP:0012566.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion in radius
HP:0012566.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the radius, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

HP:0012567.label: Premature epimetaphyseal fusion in ulna
HP:0012567.definition: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the ulna, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

HP:0012568.label: Lower eyelid edema
HP:0012568.definition: Edema in the region of the Lower eyelid.

HP:0012569.label: Delayed menarche
HP:0012569.definition: First period after the age of 15 years.

HP:0012570.label: Synovial sarcoma
HP:0012570.definition: A type of mesenchymal tissue cell tumor that exhibits epithelial differentiation, which most frequently arises in the extremities.
HP:0012570.comment: Synovial sarcoma is a high-grade tumor that is associated with poor prognosis.

HP:0012571.label: Ureter fissus
HP:0012571.definition: A partial duplication of the ureter where the duplicated ureters fuse to a single ureter before their insertion into the bladder.
HP:0012571.comment: This anomaly is only seen in the presence of renal duplication.

HP:0012572.label: Ureter duplex
HP:0012572.definition: A complete duplication of the ureter, where the duplicated ureters have separate insertions into the bladder.

HP:0012573.label: Global proximal tubulopathy
HP:0012573.definition: A type of proximal renal tubulopathy characterized by resorption defects leading to glycosuria, aminoaciduria, tubular proteinuria, renal hypophosphatemia, and urate tubular hyporeabsorption with bicarbonate loss and resulting acidosis.

HP:0012574.label: Mesangial hypercellularity
HP:0012574.definition: Increased numbers of mesangial cells per glomerulus, defined as more than 3 nuclei fully surrounded by matrix in one or more mesangial areas, not including perihilar region, on a standard 3-micron-thick tissue section, best evaluated on periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain.

HP:0012575.label: Abnormal nephron morphology
HP:0012575.definition: A structural anomaly of the nephron.

HP:0012576.label: Glomerular C3 deposition
HP:0012576.definition: The presence of complement 3 deposits in the glomerulus.

HP:0012577.label: Thin glomerular basement membrane
HP:0012577.definition: Decreased thickness of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), measured from endothelial to visceral epithelial plasma membrane and mainly attributable to a decrease in thickness of the lamina densa, generally to an overall thickness more than 2 standard deviations less than that of the normal mean GBM thickness for health age- and sex matched individuals. May be focal or diffuse, although the term thin GBMs generally implies thinning of over 50% of GBMs.
HP:0012577.comment: This finding is demonstrated on renal biopsy.

HP:0012578.label: Membranous nephropathy
HP:0012578.definition: A type of glomerulonephropathy characterized by thickening of the basement membrane and deposition of immune complexes in the subepithelial space.

HP:0012579.label: Minimal change glomerulonephritis
HP:0012579.definition: The presence of minimal changes visible by light microscopy but flattened and fused podocyte foot processes on electron microscopy in a person with nephrotic range proteinuria.

HP:0012580.label: Calcium phosphate nephrolithiasis
HP:0012580.definition: The presence of calcium- and phosphate-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

HP:0012581.label: Simple renal cyst
HP:0012581.definition: An isolated cyst of the kidney.

HP:0012582.label: Bilateral renal dysplasia
HP:0012582.definition: A bilateral form of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.

HP:0012583.label: Unilateral renal hypoplasia
HP:0012583.definition: One sided hypoplasia of the kidney.

HP:0012584.label: Bilateral renal hypoplasia
HP:0012584.definition: Two sided hypoplasia of the kidney.

HP:0012586.label: Bilateral renal atrophy
HP:0012586.definition: A two-sided form of atrophy of the kidney.

HP:0012587.label: Macroscopic hematuria
HP:0012587.definition: Hematuria that is visible upon inspection of the urine.

HP:0012588.label: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome
HP:0012588.definition: A form of nephrotic syndrome that does not respond to treatment with steroid medication, defined as persistent proteinuria despite 60mg/m2 or 2mg/kg for 8 weeks, after insuring no infection or non-adherence to medication.
HP:0012588.comment: Genetic studies and biopsy are necessary. Treatment depends on result. Genetic forms are treated symptomatically with ACE-inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blockers. Non-genetic forms are usually treated with calcineurin inhibitors. Prognosis is worse than in SSNS. 50 % progress into end-stage renal disease.

HP:0012589.label: Multidrug-resistant nephrotic syndrome
HP:0012589.definition: A form of nephrotic syndrome that does not respond to any immunosuppresive treatment.

HP:0012590.label: Abnormal urine output
HP:0012590.definition: An abnormal amount of urine production.

HP:0012591.label: Abnormal urinary electrolyte concentration
HP:0012591.definition: An abnormality in the concentration of electrolytes in the urine.

HP:0012592.label: Albuminuria
HP:0012592.definition: Increased concentration of albumin in the urine.

HP:0012593.label: Nephrotic range proteinuria
HP:0012593.definition: Severely increased amount of excretion of protein in the urine, defined as 3.5 grams per day or more in adults and 40 mg per meter-squared body surface area per hour in children.

HP:0012594.label: Moderate albuminuria
HP:0012594.definition: The presence of moderately increased concentrations of albumin in the urine, defined as and albumin-creatinine ratio (ACR) of 30 to 299 mg/gm (3.4 to 34 mg/mmol).

HP:0012595.label: Mild proteinuria
HP:0012595.definition: Mildly increased levels of protein in the urine (150-500 mg per day in adults).

HP:0012596.label: Moderate proteinuria
HP:0012596.definition: Moderately increased levels of protein in the urine (500-1000 mg per day in adults).

HP:0012597.label: Heavy proteinuria
HP:0012597.definition: Severely increased levels of protein in the urine (1000-3000 mg per day in adults).

HP:0012598.label: Abnormal urine potassium concentration
HP:0012598.definition: An abnormal concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.

HP:0012599.label: Abnormal urine phosphate concentration
HP:0012599.definition: An abnormal phosphate concentration in the urine.

HP:0012600.label: Abnormal urine chloride concentration
HP:0012600.definition: An abnormal concentration of chloride in the urine.

HP:0012601.label: Hypochloriduria
HP:0012601.definition: An decreased concentration of chloride in the urine.

HP:0012602.label: Renal chloride wasting
HP:0012602.definition: High urine chloride in the presence of hypochloridemia.

HP:0012603.label: Abnormal urine sodium concentration
HP:0012603.definition: An abnormal concentration of sodium in the urine.

HP:0012604.label: Hyponatriuria
HP:0012604.definition: An abnormally decreased sodium concentration in the urine.

HP:0012605.label: Hypernatriuria
HP:0012605.definition: An increased concentration of sodium(1+) in the urine.

HP:0012606.label: Renal sodium wasting
HP:0012606.definition: An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the urine in the presence of hyponatremia.

HP:0012607.label: Abnormal urine magnesium concentration
HP:0012607.definition: An abnormal concentration of magnesium the urine.

HP:0012608.label: Hypermagnesiuria
HP:0012608.definition: An increased concentration of magnesium the urine.

HP:0012609.label: Hypomagnesiuria
HP:0012609.definition: An decreased concentration of magnesium the urine.

HP:0012610.label: Abnormality of urinary uric acid level
HP:0012610.definition: Abnormal amount of urate in the urine.
HP:0012610.comment: Xanthine oxidase oxidizes oxypurines such as xanthine and hypoxanthine to uric acid. Uric acid is the final oxidation product of purine catabolism.

HP:0012612.label: Abnormal urinary sulfate concentration
HP:0012612.definition: Abnormal concentration of sulfate in the urine.

HP:0012613.label: Increased urinary sulfate
HP:0012613.definition: Elevated concentration of SO4(2-), i.e., sulfate, in the urine.

HP:0012614.label: Abnormal urine cytology
HP:0012614.definition: An anomalous finding in the examination of the urine for cells.

HP:0012615.label: Cylindruria
HP:0012615.definition: The presence of renal casts (cylindrical, cigar-shaped structures produced by the kidney in certain disease states) in the urine.
HP:0012615.comment: Urinary casts are formed in the distal convoluted tubule or the collecting duct by solidification of protein in the lumen of the kidney tubules. The casts are suibsequently eliminated via the urine and may be seen by microscopy of the urine sediment. A large number of casts can indicate kidney disease. Urinary casts are composed of Tamm-Horsfall protein, which is a mucoprotein that is secreted by the distal loop of Henle.

HP:0012616.label: Leukocyte cylindruria
HP:0012616.definition: Presence of leukocyte casts (cylindrical structures produced by the kidney in certain disease states) in the urine.

HP:0012617.label: Erythrocyte cylindruria
HP:0012617.definition: Presence of erythrocyte casts (cylindrical structures produced by the kidney in certain disease states) in the urine.

HP:0012618.label: Urachal cyst
HP:0012618.definition: A cyst located along the allantois canal.

HP:0012619.label: Multiple bladder diverticula
HP:0012619.definition: Presence of a many diverticula (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urinary bladder.

HP:0012620.label: Cloacal abnormality
HP:0012620.definition: A developmental anomaly associated with the failure of rectum, vagina, and bladder to separate.

HP:0012621.label: Persistent cloaca
HP:0012621.definition: Developmental anomaly in which the vagina, bladder, and rectum fuse resulting in a common channel.

HP:0012622.label: Chronic kidney disease
HP:0012622.definition: Functional anomaly of the kidney persisting for at least three months.

HP:0012623.label: Stage 1 chronic kidney disease
HP:0012623.definition: A type of chronic kidney disease with normal or increased glomerular filtration rate (GFR at least 90 mL/min/1.73 m2).
HP:0012623.comment: Proteinuria is commonly seen in stage 1 chronic kidney disease.

HP:0012624.label: Stage 2 chronic kidney disease
HP:0012624.definition: A type of chronic kidney disease with mildly reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m2).

HP:0012625.label: Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
HP:0012625.definition: A type of chronic kidney disease with moderately reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m2).

HP:0012626.label: Stage 4 chronic kidney disease
HP:0012626.definition: A type of chronic kidney disease with severely reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m2).

HP:0012627.label: Pseudoexfoliation
HP:0012627.definition: Deposition of fibrillar material that can be found on all anterior segment structures bathed by aqueous humor.
HP:0012627.comment: In the eye, pseudoexfoliation syndrome is characterized by the deposition of fibrillar material that can be found on all anterior segment structures bathed by aqueous humor. PXM can be observed in vivo during slit lamp examination. It appears as 'dandruff-like' material in the anterior chamber or most characteristically on the anterior lens capsule deposited in a double concentric ring pattern. The rings are separated by a clear zone presumably created because of the movement of the iris on the anterior lens surface. The central ring is located at the area of the iris sphincter, while the peripheral ring is only visible after pupil dilation. PXM is also often observed by slit lamp examination at the pupillary margin, on the lens zonules and on the trabecular meshwork. The site of production of this material which is a complex of various glycoproteins is unclear, but PXM can potentially originate from the iris, lens epithelium, ciliary body, or the trabecular meshwork.

HP:0012628.label: Abnormal suspensory ligament of lens morphology
HP:0012628.definition: An anomaly of the suspensory ligament of lens, also known as the ciliary zonule. These ligaments represent a series of fibers connecting the ciliary body and lens of the eye, holding the lens in place.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the suspensory ligament of lens

HP:0012629.label: Phakodonesis
HP:0012629.definition: Tremulousness (trembling) of the lens of the eye.
HP:0012629.comment: Phacodonesis results from lesions of some or most of the zonular fibers are broken.

HP:0012630.label: Abnormal trabecular meshwork morphology
HP:0012630.definition: An anomaly of the trabecular meshwork, which is the porelike structure surrounding the entire circumference of the anterior chamber at the base of the cornea and near the ciliary body. The trabecular mesh work is responsible for draining the aqueous humor into the canal of Schlemm.

HP:0012631.label: Pigment deposition in the trabecular meshwork
HP:0012631.definition: Accumulation of abnormal amounts of pigment within the trabecular meshwork.
HP:0012631.comment: Gonioscopy can be used to reveal pigment deposition on the trabecular meshwork.

HP:0012632.label: Abnormal intraocular pressure
HP:0012632.definition: An anomaly in the amount of force per unit area exerted by the intraocular fluid within the eye.

HP:0012633.label: Asymmetry of intraocular pressure
HP:0012633.definition: A difference in the amount of intraocular pressure in the right and left eye.

HP:0012634.label: Iris pigment dispersion
HP:0012634.definition: Shedding of the pigment granules that normally adhere to the back of the iris into the aqueous humor.
HP:0012634.comment: These pigment granules can accumulate in the trabucular meshwork and lead to increased intraocular pressure. That is coded separately as HP:001263.

HP:0012635.label: Iris hypoperfusion
HP:0012635.definition: Reduction in the amount of blood flow to the iris.
HP:0012635.comment: This feature can be diagnosed by iris angiography.

HP:0012636.label: Retinal venous occlusion
HP:0012636.definition: Blockage of a retinal vein or venule, occurring typically at an arteriovenous crossing. Typically presenting with dilated veins, retinal hemorrhages and in some cases non-perfusion.
HP:0012636.comment: Retinal vein occlusion is generally associated with systemic cardiovascular diseases.

HP:0012637.label: Renal calcium wasting
HP:0012637.definition: High urine calcium in the presence of hypocalcemia.

HP:0012638.label: Abnormal nervous system physiology
HP:0012638.definition: A functional anomaly of the nervous system.

HP:0012639.label: Abnormal nervous system morphology
HP:0012639.definition: A structural anomaly of the nervous system.

HP:0012640.label: Abnormality of intracranial pressure
HP:0012640.definition: A deviation from the norm of the intracranial pressure.
HP:0012640.comment: Intracranial pressure (i.e., the pressure inside the skull) represents the pressure in the brain tissue and in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Deviations from normal are generally identified by measuring the pressure of the CSF.

HP:0012641.label: Decreased intracranial pressure
HP:0012641.definition: A reduction of the pressure inside the cranium (skull) and thereby in the brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid.

HP:0012642.label: Cerebellar agenesis
HP:0012642.definition: Cerebellar agenesis is defined by the near complete absence of cerebellar tissue with only remnants of the anterior vermis, flocculus, and/or middle cerebellar peduncles.
HP:0012642.comment: Usually, small remnants of the cerebellum are present; therefore the term subtotal cerebellar agenesis is also used in the literature. A secondary pontine hypoplasia is typically seen. The definition of cerebellar agenesis is based on the morphologic pattern and does not suggest the pathogenesis. Cerebellar agenesis may represent a malformation (e.g., mutations in PTF1A) or a disruption (e.g., hemorrhage that occurs during gestation or in the perinatal period, vascular insufficiency in Chiari II malformation and cerebellar herniation, and as a sequela of prematurity).

HP:0012643.label: Foveal hypopigmentation
HP:0012643.definition: Decreased amount of pigmentation in the fovea.

HP:0012644.label: Increased caudate lactate level
HP:0012644.definition: An elevated concentration of lactate in the caudate nucleus. This finding can be elicited by magnetic resonance spectroscopy imaging.

HP:0012645.label: Enlarged peripheral nerve
HP:0012645.definition: Increase in size of a peripheral nerve. This finding can be appreciated by palpation along the axis of the nerve.
HP:0012645.comment: This feature can be appreciated by imaging studies (magnetic resonancy tomography), by palpation along the axis of a nerve, and by biopsy, and may be caused by axonal swelling or by myelin thickening. The differential diagnosis of enlarged peripheral nerves includes leprosy, hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy type 1 (about 30% of patients), but not type 2 (the axonal form), some other polyneuropathies, neurofibromatosis, and nerve tumors. A good review is available in Practical Neurology, 2003,3:40-45 by Michael Donaghy (no pubmed id).

HP:0012646.label: Retractile testis
HP:0012646.definition: A testis that is located at the upper scrotum or lower inguinal canal and that can be made to descend completely into the scrotum without resistance by manual reduction but returns to its original position by the cremasteric reflex.

HP:0012647.label: Abnormal inflammatory response
HP:0012647.definition: Any anomaly of the inflammatory response, a response to injury or infection characterized by local vasodilation, extravasation of plasma into intercellular spaces and accumulation of white blood cells and macrophages.

HP:0012648.label: Decreased inflammatory response
HP:0012648.definition: An abnormal reduction in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.

HP:0012649.label: Increased inflammatory response
HP:0012649.definition: A abnormal increase in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.

HP:0012650.label: Perisylvian polymicrogyria
HP:0012650.definition: Polymicrogyria (an excessive number of small gyri or convolutions) that is maximal in perisylvian regions (the regions that surround the Sylvian fissures), which may be symmetric or asymmetric and may extend beyond perisylvian regions. The Sylvian fissures often extend posteriorly and superiorly.
HP:0012650.comment: The Sylvian fissure (also known as the lateral sulcus) separates the frontal and parietal lobes superiorly from the temporal lobe inferiorly.

HP:0012651.label: Abasia
HP:0012651.definition: A severe form of gait ataxia such that an affected person cannot walk at all.

HP:0012653.label: Status asthmaticus
HP:0012653.definition: Severe asthma unresponsive to repeated courses of beta-agonist therapy such as inhaled albuterol, levalbuterol, or subcutaneous epinephrine.

HP:0012654.label: Abnormal CSF dopamine concentration
HP:0012654.definition: Abnormal concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP:0012655.label: Elevated CSF dopamine concentration
HP:0012655.definition: Increased concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP:0012656.label: Reduced CSF dopamine concentration
HP:0012656.definition: Decreased concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP:0012657.label: Abnormal brain positron emission tomography
HP:0012657.definition: A functional brain anomaly detectable by positron emission tomography (PET). PET scanning is a method for functional brain imaging, and its measurements reflect the amount of brain activity in the various regions of the brain.
HP:0012657.comment: Note that while structural brain anomalies can cause abnormal brain PET scan results, structural abnormalities are detectable by multiple neuroimaging modalities and should be coded using terms from the hierarchy under 'Abnormality of nervous system morphology' (HP:0012639).

HP:0012658.label: Abnormal brain FDG positron emission tomography
HP:0012658.definition: An anomaly detectable in [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) brain scans. Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity.

HP:0012659.label: Prefrontal hypometabolism in FDG PET
HP:0012659.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the prefrontal cortex as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
HP:0012659.comment: Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity, thus this sign indicates reduced metabolic activity in the prefrontal cortex.

HP:0012660.label: Thalamic hypometabolism in FDG PET
HP:0012660.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the thalamus as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
HP:0012660.comment: Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity, thus this sign indicates reduced metabolic activity in the thalamus.

HP:0012661.label: Hypothalamic hypometabolism in FDG PET
HP:0012661.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the hypothalamus as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
HP:0012661.comment: Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity, thus this sign indicates reduced metabolic activity in the hypothalamus.

HP:0012662.label: Parietal hypometabolism in FDG PET
HP:0012662.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the parietal cortex as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
HP:0012662.comment: Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity, thus this sign indicates reduced metabolic activity in the parietal cortex.

HP:0012663.label: Mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP:0012663.definition: A small reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at least 50 percent, and a mild reduction is defined as 40-49 percent.

HP:0012664.label: Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP:0012664.definition: A diminution of the volumetric fraction of blood pumped out of the ventricle with each cardiac cycle.
HP:0012664.comment: The normal range is at least 55 percent.

HP:0012665.label: Moderately reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP:0012665.definition: A medium reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle, defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30-39 percent.
HP:0012665.comment: The normal range in adults is over 50 percent, and a moderate reduction can be defined as 30-39 percent.

HP:0012666.label: Severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP:0012666.definition: A large reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at over 50 percent, and a severe reduction is defined as less than 30 percent.

HP:0012667.label: Regional left ventricular wall motion abnormality
HP:0012667.definition: An abnormal motion of a segment of the left ventricle during the cardiac cycle.
HP:0012667.comment: This feature can be appreciated using color kinesis, which tracks the motion of the endocardium in real time throughout systole and results in color-encoded images reflecting the magnitude and timing of endocardial motion.

HP:0012668.label: Vasovagal syncope
HP:0012668.definition: A vasovagal episode or vasovagal syncope is the most common form of reflex syncope. Reflex syncope is a general term used to describe types of syncope resulting from a failure in autoregulation of blood pressure, and ultimately, in cerebral perfusion pressure resulting in transient loss of consciousness. The mechanisms responsible for this are complex and involve both depression of cardiac output as well as a decrease in vascular tone.

HP:0012669.label: Carotid sinus syncope
HP:0012669.definition: An exaggerated response to carotid sinus baroreceptor stimulation resulting in syncope from transient diminished cerebral perfusion.
HP:0012669.comment: Carotid sinus syncope cam be elicited mechanical manipulation of the carotid sinuses (eg, taking pulses in the neck, shaving).

HP:0012670.label: Orthostatic syncope
HP:0012670.definition: Syncope following a quick change in position from lying down to standing.

HP:0012671.label: Abulia
HP:0012671.definition: Abulia is characterized by difficulty in initiating and sustaining spontaneous movements; the person often appears frozen but will move hesitantly on request. There are frequently substantial reductions in emotional responsiveness, spontaneous speech, and social interaction. The individual appears to be content to remain still and inactive with minimal movement, but moves or reacts hesitantly in response to interactions.
HP:0012671.comment: Abulia is less severe than kinetic mutism and more severe than apathy.

HP:0012672.label: Akinetic mutism
HP:0012672.definition: The combined absence of spontaneous movement (akinesia) and speech (mutism). There may be eye movements consistent with visual tracking and the person may remember the events occurring at the time of the experience of stupor.
HP:0012672.comment: Akinetic mutism is essentially characterized by a total absence of spontaneous behavior and speech occurring in the presence of preserved visual tracking.

HP:0012673.label: Aplasia of the upper vagina
HP:0012673.definition: A failure to develop of the upper vagina.
HP:0012673.comment: The female reproductive tract primarily develops from the Mullerian ducts (MD), which form as an invagination of the coelomic epithelium and further develop into the upper two-thirds of the vagina, the uterus and the Fallopian tubes. Complete aplasia of the uterus, cervix, and upper vagina is termed Mullerian aplasia. This term refers to the aplasia of the upper roughly two thirds of the vagina that is characteristic of Mullerian aplasia.

HP:0012674.label: Aplasia of the lower vagina
HP:0012674.definition: A failure to develop of the lower part of the vagina.

HP:0012675.label: Iron accumulation in brain
HP:0012675.definition: An abnormal build up of iron (Fe) in brain tissue.

HP:0012676.label: Copper accumulation in brain
HP:0012676.definition: An anomalous build up of copper (Cu) in the brain.

HP:0012677.label: obsolete Iron accumulation in globus pallidus

HP:0012678.label: Iron accumulation in substantia nigra
HP:0012678.definition: An anomalous build up of iron (Fe) in the substantia nigra.

HP:0012679.label: Widened interpedicular distance
HP:0012679.definition: An increase in the distance between vertebral pedicles, which are the two short, thick processes, which project backward, one on either side, from the upper part of the vertebral body, at the junction of its posterior and lateral surfaces.

HP:0012680.label: Abnormality of the pineal gland
HP:0012680.definition: An anomaly of the pineal gland,a small endocrine gland in the brain that produces melatonin.

HP:0012681.label: Abnormal pineal morphology
HP:0012681.definition: A structural abnormality of the pineal gland.
HP:0012681.comment: The pineal gland typically measures 7 x 6 x 3mm in size and is located in a groove between the laterally placed thalamic bodies.

HP:0012682.label: Pineal gland calcification
HP:0012682.definition: Accumulation of calcium salts in the pineal gland.
HP:0012682.comment: This feature can be appreciated on skull radiography.

HP:0012683.label: Pineal cyst
HP:0012683.definition: A glial uniloculated or multiloculated fluid-filled sac that either reside within or completely replace the pineal gland.
HP:0012683.comment: Pineal cysts are benign and often asymptomatic lesions. They are typically visualized by computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging.

HP:0012684.label: Abnormal pineal volume
HP:0012684.definition: An abnormal increase or decrease in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.
HP:0012684.comment: This feature is typically assessed by magnetic resonance tomography of the brain.

HP:0012685.label: Decreased pineal volume
HP:0012685.definition: An abnormal reduction in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.

HP:0012686.label: Increased pineal volume
HP:0012686.definition: An abnormal elevation in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.

HP:0012687.label: Agenesis of pineal gland
HP:0012687.definition: Failure to develop of the pineal gland, defined clinically as the absence of the pineal gland with no indication of the pineal gland even having been present.

HP:0012688.label: Abnormality of pineal physiology
HP:0012688.definition: A functional abnormality of the pineal gland.

HP:0012689.label: Abnormal pineal melatonin secretion
HP:0012689.definition: An anomaly in the amount or timing of melatonin secretion by the pineal gland. Note that melatonin is also synthesized by multiple tissues outside of the pineal gland.
HP:0012689.comment: The rhythm of melatonin synthesized in and released from the pineal gland is characterized by a prominent nocturnal peak, which also contains temporal information that had originated in the suprachiasmatic nucleus. Strong reductions of circulating melatonin are also observed in numerous disorders and diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, various other neurological and stressful conditions, pain, cardiovascular diseases, cases of cancer, endocrine and metabolic disorders, in particular diabetes type 2.

HP:0012690.label: T2 hypointense thalamus
HP:0012690.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus. This term refers to a diffuse hypointensity affecting the entire thalamus.

HP:0012691.label: Focal T2 hypointense thalamic lesion
HP:0012691.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the thalamus.

HP:0012692.label: Focal T2 hyperintense thalamic lesion
HP:0012692.definition: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the thalamus.
HP:0012692.comment: The term "unidentified bright object" has been used to describe T2 hyperintense lesions in the thalamus and elsewhere in patients with neurofibromatosis.

HP:0012693.label: Abnormal thalamic size
HP:0012693.definition: Deviation from the normal range of size of the thalamus.

HP:0012694.label: Enlarged thalamic volume
HP:0012694.definition: An increase in the quantity of space occupied by the thalamus.

HP:0012695.label: Decreased thalamic volume
HP:0012695.definition: A reduction in the quantity of space occupied by the thalamus.

HP:0012696.label: Abnormal thalamic MRI signal intensity
HP:0012696.definition: A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus.

HP:0012697.label: Small basal ganglia
HP:0012697.definition: Decreased size of the basal ganglia.

HP:0012698.label: Cerebellar gliosis
HP:0012698.definition: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the cerebellum.

HP:0012699.label: Anomaly of lower limb diaphyses
HP:0012699.definition: A structural abnormality of a diaphysis of the leg.
exact_synonyms: Anomaly of shaft of long bone of lower limb

HP:0012700.label: Abnormal large intestine physiology
HP:0012700.definition: A functional anomaly of the large intestine.

HP:0012701.label: Bowel urgency
HP:0012701.definition: A sudden, irresistible need to have a bowel movement.

HP:0012702.label: Tenesmus
HP:0012702.definition: A repeated, painful urge to defecate without excreting stool.

HP:0012703.label: Abnormal subarachnoid space morphology
HP:0012703.definition: Abnormality in the space in the meninges beneath the arachnoid membrane and above the pia mater that contains the cerebrospinal fluid.

HP:0012704.label: Widened subarachnoid space
HP:0012704.definition: An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater.

HP:0012705.label: Abnormal metabolic brain imaging by MRS
HP:0012705.definition: An anomaly of metabolism in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP:0012705.comment: MRS can only detect a few metabolites as least millimolar concentrations are necessary for the metabolites to be detected. The major brain metabolites detected are choline (Cho), creatine (Cr), N-acetyl aspartate (NAA), lactate, myo-inositol, glutamine and glutamate, lipids, and the amino acids leucine and alanine.

HP:0012706.label: Elevated brain choline level by MRS
HP:0012706.definition: An increase in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP:0012706.comment: The Choline (Cho) peak is a heterogeneous peak representing various choline-containing compounds such as acetylcholine, phosphocholine (lecithin), glycerophosphocholine, and various other intermediates of phospholipids metabolism. It is an indicator of cell density and cell wall turnover. Elevated levels are found in tumors, especially malignant ones, and in certain demyelinating diseases. Choline resonance presents at 3.22 ppm. Studies have shown there is also a direct association between Cho and levels of Ki-67, a protein expressed in all phases of the cell cycle except GO that serves as a good marker for cellular proliferation. This observation makes Cho a reliable predictor of cellular activity in tumor tissue.

HP:0012707.label: Elevated brain lactate level by MRS
HP:0012707.definition: An increase in the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP:0012707.comment: Lactate (Lac) is absent in normal brain tissue and its presence is indicative of anerobic glycolysis at the cellular level. Elevated levels are associated with ischemic conditions or metabolic disorders (where anerobic glycolysis predominates) but is also noted at the edges of large brain tumors. The peak is very sensitive to the technique employed and unless the correct echo time is employed, it may be artifactually suppressed. The spectral peak lies at 1:33 ppm. The peak is often inverted or bifid.

HP:0012708.label: Reduced brain N-acetyl aspartate level by MRS
HP:0012708.definition: A decrease in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP:0012708.comment: N-Acetyl Aspartate (NAA) is an amino acid found exclusively in neurons. It is regarded as a non-specific marker and is thought to be involved in Coenzyme A interactions and lipogenesis within the brain. It is a marker of neuronal viability. Normal NAA concentration is in the range of 8-9 mmol/kg in healthy adult brain. Concentrations are decreased in conditions leading to axonal injury or neuronal loss. NAA is also decreased in other conditions such as neoplasm, infarction, and inflammatory conditions such as multiple sclerosis. NAA peak is seen at 2.0 ppm (parts per million) on MR spectra.
exact_synonyms: Reduced brain N-acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
MR Spectroscopy: N-acetylaspartate low in brain

HP:0012709.label: Abnormal brain choline/creatine ratio by MRS
HP:0012709.definition: A deviation from normal in the ratio of choline to creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP:0012709.comment: Creatine (Cr) is related to cell energy pathways, being both the substrate and product of creatine kinase. Creatine reflects the energy potential available in brain tissue. Its concentration in normal brain remains very high and stable due to high metabolic energy needs of brain cells. Its peak is noticed at 3.0 ppm. Creatine-Choline ratios are an important indicator of disease states such as demyelization.

HP:0012710.label: Ingrown nail
HP:0012710.definition: Excessive growth of a nail laterally into the nail fold.

HP:0012711.label: Delayed ossification of vertebral epiphysis
HP:0012711.definition: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more vertebrae.
related_synonyms: Delayed maturation of the end part of the vertebral bone

HP:0012712.label: Mild hearing impairment
HP:0012712.definition: The presence of a mild form of hearing impairment.

HP:0012713.label: Moderate hearing impairment
HP:0012713.definition: The presence of a moderate form of hearing impairment.

HP:0012714.label: Severe hearing impairment
HP:0012714.definition: A severe form of hearing impairment.

HP:0012715.label: Profound hearing impairment
HP:0012715.definition: A profound (essentially complete) form of hearing impairment.

HP:0012716.label: Moderate conductive hearing impairment
HP:0012716.definition: The presence of a moderate form of conductive hearing impairment.
HP:0012716.comment: Conductive hearing impairment with 21-40 dB deficit.

HP:0012717.label: Severe conductive hearing impairment
HP:0012717.definition: A severe form of conductive hearing impairment.
HP:0012717.comment: Conductive hearing impairment with 21-40 dB deficit.

HP:0012718.label: Abnormal gastrointestinal tract morphology
HP:0012718.definition: Abnormal structure of the gastrointestinal tract.
exact_synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
Morphological anomaly of the digestive system
Morphological abnormality of the GI tract
Abnormal shape of the digestive system

HP:0012719.label: Functional abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
HP:0012719.definition: Abnormal functionality of the gastrointestinal tract.
exact_synonyms: Functional abnormality of the GI tract

HP:0012720.label: Neoplasm of the nose
HP:0012720.definition: Tumor (An abnormal mass of tissue resulting from abnormally dividing cells) of the nasal cavity.

HP:0012721.label: Venous malformation
HP:0012721.definition: A vascular malformation resulting from a developmental error of venous tissue composed of dysmorphic channels lined by flattened endothelium and exhibiting slow turnover. A venous malformation may present as a blue patch on the skin ranging to a soft blue mass. Venous malformations are easily compressible and usually swell in thewhen venous pressure increases (e.g., when held in a dependent position or when a child cries). They may be relatively localized or quite extensive within an anatomic region.
HP:0012721.comment: Venous malformations are always present at birth, and usually involve the skin of the face, limbs, or trunk.

HP:0012722.label: Heart block
HP:0012722.definition: Impaired conduction of cardiac impulse occurring anywhere along the conduction pathway.

HP:0012723.label: Sinoatrial block
HP:0012723.definition: Disturbance in the atrial activation that is caused by transient failure of impulse conduction from the sinoatrial node to the cardiac atria.
HP:0012723.comment: Sinoatrial block is characterized by a delayed in heartbeat and pauses between P waves as demonstrated by electrocardiography.

HP:0012724.label: Upper eyelid edema
HP:0012724.definition: Edema in the region of the upper eyelid.

HP:0012725.label: Cutaneous syndactyly
HP:0012725.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints, or a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits that lies significantly distal to the flexion crease that overlies the metacarpophalangeal or metatarsophalangeal joint of the adjacent digits.

HP:0012726.label: Episodic hypokalemia
HP:0012726.definition: An abnormally decreased potassium concentration in the blood occurring periodically with a return to normal between the episodes.

HP:0012727.label: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
HP:0012727.definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the thoracic aorta.
HP:0012727.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0012728.label: Fusiform descending thoracic aortic aneurysm
HP:0012728.definition: A concentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta that involves the full circumference of the vessel wall
HP:0012728.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0012729.label: Saccular descending thoracic aortic aneurysm
HP:0012729.definition: An eccentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta that involves only a portion of the circumference of the vessel wall
HP:0012729.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0012730.label: Aglossia
HP:0012730.definition: Absence of the tongue owing to a developmental abnormality.

HP:0012731.label: Ectopic anterior pituitary gland
HP:0012731.definition: Abnormal anatomic location of the anterior pituitary gland.

HP:0012732.label: Anorectal anomaly
HP:0012732.definition: An abnormality of the anus or rectum.

HP:0012733.label: Macule
HP:0012733.definition: A flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin.

HP:0012734.label: Ketotic hypoglycemia
HP:0012734.definition: Low blood glucose is accompanied by elevated levels of ketone bodies in the body.

HP:0012735.label: Cough
HP:0012735.definition: A sudden, audible expulsion of air from the lungs through a partially closed glottis, preceded by inhalation.
HP:0012735.comment: The European Respiratory Society Task Force recommended two possible definitions of cough: (1) A three-phase expulsive motor act characterized by an inspiratory effort (inspiratory phase) followed by a forced expiratory effort against a closed glottis (compressive phase) and then by opening of the glottis and rapid expiratory airflow (expulsive phase);and (2) A forced expiratory maneuver, usually against a closed glottis and associated with a characteristic sound. The term Cough or any of its more specific descendents can be modified by the terms Acute (HP:0011009), Subacute (HP:0011011), and Chronic (HP:0011010). In adults, an acute cough lasts less than 3 weeks, a subacute cough from 3 to 8 weeks, and a chronic cough longer than 8 weeks. In children aged less than 15 years a chronic cough is defined as a daily cough lasting for over 4 weeks.

HP:0012736.label: Profound global developmental delay
HP:0012736.definition: A profound delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.

HP:0012737.label: Small intestinal polyp
HP:0012737.definition: A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the small intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.
HP:0012737.comment: Polyp is a morphological description rather than a histological diagnosis. morphologic description, not a specific histologic diagnosis. Polyps can be neoplastic (e.g., adenoma, carcinoma) or non-neoplastic (e.g., hyperplastic, inflammatory, or hamartomatous).

HP:0012738.label: Agenesis of canine
exact_synonyms: Failure of development of eye tooth

HP:0012739.label: Agenesis of the small intestine
HP:0012739.definition: Failure to develop of the small intestine.

HP:0012740.label: Papilloma
HP:0012740.definition: A tumor of the skin or mucous membrane with finger-like projections.
HP:0012740.comment: The vast majority of papillomas are benign. Papillomas on the skin (cutaneous papillomas) are commonly referred to as warts.

HP:0012741.label: Unilateral cryptorchidism
HP:0012741.definition: Absence of a testis from the scrotum on one side owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

HP:0012742.label: Thin fingernail
HP:0012742.definition: Fingernail that appears thin when viewed on end.
HP:0012742.comment: No objective standard for nail thickness could be identified. An unsupported claim suggests that nails are 0.5 mm in females and 0.6 mm in males (http://www.emedicine.com/orthoped/topic421.htm). Thin nails are usually brittle, may easily fray, or break at the free edge. Thin nails usually grow slowly but this definition does not require slow growth of the nail. Note that the term koilonychia is an abnormal shape of the fingernail where the nail has raised ridges and is thin and concave. Since it include other characteristics besides thin nails, it should not be used to indicate this. The affected digits should be specified.

HP:0012743.label: Abdominal obesity
HP:0012743.definition: Excessive fat around the stomach and abdomen.

HP:0012744.label: Femoral aplasia
HP:0012744.definition: Failure of the femur to develop.

HP:0012745.label: Short palpebral fissure
HP:0012745.definition: Distance between the medial and lateral canthi is more than 2 SD below the mean for age (objective); or, apparently reduced length of the palpebral fissures.

HP:0012746.label: Thin toenail
