exact_synonyms: Contracture of the outermost hinge joint of the 5th toe

HP:0100356.label: Contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 2nd toe
HP:0100356.definition: The joint between the second metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the 2nd toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0100357.label: Contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 3rd toe
HP:0100357.definition: The joint between the third metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the third toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0100358.label: Contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 4th toe
HP:0100358.definition: The joint between the fourth metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the fourth toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0100359.label: Contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 5th toe
HP:0100359.definition: The joint between the fifth metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

HP:0100360.label: Upper-limb joint contracture
HP:0100360.definition: A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint of the upper limb resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.
exact_synonyms: Contractures of the joints of the upper limbs

HP:0100490.label: Camptodactyly of finger
HP:0100490.definition: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.
HP:0100490.comment: Note that some restrict the use of the term to inability to extend the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fifth finger. We do not restrict the term in this way. This term should not be used if the patient has Clenched hand. A similar effect can be created by radial angulation within the distal phalanx with thickening of the epiphysis, which is called Kirner deformity or dystelephalangy. The affected digits should be specified.
exact_synonyms: Flexion contractures of proximal interphalangeal joints
Contractures of the proximal interphalangeal joints of the fingers

HP:0100491.label: Abnormality of lower limb joint
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the joints of the lower limbs

HP:0100492.label: obsolete Joint contractures involving the joints of the feet

HP:0100493.label: Hypoammonemia
HP:0100493.definition: A decreased concentration of ammonia in the blood.

HP:0100494.label: Abnormal mast cell morphology
HP:0100494.definition: Any structural anomaly of mast cells, which are found in almost all tissues and contain numerous basophilic granules and are capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.
HP:0100494.comment: Mast cells (or mastocytes) can be found in several types of tissues and contain many granules rich in histamine and heparin. Although best known for their role in allergy and anaphylaxis, mast cells play an important protective role as well, being intimately involved in wound healing and defense against pathogens. Mast cells possess a non-lobed nucleus and can work with basophils in the immune defense against worms. Their cell membrane is covered with Fc recepros that may be attached to class E antibodies.

HP:0100495.label: Mastocytosis
HP:0100495.definition: The presence of an increased number of mast cells and CD34+ mast cell precursors in the body.

HP:0100496.label: Abnormality of the vitamin B3 metabolism
HP:0100496.comment: Vitamin B3 is also known as nicotinic acid, vitamin PP or Niacin and is one of the forty to eighty essential human nutrients.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the vitamin B3 metabolism

HP:0100501.label: Recurrent bronchiolitis
HP:0100501.definition: An increased susceptibility to bronchiolitis as manifested by a history of recurrent bronchiolitis.

HP:0100502.label: Decreased circulating vitamin B12 concentration
HP:0100502.definition: The concentration of vitamin B12 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100503.label: Decreased circulating vitamin B1 concentration
HP:0100503.definition: The concentration of vitamin B1 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100504.label: Decreased circulating vitamin B2 concentration
HP:0100504.definition: The concentration of vitamin B2 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100505.label: Decreased circulating vitamin B5 concentration
HP:0100505.definition: The concentration of vitamin B5 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100506.label: Decreased circulating vitamin B8 concentration
HP:0100506.definition: The concentration of vitamin B8 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100507.label: Reduced blood folate concentration
HP:0100507.definition: A reduced circulating concentration of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9.

HP:0100508.label: Abnormality of vitamin metabolism
HP:0100508.definition: An anomaly in the metabolism of a vitamin.
HP:0100508.comment: Vitamins are organic substances that are essential in minute quantities and not produced within the body, instead being present in natural foodstuffs. Vitamins act as coenzymes or precursors of coenzymes in the regulation of metabolic processes.

HP:0100510.label: Decreased circulating vitamin C concentration
HP:0100510.definition: The concentration of vitamin C in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100512.label: Decreased circulating vitamin D concentration
HP:0100512.definition: The concentration of vitamin D in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

HP:0100513.label: Decreased circulating vitamin E concentration
HP:0100513.definition: A reduced concentration of vitamin E in the blood circulation. Vitamin E is a lipophilic vitamin that is also known as alpha-tocopherol.

HP:0100514.label: Abnormal circulating vitamin E concentration
HP:0100514.definition: Concentration of vitamin E in the blood circulation outside of normal limits.

HP:0100516.label: Neoplasm of the ureter
HP:0100516.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the ureter.

HP:0100517.label: Neoplasm of the urethra
HP:0100517.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the urethra.

HP:0100519.label: Anuria
HP:0100519.definition: Absence of urine, clinically classified as below 50ml/day.

HP:0100520.label: Oliguria
HP:0100520.definition: Low output of urine, clinically classified as an output below 300-500ml/day.
HP:0100520.comment: The decreased output of urine may be a sign of dehydration, renal failure, hypovolemic shock, multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, or urinary obstruction/urinary retention.

HP:0100521.label: Neoplasm of the thymus
HP:0100521.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the thymus.

HP:0100522.label: Thymoma
HP:0100522.definition: A tumor originating from the epithelial cells of the thymus.
HP:0100522.comment: Malignant lymphomas that involve the thymus, such as lymphoblastic lymphoma and Hodgkin lymphoma (erroneously termed "granulomatous thymoma" in the past), should not be regarded as thymomas. Thymoma is an uncommon tumor, best known for its association with the neuromuscular disorder myasthenia gravis. Thymoma is found in 15% of patients with myasthenia gravis.

HP:0100523.label: Liver abscess
HP:0100523.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the liver.

HP:0100524.label: Limb duplication
HP:0100524.definition: Congenital duplication of all or part of a limb.

HP:0100525.label: Urachus fistula
HP:0100525.definition: Persistence of the urachal canal with drainage of urine from the bladder through the persistent allantois canal to the umbilicus.

HP:0100528.label: Pleuropulmonary blastoma
HP:0100528.definition: A rare cancer originating in the lung or pleural cavity that occurs most often in infants and young children but also has been reported in adults. Pleuropulmonary blastoma is regarded as malignant.

HP:0100529.label: Abnormal blood phosphate concentration
HP:0100529.definition: An abnormality of phosphate homeostasis or concentration in the body.

HP:0100530.label: Abnormal circulating calcium-phosphate regulating hormone concentration
HP:0100530.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of a hormone that is involved in the regulation of phosphate and calcium.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal Ca2+ PO4 regulating hormone level

HP:0100531.label: Wind-swept deformity of the knees
HP:0100531.definition: The appearance of abnormal valgus deformity in one knee in association with varus deformity in the other.

HP:0100532.label: Scleritis
HP:0100532.comment: Scleritis may be accompanied by blurred vision, eye pain, redness of the (normally white) sclera, photophobia, and tearing.

HP:0100533.label: Inflammatory abnormality of the eye
HP:0100533.definition: Inflammation of the eye, parts of the eye or the periorbital region.

HP:0100534.label: Episcleritis
HP:0100534.definition: Inflammation of the episclera, a thin layer of tissue covering the white part (sclera) of the eye.
HP:0100534.comment: In contrast to conjunctivitis, with episcleritis the inflammation is generally limited to isolated parts of the sclera and is not diffuse.One can observe dilated episcleral blood vessels between regions of white sclera.
exact_synonyms: Inflammation of the thin layer on top of the white part of eye

HP:0100537.label: Fasciitis
HP:0100537.definition: Inflammation of fascia, the tissue under the skin and over the muscle.

HP:0100538.label: Abnormality of the supraorbital ridges
HP:0100538.definition: An anomaly of the supraorbital portion of the frontal bones.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the brow of the face

HP:0100539.label: Periorbital edema
HP:0100539.definition: Edema affecting the region situated around the orbit of the eye.

HP:0100540.label: Palpebral edema
HP:0100540.definition: Edema in the region of the eyelids.

HP:0100541.label: Femoral hernia
HP:0100541.definition: A hernia which occurs just below the inguinal ligament, where abdominal contents pass through a naturally occurring weakness called the femoral canal.
HP:0100541.comment: Femoral hernias are a relatively uncommon type, accounting for only 3% of all hernias. Femoral hernia appears as a bulge in the upper thigh.

HP:0100542.label: Abnormal localization of kidney
HP:0100542.definition: An abnormal site of the kidney.

HP:0100543.label: Cognitive impairment
HP:0100543.definition: Abnormal cognition is characterized by deficits in thinking, reasoning, or remembering.
HP:0100543.comment: An individual with cognitive impairment may experience difficulties in remembering, learning new things, concentrating, or making decisions.

HP:0100544.label: Neoplasm of the heart
HP:0100544.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the heart.

HP:0100545.label: Arterial stenosis
HP:0100545.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of an artery.

HP:0100546.label: Carotid artery stenosis
HP:0100546.comment: Carotid artery stenosis is usually caused by caused by atherosclerosis.

HP:0100547.label: Abnormal forebrain morphology
HP:0100547.definition: An abnormality of the forebrain, which has as its parts the telencephalon, diencephalon, lateral ventricles and third ventricle.

HP:0100548.label: Exstrophy
HP:0100548.definition: Eversion of a hollow organ and exposure, inside out, and protruded through the abdominal wall.

HP:0100550.label: Tendon rupture
HP:0100550.comment: Tendon rupture is usually painful,and accompanied by swelling, inability to move, and bunching up of the muscle normally attached to the tendon.

HP:0100555.label: Asymmetric growth
HP:0100555.definition: A growth pattern that displays an abnormal difference between the left and the right side.
exact_synonyms: Uneven or disproportionate growth of one body part compared to another

HP:0100556.label: Hemiatrophy
HP:0100556.definition: Undergrowth of the limbs that affects only one side.

HP:0100557.label: Hemiatrophy of lower limb
HP:0100557.definition: Unilateral atrophy (reduction in size) of a leg.

HP:0100558.label: Hemiatrophy of upper limb
HP:0100558.definition: Unilateral atrophy (reduction in size) of an arm.

HP:0100559.label: Lower limb asymmetry
HP:0100559.definition: A difference in length or diameter between the left and right leg.
exact_synonyms: Left and right leg differ in length or width

HP:0100560.label: Upper limb asymmetry
HP:0100560.definition: Difference in length or size between the right and left arm.

HP:0100563.label: Diastomatomyelia
HP:0100563.definition: Coexistence of two hemicords, at variable levels, causing splaying of the posterior vertebral elements. Results in neurological deficits in lower limb or perineum.

HP:0100564.label: Triplomyelia
HP:0100564.definition: Triplication of the spinal cord - extremely rare.

HP:0100565.label: Hydromyelia
HP:0100565.definition: Dilation of central canal from incomplete fusion of the posterior columns or persistence of the primitive large canal of the embryo.

HP:0100566.label: Amyelia
HP:0100566.definition: Congenital absence of the spinal cord.

HP:0100568.label: Neoplasm of the endocrine system
HP:0100568.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the endocrine system.

HP:0100569.label: Abnormally ossified vertebrae
HP:0100569.definition: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of one or more vertebrae.

HP:0100570.label: Carcinoid tumor
HP:0100570.definition: A tumor formed from the endocrine (argentaffin) cells of the mucosal lining of a variety of organs including the stomach and intestine. These cells are from neuroectodermal origin.

HP:0100571.label: Cardiac diverticulum
HP:0100571.definition: A cardiac diverticulum is a rare congenital malformation which is either fibrous or muscular.

HP:0100572.label: Fibrous cardiac diverticulum
HP:0100572.definition: A fibrous cardiac diverticulum refers to an aneurysm and usually appears as an isolated congenital anomaly.

HP:0100574.label: Biliary tract neoplasm
HP:0100574.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the biliary system.

HP:0100575.label: Neoplasm of the gallbladder
HP:0100575.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the gallbladder.

HP:0100576.label: Amaurosis fugax
HP:0100576.definition: A transient visual disturbance that is typically caused by a circulatory, ocular or neurological underlying condition.

HP:0100578.label: Lipoatrophy
HP:0100578.comment: This may occur as a result of subcutanous injections of insulin in the treatment of diabetes, from the use of human growth hormone or from subcutanous injections of Copaxone used for the treatment of multiple sclerosis. In the latter case, an injection may produce a small dent at the injection site. Lipoatrophy is also an adverse drug reaction that is associated with some antiretroviral drugs.
exact_synonyms: Loss of fat tissue in localized area
Loss of fat tissue in localised area

HP:0100579.label: Mucosal telangiectasiae
HP:0100579.definition: Telangiectasia of the mucosa, the mucous membranes which are involved in absorption and secretion that line cavities that are exposed to the external environment and internal organs.

HP:0100580.label: Barrett esophagus
HP:0100580.definition: An abnormal change (metaplasia) in the cells of the inferior portion of the esophagus. The normal squamous epithelium lining of the esophagus is replaced by metaplastic columnar epithelium. Columnar epithelium refers to a cell type that is typically found in more distal parts of the gastrointestinal system.
HP:0100580.comment: The medical significance of Barrett esophagus is its strong association with esophageal adenocarcinoma, a particularly lethal cancer.

HP:0100581.label: Dilatation of renal calices
HP:0100581.definition: An abnormal enlargement of the renal calices, the system of ducts of the kidney that collect urine.

HP:0100582.label: Nasal polyposis
HP:0100582.definition: Polypoidal masses arising mainly from the mucous membranes of the nose and paranasal sinuses. They are freely movable and nontender overgrowths of the mucosa that frequently accompany allergic rhinitis.
HP:0100582.comment: Nasal polyps (NP) are benign lesions arising from the mucosa of the nasal sinuses (commonly at the outflow tract of one or more of the sinuses) or from the mucosa of the nasal cavity. The main presenting symptom of NP is nasal obstruction which is constant but can vary depending on the site and size of the polyps. Sufferers will also frequently complain of watery rhinorrhea and postnasal drip. Anosmia or hyposmia with an ensuing alteration in taste are also characteristic symptoms of NP.

HP:0100583.label: Corneal perforation
HP:0100583.definition: A rupture of the cornea through which a portion of the iris protrudes.

HP:0100584.label: Endocarditis
HP:0100584.definition: An inflammation of the endocardium, the inner layer of the heart, which usually involves the heart valves.

HP:0100585.label: Telangiectasia of the skin
HP:0100585.definition: Presence of small, permanently dilated blood vessels near the surface of the skin, visible as small focal red lesions.

HP:0100586.label: Sterile pyuria
HP:0100586.definition: Patients who routinely have greater than 20 leukocytes per microliter, but have abacterial urine, are said to have sterile pyuria.

HP:0100587.label: Abnormal preputium morphology
HP:0100587.definition: An abnormality of the retractable fold of skin that covers the tip of the penis.

HP:0100588.label: Paraphimosis
HP:0100588.definition: The foreskin becomes trapped behind the glans penis, and cannot be pulled back to its normal flaccid position covering the glans penis.

HP:0100589.label: Urogenital fistula
HP:0100589.definition: The presence of a fistula affecting the genitourinary system.

HP:0100590.label: Rectal fistula
HP:0100590.definition: The presence of a fistula affecting the rectum.

HP:0100592.label: Peritoneal abscess
HP:0100592.definition: The presence of an abscess of the peritoneum.

HP:0100593.label: Calcification of cartilage
HP:0100593.definition: The presence of calcium deposition in cartilage.

HP:0100594.label: Esophageal web
HP:0100594.definition: Thin (2-3mm) membranes of normal esophageal tissue consisting of mucosa and submucosa that can be congenital or acquired. Congenital webs commonly appear in the middle and inferior third of the esophagus, and they are more likely to be circumferential with a central or eccentric orifice. Acquired webs are much more common than congenital webs and typically appear in the cervical area (postcricoid). Clinical symptoms of this condition are selective (solid more than liquids) dysphagia, thoracic pain, nasopharyngeal reflux, aspiration, perforation and food impaction (the last two are very rare).

HP:0100595.label: Camptocormia
HP:0100595.definition: An abnormal forward-flexed posture e.g. forward flexion of the spine, which is noticeable when standing or walking but disappears when lying down. It is becoming an increasingly recognized feature of Parkinson's disease and dystonic disorders.

HP:0100596.label: Absent nares
HP:0100596.definition: The nostrils (the paired channels of the nose) are not present.

HP:0100599.label: Bifid penis
HP:0100599.definition: Two penile structures, separated from the tip to the base of the shaft.
HP:0100599.comment: In individuals with complete duplication often one will find Hypospadias, Epispadias, Bladder exstrophy, or Bifid scrotum, which should be coded separately, as well as urinary tract duplications, renal anomalies, and gastrointestinal duplications. The terms indicate the presence of (part of) two penises, but do not indicate whether they are caused by splitting or double formation.

HP:0100600.label: Penoscrotal transposition
HP:0100600.definition: A partial or complete positional exchange between the penis and the scrotum, with positioning of the scrotum superior to the penis.

HP:0100601.label: Eclampsia
HP:0100601.definition: An acute and life-threatening complication of pregnancy, which is characterized by the appearance of tonic-clonic seizures, usually in a patient who had developed pre-eclampsia. Eclampsia includes seizures and coma that happen during pregnancy but are not due to preexisting or organic brain disorders.

HP:0100602.label: Preeclampsia
HP:0100602.definition: Pregnancy-induced hypertension in association with significant amounts of protein in the urine.

HP:0100603.label: Toxemia of pregnancy
HP:0100603.definition: Pregnancy-induced toxic reactions of the mother that can be as harmless as slight Maternal hypertension or as life threatening as Eclampsia.

HP:0100604.label: Neoplasm of the lip
HP:0100604.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the lip.

HP:0100606.label: Neoplasm of the respiratory system
HP:0100606.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the respiratory system.

HP:0100607.label: Dysmenorrhea
HP:0100607.definition: Pain during menstruation that interferes with daily activities.

HP:0100610.label: Maternal hyperphenylalaninemia
HP:0100610.definition: A medical history of exposure during the fetal period to hyperphenylalaninemia because the mother had phenylketonuria with inadequate control during pregnancy.
exact_synonyms: High blood phenylalanine level in mother

HP:0100611.label: Multiple glomerular cysts
HP:0100611.definition: The presence of many cysts in the glomerulus of the kidney related to dilatation of the Bowman's capsule.
HP:0100611.comment: Glomerular cysts, defined as Bowman space dilatation greater than 2 to 3 times normal size, are found in disorders of diverse etiology and with a spectrum of clinical manifestations. The term glomerulocystic kidney refers to a kidney with greater than 5% cystic glomeruli.

HP:0100612.label: Odontogenic neoplasm
HP:0100612.definition: Neoplasm involving odontogenic cells, an odontogenic tumor.
HP:0100612.comment: Examples for odontogenic neoplasia are Adenomatoid odontogenic tumors, Ameloblastomas, Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumors, Calcifying odontogenic cysts, Dentigerous cysts, Odontogenic keratocysts, Dontogenic myxomas, Odontomas.

HP:0100613.label: Death in early adulthood
HP:0100613.definition: Death between the age of 16 and 40 years.

HP:0100614.label: Myositis
HP:0100614.definition: A general term for inflammation of the muscles without respect to the underlying cause.
HP:0100614.comment: Many such conditions are considered likely to be caused by autoimmune conditions, rather than directly due to infection, although autoimmune conditions can be activated or exacerbated by infections. It is also a documented side effect of the lipid-lowering drugs such as statins and fibrates. Elevation of creatine kinase in blood is indicative of myositis.

HP:0100615.label: Ovarian neoplasm
HP:0100615.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the ovary.

HP:0100616.label: Testicular teratoma
HP:0100616.definition: The presence of a teratoma of the testis.
HP:0100616.comment: An encapsulated tumor of the testis with tissue or organ components resembling normal derivatives of all three germ layers.

HP:0100617.label: Testicular seminoma
HP:0100617.definition: The presence of a seminoma, an undifferentiated germ cell tumor of the testis.

HP:0100618.label: Leydig cell neoplasia
HP:0100618.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the testis with origin in a Leydig cell.

HP:0100619.label: Sertoli cell neoplasm
HP:0100619.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the testis with origin in a Sertoli cell.

HP:0100620.label: Germinoma
HP:0100620.definition: A type of undifferentiated germ cell tumor that may be benign or malignant.

HP:0100621.label: Dysgerminoma
HP:0100621.definition: The presence of a dysgerminoma, i.e., an undifferentiated germ cell tumor of the ovary.

HP:0100623.label: Abnormal corpus cavernosum morphology
HP:0100623.definition: A structural anomaly of the corpus cavernosum, the erectile tissue of the penis.

HP:0100627.label: Displacement of the urethral meatus
HP:0100627.definition: A displacement of the external urethral orifice from its normal position (in males normally placed at the tip of glans penis, in females normally placed about 2.5 cm behind the glans clitoridis and immediately in front of that of the vagina).
HP:0100627.comment: Congenital misplacement of the urethral orifice is called hypospadias when it is located in the underside (ventral aspect) of the penis, and epispadias when located in the dorsum (upper aspect).
exact_synonyms: Displacement of the external urethral orifice
Displacement of the male external urethral orifice

HP:0100628.label: Esophageal diverticulum
HP:0100628.definition: The presence of a diverticulum of the esophagus.
HP:0100628.comment: A diverticulum is a blind ended outpouching through the wall of a tubular organ or bounded cavity.

HP:0100629.label: Midline facial cleft
HP:0100629.definition: A congenital malformation with a cleft (gap or opening) in the midline of the face.
HP:0100629.comment: Midline facial clefts correspond to Tessier number 0,14, and 30.

HP:0100631.label: Neoplasm of the adrenal gland
HP:0100631.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the adrenal gland.

HP:0100632.label: Pulmonary sequestration
HP:0100632.definition: The presence of a piece lung tissue which is not attached to the pulmonary blood supply and does not communicate with the other lung tissue (not connected to the standard bronchial airways and not performing a function in respiration).
HP:0100632.comment: Typically, the sequestered lung tissue receives all or most of its blood supply from an anomalous systemic artery, with the origin of this artery being variable.

HP:0100634.label: Neuroendocrine neoplasm
HP:0100634.definition: A tumor that originates from a neuroendocrine cell.
HP:0100634.comment: Neuroendocrine tumors are often diagnosed incidentally or when patients present with symptoms related to hormone production and/or tumor burden.

HP:0100635.label: Carotid paraganglioma
HP:0100635.definition: A paraganglioma (a neuroendocrine neoplasm) originating in a carotid artery.

HP:0100636.label: Pulmonary paraglioma
HP:0100636.definition: A rare paranglioma of the lung, tumors that arise from extra-adrenal chromaffin cells.

HP:0100638.label: Neoplasm of the pharynx
HP:0100638.definition: A neoplasm originating in the pharynx.
HP:0100638.comment: Tumors of pharynx may present with nonspecific findings such as otalgia or unilateral otitis media.

HP:0100639.label: Erectile dysfunction
HP:0100639.definition: A multidimensional but common male sexual dysfunction that involves an alteration in any of the components of the erectile response, including organic, relational and psychological.

HP:0100640.label: Laryngeal cyst
HP:0100640.definition: Presence of a cyst (sac-like structure) located in the larynx.

HP:0100641.label: Neoplasm of the adrenal cortex
HP:0100641.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the adrenal cortex.

HP:0100642.label: Neoplasm of the adrenal medulla
HP:0100642.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the adrenal medulla.

HP:0100643.label: Abnormality of nail color
HP:0100643.definition: An anomaly of the color of the nail.

HP:0100644.label: Melanonychia
HP:0100644.definition: Dark discoloration of a fingernail or toenail (brown, black, bluish and reddish).
HP:0100644.comment: The most serious disease of the nail unit, melanoma, primarily presents with melanonychia. However, melanonychia most often occurs as a result of benign etiologies such as nail matrix melanocytic activation, nail matrix melanocytic hyperplasia, subungual hematoma, glomus tumor, and nail invasion by melanin-producing pathogens.

HP:0100645.label: Cystocele
HP:0100645.definition: Anterior vaginal wall prolapse with bulging of the bladder into the vagina.
HP:0100645.comment: Cystocele occurs owing to weakening and stretching of the suppoortive tissue between the bladder and the vaginal wall.

HP:0100647.label: Graves disease
HP:0100647.definition: An autoimmune disease where the thyroid is overactive, producing an excessive amount of thyroid hormones (a serious metabolic imbalance known as hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis). This is caused by autoantibodies to the TSH-receptor (TSHR-Ab) that activate that TSH-receptor (TSHR), thereby stimulating thyroid hormone synthesis and secretion, and thyroid growth (causing a diffusely enlarged goiter). The resulting state of hyperthyroidism can cause a dramatic constellation of neuropsychological and physical signs and symptoms, which can severely compromise the patients.

HP:0100648.label: Neoplasm of the tongue
HP:0100648.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the tongue.

HP:0100649.label: Neoplasm of the oral cavity
HP:0100649.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the oral cavity.

HP:0100650.label: Vaginal neoplasm
HP:0100650.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the vagina.

HP:0100651.label: Type I diabetes mellitus
HP:0100651.definition: A chronic condition in which the pancreas produces little or no insulin. Type I diabetes mellitus is manifested by the sudden onset of severe hyperglycemia with rapid progression to diabetic ketoacidosis unless treated with insulin.
HP:0100651.comment: The onset of type 1 diabetes is typically during adolescence, but it can develop at any age.

HP:0100653.label: Optic neuritis
HP:0100653.comment: Optic neuritis can cause loss of vision because of swelling and destruction of the myelin sheath covering the optic nerve and/or direct axonal damage.

HP:0100654.label: Retrobulbar optic neuritis
HP:0100654.definition: Optic neuritis that occurs in the section of the optic nerve located behind the eyeball.

HP:0100656.label: Thoracoabdominal wall defect
HP:0100656.definition: Failure of the chest and abdominal wall to close, which is likely caused by the failure of the ventral wall to close during week 4 of development.
HP:0100656.comment: Thoracoschisis is a very rare congenital anomaly defined by the herniation of intra-abdominal organs through a defect in the thoracic wall. It be accompanied by thoracic ectopia cordis and gastroschisis.

HP:0100657.label: Thoracoabdominal eventration
HP:0100657.definition: Congenital protrusion of the abdominal or thoracic viscera, usually with a defect of the sternum and ribs as well as of the abdominal walls.

HP:0100658.label: Cellulitis
HP:0100658.definition: A bacterial infection and inflammation of the skin und subcutaneous tissues.
HP:0100658.comment: In contrast to impetigo, which is a very superficial skin infection, cellulitis involves both the dermis and the underlying subcutaneous tissue.

HP:0100659.label: Abnormal cerebral vascular morphology
HP:0100659.definition: An anomaly of the cerebral blood vessels.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the cerebral blood vessels

HP:0100660.label: Dyskinesia
HP:0100660.definition: A movement disorder which consists of effects including diminished voluntary movements and the presence of involuntary movements.

HP:0100661.label: Trigeminal neuralgia
HP:0100661.definition: A neuropathic disorder characterized by episodes of intense pain in the face, originating from the trigeminal nerve. One, two, or all three branches of the nerve may be affected.

HP:0100663.label: Synotia
HP:0100663.definition: A congenital malformation characterized by the union or approximation of the ears in front of the neck, often accompanied by the absence or defective development of the lower jaw.

HP:0100665.label: Angioedema
HP:0100665.definition: Rapid swelling (edema) of the dermis, subcutaneous tissue, mucosa and submucosal tissues of the skin of the face, normally around the mouth, and the mucosa of the mouth and/or throat, as well as the tongue during a period of minutes to several hours. The swelling can also occur elsewhere, typically in the hands. Angioedema is similar to urticaria, but the swelling is subcutaneous rather than on the epidermis.
HP:0100665.comment: Apart from the common form, mediated by allergy, it has been reported as a side effect of some medications, in particular ACE inhibitors. Additionally, there are three autosomal dominant inherited forms known, due to mutations in the genes that control the clotting cascade, including the SERPING1 gene, which results in deficiency of the blood protein C1-inhibitor (type I HAE) and the F12 gene, which controls Factor XII (type III HAE). There is an additional type in which C1 levels are normal but C1 function is decreased (type II HAE). All three forms are called hereditary angioedema (HAE) or occasionally by the outdated term 'hereditary angioneurotic edema' (HANE). In all forms of HAE, swelling may also occur in the digestive tract and other organs. It is life-threatening when it involves the larynx due to the potential for asphyxiation.

HP:0100668.label: Intestinal duplication
HP:0100668.definition: A developmental disorder in which there is a duplication the entire intestine or of a portion of the intestine.

HP:0100669.label: Abnormal pigmentation of the oral mucosa
HP:0100669.definition: An abnormality of the pigmentation of the mucosa of the mouth.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal pigmentation of the oral mucosa/gingivae
Abnormal pigmentation of oral mucous membrane

HP:0100670.label: Coarse metaphyseal trabecularization
HP:0100670.definition: Coarse appearance of the components of the network of osseous tissue that makes up the cancellous structure of a bone, i.e., thickening of the (usually fine) white lines that are produced by trabeculae in radiograms.

HP:0100671.label: Abnormal trabecular bone morphology
HP:0100671.definition: Abnormal structure or form of trabecular bone.

HP:0100672.label: Vaginal hernia
HP:0100672.definition: The presence of a hernia of the vagina.

HP:0100673.label: Vaginal hydrocele
HP:0100673.definition: A type of hydrocele testis in which the processus vaginalis remains patent only around the testes, and, as fluid accumulates, it renders the testes impalpable.
HP:0100673.comment: "vaginal" refers to the tunica vaginalis of the testis, not to the vagina.

HP:0100674.label: Vaginal hematocele
HP:0100674.comment: "vaginal" refers to the tunica vaginalis of the testis, not to the vagina.

HP:0100675.label: Vaginal pyocele
HP:0100675.comment: "vaginal" refers to the tunica vaginalis of the testis, not to the vagina.

HP:0100676.label: Vaginal lymphocele
HP:0100676.comment: "vaginal" refers to the tunica vaginalis of the testis, not to the vagina.

HP:0100677.label: Vulval varicose vein
HP:0100677.definition: Varicosity of veins in the vulval region.

HP:0100678.label: Premature skin wrinkling
HP:0100678.definition: The presence of an increased degree of wrinkling (irregular folds and indentations) of the skin as compared with age-related norms.

HP:0100681.label: Esophageal duplication
HP:0100681.definition: A developmental disorder in which there is a duplication of a portion of the muscle and submucosa of the esophagus without epithelial duplication.
HP:0100681.comment: Esophageal duplication is a rare cause of mediastinal mass. An esophageal duplication may be a simple epithelial cyst or duplication that contains muscle and submucosa but not epithelium. In most cases, the duplication is located in the lower third of the esophagus, and the most common associated symptom is difficulty in swallowing. Esophageal duplication occurs because of maldevelopment of the posterior division of embryonic foregut.

HP:0100682.label: Tracheal atresia
HP:0100682.definition: A congenital absence or considerable underdevelopment of the trachea such that communication between the larynx proximally and the alveoli of the lungs distally is lacking.
HP:0100682.comment: Diagnosis can be made if the neonate presents with respiratory distress at birth, unable to produce an audible cry in spite of an obvious physical effort, and cannot be intubated but shows some improvement when ventilated by bag and mask.

HP:0100684.label: Salivary gland neoplasm
HP:0100684.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of a salivary gland.

HP:0100685.label: Abnormal Sharpey fiber morphology
HP:0100685.definition: An abnormality of Sharpey's fibers (bone fibers, or perforating fibers), which are a matrix of connective tissue consisting of bundles of strong collagenous fibers connecting periosteum to bone.

HP:0100687.label: Polyotia
HP:0100687.definition: The presence of an extra auricle on one or both sides of the head.

HP:0100689.label: Decreased corneal thickness
HP:0100689.definition: A decreased anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.

HP:0100691.label: Abnormality of the curvature of the cornea

HP:0100692.label: Increased corneal curvature
HP:0100692.definition: An increase in the degree of curvature of the cornea compared to normal.

HP:0100693.label: Iridodonesis
HP:0100693.definition: Tremulousness of the iris on movement of the eye, occurring in subluxation of the lens.

HP:0100694.label: Tibial torsion
HP:0100694.definition: Twisted position of the tibia (shin bone) associated with pathological rotation of the leg.
HP:0100694.comment: Normally, lateral rotation of the tibia increases from approximately 5 degrees at birth to approximately 15 degrees at maturity. Tibial torsion is the most common cause of intoeing. In a study by Mullaji et al to determine tibial torsion norms, individuals in India were found to have less tibial torsion than Caucasians but about the same amount as the Japanese population. The differences in normal tibial torsion values are expected to be caused by the different lifestyles and postures of the different populations, such as cross-legged sitting positions.

HP:0100695.label: Lipedema
HP:0100695.definition: Excess deposit and expansion of adipose tissue in an unusual pattern which cannot be lost through diet and exercise .
HP:0100695.comment: The pattern of fat deposition is most often bilateral, symmetrical and usually from the waist to a distinct line just above the ankles.

HP:0100697.label: Neurofibrosarcoma
HP:0100697.definition: A form of malignant cancer of the connective tissue surrounding nerves. Given its origin and behavior, it is classified as a sarcoma.
HP:0100697.comment: About half the cases are diagnosed in people with neurofibromatosis.

HP:0100698.label: Subcutaneous neurofibroma
HP:0100698.definition: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the subcutis (subcutaneous region).

HP:0100699.label: Scarring
HP:0100699.definition: A scar refers to a lesion in which wound, burn, or sore has not healed completely and fibrous connective tissue has developed.

HP:0100700.label: Abnormal arachnoid mater morphology
HP:0100700.definition: An abnormality of the Arachnoid mater.

HP:0100701.label: Abnormal pia mater
HP:0100701.definition: An abnormality of the pia mater.

HP:0100702.label: Arachnoid cyst
HP:0100702.definition: An extra-parenchymal and intra-arachnoidal collection of fluid with a composition similar to that of cerebrospinal fluid.
HP:0100702.comment: Arachnoid cysts can be found on the brain, or on the spine. Intracranial arachnoid cysts usually occur adjacent to the arachnoidal cistern. Spinal arachnoid cysts may be extradural, intradural, or perineural.
exact_synonyms: Fluid-filled sac located in membrane surrounding brain or spinal cord

HP:0100703.label: Tongue thrusting
HP:0100703.definition: Pressing forward of the tongue in the mouth, a retained motoric habit from infantile swallowing patterns

HP:0100704.label: Cerebral visual impairment
HP:0100704.definition: A form of loss of vision caused by damage to the visual cortex rather than a defect in the eye.
HP:0100704.comment: The term cortical/cerebral visual impairment (CVI) was coined to describe damage to visual pathways and structures occurring during early perinatal development. The term cortical visual impairment was originally proposed to describe visual dysfunction in pediatric populations of non-ocular cause, and its presumed association with damage to early visual cortical areas. However, as further characterization of this condition progressed, it became evident that CVI was often associated with damage to sites beyond early visual cortex including subcortical structures, white matter pathways, as well as higher-order associative processing areas of the cortex. Thus, the word cortical has been viewed as somewhat of a misnomer, and there has been the suggestion that the term cerebral would be a more encompassing and appropriate term. Although there is still a debate in the community about the most appropriate nomenclature, the HPO will regard these terms as synonymous. It is recommended that more specific terms be used as appropriate for annotation.

HP:0100705.label: Abnormal glial cell morphology
HP:0100705.definition: An abnormality of the glia cell.
HP:0100705.comment: Glia are nonneuronal cells of the nervous system that provide physical support, respond to injury, regulate the composition of the extracellular milieu, guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons.

HP:0100706.label: Abnormal oligodendroglia morphology
HP:0100706.definition: One of the three types of glia cells that, with the nerve cells, compose the central nervous system and are characterized by sheetlike processes that wrap around individual axons to form the myelin sheath of nerve fibers.

HP:0100707.label: Abnormal astrocyte morphology
HP:0100707.comment: Astrocytes represent a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system.

HP:0100708.label: Abnormal microglia morphology
HP:0100708.definition: An abnormality of the microglial cells. They are also known as brain-resident macrophages or Hortega cells.
HP:0100708.comment: Microglial cells represent a central nervous system macrophage found in the parenchyma of the central nervous system.

HP:0100710.label: Impulsivity
HP:0100710.definition: Acting on the spur of the moment or on a momentary basis without consideration of outcomes; having difficulty establishing or following plans; experiencing a sense of urgency and engaging in behavior that is uninhibited, cannot be inhibited, and is uncontrolled. The possibility of repression is inconceivable.

HP:0100711.label: Abnormal thoracic spine morphology
HP:0100711.definition: An abnormality of the thoracic vertebral column.

HP:0100712.label: Abnormal lumbar spine morphology
HP:0100712.definition: Any structural abnormality of the lumbar vertebral column.

HP:0100716.label: Self-injurious behavior
HP:0100716.comment: All of these actions can be impulsive, compulsive, or planned.

HP:0100717.label: Abnormal cementum morphology
HP:0100717.definition: Any structural anomaly of the cementum, which is the mineralized connective tissue covering the dental root. The cementum allows anchoring of the fibers of the periodontal ligament. Cementum is secreted by cementoblasts, which may be, later on, embedded in the cementum. Cementum can be acellular (along the two third coronal portion of the root) and cellular (in the apical and interradicular part of the root).

HP:0100719.label: Lens coloboma
HP:0100719.definition: A sectoral indentation of the crystalline lens, usually due to zonular weakness or absence.

HP:0100721.label: Mediastinal lymphadenopathy
HP:0100721.definition: Swelling of lymph nodes within the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavities that contains the heart and the great vessels, the esophagus, and trachea and other structures including lymph nodes.
exact_synonyms: Swollen lymph nodes in center of chest
Swollen lymph nodes in centre of chest

HP:0100724.label: Hypercoagulability
HP:0100724.definition: An abnormality of coagulation associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

HP:0100725.label: Lichenification
HP:0100725.definition: Thickening and hardening of the epidermis seen with exaggeration of normal skin lines.

HP:0100726.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
HP:0100726.definition: A systemic disease which can present with cutaneous lesions with or without internal involvement. Tumors are caused by Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV8), also known as Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV).

HP:0100727.label: Histiocytosis
HP:0100727.definition: An excessive number of histiocytes (tissue macrophages).

HP:0100730.label: Bronchogenic cyst
HP:0100730.definition: A rare congenital cystic lesion of the lungs in the mediastinum.
HP:0100730.comment: Bronchogenic cysts (BCs) are congenital lesions thought to result from abnormal budding of the embryonic foregut. The most frequent symptoms are pain, cough, fever, respiratory distress, or dyspnea. Intrapulmonary bronchogenic cysts are usually sharply defined, solitary, non-calcified, round, or oval opacities confined to a single lobe. These can present as a homogeneous water density, an air- filled cyst, or with an air-fluid level. The cyst can rupture into the trachea, pericardial cavity, or pleural cavity. Infection of the cyst may lead to surrounding acinar shadow. An air-filled cyst or one with an air-fluid level may be present if a complicating tracheo-bronchial connection develops.

HP:0100731.label: Transverse facial cleft
HP:0100731.definition: A horizontal cleft of the face, varying from slight widening of the mouth, to a cleft extending to the ear.
HP:0100731.comment: Usually, these clefts are unilateral and do not extend beyond the anterior border of the masseter. Transverse clefts are thought to develop either due to failure of the maxillary and mandibular processes to fuse or a disruption in the processes after fusing.

HP:0100733.label: Neoplasm of the parathyroid gland
HP:0100733.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the parathyroid gland.

HP:0100734.label: Abnormal vertebral epiphysis morphology
HP:0100734.definition: An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of one or more vertebrae.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal shape of the end part of the vertebra bone

HP:0100736.label: Abnormal soft palate morphology
HP:0100736.definition: An abnormality of the soft palate.

HP:0100738.label: Abnormal eating behavior
HP:0100738.definition: Abnormal eating habits involve excessive or insufficient consumption of food, or any other abnormal pattern of food consumption.
HP:0100738.comment: Please note that this HPO term refers to an abnormal eating habit but does not directly refer to an eating disorder. An eating disorder is a psychological disorder characterized by one or more abnormal eating behaviors.

HP:0100739.label: Bulimia
HP:0100739.definition: A form of anomalous eating behavior characterized by binge eating is followed by self-induced vomiting or other compensatory behavior intended to prevent weight gain (purging, fasting or exercising or a combination of these).

HP:0100742.label: Vascular neoplasm
HP:0100742.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) originating in the vascular system.

HP:0100745.label: Abnormality of the humeroulnar joint
HP:0100745.definition: An anomaly of the joint between the trochlear notch of ulna and the trochlea of humerus, which is part of the elbow joint.

HP:0100746.label: Macrodactyly of finger
HP:0100746.definition: A type of Macrodactyly affecting one or several fingers.

HP:0100747.label: Macrodactyly of toe
HP:0100747.definition: A type of Macrodactyly affecting one or several toes.

HP:0100749.label: Chest pain
HP:0100749.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the chest.

HP:0100750.label: Atelectasis
HP:0100750.definition: Collapse of part of a lung associated with absence of inflation (air) of that part.
exact_synonyms: Partial or complete collapse of part or entire lung

HP:0100751.label: Esophageal neoplasm
HP:0100751.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the esophagus.

HP:0100752.label: Abnormal liver lobulation
HP:0100752.definition: Formation of abnormal lobules (small masses of tissue) in the liver.

HP:0100753.label: Schizophrenia
HP:0100753.definition: A mental disorder characterized by a disintegration of thought processes and emotional responsiveness. It most commonly manifests as auditory hallucinations, paranoid or bizarre delusions, or disorganized speech and thinking. It is accompanied by significant social or occupational dysfunction. The onset of symptoms typically occurs in young adulthood, with a global lifetime prevalence of about 1%. This term is not a helpful parent term to describe abnormal experiences.
HP:0100753.comment: Positive symptoms, such as delusions and hallucinations (especially of voices), are common, and any Schneiderian first-rank symptoms are particularly indicative of the illness. Negative symptoms include social withdrawal, impairment of ego boundaries, and loss of energy and initiative. Schizophrenia is diagnosed only if symptoms persist for at least one month. The illness can spontaneously remit, run a course with infrequent or frequent relapses, or become chronic. The prognosis has improved with antipsychotic drugs and with vigorous psychological and social management and rehabilitation. The many causes include genetic factors, environmental stress, and various triggering factors.

HP:0100754.label: Mania
HP:0100754.definition: A state of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.

HP:0100757.label: Pancreatoblastoma
HP:0100757.definition: A rare pediatric carcinoma of the pancreas.

HP:0100758.label: Gangrene
HP:0100758.definition: A serious and potentially life-threatening condition that arises when a considerable mass of body tissue dies (necrosis).
HP:0100758.comment: This may occur after an injury or infection, or in people suffering from any chronic health problem affecting blood circulation. The prime cause of gangrene is reduced blood supply to the affected tissues, which results in cell death. Diabetes and long-term smoking increase the risk of suffering from gangrene. There are different types of gangrene with different symptoms, such as dry gangrene, wet gangrene, gas gangrene, internal gangrene and necrotising fasciitis. Treatment options include debridement (or, in severe cases, amputation) of the affected body parts, antibiotics, vascular surgery, maggot therapy or hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
exact_synonyms: Death of body tissue due to lack of blood flow or infection

HP:0100759.label: Clubbing of fingers
HP:0100759.definition: Terminal broadening of the fingers (distal phalanges of the fingers).

HP:0100760.label: Clubbing of toes
HP:0100760.definition: Terminal broadening of the toes (distal phalanges of the toes).

HP:0100763.label: Abnormality of the lymphatic system
HP:0100763.definition: An anomaly of the lymphatic system, a network of lymphatic vessels that carry a clear fluid called lymph unidirectionally towards either the right lymphatic duct or the thoracic duct, which in turn drain into the right and left subclavian veins respectively.

HP:0100764.label: Lymphangioma
HP:0100764.definition: Lymphangiomas are rare congenital malformations consisting of focal proliferations of well-differentiated lymphatic tissue in multi cystic or sponge like structures. Lymphangioma is usually asymptomatic due to its soft consistency but compression of adjacent structures can be seen due to the mass effect of a large tumor.

HP:0100766.label: Abnormal lymphatic vessel morphology
HP:0100766.definition: A structural anomaly of the vessel that contains or conveys lymph fluid.

HP:0100767.label: Abnormal placenta morphology
HP:0100767.definition: An abnormality of the placenta, the organ that connects the developing fetus to the uterine wall to enable nutrient uptake, waste elimination, and gas exchange.
HP:0100767.comment: The placenta is a fetomaternal organ. The fetal portion of the placenta is the villous chorion and the maternal portion is the decidua basalis. The two portions are connected by anchoring villi that are anchored to the decidua basalis by the cytotrophoblastic shell.

HP:0100768.label: Choriocarcinoma
HP:0100768.definition: A malignant, trophoblastic and aggressive cancer, usually of the placenta. It is characterized by early hematogenous spread to the lungs and belongs to the far end of the spectrum of gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD), a subset of germ cell tumors.

HP:0100770.label: Hyperperistalsis
HP:0100770.definition: Excessively active peristalsis (wave of contraction of the tubular organs of the gastrointestinal tract) marked by excessive rapidity of the passage of food through the stomach and intestine.

HP:0100771.label: Hypoperistalsis
HP:0100771.definition: Reduced or inadequate peristalsis, with resultant slow passage of contents through the digestive tract.

HP:0100774.label: Hyperostosis
HP:0100774.definition: Excessive growth or abnormal thickening of bone tissue.
HP:0100774.comment: Hyperostosis refers to a localized bone overgrowth process (as opposed to sclerosis, which refers to a generalized disturbance with increased bone density).

HP:0100775.label: Dural ectasia
HP:0100775.definition: A widening or ballooning of the dural sac surrounding the spinal cord usually at the lumbosacral level.
HP:0100775.comment: Dural ectasia is one of the major manifestations of Marfan syndrome. It may cause low back pain, headaches and neurological signs such as weakness and loss of bowel and bladder function, but in many patients it is asymptomatic. It is also a cause of posterior vertebral scalloping present in radiographs in patients who are diagnosed with Neurofibromatosis. Dural ectasia may also manifest in Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, cauda equina syndrome and in ankylosing spondylitis.

HP:0100776.label: Recurrent pharyngitis
HP:0100776.definition: An increased susceptibility to pharyngitis as manifested by a history of recurrent pharyngitis.

HP:0100777.label: Exostoses
HP:0100777.definition: An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage, and arises from a bone that develops from cartilage.
exact_synonyms: Formation of new noncancerous bone on top of existing bone

HP:0100778.label: Cryoglobulinemia
HP:0100778.definition: Increased level of cryoglobulins in the blood. Cryoglobulins are abnormal immunoglobulins, especially IGG or IGM, that precipitate spontaneously when serum is cooled below 37 degrees Celsius.

HP:0100779.label: Urogenital sinus anomaly
HP:0100779.definition: A rare birth defect in women where the urethra and vagina both open into a common channel.

HP:0100780.label: Conjunctival hamartoma
HP:0100780.definition: A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) of the conjunctiva.

HP:0100781.label: Abnormal sacroiliac joint morphology
HP:0100781.definition: An anomaly of the sacroiliac joint, which connects the base of the spine (sacrum) to the ilium (a hip bone).
HP:0100781.comment: The sacroiliac joint (SIJ) is a true diarthrodial joint: matching articular surfaces separated by a joint space containing synovial fluid and enveloped by a fibrous capsule. It does, however, have unique characteristics not typically found in other diarthrodial joints. The SIJ has fibrocartilage in addition to hyaline cartilage. There is discontinuity of the posterior capsule. Rather than being smooth, the articular surfaces have many ridges and depressions that minimize movement and enhance stability. Primary stability, however, is attributed to the many adjacent ligaments.

HP:0100783.label: Breast aplasia
HP:0100783.definition: Failure to develop and congenital absence of the breast.

HP:0100785.label: Insomnia
HP:0100785.definition: Persistent difficulty in starting or maintaining sleep, or waking up earlier than desired, despite having adequate opportunities and conditions for sleep.
HP:0100785.comment: The individual subjectively reports the inability to sleep, which may manifest as prolonged sleep latency, frequent awakenings, or premature morning awakening. This phenomenon is often linked or associated with distress, reduced daytime functioning, or dissatisfaction with sleep.

HP:0100788.label: Fused lips
HP:0100788.definition: Lack of separation of the upper and lower lips.
exact_synonyms: Fusion of upper and lower lips
Adhesion of upper and lower lips

HP:0100789.label: Torus palatinus
HP:0100789.definition: A bony protrusion present on the midline of the hard palate.

HP:0100792.label: Acantholysis
HP:0100792.definition: The loss of intercellular connections, such as desmosomes, resulting in loss of cohesion between keratinocytes.
HP:0100792.comment: Acantolysis results in a positive Nikolsky's sign in which slight rubbing of the skin results in exfoliation of the outermost layer.

HP:0100795.label: Abnormally straight spine
HP:0100795.definition: The absence of the normal curvature of the vertebral column.

HP:0100797.label: Toenail dysplasia
HP:0100797.definition: An abnormality of the development of the toenails.

HP:0100798.label: Fingernail dysplasia
HP:0100798.definition: An abnormality of the development of the fingernails.
HP:0100798.comment: If possible, a more precise term should be chosen for annotation.

HP:0100799.label: Neoplasm of the middle ear
HP:0100799.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the middle ear.

HP:0100800.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the pancreas
HP:0100800.definition: A congenital underdevelopment (aplasia or hypoplasia) of the pancreas.

HP:0100802.label: Malposition of the stomach
HP:0100802.definition: Abnormal anatomical location of the stomach. This feature may be due to intestinal malrotation.

HP:0100803.label: Abnormal periungual morphology
HP:0100803.definition: An abnormality of the region around the nails of the fingers or toes.

HP:0100804.label: Ungual fibroma
HP:0100804.definition: Flesh-colored papule in or around the nail bed. Ungual fibromas may be periungual (arising under the proximal nail fold) or subungual (originating under the nail plate).
HP:0100804.comment: Ungual fibromas are characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.

HP:0100806.label: Sepsis
HP:0100806.definition: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.
HP:0100806.comment: For clinical operationalization, organ dysfunction can be represented by an increase in the Sequential Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score of 2 points or more.

HP:0100807.label: Long fingers
HP:0100807.definition: The middle finger is more than 2 SD above the mean for newborns 27 to 41 weeks EGA or above the 97th centile for children from birth to 16 years of age AND the five digits retain their normal length proportions relative to each other (i.e., it is not the case that the middle finger is the only lengthened digit), or, Fingers that appear disproportionately long compared to the palm of the hand.

HP:0100808.label: Gastric diverticulum
HP:0100808.definition: An outpouching of the gastric wall.
HP:0100808.comment: Gastric diverticulum may be asymptomatic or may present with a vague sensation of fullness or discomfort in the upper abdomen, or with acute upper gastrointestinal bleed or perforation.

HP:0100809.label: Scalp tenderness
HP:0100809.definition: Pain or discomfort of the scalp elicited by palpation.

HP:0100811.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the colon
HP:0100811.definition: Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the colon.

HP:0100812.label: Halitosis
HP:0100812.definition: Noticeably unpleasant odors exhaled in breathing.

HP:0100813.label: Testicular torsion
HP:0100813.definition: Testicular torsion is when the spermatic cord to a testicle twists, cutting off the blood supply. The most common symptom is acute testicular pain.
HP:0100813.comment: Many of the symptoms of testicular torsion are similar to the infection epididymitis.

HP:0100814.label: Blue nevus
HP:0100814.definition: A solitary, bluish, smooth surfaced macule, papule or plaque that is generally round or oval in shape. The histopathology of blue nevi varies by subtype, but general characteristics include a vertical wedge or bulbous shaped proliferation of spindle cells, dendritic melanocytes, and melanophages into a sclerotic dermis or subcutis.

HP:0100816.label: Lip hyperpigmentation
exact_synonyms: Darkening of skin of the lips

HP:0100817.label: Renovascular hypertension
HP:0100817.definition: The presence of hypertension related to stenosis of the renal artery.
HP:0100817.comment: Renal artery stenosis can lead to hypertension and chronic kidney disease (due to chronic renal ischemia). The hypertension is caused by activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.
exact_synonyms: Hypertension due to renal artery hyperplasia

HP:0100818.label: Long thorax
HP:0100818.definition: Increased inferior to superior extent of the thorax.

HP:0100819.label: Intestinal fistula
HP:0100819.definition: An abnormal connection between the gut and another hollow organ, such as the bladder, urethra, vagina, or other regions of the gastrointestinal tract.

HP:0100820.label: Glomerulopathy
HP:0100820.definition: Inflammatory or noninflammatory diseases affecting the glomeruli of the nephron.

HP:0100821.label: Urethrocele
HP:0100821.definition: The prolapse of the female urethra into the vagina.

HP:0100822.label: Rectocele
HP:0100822.definition: A Rectocele results from a tear in the rectovaginal septum (which is normally a tough, fibrous, sheet-like divider between the rectum and vagina). Rectal tissue bulges through this tear and into the vagina as a hernia. There are two main causes of this tear: childbirth, and hysterectomy.

HP:0100825.label: Cheilitis
HP:0100825.comment: It is associated with many conditions, including megaloblastic anemia from vitamin B12 deficiency, iron deficiency anemia (which in severe cases can lead to Plummer-Vinson syndrome) and oral candidiasis. It can also be a symptom of allergies, such as allergy to Balsam of Peru. Cheilitis can also be caused by taking the (retinoid) drug Isotretinoin. It may also be a pre-malignant lesion for squamous cell carcinoma.

HP:0100826.label: Neoplasm of the nail
HP:0100826.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the nail.

HP:0100827.label: Increased total lymphocyte count
HP:0100827.definition: Increase in the number or proportion of lymphocytes in the blood.

HP:0100828.label: Increased total T cell count
HP:0100828.definition: The absolute number of T cells per volume is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0100829.label: Galactorrhea
HP:0100829.definition: Spontaneous flow of milk from the breast, unassociated with childbirth or nursing.

HP:0100831.label: Abnormality of vitamin K metabolism
HP:0100831.definition: Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin with a role in promoting the coagulation cascade.

HP:0100832.label: Vitreous floaters
HP:0100832.definition: Deposits of various size, shape, consistency, refractive index, and motility within the eye's vitreous humor, which is normally transparent.
HP:0100832.comment: Vitreous floaters are described as vitreous condensations (or vitreous debris or vitreous opacities) as a finding upon ophthalmological examination. Floaters can take many forms from little dots, circles, lines, to clouds or cobwebs. The floaters are created by a shadow of the floating vitreal debris that is projected onto the retina, which is described as a veil.

HP:0100833.label: Neoplasm of the small intestine
HP:0100833.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the small intestine.
HP:0100833.comment: An estimated 40% of small bowel cancers are adenocarcinomas, 40% are carcinoids, 15% are sarcomas (GI stromal tumors), and less than 5% are lymphomas.

HP:0100834.label: Neoplasm of the large intestine
HP:0100834.definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the large intestine.

HP:0100835.label: Benign neoplasm of the central nervous system

HP:0100836.label: Malignant neoplasm of the central nervous system
HP:0100836.definition: A tumor that originates in the pineal gland, has moderate cellularity and tends to form rosette patterns.

HP:0100837.label: Atrophodermia vermiculata
HP:0100837.definition: Symmetrical vermiform facial atrophy that affects mainly the forehead, the chin, the ear lobes and helices. Atrophodermia vermiculata is characterized by erythema and follicular plugs on the cheeks, developing into painless reticular impressions.
HP:0100837.comment: The onset of atrophodermia vermiculata is usually between the ages of 5 and 12 years.

HP:0100838.label: Recurrent cutaneous abscess formation
HP:0100838.definition: An increased susceptibility to cutaneous abscess formation, as manifested by a medical history of recurrent cutaneous abscesses.

HP:0100839.label: Hepatic agenesis
HP:0100839.definition: Absence of the liver owing to a failure of the liver to develop.

HP:0100840.label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the eyebrow
HP:0100840.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the eyebrow.

HP:0100841.label: Microgastria
HP:0100841.definition: A developmental anomaly with a small tubular or saccular midline stomach.
HP:0100841.comment: Patients with microgastria usually have poor growth, inadequate food consumption, or a complication of the small gastric cavity and gastroesophageal reflux, including frequent vomiting or pneumonia.

HP:0100842.label: Septo-optic dysplasia
HP:0100842.definition: Underdevelopment of the optic nerve and absence of the septum pellucidum.

HP:0100845.label: Anaphylactic shock
HP:0100845.definition: An acute hypersensitivity reaction due to exposure to a previously encountered antigen.
HP:0100845.comment: Anaphylaxis may lead to rapidly progressing urticaria, respiratory distress, vascular collapse, systemic shock, and death if untreated.

HP:0100847.label: Palmoplantar pustulosis
HP:0100847.definition: A chronic, relapsing, pustular eruption that is localized to the palms and soles.
HP:0100847.comment: There are recurrent and painful eruptions of pustules on the palms and the soles of feet that may resolve with red-brown discoloration.

HP:0100848.label: Neoplasm of the male external genitalia
HP:0100848.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the male external genitalia.
exact_synonyms: Neoplasia of the male external genitalia

HP:0100849.label: Neoplasm of the scrotum
HP:0100849.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the scrotum.

HP:0100850.label: Neoplasm of the penis
HP:0100850.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the penis.

HP:0100851.label: Abnormal emotional state
HP:0100851.definition: A disturbance in the experience or expression of emotion, characterized by alterations in valence, intensity, frequency, or duration. It may also involve emotional responses that are mismatched, exaggerated, or incongruent relative to internal expectations or external contextual stimuli, such as experiencing negative affect in response to neutral or positive events.
HP:0100851.comment: Emotions are complex psychological and physiological states that may include any combination of: a subjective internal experience, a physiological response, and a behavioral or expressive component. Behavioral expression is not required for the emotional state to be considered present or clinically relevant. The assessment of abnormal emotional states should consider sociocultural and individual context, as well as intra-individual baselines. The term 'abnormal' is used descriptively and non-pejoratively, to denote deviations from typical emotional patterns, which may or may not reach the threshold of clinical disorder.

HP:0100852.label: Abnormal fear-induced behavior
HP:0100852.definition: An abnormal fear-induced behavior includes observable actions. This behavior is characterized by abnormal responses to fear or abnormal fear levels. Examples of such behavior include avoiding fear-inducing situations.
HP:0100852.comment: Internal responses to fear, which are experienced by an individual and do not necessarily involve clear behavioral changes (observable actions), should be labeled with a term for fear-related cognition, such as HP:5200230.

HP:0100853.label: Hypoplastic areola
HP:0100853.definition: Underdevelopment of the areola, the circular area of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple.

HP:0100856.label: Poorly ossified vertebrae
HP:0100856.definition: Decreased ossification of the vertebral bodies.

HP:0100858.label: Dilatation of celiac artery
HP:0100858.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the celiac artery.
HP:0100858.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0100859.label: Dilatation of superior mesenteric artery
HP:0100859.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the superior mesenteric artery .
HP:0100859.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0100860.label: Dilatation of Inferior mesenteric artery
HP:0100860.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the inferior mesenteric artery .
HP:0100860.comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

HP:0100861.label: Sclerotic vertebral body
HP:0100861.definition: Increase in bone density of the vertebral body.

HP:0100864.label: Short femoral neck
HP:0100864.definition: An abnormally short femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

HP:0100865.label: Broad ischia
HP:0100865.definition: Increased width of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.

HP:0100867.label: Duodenal stenosis
HP:0100867.definition: The narrowing or partial blockage of a portion of the duodenum.

HP:0100869.label: Palmar telangiectasia
HP:0100869.definition: The presence of telangiectases on the skin of palm of hand.

HP:0100870.label: Plantar telangiectasia
HP:0100870.definition: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located on the skin of sole of foot.

HP:0100871.label: Abnormal palm morphology
HP:0100871.definition: An abnormality of the palm, that is, of the front of the hand.

HP:0100872.label: Abnormality of the plantar skin of foot
HP:0100872.definition: An abnormality of the plantar part of foot, that is of the soles of the feet.

HP:0100874.label: Thick hair
HP:0100874.definition: Increased density of hairs, i.e., and elevated number of hairs per unit area.

HP:0100875.label: Hemimacroglossia
HP:0100875.definition: Increased length and width of one half of the tongue.
exact_synonyms: Hypertrophy of half of the tongue
Increased size of half of the tongue

HP:0100876.label: Infra-orbital crease
HP:0100876.definition: Skin crease extending from below the inner canthus laterally along the malar process of the maxilla and zygoma.
HP:0100876.comment: This feature is often found in the presence of hypoplasia of the malar process of the maxilla or zygoma, but should be coded separately.
exact_synonyms: Groove in skin under the eye
Crease in skin under the eye

HP:0100877.label: Renal diverticulum
HP:0100877.definition: Cystic, urine-containing intrarenal cavities lined with transitional cell epithelium that communicate through a narrow channel with the collecting system.

HP:0100880.label: Nephrogenic rest
HP:0100880.definition: Abnormally persistent clusters of embryonal cells, representing microscopic malformations (dysplasias) of the developing kidney.
HP:0100880.comment: Though NR are best known as precursors of Wilms tumor (WT), many alternative fates are observed, and most rests are destined for eventual atresia. Nephroblastomatosis refers to the presence of multifocal or diffuse nephrogenic rests.

HP:0100881.label: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma
HP:0100881.definition: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma is a type of kidney tumor that is usually found before birth by ultrasound or within the first 3 months of life. It contains fibroblastic cells (connective tissue cells), and may spread to the other kidney or to nearby tissue.
HP:0100881.comment: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma is more common in males.

HP:0100882.label: Fibrous hamartoma
HP:0100882.definition: A rare, benign soft tissue tumor that typically occurs within the first two years of life.

HP:0100883.label: Chorangioma
HP:0100883.definition: Hamartoma-like growth in the placenta consisting of blood vessels.
HP:0100883.comment: Chorioangiomas (also known as placental hemangiomas) are benign hamartomatous growth of the placenta comprising vascular tissue. The classification is controversial due to its pathologic features and clinical implications. Some authors call placental hemangiomas as true nontrophoblastic neoplastic tissues. As this abnormal vascular growth seems like the native placental tissue and it does not metastasize, some authors call it just as placental hamartoma. The general incidence is approximately 0.6 percent. Giant chorioangiomas with a diameter over 5 cm are very rare, with an incidence of one in 16-50 thousand pregnancies. Small tumors do not cause any adverse outcomes and they are asymptomatic. In contrast, tumors larger than 5 cm may lead to several complications.

HP:0100884.label: Compensatory scoliosis
HP:0100884.definition: A scoliosis which is the results of a difference in leg length (which might be due to hemihypertrophy or hemihypotrophy of a leg) and the resulting tilting of the pelvis. If untreated this will lead to the development of scoliosis over time.

HP:0100885.label: Lateral venous anomaly
HP:0100885.definition: Persistence of the embryonic dorsal or sciatic vein system that normally should have involuted around the tenth to twelfth week of intrauterine life.
HP:0100885.comment: Embryonic leg veins usually regress before birth, but in Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) a persistent embryonic vein (PEV) may be located on the lateral aspect of the affected leg. Known PEVs of the leg are the lateral marginal vein (LMV) and the persistent sciatic vein (PSV). The nomenclature can be confusing because various terms are used to indicate the same aberrant leg vein in KTS (e.g. vein of Servelle, Klippel-Trenaunay vein, lateral marginal vein).

HP:0100886.label: Abnormality of globe location
HP:0100886.definition: An abnormality in the placement of the ocular globe (eyeball).

HP:0100887.label: Abnormality of globe size
HP:0100887.definition: An abnormality in the size of the ocular globe (eyeball).

HP:0100889.label: Abnormal ductus choledochus morphology
HP:0100889.definition: An abnormality of the Common bile duct, a tube-like anatomic structure in the human gastrointestinal tract, formed by the union of the Common hepatic duct and the Cystic duct from the gall bladder.
exact_synonyms: Abnormality of the common bile duct

HP:0100891.label: Bifid xiphoid process
HP:0100891.definition: A cleft of the xiphoid process of the sternum.

HP:0100892.label: Abnormality of the xiphoid process
HP:0100892.definition: An abnormality of the xiphoid process of the sternum.

HP:0100893.label: Prominent xiphoid process
HP:0100893.definition: Increased prominence of the xiphoid process of the sternum.

HP:0100894.label: Broad xiphoid process
HP:0100894.definition: Increased side-to-side width of the xiphoid process of the sternum.

HP:0100896.label: Rectal polyposis
HP:0100896.definition: The presence of multiple rectal hyperplastic/adenomatous polyps.

HP:0100898.label: Connective tissue nevi
HP:0100898.definition: Connective tissue nevi are hamartomas in which one or several components of the dermis is altered.
HP:0100898.comment: Lesions in which collagen predominates are called collagenomas; lesions in which elastin predominates are called elastomas. A nevus mucinosis is a lesion in which an alteration in the amount of dermal glycosaminoglycan is present. The name nevus mucinosis is also used for lesions in which an alteration in more than one dermal component is present. Connective tissue nevi may be solitary or multiple, sporadic or inherited. They may occur as isolated skin lesions, or they may be associated with a number of syndromes.
