HP:0100950.comment: Previously, 3-alpha-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase was referred to as short-chain 3-alpha-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase as well as medium and short-chain L-3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase.
related_synonyms: Long chain 3 hydroxyacyl coA dehydrogenase deficiency
Medium and short-chain L-3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency

HP:0100952.label: Enlarged sylvian cistern
HP:0100952.definition: An increase in size of the subarachnoid space associated with the lateral cerebral sulcus (Sylvian fissure).

HP:0100957.label: Abnormal renal medulla morphology
HP:0100957.definition: Any structural abnormality of the medulla of the kidney.
HP:0100957.comment: The renal pyramids of the adult kidney resemble a cone with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla. The adult renal medulla is made up of 10-18 pyramids. A pyramid consists of the medullary collecting ducts, loops of Henle, vasa recta (straight capillaries) and the interstitium. The main function of the medulla is to regulate concentration of the urine. The urine flows from the collecting ducts into the renal calyces and pelvis.

HP:0100958.label: Narrow foramen obturatorium
HP:0100958.definition: Decreased width of the foramen obturatorium. The foramen obturatorium (also known as the obturator foramen) is a hole located between the ischium and pubis bones of the pelvis.

HP:0100959.label: Dense metaphyseal bands
HP:0100959.definition: Dense radiopaque bands of bone which are thicker than the adjacent diaphyseal cortex and may form at the metaphysis of growing bones. They appear on radiographs as bone that is more radiopaque that the adjacent diaphyseal cortex.
exact_synonyms: Lead lines in metaphyses of bones

HP:0100960.label: Lateral ventricular asymmetry
HP:0100960.definition: Abnormal difference in size between the left and right lateral cerebral ventricles.

HP:0100961.label: Enlarged hippocampus
HP:0100961.definition: Increase in size of the hippocampus.
HP:0100961.comment: The hippocampus is part of the limbic system and plays a role in long- and short-term memory.

HP:0100962.label: Excessive shyness
HP:0100962.definition: Atypically high degree of awkwardness or apprehension experienced when approaching or being approached by others.

HP:0100963.label: Hyperesthesia
HP:0100963.definition: Increased sensitivity to stimulation, excluding the special senses, which may refer to various modes of cutaneous sensibility including touch and thermal sensation without pain, as well as to pain.
HP:0100963.comment: Hyperesthesia is a common symptom of neuropathic pain. Neuropathic pain is defined by the International Association for the Study of Pain as pain caused by a lesion or disease of the somatosensory system. The neuropathic pain phenotype contains a spectrum of symptoms that can be roughly categorized into positive and negative symptoms. Hyperesthesia is a positive symptom of neuropathic pain. Positive symptoms are categorized as stimulus-dependent pain, stimulus-independent pain, and paresthesias.

HP:0200000.label: Dysharmonic skeletal maturation
HP:0200000.definition: Different levels of maturation of different bones.
HP:0200000.comment: Bone age is usually determined by using a radiograph of the left hand to compare with images in the Greulich-Pyle atlas and approximating the closest skeletal age. If the skeletal ages of individuals bones are different, i.e., different bones have (clearly) different levels of maturation, then it is referred to as dysharmonic skeletal maturation.

HP:0200001.label: Dysharmonic accelerated bone age
HP:0200001.definition: A type of dysharmonic skeletal maturation in which there is an acceleration in skeletal maturation whose degree differs markedly in different bones.

HP:0200005.label: Abnormal shape of the palpebral fissure
HP:0200005.definition: The presence of an abnormal shape of the palpebral fissure.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal morphology of the palpebral fissure
Abnormal shape of the opening between the eyelids

HP:0200006.label: Slanting of the palpebral fissure
exact_synonyms: Slanting of the opening between the eyelids

HP:0200007.label: Abnormal size of the palpebral fissures
HP:0200007.definition: An abnormal size of the palpebral fissures for example unusually long or short palpebral fissures.
exact_synonyms: Abnormal size of the opening between the eyelids

HP:0200008.label: Intestinal polyposis
HP:0200008.definition: The presence of multiple polyps in the intestine.

HP:0200013.label: Neoplasm of fatty tissue
HP:0200013.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of adipose tissue.

HP:0200016.label: Acrokeratosis
HP:0200016.definition: Overgrowth of the stratum corneum characterized by flesh-coloured or slightly pigmented smooth or warty papules on the upper surface of hands and feet.

HP:0200017.label: Cerebral white matter agenesis
HP:0200017.definition: Congenital defect with failure of the development of the cerebral white matter.
exact_synonyms: Agenesis of the cerebral white matter

HP:0200018.label: Protanomaly
HP:0200018.definition: A type of anomalous trichromacy associated with defective long-wavelength-sensitive (L) cones, causing the sensitivity spectrum to be shifted toward medium wavelengths. This leads to difficulties especially in distinguishing red and green.
HP:0200018.comment: Note that protanomaly and deuteranomaly are both associated with difficulties distinguishing red and green.

HP:0200020.label: Corneal erosion
HP:0200020.definition: An erosion or abrasion of the cornea's outermost layer of epithelial cells.
exact_synonyms: Damage to outer layer of the cornea of the eye

HP:0200022.label: Choroid plexus papilloma
HP:0200022.definition: Choroid plexus papilloma is a histologically benign neoplasm located in the ventricular system of the choroid plexus.

HP:0200023.label: Priapism
HP:0200023.definition: A painful and harmful medical condition in which the erect penis doesn't return to its flaccid state, despite the absence of both physical and psychological stimulation, within four hours.

HP:0200024.label: Premature chromatid separation
HP:0200024.definition: The presence of premature sister chromatid segregation.

HP:0200025.label: Mandibular pain
HP:0200025.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the mandible.

HP:0200026.label: Ocular pain
HP:0200026.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the eye.

HP:0200028.label: Pretibial myxedema
HP:0200028.definition: A diffuse, non-pitting edema and thickening of the skin usually on the anterior aspect of the lower legs spreading to the dorsum of the feet.

HP:0200029.label: Vasculitis in the skin
HP:0200029.definition: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) that affects skeletal muscle tissue.

HP:0200032.label: Kayser-Fleischer ring
HP:0200032.definition: Grey-green or brownish-pigmented ring in the deep epithelial layers at the outer border of the cornea.

HP:0200034.label: Papule
HP:0200034.definition: A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point.

HP:0200035.label: Skin plaque
HP:0200035.definition: A plaque is a solid, raised, plateau-like (flat-topped) lesion greater than 1 cm in diameter.

HP:0200036.label: Skin nodule
HP:0200036.definition: Morphologically similar to a papule, but greater than either 10mm in both width and depth, and most frequently centered in the dermis or subcutaneous fat.
HP:0200036.comment: A nodule is a palpable, solid, round lesion in the deep skin or subcuteaneous tissues that is larger and deeper than a papule. Nodules are solid circumscribed masses. A common definition is that a skin nodule has a diameter of more than 5 mm in infants and more than 10 mm in older children.
exact_synonyms: Growth of abnormal tissue on or under the skin

HP:0200037.label: Skin vesicle
HP:0200037.definition: A circumscribed, fluid-containing, epidermal elevation less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point that (i) Contain serous exudates or serum mixed with blood or pus; (ii) Are discrete, grouped, irregularly distributed, or linear as in Rhus dermatitis; (iii) Are short-lived. Vesicles may break spontaneously or evolve into bullae by enlarging or coalescing with other vesicles.
HP:0200037.comment: Vesicles should be distinguished from bullae, which are are blisters that are greater than one cm in diameter containing serous or seropurulent fluid. Puss-filled vesicles are termed pustules.

HP:0200039.label: Pustule
HP:0200039.definition: A small elevation of the skin containing cloudy or purulent material usually consisting of necrotic inflammatory cells.

HP:0200040.label: Epidermoid cyst
HP:0200040.definition: Nontender, round and firm, but slightly compressible, intradermal or subcutaneous cyst measuring 0.5-5 cm in diameter. Epidermal cysts are intradermal or subcutaneous tumors, grow slowly and occur on the face, neck, back and scrotum. They usually appear at or around puberty, and as a rule an affected individual has one solitary or a few cysts. A central, dark comedone opening (punctum) may be present.
HP:0200040.comment: A cyst is a cavity containing liquid, semisolid, or solid material. An epidermoid cyst is a benign cyst that develops out of ectodermal tissue and consists of a thin layer of squamous epithelium. An epidermal cyst may or may not be painful or release pus, and are usually noticed as a bump on the skin. Epidermal cysts and trichilemmal cysts are clinically indistinguishable. The wall of the epidermal cyst conserves the epidermal layers, but the wall of the trichilemmal cysts, which arise from the external root sheath, shows palisading of unlayered epithelial cells. Homogeneous horny material that is further degraded to fat and cholesterol forms within both types of cysts.

HP:0200041.label: Skin erosion
HP:0200041.definition: A discontinuity of the skin exhibiting incomplete loss of the epidermis, a lesion that is moist, circumscribed, and usually depressed.

HP:0200042.label: Skin ulcer
HP:0200042.definition: A discontinuity of the skin exhibiting complete loss of the epidermis and often portions of the dermis and even subcutaneous fat.

HP:0200043.label: Verrucae
HP:0200043.definition: Warts, benign growths on the skin or mucous membranes that cause cosmetic problems as well as pain and discomfort. Warts most often occur on the hands, feet, and genital areas.
HP:0200043.comment: Cause is a virus called HPV (human papilloma virus), which infects the skin and causes the abnormal growth. There are many different varieties of the virus, which usually depends on the location of the lesion.

HP:0200044.label: Porokeratosis
HP:0200044.definition: A clonal disorder of keratinization with one or multiple atrophic patches surrounded by a clinically and histologically distinctive hyperkeratotic ridgelike border called the cornoid lamella.

HP:0200046.label: Cat cry
HP:0200046.definition: The presence of a characteristic high-pitched cry that sounds similar to the meowing of a kitten.
HP:0200046.comment: This unusual cry is characteristic of the cri du chat syndrome which results from a deletion on the p arm of chromosome 5. It is thought to be due to laryngeal hypoplasia, floppy epiglottis, small larynx, and asymmetric vocal cords, but is probably also related to dysfunction of the central nervous system. This sign occurs in infants and disappears with age.

HP:0200047.label: Chondritis of pinna
HP:0200047.definition: Inflammation of the cartilage of the external ear.

HP:0200049.label: Upper limb hypertonia
HP:0200049.definition: Increased muscle tone observed in the arms of the affected person.

HP:0200050.label: Bracket metacarpal epiphyses
exact_synonyms: Bracket shaped end part of long bone of hand

HP:0200053.label: Hemihypotrophy of lower limb
HP:0200053.definition: Shortening of a leg affecting only one side.

HP:0200056.label: Macular scar
HP:0200056.definition: Fibrous connective tissue consequent upon healing of a wound (i.e., a scar) located in the macula.

HP:0200057.label: Marcus Gunn pupil
HP:0200057.definition: An aberrant pupillary response characterized by (i) Constriction of pupils of both eyes when the light stimulus is applied to the normal eye, and (ii) Dilatation of pupils of both eyes when the light stimulus is rapidly transferred from the normal eye (after brief light exposure to the normal eye) to the affected eye.

HP:0200063.label: Colorectal polyposis
HP:0200063.definition: Multiple abnormal growths that arise from the lining of the large intestine (colon or rectum) and protrude into the intestinal lumen.

HP:0200064.label: Asymmetry of iris pigmentation
HP:0200064.definition: Asymmetry between the two irides or asymmetry between different parts of one iris.

HP:0200067.label: Recurrent spontaneous abortion
HP:0200067.definition: Repeated episodes of abortion (Expulsion of the product of fertilization before completing the term of gestation) without deliberate interference.

HP:0200070.label: Peripheral retinal atrophy
HP:0200070.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the peripheral retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells.

HP:0200071.label: Peripheral vitreoretinal degeneration
HP:0200071.definition: A type of vitreoretinal degeneration with manifestations that are concentrated at the periphery of the retina.

HP:0200072.label: Episodic quadriplegia
HP:0200072.definition: Intermittent episodes of paralysis of all four limbs.

HP:0200073.label: Respiratory insufficiency due to defective ciliary clearance

HP:0200084.label: Giant cell hepatitis
HP:0200084.definition: Chronic hepatitis characterized by parenchymal inflammation with formation of large multinucleated hepatocytes in response to a variety of insults to the liver.
related_synonyms: Giant cell hepatitis shown on biopsy
Giant cell hepatitis on liver biopsy

HP:0200096.label: Triangular-shaped open mouth
HP:0200096.definition: A facial appearance characterized by a permanently or nearly permanently opened mouth, in which the upper lip is tented in a way that the opened mouth has the appearance of a triangle.

HP:0200102.label: Sparse or absent eyelashes
related_synonyms: Partial to total absence of eyelashes

HP:0200104.label: Absent fifth fingernail
HP:0200104.definition: Absence of nail of little finger.

HP:0200109.label: Absent/shortened outer dynein arms
related_synonyms: Respiratory cilia have shortened or absent outer dynein arms

HP:0200114.label: Metabolic alkalosis
HP:0200114.definition: Metabolic alkalosis is defined as a disease state where the pH is elevated to greater than 7.45 secondary to some metabolic process.

HP:0200117.label: Recurrent upper and lower respiratory tract infections
HP:0200117.definition: Increased susceptibility to upper and lower respiratory tract infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of upper and lower respiratory tract infections.

HP:0200118.label: Malabsorption of Vitamin B12
related_synonyms: Vitamin B12 deficiency caused by intestinal malabsorption

HP:0200119.label: Acute hepatitis
HP:0200119.definition: Acute hepatic injury resulting from inflammation typically accompanied by increased serum alanine transaminase activity. Etiologies include viral hepatitis, drugs, toxins, and autoimmune disorders.

HP:0200120.label: Chronic active hepatitis
HP:0200120.definition: Chronic hepatitis associated with recurrent clinical exacerbations, extrahepatic manifestations, and progression to cirrhosis.

HP:0200123.label: Chronic hepatitis
HP:0200123.definition: Hepatitis that lasts for more than six months.

HP:0200124.label: Chronic hepatitis due to cryptosporidium infection
HP:0200124.definition: Chronic hepatitis associated with infection by cryptosporidia, as demonstrated (for example) by immunohistochemistry of liver tissue.
related_synonyms: Hepatitis, chronic, due to cryptosporidium infection

HP:0200127.label: Atrial cardiomyopathy
HP:0200127.definition: Any complex of structural, architectural, contractile or electrophysiological changes affecting the atria with the potential to produce clinically relevant manifestations.

HP:0200128.label: Biventricular hypertrophy
HP:0200128.definition: Thickening of the heart walls in both ventricles.

HP:0200134.label: Epileptic encephalopathy
HP:0200134.definition: A condition in which epileptiform abnormalities are believed to contribute to the progressive disturbance in cerebral function. Epileptic encephalaopathy is characterized by (1) electrographic EEG paroxysmal activity that is often aggressive, (2) seizures that are usually multiform and intractable, (3) cognitive, behavioral and neurological deficits that may be relentless, and (4) sometimes early death.
HP:0200134.comment: Seizures alone without any underlying neurologic or medical illness can be the sole cause of encephalopathy. Patients with seizures as a cause or consequence of encephalopathy present with a wide variety of neurologic symptoms from mild reduction or alteration of consciousness to coma. Findings on neurologic exam are often nonfocal, nonspecific, and not predictive of the presence of seizures. Patients may or may not have subtle motor findings accompanying the presentation of encephalopathy. Signs range from very focal findings, such as nystagmus, eye flutter, blinking, and eye deviation to more widespread signs, such as myoclonus, tremulousness, and autonomic instability.

HP:0200143.label: Megaloblastic erythroid hyperplasia
related_synonyms: Bone marrow biopsy shows megaloblastic erythroid hyperplasia

HP:0200146.label: Mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
HP:0200146.definition: An increase of medial mucoid extracellular matrix creating translamellar and/or intralamellar expansions including extracellular pools as noted on an H&E stain and/or a stain to highlight extracellular matrix material (Movat's pentachrome, Alcian blue, etc.).
HP:0200146.comment: MEMA replaces a variety of terms used in the past such as cystic medial necrosis, cystonecrosis, cystic degeneration, mucoid degeneration which, while generally understood by pathologists, are inaccurate. This histopathology can be subclassified and graded according to distribution, severity, and/or whether it crosses over multiple lamellar units as described. The grading should be reported as mild/moderate/severe and the distribution should be reported as focal, multifocal, or extensive.
exact_synonyms: Cystic medial necrosis of the aorta

HP:3000047.label: Abnormal glossopharyngeal nerve morphology
HP:3000047.definition: Any structural anomaly of the glossopharyngeal nerve, the ninth paired cranial nerve (CN IX).
HP:3000047.comment: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates in the medulla oblongata. It Innervates the oropharynx, carotid body and sinus, as well as the posterior third of the tongue (where it mediates taste sensation), the middle ear cavity and the Eustachian tube. Additionally, it innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle of the pharynx.

HP:3000048.label: Abnormal great auricular nerve morphology
HP:3000048.definition: Any structural anomaly of a great auricular nerve.
HP:3000048.comment: The great auricular nerve originates from the cervical plexus and ascends to the posterior inferior region of the parotid gland, where it divides into several small branches. The nerve supplies sensation for an extensive area of the face including the skin over the parotid gland and the mastoid process and the surface of the external ear. The great auricular nerve winds around the posterior aspect of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. After perforating the deep fascia, it ascends upon the sternocleidomastoid muscle beneath the platysma to the parotid gland, where it divides into an anterior and a posterior branch. The anterior branch provides sensory innervation to the skin overlying the parotid gland and communicates with the facial nerve in the substance of the gland. The posterior branch innervates the skin over the mastoid and the posterior surface of the auricle except at its upper part.
